GEN 1:1 1 When God began to create the heavens and the earth—
GEN 1:2 2 the earth was without shape or form, it was dark over the deep sea, and God’s wind swept over the waters—
GEN 1:3 3 God said, “Let there be light.” And so light appeared.
GEN 1:4 4 God saw how good the light was. God separated the light from the darkness.
GEN 1:5 5 God named the light Day and the darkness Night. There was evening and there was morning: the first day.
GEN 1:6 6 God said, “Let there be a dome in the middle of the waters to separate the waters from each other.”
GEN 1:7 7 God made the dome and separated the waters under the dome from the waters above the dome. And it happened in that way.
GEN 1:8 8 God named the dome Sky. There was evening and there was morning: the second day.
GEN 1:9 9 God said, “Let the waters under the sky come together into one place so that the dry land can appear.” And that’s what happened.
GEN 1:10 10 God named the dry land Earth, and he named the gathered waters Seas. God saw how good it was.
GEN 1:11 11 God said, “Let the earth grow plant life: plants yielding seeds and fruit trees bearing fruit with seeds inside it, each according to its kind throughout the earth.” And that’s what happened.
GEN 1:12 12 The earth produced plant life: plants yielding seeds, each according to its kind, and trees bearing fruit with seeds inside it, each according to its kind. God saw how good it was.
GEN 1:13 13 There was evening and there was morning: the third day.
GEN 1:14 14 God said, “Let there be lights in the dome of the sky to separate the day from the night. They will mark events, sacred seasons, days, and years.
GEN 1:15 15 They will be lights in the dome of the sky to shine on the earth.” And that’s what happened.
GEN 1:16 16 God made the stars and two great lights: the larger light to rule over the day and the smaller light to rule over the night.
GEN 1:17 17 God put them in the dome of the sky to shine on the earth,
GEN 1:18 18 to rule over the day and over the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. God saw how good it was.
GEN 1:19 19 There was evening and there was morning: the fourth day.
GEN 1:20 20 God said, “Let the waters swarm with living things, and let birds fly above the earth up in the dome of the sky.”
GEN 1:21 21 God created the great sea animals and all the tiny living things that swarm in the waters, each according to its kind, and all the winged birds, each according to its kind. God saw how good it was.
GEN 1:22 22 Then God blessed them: “Be fertile and multiply and fill the waters in the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth.”
GEN 1:23 23 There was evening and there was morning: the fifth day.
GEN 1:24 24 God said, “Let the earth produce every kind of living thing: livestock, crawling things, and wildlife.” And that’s what happened.
GEN 1:25 25 God made every kind of wildlife, every kind of livestock, and every kind of creature that crawls on the ground. God saw how good it was.
GEN 1:26 26 Then God said, “Let us make humanity in our image to resemble us so that they may take charge of the fish of the sea, the birds in the sky, the livestock, all the earth, and all the crawling things on earth.”
GEN 1:27 27 God created humanity in God’s own image, in the divine image God created them, male and female God created them.
GEN 1:28 28 God blessed them and said to them, “Be fertile and multiply; fill the earth and master it. Take charge of the fish of the sea, the birds in the sky, and everything crawling on the ground.”
GEN 1:29 29 Then God said, “I now give to you all the plants on the earth that yield seeds and all the trees whose fruit produces its seeds within it. These will be your food.
GEN 1:30 30 To all wildlife, to all the birds in the sky, and to everything crawling on the ground—to everything that breathes—I give all the green grasses for food.” And that’s what happened.
GEN 1:31 31 God saw everything he had made: it was supremely good. There was evening and there was morning: the sixth day.
GEN 2:1 1 The heavens and the earth and all who live in them were completed.
GEN 2:2 2 On the sixth day God completed all the work that he had done, and on the seventh day God rested from all the work that he had done.
GEN 2:3 3 God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, because on it God rested from all the work of creation.
GEN 2:4 4 This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created. On the day the LORD God made earth and sky—
GEN 2:5 5 before any wild plants appeared on the earth, and before any field crops grew, because the LORD God hadn’t yet sent rain on the earth and there was still no human being to farm the fertile land,
GEN 2:6 6 though a stream rose from the earth and watered all of the fertile land—
GEN 2:7 7 the LORD God formed the human from the topsoil of the fertile land and blew life’s breath into his nostrils. The human came to life.
GEN 2:8 8 The LORD God planted a garden in Eden in the east and put there the human he had formed.
GEN 2:9 9 In the fertile land, the LORD God grew every beautiful tree with edible fruit, and also he grew the tree of life in the middle of the garden and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
GEN 2:10 10 A river flows from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divides into four headwaters.
GEN 2:11 11 The name of the first river is the Pishon. It flows around the entire land of Havilah, where there is gold.
GEN 2:12 12 That land’s gold is pure, and the land also has sweet-smelling resins and gemstones.
GEN 2:13 13 The name of the second river is the Gihon. It flows around the entire land of Cush.
GEN 2:14 14 The name of the third river is the Tigris, flowing east of Assyria; and the name of the fourth river is the Euphrates.
GEN 2:15 15 The LORD God took the human and settled him in the garden of Eden to farm it and to take care of it.
GEN 2:16 16 The LORD God commanded the human, “Eat your fill from all of the garden’s trees;
GEN 2:17 17 but don’t eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, because on the day you eat from it, you will die!”
GEN 2:18 18 Then the LORD God said, “It’s not good that the human is alone. I will make him a helper that is perfect for him.”
GEN 2:19 19 So the LORD God formed from the fertile land all the wild animals and all the birds in the sky and brought them to the human to see what he would name them. The human gave each living being its name.
GEN 2:20 20 The human named all the livestock, all the birds in the sky, and all the wild animals. But a helper perfect for him was nowhere to be found.
GEN 2:21 21 So the LORD God put the human into a deep and heavy sleep, and took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh over it.
GEN 2:22 22 With the rib taken from the human, the LORD God fashioned a woman and brought her to the human being.
GEN 2:23 23 The human said, “This one finally is bone from my bones and flesh from my flesh. She will be called a woman because from a man she was taken.”
GEN 2:24 24 This is the reason that a man leaves his father and mother and embraces his wife, and they become one flesh.
GEN 2:25 25 The two of them were naked, the man and his wife, but they weren’t embarrassed.
GEN 3:1 1 The snake was the most intelligent of all the wild animals that the LORD God had made. He said to the woman, “Did God really say that you shouldn’t eat from any tree in the garden?”
GEN 3:2 2 The woman said to the snake, “We may eat the fruit of the garden’s trees
GEN 3:3 3 but not the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden. God said, ‘Don’t eat from it, and don’t touch it, or you will die.’”
GEN 3:4 4 The snake said to the woman, “You won’t die!
GEN 3:5 5 God knows that on the day you eat from it, you will see clearly and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”
GEN 3:6 6 The woman saw that the tree was beautiful with delicious food and that the tree would provide wisdom, so she took some of its fruit and ate it, and also gave some to her husband, who was with her, and he ate it.
GEN 3:7 7 Then they both saw clearly and knew that they were naked. So they sewed fig leaves together and made garments for themselves.
GEN 3:8 8 During that day’s cool evening breeze, they heard the sound of the LORD God walking in the garden; and the man and his wife hid themselves from the LORD God in the middle of the garden’s trees.
GEN 3:9 9 The LORD God called to the man and said to him, “Where are you?”
GEN 3:10 10 The man replied, “I heard your sound in the garden; I was afraid because I was naked, and I hid myself.”
GEN 3:11 11 He said, “Who told you that you were naked? Did you eat from the tree, which I commanded you not to eat?”
GEN 3:12 12 The man said, “The woman you gave me, she gave me some fruit from the tree, and I ate.”
GEN 3:13 13 The LORD God said to the woman, “What have you done?!” And the woman said, “The snake tricked me, and I ate.”
GEN 3:14 14 The LORD God said to the snake, “Because you did this, you are the one cursed out of all the farm animals, out of all the wild animals. On your belly you will crawl, and dust you will eat every day of your life.
GEN 3:15 15 I will put contempt between you and the woman, between your offspring and hers. They will strike your head, but you will strike at their heels.”
GEN 3:16 16 To the woman he said, “I will make your pregnancy very painful; in pain you will bear children. You will desire your husband, but he will rule over you.”
GEN 3:17 17 To the man he said, “Because you listened to your wife’s voice and you ate from the tree that I commanded, ‘Don’t eat from it,’ cursed is the fertile land because of you; in pain you will eat from it every day of your life.
GEN 3:18 18 Weeds and thistles will grow for you, even as you eat the field’s plants;
GEN 3:19 19 by the sweat of your face you will eat bread— until you return to the fertile land, since from it you were taken; you are soil, to the soil you will return.”
GEN 3:20 20 The man named his wife Eve because she is the mother of everyone who lives.
GEN 3:21 21 The LORD God made the man and his wife leather clothes and dressed them.
GEN 3:22 22 The LORD God said, “The human being has now become like one of us, knowing good and evil.” Now, so he doesn’t stretch out his hand and take also from the tree of life and eat and live forever,
GEN 3:23 23 the LORD God sent him out of the garden of Eden to farm the fertile land from which he was taken.
GEN 3:24 24 He drove out the human. To the east of the garden of Eden, he stationed winged creatures wielding flaming swords to guard the way to the tree of life.
GEN 4:1 1 The man Adam knew his wife Eve intimately. She became pregnant and gave birth to Cain, and said, “I have given life to a man with the LORD ’s help.”
GEN 4:2 2 She gave birth a second time to Cain’s brother Abel. Abel cared for the flocks, and Cain farmed the fertile land.
GEN 4:3 3 Some time later, Cain presented an offering to the LORD from the land’s crops
GEN 4:4 4 while Abel presented his flock’s oldest offspring with their fat. The LORD looked favorably on Abel and his sacrifice
GEN 4:5 5 but didn’t look favorably on Cain and his sacrifice. Cain became very angry and looked resentful.
GEN 4:6 6 The LORD said to Cain, “Why are you angry, and why do you look so resentful?
GEN 4:7 7 If you do the right thing, won’t you be accepted? But if you don’t do the right thing, sin will be waiting at the door ready to strike! It will entice you, but you must rule over it.”
GEN 4:8 8 Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let’s go out to the field.” When they were in the field, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.
GEN 4:9 9 The LORD said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” Cain said, “I don’t know. Am I my brother’s guardian?”
GEN 4:10 10 The LORD said, “What did you do? The voice of your brother’s blood is crying to me from the ground.
GEN 4:11 11 You are now cursed from the ground that opened its mouth to take your brother’s blood from your hand.
GEN 4:12 12 When you farm the fertile land, it will no longer grow anything for you, and you will become a roving nomad on the earth.”
GEN 4:13 13 Cain said to the LORD , “My punishment is more than I can bear.
GEN 4:14 14 Now that you’ve driven me away from the fertile land and I am hidden from your presence, I’m about to become a roving nomad on the earth, and anyone who finds me will kill me.”
GEN 4:15 15 The LORD said to him, “It won’t happen; anyone who kills Cain will be paid back seven times.” The LORD put a sign on Cain so that no one who found him would assault him.
GEN 4:16 16 Cain left the LORD ’s presence, and he settled down in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
GEN 4:17 17 Cain knew his wife intimately. She became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. Cain built a city and named the city after his son Enoch.
GEN 4:18 18 Irad was born to Enoch. Irad fathered Mehujael, Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
GEN 4:19 19 Lamech took two wives, the first named Adah and the second Zillah.
GEN 4:20 20 Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the ancestor of those who live in tents and own livestock.
GEN 4:21 21 His brother’s name was Jubal; he was the ancestor of those who play stringed and wind instruments.
GEN 4:22 22 Zillah also gave birth to Tubal-cain, the ancestor of blacksmiths and all artisans of bronze and iron. Tubal-cain’s sister was Naamah.
GEN 4:23 23 Lamech said to his wives, “Adah and Zillah, listen to my voice; wives of Lamech, pay attention to my words: I killed a man for wounding me, a boy for striking me;
GEN 4:24 24 so Cain will be paid back seven times and Lamech seventy-seven times.”
GEN 4:25 25 Adam knew his wife intimately again, and she gave birth to a son. She named him Seth “because God has given me another child in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.”
GEN 4:26 26 Seth also fathered a son and named him Enosh. At that time, people began to worship in the LORD ’s name.
GEN 5:1 1 This is the record of Adam’s descendants. On the day God created humanity, he made them to resemble God
GEN 5:2 2 and created them male and female. He blessed them and called them humanity on the day they were created.
GEN 5:3 3 When Adam was 130 years old, he became the father of a son in his image, resembling him, and named him Seth.
GEN 5:4 4 After Seth’s birth, Adam lived 800 years; he had other sons and daughters.
GEN 5:5 5 In all, Adam lived 930 years, and he died.
GEN 5:6 6 When Seth was 105 years old, he became the father of Enosh.
GEN 5:7 7 After the birth of Enosh, Seth lived 807 years; and he had other sons and daughters.
GEN 5:8 8 In all, Seth lived 912 years, and he died.
GEN 5:9 9 When Enosh was 90 years old, he became the father of Kenan.
GEN 5:10 10 After Kenan’s birth, Enosh lived 815 years; and he had other sons and daughters.
GEN 5:11 11 In all, Enosh lived 905 years, and he died.
GEN 5:12 12 When Kenan was 70 years old, he became the father of Mahalalel.
GEN 5:13 13 After the birth of Mahalalel, Kenan lived 840 years; and he had other sons and daughters.
GEN 5:14 14 In all, Kenan lived 910 years, and he died.
GEN 5:15 15 When Mahalalel was 65 years old, he became the father of Jared.
GEN 5:16 16 After Jared’s birth, Mahalalel lived 830 years; and he had other sons and daughters.
GEN 5:17 17 In all, Mahalalel lived 895 years, and he died.
GEN 5:18 18 When Jared was 162 years old, he became the father of Enoch.
GEN 5:19 19 After Enoch’s birth, Jared lived 800 years; and he had other sons and daughters.
GEN 5:20 20 In all, Jared lived 962 years, and he died.
GEN 5:21 21 When Enoch was 65 years old, he became the father of Methuselah.
GEN 5:22 22 Enoch walked with God. After Methuselah’s birth, Enoch lived 300 years; and he had other sons and daughters.
GEN 5:23 23 In all, Enoch lived 365 years.
GEN 5:24 24 Enoch walked with God and disappeared because God took him.
GEN 5:25 25 When Methuselah was 187 years old, he became the father of Lamech.
GEN 5:26 26 After Lamech’s birth, Methuselah lived 782 years; and he had other sons and daughters.
GEN 5:27 27 In all, Methuselah lived 969 years, and he died.
GEN 5:28 28 When Lamech was 182 years old, he became the father of a son
GEN 5:29 29 and named him Noah, saying, “This one will give us relief from our hard work, from the pain in our hands, because of the fertile land that the LORD cursed.”
GEN 5:30 30 After Noah’s birth, Lamech lived 595 years; and he had other sons and daughters.
GEN 5:31 31 In all, Lamech lived 777 years, and he died.
GEN 5:32 32 When Noah was 500 years old, Noah became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
GEN 6:1 1 When the number of people started to increase throughout the fertile land, daughters were born to them.
GEN 6:2 2 The divine beings saw how beautiful these human women were, so they married the ones they chose.
GEN 6:3 3 The LORD said, “My breath will not remain in humans forever, because they are flesh. They will live one hundred twenty years.”
GEN 6:4 4 In those days, giants lived on the earth and also afterward, when divine beings and human daughters had sexual relations and gave birth to children. These were the ancient heroes, famous men.
GEN 6:5 5 The LORD saw that humanity had become thoroughly evil on the earth and that every idea their minds thought up was always completely evil.
GEN 6:6 6 The LORD regretted making human beings on the earth, and he was heartbroken.
GEN 6:7 7 So the LORD said, “I will wipe off of the land the human race that I’ve created: from human beings to livestock to the crawling things to the birds in the skies, because I regret I ever made them.”
GEN 6:8 8 But as for Noah, the LORD approved of him.
GEN 6:9 9 These are Noah’s descendants. In his generation, Noah was a moral and exemplary man; he walked with God.
GEN 6:10 10 Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
GEN 6:11 11 In God’s sight, the earth had become corrupt and was filled with violence.
GEN 6:12 12 God saw that the earth was corrupt, because all creatures behaved corruptly on the earth.
GEN 6:13 13 God said to Noah, “The end has come for all creatures, since they have filled the earth with violence. I am now about to destroy them along with the earth,
GEN 6:14 14 so make a wooden ark. Make the ark with nesting places and cover it inside and out with tar.
GEN 6:15 15 This is how you should make it: four hundred fifty feet long, seventy-five feet wide, and forty-five feet high.
GEN 6:16 16 Make a roof for the ark and complete it one foot from the top. Put a door in its side. In the hold below, make the second and third decks.
GEN 6:17 17 “I am now bringing the floodwaters over the earth to destroy everything under the sky that breathes. Everything on earth is about to take its last breath.
GEN 6:18 18 But I will set up my covenant with you. You will go into the ark together with your sons, your wife, and your sons’ wives.
GEN 6:19 19 From all living things—from all creatures—you are to bring a pair, male and female, into the ark with you to keep them alive.
GEN 6:20 20 From each kind of bird, from each kind of livestock, and from each kind of everything that crawls on the ground—a pair from each will go in with you to stay alive.
GEN 6:21 21 Take some from every kind of food and stow it as food for you and for the animals.”
GEN 6:22 22 Noah did everything exactly as God commanded him.
GEN 7:1 1 The LORD said to Noah, “Go into the ark with your whole household, because among this generation I’ve seen that you are a moral man.
GEN 7:2 2 From every clean animal, take seven pairs, a male and his mate; and from every unclean animal, take one pair, a male and his mate;
GEN 7:3 3 and from the birds in the sky as well, take seven pairs, male and female, so that their offspring will survive throughout the earth.
GEN 7:4 4 In seven days from now I will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights. I will wipe off from the fertile land every living thing that I have made.”
GEN 7:5 5 Noah did everything the LORD commanded him.
GEN 7:6 6 Noah was 600 years old when the floodwaters arrived on earth.
GEN 7:7 7 Noah, his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives with him entered the ark to escape the floodwaters.
GEN 7:8 8 From the clean and unclean animals, from the birds and everything crawling on the ground,
GEN 7:9 9 two of each, male and female, went into the ark with Noah, just as God commanded Noah.
GEN 7:10 10 After seven days, the floodwaters arrived on the earth.
GEN 7:11 11 In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day—on that day all the springs of the deep sea erupted, and the windows in the skies opened.
GEN 7:12 12 It rained on the earth forty days and forty nights.
GEN 7:13 13 That same day Noah, with his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, Noah’s wife, and his sons’ three wives, went into the ark.
GEN 7:14 14 They and every kind of animal—every kind of livestock, every kind that crawls on the ground, every kind of bird —
GEN 7:15 15 they came to Noah and entered the ark, two of every creature that breathes.
GEN 7:16 16 Male and female of every creature went in, just as God had commanded him. Then the LORD closed the door behind them.
GEN 7:17 17 The flood remained on the earth for forty days. The waters rose, lifted the ark, and it rode high above the earth.
GEN 7:18 18 The waters rose and spread out over the earth. The ark floated on the surface of the waters.
GEN 7:19 19 The waters rose even higher over the earth; they covered all of the highest mountains under the sky.
GEN 7:20 20 The waters rose twenty-three feet high, covering the mountains.
GEN 7:21 21 Every creature took its last breath: the things crawling on the ground, birds, livestock, wild animals, everything swarming on the ground, and every human being.
GEN 7:22 22 Everything on dry land with life’s breath in its nostrils died.
GEN 7:23 23 God wiped away every living thing that was on the fertile land—from human beings to livestock to crawling things to birds in the sky. They were wiped off the earth. Only Noah and those with him in the ark were left.
GEN 7:24 24 The waters rose over the earth for one hundred fifty days.
GEN 8:1 1 God remembered Noah, all those alive, and all the animals with him in the ark. God sent a wind over the earth so that the waters receded.
GEN 8:2 2 The springs of the deep sea and the skies closed up. The skies held back the rain.
GEN 8:3 3 The waters receded gradually from the earth. After one hundred fifty days, the waters decreased;
GEN 8:4 4 and in the seventh month, on the seventeenth day, the ark came to rest on the Ararat mountains.
GEN 8:5 5 The waters decreased gradually until the tenth month, and on the first day of the tenth month the mountain peaks appeared.
GEN 8:6 6 After forty days, Noah opened the window of the ark that he had made.
GEN 8:7 7 He sent out a raven, and it flew back and forth until the waters over the entire earth had dried up.
GEN 8:8 8 Then he sent out a dove to see if the waters on all of the fertile land had subsided,
GEN 8:9 9 but the dove found no place to set its foot. It returned to him in the ark since waters still covered the entire earth. Noah stretched out his hand, took it, and brought it back into the ark.
GEN 8:10 10 He waited seven more days and sent the dove out from the ark again.
GEN 8:11 11 The dove came back to him in the evening, grasping a torn olive leaf in its beak. Then Noah knew that the waters were subsiding from the earth.
GEN 8:12 12 He waited seven more days and sent out the dove, but it didn’t come back to him again.
GEN 8:13 13 In Noah’s six hundred first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters dried up from the earth. Noah removed the ark’s hatch and saw that the surface of the fertile land had dried up.
GEN 8:14 14 In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day, the earth was dry.
GEN 8:15 15 God spoke to Noah,
GEN 8:16 16 “Go out of the ark, you and your wife, your sons, and your sons’ wives with you.
GEN 8:17 17 Bring out with you all the animals of every kind—birds, livestock, everything crawling on the ground—so that they may populate the earth, be fertile, and multiply on the earth.”
GEN 8:18 18 So Noah went out of the ark with his sons, his wife, and his sons’ wives.
GEN 8:19 19 All the animals, all the livestock, all the birds, and everything crawling on the ground, came out of the ark by their families.
GEN 8:20 20 Noah built an altar to the LORD . He took some of the clean large animals and some of the clean birds, and placed entirely burned offerings on the altar.
GEN 8:21 21 The LORD smelled the pleasing scent, and the LORD thought to himself, I will not curse the fertile land anymore because of human beings since the ideas of the human mind are evil from their youth. I will never again destroy every living thing as I have done.
GEN 8:22 22 As long as the earth exists, seedtime and harvest, cold and hot, summer and autumn, day and night will not cease.
GEN 9:1 1 God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them, “Be fertile, multiply, and fill the earth.
GEN 9:2 2 All of the animals on the earth will fear you and dread you—all the birds in the skies, everything crawling on the ground, and all of the sea’s fish. They are in your power.
GEN 9:3 3 Everything that lives and moves will be your food. Just as I gave you the green grasses, I now give you everything.
GEN 9:4 4 However, you must not eat meat with its life, its blood, in it.
GEN 9:5 5 I will surely demand your blood for a human life, from every living thing I will demand it. From humans, from a man for his brother, I will demand something for a human life.
GEN 9:6 6 Whoever sheds human blood, by a human his blood will be shed; for in the divine image God made human beings.
GEN 9:7 7 As for you, be fertile and multiply. Populate the earth and multiply in it.”
GEN 9:8 8 God said to Noah and to his sons with him,
GEN 9:9 9 “I am now setting up my covenant with you, with your descendants,
GEN 9:10 10 and with every living being with you—with the birds, with the large animals, and with all the animals of the earth, leaving the ark with you.
GEN 9:11 11 I will set up my covenant with you so that never again will all life be cut off by floodwaters. There will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”
GEN 9:12 12 God said, “This is the symbol of the covenant that I am drawing up between me and you and every living thing with you, on behalf of every future generation.
GEN 9:13 13 I have placed my bow in the clouds; it will be the symbol of the covenant between me and the earth.
GEN 9:14 14 When I bring clouds over the earth and the bow appears in the clouds,
GEN 9:15 15 I will remember the covenant between me and you and every living being among all the creatures. Floodwaters will never again destroy all creatures.
GEN 9:16 16 The bow will be in the clouds, and upon seeing it I will remember the enduring covenant between God and every living being of all the earth’s creatures.”
GEN 9:17 17 God said to Noah, “This is the symbol of the covenant that I have set up between me and all creatures on earth.”
GEN 9:18 18 Noah’s sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth came out of the ark. Now Ham was Canaan’s father.
GEN 9:19 19 These were Noah’s three sons, and from them the whole earth was populated.
GEN 9:20 20 Noah, a farmer, made a new start and planted a vineyard.
GEN 9:21 21 He drank some of the wine, became drunk, and took off his clothes in his tent.
GEN 9:22 22 Ham, Canaan’s father, saw his father naked and told his two brothers who were outside.
GEN 9:23 23 Shem and Japheth took a robe, threw it over their shoulders, walked backward, and covered their naked father without looking at him because they turned away.
GEN 9:24 24 When Noah woke up from his wine, he discovered what his youngest son had done to him.
GEN 9:25 25 He said, “Cursed be Canaan: the lowest servant he will be for his brothers.”
GEN 9:26 26 He also said, “Bless the LORD , the God of Shem; Canaan will be his servant.
GEN 9:27 27 May God give space to Japheth; he will live in Shem’s tents, and Canaan will be his servant.”
GEN 9:28 28 After the flood, Noah lived 350 years.
GEN 9:29 29 In all, Noah lived 950 years; then he died.
GEN 10:1 1 These are the descendants of Noah’s sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, to whom children were born after the flood.
GEN 10:2 2 Japheth’s sons: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
GEN 10:3 3 Gomer’s sons: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
GEN 10:4 4 Javan’s sons: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
GEN 10:5 5 From these the island-nations were divided into their own countries, each according to their languages and their clans within their nations.
GEN 10:6 6 Ham’s sons: Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.
GEN 10:7 7 Cush’s sons: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah’s sons: Sheba and Dedan.
GEN 10:8 8 Cush fathered Nimrod, the first great warrior on earth.
GEN 10:9 9 The LORD saw him as a great hunter, and so it is said, “Like Nimrod, whom the LORD saw as a great hunter.”
GEN 10:10 10 The most important cities in his kingdom were Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar.
GEN 10:11 11 Asshur left that land and built Nineveh, Rehoboth City, Calah,
GEN 10:12 12 and Resen, the great city between Nineveh and Calah.
GEN 10:13 13 Egypt fathered Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,
GEN 10:14 14 Pathrusim, Casluhim, and Caphtorim, from which the Philistines came.
GEN 10:15 15 Canaan fathered Sidon his oldest son, and Heth,

EXO 1:17 17 Now the two midwives respected God so they didn’t obey the Egyptian king’s order. Instead, they let the baby boys live.
EXO 1:18 18 So the king of Egypt called the two midwives and said to them, “Why are you doing this? Why are you letting the baby boys live?”
EXO 1:19 19 The two midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because Hebrew women aren’t like Egyptian women. They’re much stronger and give birth before any midwives can get to them.”
EXO 1:20 20 So God treated the midwives well, and the people kept on multiplying and became very strong.

EXO 3:1 1 Moses was taking care of the flock for his father-in-law Jethro, Midian’s priest. He led his flock out to the edge of the desert, and he came to God’s mountain called Horeb.
EXO 3:2 2 The LORD ’s messenger appeared to him in a flame of fire in the middle of a bush. Moses saw that the bush was in flames, but it didn’t burn up.
EXO 3:3 3 Then Moses said to himself, Let me check out this amazing sight and find out why the bush isn’t burning up.
EXO 3:4 4 When the LORD saw that he was coming to look, God called to him out of the bush, “Moses, Moses!” Moses said, “I’m here.”
EXO 3:5 5 Then the LORD said, “Don’t come any closer! Take off your sandals, because you are standing on holy ground.”
EXO 3:6 6 He continued, “I am the God of your father, Abraham’s God, Isaac’s God, and Jacob’s God.” Moses hid his face because he was afraid to look at God.
EXO 3:7 7 Then the LORD said, “I’ve clearly seen my people oppressed in Egypt. I’ve heard their cry of injustice because of their slave masters. I know about their pain.
EXO 3:8 8 I’ve come down to rescue them from the Egyptians in order to take them out of that land and bring them to a good and broad land, a land that’s full of milk and honey, a place where the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites all live.
EXO 3:9 9 Now the Israelites’ cries of injustice have reached me. I’ve seen just how much the Egyptians have oppressed them.
EXO 3:10 10 So get going. I’m sending you to Pharaoh to bring my people, the Israelites, out of Egypt.”
EXO 3:11 11 But Moses said to God, “Who am I to go to Pharaoh and to bring the Israelites out of Egypt?”
EXO 3:12 12 God said, “I’ll be with you. And this will show you that I’m the one who sent you. After you bring the people out of Egypt, you will come back here and worship God on this mountain.”
EXO 3:13 13 But Moses said to God, “If I now come to the Israelites and say to them, ‘The God of your ancestors has sent me to you,’ they are going to ask me, ‘What’s this God’s name?’ What am I supposed to say to them?”
EXO 3:14 14 God said to Moses, “I Am Who I Am. So say to the Israelites, ‘I Am has sent me to you.’”
EXO 3:15 15 God continued, “Say to the Israelites, ‘The LORD , the God of your ancestors, Abraham’s God, Isaac’s God, and Jacob’s God, has sent me to you.’ This is my name forever; this is how all generations will remember me.
EXO 3:16 16 “Go and get Israel’s elders together and say to them, ‘The LORD , the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob, has appeared to me. The LORD said, “I’ve been paying close attention to you and to what has been done to you in Egypt.
EXO 3:17 17 I’ve decided to take you away from the harassment in Egypt to the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, a land full of milk and honey.”’
EXO 3:18 18 They will accept what you say to them. Then you and Israel’s elders will go to Egypt’s king and say to him, ‘The LORD , the Hebrews’ God, has met with us. So now let us go on a three-day journey into the desert so that we can offer sacrifices to the LORD our God.’
EXO 3:19 19 However, I know that Egypt’s king won’t let you go unless he’s forced to do it.
EXO 3:20 20 So I’ll use my strength and hit Egypt with dramatic displays of my power. After that, he’ll let you go.
EXO 3:21 21 “I’ll make it so that when you leave Egypt, the Egyptians will be kind to you and you won’t go away empty-handed.
EXO 3:22 22 Every woman will ask her neighbor along with the immigrant in her household for their silver and their gold jewelry as well as their clothing. Then you will put it on your sons and daughters, and you will rob the Egyptians.”
EXO 4:1 1 Then Moses replied, “But what if they don’t believe me or pay attention to me? They might say to me, ‘The LORD didn’t appear to you!’”
EXO 4:2 2 The LORD said to him, “What’s that in your hand?” Moses replied, “A shepherd’s rod.”
EXO 4:3 3 The LORD said, “Throw it down on the ground.” So Moses threw it on the ground, and it turned into a snake. Moses jumped back from it.
EXO 4:4 4 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Reach out and grab the snake by the tail.” So Moses reached out and grabbed it, and it turned back into a rod in his hand.
EXO 4:5 5 “Do this so that they will believe that the LORD , the God of their ancestors, Abraham’s God, Isaac’s God, and Jacob’s God has in fact appeared to you.”
EXO 4:6 6 Again, the LORD said to Moses, “Put your hand inside your coat.” So Moses put his hand inside his coat. When he took his hand out, his hand had a skin disease flaky like snow.
EXO 4:7 7 Then God said, “Put your hand back inside your coat.” So Moses put his hand back inside his coat. When he took it back out again, the skin of his hand had returned to normal.
EXO 4:8 8 “If they won’t believe you or pay attention to the first sign, they may believe the second sign.
EXO 4:9 9 If they won’t believe even these two signs or pay attention to you, then take some water from the Nile River and pour it out on dry ground. The water that you take from the Nile will turn into blood on the dry ground.”
EXO 4:10 10 But Moses said to the LORD , “My Lord, I’ve never been able to speak well, not yesterday, not the day before, and certainly not now since you’ve been talking to your servant. I have a slow mouth and a thick tongue.”
EXO 4:11 11 Then the LORD said to him, “Who gives people the ability to speak? Who’s responsible for making them unable to speak or hard of hearing, sighted or blind? Isn’t it I, the LORD ?
EXO 4:12 12 Now go! I’ll help you speak, and I’ll teach you what you should say.”
EXO 4:13 13 But Moses said, “Please, my Lord, just send someone else.”
EXO 4:14 14 Then the LORD got angry at Moses and said, “What about your brother Aaron the Levite? I know he can speak very well. He’s on his way out to meet you now, and he’s looking forward to seeing you.
EXO 4:15 15 Speak to him and tell him what he’s supposed to say. I’ll help both of you speak, and I’ll teach both of you what to do.
EXO 4:16 16 Aaron will speak for you to the people. He’ll be a spokesperson for you, and you will be like God for him.
EXO 4:17 17 Take this shepherd’s rod with you too so that you can do the signs.”
EXO 4:18 18 Moses went back to his father-in-law Jethro and said to him, “Please let me go back to my family in Egypt and see whether or not they are still living.” Jethro said to Moses, “Go in peace.”
EXO 4:19 19 The LORD said to Moses in Midian, “Go back to Egypt because everyone there who wanted to kill you has died.”
EXO 4:20 20 So Moses took his wife and his children, put them on a donkey, and went back to the land of Egypt. Moses also carried the shepherd’s rod from God in his hand.
EXO 4:21 21 The LORD said to Moses, “When you go back to Egypt, make sure that you appear before Pharaoh and do all the amazing acts that I’ve given you the power to do. But I’ll make him stubborn so that he won’t let the people go.
EXO 4:22 22 Then say to Pharaoh, ‘This is what the LORD says: Israel is my oldest son.
EXO 4:23 23 I said to you, “Let my son go so he could worship me.” But you refused to let him go. As a result, now I’m going to kill your oldest son.’”
EXO 4:24 24 During their journey, as they camped overnight, the LORD met Moses and tried to kill him.
EXO 4:25 25 But Zipporah took a sharp-edged flint stone and cut off her son’s foreskin. Then she touched Moses’ genitals with it, and she said, “You are my bridegroom because of bloodshed.”
EXO 4:26 26 So the LORD let him alone. At that time, she announced, “A bridegroom because of bloodshed by circumcision.”
EXO 4:27 27 The LORD said to Aaron, “Go into the desert to meet Moses.” So he went, and Aaron met him at God’s mountain and greeted him with a kiss.
EXO 4:28 28 Moses told Aaron what the LORD had said about his mission and all the signs that the LORD had told him to do.
EXO 4:29 29 Then Moses and Aaron called together all the Israelite elders.
EXO 4:30 30 Aaron told them everything that the LORD had told to Moses, and he performed the signs in front of the people.
EXO 4:31 31 The people believed. When they heard that the LORD had paid attention to the Israelites and had seen their oppression, they bowed down and worshipped.
EXO 5:1 1 Afterward, Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, “This is what the LORD , Israel’s God, says: ‘Let my people go so that they can hold a festival for me in the desert.’”
EXO 5:2 2 But Pharaoh said, “Who is this LORD whom I’m supposed to obey by letting Israel go? I don’t know this LORD , and I certainly won’t let Israel go.”
EXO 5:3 3 Then they said, “The Hebrews’ God has appeared to us. Let us go on a three-day journey into the desert so we can offer sacrifices to the LORD our God. Otherwise, the LORD will give us a deadly disease or violence.”
EXO 5:4 4 The king of Egypt said to them, “Moses and Aaron, why are you making the people slack off from their work? Do the hard work yourselves!”
EXO 5:5 5 Pharaoh continued, “The land’s people are now numerous. Yet you want them to stop their hard work?”
EXO 5:6 6 On the very same day Pharaoh commanded the people’s slave masters and supervisors,
EXO 5:7 7 “Don’t supply the people with the straw they need to make bricks like you did before. Let them go out and gather the straw for themselves.
EXO 5:8 8 But still make sure that they produce the same number of bricks as they made before. Don’t reduce the number! They are weak and lazy, and that’s why they cry, ‘Let’s go and offer sacrifices to our God.’
EXO 5:9 9 Make the men’s work so hard that it’s all they can do, and they can’t focus on these empty lies.”
EXO 5:10 10 So the people’s slave masters and supervisors came out and spoke to the people, “This is what Pharaoh says, ‘I’m not giving you straw anymore.
EXO 5:11 11 Go and get the straw on your own, wherever you can find it. But your work won’t be reduced at all.’”
EXO 5:12 12 So the people spread out all through the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
EXO 5:13 13 The slave masters drove them hard and said, “Make sure you make the same daily quota as when you had the straw.”
EXO 5:14 14 The Israelite supervisors, whom Pharaoh’s slave masters had set over them, were also beaten and asked, “Why didn’t you produce the same number of bricks yesterday and today as you did before?”
EXO 5:15 15 Then the Israelite supervisors came and pleaded to Pharaoh, “Why do you treat your servants like this?
EXO 5:16 16 No straw is supplied to your servants, yet they say to us, ‘Make bricks!’ Look at how your servants are being beaten! Your own people are to blame!”
EXO 5:17 17 Pharaoh replied, “You are lazy bums, nothing but lazy bums. That’s why you say, ‘Let us go and offer sacrifices to the LORD .’
EXO 5:18 18 Go and get back to work! No straw will be given to you, but you still need to make the same number of bricks.”
EXO 5:19 19 The Israelite supervisors saw how impossible their situation was when they were commanded, “Don’t reduce your daily quota of bricks.”
EXO 5:20 20 When they left Pharaoh, they met Moses and Aaron, who were waiting for them.
EXO 5:21 21 The supervisors said to them, “Let the LORD see and judge what you’ve done! You’ve made us stink in the opinion of Pharaoh and his servants. You’ve given them a reason to kill us.”
EXO 5:22 22 Then Moses turned to the LORD and said, “My Lord, why have you abused this people? Why did you send me for this?
EXO 5:23 23 Ever since I first came to Pharaoh to speak in your name, he has abused this people. And you’ve done absolutely nothing to rescue your people.”
EXO 6:1 1 The LORD replied to Moses, “Now you will see what I’ll do to Pharaoh. In fact, he’ll be so eager to let them go that he’ll drive them out of his land by force.”
EXO 6:2 2 God also said to Moses: “I am the LORD .
EXO 6:3 3 I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as God Almighty, but I didn’t reveal myself to them by my name ‘The LORD .’
EXO 6:4 4 I also set up my covenant with them to give them the land of Canaan where they lived as immigrants.
EXO 6:5 5 I’ve also heard the cry of grief of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians have turned into slaves, and I’ve remembered my covenant.
EXO 6:6 6 Therefore, say to the Israelites, ‘I am the LORD . I’ll bring you out from Egyptian forced labor. I’ll rescue you from your slavery to them. I’ll set you free with great power and with momentous events of justice.
EXO 6:7 7 I’ll take you as my people, and I’ll be your God. You will know that I, the LORD , am your God, who has freed you from Egyptian forced labor.
EXO 6:8 8 I’ll bring you into the land that I promised to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I’ll give it to you as your possession. I am the LORD .’”
EXO 6:9 9 Moses told this to the Israelites. But they didn’t listen to Moses, because of their complete exhaustion and their hard labor.
EXO 6:10 10 Then the LORD said to Moses,
EXO 6:11 11 “Go and tell Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, to let the Israelites out of his land.”
EXO 6:12 12 But Moses said to the LORD , “The Israelites haven’t even listened to me. How can I expect Pharaoh to listen to me, especially since I’m not a very good speaker?”
EXO 6:13 13 Nevertheless, the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron about the Israelites and Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, giving them orders to let the Israelites go from the land of Egypt.
EXO 6:14 14 These were the leaders of their households. The descendants of Reuben, Israel’s oldest son: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. These were Reuben’s clans.
EXO 6:15 15 The Simeonites: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, a Canaanite woman’s son. These were Simeon’s clans.
EXO 6:16 16 These were the Levites’ names by their generations: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.
EXO 6:17 17 The Gershonites: Libni and Shimei and their clans.
EXO 6:18 18 The Kohathites: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.
EXO 6:19 19 The Merarites: Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite clans by their generations.
EXO 6:20 20 Amram married Jochebed, his father’s sister. She gave birth to Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years.
EXO 6:21 21 The Izharites: Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
EXO 6:22 22 The Uzzielites: Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
EXO 6:23 23 Aaron married Elisheba, Amminadab’s daughter and Nahshon’s sister. She gave birth to Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
EXO 6:24 24 The Korahites: Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. These were the Korahite clans.
EXO 6:25 25 Aaron’s son Eleazar married one of Putiel’s daughters. She gave birth to Phinehas. These were the leaders of Levite households by their clans.
EXO 6:26 26 It was this same Aaron and Moses whom the LORD commanded, “Bring the Israelites out of the land of Egypt in military formation.”
EXO 6:27 27 It was also this same Moses and Aaron who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt to bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
EXO 6:28 28 At the time the LORD spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
EXO 6:29 29 the LORD said to him, “I am the LORD . Tell Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, everything that I’ve said to you.”
EXO 6:30 30 But Moses replied to the LORD , “Look, I’m not a very good speaker. How is Pharaoh ever going to listen to me?”
EXO 7:1 1 The LORD said to Moses, “See, I’ve made you like God to Pharaoh, and your brother Aaron will be your prophet.
EXO 7:2 2 You will say everything that I command you, and your brother Aaron will tell Pharaoh to let the Israelites out of his land.
EXO 7:3 3 But I’ll make Pharaoh stubborn, and I’ll perform many of my signs and amazing acts in the land of Egypt.
EXO 7:4 4 When Pharaoh refuses to listen to you, then I’ll act against Egypt and I’ll bring my people the Israelites out of the land of Egypt in military formation by momentous events of justice.
EXO 7:5 5 The Egyptians will come to know that I am the LORD , when I act against Egypt and bring the Israelites out from among them.”
EXO 7:6 6 Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD commanded them.
EXO 7:7 7 Moses was 80 years old and Aaron was 83 when they spoke to Pharaoh.
EXO 7:8 8 The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
EXO 7:9 9 “When Pharaoh says to you, ‘Do one of your amazing acts,’ then say to Aaron, ‘Take your shepherd’s rod and throw it down in front of Pharaoh, and it will turn into a cobra.’”
EXO 7:10 10 So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the LORD commanded. Aaron threw down his shepherd’s rod in front of Pharaoh and his officials, and it turned into a cobra.
EXO 7:11 11 Then Pharaoh called together his wise men and wizards, and Egypt’s religious experts did the same thing by using their secret knowledge.
EXO 7:12 12 Each one threw down his rod, and they turned into cobras. But then Aaron’s rod swallowed up each of their rods.
EXO 7:13 13 However, Pharaoh remained stubborn. He wouldn’t listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
EXO 7:14 14 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh is stubborn. He still refuses to let the people go.
EXO 7:15 15 Go to Pharaoh in the morning. As he is going out to the water, make sure you stand at the bank of the Nile River so you will run into him. Bring along the shepherd’s rod that turned into a snake.
EXO 7:16 16 Say to him, The LORD , the Hebrews’ God, has sent me to you with this message: Let my people go so that they can worship me in the desert. Up to now you still haven’t listened.
EXO 7:17 17 This is what the LORD says: By this you will know that I am the LORD . I’m now going to hit the water of the Nile River with this rod in my hand, and it will turn into blood.
EXO 7:18 18 The fish in the Nile are going to die, the Nile will stink, and the Egyptians won’t be able to drink water from the Nile.”
EXO 7:19 19 The LORD said to Moses, “Say to Aaron, ‘Take your shepherd’s rod and stretch out your hand over Egypt’s waters—over their rivers, their canals, their marshes, and all their bodies of water—so that they turn into blood. There will be blood all over the land of Egypt, even in wooden and stone containers.’”
EXO 7:20 20 Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD commanded. He raised the shepherd’s rod and hit the water in the Nile in front of Pharaoh and his officials, and all the water in the Nile turned into blood.
EXO 7:21 21 The fish in the Nile died, and the Nile began to stink so that the Egyptians couldn’t drink water from the Nile. There was blood all over the land of Egypt.
EXO 7:22 22 But the Egyptian religious experts did the same thing with their secret knowledge. As a result, Pharaoh remained stubborn, and he wouldn’t listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
EXO 7:23 23 Pharaoh turned and went back to his palace. He wasn’t impressed even by this.
EXO 7:24 24 Meanwhile, all the Egyptians had to dig for drinking water along the banks of the Nile River, because they couldn’t drink the water of the Nile itself.
EXO 7:25 25 Seven days went by after the LORD had struck the Nile River.
EXO 8:1 1 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and tell him: This is what the LORD says: Let my people go so that they can worship me.
EXO 8:2 2 If you refuse to let them go, then I’ll send a plague of frogs over your whole country.
EXO 8:3 3 The Nile will overflow with frogs. They’ll get into your palace, into your bedroom and onto your bed, into your officials’ houses, and among all your people, and even into your ovens and bread pans.
EXO 8:4 4 The frogs will crawl up on you, your people, and all your officials.”
EXO 8:5 5 And the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your hand with your shepherd’s rod over the rivers, the canals, and the marshes, and make the frogs crawl up all over the land of Egypt.’”
EXO 8:6 6 So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt. The frogs crawled up and covered the land of Egypt.
EXO 8:7 7 However, the Egyptian religious experts were able to do the same thing by their secret knowledge. They too made frogs crawl up onto the land of Egypt.
EXO 8:8 8 Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said, “If you pray to the LORD to get rid of the frogs from me and my people, then I’ll let the people go so that they can offer sacrifices to the LORD .”
EXO 8:9 9 Moses said to Pharaoh, “Have it your way. When should I pray for you and your officials and your people to remove the frogs from your houses, courtyards, and fields? They’ll stay only in the Nile.”
EXO 8:10 10 Pharaoh said, “Tomorrow!” Moses said, “Just as you say! That way you will know that there is no one like the LORD our God.
EXO 8:11 11 The frogs will leave you, your houses, your officials, and your people. They’ll stay only in the Nile.”
EXO 8:12 12 After Moses and Aaron had left Pharaoh, Moses cried out to the LORD about the frogs that the LORD had brought on Pharaoh.
EXO 8:13 13 The LORD did as Moses asked. The frogs died inside the houses, out in the yards, and in the fields.
EXO 8:14 14 They gathered them together in big piles, and the land began to stink.
EXO 8:15 15 But when Pharaoh saw that the disaster was over, he became stubborn again and wouldn’t listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
EXO 8:16 16 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron, ‘Stretch out your shepherd’s rod and hit the land’s dirt so that lice appear in the whole land of Egypt.’”
EXO 8:17 17 They did this. Aaron stretched out his hand with his shepherd’s rod, hit the land’s dirt, and lice appeared on both people and animals. All the land’s dirt turned into lice throughout the whole land of Egypt.
EXO 8:18 18 The religious experts tried to produce lice by their secret knowledge, but they weren’t able to do it. There were lice on people and animals.
EXO 8:19 19 The religious experts said to Pharaoh, “This is something only God could do!” But Pharaoh was stubborn, and he wouldn’t listen to them, just as the LORD had said.
EXO 8:20 20 The LORD said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning and confront Pharaoh as he goes out to the water. Say to him, This is what the LORD says: Let my people go so that they can worship me.
EXO 8:21 21 If you refuse to let my people go, I’ll send swarms of insects on you, your officials, your people, and your houses. All Egyptian houses will be filled with swarms of insects and also the ground that they cover.
EXO 8:22 22 But on that day I’ll set apart the land of Goshen, where my people live. No swarms of insects will come there so you will know that I, the LORD , am in this land.
EXO 8:23 23 I’ll put a barrier between my people and your people. This sign will happen tomorrow.”
EXO 8:24 24 The LORD did this. Great swarms of insects came into the houses of Pharaoh and his officials and into the whole land of Egypt. The land was ruined by the insects.
EXO 8:25 25 Then Pharaoh called in Moses and Aaron and said, “Go, offer sacrifices to your God within the land.”
EXO 8:26 26 Moses replied, “It wouldn’t be right to do that, because the sacrifices that we offer to the LORD our God will offend Egyptians. If we openly offer sacrifices that offend Egyptians, won’t they stone us to death?
EXO 8:27 27 We need to go for a three-day journey into the desert to offer sacrifices to the LORD our God as he has ordered us.”
EXO 8:28 28 So Pharaoh said, “I’ll let you go to offer sacrifices to the LORD your God in the desert, provided you don’t go too far away and you pray for me.”
EXO 8:29 29 Moses said, “I’ll leave you now, and I’ll pray to the LORD . Tomorrow the swarms of insects will leave Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. Just don’t let Pharaoh lie to us again and not let the people go to offer sacrifices to the LORD .”
EXO 8:30 30 So Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD .
EXO 8:31 31 The LORD did as Moses asked and removed the swarms of insects from Pharaoh, from his officials, and from his people. Not one insect remained.
EXO 8:32 32 But Pharaoh was stubborn once again, and he wouldn’t let the people go.
EXO 9:1 1 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh and say to him, This is what the LORD , the Hebrews’ God, says: Let my people go so that they can worship me.
EXO 9:2 2 If you refuse to let them go and you continue to hold them back,
EXO 9:3 3 the LORD will send a very deadly disease on your livestock in the field: on horses, donkeys, camels, cattle, and flocks.
EXO 9:4 4 But the LORD will distinguish Israel’s livestock from Egypt’s livestock so that not one that belongs to the Israelites will die.”
EXO 9:5 5 The LORD set a time and said, “Tomorrow the LORD will do this in the land.”
EXO 9:6 6 And the next day the LORD did it. All of the Egyptian livestock died, but not one animal that belonged to the Israelites died.
EXO 9:7 7 Pharaoh asked around and found out that not one of Israel’s livestock had died. But Pharaoh was stubborn, and he wouldn’t let the people go.
EXO 9:8 8 Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Take handfuls of ashes from a furnace and have Moses throw it up in the air in front of Pharaoh.
EXO 9:9 9 The ashes will turn to soot over the whole land of Egypt. It will cause skin sores that will break out in blisters on people and animals in the whole land of Egypt.”
EXO 9:10 10 So they took ashes from the furnace, and they stood in front of Pharaoh. Moses threw the ash up in the air, and it caused skin sores and blisters to break out on people and animals.
EXO 9:11 11 The religious experts couldn’t stand up to Moses because of the skin sores, because there were skin sores on the religious experts as well as on all the Egyptians.
EXO 9:12 12 But the LORD made Pharaoh stubborn, and Pharaoh wouldn’t listen to them, just as the LORD had said to Moses.
EXO 9:13 13 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Get up early in the morning and confront Pharaoh. Say to him, This is what the LORD , the God of the Hebrews, says: Let my people go so that they can worship me.
EXO 9:14 14 This time I’m going to send all my plagues on you, your officials, and your people so that you will know that there is no one like me in the whole world.
EXO 9:15 15 By now I could have used my power to strike you and your people with a deadly disease so that you would have disappeared from the earth.
EXO 9:16 16 But I’ve left you standing for this reason: in order to show you my power and in order to make my name known in the whole world.
EXO 9:17 17 You are still abusing your power against my people, and you refuse to let them go.
EXO 9:18 18 Tomorrow at this time I’ll cause the heaviest hail to fall on Egypt that has ever fallen from the day Egypt was founded until now.
EXO 9:19 19 So bring under shelter your livestock and all that belongs to you that is out in the open. Every person or animal that is out in the open field and isn’t brought inside will die when the hail rains down on them.”
EXO 9:20 20 Some of Pharaoh’s officials who took the LORD ’s word seriously rushed to bring their servants and livestock inside for shelter.
EXO 9:21 21 Others who didn’t take the LORD ’s word to heart left their servants and livestock out in the open field.
EXO 9:22 22 The LORD said to Moses, “Raise your hand toward the sky so that hail will fall on the whole land of Egypt, on people and animals and all the grain in the fields in the land of Egypt.”
EXO 9:23 23 Then Moses raised his shepherd’s rod toward the sky, and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and lightning struck the earth. The LORD rained hail on the land of Egypt.
EXO 9:24 24 The hail and the lightning flashing in the middle of the hail were so severe that there had been nothing like it in the entire land of Egypt since it first became a nation.
EXO 9:25 25 The hail beat down everything that was in the open field throughout the entire land of Egypt, both people and animals. The hail also beat down all the grain in the fields, and it shattered every tree out in the field.
EXO 9:26 26 The only place where hail didn’t fall was in the land of Goshen where the Israelites lived.
EXO 9:27 27 Then Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron and said to them, “This time I’ve sinned. The LORD is right, and I and my people are wrong.
EXO 9:28 28 Pray to the LORD ! Enough of God’s thunder and hail! I’m going to let you go. You don’t need to stay here any longer.”
EXO 9:29 29 Moses said to him, “As soon as I’ve left the city, I’ll spread out my hands to the LORD . Then the thunder and the hail will stop and won’t return so that you will know that the earth belongs to the LORD .
EXO 9:30 30 But I know that you and your officials still don’t take the LORD God seriously.” (
EXO 9:31 31 Now the flax and the barley were destroyed, because the barley had ears of grain and the flax had buds.
EXO 9:32 32 But both durum and spelt wheat weren’t ruined, because they hadn’t come up.)
EXO 9:33 33 Moses left Pharaoh and the city, and spread out his hands to the LORD . Then the thunder and the hail stopped, and the rain stopped pouring down on the earth.
EXO 9:34 34 But when Pharaoh saw that the rain, hail, and thunder had stopped, he sinned again. Pharaoh and his officials became stubborn.
EXO 9:35 35 Because of his stubbornness, Pharaoh refused to let the Israelites go, just as the LORD had told Moses.
EXO 10:1 1 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh. I’ve made him and his officials stubborn so that I can show them my signs
EXO 10:2 2 and so that you can tell your children and grandchildren how I overpowered the Egyptians with the signs I did among them. You will know that I am the LORD .”
EXO 10:3 3 So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, “This is what the LORD , the Hebrews’ God, says: How long will you refuse to respect me? Let my people go so that they can worship me.
EXO 10:4 4 Otherwise, if you refuse to let my people go, I’m going to bring locusts into your country tomorrow.
EXO 10:5 5 They will cover the landscape so that you won’t be able to see the ground. They will eat the last bit of vegetation that was left after the hail. They will eat all your trees growing in the fields.
EXO 10:6 6 The locusts will fill your houses and all your officials’ houses and all the Egyptians’ houses. Your parents and even your grandparents have never seen anything like it during their entire lifetimes in this fertile land.” Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh.
EXO 10:7 7 Pharaoh’s officials said to him, “How long will this man trap us in a corner like this? Let the people go so that they can worship the LORD their God. Don’t you get it? Egypt is being destroyed!”
EXO 10:8 8 So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, “Go! Worship the LORD your God! But who exactly is going with you?”
EXO 10:9 9 Moses said, “We’ll go with our young and old, with our sons and daughters, and with our flocks and herds, because we all must observe the LORD ’s festival.”
EXO 10:10 10 Pharaoh said to them, “Yes, the LORD will be with you, all right, especially if I let your children go with you! Obviously, you are plotting some evil scheme.
EXO 10:11 11 No way! Only your men can go and worship the LORD , because that’s what you asked for.” Then Pharaoh had them chased out of his presence.
EXO 10:12 12 Then the LORD said to Moses: “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt so that the locusts will swarm over the land of Egypt and eat all of the land’s grain and everything that the hail left.”
EXO 10:13 13 So Moses stretched out his shepherd’s rod over the land of Egypt, and the LORD made an east wind blow over the land all that day and all that night. When morning came, the east wind had carried in the locusts.
EXO 10:14 14 The locusts swarmed over the whole land of Egypt and settled on the whole country. Such a huge swarming of locusts had never happened before and would never happen ever again.
EXO 10:15 15 They covered the whole landscape so that the land turned black with them. They ate all of the land’s grain and all of the orchards’ fruit that the hail had left. Nothing green was left in any orchard or in any grain field in the whole land of Egypt.
EXO 10:16 16 Pharaoh called urgently for Moses and Aaron and said, “I’ve sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
EXO 10:17 17 Please forgive my sin this time. Pray to the LORD your God just to take this deathly disaster away from me.”
EXO 10:18 18 So Moses left Pharaoh and prayed to the LORD .
EXO 10:19 19 The LORD turned the wind into a very strong west wind that lifted the locusts and drove them into the Reed Sea. Not a single locust was left in the whole country of Egypt.
EXO 10:20 20 But the LORD made Pharaoh stubborn so that he wouldn’t let the Israelites go.
EXO 10:21 21 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Raise your hand toward the sky so that darkness spreads over the land of Egypt, a darkness that you can feel.”
EXO 10:22 22 So Moses raised his hand toward the sky, and an intense darkness fell on the whole land of Egypt for three days.
EXO 10:23 23 People couldn’t see each other, and they couldn’t go anywhere for three days. But the Israelites all had light where they lived.
EXO 10:24 24 Then Pharaoh called Moses and said, “Go! Worship the LORD ! Only your flocks and herds need to stay behind. Even your children can go with you.”
EXO 10:25 25 But Moses said, “You need to let us have sacrifices and entirely burned offerings to present to the LORD our God.
EXO 10:26 26 So our livestock must go with us. Not one animal can be left behind. We’ll need some of them for worshipping the LORD our God. We won’t know which to use to worship the LORD until we get there.”
EXO 10:27 27 But the LORD made Pharaoh stubborn so that he wasn’t willing to let them go.
EXO 10:28 28 Pharaoh said to him, “Get out of here! Make sure you never see my face again, because the next time you see my face you will die.”
EXO 10:29 29 Moses said, “You’ve said it! I’ll never see your face again!”
EXO 11:1 1 The LORD said to Moses, “I’ll bring one more disaster on Pharaoh and on Egypt. After that, he’ll let you go from here. In fact, when he lets you go, he’ll eagerly chase you out of here.
EXO 11:2 2 Tell every man to ask his neighbor and every woman to ask her neighbor for all their silver and gold jewelry.”
EXO 11:3 3 The LORD made sure that the Egyptians were kind to the Hebrew people. In addition, Pharaoh’s officials and the Egyptian people even came to honor Moses as a great and important man in the land.
EXO 11:4 4 Moses said, “This is what the LORD says: At midnight I’ll go throughout Egypt.
EXO 11:5 5 Every oldest child in the land of Egypt will die, from the oldest child of Pharaoh who sits on his throne to the oldest child of the servant woman by the millstones, and all the first offspring of the animals.
EXO 11:6 6 Then a terrible cry of agony will echo through the whole land of Egypt unlike any heard before or that ever will be again.
EXO 11:7 7 But as for the Israelites, not even a dog will growl at them, at the people, or at their animals. By this, you will know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.
EXO 11:8 8 Then all your officials will come down to me, bow to me, and say, ‘Get out, you and all your followers!’ After that I’ll leave.” Then Moses, furious, left Pharaoh.
EXO 11:9 9 The LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh won’t listen to you so that I can perform even more amazing acts in the land of Egypt.”
EXO 11:10 10 Now Moses and Aaron did all these amazing acts in front of Pharaoh, but the LORD made Pharaoh stubborn so that he didn’t let the Israelites go from his land.
EXO 12:1 1 The LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt,
EXO 12:2 2 “This month will be the first month; it will be the first month of the year for you.
EXO 12:3 3 Tell the whole Israelite community: On the tenth day of this month they must take a lamb for each household, a lamb per house.
EXO 12:4 4 If a household is too small for a lamb, it should share one with a neighbor nearby. You should divide the lamb in proportion to the number of people who will be eating it.
EXO 12:5 5 Your lamb should be a flawless year-old male. You may take it from the sheep or from the goats.
EXO 12:6 6 You should keep close watch over it until the fourteenth day of this month. At twilight on that day, the whole assembled Israelite community should slaughter their lambs.
EXO 12:7 7 They should take some of the blood and smear it on the two doorposts and on the beam over the door of the houses in which they are eating.
EXO 12:8 8 That same night they should eat the meat roasted over the fire. They should eat it along with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
EXO 12:9 9 Don’t eat any of it raw or boiled in water, but roasted over fire with its head, legs, and internal organs.
EXO 12:10 10 Don’t let any of it remain until morning, and burn any of it left over in the morning.
EXO 12:11 11 This is how you should eat it. You should be dressed, with your sandals on your feet and your walking stick in your hand. You should eat the meal in a hurry. It is the Passover of the LORD .
EXO 12:12 12 I’ll pass through the land of Egypt that night, and I’ll strike down every oldest child in the land of Egypt, both humans and animals. I’ll impose judgments on all the gods of Egypt. I am the LORD .
EXO 12:13 13 The blood will be your sign on the houses where you live. Whenever I see the blood, I’ll pass over you. No plague will destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
EXO 12:14 14 “This day will be a day of remembering for you. You will observe it as a festival to the LORD . You will observe it in every generation as a regulation for all time.
EXO 12:15 15 You will eat unleavened bread for seven days. On the first day you must remove yeast from your houses because anyone who eats leavened bread anytime during those seven days will be cut off from Israel.
EXO 12:16 16 The first day and the seventh day will be a holy occasion for you. No work at all should be done on those days, except for preparing the food that everyone is going to eat. That is the only work you may do.
EXO 12:17 17 You should observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because on this precise day I brought you out of the land of Egypt in military formation. You should observe this day in every generation as a regulation for all time.
EXO 12:18 18 In the first month, from the evening of the fourteenth day until the evening of the twenty-first day, you should eat unleavened bread.
EXO 12:19 19 For seven days no yeast should be found in your houses because whoever eats leavened bread will be cut off from the Israelite community, whether the person is an immigrant or a native of the land.
EXO 12:20 20 You should not eat anything made with yeast in all your settlements. You should eat only unleavened bread.”
EXO 12:21 21 Then Moses called together all of Israel’s elders and said to them, “Go pick out one of the flock for your families, and slaughter the Passover lamb.
EXO 12:22 22 Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it into the blood that is in the bowl, and touch the beam above the door and the two doorposts with the blood in the bowl. None of you should go out the door of your house until morning.
EXO 12:23 23 When the LORD comes by to strike down the Egyptians and sees the blood on the beam above the door and on the two doorposts, the LORD will pass over that door. He won’t let the destroyer enter your houses to strike you down.
EXO 12:24 24 You should observe this ritual as a regulation for all time for you and your children.
EXO 12:25 25 When you enter the land that the LORD has promised to give you, be sure that you observe this ritual.
EXO 12:26 26 And when your children ask you, ‘What does this ritual mean to you?’
EXO 12:27 27 you will say, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD , for the LORD passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt. When he struck down the Egyptians, he spared our houses.’” The people then bowed down and worshipped.
EXO 12:28 28 The Israelites went and did exactly what the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron to do.
EXO 12:29 29 At midnight the LORD struck down all the first offspring in the land of Egypt, from the oldest child of Pharaoh sitting on his throne to the oldest child of the prisoner in jail, and all the first offspring of the animals.
EXO 12:30 30 When Pharaoh, all his officials, and all the Egyptians got up that night, a terrible cry of agony rang out across Egypt because every house had someone in it who had died.
EXO 12:31 31 Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron that night and said, “Get up! Get away from my people, both you and the Israelites! Go! Worship the LORD , as you said!
EXO 12:32 32 You can even take your flocks and herds, as you asked. Just go! And bring a blessing on me as well!”
EXO 12:33 33 The Egyptians urged the people to hurry and leave the land because they thought, We’ll all be dead.
EXO 12:34 34 So the people picked up their bread dough before the yeast made it rise, with their bread pans wrapped in their robes on their shoulders.
EXO 12:35 35 The Israelites did as Moses had told them and asked the Egyptians for their silver and gold jewelry as well as their clothing.
EXO 12:36 36 The LORD made sure that the Egyptians were kind to the people so that they let them have whatever they asked for. And so they robbed the Egyptians.
EXO 12:37 37 The Israelites traveled from Rameses to Succoth. They numbered about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides children.
EXO 12:38 38 A diverse crowd also went up with them along with a huge number of livestock, both flocks and herds.
EXO 12:39 39 They baked unleavened cakes from the dough they had brought out of Egypt. The dough didn’t rise because they were driven out of Egypt and they couldn’t wait. In fact, they didn’t have time to prepare any food for themselves.
EXO 12:40 40 The length of time that the Israelites had lived in Egypt was four hundred thirty years.
EXO 12:41 41 At the end of four hundred thirty years, on that precise day, all the LORD ’s people in military formation left the land of Egypt.
EXO 12:42 42 For the LORD , that was a night of intent watching, to bring them out of the land of Egypt. For all Israelites in every generation, this same night is a time of intent watching to honor the LORD .
EXO 12:43 43 The LORD said to Moses and Aaron: This is the regulation for the Passover. No foreigner may eat it.
EXO 12:44 44 However, any slave who has been bought may eat it after he’s been circumcised.
EXO 12:45 45 No temporary foreign resident or day laborer may eat it.
EXO 12:46 46 It should be eaten in one house. You shouldn’t take any of the meat outside the house, and you shouldn’t break the bones.
EXO 12:47 47 The whole Israelite community should observe it.
EXO 12:48 48 If an immigrant who lives with you wants to observe the Passover to the LORD , then he and all his males should be circumcised. Then he may join in observing it. He should be regarded as a native of the land. But no uncircumcised person may eat it.
EXO 12:49 49 There will be one Instruction for the native and for the immigrant who lives with you.
EXO 12:50 50 All the Israelites did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.
EXO 12:51 51 On that precise day, the LORD brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt in military formation.
EXO 13:1 1 The LORD said to Moses:
EXO 13:2 2 Dedicate to me all your oldest children. Each first offspring from any Israelite womb belongs to me, whether human or animal.
EXO 13:3 3 Moses said to the people, “Remember this day which is the day that you came out of Egypt, out of the place you were slaves, because the LORD acted with power to bring you out of there. No leavened bread may be eaten.
EXO 13:4 4 Today, in the month of Abib, you are going to leave.
EXO 13:5 5 The LORD will bring you to the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. It is the land that the LORD promised your ancestors to give to you, a land full of milk and honey. You should perform this ritual in this month.
EXO 13:6 6 You must eat unleavened bread for seven days. The seventh day is a festival to the LORD .
EXO 13:7 7 Only unleavened bread should be eaten for seven days. No leavened bread and no yeast should be seen among you in your whole country.
EXO 13:8 8 You should explain to your child on that day, ‘It’s because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’
EXO 13:9 9 “It will be a sign on your hand and a reminder on your forehead so that you will often discuss the LORD ’s Instruction, for the LORD brought you out of Egypt with great power.
EXO 13:10 10 So you should follow this regulation at its appointed time every year.
EXO 13:11 11 “When the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and gives it to you as promised to you and your ancestors,
EXO 13:12 12 you should set aside for the LORD whatever comes out of the womb first. All of the first males born to your animal belong to the LORD .
EXO 13:13 13 But every first male donkey you should ransom with a sheep. If you don’t ransom it, you must break its neck. You should ransom every oldest male among your children.
EXO 13:14 14 When in the future your child asks you, ‘What does this mean?’ you should answer, ‘The LORD brought us with great power out of Egypt, out of the place we were slaves.
EXO 13:15 15 When Pharaoh refused to let us go, the LORD killed all the oldest offspring in the land of Egypt, from the oldest sons to the oldest male animals. That is why I offer to the LORD as a sacrifice every male that first comes out of the womb. But I ransom my oldest sons.’
EXO 13:16 16 It will be a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead that the LORD brought us out of Egypt with great power.”
EXO 13:17 17 When Pharaoh let the people go, God didn’t lead them by way of the land of the Philistines, even though that was the shorter route. God thought, If the people have to fight and face war, they will run back to Egypt.
EXO 13:18 18 So God led the people by the roundabout way of the Reed Sea desert. The Israelites went up out of the land of Egypt ready for battle.
EXO 13:19 19 Moses took with him Joseph’s bones just as Joseph had made Israel’s sons promise when he said to them, “When God takes care of you, you must carry my bones out of here with you.”
EXO 13:20 20 They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham on the edge of the desert.
EXO 13:21 21 The LORD went in front of them during the day in a column of cloud to guide them and at night in a column of lightning to give them light. This way they could travel during the day and at night.
EXO 13:22 22 The column of cloud during the day and the column of lightning at night never left its place in front of the people.
EXO 14:1 1 Then the LORD said to Moses:
EXO 14:2 2 Tell the Israelites to turn back and set up camp in front of Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea in front of Baal-zephon. You should set up camp in front of it by the sea.
EXO 14:3 3 Pharaoh will think to himself, The Israelites are lost and confused in the land. The desert has trapped them.
EXO 14:4 4 I’ll make Pharaoh stubborn, and he’ll chase them. I’ll gain honor at the expense of Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD . And they did exactly that.
EXO 14:5 5 When Egypt’s king was told that the people had run away, Pharaoh and his officials changed their minds about the people. They said, “What have we done, letting Israel go free from their slavery to us?”
EXO 14:6 6 So he sent for his chariot and took his army with him.
EXO 14:7 7 He took six hundred elite chariots and all of Egypt’s other chariots with captains on all of them.
EXO 14:8 8 The LORD made Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, stubborn, and he chased the Israelites, who were leaving confidently.
EXO 14:9 9 The Egyptians, including all of Pharaoh’s horse-drawn chariots, his cavalry, and his army, chased them and caught up with them as they were camped by the sea, by Pi-hahiroth in front of Baal-zephon.
EXO 14:10 10 As Pharaoh drew closer, the Israelites looked back and saw the Egyptians marching toward them. The Israelites were terrified and cried out to the LORD .
EXO 14:11 11 They said to Moses, “Weren’t there enough graves in Egypt that you took us away to die in the desert? What have you done to us by bringing us out of Egypt like this?
EXO 14:12 12 Didn’t we tell you the same thing in Egypt? ‘Leave us alone! Let us work for the Egyptians!’ It would have been better for us to work for the Egyptians than to die in the desert.”
EXO 14:13 13 But Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid. Stand your ground, and watch the LORD rescue you today. The Egyptians you see today you will never ever see again.
EXO 14:14 14 The LORD will fight for you. You just keep still.”
EXO 14:15 15 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Why do you cry out to me? Tell the Israelites to get moving.
EXO 14:16 16 As for you, lift your shepherd’s rod, stretch out your hand over the sea, and split it in two so that the Israelites can go into the sea on dry ground.
EXO 14:17 17 But me, I’ll make the Egyptians stubborn so that they will go in after them, and I’ll gain honor at the expense of Pharaoh, all his army, his chariots, and his cavalry.
EXO 14:18 18 The Egyptians will know that I am the LORD , when I gain honor at the expense of Pharaoh, his chariots, and his cavalry.”
EXO 14:19 19 God’s messenger, who had been in front of Israel’s camp, moved and went behind them. The column of cloud moved from the front and took its place behind them.
EXO 14:20 20 It stood between Egypt’s camp and Israel’s camp. The cloud remained there, and when darkness fell it lit up the night. They didn’t come near each other all night.
EXO 14:21 21 Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. The LORD pushed the sea back by a strong east wind all night, turning the sea into dry land. The waters were split into two.
EXO 14:22 22 The Israelites walked into the sea on dry ground. The waters formed a wall for them on their right hand and on their left.
EXO 14:23 23 The Egyptians chased them and went into the sea after them, all of Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and cavalry.
EXO 14:24 24 As morning approached, the LORD looked down on the Egyptian camp from the column of lightning and cloud and threw the Egyptian camp into a panic.
