EXO 14:25 25 The LORD jammed their chariot wheels so that they wouldn’t turn easily. The Egyptians said, “Let’s get away from the Israelites, because the LORD is fighting for them against Egypt!”
EXO 14:26 26 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea so that the water comes back and covers the Egyptians, their chariots, and their cavalry.”
EXO 14:27 27 So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea. At daybreak, the sea returned to its normal depth. The Egyptians were driving toward it, and the LORD tossed the Egyptians into the sea.
EXO 14:28 28 The waters returned and covered the chariots and the cavalry, Pharaoh’s entire army that had followed them into the sea. Not one of them remained.
EXO 14:29 29 The Israelites, however, walked on dry ground through the sea. The waters formed a wall for them on their right hand and on their left.
EXO 14:30 30 The LORD rescued Israel from the Egyptians that day. Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.
EXO 14:31 31 Israel saw the amazing power of the LORD against the Egyptians. The people were in awe of the LORD , and they believed in the LORD and in his servant Moses.
EXO 15:1 1 Then Moses and the Israelites sang this song to the LORD : I will sing to the LORD , for an overflowing victory! Horse and rider he threw into the sea!
EXO 15:2 2 The LORD is my strength and my power; he has become my salvation. This is my God, whom I will praise, the God of my ancestors, whom I will acclaim.
EXO 15:3 3 The LORD is a warrior; the LORD is his name.
EXO 15:4 4 Pharaoh’s chariots and his army he hurled into the sea; his elite captains were sunk in the Reed Sea.
EXO 15:5 5 The deep sea covered them; they sank into the deep waters like a stone.
EXO 15:6 6 Your strong hand, LORD , is dominant in power; your strong hand, LORD , shatters the enemy!
EXO 15:7 7 With your great surge you overthrow your opponents; you send out your hot anger; it burns them up like straw.
EXO 15:8 8 With the breath of your nostrils the waters swelled up, the floods surged up in a great wave; the deep waters foamed in the depths of the sea.
EXO 15:9 9 The enemy said, “I’ll pursue, I’ll overtake, I’ll divide the spoils of war. I’ll be overfilled with them. I’ll draw my sword; my hand will destroy them.”
EXO 15:10 10 You blew with your wind; the sea covered over them. They sank like lead in the towering waters.
EXO 15:11 11 Who is like you among the gods, LORD ? Who is like you, foremost in holiness, worthy of highest praise, doing awesome deeds?
EXO 15:12 12 You raised your strong hand; earth swallowed them up.
EXO 15:13 13 With your great loyalty you led the people you rescued; with your power you guided them to your sanctuary.
EXO 15:14 14 The peoples heard, they shook in terror; horror grabbed hold of Philistia’s inhabitants.
EXO 15:15 15 Then Edom’s tribal chiefs were terrified; panic grabbed hold of Moab’s rulers; all of Canaan’s inhabitants melted in fear.
EXO 15:16 16 Terror and fear came over them; because of your great power, they were as still as a stone until your people, LORD , passed by, until the people you made your own passed by.
EXO 15:17 17 You brought them in and planted them on your own mountain, the place, LORD , that you made your home, the sanctuary, LORD , that your hand created.
EXO 15:18 18 The LORD will rule forever and always.
EXO 15:19 19 When Pharaoh’s horses, chariots, and cavalry went into the sea, the LORD brought back the waters of the sea over them. But the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.
EXO 15:20 20 Then the prophet Miriam, Aaron’s sister, took a tambourine in her hand. All the women followed her playing tambourines and dancing.
EXO 15:21 21 Miriam sang the refrain back to them: Sing to the LORD , for an overflowing victory! Horse and rider he threw into the sea!
EXO 15:22 22 Then Moses had Israel leave the Reed Sea and go out into the Shur desert. They traveled for three days in the desert and found no water.
EXO 15:23 23 When they came to Marah, they couldn’t drink Marah’s water because it was bitter. That’s why it was called Marah.
EXO 15:24 24 The people complained against Moses, “What will we drink?”
EXO 15:25 25 Moses cried out to the LORD , and the LORD pointed out a tree to him. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. The LORD made a regulation and a ruling there, and there he tested them.
EXO 15:26 26 The LORD said, “If you are careful to obey the LORD your God, do what God thinks is right, pay attention to his commandments, and keep all of his regulations, then I won’t bring on you any of the diseases that I brought on the Egyptians. I am the LORD who heals you.”
EXO 15:27 27 Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees. They camped there by the water.
EXO 16:1 1 The whole Israelite community set out from Elim and came to the Sin desert, which is located between Elim and Sinai. They set out on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt.
EXO 16:2 2 The whole Israelite community complained against Moses and Aaron in the desert.
EXO 16:3 3 The Israelites said to them, “Oh, how we wish that the LORD had just put us to death while we were still in the land of Egypt. There we could sit by the pots cooking meat and eat our fill of bread. Instead, you’ve brought us out into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death.”
EXO 16:4 4 Then the LORD said to Moses, “I’m going to make bread rain down from the sky for you. The people will go out each day and gather just enough for that day. In this way, I’ll test them to see whether or not they follow my Instruction.
EXO 16:5 5 On the sixth day, when they measure out what they have collected, it will be twice as much as they collected on other days.”
EXO 16:6 6 So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, “This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
EXO 16:7 7 And in the morning you will see the LORD ’s glorious presence, because your complaints against the LORD have been heard. Who are we? Why blame us?”
EXO 16:8 8 Moses continued, “The LORD will give you meat to eat in the evening and your fill of bread in the morning because the LORD heard the complaints you made against him. Who are we? Your complaints aren’t against us but against the LORD .”
EXO 16:9 9 Then Moses said to Aaron, “Say to the whole Israelite community, ‘Come near to the LORD , because he’s heard your complaints.’”
EXO 16:10 10 As Aaron spoke to the whole Israelite community, they turned to look toward the desert, and just then the glorious presence of the LORD appeared in the cloud.
EXO 16:11 11 The LORD spoke to Moses,
EXO 16:12 12 “I’ve heard the complaints of the Israelites. Tell them, ‘At twilight you will eat meat. And in the morning you will have your fill of bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.’”
EXO 16:13 13 In the evening a flock of quail flew down and covered the camp. And in the morning there was a layer of dew all around the camp.
EXO 16:14 14 When the layer of dew lifted, there on the desert surface were thin flakes, as thin as frost on the ground.
EXO 16:15 15 When the Israelites saw it, they said to each other, “What is it?” They didn’t know what it was. Moses said to them, “This is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.
EXO 16:16 16 This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Collect as much of it as each of you can eat, one omer per person. You may collect for the number of people in your household.’”
EXO 16:17 17 The Israelites did as Moses said, some collecting more, some less.
EXO 16:18 18 But when they measured it out by the omer, the ones who had collected more had nothing left over, and the ones who had collected less had no shortage. Everyone collected just as much as they could eat.
EXO 16:19 19 Moses said to them, “Don’t keep any of it until morning.”
EXO 16:20 20 But they didn’t listen to Moses. Some kept part of it until morning, but it became infested with worms and stank. Moses got angry with them.
EXO 16:21 21 Every morning they gathered it, as much as each person could eat. But when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
EXO 16:22 22 On the sixth day the people collected twice as much food as usual, two omers per person. All the chiefs of the community came and told Moses.
EXO 16:23 23 He said to them, “This is what the LORD has said, ‘Tomorrow is a day of rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD . Bake what you want to bake and boil what you want to boil. But you can set aside and keep all the leftovers until the next morning.’”
EXO 16:24 24 So they set the leftovers aside until morning, as Moses had commanded. They didn’t stink or become infested with worms.
EXO 16:25 25 The next day Moses said, “Eat it today, because today is a Sabbath to the LORD . Today you won’t find it out in the field.
EXO 16:26 26 Six days you will gather it. But on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will be nothing to gather.”
EXO 16:27 27 On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather bread, but they found nothing.
EXO 16:28 28 The LORD said to Moses, “How long will you refuse to obey my commandments and instructions?
EXO 16:29 29 Look! The LORD has given you the Sabbath. Therefore, on the sixth day he gives you enough food for two days. Each of you should stay where you are and not leave your place on the seventh day.”
EXO 16:30 30 So the people rested on the seventh day.
EXO 16:31 31 The Israelite people called it manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and tasted like honey wafers.
EXO 16:32 32 Moses said, “This is what the LORD has commanded: ‘Let an omer of it be kept safe for future generations so that they can see the food that I used to feed you in the desert when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’”
EXO 16:33 33 Moses said to Aaron, “Take a jar, and put one full omer of manna in it. Then set it in the LORD ’s presence, where it should be kept safe for future generations.”
EXO 16:34 34 Aaron did as the LORD commanded Moses, and he put it in front of the covenant document for safekeeping.
EXO 16:35 35 The Israelites ate manna for forty years, until they came to a livable land. They ate manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan. (
EXO 16:36 36 An omer is one-tenth of an ephah.)
EXO 17:1 1 The whole Israelite community broke camp and set out from the Sin desert to continue their journey, as the LORD commanded. They set up their camp at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
EXO 17:2 2 The people argued with Moses and said, “Give us water to drink.” Moses said to them, “Why are you arguing with me? Why are you testing the LORD ?”
EXO 17:3 3 But the people were very thirsty for water there, and they complained to Moses, “Why did you bring us out of Egypt to kill us, our children, and our livestock with thirst?”
EXO 17:4 4 So Moses cried out to the LORD , “What should I do with this people? They are getting ready to stone me.”
EXO 17:5 5 The LORD said to Moses, “Go on ahead of the people, and take some of Israel’s elders with you. Take in your hand the shepherd’s rod that you used to strike the Nile River, and go.
EXO 17:6 6 I’ll be standing there in front of you on the rock at Horeb. Hit the rock. Water will come out of it, and the people will be able to drink.” Moses did so while Israel’s elders watched.
EXO 17:7 7 He called the place Massah and Meribah, because the Israelites argued with and tested the LORD , asking, “Is the LORD really with us or not?”
EXO 17:8 8 Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.
EXO 17:9 9 Moses said to Joshua, “Choose some men for us and go fight with Amalek. Tomorrow I’ll stand on top of the hill with the shepherd’s rod of God in my hand.”
EXO 17:10 10 So Joshua did as Moses told him. He fought with Amalek while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
EXO 17:11 11 Whenever Moses held up his hand, Israel would start winning the battle. Whenever Moses lowered his hand, Amalek would start winning.
EXO 17:12 12 But Moses’ hands grew tired. So they took a stone and put it under Moses so he could sit down on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on each side of him so that his hands remained steady until sunset.
EXO 17:13 13 So Joshua defeated Amalek and his army with the sword.
EXO 17:14 14 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this as a reminder on a scroll and read it to Joshua: I will completely wipe out the memory of Amalek under the sky.”
EXO 17:15 15 Moses built an altar there and called it, “The LORD is my banner.”
EXO 17:16 16 He said, “The power of the LORD ’s banner! The LORD is at war with Amalek in every generation.”
EXO 18:1 1 Jethro, Midian’s priest and Moses’ father-in-law, heard about everything that God had done for Moses and for God’s people Israel, how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
EXO 18:2 2 Moses’ father-in-law Jethro took with him Zipporah, Moses’ wife whom he had sent away,
EXO 18:3 3 along with her two sons. One was named Gershom because he said, “I have been an immigrant living in a foreign land.”
EXO 18:4 4 The other was named Eliezer because he said, “The God of my ancestors was my helper who rescued me from Pharaoh’s sword.”
EXO 18:5 5 Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, brought Moses’ sons and wife back to him in the desert where he had set up camp at God’s mountain.
EXO 18:6 6 He sent word to Moses: “I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you along with your wife and her two sons.”
EXO 18:7 7 Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, and he bowed down and kissed him. They asked each other how they were doing, and then they went into the tent.
EXO 18:8 8 Moses then told his father-in-law everything that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians on Israel’s behalf, all the difficulty they had on their journey, and how the LORD had rescued them.
EXO 18:9 9 Jethro was glad about all the good things that the LORD had done for Israel in saving them from the Egyptians’ power.
EXO 18:10 10 Jethro said, “Bless the LORD who rescued you from the Egyptians’ power and from Pharaoh’s power, who rescued the people from Egypt’s oppressive power.
EXO 18:11 11 Now I know that the LORD is greater than all the gods, because of what happened when the Egyptians plotted against them.”
EXO 18:12 12 Then Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, brought an entirely burned offering and sacrifices to God. Aaron came with all of Israel’s elders to eat a meal with Moses’ father-in-law in God’s presence.
EXO 18:13 13 The next day Moses sat as a judge for the people, while the people stood around Moses from morning until evening.
EXO 18:14 14 When Moses’ father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, “What’s this that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people are standing around you from morning until evening?”
EXO 18:15 15 Moses said to his father-in-law, “Because the people come to me to inquire of God.
EXO 18:16 16 When a conflict arises between them, they come to me and I judge between the two of them. I also teach them God’s regulations and instructions.”
EXO 18:17 17 Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “What you are doing isn’t good.
EXO 18:18 18 You will end up totally wearing yourself out, both you and these people who are with you. The work is too difficult for you. You can’t do it alone.
EXO 18:19 19 Now listen to me and let me give you some advice. And may God be with you! Your role should be to represent the people before God. You should bring their disputes before God yourself.
EXO 18:20 20 Explain the regulations and instructions to them. Let them know the way they are supposed to go and the things they are supposed to do.
EXO 18:21 21 But you should also look among all the people for capable persons who respect God. They should be trustworthy and not corrupt. Set these persons over the people as officers of groups of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
EXO 18:22 22 Let them sit as judges for the people at all times. They should bring every major dispute to you, but they should decide all of the minor cases themselves. This will be much easier for you, and they will share your load.
EXO 18:23 23 If you do this and God directs you, then you will be able to endure. And all these people will be able to go back to their homes much happier.”
EXO 18:24 24 Moses listened to his father-in-law’s suggestions and did everything that he had said.
EXO 18:25 25 Moses chose capable persons from all Israel and set them as leaders over the people, as officers over groups of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
EXO 18:26 26 They acted as judges for the people at all times. They would refer the hard cases to Moses, but all of the minor cases they decided themselves.
EXO 18:27 27 Then Moses said good-bye to his father-in-law, and Jethro went back to his own country.
EXO 19:1 1 On exactly the third-month anniversary of the Israelites’ leaving the land of Egypt, they came into the Sinai desert.
EXO 19:2 2 They traveled from Rephidim, came into the Sinai desert, and set up camp there. Israel camped there in front of the mountain
EXO 19:3 3 while Moses went up to God. The LORD called to him from the mountain, “This is what you should say to Jacob’s household and declare to the Israelites:
EXO 19:4 4 You saw what I did to the Egyptians, and how I lifted you up on eagles’ wings and brought you to me.
EXO 19:5 5 So now, if you faithfully obey me and stay true to my covenant, you will be my most precious possession out of all the peoples, since the whole earth belongs to me.
EXO 19:6 6 You will be a kingdom of priests for me and a holy nation. These are the words you should say to the Israelites.”
EXO 19:7 7 So Moses came down, called together the people’s elders, and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
EXO 19:8 8 The people all responded with one voice: “Everything that the LORD has said we will do.” Moses reported to the LORD what the people said.
EXO 19:9 9 Then the LORD said to Moses, “I’m about to come to you in a thick cloud in order that the people will hear me talking with you so that they will always trust you.” Moses told the LORD what the people said,
EXO 19:10 10 and the LORD said to Moses: “Go to the people and take today and tomorrow to make them holy. Have them wash their clothes.
EXO 19:11 11 Be ready for the third day, because on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai for all the people to see.
EXO 19:12 12 Set up a fence for the people all around and tell them, ‘Be careful not to go up the mountain or to touch any part of it.’ Anyone who even touches the mountain must be put to death.
EXO 19:13 13 No one should touch anyone who has touched it, or they must be either stoned to death or shot with arrows. Whether an animal or a human being, they must not be allowed to live. Only when the ram’s horn sounds may they go up on the mountain.”
EXO 19:14 14 So Moses went down the mountain to the people. He made sure the people were holy and that they washed their clothes.
EXO 19:15 15 He told the men, “Prepare yourselves for three days. Don’t go near a woman.”
EXO 19:16 16 When morning dawned on the third day, there was thunder, lightning, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and a very loud blast of a horn. All the people in the camp shook with fear.
EXO 19:17 17 Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they took their place at the foot of the mountain.
EXO 19:18 18 Mount Sinai was all in smoke because the LORD had come down on it with lightning. The smoke went up like the smoke of a hot furnace, while the whole mountain shook violently.
EXO 19:19 19 The blasts of the horn grew louder and louder. Moses would speak, and God would answer him with thunder.
EXO 19:20 20 The LORD came down on Mount Sinai to the top of the mountain. The LORD called Moses to come up to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
EXO 19:21 21 The LORD said to Moses, “Go down and warn the people not to break through to try to see the LORD , or many of them will fall dead.
EXO 19:22 22 Even the priests who come near to the LORD must keep themselves holy, or the LORD will break loose against them.”
EXO 19:23 23 Moses said to the LORD , “The people aren’t allowed to come up on Mount Sinai because you warned us and said, ‘Set up a fence around the mountain to keep it holy.’”
EXO 19:24 24 The LORD said to him, “Go down, and bring Aaron back up with you. But the priests and the people must not break through and come up to the LORD . Otherwise, the LORD will break loose against them.”
EXO 19:25 25 So Moses went down to the people and told them.
EXO 20:1 1 Then God spoke all these words:
EXO 20:2 2 I am the LORD your God who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
EXO 20:3 3 You must have no other gods before me.
EXO 20:4 4 Do not make an idol for yourself—no form whatsoever—of anything in the sky above or on the earth below or in the waters under the earth.
EXO 20:5 5 Do not bow down to them or worship them, because I, the LORD your God, am a passionate God. I punish children for their parents’ sins even to the third and fourth generations of those who hate me.
EXO 20:6 6 But I am loyal and gracious to the thousandth generation of those who love me and keep my commandments.
EXO 20:7 7 Do not use the LORD your God’s name as if it were of no significance; the LORD won’t forgive anyone who uses his name that way.
EXO 20:8 8 Remember the Sabbath day and treat it as holy.
EXO 20:9 9 Six days you may work and do all your tasks,
EXO 20:10 10 but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. Do not do any work on it—not you, your sons or daughters, your male or female servants, your animals, or the immigrant who is living with you.
EXO 20:11 11 Because the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and everything that is in them in six days, but rested on the seventh day. That is why the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
EXO 20:12 12 Honor your father and your mother so that your life will be long on the fertile land that the LORD your God is giving you.
EXO 20:13 13 Do not kill.
EXO 20:14 14 Do not commit adultery.
EXO 20:15 15 Do not steal.
EXO 20:16 16 Do not testify falsely against your neighbor.
EXO 20:17 17 Do not desire and try to take your neighbor’s house. Do not desire and try to take your neighbor’s wife, male or female servant, ox, donkey, or anything else that belongs to your neighbor.
EXO 20:18 18 When all the people witnessed the thunder and lightning, the sound of the horn, and the mountain smoking, the people shook with fear and stood at a distance.
EXO 20:19 19 They said to Moses, “You speak to us, and we’ll listen. But don’t let God speak to us, or we’ll die.”
EXO 20:20 20 Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid, because God has come only to test you and to make sure you are always in awe of God so that you don’t sin.”
EXO 20:21 21 The people stood at a distance while Moses approached the thick darkness in which God was present.
EXO 20:22 22 The LORD said to Moses: “Say this to the Israelites: You saw for yourselves how I spoke with you from heaven.
EXO 20:23 23 Don’t make alongside me gods of silver or gold for yourselves.
EXO 20:24 24 Make for me an altar from fertile soil on which to sacrifice your entirely burned offerings, your well-being sacrifices, your sheep, and your oxen. I will come to you and bless you in every place where I make sure my name is remembered.
EXO 20:25 25 But if you do make for me an altar from stones, don’t build it with chiseled stone since using your chisel on the stone will make it impure.
EXO 20:26 26 Don’t climb onto my altar using steps: then your genitals won’t be exposed by doing so.”
EXO 21:1 1 These are the case laws that you should set before them:
EXO 21:2 2 When you buy a male Hebrew slave, he will serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he will go free without any payment.
EXO 21:3 3 If he came in single, he will leave single. If he came in married, then his wife will leave with him.
EXO 21:4 4 If his master gave him a wife and she bore him sons or daughters, the wife and her children will belong to her master. He will leave single.
EXO 21:5 5 However, if the slave clearly states, “I love my master, my wife, and my children, and I don’t want to go free,”
EXO 21:6 6 then his master will bring him before God. He will bring him to the door or the doorpost. There his master will pierce his ear with a pointed tool, and he will serve him as his slave for life.
EXO 21:7 7 When a man sells his daughter as a slave, she shouldn’t be set free in the same way as male slaves are set free.
EXO 21:8 8 If she doesn’t please her master who chose her for himself, then her master must let her be bought back by her family. He has no right to sell her to a foreign people since he has treated her unfairly.
EXO 21:9 9 If he assigns her to his son, he must give her the rights of a daughter.
EXO 21:10 10 If he takes another woman for himself, he may not reduce her food, clothing, or marital rights.
EXO 21:11 11 If he doesn’t do these three things for her, she will go free without any payment, for no money.
EXO 21:12 12 Anyone who hits and kills someone should be put to death.
EXO 21:13 13 If the killing wasn’t on purpose but an accident allowed by God, then I will designate a place to which the killer can run away.
EXO 21:14 14 But if someone plots and kills another person on purpose, you should remove the killer from my altar and put him to death.
EXO 21:15 15 Anyone who violently hits their father or mother should be put to death.
EXO 21:16 16 Anyone who kidnaps a person, whether they have been sold or are still being held, should be put to death.
EXO 21:17 17 Anyone who curses their father or mother should be put to death.
EXO 21:18 18 When two people are fighting and one hits the other with a stone or with his fist so that he is in bed for a while but doesn’t die—
EXO 21:19 19 if he recovers and is able to walk around outside with a cane, then the one who hit him shouldn’t be punished, except to pay for the loss of time from work and to pay for his full recovery.
EXO 21:20 20 When a slave owner hits a male or female slave with a rod and the slave dies immediately, the owner should be punished.
EXO 21:21 21 But if the slave gets up after a day or two, the slave owner shouldn’t be punished because the slave is the owner’s property.
EXO 21:22 22 When people who are fighting injure a pregnant woman so that she has a miscarriage but no other injury occurs, then the guilty party will be fined what the woman’s husband demands, as negotiated with the judges.
EXO 21:23 23 If there is further injury, then you will give a life for a life,
EXO 21:24 24 an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot,
EXO 21:25 25 a burn for a burn, a bruise for a bruise, a wound for a wound.
EXO 21:26 26 When a slave owner hits and blinds the eye of a male or female slave, he should let the slave go free on account of the eye.
EXO 21:27 27 If he knocks out a tooth of a male or female slave, he should let the slave go free on account of the tooth.
EXO 21:28 28 When an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox should be stoned to death, and the meat of the ox shouldn’t be eaten. But the owner of the ox shouldn’t be punished.
EXO 21:29 29 However, if the ox had gored people in the past and its owner had been warned but didn’t watch out for it, and the ox ends up killing a man or a woman, then the ox should be stoned to death, and its owner should also be put to death.
EXO 21:30 30 If the owner has to pay compensation instead, he must pay the agreed amount to save his life.
EXO 21:31 31 If the ox gores a boy or a girl, this same case law applies to the owner.
EXO 21:32 32 If the ox gores a male or female slave, the owner will pay thirty silver shekels to the slave’s owner, and the ox will be stoned to death.
EXO 21:33 33 When someone leaves a pit open or digs a pit and doesn’t cover it and an ox or a donkey falls into the pit,
EXO 21:34 34 the owner of the pit must make good on the loss. He should pay money to the ox’s owner, but he may keep the dead animal.
EXO 21:35 35 When someone’s ox hurts someone else’s ox and it dies, then they should sell the live ox and divide its price. They should also divide the dead animal between them.
EXO 21:36 36 But if the ox was known for goring in the past and its owner hadn’t watched out for it, the owner must make good the loss, an ox for an ox, but may keep the dead animal.
EXO 22:1 1 When someone steals an ox or a sheep and then slaughters or sells it, the thief must pay back five oxen for the one ox or four sheep for the one sheep.
EXO 22:2 2 If the thief is caught breaking in and is beaten and dies, the one who killed him won’t be guilty of bloodshed.
EXO 22:3 3 However, if this happens in broad daylight, then the one who killed him is guilty of bloodshed. For his part, the thief must make good on what he stole. If he has nothing, he must be sold to pay for his theft.
EXO 22:4 4 If an animal (whether ox, donkey, or sheep) is found alive in the thief’s possession, he must pay back double.
EXO 22:5 5 When someone lets an animal loose to eat in another person’s field and causes the field or vineyard to be stripped of its crop, the owner must pay them back with the best from his own field or vineyard.
EXO 22:6 6 When someone starts a fire and it catches in thorns and then spreads to someone else’s stacked grain, standing grain, or a whole field, the one who started the fire must fully repay the loss.
EXO 22:7 7 When someone entrusts money or other items to another person to keep safe and they are stolen from the other person’s house and the thief is caught, the thief must pay back double.
EXO 22:8 8 If the thief isn’t caught, the owner of the house should be brought before God to determine whether or not the owner stole the other’s property.
EXO 22:9 9 When any dispute of ownership over an ox, donkey, sheep, piece of clothing, or any other loss arises in which someone claims, “This is mine,” the cases of both parties should come before God. The one whom God finds at fault must pay double to the other.
EXO 22:10 10 When someone gives a donkey, ox, sheep, or any other animal to another person to keep safe, and the animal dies or is injured or taken and no one saw what happened,
EXO 22:11 11 the person should swear a solemn pledge before the LORD in the presence of the owner that he didn’t touch the other’s property. The owner must accept that, and no payment needs to be made.
EXO 22:12 12 But if the animal was stolen, the person must make full payment to its owner.
EXO 22:13 13 If the animal was attacked and ripped apart and its torn body is brought as evidence, no payment needs to be made.
EXO 22:14 14 When someone borrows an animal from another and it is injured or dies while the owner isn’t present, full payment must be made.
EXO 22:15 15 If the owner was present, no payment needs to be made. If the animal was hired, only the fee for hiring the animal is due.
EXO 22:16 16 When a man seduces a young woman who isn’t engaged to be married yet and he sleeps with her, he must marry her and pay the bride-price for her.
EXO 22:17 17 But if her father absolutely refuses to let them marry, he must still pay the same amount as the bride-price for young women.
EXO 22:18 18 Don’t allow a female sorcerer to live.
EXO 22:19 19 Anyone who has sexual relations with an animal should be put to death.
EXO 22:20 20 Anyone who offers sacrifices to any god, other than the LORD alone, should be destroyed.
EXO 22:21 21 Don’t mistreat or oppress an immigrant, because you were once immigrants in the land of Egypt.
EXO 22:22 22 Don’t treat any widow or orphan badly.
EXO 22:23 23 If you do treat them badly and they cry out to me, you can be sure that I’ll hear their cry.
EXO 22:24 24 I’ll be furious, and I’ll kill you with the sword. Then your wives will be widows, and your children will be orphans.
EXO 22:25 25 If you lend money to my people who are poor among you, don’t be a creditor and charge them interest.
EXO 22:26 26 If you take a piece of clothing from someone as a security deposit, you should return it before the sun goes down.
EXO 22:27 27 His clothing may well be his only blanket to cover himself. What else will that person have to sleep in? And if he cries out to me, I’ll listen, because I’m compassionate.
EXO 22:28 28 Don’t say a curse against God, and don’t curse your people’s chief.
EXO 22:29 29 Don’t delay offering the produce of your vineyards and winepresses. Give me your oldest son.
EXO 22:30 30 Do the same with your oxen and with your sheep. They should stay with their mother for seven days. On the eighth day, you should give them to me.
EXO 22:31 31 You are holy people to me. Don’t eat any meat killed by wild animals out in the field. Throw it to the dogs instead.
EXO 23:1 1 Don’t spread false rumors. Don’t plot with evil people to act as a lying witness.
EXO 23:2 2 Don’t take sides with important people to do wrong. When you act as a witness, don’t stretch the truth to favor important people.
EXO 23:3 3 But don’t privilege unimportant people in their lawsuits either.
EXO 23:4 4 When you happen to come upon your enemy’s ox or donkey that has wandered off, you should bring it back to them.
EXO 23:5 5 When you see a donkey that belongs to someone who hates you and it’s lying down under its load and you are inclined not to help set it free, you must help set it free.
EXO 23:6 6 Don’t undermine the justice that your poor deserve in their lawsuits.
EXO 23:7 7 Stay away from making a false charge. Don’t put an innocent person who is in the right to death, because I will not consider innocent those who do such evil.
EXO 23:8 8 Don’t take a bribe, because a bribe blinds the clear-sighted and subverts the cause of those who are in the right.
EXO 23:9 9 Don’t oppress an immigrant. You know what it’s like to be an immigrant, because you were immigrants in the land of Egypt.
EXO 23:10 10 For six years you should plant crops on your land and gather in its produce.
EXO 23:11 11 But in the seventh year you should leave it alone and undisturbed so that the poor among your people may eat. What they leave behind, the wild animals may eat. You should do the same with your vineyard and your olive trees.
EXO 23:12 12 Do your work in six days. But on the seventh day you should rest so that your ox and donkey may rest, and even the child of your female slave and the immigrant may be refreshed.
EXO 23:13 13 Be careful to obey everything that I have said to you. Don’t call on the names of other gods. Don’t even mention them.
EXO 23:14 14 You should observe a festival for me three times a year.
EXO 23:15 15 Observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread, as I commanded you. Eat unleavened bread for seven days at the appointed time in the month of Abib, because it was in that month that you came out of Egypt. No one should appear before me empty-handed.
EXO 23:16 16 Observe the Harvest Festival for the early produce of your crops that you planted in the field, and the Gathering Festival at the end of the year, when you gather your crop of fruit from the field.
EXO 23:17 17 All your males should appear three times a year before the LORD God.
EXO 23:18 18 Don’t offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened. Don’t let the fat of my festival offering be left over until the morning.
EXO 23:19 19 Bring the best of your land’s early produce to the LORD your God’s temple. Don’t boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
EXO 23:20 20 I’m about to send a messenger in front of you to guard you on your way and to bring you to the place that I’ve made ready.
EXO 23:21 21 Pay attention to him and do as he says. Don’t rebel against him. He won’t forgive the things you do wrong because I am with him.
EXO 23:22 22 But if you listen carefully to what he says and do all that I say, then I’ll be an enemy to your enemies and fight those fighting you.
EXO 23:23 23 When my messenger goes in front of you and brings you to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, and I wipe them out,
EXO 23:24 24 don’t bow down to their gods, worship them, or do what they do. Instead, you should completely destroy them and smash their sacred stone pillars to bits.
EXO 23:25 25 If you worship the LORD your God, the LORD will bless your bread and your water. I’ll take sickness away from you,
EXO 23:26 26 and no woman will miscarry or be infertile in your land. I’ll let you live a full, long life.
EXO 23:27 27 My terrifying reputation will precede you, and I’ll throw all the people that you meet into a panic. I’ll make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
EXO 23:28 28 I’ll send insect swarms in front of you and drive out the Hivites, the Canaanites, and the Hittites before you.
EXO 23:29 29 I won’t drive them out before you in a single year so the land won’t be abandoned and the wild animals won’t multiply around you.
EXO 23:30 30 I’ll drive them out before you little by little, until your numbers grow and you eventually possess the land.
EXO 23:31 31 I’ll set your borders from the Reed Sea to the Philistine Sea and from the desert to the River. I’ll hand the inhabitants of the land over to you, and you will drive them out before you.
EXO 23:32 32 Don’t make any covenants with them or their gods.
EXO 23:33 33 Don’t allow them to live in your land, or else they will lead you to sin against me. If you worship their gods, it will become a dangerous trap for you.
EXO 24:1 1 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Come up to the LORD , you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of Israel’s elders, and worship from a distance.
EXO 24:2 2 Only Moses may come near to the LORD . The others shouldn’t come near, while the people shouldn’t come up with him at all.”
EXO 24:3 3 Moses came and told the people all the LORD ’s words and all the case laws. All the people answered in unison, “Everything that the LORD has said we will do.”
EXO 24:4 4 Moses then wrote down all the LORD ’s words. He got up early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain. He set up twelve sacred stone pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
EXO 24:5 5 He appointed certain young Israelite men to offer entirely burned offerings and slaughter oxen as well-being sacrifices to the LORD .
EXO 24:6 6 Moses took half of the blood and put it in large bowls. The other half of the blood he threw against the altar.
EXO 24:7 7 Then he took the covenant scroll and read it out loud for the people to hear. They responded, “Everything that the LORD has said we will do, and we will obey.”
EXO 24:8 8 Moses then took the blood and threw it over the people. Moses said, “This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD now makes with you on the basis of all these words.”
EXO 24:9 9 Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy elders of Israel went up,
EXO 24:10 10 and they saw Israel’s God. Under God’s feet there was what looked like a floor of lapis-lazuli tiles, dazzlingly pure like the sky.
EXO 24:11 11 God didn’t harm the Israelite leaders, though they looked at God, and they ate and drank.
EXO 24:12 12 The LORD said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and wait there. I’ll give you the stone tablets with the instructions and the commandments that I’ve written in order to teach them.”
EXO 24:13 13 So Moses and his assistant Joshua got up, and Moses went up God’s mountain.
EXO 24:14 14 Moses had said to the elders, “Wait for us here until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur will be here with you. Whoever has a legal dispute may go to them.”
EXO 24:15 15 Then Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
EXO 24:16 16 The LORD ’s glorious presence settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day the LORD called to Moses from the cloud.
EXO 24:17 17 To the Israelites, the LORD ’s glorious presence looked like a blazing fire on top of the mountain.
EXO 24:18 18 Moses entered the cloud and went up the mountain. Moses stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.
EXO 25:1 1 The LORD said to Moses:
EXO 25:2 2 Tell the Israelites to collect gift offerings for me. Receive my gift offerings from everyone who freely wants to give.
EXO 25:3 3 These are the gift offerings that you should receive from them: gold, silver, and copper;
EXO 25:4 4 blue, purple, and deep red yarns; fine linen; goats’ hair;
EXO 25:5 5 rams’ skins dyed red; beaded leather; acacia wood;
EXO 25:6 6 oil for the lamps; spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet-smelling incense;
EXO 25:7 7 gemstones; and gems for setting in the priest’s vest and chest piece.
EXO 25:8 8 They should make me a sanctuary so I can be present among them.
EXO 25:9 9 You should follow the blueprints that I will show you for the dwelling and for all its equipment.
EXO 25:10 10 Have them make an acacia-wood chest. It should be forty-five inches long, twenty-seven inches wide, and twenty-seven inches high.
EXO 25:11 11 Cover it with pure gold, inside and out, and make a gold molding all around it.
EXO 25:12 12 Cast four gold rings for it and put them on its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
EXO 25:13 13 Make acacia-wood poles and cover them with gold.
EXO 25:14 14 Then put the poles into the rings on the chest’s sides and use them to carry the chest.
EXO 25:15 15 The poles should stay in the chest’s rings. They shouldn’t be taken out of them.
EXO 25:16 16 Put the covenant document that I will give you into the chest.
EXO 25:17 17 Then make a cover of pure gold, forty-five inches long and twenty-seven inches wide.
EXO 25:18 18 Make two winged heavenly creatures of hammered gold, one for each end of the cover.
EXO 25:19 19 Put one winged heavenly creature at one end and one winged heavenly creature at the other. Place the winged heavenly creatures at the cover’s two ends.
EXO 25:20 20 The heavenly creatures should have their wings spread out above, shielding the cover with their wings. The winged heavenly creatures should face each other toward the cover’s center.
EXO 25:21 21 Put the gold cover on top of the chest and put the covenant document that I will give you inside the chest.
EXO 25:22 22 There I will meet with you. From there above the cover, from between the two winged heavenly creatures that are on top of the chest containing the covenant, I will deliver to you all that I command you concerning the Israelites.
EXO 25:23 23 Make an acacia-wood table, three feet long, eighteen inches wide, and twenty-seven inches high.
EXO 25:24 24 Cover it with pure gold and make a gold molding all around it.
EXO 25:25 25 Make a frame around it that is four inches wide and a gold molding around the frame.
EXO 25:26 26 Make four gold rings for the table. Fasten the rings to the four corners at its four legs.
EXO 25:27 27 The rings that house the poles used for carrying the table should be close to the frame.
EXO 25:28 28 Make the poles from acacia wood and cover them with gold. The table should be carried with these poles.
EXO 25:29 29 Make its plates, dishes, jars, and bowls for pouring drink offerings. Make them of pure gold.
EXO 25:30 30 Set the bread of the presence on the table so it is always in front of me.
EXO 25:31 31 Make a lampstand of pure hammered gold. The lampstand’s base, branches, cups, flowers, and petals should all be attached to it.
EXO 25:32 32 It should have six branches growing out from its sides, three branches on one side of the lampstand and three branches on the other side of the lampstand.
EXO 25:33 33 One branch will have three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with a flower and petals, and the next branch will also have three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with a flower and petals. So it will be for the six branches that grow out of the lampstand.
EXO 25:34 34 In addition, on the lampstand itself there will be four cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with its flower and petals.
EXO 25:35 35 There will be a flower attached under the first pair of branches, a flower attached under the next pair of branches, and a flower attached under the last pair of branches. So it will be for the six branches that grow out of the lampstand.
EXO 25:36 36 Their flowers and their branches will be permanently attached to it. The whole lampstand should be one piece of pure hammered gold.
EXO 25:37 37 Make its seven lamps and set up its lamps so that they direct their light in front of the lampstand.
EXO 25:38 38 You should also make its tongs and fire pans out of pure gold.
EXO 25:39 39 All these items should be made from pure gold weighing one kikkar.
EXO 25:40 40 See to it that you make them according to the blueprint for them that you were shown on the mountain.
EXO 26:1 1 Make the dwelling with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and deep red yarns. Work figures of winged heavenly creatures into their design.
EXO 26:2 2 Each curtain should be forty-two feet long and each curtain six feet wide. All the curtains should be the same size.
EXO 26:3 3 Five curtains will be joined to each other as one set, while the other five curtains will be joined together as a second set.
EXO 26:4 4 Make loops of blue thread on the edge of the outer curtain in the first set. Do the same on the edge of the outer curtain in the second set.
EXO 26:5 5 Make fifty loops on the one curtain in the first set and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain that is in the second set. The loops should be opposite each other.
EXO 26:6 6 Then make fifty gold clasps. Join the curtains to each other with the clasps so that the dwelling becomes one whole structure.
EXO 26:7 7 You should also make curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the dwelling. Make eleven curtains.
EXO 26:8 8 Each curtain should be forty-five feet long and each curtain six feet wide. The eleven curtains should all be the same size.
EXO 26:9 9 Join five of the curtains together, and join the six other curtains together. Double over the sixth curtain at the front of the tent.
EXO 26:10 10 Make fifty loops on the edge of the outer curtain in one set and fifty loops on the edge of the outer curtain in the second set.
EXO 26:11 11 Make fifty copper clasps. Put the clasps into the loops and join the tent together so that it becomes one whole structure.
EXO 26:12 12 The extra cloth that is left over from the tent curtains, that is, the half curtain that remains, should hang over the back of the dwelling.
EXO 26:13 13 Eighteen inches on one side and eighteen inches on the other side of the leftover length of the tent’s curtains will hang over the two sides of the dwelling to cover it.
EXO 26:14 14 Then for the tent, make a covering of rams’ skins dyed red and an outer covering of beaded leather.
EXO 26:15 15 Make acacia-wood boards to stand upright as a frame for the dwelling.
EXO 26:16 16 Each board will be fifteen feet long and twenty-seven inches wide.
EXO 26:17 17 Put two pegs on each board for joining them to each other. Do this for all the dwelling’s boards.
EXO 26:18 18 Make twenty boards for the dwelling’s southern side.
EXO 26:19 19 Then make forty silver bases to go under the twenty boards. There will be two bases under the first board for its two pegs, two bases under the next board for its two pegs, and so on.
EXO 26:20 20 For the dwelling’s other side on the north, make twenty boards
EXO 26:21 21 and their forty silver bases, two bases under the first board, two bases under the next board, and so on.
EXO 26:22 22 For the back of the dwelling on the west, make six boards.
EXO 26:23 23 Make two additional boards for the dwelling’s rear corners.
EXO 26:24 24 They should be spread out at the bottom but joined together at the top with one ring. In this way, these two boards will form the two corners.
EXO 26:25 25 And so there will be eight boards with their sixteen silver bases, two bases under the first board, two bases under the next board, and so on.
EXO 26:26 26 You should also make acacia-wood bars: five for the boards on one side of the dwelling,
EXO 26:27 27 five bars for the boards on the other side of the dwelling, and five bars for the boards on the back wall of the dwelling on the west.
EXO 26:28 28 The middle bar, halfway up the boards, should run from one end to the other.
EXO 26:29 29 Cover the boards with gold. Make gold rings to house the bars. Cover the bars with gold.
EXO 26:30 30 Then set up the dwelling according to the plan for it that you were shown on the mountain.
EXO 26:31 31 Make a veil of blue, purple, and deep red yarns and of fine twisted linen. Work figures of winged heavenly creatures into its design.
EXO 26:32 32 Hang it on four acacia-wood posts covered in gold. They should have gold hooks and stand on four silver bases.
EXO 26:33 33 Hang the veil under the clasps, and put the chest containing the covenant there behind the veil. The veil will separate for you the holy from the holiest space.
EXO 26:34 34 Place the gold cover on the chest containing the covenant in the holiest space.
EXO 26:35 35 Place the table outside the veil, and set the lampstand opposite the table by the south wall of the dwelling. Place the table by the north wall.
EXO 26:36 36 Make a screen for the tent’s entrance of blue, purple, and deep red yarns and of fine twisted linen, decorated with needlework.
EXO 26:37 37 Make five acacia-wood posts for the screen. Cover the posts with gold. Their hooks should be gold. Cast five copper bases for the posts.
EXO 27:1 1 Make an acacia-wood altar. The altar should be square, seven and a half feet long and seven and a half feet wide. It should be four and a half feet high.
EXO 27:2 2 Make horns for the altar and attach them to it, one horn on each of its four corners. Cover it with copper.
EXO 27:3 3 Make pails for removing its ashes and its shovels, bowls, meat forks, and trays. Make all its equipment out of copper.
EXO 27:4 4 Make for the altar a grate made of copper mesh. Make four copper rings for each of the four corners of the mesh.
EXO 27:5 5 Slide the mesh underneath the bottom edge of the altar and then extend the mesh halfway up to the middle of the altar.
EXO 27:6 6 Make acacia-wood poles for the altar and cover them with copper.
EXO 27:7 7 Put the poles through the rings so that the poles will be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
EXO 27:8 8 Make the altar with planks but hollow inside. All these should be made just as you were shown on the mountain.
EXO 27:9 9 You should also set up the dwelling’s courtyard. The courtyard’s south side should have drapes of fine twisted linen stretching one hundred fifty feet on that side,
EXO 27:10 10 with twenty posts, twenty copper bases, and silver hooks and bands for the posts.
EXO 27:11 11 Likewise along the north side the drapes should stretch one hundred fifty feet, with twenty posts, twenty copper bases, and silver hooks and bands for the posts.
EXO 27:12 12 The courtyard’s width on the west side should consist of seventy-five feet of drapes with their ten posts and their ten bases.
EXO 27:13 13 The courtyard’s width on the front, facing east, should be seventy-five feet.
EXO 27:14 14 There should be twenty-two and a half feet of drapes on one side with three posts and three bases for them.
EXO 27:15 15 There should be twenty-two and a half feet of drapes on the other side with three posts and three bases for them.
EXO 27:16 16 For the gate into the courtyard there will be a screen thirty feet long, made of blue, purple, and deep red yarns and of fine twisted linen, decorated with needlework. It will have four posts with their four bases.
EXO 27:17 17 All the posts around the courtyard will have silver bands, silver hooks, and copper bases.
EXO 27:18 18 The courtyard will be one hundred fifty feet long and seventy-five feet wide. Its walls’ height will be seven and a half feet of fine twisted linen and its copper bases.
EXO 27:19 19 All the dwelling’s equipment for any use and all its tent pegs and all the courtyard’s tent pegs will be made of copper.
EXO 27:20 20 You must require the Israelites to bring you pure oil of crushed olives for the light so that the lamp may be set up to burn continually.
EXO 27:21 21 In the meeting tent, outside the veil that hangs in front of the covenant document, Aaron and his sons will tend the lamp from evening to morning in the LORD ’s presence. It will be a permanent regulation for the Israelites in every generation.
EXO 28:1 1 Summon to you your brother Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites to serve me as priests—Aaron and Aaron’s sons, Nadab and Abihu, and Eleazar and Ithamar.
EXO 28:2 2 Make holy clothing that will give honor and dignity to your brother Aaron.
EXO 28:3 3 Tell all who are skilled, to whom I have given special abilities, to make clothing for Aaron for his dedication to serve me as a priest.
EXO 28:4 4 These are the articles of clothing that they should make: a chest pendant, a vest, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. When they make this holy clothing for your brother Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests,
EXO 28:5 5 they should use gold, blue, purple, and deep red yarns and fine linen.
EXO 28:6 6 They should make the vest of gold, of blue, purple, and deep red yarns and of fine twisted linen with embroidered designs.
EXO 28:7 7 The vest will have two shoulder pieces attached to its two edges so that they may be joined together.
EXO 28:8 8 The vest’s belt should be attached to it and made in the same way of gold, of blue, purple, and deep red yarns and fine twisted linen.
EXO 28:9 9 Take two gemstones and engrave on them the names of Israel’s sons,
EXO 28:10 10 six names on one stone and the other six names on the other stone, in the order of their birth.
EXO 28:11 11 Like a gem cutter who engraves official seals, you will engrave the two stones with the names of Israel’s sons. Mount them in gold settings.
EXO 28:12 12 Attach the two stones to the vest’s shoulder pieces as stones of reminder for the Israelites. Aaron will carry into the LORD ’s presence their names on his two shoulders as a reminder.
EXO 28:13 13 Then make gold settings
EXO 28:14 14 along with two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords. Attach the corded chains to the gold settings.
EXO 28:15 15 Make an embroidered chest pendant used for making decisions. Make it in the style of the vest, using gold, blue and purple and deep red yarns, and fine twisted linen.
EXO 28:16 16 It will be square and doubled, nine inches long and nine inches wide.
EXO 28:17 17 Set in it four rows of gemstone settings. The first row will be a row of carnelian, topaz, and emerald stones.
EXO 28:18 18 The second row will be a turquoise, a sapphire, and a moonstone.
EXO 28:19 19 The third row will be a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
EXO 28:20 20 The fourth row will be a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Their settings will be made of decorative gold.
EXO 28:21 21 There will be twelve stones with names corresponding to the names of Israel’s sons. They will be engraved like official seals, each with its name for the twelve tribes.
EXO 28:22 22 Make chains of pure gold twisted like cords for the chest pendant.
EXO 28:23 23 Make two gold rings for the chest pendant and attach the two rings to the two edges of the chest pendant.
EXO 28:24 24 Attach the two gold cords to the two rings at the edges of the chest pendant.
EXO 28:25 25 Then fasten the two ends of the cords to the two settings, which you should attach to the vest’s two front shoulder pieces.
EXO 28:26 26 Make two gold rings and attach them to the two ends of the chest pendant on its inside edge facing the vest.
EXO 28:27 27 Make two gold rings and fasten them on the front of the lower part of the two shoulder pieces of the vest, at its seam just above the vest’s belt.
EXO 28:28 28 The chest pendant should be held in place by a blue cord binding its rings to the vest’s rings so that the chest pendant rests on the vest’s belt and won’t come loose from the vest.
EXO 28:29 29 In this way, Aaron will carry the names of Israel’s sons on the chest pendant for making decisions over his heart when he goes into the sanctuary as a reminder before the LORD at all times.
EXO 28:30 30 Put into the chest pendant used for making decisions the Urim and the Thummim, so they will be over Aaron’s heart when he goes into the LORD ’s presence. In this way, Aaron will carry the means to make decisions for the Israelites over his heart when in the LORD ’s presence at all times.
EXO 28:31 31 You will make the robe for the vest all of blue.
EXO 28:32 32 The opening for the head should be in the middle of it. The opening should be reinforced by a woven binding, a strong border so that it doesn’t tear.
EXO 28:33 33 On its lower hem add pomegranates made of blue, purple, and deep red yarns all around the lower hem, with gold bells between the pomegranates all around it.
EXO 28:34 34 A gold bell and a pomegranate should alternate all around the lower hem of the robe.
EXO 28:35 35 Aaron will wear the robe when he ministers as a priest. Its sound will be heard when he goes into the sanctuary in the LORD ’s presence and when he comes out, so that he will not die.
EXO 28:36 36 Make a flower ornament of pure gold and engrave on it like an official seal: “Holy to the LORD .”
EXO 28:37 37 You should fasten it on the turban with a blue cord. It should be on the front of the turban.
EXO 28:38 38 It will be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron will take on himself any guilt connected with the holy offerings that the Israelites give as their sacred donations. It will always be on his forehead so that the people may be remembered favorably in the LORD ’s presence.
EXO 28:39 39 Weave the tunic out of fine linen. Make the turban out of fine linen. Make a sash decorated with needlework.
EXO 28:40 40 For Aaron’s sons, you should also make tunics, sashes, and turbans to mark their honor and dignity.
EXO 28:41 41 Put these garments on your brother Aaron and on his sons with him. Anoint them with oil, ordain them, and make them holy to serve me as priests.
EXO 28:42 42 You should also make linen undergarments for them to cover their naked skin from their hips to their thighs.
EXO 28:43 43 Aaron and his sons should wear this clothing when they go into the meeting tent or when they approach the altar to minister as priests in the sanctuary. Otherwise, they will bring guilt on themselves and die. This will be a permanent regulation for him and for his descendants after him.
EXO 29:1 1 Now this is what you should do to make them holy in order to serve me as priests. Take a young bull and two flawless rams.
EXO 29:2 2 Take unleavened bread, unleavened flatbread made with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil. Make them out of high-quality wheat flour.
EXO 29:3 3 Put them all in one basket and present them in the basket along with the bull and the two rams.
EXO 29:4 4 Present Aaron and his sons at the entrance to the meeting tent and wash them with water.
EXO 29:5 5 Then take the priestly clothes and put them on Aaron: the tunic, the vest’s robe, the vest itself, and the chest pendant. Put the vest on him with the vest’s belt.
EXO 29:6 6 Set the turban on his head and place the holy crown on the turban.
EXO 29:7 7 Take the anointing oil and pour it on his head to anoint him.
EXO 29:8 8 Then present his sons and put the tunics on them.
EXO 29:9 9 Tighten the sashes on them, on both Aaron and his sons. Wrap the turbans on their heads. It will be a permanent regulation that the duties of priesthood belong to them. In this way, you will ordain Aaron and his sons.
EXO 29:10 10 Present the bull at the front of the meeting tent. Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on the bull’s head.
EXO 29:11 11 Then slaughter the bull in the LORD ’s presence at the meeting tent’s entrance.
EXO 29:12 12 Take some of the bull’s blood and smear it on the altar’s horns with your finger. Pour out the rest of the blood at the altar’s base.
EXO 29:13 13 Then take all the fat that covers the inner organs, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys along with the fat that is on them, and burn them up in smoke on the altar.
EXO 29:14 14 Burn the rest of the meat of the bull, its hide, and the intestines with their contents with a fire outside the camp. It is a purification offering.
EXO 29:15 15 Choose one of the rams, and have Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the ram’s head.
EXO 29:16 16 Then slaughter the ram. Take its blood and throw it against all the altar’s sides.
EXO 29:17 17 Cut up the ram into parts. Wash its inner organs and legs, and put them together with its parts and its head.
EXO 29:18 18 Then turn the entire ram into smoke by burning it on the altar. It is an entirely burned offering for the LORD , a soothing smell, a food gift for the LORD .
EXO 29:19 19 Take the second ram, and have Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the ram’s head.
EXO 29:20 20 Slaughter the ram. Take some of its blood and smear it on the right earlobes of Aaron and his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Throw the rest of the blood against all the altar’s sides.
EXO 29:21 21 Then take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle them on Aaron and on his clothes and on his sons and on his sons’ clothes. In this way, Aaron, his sons, and all their priestly garments will be holy.
EXO 29:22 22 Take the fatty parts of the ram: the fat tail, the fat around the inner organs, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat around them, and the right thigh (because it is a ram for ordination).
EXO 29:23 23 Add one loaf of bread, one flatbread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that was presented to the LORD .
EXO 29:24 24 Place all of these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and lift them as an uplifted offering in the LORD ’s presence.
EXO 29:25 25 Then take them from their hands and turn them into smoke by burning them on the altar with the entirely burned offering as a soothing smell in the LORD ’s presence. It is a food gift for the LORD .
EXO 29:26 26 Take the breast of the ram for Aaron’s ordination and lift it as an uplifted offering in the LORD ’s presence. It will be your portion.
EXO 29:27 27 Make holy the breast that was lifted for the uplifted offering and the thigh that was raised for the gift offering from the ram for the ordination. They belong to Aaron and his sons.
EXO 29:28 28 Those parts will be given to Aaron and his sons from the Israelites as a permanent provision, because they are a gift offering. They will be a gift offering from the Israelites, their gift offering to the LORD from their well-being sacrifices.
EXO 29:29 29 Aaron’s holy clothes should be passed on to his sons after him. His sons should be anointed in them and ordained in them.
EXO 29:30 30 The son who is priest in his place should wear them seven days when he comes into the meeting tent to minister in the sanctuary.
EXO 29:31 31 Take the ram for the ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
EXO 29:32 32 Aaron and his sons will eat the ram’s meat and the bread that is in the basket at the meeting tent’s entrance.
EXO 29:33 33 They alone should eat the food that was used to purify them, to ordain them, and to make them holy. No one else should eat it because it is holy.
EXO 29:34 34 If any meat for the ordination or any of the bread is left over until morning, then you should burn the leftovers with fire. It shouldn’t be eaten because it’s holy.
EXO 29:35 35 Treat Aaron and his sons just as I have commanded you. Ordain them for seven days.
EXO 29:36 36 Every day you should offer a bull as a purification offering for reconciliation. You should remove the sin from the altar through a ritual of reconciliation, and you should anoint the altar to make it holy.
EXO 29:37 37 Seven days you should perform the ritual of reconciliation for the altar and make it holy. In this way, the altar will become most holy, and whatever touches the altar will also become holy.
EXO 29:38 38 Now this is what you should offer on the altar: two one-year-old lambs regularly every day.
EXO 29:39 39 Offer one lamb in the morning and offer the other lamb at twilight.
EXO 29:40 40 With the first lamb, add one-tenth of a measure of the high-quality flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil from crushed olives and a quarter of a hin of wine for a drink offering.
EXO 29:41 41 With the second lamb offered at twilight, again include a grain offering and its drink offering as in the morning as a soothing smell, a gift offering for the LORD .
EXO 29:42 42 This should be the regular entirely burned offering in every generation at the meeting tent’s entrance in the LORD ’s presence. There I will meet with you, and there I will speak to you.
EXO 29:43 43 I will meet with the Israelites there, and it will be made holy by my glorious presence.
EXO 29:44 44 I will make the meeting tent and the altar holy. Likewise, I will make Aaron and his sons holy to serve me as priests.
EXO 29:45 45 I will be at home among the Israelites, and I will be their God.
EXO 29:46 46 They will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I could make a home among them. I am the LORD their God.
EXO 30:1 1 Make an acacia-wood altar for burning incense.
EXO 30:2 2 The altar should be square, eighteen inches long and eighteen inches wide. It should be three feet high. Its horns should be permanently attached.
EXO 30:3 3 Cover the altar with pure gold, including its top, all its sides, and its horns. You should also make a gold molding all around it.
EXO 30:4 4 Make two gold rings and attach them under the molding on two opposite sides of the altar. They will house the poles used to carry the altar.
EXO 30:5 5 Make acacia-wood poles and cover them with gold.
EXO 30:6 6 Place the incense altar in front of the veil that hangs before the chest containing the covenant, in front of the cover that is on top of the covenant document where I will meet with you.
EXO 30:7 7 Aaron will burn sweet-smelling incense on the incense altar every morning when he takes care of the lamps.
EXO 30:8 8 And again when Aaron lights the lamps at twilight, he will burn incense. It should be a regular incense offering in the LORD ’s presence in every generation.
EXO 30:9 9 Don’t offer the wrong incense on the altar or an entirely burned offering or a grain offering. Don’t pour a drink offering on it.
EXO 30:10 10 Once a year Aaron should perform a ritual of reconciliation on its horns with the blood of the purification offering for reconciliation. Once a year in every generation he should perform a ritual of reconciliation at the altar. It is most holy to the LORD .
EXO 30:11 11 The LORD spoke to Moses:
EXO 30:12 12 When you take a census of the Israelites to count them, each of them should pay compensation for their life to the LORD when they are counted. Then no plague will descend on them when they are counted.
EXO 30:13 13 Every one who is counted should pay a half shekel according to the official shekel of the sanctuary (the shekel is twenty gerahs). The half shekel is a gift offering to the LORD .
EXO 30:14 14 Every one who is counted, from 20 years old and above, should present a gift offering to the LORD .
EXO 30:15 15 When you bring this gift offering to the LORD to pay compensation for your lives, the rich shouldn’t give more and the poor shouldn’t give less than the half shekel.
EXO 30:16 16 Take the compensation money from the Israelites and use it to support the service of the meeting tent. It will serve for the Israelites as a reminder in the LORD ’s presence of the compensation paid for your lives.
EXO 30:17 17 The LORD spoke to Moses:
EXO 30:18 18 Make a copper basin for washing along with its copper stand. Put it between the meeting tent and the altar, and put water in it.
EXO 30:19 19 Aaron and his sons will use it to wash their hands and their feet.
EXO 30:20 20 When they go into the meeting tent or approach the altar to minister and to offer a food gift to the LORD , they must wash with water so that they don’t die.
EXO 30:21 21 They must wash their hands and their feet so that they don’t die. This will be a permanent regulation for them, for Aaron and his descendants in every generation.
EXO 30:22 22 The LORD spoke to Moses:
EXO 30:23 23 Now take for yourself high-quality spices: five hundred weight of solid myrrh; half as much of sweet-smelling cinnamon, that is, two hundred fifty; two hundred fifty weight of sweet-smelling cane;
EXO 30:24 24 five hundred of cassia—measured by the sanctuary shekel—and a hin of olive oil.
EXO 30:25 25 Prepare a holy anointing oil, blending them like a skilled perfume maker to produce the holy anointing oil.
EXO 30:26 26 Use it to anoint the meeting tent, the chest containing the covenant,
EXO 30:27 27 the table and all its equipment, the lampstand and its equipment, the incense altar,
EXO 30:28 28 the altar for entirely burned offerings and all its equipment, and the washbasin with its stand.
EXO 30:29 29 Make them holy so that they may be perfectly holy. Whatever touches them will become holy.
EXO 30:30 30 Then anoint Aaron and his sons and make them holy to serve me as priests.
EXO 30:31 31 Say to the Israelites: This will be my holy anointing oil in every generation.
EXO 30:32 32 Don’t allow anyone else to use this oil. Don’t make another oil like it by using the same formula. This oil is holy, and you should regard it as holy.
EXO 30:33 33 Whoever blends an oil like it or whoever uses the oil on someone else will be cut off from the people.
EXO 30:34 34 The LORD said to Moses: Take an equal amount of each of these spices: gum resin, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense.
EXO 30:35 35 Like a skilled perfume maker, carefully blend them together and make incense, seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
EXO 30:36 36 Beat some of it into a fine powder and put part of it in front of the covenant document in the meeting tent where I will meet with you. You should regard it as perfectly holy.
EXO 30:37 37 When you make incense according to this formula, you shouldn’t make any of it for your own use. You should regard it as holy to the LORD .
EXO 30:38 38 Whoever makes incense with this same formula to enjoy its fragrance will be cut off from the people.
EXO 31:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses:
EXO 31:2 2 Look, I have chosen Bezalel, Uri’s son and Hur’s grandson from the tribe of Judah.
EXO 31:3 3 I have filled him with the divine spirit, with skill, ability, and knowledge for every kind of work.
EXO 31:4 4 He will be able to create designs; do metalwork in gold, silver, and copper;
EXO 31:5 5 cut stones for setting; carve wood; and do every kind of work.
EXO 31:6 6 I have also appointed with him Oholiab, Ahisamach’s son from the tribe of Dan. To all who are skillful, I have given the skill to make everything that I have commanded you:
EXO 31:7 7 the meeting tent, the chest containing the covenant, the cover that is on top of it, all the tent’s furnishings,
EXO 31:8 8 the table and its equipment, the pure lampstand with all its equipment, the incense altar,
EXO 31:9 9 the altar for entirely burned offerings with all its equipment, the washbasin with its stand,
EXO 31:10 10 the woven clothing, the holy clothes for Aaron the priest and for his sons for their service as priests,
EXO 31:11 11 the anointing oil, and the sweet-smelling incense for the sanctuary. They will do just as I have commanded you.
EXO 31:12 12 The LORD said to Moses:
EXO 31:13 13 Tell the Israelites: “Be sure to keep my sabbaths, because the Sabbath is a sign between me and you in every generation so you will know that I am the LORD who makes you holy.
EXO 31:14 14 Keep the Sabbath, because it is holy for you. Everyone who violates the Sabbath will be put to death. Whoever does any work on the Sabbath, that person will be cut off from the people.
EXO 31:15 15 Do your work for six days. But the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest that is holy to the LORD . Whoever does any work on the Sabbath day will be put to death.
EXO 31:16 16 The Israelites should keep the Sabbath. They should observe the Sabbath in every generation as a covenant for all time.
EXO 31:17 17 It is a sign forever between me and the Israelites that in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day the LORD rested and was refreshed.”
EXO 31:18 18 When God finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, God gave him the two covenant tablets, the stone tablets written by God’s finger.
EXO 32:1 1 The people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain. They gathered around Aaron and said to him, “Come on! Make us gods who can lead us. As for this man Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we don’t have a clue what has happened to him.”
EXO 32:2 2 Aaron said to them, “All right, take out the gold rings from the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.”
EXO 32:3 3 So all the people took out the gold rings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.
EXO 32:4 4 He collected them and tied them up in a cloth. Then he made a metal image of a bull calf, and the people declared, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!”
EXO 32:5 5 When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf. Then Aaron announced, “Tomorrow will be a festival to the LORD !”
EXO 32:6 6 They got up early the next day and offered up entirely burned offerings and brought well-being sacrifices. The people sat down to eat and drink and then got up to celebrate.
EXO 32:7 7 The LORD spoke to Moses: “Hurry up and go down! Your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, are ruining everything!
EXO 32:8 8 They’ve already abandoned the path that I commanded. They have made a metal bull calf for themselves. They’ve bowed down to it and offered sacrifices to it and declared, ‘These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!’”
EXO 32:9 9 The LORD said to Moses, “I’ve been watching these people, and I’ve seen how stubborn they are.
EXO 32:10 10 Now leave me alone! Let my fury burn and devour them. Then I’ll make a great nation out of you.”
EXO 32:11 11 But Moses pleaded with the LORD his God, “ LORD , why does your fury burn against your own people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and amazing force?
EXO 32:12 12 Why should the Egyptians say, ‘He had an evil plan to take the people out and kill them in the mountains and so wipe them off the earth’? Calm down your fierce anger. Change your mind about doing terrible things to your own people.
EXO 32:13 13 Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants, whom you yourself promised, ‘I’ll make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky. And I’ve promised to give your descendants this whole land to possess for all time.’”
EXO 32:14 14 Then the LORD changed his mind about the terrible things he said he would do to his people.
EXO 32:15 15 Moses then turned around and came down the mountain. He carried the two covenant tablets in his hands. The tablets were written on both sides, front and back.
EXO 32:16 16 The tablets were God’s own work. What was written there was God’s own writing inscribed on the tablets.
EXO 32:17 17 When Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted, he said to Moses, “It sounds like war in the camp.”
EXO 32:18 18 But Moses said, “It isn’t the sound of a victory song. It isn’t the sound of a song of defeat. The sound of party songs is what I hear.”
EXO 32:19 19 When he got near the camp and saw the bull calf and the dancing, Moses was furious. He hurled the tablets down and shattered them in pieces at the foot of the mountain.
EXO 32:20 20 He took the calf that they had made and burned it in a fire. Then he ground it down to crushed powder, scattered it on the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
EXO 32:21 21 Moses said to Aaron, “What did these people do to you that you led them to commit such a terrible sin?”
EXO 32:22 22 Aaron replied, “Don’t get angry with me, sir. You know yourself that these people are out of control.
EXO 32:23 23 They said to me, ‘Make us gods who can lead us. As for this man Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we don’t have a clue what has happened to him.’
EXO 32:24 24 So I said to them, ‘Whoever has gold, take it off!’ So they gave it to me, I threw it into the fire, and out came this bull calf!”
EXO 32:25 25 Moses saw that the people were out of control because Aaron had let them get out of control, making them an easy target for their enemies.
EXO 32:26 26 So Moses stood at the camp’s gate and said, “Whoever is on the LORD ’s side, come to me!” All the Levites gathered around him.
EXO 32:27 27 Moses said to them, “This is what the LORD , Israel’s God, says: Each of you, strap on your sword! Go back and forth from one end of the camp to the other. Each of you, kill your brother, your friend, and your neighbor!”
EXO 32:28 28 The Levites did as Moses commanded. About three thousand people were killed that day.
EXO 32:29 29 Moses said, “Today you’ve been ordained to the LORD , each one of you at the cost of a son or a brother. Today you’ve gained a special blessing for yourselves.”
EXO 32:30 30 The next day Moses said to the people, “You’ve committed a terrible sin. So now I will go up to the LORD . Maybe I can arrange reconciliation on account of your sin.”
EXO 32:31 31 So Moses went back to the LORD and said, “Oh, what a terrible sin these people have committed! They made for themselves gods of gold.
EXO 32:32 32 But now, please forgive their sin! And if not, then wipe me out of your scroll that you’ve written.”
EXO 32:33 33 But the LORD said to Moses, “The ones I’ll wipe out of my scroll are those who sinned against me.
EXO 32:34 34 Now go and lead the people to the place I described to you. My messenger here will go in front of you. When the day of reckoning comes, I’ll count their sin against them.”
EXO 32:35 35 Then the LORD sent a plague on the people because of what they did with the bull calf that Aaron made.
EXO 33:1 1 The LORD said to Moses, “Go and leave this place, you and the people whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt. Go to the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I said, ‘I’ll give it to your descendants.’
EXO 33:2 2 I’ll send a messenger before you. I’ll drive out the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
EXO 33:3 3 Go to this land full of milk and honey. But I won’t go up with you because I would end up destroying you along the way since you are a stubborn people.”
EXO 33:4 4 When the people heard the bad news, they were sorry. No one put on any jewelry,
EXO 33:5 5 because the LORD had said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites, ‘You are a stubborn people. If I were to go up with you even for a single moment, I would destroy you. So now take off your jewelry, while I figure out what to do with you.’”
EXO 33:6 6 So after leaving Mount Horeb the Israelites rid themselves of their jewelry.
EXO 33:7 7 Moses took the tent and pitched it outside the camp, far away from the camp. He called it the meeting tent. Everyone who wanted advice from the LORD would go out to the meeting tent outside the camp.
EXO 33:8 8 Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand at the entrance to their tents and watch Moses until he had gone into the tent.
EXO 33:9 9 When Moses entered the tent, the column of cloud would come down and stand at the tent’s entrance while the LORD talked with Moses.
EXO 33:10 10 When all the people saw the column of cloud standing at the tent’s entrance, they would all rise and then bow down at the entrances to their tents.
