EXO 33:11 11 In this way the LORD used to speak to Moses face-to-face, like two people talking to each other. Then Moses would come back to the camp. But his young assistant Joshua, Nun’s son, wouldn’t leave the tent.
EXO 33:12 12 Moses said to the LORD , “Look, you’ve been telling me, ‘Lead these people forward.’ But you haven’t told me whom you will send with me. Yet you’ve assured me, ‘I know you by name and think highly of you.’
EXO 33:13 13 Now if you do think highly of me, show me your ways so that I may know you and so that you may really approve of me. Remember too that this nation is your people.”
EXO 33:14 14 The LORD replied, “I’ll go myself, and I’ll help you.”
EXO 33:15 15 Moses replied, “If you won’t go yourself, don’t make us leave here.
EXO 33:16 16 Because how will anyone know that we have your special approval, both I and your people, unless you go with us? Only that distinguishes us, me and your people, from every other people on the earth.”
EXO 33:17 17 The LORD said to Moses, “I’ll do exactly what you’ve asked because you have my special approval, and I know you by name.”
EXO 33:18 18 Moses said, “Please show me your glorious presence.”
EXO 33:19 19 The LORD said, “I’ll make all my goodness pass in front of you, and I’ll proclaim before you the name, ‘The LORD .’ I will be kind to whomever I wish to be kind, and I will have compassion to whomever I wish to be compassionate.
EXO 33:20 20 But,” the LORD said, “you can’t see my face because no one can see me and live.”
EXO 33:21 21 The LORD said, “Here is a place near me where you will stand beside the rock.
EXO 33:22 22 As my glorious presence passes by, I’ll set you in a gap in the rock, and I’ll cover you with my hand until I’ve passed by.
EXO 33:23 23 Then I’ll take away my hand, and you will see my back, but my face won’t be visible.”
EXO 34:1 1 The LORD said to Moses, “Cut two stone tablets like the first ones. I’ll write on these tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke into pieces.
EXO 34:2 2 Get ready in the morning and come up to Mount Sinai. Stand there on top of the mountain in front of me.
EXO 34:3 3 No one else can come up with you. Don’t allow anyone even to be seen anywhere on the mountain. Don’t even let sheep and cattle graze in front of the mountain.”
EXO 34:4 4 So Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones. He got up early in the morning and climbed up Mount Sinai, just as the LORD had commanded him. He carried the two stone tablets in his hands.
EXO 34:5 5 The LORD came down in the cloud and stood there with him, and proclaimed the name, “The LORD .”
EXO 34:6 6 The LORD passed in front of him and proclaimed: “The LORD ! The LORD ! a God who is compassionate and merciful, very patient, full of great loyalty and faithfulness,
EXO 34:7 7 showing great loyalty to a thousand generations, forgiving every kind of sin and rebellion, yet by no means clearing the guilty, punishing for their parents’ sins their children and their grandchildren, as well as the third and the fourth generation.”
EXO 34:8 8 At once Moses bowed to the ground and worshipped.
EXO 34:9 9 He said, “If you approve of me, my Lord, please go along with us. Although these are stubborn people, forgive our guilt and our sin and take us as your own possession.”
EXO 34:10 10 The LORD said: I now make a covenant. In front of all your people, I’ll perform dramatic displays of power that have never been done before anywhere on earth or in any nation. All the people who are around you will see what the LORD does, because I will do an awesome thing with you.
EXO 34:11 11 Be sure to obey what I command you today. I’m about to drive out before you the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
EXO 34:12 12 Be careful that you don’t make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land to which you are going, or it will become a dangerous trap for you.
EXO 34:13 13 You must tear down their altars, smash their sacred stone pillars, and cut down their sacred poles.
EXO 34:14 14 You must not bow down to another god, because the LORD is passionate: the LORD ’s name means “a passionate God.”
EXO 34:15 15 Don’t make a covenant with those who live in the land. When they prostitute themselves with their gods and sacrifice to their gods, they may invite you and you may end up eating some of the sacrifice.
EXO 34:16 16 Then you might go and choose their daughters as wives for your sons. And their daughters who prostitute themselves with their gods might lead your sons to prostitute themselves with their gods.
EXO 34:17 17 Don’t make metal gods for yourself.
EXO 34:18 18 Observe the Festival of Unleavened Bread. You should eat unleavened bread for seven days, as I commanded you, at the set time in the month of Abib, because it was in the month of Abib that you came out of Egypt.
EXO 34:19 19 Every first offspring is mine. That includes all your male livestock, the oldest offspring of cows and sheep.
EXO 34:20 20 But a donkey’s oldest offspring you may ransom with a sheep. Or if you don’t ransom it, you must break its neck. You should ransom all of your oldest sons. No one should appear before me empty-handed.
EXO 34:21 21 You should do your work for six days, but on the seventh day you should rest. Even during plowing or harvesttime you should rest.
EXO 34:22 22 You should observe the Festival of Weeks, for the early produce of the wheat harvest, and the Gathering Festival at the end of the year.
EXO 34:23 23 All your males should appear three times a year before the LORD God, Israel’s God.
EXO 34:24 24 I will drive out nations before you and extend your borders. No one will desire and try to take your land if you go up and appear before the LORD your God three times a year.
EXO 34:25 25 Don’t slaughter the blood of my sacrifice with anything leavened. The sacrifice of the Passover Festival shouldn’t be left over until the morning.
EXO 34:26 26 Bring the best of the early produce of your farmland to the LORD your God’s temple. Don’t boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
EXO 34:27 27 The LORD said to Moses: “Write down these words because by these words I hereby make a covenant with you and with Israel.”
EXO 34:28 28 Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights. He didn’t eat any bread or drink any water. He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten words.
EXO 34:29 29 Moses came down from Mount Sinai. As he came down from the mountain with the two covenant tablets in his hand, Moses didn’t realize that the skin of his face shone brightly because he had been talking with God.
EXO 34:30 30 When Aaron and all the Israelites saw the skin of Moses’ face shining brightly, they were afraid to come near him.
EXO 34:31 31 But Moses called them closer. So Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and Moses spoke with them.
EXO 34:32 32 After that, all the Israelites came near as well, and Moses commanded them everything that the LORD had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
EXO 34:33 33 When Moses finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
EXO 34:34 34 Whenever Moses went into the LORD ’s presence to speak with him, Moses would take the veil off until he came out again. When Moses came out and told the Israelites what he had been commanded,
EXO 34:35 35 the Israelites would see that the skin of Moses’ face was shining brightly. So Moses would put the veil on his face again until the next time he went in to speak with the LORD .

EXO 36:5 5 and say to Moses, “The people are contributing way too much material for doing the work that the LORD has commanded us to do.”

EXO 36:32 32 five bars for the boards on the other side of the dwelling, and five bars for the boards on the back wall of the dwelling on the west.

EXO 37:27 27 He made two gold rings, and he attached them under the molding on two opposite sides of the altar. They housed the poles used to carry it.
EXO 37:28 28 He made the poles of acacia wood, and he covered them with gold.
EXO 37:29 29 He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure sweet-smelling incense like a skilled perfume maker.
EXO 38:1 1 He made the altar for entirely burned offerings out of acacia wood. The altar was square, seven and a half feet long and seven and a half feet wide. It was four and a half feet high.
EXO 38:2 2 He made horns for it, one horn on each of its four corners. Its horns were attached to the altar, and he covered it with copper.
EXO 38:3 3 He made all the altar’s equipment: the pails, the shovels, the bowls, the meat forks, and the trays. He made all its equipment out of copper.
EXO 38:4 4 He made a grate for the altar of copper mesh underneath its bottom edge and extending halfway up to the middle of the altar.
EXO 38:5 5 He made four rings for each of the four corners of the copper grate to house the poles.
EXO 38:6 6 He made the poles out of acacia wood, and he covered them with copper.
EXO 38:7 7 He put the poles through the rings so that the poles were on the two sides of the altar when it was carried. He made the altar with planks but hollow inside.
EXO 38:8 8 He made the copper washbasin with its copper stand from the copper mirrors among the ranks of women assigned to the meeting tent’s entrance.
EXO 38:9 9 He also set up the courtyard. The courtyard’s south side had drapes of fine twisted linen stretching one hundred fifty feet
EXO 38:10 10 with twenty posts, twenty copper bases, and silver hooks and bands for the posts.
EXO 38:11 11 Likewise the north side stretched one hundred fifty feet, with twenty posts, twenty copper bases, and silver hooks and bands for the posts.
EXO 38:12 12 On the west side the drapes stretched seventy-five feet, with their ten posts, their ten bases, and silver hooks and bands for the posts.
EXO 38:13 13 The front side facing east was seventy-five feet.
EXO 38:14 14 There were twenty-two and a half feet of drapes on one side with three posts and three bases for them.
EXO 38:15 15 Likewise, there were twenty-two and a half feet of drapes on the other side of the plaza’s gate with three posts and three bases for them.
EXO 38:16 16 All the drapes around the courtyard were made of fine twisted linen.
EXO 38:17 17 The bases for the posts were made of copper, but the hooks for the posts and their bands were made of silver. The tops of the posts were covered with silver, and all the posts surrounding the courtyard had silver bands.
EXO 38:18 18 The screen for the gate into the courtyard was made with blue, purple, and deep red yarns and fine twisted linen, decorated with needlework. It was thirty feet long and, along the width of it, seven and a half feet high, corresponding to the courtyard’s drapes.
EXO 38:19 19 It had four posts, their four copper bases, their silver hooks, and their tops and bands covered with silver.
EXO 38:20 20 All the tent pegs for the dwelling and for the courtyard all around were made of copper.
EXO 38:21 21 These are the accounts of the dwelling, the covenant dwelling, that were recorded at Moses’ instructions. They are the work of the Levites, under the direction of Ithamar, Aaron the priest’s son.
EXO 38:22 22 Bezalel, Uri’s son and Hur’s grandson from the tribe of Judah, made everything that the LORD had commanded Moses to make.
EXO 38:23 23 Working with Bezalel was Oholiab, Ahisamach’s son from the tribe of Dan, who was a gem cutter, a designer, and a needleworker in blue, purple, and deep red yarns and in fine linen.
EXO 38:24 24 The total amount of the gold that was used for construction of the whole sanctuary, gold from the uplifted offerings, was twenty-nine kikkars and seven hundred thirty shekels in weight, measured by the sanctuary shekel.
EXO 38:25 25 The silver from the community census totaled one hundred kikkars and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels in weight, measured by the sanctuary shekel.
EXO 38:26 26 They gave a beqa per person (that is, half a shekel, measured by the sanctuary shekel) for everyone who was counted in the census, 20 years old and above, 603,550 men.
EXO 38:27 27 One hundred kikkars of silver were used to cast the bases for the sanctuary and the bases for the veil, one hundred bases from one hundred kikkars of silver, one kikkar for every base.
EXO 38:28 28 He used one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels of silver to make the hooks for the posts, cover their tops, and make bands for them.
EXO 38:29 29 The amount of copper from the uplifted offering was seventy kikkars and two thousand four hundred shekels in weight.
EXO 38:30 30 He used it to make the bases for the meeting tent’s entrance, the copper altar, its copper grate, and all the altar’s equipment,
EXO 38:31 31 the bases all around the courtyard, and the bases for the courtyard’s gate, all the dwelling’s tent pegs, and all the tent pegs used around the courtyard.
EXO 39:1 1 They used the blue, purple, and deep red yarns to make the woven clothing for those ministering as priests in the sanctuary. They made the holy clothes for Aaron as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 39:2 2 They made the vest of gold, of blue, purple, and deep red yarns, and of fine twisted linen.
EXO 39:3 3 They beat out thin sheets of gold and cut them into threads to work into designs among the blue, purple, and deep red yarns and the fine linen.
EXO 39:4 4 They made shoulder pieces for it attached to its two edges so that they could be joined together.
EXO 39:5 5 The vest’s belt was attached to it and made in the same way of gold, of blue, purple, and deep red yarns, and of fine twisted linen, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 39:6 6 They prepared the gemstones by mounting them in gold settings and engraving on them the names of Israel’s sons, like an official seal is engraved.
EXO 39:7 7 The stones were attached to the vest’s shoulder pieces as reminder stones for the Israelites, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 39:8 8 They made the embroidered chest pendant in the style of the vest, using gold, blue, purple, and deep red yarns, and fine twisted linen.
EXO 39:9 9 They made the chest pendant square and doubled, nine inches long and nine inches wide when doubled.
EXO 39:10 10 They set in it four rows of gemstones. The first row was a row of carnelian, topaz, and emerald stones.
EXO 39:11 11 The second row was a turquoise, a sapphire, and a moonstone.
EXO 39:12 12 The third row was a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
EXO 39:13 13 The fourth row was a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. The settings around them were decorative gold.
EXO 39:14 14 There were twelve stones with names corresponding to the names of Israel’s sons. They were engraved like official seals, each with its name for the twelve tribes.
EXO 39:15 15 They made chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, for the chest pendant.
EXO 39:16 16 They made two gold settings and two gold rings. They attached the two rings to the two edges of the chest pendant.
EXO 39:17 17 They attached the two gold cords to the two rings at the edges of the chest pendant.
EXO 39:18 18 Then they fastened the two ends of the two cords to the two gold settings and attached them to the front of the vest’s shoulder pieces.
EXO 39:19 19 They made two gold rings, and they attached them to the two edges of the chest pendant, on its inside edge facing the vest.
EXO 39:20 20 They made two gold rings and fastened them on the front of the lower part of the two shoulder pieces of the vest, at its seam just above the vest’s belt.
EXO 39:21 21 The chest pendant was held in place by a blue cord binding its rings to the vest’s rings so that the chest pendant rested on the vest’s belt and didn’t come loose from the vest, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 39:22 22 They also made the vest’s robe, woven completely in blue.
EXO 39:23 23 The opening of the robe in the middle of it was reinforced with a strong border so that it didn’t tear.
EXO 39:24 24 On the robe’s lower hem, they added pomegranates made of blue, purple, and deep red yarns and of fine twisted linen.
EXO 39:25 25 They also made pure gold bells and sewed the bells between the pomegranates, all around the robe’s lower hem,
EXO 39:26 26 with a bell and a pomegranate alternating all around the lower hem of the robe that is used for ministering as a priest, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 39:27 27 They also made the tunics woven out of fine linen for Aaron and his sons,
EXO 39:28 28 the turban of fine linen, the decorated turbans of fine linen, the linen undergarments of fine twisted linen,
EXO 39:29 29 the sashes of fine twisted linen, and of blue, purple, and crimson yarns, decorated with needlework, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 39:30 30 They made the flower ornament for the holy crown out of pure gold. Like the engraving on an official seal, they engraved on it the saying “Holy to the LORD .”
EXO 39:31 31 They fastened to it a blue cord to tie it to the top of the turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 39:32 32 In this way all the work of the meeting tent dwelling was finished. The Israelites did everything just exactly as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 39:33 33 Then they brought to Moses the dwelling, the tent, and all its equipment: its clasps, its boards, its bars, its posts, and its bases,
EXO 39:34 34 the covering of rams’ skins dyed red, the covering of beaded leather, and the veil for a screen,
EXO 39:35 35 the chest containing the covenant with its poles and the cover,
EXO 39:36 36 the table with all its equipment and the bread of the presence,
EXO 39:37 37 the pure lampstand with its lamps set on it and all its equipment, and the oil for the light,
EXO 39:38 38 the gold altar, the anointing oil, and the sweet-smelling incense, the screen for the tent’s entrance,
EXO 39:39 39 the copper altar and its copper grate, its poles, and all its equipment, the washbasin with its stand,
EXO 39:40 40 the courtyard’s drapes, its posts, and its bases, the screen for the plaza’s gate, its cords, and its tent pegs, and all the other equipment for the service of the dwelling, for the meeting tent,
EXO 39:41 41 the woven clothes for ministering as priests in the sanctuary, the holy clothes for the priest Aaron and the clothes for his sons to serve as priests.
EXO 39:42 42 The Israelites did all of the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 39:43 43 When Moses saw that they in fact had done all the work exactly as the LORD had commanded, Moses blessed them.
EXO 40:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses:
EXO 40:2 2 Set up the meeting tent dwelling on the first day of the first month.
EXO 40:3 3 Place the chest containing the covenant inside the dwelling. Hide the chest from view with the veil.
EXO 40:4 4 Bring in the table and arrange its items. Bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
EXO 40:5 5 Place the gold altar for burning incense in front of the chest containing the covenant. Set up the screen at the dwelling’s entrance.
EXO 40:6 6 Put the altar for entirely burned offerings in front of the entrance to the meeting tent dwelling.
EXO 40:7 7 Put the washbasin between the meeting tent and the altar and put water in it.
EXO 40:8 8 Set up the courtyard all around. Hang up the screen at the courtyard gate.
EXO 40:9 9 Then take the anointing oil and anoint the dwelling and everything in it. Make holy the dwelling and all its equipment, and it will be holy.
EXO 40:10 10 Anoint the altar for entirely burned offerings and all its equipment. Make the altar holy, and the altar will be most holy.
EXO 40:11 11 Anoint the washbasin with its stand and make it holy.
EXO 40:12 12 Then bring Aaron and his sons to the meeting tent’s entrance and wash them with water.
EXO 40:13 13 Dress Aaron in the holy clothes. Anoint him and make him holy so that he may serve me as priest.
EXO 40:14 14 Then bring his sons and dress them in tunics.
EXO 40:15 15 Anoint them like you anointed their father so that they may serve me as priests. Their anointing is to the priesthood for all time in every generation.
EXO 40:16 16 Moses did everything exactly as the LORD had commanded him.
EXO 40:17 17 In the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, the dwelling was set up.
EXO 40:18 18 Moses set up the dwelling. He laid out its bases. He set up its boards, inserted its bars, and raised up its posts.
EXO 40:19 19 He spread the tent out over the dwelling, and he put the covering of the tent over it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 40:20 20 He took the covenant document and placed it inside the chest. He put the poles on the chest, and he set the cover on top of the chest.
EXO 40:21 21 He brought the chest into the dwelling. He set up the veil as a screen to hide from view the chest containing the covenant, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 40:22 22 He placed the table in the meeting tent, on the north side of the dwelling, outside the veil.
EXO 40:23 23 He set the bread in its proper place on the table in the LORD ’s presence, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 40:24 24 He put the lampstand in the meeting tent, opposite the table on the south side of the dwelling.
EXO 40:25 25 He set up the lamps in the LORD ’s presence, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 40:26 26 He put the gold altar in the meeting tent in front of the veil.
EXO 40:27 27 He burned sweet-smelling incense on it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 40:28 28 He also set up the screen at the entrance to the dwelling.
EXO 40:29 29 He placed the altar for entirely burned offerings at the entrance to the meeting tent dwelling. He offered the entirely burned offering and the grain offering on it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 40:30 30 He put the washbasin between the meeting tent and the altar, and put water in it for washing.
EXO 40:31 31 Moses, Aaron, and his sons used it to wash their hands and their feet.
EXO 40:32 32 Whenever they went into the meeting tent and whenever they approached the altar, they washed themselves, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
EXO 40:33 33 He set up the courtyard around the dwelling and the altar, and he hung up the screen at the courtyard’s gate. When Moses had finished all the work,
EXO 40:34 34 the cloud covered the meeting tent and the LORD ’s glorious presence filled the dwelling.
EXO 40:35 35 Moses couldn’t enter the meeting tent because the cloud had settled on it, and the LORD ’s glorious presence filled the dwelling.
EXO 40:36 36 Whenever the cloud rose from the dwelling, the Israelites would set out on their journeys.
EXO 40:37 37 But if the cloud didn’t rise, then they didn’t set out until the day it rose.
EXO 40:38 38 The LORD ’s cloud stayed over the dwelling during the day, with lightning in it at night, clearly visible to the whole household of Israel at every stage of their journey.
LEV 1:1 1 Then the LORD called to Moses and said to him from the meeting tent,
LEV 1:2 2 Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When any of you present a livestock offering to the LORD , you can present it from either the herd or the flock.
LEV 1:3 3 If the offering is an entirely burned offering from the herd, you must present a flawless male, bringing it to the meeting tent’s entrance for its acceptance before the LORD .
LEV 1:4 4 You must press your hand on the head of the entirely burned offering so that it will be accepted for you, to make reconciliation for you.
LEV 1:5 5 Then you will slaughter the bull before the LORD . Aaron’s sons the priests will present the blood and toss it against every side of the altar at the meeting tent’s entrance.
LEV 1:6 6 Then the entirely burned offering will be skinned and cut up into pieces.
LEV 1:7 7 The sons of Aaron the priest will light the altar and lay wood on the fire.
LEV 1:8 8 Then Aaron’s sons the priests will arrange the pieces, the head, and the fat on the wood that is on the altar fire,
LEV 1:9 9 but the animal’s insides and lower legs must be washed with water. The priest will then completely burn all of it on the altar as an entirely burned offering, a food gift of soothing smell to the LORD .
LEV 1:10 10 If the offering is an entirely burned offering from the flock—whether sheep or goat—you must present a flawless male.
LEV 1:11 11 You must slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD . Aaron’s sons the priests will toss its blood against every side of the altar.
LEV 1:12 12 Once it has been cut into pieces, including the head and the fat, the priest will arrange these out on the wood that is on the altar fire,
LEV 1:13 13 but its insides and lower legs must be washed with water. Then the priest will present all of it and completely burn it on the altar. It is an entirely burned offering, a food gift of soothing smell to the LORD .
LEV 1:14 14 If the offering for the LORD is an entirely burned offering from the birds, you can present your offering from the doves or pigeons.
LEV 1:15 15 The priest will bring it to the altar. He will tear off its head and completely burn it on the altar. Its blood will be drained against the side of the altar.
LEV 1:16 16 Then the priest will remove its throat along with its contents and throw it by the east side of the altar, into the place for the ashes.
LEV 1:17 17 He will then tear the bird open by its wings, without splitting it. The priest will completely burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the altar fire. It is an entirely burned offering, a food gift of soothing smell to the LORD .
LEV 2:1 1 When anyone presents a grain offering to the LORD , the offering must be of choice flour. They must pour oil on it and put frankincense on it,
LEV 2:2 2 then bring it to Aaron’s sons, the priests. A priest will take a handful of its choice flour and oil, along with all of its frankincense, and will completely burn this token portion on the altar as a food gift of soothing smell to the LORD .
LEV 2:3 3 The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons as a most holy portion from the LORD ’s food gifts.
LEV 2:4 4 When you present a grain offering baked in an oven, it must be of choice flour: unleavened flatbread mixed with oil or unleavened wafers spread with oil.
LEV 2:5 5 If your offering is grain prepared on a griddle, it must be of choice flour mixed with oil and it must be unleavened.
LEV 2:6 6 Crumble it into pieces and pour oil on it; it is a grain offering.
LEV 2:7 7 If your offering is grain prepared in a pan, it must be made of choice flour with oil.
LEV 2:8 8 You will bring the grain offering made in one of these ways to the LORD , presenting it to the priest, who will then bring it to the altar.
LEV 2:9 9 The priest will remove from the grain offering the token portion and completely burn it on the altar as a food gift of soothing smell to the LORD .
LEV 2:10 10 The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons as a most holy portion from the LORD ’s food gifts.
LEV 2:11 11 No grain offering that you give to the LORD can be made with yeast. You must not completely burn any yeast or honey as a food gift for the LORD .
LEV 2:12 12 You can present those as first-choice offerings to the LORD , but they must not be entirely burned up on the altar as a soothing smell.
LEV 2:13 13 You must season all your grain offerings with salt. Do not omit the salt of your God’s covenant from your grain offering. You must offer salt with all your offerings.
LEV 2:14 14 If you present a grain offering to the LORD from the first produce, you must make such an offering from the crushed heads of newly ripe grain, roasted with fire.
LEV 2:15 15 You must put oil and frankincense on it; it is a grain offering.
LEV 2:16 16 The priest will completely burn the token portion—some of the crushed new grain and oil along with all of the frankincense—as a food gift for the LORD .
LEV 3:1 1 If the offering is a communal sacrifice of well-being, the one who offers the herd animal—whether it is male or female—must present a flawless specimen before the LORD .
LEV 3:2 2 You must press your hand on the head of the offering and slaughter it at the meeting tent’s entrance. Aaron’s sons the priests will toss the blood against every side of the altar.
LEV 3:3 3 Then you can offer a food gift to the LORD from the communal sacrifice of well-being: the fat that covers and surrounds the insides;
LEV 3:4 4 the two kidneys and the fat around them at the loins; and the lobe on the liver, which should be removed with the kidneys.
LEV 3:5 5 Aaron’s sons will completely burn all of this on the altar—along with the entirely burned offering on the wood that is on the altar fire—as a food gift of soothing smell to the LORD .
LEV 3:6 6 If the offering for a communal sacrifice of well-being for the LORD is from the flock—whether it is male or female—you must present a flawless specimen.
LEV 3:7 7 If you present a sheep as the offering, you must present it before the LORD .
LEV 3:8 8 You must press your hand on the head of the offering and slaughter it before the meeting tent. Aaron’s sons will toss the blood against every side of the altar.
LEV 3:9 9 Then you may offer the fat from the communal sacrifice of well-being as a food gift for the LORD : the whole fat tail, which should be removed close to the tailbone; the fat that covers and surrounds the insides;
LEV 3:10 10 the two kidneys and the fat around them at the loins; and the lobe on the liver, which should be removed with the kidneys.
LEV 3:11 11 The priest will then completely burn all of this on the altar as food—as a food gift for the LORD .
LEV 3:12 12 If the offering is a goat, you must present it before the LORD .
LEV 3:13 13 You must press your hand on its head and slaughter it before the meeting tent. Aaron’s sons will toss its blood against every side of the altar.
LEV 3:14 14 Then you may present as your offering—a food gift for the LORD —the fat that covers and surrounds the insides;
LEV 3:15 15 the two kidneys and the fat around them at the loins; and the lobe on the liver, which should be removed with the kidneys.
LEV 3:16 16 The priest will then completely burn all of this on the altar as food—as a food gift for a soothing smell. All fat belongs to the LORD .
LEV 3:17 17 This is a permanent rule for your future generations, wherever you live: you must not eat any fat or blood.
LEV 4:1 1 The LORD said to Moses,
LEV 4:2 2 Say to the Israelites: Do the following whenever someone sins unintentionally against any of the LORD ’s commands, doing something that shouldn’t be done:
LEV 4:3 3 If it is the anointed priest who has sinned, making the people guilty of sin, he must present to the LORD a flawless bull from the herd as a purification offering for the sin he has committed.
LEV 4:4 4 He will bring the bull before the LORD at the entrance to the meeting tent and press his hand on the bull’s head. Then he will slaughter the bull before the LORD .
LEV 4:5 5 The anointed priest will take some of the bull’s blood and take it into the meeting tent.
LEV 4:6 6 The priest will dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle some of it seven times before the LORD , toward the sanctuary’s inner curtain.
LEV 4:7 7 Then the priest will put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of perfumed incense, which is in the meeting tent before the LORD . But he will pour out all the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of entirely burned offerings, which is at the meeting tent’s entrance.
LEV 4:8 8 Then he will remove all the fat from the bull for the purification offering: the fat that covers and surrounds the insides;
LEV 4:9 9 the two kidneys and the fat around them at the loins; and the lobe on the liver, which he will remove with the kidneys,
LEV 4:10 10 just as this is removed from the ox for the communal sacrifice of well-being. Then the priest will completely burn these on the altar of entirely burned offerings.
LEV 4:11 11 But the bull’s hide and all of its flesh, along with its head, lower legs, entrails, and dung—
LEV 4:12 12 all that remains of the bull—will be taken to a clean location outside the camp, to the ash heap. It should be burned there at the ash heap on a wood fire.
LEV 4:13 13 If it is the entire Israelite community that has done something wrong unintentionally and the deed escapes the assembly’s notice—but they’ve done something that shouldn’t be done in violation of the LORD ’s commands, becoming guilty of sin—
LEV 4:14 14 once the sin that they committed becomes known, the assembly must present a bull from the herd as a purification offering. They will bring it before the meeting tent.
LEV 4:15 15 The community elders will press their hands on the bull’s head before the LORD and then slaughter it before the LORD .
LEV 4:16 16 The anointed priest will take some of the bull’s blood into the meeting tent.
LEV 4:17 17 The priest will dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD toward the inner curtain.
LEV 4:18 18 Then he will put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that is before the LORD in the meeting tent. But he will pour all the rest of the blood out at the base of the altar of entirely burned offerings that is at the meeting tent’s entrance.
LEV 4:19 19 Then he will remove all the fat from it and completely burn it on the altar.
LEV 4:20 20 He will do the same with this bull as he did with the other bull for the purification offering; that is exactly what he must do. In this way, the priest will make reconciliation for them, and they will be forgiven.
LEV 4:21 21 Then the priest will take the bull outside the camp and burn it, just as the first bull was burned. It is the purification offering for the assembly.
LEV 4:22 22 If a leader sins by unintentionally breaking any of the commands of the LORD his God, doing something that shouldn’t be done, and becomes guilty of sin—
LEV 4:23 23 once the sin that he committed is made known to him—he must bring as his offering a flawless male goat.
LEV 4:24 24 He will press his hand on the goat’s head. It will be slaughtered at the place where an entirely burned offering would be slaughtered before the LORD . It is a purification offering.
LEV 4:25 25 The priest will take some of the blood from the purification offering and, using his finger, will put it on the horns of the altar of entirely burned offerings. But he will pour the rest of the blood out at the base of the altar of entirely burned offerings.
LEV 4:26 26 He will completely burn all of its fat on the altar just as the fat of the communal sacrifice of well-being is burned. In this way the priest will make reconciliation for the leader to remove his sin, and he will be forgiven.
LEV 4:27 27 If any ordinary person sins unintentionally by breaking one of the LORD ’s commands, doing something that shouldn’t be done, and becomes guilty of sin—
LEV 4:28 28 once the sin they committed is made known to them—they must bring as their offering a flawless female goat because of the sin that was committed.
LEV 4:29 29 They will press their hand on the head of the purification offering. It will be slaughtered at the place for the entirely burned offerings.
LEV 4:30 30 The priest will take some of its blood and, using his finger, will put it on the horns of the altar of entirely burned offerings. But he will pour all the rest of the blood out at the base of the altar.
LEV 4:31 31 He will remove all of its fat, just as the fat from a communal sacrifice of well-being is removed. Then the priest will completely burn it on the altar as a soothing smell to the LORD . In this way, the priest will make reconciliation for them, and they will be forgiven.
LEV 4:32 32 If you offer a sheep as a purification offering, it must be a flawless female.
LEV 4:33 33 You must press your hand on the head of the purification offering. It will be slaughtered as a purification offering in the place where the entirely burned offering is slaughtered.
LEV 4:34 34 Then the priest will take some of the blood from the purification offering and, using his finger, will put it on the horns of the altar of entirely burned offerings. But he will pour all the rest of the blood out at the base of the altar.
LEV 4:35 35 He will remove all of its fat, just as the fat of a sheep would be removed from the communal sacrifice of well-being. Then the priest will completely burn it on the altar along with the LORD ’s food gifts. In this way, the priest will make reconciliation for you for the sin you committed, and you will be forgiven.
LEV 5:1 1 If you sin: by not providing information after hearing a public solemn pledge even though you are a witness, knowing something, or having seen something so that you become liable to punishment;
LEV 5:2 2 or by touching some unclean thing—the dead body of an unclean wild animal, unclean livestock, or unclean swarming creature—but the fact goes unknown so that you become unclean and guilty of sin;
LEV 5:3 3 or by touching human uncleanness—any uncleanness that makes one unclean—and the fact goes unknown, but you later learn of it and become guilty of sin;
LEV 5:4 4 or by carelessly swearing to do something, whether bad or good—whatever one might swear carelessly—and the fact goes unknown, but you later learn of it and become guilty of sin concerning one of these things—
LEV 5:5 5 at that point, when you have become guilty of sin in one of these ways, you must confess how you have sinned
LEV 5:6 6 and bring to the LORD as compensation for the sin that was committed a female from the flock, either a sheep or goat, as a purification offering. The priest will then make reconciliation for you, to remove your sin.
LEV 5:7 7 If you can’t afford an animal from the flock, you can bring to the LORD as compensation for your sin two doves or two pigeons, one as a purification offering and the other as an entirely burned offering.
LEV 5:8 8 You will bring them to the priest, who will first present the one for the purification offering. He will pinch off its head at the back of its neck without splitting it.
LEV 5:9 9 Then he will sprinkle some of the blood of the purification offering on the side of the altar. The rest of the blood will be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a purification offering.
LEV 5:10 10 Then, with the second bird, the priest will perform an entirely burned offering according to the regulation. In this way, the priest will make reconciliation for you because of the sin you committed, and you will be forgiven.
LEV 5:11 11 If you cannot afford two doves or two pigeons, you can bring as the offering for your sin a tenth of an ephah of choice flour as a purification offering. You must not put any oil on it, nor any frankincense, because it is a purification offering.
LEV 5:12 12 You will bring it to the priest, and the priest will take a handful from it—the token portion—and will burn it completely on the altar along with the food gifts for the LORD . It is a purification offering.
LEV 5:13 13 In this way, the priest will make reconciliation for you for whichever one of the sins you committed, and you will be forgiven. The rest of the offering will belong to the priest like the grain offering.
LEV 5:14 14 The LORD said to Moses,
LEV 5:15 15 Whenever you commit wrongdoing, unintentionally sinning against any of the LORD ’s holy things, you must bring to the LORD as your compensation a flawless ram from the flock, its value calculated in silver shekels according to the sanctuary’s shekel, as a compensation offering.
LEV 5:16 16 You will make amends for the way you have sinned against the holy thing: you will add one-fifth to its value and give it to the priest. Then the priest will make reconciliation for you with the ram for the compensation offering, and you will be forgiven.
LEV 5:17 17 If you sin by breaking any of the LORD ’s commands, but without realizing it, doing something that shouldn’t be done, and then become guilty and liable to punishment,
LEV 5:18 18 you must bring a flawless ram from the flock, at the standard value, as a compensation offering to the priest. The priest will make reconciliation for you for the unintentional fault that you committed, even though you didn’t realize it, and you will be forgiven.
LEV 5:19 19 It is a compensation offering. You have definitely become guilty before the LORD .
LEV 6:1 1 The LORD said to Moses,
LEV 6:2 2 If you sin: by acting unfaithfully against the LORD ; by deceiving a fellow citizen concerning a deposit or pledged property; by cheating a fellow citizen through robbery;
LEV 6:3 3 or, though you’ve found lost property, you lie about it; or by swearing falsely about anything that someone might do and so sin,
LEV 6:4 4 at that point, once you have sinned and become guilty of sin, you must return the property you took by robbery or fraud, or the deposit that was left with you for safekeeping, or the lost property that you found,
LEV 6:5 5 or whatever it was that you swore falsely about. You must make amends for the principal amount and add one-fifth to it. You must give it to the owner on the day you become guilty.
LEV 6:6 6 You must bring to the priest as your compensation to the LORD a flawless ram from the flock at the standard value as a compensation offering.
LEV 6:7 7 The priest will make reconciliation for you before the LORD , and you will be forgiven for anything you may have done that made you guilty.
LEV 6:8 8 The LORD said to Moses:
LEV 6:9 9 Command Aaron and his sons: This is the Instruction for the entirely burned offering—the entirely burned offering that must remain on the altar hearth all night until morning, while the fire is kept burning.
LEV 6:10 10 The priest will dress in his linen robe, with linen undergarments on his body. Because the fire will have devoured the entirely burned offering on the altar, he must remove the ashes and place them beside the altar.
LEV 6:11 11 The priest will then take off his clothes, dress in a different set of clothes, and take the ashes outside the camp to a clean location.
LEV 6:12 12 The altar fire must be kept burning; it must not go out. Each morning the priest will burn wood on it, will lay out the entirely burned offering on it, and will completely burn the fat of the well-being offering on it.
LEV 6:13 13 A continuous fire must be kept burning on the altar; it must not go out.
LEV 6:14 14 This is the Instruction for the grain offering: Aaron’s sons will present it before the LORD in front of the altar.
LEV 6:15 15 The priest will remove a handful of the choice flour and oil from the grain offering, and all of the frankincense that is on it, and burn this token portion completely on the altar as a soothing smell to the LORD .
LEV 6:16 16 Aaron and his sons will eat the rest of it. It must be eaten as unleavened bread in a holy place; the priests must eat it in the meeting tent’s courtyard.
LEV 6:17 17 It must not be baked with leaven. I have made it the priests’ share from my food gifts. It is most holy like the purification offering and the compensation offering.
LEV 6:18 18 Only the males from Aaron’s descendants can eat it as a permanent portion from the LORD ’s food gifts throughout your future generations. Anything that touches these food gifts will become holy.
LEV 6:19 19 The LORD said to Moses,
LEV 6:20 20 This is the offering that Aaron and his sons must present to the LORD on the day of his anointment: one-tenth of an ephah of choice flour as a regular grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
LEV 6:21 21 It must be prepared on a griddle with oil. You must bring it thoroughly mixed up and must present it as a grain offering of crumbled pieces as a soothing smell to the LORD .
LEV 6:22 22 The priest who is anointed from among Aaron’s sons to succeed him will prepare the offering as a permanent portion for the LORD . It will be completely burned as a complete offering.
LEV 6:23 23 Every priestly grain offering must be a complete offering; it must not be eaten.
LEV 6:24 24 The LORD said to Moses,
LEV 6:25 25 Say to Aaron and his sons: This is the Instruction for the purification offering: The purification offering must be slaughtered before the LORD at the same place the entirely burned offering is slaughtered; it is most holy.
LEV 6:26 26 The priest who offers it as a purification offering will eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place, in the meeting tent’s courtyard.
LEV 6:27 27 Anything that touches the purification offering’s flesh will become holy. If some of its blood splashes on a garment, you must wash the bloodied part in a holy place.
LEV 6:28 28 A pottery container in which the purification offering is cooked must be broken, but if it is cooked in a bronze container, that must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
LEV 6:29 29 Any male priest can eat it; it is most holy.
LEV 6:30 30 But no purification offering can be eaten if blood from it is brought into the meeting tent to make reconciliation in the holy place; it must be burned with fire.
LEV 7:1 1 This is the Instruction for the compensation offering: It is most holy.
LEV 7:2 2 The compensation offering must be slaughtered at the same place where the entirely burned offering is slaughtered, and its blood must be tossed against all sides of the altar.
LEV 7:3 3 All of its fat will be offered: the fat tail; the fat that covers the insides;
LEV 7:4 4 the two kidneys and the fat around them at the loins; and the lobe on the liver, which must be removed with the kidneys.
LEV 7:5 5 The priest must burn them completely on the altar as a food gift for the LORD ; it is a compensation offering.
LEV 7:6 6 Any male priest can eat it. It must be eaten in a holy place; it is most holy.
LEV 7:7 7 The compensation offering is like the purification offering—they share the same Instruction: It belongs to the priest who makes reconciliation with it.
LEV 7:8 8 The hide of the entirely burned offering that a priest has offered belongs to the priest who offered it.
LEV 7:9 9 Any grain offering that is baked in an oven or that is prepared in a pan or on a griddle also belongs to the priest who offered it.
LEV 7:10 10 But every other grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, will belong to all of Aaron’s sons equally.
LEV 7:11 11 This is the Instruction for the communal sacrifice of well-being that someone may offer to the LORD :
LEV 7:12 12 If you are offering it for thanksgiving, you must offer the following with the communal sacrifice of thanksgiving: unleavened flatbread mixed with oil, unleavened thin loaves spread with oil, and flatbread of choice flour thoroughly mixed with oil.
LEV 7:13 13 You must present this offering, plus the leavened flatbread, with the communal thanksgiving sacrifice of well-being.
LEV 7:14 14 From this you will present one of each kind of offering as a gift to the LORD . It will belong to the priest who tosses the blood of the well-being offering.
LEV 7:15 15 The flesh of your communal thanksgiving sacrifice of well-being must be eaten on the day you offer it; you cannot save any of it until morning.
LEV 7:16 16 But if your communal sacrifice of well-being is payment for a solemn promise or if it is a spontaneous gift, it may be eaten on the day you offer it as your communal sacrifice, and whatever is left over can be eaten the next day.
LEV 7:17 17 But whatever is left over of the flesh of the communal sacrifice on the third day must be burned with fire.
LEV 7:18 18 If any of it is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who offered it. It will be considered foul, and the person who eats of it will be liable to punishment.
LEV 7:19 19 Flesh that touches any unclean thing must not be eaten; it must be burned with fire. Any clean person may eat the flesh,
LEV 7:20 20 but anyone who eats the flesh of a communal sacrifice of well-being that belongs to the LORD while in an unclean state will be cut off from their people.
LEV 7:21 21 Whenever anyone touches any unclean thing—whether it is human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean and disgusting creature—and then eats the flesh of a communal sacrifice of well-being that belongs to the LORD , that person will be cut off from their people.
LEV 7:22 22 The LORD said to Moses:
LEV 7:23 23 Tell the Israelites: You must not eat the fat of an ox, sheep, or goat.
LEV 7:24 24 The fat of an animal that has died naturally or the fat of an animal that was killed by another animal may be put to any use, but you must definitely not eat it.
LEV 7:25 25 If anyone eats the fat of an animal from which a food gift could be offered to the LORD , that person will be cut off from their people.
LEV 7:26 26 You must not consume any blood whatsoever—whether bird or animal blood—wherever you may live.
LEV 7:27 27 Any person who consumes any blood whatsoever will be cut off from their people.
LEV 7:28 28 The LORD said to Moses:
LEV 7:29 29 Say to the Israelites: If you wish to offer a communal sacrifice of well-being to the LORD , you are allowed to bring your offering to the LORD as your communal sacrifice of well-being.
LEV 7:30 30 Your own hands must bring the LORD ’s food gifts. You will bring the fat with the breast so that the breast can be lifted as an uplifted offering before the LORD .
LEV 7:31 31 The priest will completely burn the fat on the altar, but the breast will go to Aaron and his sons.
LEV 7:32 32 You will give the right thigh of your communal sacrifice of well-being to the priest as a gift.
LEV 7:33 33 The right thigh will belong to the son of Aaron who offers the blood and fat of the well-being offering.
LEV 7:34 34 I have taken the breast of the uplifted offering and the thigh that is given by the Israelites from their communal sacrifices of well-being, and have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as a permanent portion from the Israelites.
LEV 7:35 35 This is what Aaron and his sons are allotted from the LORD ’s food gifts once they have been presented to serve the LORD as priests.
LEV 7:36 36 The LORD commanded that these things be given to the priests by the Israelites, following their anointment. It is their permanent portion throughout their future generations.
LEV 7:37 37 This concludes the Instructions for the entirely burned offering, the grain offering, the purification offering, the compensation offering, the ordination offering, and the communal sacrifice of well-being,
LEV 7:38 38 which the LORD commanded Moses at Mount Sinai on the day when he ordered the Israelites to present their offerings to the LORD , in the Sinai desert.
LEV 8:1 1 The LORD said to Moses,
LEV 8:2 2 Take Aaron and his sons with him, the priestly clothing, the anointing oil, a bull for the purification offering, two rams, and a basket of unleavened bread,
LEV 8:3 3 and assemble the whole community at the meeting tent’s entrance.
LEV 8:4 4 Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the community assembled at the meeting tent’s entrance.
LEV 8:5 5 Moses said to the community, “This is what the LORD has commanded us to do.”
LEV 8:6 6 Then Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them in water.
LEV 8:7 7 Moses put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around him, and dressed him in the robe. Moses then put the priestly vest on Aaron, tied the woven waistband of the vest around him, and secured the vest to him with it.
LEV 8:8 8 Then Moses placed the chest piece on Aaron and set the Urim and Thummim into the chest piece.
LEV 8:9 9 Moses placed the turban on Aaron’s head and put the gold flower ornament, the holy crown, on the turban’s front, just as the LORD had commanded him.
LEV 8:10 10 Moses then took the anointing oil and anointed the dwelling and everything in it, making them holy by doing so.
LEV 8:11 11 He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its equipment, as well as the basin and its base, to make them holy.
LEV 8:12 12 He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, thereby anointing him to make him holy.
LEV 8:13 13 Then Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, dressed them in tunics, tied sashes around them, and wrapped headbands on them, just as the LORD had commanded him.
LEV 8:14 14 Next Moses brought forward the bull for the purification offering. Aaron and his sons pressed their hands on its head.
LEV 8:15 15 Moses slaughtered it, then took the blood and, using his finger, put it on all of the altar’s horns, purifying the altar. He poured the rest of the blood out at the altar’s base. Then he made the altar holy so that reconciliation could be performed on it.
LEV 8:16 16 Moses removed all the fat that was around the insides, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and their fat, and he completely burned it on the altar.
LEV 8:17 17 But the rest of the bull, including its hide, its flesh, and its dung, he burned with fire outside the camp just as the LORD had commanded him.
LEV 8:18 18 Then Moses presented the ram for the entirely burned offering, and Aaron and his sons pressed their hands on its head.
LEV 8:19 19 Moses slaughtered it, then tossed the blood against all sides of the altar.
LEV 8:20 20 He cut up the ram into pieces, and then completely burned the head, pieces, and fat.
LEV 8:21 21 After he washed the insides and lower legs with water, Moses completely burned the whole ram on the altar. It was an entirely burned offering for a soothing smell; it was a food gift for the LORD , as the LORD had commanded Moses.
LEV 8:22 22 Moses then presented the second ram, the ram for ordination, and Aaron and his sons pressed their hands on its head.
LEV 8:23 23 Moses slaughtered it, then took some of its blood and put it on Aaron’s right earlobe, on his right thumb, and on his right big toe.
LEV 8:24 24 Then Moses brought forward Aaron’s sons and put some of the blood on their right earlobes, their right thumbs, and their right big toes. Moses tossed the rest of the blood against all of the altar’s sides.
LEV 8:25 25 Then he took the fat—the fat tail, all the fat that was around the insides, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and their fat—as well as the right thigh.
LEV 8:26 26 From the basket of unleavened bread that was before the LORD , he took one loaf of unleavened flatbread, one loaf of flatbread made with oil, and one unleavened wafer, and he placed these on the fat pieces and on the right thigh.
LEV 8:27 27 Moses set all of this in Aaron’s and his sons’ hands, then lifted them as an uplifted offering before the LORD .
LEV 8:28 28 Next Moses took this out of their hands and completely burned it on the altar, along with the entirely burned offering. This was an ordination offering for a soothing smell; it was a food gift for the LORD .
LEV 8:29 29 Next Moses took the breast from the ram for the ordination offering and lifted it as an uplifted offering before the LORD . It belonged to Moses as his portion, just as the LORD had commanded him.
LEV 8:30 30 Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that was on the altar and sprinkled it on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes as well. In this way, Moses made holy Aaron, his clothing, and Aaron’s sons and their clothing.
LEV 8:31 31 Moses said to Aaron and his sons: “Cook the meat at the meeting tent’s entrance. You may eat it there along with the bread that is in the basket of the ordination offering, just as I was commanded, ‘Aaron and his sons can eat it.’
LEV 8:32 32 But you must burn whatever is left over of the meat and bread with fire.
LEV 8:33 33 You must not leave the meeting tent’s entrance for seven days, until the period of your ordination is completed, because your ordination takes seven days.
LEV 8:34 34 What was done today was commanded by the LORD , to make reconciliation for you.
LEV 8:35 35 You must stay at the meeting tent’s entrance for seven days, day and night, observing the LORD ’s requirement so you don’t die, because that’s what I was commanded.”
LEV 8:36 36 Aaron and his sons did everything the LORD commanded through Moses.
LEV 9:1 1 On the eighth day, Moses called for Aaron, Aaron’s sons, and Israel’s elders.
LEV 9:2 2 He said to Aaron, “Take a young bull from the herd as a purification offering and a ram as an entirely burned offering, both flawless animals, and bring them before the LORD .
LEV 9:3 3 Then tell the Israelites, ‘Take a male goat as a purification offering; a young bull and a sheep—both one-year-old flawless animals—as an entirely burned offering;
LEV 9:4 4 an ox and a ram as a well-being sacrifice before the LORD ; and a grain offering mixed with oil, because today the LORD will appear to you.’”
LEV 9:5 5 They brought what Moses had commanded to the front of the meeting tent. Then the whole community came forward and stood before the LORD .
LEV 9:6 6 Moses said, “The LORD has ordered you to do this so that the LORD ’s glorious presence will appear to you.”
LEV 9:7 7 Moses said to Aaron, “Come up to the altar and perform your purification offering and your entirely burned offering, making reconciliation for yourself and the people. Then perform the people’s offering in order to make reconciliation for them, just as the LORD commanded.”
LEV 9:8 8 Aaron went to the altar and slaughtered the young bull for his purification offering.
LEV 9:9 9 Then Aaron’s sons presented the blood to him, and he dipped his finger into the blood and put it on the altar’s horns. He poured the rest of the blood out at the altar’s base.
LEV 9:10 10 He completely burned on the altar the fat, kidneys, and lobe of the liver from the purification offering, just as the LORD commanded Moses.
LEV 9:11 11 But he burned the flesh and hide with fire outside the camp.
LEV 9:12 12 Then Aaron slaughtered the entirely burned offering. Aaron’s sons handed him the blood, and he tossed it against all sides of the altar.
LEV 9:13 13 They handed him the entirely burned offering in pieces, including the head, and he completely burned them on the altar.
LEV 9:14 14 Then he washed the insides and lower legs and completely burned them on the altar along with the rest of the entirely burned offering.
LEV 9:15 15 Next, Aaron presented the people’s offering. He took the male goat for the people’s purification offering, slaughtered it, and offered it as a purification offering like the first purification offering.
LEV 9:16 16 He presented the entirely burned offering and did with it according to the regulation.
LEV 9:17 17 Then he presented the grain offering, took a handful from it, and completely burned it on the altar, in addition to the morning’s entirely burned offering.
LEV 9:18 18 Aaron then slaughtered the ox and the ram—the people’s communal sacrifice of well-being. Aaron’s sons handed him the blood, which he tossed against all sides of the altar,
LEV 9:19 19 and the fat pieces of the ox and ram—the fat tail, the covering fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.
LEV 9:20 20 They placed these fat pieces on the animals’ breasts, and Aaron completely burned them on the altar.
LEV 9:21 21 But Aaron lifted up the breasts and the right thigh as an uplifted offering before the LORD , just as Moses had commanded.
LEV 9:22 22 Aaron then raised his hands toward the people and blessed them. After performing the purification offering, the entirely burned offering, and the well-being sacrifice, he came down.
LEV 9:23 23 Moses and Aaron then entered the meeting tent. When they came out, they blessed the people, and the LORD ’s glorious presence appeared to all the people.
LEV 9:24 24 Fire flew out from before the LORD and devoured the entirely burned offering and the fat pieces on the altar. All the people saw it. They shouted for joy and fell facedown.
LEV 10:1 1 Now Nadab and Abihu, two of Aaron’s sons, each took an incense pan. They put fire and incense on them and offered unauthorized fire before the LORD , which he had not commanded them.
LEV 10:2 2 Then fire flew out from before the LORD and devoured them, and they died before the LORD .
LEV 10:3 3 Moses said to Aaron, “When the LORD said, ‘I will show that I am holy among those near me, and before all the people I will manifest my glorious presence,’ this is what he meant!” But Aaron was silent.
LEV 10:4 4 Then Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan the sons of Uzziel, Aaron’s uncle, and told them, “Go carry your relatives out from the front of the sanctuary to a place outside the camp.”
LEV 10:5 5 So they went forward and carried Nadab and Abihu out by their tunics to a place outside the camp, just as Moses had ordered.
LEV 10:6 6 Moses then said to Aaron and his sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, “Don’t dishevel your hair and don’t rip your clothes into pieces, or you will die and bring anger upon the whole community. Your family—all of Israel’s house—will mourn the burning the LORD has done.
LEV 10:7 7 But you must not leave the meeting tent, or you will die because the LORD ’s anointing oil is on you.” So they did what Moses ordered.
LEV 10:8 8 The LORD said to Aaron:
LEV 10:9 9 Both you and your sons must not drink wine or beer when you enter the meeting tent so that you don’t die—this is a permanent rule throughout your future generations—
LEV 10:10 10 so that you can distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean,
LEV 10:11 11 and so that you can teach the Israelites all the rules that the LORD spoke to them through Moses.
LEV 10:12 12 Moses then told Aaron and his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, “Take the grain offering that is left over from the LORD ’s food gifts and eat it unleavened next to the altar, because it is most holy.
LEV 10:13 13 You must eat it in a holy place because it is your portion and your sons’ portion from the LORD ’s food gifts, as I have been commanded.
LEV 10:14 14 You must eat the breast for the uplifted offering and the thigh for the gift offering in a clean place—both you and your sons and daughters. These things are designated as your portion and your children’s portion from the Israelites’ communal sacrifices of well-being.
LEV 10:15 15 The Israelites must bring the thigh for the gift and the breast for the uplifted offering along with the food gifts of the fat pieces, to be lifted up as an uplifted offering before the LORD . These will belong to both you and your children as a permanent portion, just as the LORD has commanded.”
LEV 10:16 16 Then Moses asked about the male goat for the purification offering, and discovered that it had already been burned. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons, and asked,
LEV 10:17 17 “Why didn’t you eat the purification offering in the holy area? It’s most holy, and it was assigned to you for bearing the community’s punishment by making reconciliation for them before the LORD .
LEV 10:18 18 Since its blood wasn’t brought into the sanctuary’s interior, you were to have eaten it in the sanctuary, just as I was commanded.”
LEV 10:19 19 “Look,” Aaron said to Moses, “today they offered their purification offerings and their entirely burned offerings before the LORD , but these things still happened to me! Would the LORD have approved if I had eaten a purification offering today?”
LEV 10:20 20 When Moses heard that, he approved.
LEV 11:1 1 The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
LEV 11:2 2 Say to the Israelites: These are the creatures that you are allowed to eat from the land animals:
LEV 11:3 3 You can eat any animal that has divided hoofs, completely split, and that rechews food.
LEV 11:4 4 But of animals that rechew food and have divided hoofs you must not eat the following: the camel—though it rechews food, it does not have divided hoofs, so it is unclean for you;
LEV 11:5 5 the rock badger—though it rechews food, it does not have divided hoofs, so it is unclean for you;
LEV 11:6 6 the hare—though it rechews food, it does not have divided hoofs, so it is unclean for you;
LEV 11:7 7 the pig—though it has completely divided hoofs, it does not rechew food, so it is unclean for you.
LEV 11:8 8 You must not eat the flesh of these animals or touch their dead bodies; they are unclean for you.
LEV 11:9 9 You are allowed to eat the following from all water animals: You may eat anything in the water that has fins and scales, whether in sea or stream.
LEV 11:10 10 But anything in the seas or streams that does not have fins and scales—whether it be any of the swarming creatures in the water or any of the other living creatures in the water—is detestable to you
LEV 11:11 11 and must remain so. You must not eat their flesh, and you must detest their dead bodies.
LEV 11:12 12 Anything in the water that does not have fins or scales is detestable to you.
LEV 11:13 13 Of the birds, the following are the ones you must detest—they must not be eaten; they are detestable: the eagle, the black vulture, the bearded vulture,
LEV 11:14 14 the kite, any kind of falcon,
LEV 11:15 15 any kind of raven,
LEV 11:16 16 the eagle owl, the short-eared owl, the long-eared owl, any kind of hawk,
LEV 11:17 17 the tawny owl, the fisher owl, the screech owl,
LEV 11:18 18 the white owl, the scops owl, the osprey,
LEV 11:19 19 the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
LEV 11:20 20 Any flying insect that walks on four feet is detestable to you,
LEV 11:21 21 but you can eat four-footed flying insects that have jointed legs above their feet with which they hop on the ground.
LEV 11:22 22 Of these you can eat the following: any kind of migrating locust, any kind of bald locust, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.
LEV 11:23 23 But every other flying insect that has four feet is detestable to you.
LEV 11:24 24 You make yourself unclean by the following animals—whoever touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening,
LEV 11:25 25 and anyone who carries any part of their dead bodies must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening:
LEV 11:26 26 All animals that have divided hoofs, but they are not completely split, and that do not rechew food are unclean for you—whoever touches them will be unclean.
LEV 11:27 27 Of all the animals that walk on four feet, the ones that walk on their paws are unclean for you—anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until evening.
LEV 11:28 28 Anyone who carries one of their dead bodies must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening; these animals are unclean for you.
LEV 11:29 29 The following are unclean for you among the small creatures that move about on the ground: the rat, the mouse, any kind of large lizard,
LEV 11:30 30 the gecko, the spotted lizard, the lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
LEV 11:31 31 Of all small moving creatures, these are unclean for you—anyone who touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.
LEV 11:32 32 Moreover, anything on which one of these creatures falls when it is dead will be unclean, whether it is wood, cloth, skin, or funeral clothing—any such item that can be used to do work. It must be put into water and will be unclean until evening. Then it will be clean again.
LEV 11:33 33 If any of these creatures fall into a pottery jar, everything inside it will be unclean; you must smash the pot.
LEV 11:34 34 If water from such a jar gets on any edible food, it will be unclean; any drinkable beverage in such a jar will be unclean.
LEV 11:35 35 Anything on which a part of these animals’ dead bodies might fall will be unclean. If it is an oven or stove, it must be destroyed; they are unclean for you and must remain that way.
LEV 11:36 36 Now, a spring or cistern that collects water is clean, but anyone who touches one of these animals’ dead bodies in it will be unclean.
LEV 11:37 37 If any part of these animals’ dead bodies falls on seed that is to be planted, the seed is still clean.
LEV 11:38 38 But if water is poured on some seed and part of their dead bodies falls on it, it is unclean for you.
LEV 11:39 39 If one of the animals that you are allowed to eat dies naturally, anyone who touches its dead body will be unclean until evening.
LEV 11:40 40 Anyone who eats from the dead body must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening. Anyone who carries such a dead body must wash their clothes and will be unclean until evening.
LEV 11:41 41 Every creature that swarms on the earth is detestable; it must not be eaten.
LEV 11:42 42 Among all such creatures that swarm on the earth, you must not eat anything that moves on its belly or anything that walks on four or more feet because they are detestable.
LEV 11:43 43 Do not make yourselves detestable by means of any swarming creatures. Do not make yourselves unclean with them or be made unclean by them.
LEV 11:44 44 I am the LORD your God. You must keep yourselves holy and be holy, because I am holy. You must not make yourselves unclean by any swarming creature that crawls on the ground.
LEV 11:45 45 I am the LORD , who brought you up from the land of Egypt to be your God. You must be holy, because I am holy.
LEV 11:46 46 This concludes the Instruction concerning animals, birds, all creatures that live in water, and all the creatures that swarm on the earth,
LEV 11:47 47 in order to distinguish between the unclean and the clean and between creatures that can be eaten and those that cannot.
LEV 12:1 1 The LORD said to Moses:
LEV 12:2 2 Say to the Israelites: If a woman conceives a child and gives birth to a son, she will be unclean for seven days—just as she is during her menstrual period.
LEV 12:3 3 On the eighth day, the flesh of the boy’s foreskin must be circumcised.
LEV 12:4 4 For thirty-three days the mother will be in a state of blood purification. She must not touch anything holy or enter the sacred area until her time of purification is completed.
LEV 12:5 5 But if the woman gives birth to a daughter, she will be unclean for two weeks—just as she is during her menstrual period—and will be in a state of blood purification for sixty-six days.
LEV 12:6 6 When the time of purification is complete, whether for a son or a daughter, the mother must bring a one-year-old lamb as an entirely burned offering and a pigeon or turtledove as a purification offering to the priest at the meeting tent’s entrance.
LEV 12:7 7 The priest will present it before the LORD and make reconciliation for her. She will then be cleansed from her blood flow. This is the Instruction for any woman who has a child, male or female.
LEV 12:8 8 But if the mother cannot afford a sheep, she can bring two turtledoves or two pigeons—one for the entirely burned offering and the other for the purification offering. The priest will then make reconciliation for her, and she will be clean.
LEV 13:1 1 The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
LEV 13:2 2 When a person has a swelling, a scab, or a shiny spot on their skin, and it becomes an infection of skin disease on their skin, they will be brought to the priests, either to Aaron or one of his sons.
LEV 13:3 3 The priest will examine the infection on the skin. If hair in the infected area has turned white and the infection appears to be deeper than the skin, then it is an infection of skin disease. Once the priest sees this, he will declare the person unclean.
LEV 13:4 4 But if the shiny spot on the skin is white and does not appear to be deeper than the skin and the hair has not turned white, the priest will quarantine the infected person for seven days.
LEV 13:5 5 On the seventh day the priest will again examine the infection. If he sees that it has remained the same—the infection has not spread on the skin—the priest will quarantine the person for seven more days.
LEV 13:6 6 On the seventh day the priest will examine it again. If the infection has faded and has not spread over the skin, the priest will declare the person clean; it is just a rash. The person must wash their clothes, then they will be clean again.
LEV 13:7 7 But if the rash continues to spread over the skin after they appeared before the priest for purification, they must again show themselves to the priest.
LEV 13:8 8 If the priest sees that the rash has spread over the skin, the priest will declare the person unclean; it is a case of skin disease.
LEV 13:9 9 Whenever someone has an infection of skin disease, they will be brought to the priest.
LEV 13:10 10 If the priest sees that there is a white swelling on the skin, it has turned the hair white, and there is a patch of raw flesh in the swelling,
LEV 13:11 11 then it is a case of chronic skin disease on their skin. The priest will declare the person unclean. The priest will not quarantine such persons, because they are already unclean.
LEV 13:12 12 But if the skin disease continues to break out so that the disease covers all of the infected person’s skin from head to toe, as far as the priest can tell—
LEV 13:13 13 then the priest will make an examination. If the skin disease has covered the person’s whole body, the priest will declare the infected person clean. The person has turned entirely white; he is clean.
LEV 13:14 14 But as soon as raw flesh appears in the swelling, they will be unclean.
LEV 13:15 15 When the priest sees the raw flesh, he will declare the person unclean. Raw flesh is unclean; it is a case of skin disease.
LEV 13:16 16 But if the raw flesh turns white again, the person will go back to the priest.
LEV 13:17 17 The priest will examine it. If the infection has turned white, the priest will declare the infected person clean; at that point, the person is clean.
LEV 13:18 18 Whenever someone has a boil on their skin, it heals,
LEV 13:19 19 and in place of the boil there is a white swelling or reddish-white shiny spot, it must be shown to the priest.
LEV 13:20 20 If the priest sees that it appears to be lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white, the priest will declare the person unclean. It is an infection of skin disease that has broken out in the boil.
LEV 13:21 21 But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in it, it is not lower than the skin, and it is faded, the priest will quarantine the person seven days.
LEV 13:22 22 If it continues to spread over the skin, the priest will declare the person unclean; it is an infection.
LEV 13:23 23 But if the shiny spot remains where it was and does not spread, it is just a scar from the boil. The priest will declare the person clean.
LEV 13:24 24 Whenever there is a burn on someone’s skin, and the raw patch of the burn becomes a reddish-white or white shiny spot,
LEV 13:25 25 the priest will examine it. If the hair has turned white in the shiny spot, and it appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a case of skin disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest will declare the person unclean; it is an infection of skin disease.
LEV 13:26 26 But if the priest examines it, and there is no white hair in the shiny spot, it is not lower than the skin, and it is faded, the priest will quarantine the person seven days.
LEV 13:27 27 On the seventh day the priest will again examine it. If it has continued to spread over the skin, the priest will declare the person unclean; it is an infection of skin disease.
LEV 13:28 28 But if the shiny spot remains where it was, has not spread over the skin, and is faded, it is just swelling from the burn. The priest will declare the person clean, because it is just the scar from the burn.
LEV 13:29 29 Whenever a man or woman has an infection, whether on the head or in the beard,
LEV 13:30 30 the priest will examine it. If it appears to be deeper than the skin, and there is thin yellow hair in it, the priest will declare the person unclean; it is a case of scabies—a skin disease of the head or beard.
LEV 13:31 31 When the priest examines the scabies infection, if it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, but there is no black hair in it, the priest will quarantine the person with the scabies infection for seven days.
LEV 13:32 32 On the seventh day the priest will examine the infection again. If the scabies has not spread, there is no yellow hair in it, and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin,
LEV 13:33 33 the person must shave the area, without shaving the scabies. The priest will then quarantine that person another seven days.
LEV 13:34 34 On the seventh day the priest will again examine the scabies. If it has not spread over the skin and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, the priest will declare the person clean. They must wash their clothes; then they will be clean again.
LEV 13:35 35 But if the scabies continues to spread over the skin after the person’s purification,
LEV 13:36 36 the priest must examine it again. If the scabies has spread over the skin at all, the priest does not need to look for the yellow hair; the person is unclean.
LEV 13:37 37 But if the priest sees that the scabies has remained the same, and black hair has grown in it, the scabies has healed. The person is clean, and the priest will declare them to be so.
LEV 13:38 38 Whenever a man or woman has many white shiny spots on their skin,
LEV 13:39 39 if the priest sees that there are faded white shiny spots on the skin of the body, it is just a rash that has broken out on the skin; the person is clean.
LEV 13:40 40 If someone loses their hair, they are bald, but they are clean.
LEV 13:41 41 If the hair is lost at the sides of the forehead, the person has a receding hairline, but they are clean.
LEV 13:42 42 But whenever there is a reddish-white infection in the bald spot or in the receding hairline, it is a case of skin disease breaking out there.
LEV 13:43 43 The priest must examine it. If the swelling of the infection is reddish white in the bald spot or receding hairline and resembles skin disease on the body,
LEV 13:44 44 the person is afflicted with skin disease; they are unclean. The priest must declare them unclean on account of the head infection.
LEV 13:45 45 Anyone with an infection of skin disease must wear torn clothes, dishevel their hair, cover their upper lip, and shout out, “Unclean! Unclean!”
LEV 13:46 46 They will be unclean as long as they are infected. They are unclean. They must live alone outside the camp.
LEV 13:47 47 Whenever there is an infection of skin disease on clothing—on wool or linen clothing,
LEV 13:48 48 in the weaving of the linen or wool, or on a skin or skin item—
LEV 13:49 49 and the infection is greenish or reddish on the clothing, the weaving, or the skin or skin item, it is an infection of skin disease. It must be shown to the priest.
LEV 13:50 50 The priest will examine the infection and quarantine the infected item seven days.
LEV 13:51 51 On the seventh day he will examine the infection again. If the infection has spread in the clothing, the weaving, or the skin, whatever it is used for, the infection is a case of infectious skin disease; the item is unclean.
LEV 13:52 52 The priest will burn the clothing, the weaving of the wool or linen, or whatever skin item in which the infection was found, because it is an infectious skin disease; it must be burned with fire.
LEV 13:53 53 But if the priest sees that the infection has not spread in the clothing, the weaving, or on any skin item,
LEV 13:54 54 the priest will order that the infected piece be washed, and he will quarantine it for another seven days.
LEV 13:55 55 After it has been washed, if the priest sees that the infection has not changed its appearance, even though the infection has not spread, it is unclean. You must burn it with fire. It is a fungus, whether it is on the inside or outside.
LEV 13:56 56 But if, after it is washed, the priest sees that the infection has faded, he will tear the infected part out of the cloth, the weaving, or the skin.
LEV 13:57 57 If it appears again in the cloth, the weaving, or any item of skin, it is starting to break out. You must burn the infected item with fire.
LEV 13:58 58 But if the infection disappears from the cloth, the weaving, or any item of skin that you washed, it must be washed again. Then it will be clean.
