NUM 7:89 89 When Moses entered the meeting tent to speak with the LORD , he would hear the voice speaking to him from above the cover that was on the chest containing the covenant, from between the two winged creatures. In this way he spoke to Moses.
NUM 8:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 8:2 2 Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you set them up, the seven lamps will give light in front of the lampstand.
NUM 8:3 3 Aaron did so. He set up its lamps in front of the lampstand as the LORD commanded Moses.
NUM 8:4 4 This is how the lampstand was made: it was hammered gold; from its base to its flower it was hammered. Moses made the lampstand according to the vision that the LORD had shown Moses.
NUM 8:5 5 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 8:6 6 Separate the Levites from the Israelites and cleanse them.
NUM 8:7 7 This is what you will do to them to cleanse them: Sprinkle water of purification on them, have them shave their bodies, wash their clothes, and cleanse themselves.
NUM 8:8 8 They will take a bull from the herd, with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil. You will take a second bull from the herd for a purification offering.
NUM 8:9 9 You will bring the Levites before the meeting tent and gather the entire Israelite community.
NUM 8:10 10 Then you will bring the Levites into the LORD ’s presence, and the Israelites will lay their hands on the Levites.
NUM 8:11 11 Aaron will present the Levites as an uplifted offering in the LORD ’s presence from the Israelites so that they may do the LORD ’s service.
NUM 8:12 12 Then the Levites will lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, and Aaron will offer one as a purification offering and the other as an entirely burned offering to the LORD in order to seek reconciliation for the Levites.
NUM 8:13 13 You will have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons and you will present them as an uplifted offering to the LORD .
NUM 8:14 14 You will separate the Levites from the Israelites, and the Levites will be mine.
NUM 8:15 15 The Levites will enter to serve the meeting tent, after you have cleansed them and presented them as an uplifted offering.
NUM 8:16 16 They are given over to me from the Israelites in place of all the newborn, the oldest of all the Israelites. I take them for myself.
NUM 8:17 17 Every oldest male among the Israelites is mine, whether human or animal. When I killed all the oldest males in the land of Egypt, I dedicated them to myself.
NUM 8:18 18 I have taken the Levites in place of all the oldest among the Israelites.
NUM 8:19 19 I have selected the Levites from the Israelites for Aaron and his sons to perform the service of the Israelites in the meeting tent and to seek reconciliation for the Israelites so that there will not be a plague when the Israelites approach the sanctuary.
NUM 8:20 20 Moses, Aaron, and the entire Israelite community carried out for the Levites everything the LORD had commanded Moses. That is what the Israelites did for the Levites.
NUM 8:21 21 The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes. Aaron presented them as an uplifted offering in the LORD ’s presence, and he sought reconciliation for them in order to cleanse them.
NUM 8:22 22 After this the Levites went in to perform their service in the meeting tent before Aaron and his sons. They did for the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses concerning them.
NUM 8:23 23 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 8:24 24 This rule applies to the Levites: Everyone 25 years old and above will enter into service, performing the duties for the meeting tent.
NUM 8:25 25 At 50 years old each will retire from service. They will perform their duties no longer.
NUM 8:26 26 Each may assist his fellow Levites in the meeting tent with some responsibilities, but he may not perform service. This is how you should assign responsibilities to the Levites.
NUM 9:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses in the Sinai desert in the first month of the second year after they had left the land of Egypt:
NUM 9:2 2 Let the Israelites keep the Passover at its appointed time.
NUM 9:3 3 On the fourteenth day of this month at twilight you will keep it at its appointed time. Keep it according to all its regulations and its customary practices.
NUM 9:4 4 Moses instructed the Israelites to keep the Passover.
NUM 9:5 5 At twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month they kept the Passover in the Sinai desert. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD commanded Moses.
NUM 9:6 6 But there were persons who were unclean from contact with a human corpse, and they were unable to keep the Passover on that day. They approached Moses and Aaron that day.
NUM 9:7 7 These persons said to him, “Although we are unclean from contact with a human corpse, why must we be prohibited from presenting the LORD ’s offering at its appointed time with the rest of the Israelites?”
NUM 9:8 8 Moses said to them, “Wait while I listen for what the LORD will command concerning you.”
NUM 9:9 9 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 9:10 10 Tell the Israelites: When any of you or your descendants are unclean from contact with a corpse or are on a long trip, they may still keep the Passover to the LORD .
NUM 9:11 11 They will keep it at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month. They will eat the Passover lamb with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
NUM 9:12 12 They must not leave any of it until morning, nor break any of its bones. They will keep the Passover according to all its regulations.
NUM 9:13 13 But any persons who are clean and not on a trip, yet don’t keep the Passover, those persons will be cut off from their people, because they didn’t present the LORD ’s offering at its appointed time. Those persons will bear their sin.
NUM 9:14 14 If an immigrant resides among you and wishes to keep the Passover to the LORD , that one also will keep it according to its regulations and its customary practices. There will be one set of regulations for both of you, for the immigrant and for the native of the land.
NUM 9:15 15 On the day the dwelling was erected, the cloud covered the dwelling, the covenant tent. At night until morning, the cloud appeared with lightning over the dwelling.
NUM 9:16 16 It was always there. The cloud covered it by day, appearing with lightning at night.
NUM 9:17 17 Whenever the cloud ascended from the tent, the Israelites would march. And the Israelites would camp wherever the cloud settled.
NUM 9:18 18 At the LORD ’s command, the Israelites would march, and at the LORD ’s command they would camp. As long as the cloud settled on the dwelling, they would camp.
NUM 9:19 19 When the cloud lingered on the meeting tent for many days, the Israelites would observe the LORD ’s direction and they wouldn’t march.
NUM 9:20 20 Sometimes the cloud would be over the dwelling for a number of days, so they would camp at the LORD ’s command, marching again only at the LORD ’s command.
NUM 9:21 21 Sometimes the cloud would settle only overnight, and they would march when the cloud ascended in the morning. Whether it was day or night, they would march when the cloud ascended.
NUM 9:22 22 Whether it was two days, or a month, or a long time, the Israelites would camp so long as the cloud lingered on the dwelling and settled on it. They wouldn’t march. But when it ascended, they would march.
NUM 9:23 23 They camped at the LORD ’s command and they marched at the LORD ’s command. They followed the LORD ’s direction according to the LORD ’s command through Moses.
NUM 10:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 10:2 2 Make two silver trumpets and make them from hammered metalwork. Use them for summoning the community and for breaking camp.
NUM 10:3 3 When both are blown, the entire community will meet you at the entrance of the meeting tent.
NUM 10:4 4 When one is blown, the chiefs, the leaders of Israel’s divisions, will meet you.
NUM 10:5 5 When you blow a series of short blasts, the camp on the east side will march.
NUM 10:6 6 And when you blow a second series of short blasts, the camp on the south side will march. You will blow a series of short blasts to announce their march.
NUM 10:7 7 To gather the assembly, blow a long blast, not a series of short blasts.
NUM 10:8 8 Aaron’s sons the priests will blow the trumpets. This will be a permanent regulation for you throughout time.
NUM 10:9 9 When you go to war in your land against an enemy who is attacking you, you will blow short blasts with the trumpets so that you may be remembered by the LORD your God and be saved from your enemies.
NUM 10:10 10 On your festival days, your appointed feasts, and at the beginning of your months, you will blow the trumpets over your entirely burned offerings and your well-being sacrifices. They will serve as a reminder of you to your God. I am the LORD your God.
NUM 10:11 11 On the twentieth day of the second month in the second year, the cloud ascended from the covenant dwelling.
NUM 10:12 12 The Israelites set out on their march from the Sinai desert, and the cloud settled in the Paran desert.
NUM 10:13 13 They marched for the first time at the LORD ’s command through Moses.
NUM 10:14 14 The banner of Judah’s camp marched first with its military units. Nahshon, Amminadab’s son, commanded its military.
NUM 10:15 15 Nethanel, Zuar’s son, commanded the military of the tribe of Issachar.
NUM 10:16 16 Eliab, Helon’s son, commanded the military of the tribe of Zebulun.
NUM 10:17 17 The dwelling was taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites, who carried the dwelling, marched.
NUM 10:18 18 The banner of Reuben’s camp marched with its military units. Elizur, Shedeur’s son, commanded its military.
NUM 10:19 19 Shelumiel, Zurishaddai’s son, commanded the military of the tribe of Simeon.
NUM 10:20 20 Eliasaph, Deuel’s son, commanded the military of the tribe of Gad.
NUM 10:21 21 The Kohathites, who carried the holy things, marched. The dwelling would be set up before their arrival.
NUM 10:22 22 The banner of Ephraim’s camp marched with its military units. Elishama, Ammihud’s son, commanded its military.
NUM 10:23 23 Gamaliel, Pedahzur’s son, commanded the military of the tribe of Manasseh.
NUM 10:24 24 Abidan, Gideoni’s son, commanded the military of the tribe of Benjamin.
NUM 10:25 25 The banner of Dan’s camp, at the rear of the whole camp, marched with its military units. Ahiezer, Ammishaddai’s son, commanded its military.
NUM 10:26 26 Pagiel, Ochran’s son, commanded the military of the tribe of Asher.
NUM 10:27 27 Ahira, Enan’s son, commanded the military of the tribe of Naphtali.
NUM 10:28 28 This was the order of departure of the Israelites with their military units when they set out.
NUM 10:29 29 Moses said to Hobab the Midianite, Reuel’s son and Moses’ father-in-law, “We’re marching to the place about which the LORD has said, ‘I’ll give it to you.’ Come with us and we’ll treat you well, for the LORD has promised to treat Israel well.”
NUM 10:30 30 Hobab said to him, “I won’t go; I’d rather go to my land and to my folk.”
NUM 10:31 31 Moses said, “Please don’t abandon us, for you know where we can camp in the desert, and you can be our eyes.
NUM 10:32 32 If you go with us, whatever good the LORD does for us, we’ll do for you.”
NUM 10:33 33 They marched from the LORD ’s mountain for three days. The LORD ’s chest containing the covenant marched ahead of them for three days to look for a resting place for them.
NUM 10:34 34 Now the LORD ’s cloud was over them by day when they marched from the camp.
NUM 10:35 35 When the chest set out, Moses would say, “Arise, LORD , let your enemies scatter, and those who hate you flee.”
NUM 10:36 36 When it rested, he would say, “Return, LORD of the ten thousand thousands of Israel.”
NUM 11:1 1 When the people complained intensely in the LORD ’s hearing, the LORD heard and became angry. Then the LORD ’s fire burned them and consumed the edges of the camp.
NUM 11:2 2 When the people cried out to Moses, Moses prayed to the LORD , and the fire subsided.
NUM 11:3 3 The name of that place was called Taberah, because the LORD ’s fire burned against them.
NUM 11:4 4 The riffraff among them had a strong craving. Even the Israelites cried again and said, “Who will give us meat to eat?
NUM 11:5 5 We remember the fish we ate in Egypt for free, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic.
NUM 11:6 6 Now our lives are wasting away. There is nothing but manna in front of us.”
NUM 11:7 7 The manna was like coriander seed and its color was like resin.
NUM 11:8 8 The people would roam around and collect it and grind it with millstones or pound it in a mortar. Then they would boil it in pots and make it into cakes. It tasted like cakes baked in olive oil.
NUM 11:9 9 When the dew fell on the camp during the night, the manna would fall with it.
NUM 11:10 10 Moses heard the people crying throughout their clans, each at his tent’s entrance. The LORD was outraged, and Moses was upset.
NUM 11:11 11 Moses said to the LORD , “Why have you treated your servant so badly? And why haven’t I found favor in your eyes, for you have placed the burden of all these people on me?
NUM 11:12 12 Did I conceive all these people? Did I give birth to them, that you would say to me, ‘Carry them at the breast, as a nurse carries an unweaned child,’ to the fertile land that you promised their ancestors?
NUM 11:13 13 Where am I to get meat for all these people? They are crying before me and saying, ‘Give us meat, so we can eat.’
NUM 11:14 14 I can’t bear this people on my own. They’re too heavy for me.
NUM 11:15 15 If you’re going to treat me like this, please kill me. If I’ve found favor in your eyes, then don’t let me endure this wretched situation.”
NUM 11:16 16 The LORD said to Moses, “Gather before me seventy men from Israel’s elders, whom you know as elders and officers of the people. Take them to the meeting tent, and let them stand there with you.
NUM 11:17 17 Then I’ll descend and speak with you there. I’ll take some of the spirit that is on you and place it on them. Then they will carry the burden of the people with you so that you won’t bear it alone.
NUM 11:18 18 To the people you will say, ‘Make yourselves holy for tomorrow; then you will eat meat, for you’ve cried in the LORD ’s hearing, “Who will give us meat to eat? It was better for us in Egypt.” The LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.
NUM 11:19 19 You won’t eat for just one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days,
NUM 11:20 20 but for a whole month until it comes out of your nostrils and nauseates you. You’ve rejected the LORD who’s been with you and you have cried before him, saying, “Why did we leave Egypt?” ’”
NUM 11:21 21 Moses said, “The people I’m with are six hundred thousand on foot and you’re saying, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat for a month.’
NUM 11:22 22 Can flocks and herds be found and slaughtered for them? Or can all the fish in the sea be found and caught for them?”
NUM 11:23 23 The LORD said to Moses, “Is the LORD ’s power too weak? Now you will see whether my word will come true for you or not.”
NUM 11:24 24 So Moses went out and told the people the LORD ’s words. He assembled seventy men from the people’s elders and placed them around the tent.
NUM 11:25 25 The LORD descended in a cloud, spoke to him, and took some of the spirit that was on him and placed it on the seventy elders. When the spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but only this once.
NUM 11:26 26 Two men had remained in the camp, one named Eldad and the second named Medad, and the spirit rested on them. They were among those registered, but they hadn’t gone out to the tent, so they prophesied in the camp.
NUM 11:27 27 A young man ran and told Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
NUM 11:28 28 Joshua, Nun’s son and Moses’ assistant since his youth, responded, “My master Moses, stop them!”
NUM 11:29 29 Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? If only all the LORD ’s people were prophets with the LORD placing his spirit on them!”
NUM 11:30 30 Moses and Israel’s elders were assembled in the camp.
NUM 11:31 31 A wind from the LORD blew up and brought quails from the sea. It let them fall by the camp, about a day’s journey all around the camp and about three feet deep on the ground.
NUM 11:32 32 Then the people arose and gathered the quail all that day, all night, and all the next day. The least collected was ten homers, and they laid them out around the camp.
NUM 11:33 33 While the meat was still between their teeth and not yet consumed, the LORD ’s anger blazed against the people. The LORD struck the people with a very great punishment.
NUM 11:34 34 The name of that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had the craving.
NUM 11:35 35 From Kibroth-hattaavah the people marched to Hazeroth.
NUM 12:1 1 When they were in Hazeroth, Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses on account of the Cushite woman whom he had married—for he had married a Cushite woman.
NUM 12:2 2 They said, “Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Hasn’t he also spoken through us?” The LORD heard it.
NUM 12:3 3 Now the man Moses was humble, more so than anyone on earth.
NUM 12:4 4 Immediately, the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “You three go out to the meeting tent.” So the three of them went out.
NUM 12:5 5 Then the LORD descended in a column of cloud, stood at the entrance of the tent, and called to Aaron and Miriam. The two of them came forward.
NUM 12:6 6 He said, “Listen to my words: If there is a prophet of the LORD among you, I make myself known to him in visions. I speak to him in dreams.
NUM 12:7 7 But not with my servant Moses. He has proved to be reliable with all my household.
NUM 12:8 8 I speak with him face-to-face, visibly, not in riddles. He sees the LORD ’s form. So why aren’t you afraid to criticize my servant Moses?”
NUM 12:9 9 The LORD ’s anger blazed against them, and they went back.
NUM 12:10 10 When the cloud went away from over the tent, Miriam suddenly developed a skin disease flaky like snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam and saw her skin disease.
NUM 12:11 11 Then Aaron said to Moses, “Oh, my master, please don’t punish us for the sin that we foolishly committed.
NUM 12:12 12 Please don’t let her be like the stillborn, whose flesh is half eaten as it comes out of the mother’s womb.”
NUM 12:13 13 So Moses cried to the LORD , “God, please heal her!”
NUM 12:14 14 The LORD said to Moses, “If her father had spit in her face, would she not be shamed for seven days? Let her be shut out of the camp for seven days, and afterward she will be brought back.”
NUM 12:15 15 So they shut Miriam out of the camp seven days. And the people didn’t march until Miriam was brought back.
NUM 12:16 16 Afterward the people marched from Hazeroth, and they camped in the Paran desert.
NUM 13:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 13:2 2 Send out men to explore the land of Canaan, which I’m giving to the Israelites. Send one man from each ancestral tribe, each a chief among them.
NUM 13:3 3 So Moses sent them out from the Paran desert according to the LORD ’s command. All the men were leaders among the Israelites.
NUM 13:4 4 These are their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua, Zaccur’s son;
NUM 13:5 5 from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat, Hori’s son;
NUM 13:6 6 from the tribe of Judah, Caleb, Jephunneh’s son;
NUM 13:7 7 from the tribe of Issachar, Igal, Joseph’s son;
NUM 13:8 8 from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea, Nun’s son;
NUM 13:9 9 from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti, Raphu’s son;
NUM 13:10 10 from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel, Sodi’s son;
NUM 13:11 11 from the tribe of Joseph: from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi, Susi’s son;
NUM 13:12 12 from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel, Gemalli’s son;
NUM 13:13 13 from the tribe of Asher, Sethur, Michael’s son;
NUM 13:14 14 from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi, Vophsi’s son;
NUM 13:15 15 from the tribe of Gad, Geuel, Machi’s son.
NUM 13:16 16 These are the names of the men whom Moses sent out to explore the land. Moses changed the name of Hoshea, Nun’s son, to Joshua.
NUM 13:17 17 When Moses sent them out to explore the land of Canaan, he said to them, “Go up there into the arid southern plain and into the mountains.
NUM 13:18 18 You must inspect the land. What is it like? Are the people who live in it strong or weak, few or many?
NUM 13:19 19 Is the land in which they live good or bad? Are the towns in which they live camps or fortresses?
NUM 13:20 20 Is the land rich or poor? Are there trees in it or not? Be courageous and bring back the land’s fruit.” It was the season of the first ripe grapes.
NUM 13:21 21 They went up and explored the land from the Zin desert to Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.
NUM 13:22 22 They went up into the arid southern plain and entered Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the descendants of the Anakites, lived. (Hebron was built seven years before Tanis in Egypt.)
NUM 13:23 23 Then they entered the Cluster ravine, cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes, and carried it on a pole between them. They also took pomegranates and figs.
NUM 13:24 24 That place was called the Cluster ravine because of the cluster of grapes that the Israelites cut down from there.
NUM 13:25 25 They returned from exploring the land after forty days.
NUM 13:26 26 They went directly to Moses, Aaron, and the entire Israelite community in the Paran desert at Kadesh. They brought back a report to them and to the entire community and showed them the land’s fruit.
NUM 13:27 27 Then they gave their report: “We entered the land to which you sent us. It’s actually full of milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
NUM 13:28 28 There are, however, powerful people who live in the land. The cities have huge fortifications. And we even saw the descendants of the Anakites there.
NUM 13:29 29 The Amalekites live in the land of the arid southern plain; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the mountains; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.”
NUM 13:30 30 Now Caleb calmed the people before Moses and said, “We must go up and take possession of it, because we are more than able to do it.”
NUM 13:31 31 But the men who went up with him said, “We can’t go up against the people because they are stronger than we.”
NUM 13:32 32 They started a rumor about the land that they had explored, telling the Israelites, “The land that we crossed over to explore is a land that devours its residents. All the people we saw in it are huge men.
NUM 13:33 33 We saw there the Nephilim (the descendants of Anak come from the Nephilim). We saw ourselves as grasshoppers, and that’s how we appeared to them.”
NUM 14:1 1 The entire community raised their voice and the people wept that night.
NUM 14:2 2 All the Israelites criticized Moses and Aaron. The entire community said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt or if only we had died in this desert!
NUM 14:3 3 Why is the LORD bringing us to this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and our children will be taken by force. Wouldn’t it be better for us to return to Egypt?”
NUM 14:4 4 So they said to each other, “Let’s pick a leader and let’s go back to Egypt.”
NUM 14:5 5 Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the assembled Israelite community.
NUM 14:6 6 But Joshua, Nun’s son, and Caleb, Jephunneh’s son, from those who had explored the land, tore their clothes
NUM 14:7 7 and said to the entire Israelite community, “The land we crossed through to explore is an exceptionally good land.
NUM 14:8 8 If the LORD is pleased with us, he’ll bring us into this land and give it to us. It’s a land that’s full of milk and honey.
NUM 14:9 9 Only don’t rebel against the LORD and don’t be afraid of the people of the land. They are our prey. Their defense has deserted them, but the LORD is with us. So don’t be afraid of them.”
NUM 14:10 10 But the entire community intended to stone them. Then the LORD ’s glory appeared in the meeting tent to all the Israelites.
NUM 14:11 11 The LORD said to Moses, “How long will these people disrespect me? And how long will they doubt me after all the signs that I performed among them?
NUM 14:12 12 I’ll strike them down with a plague and disown them. Then I’ll make you into a great nation, stronger than they.”
NUM 14:13 13 Moses said to the LORD , “The Egyptians will hear, for with your power you brought these people up from among them.
NUM 14:14 14 They’ll tell the inhabitants of this land. They’ve heard that you, LORD , are with this people. You, LORD , appear to them face-to-face. Your cloud stands over them. You go before them in a column of cloud by day and in a column of lightning by night.
NUM 14:15 15 If you kill these people, every last one of them, the nations who heard about you will say,
NUM 14:16 16 ‘The LORD wasn’t able to bring these people to the land that he solemnly promised to give them. So he slaughtered them in the desert.’
NUM 14:17 17 Now let my master’s power be as great as you declared when you said,
NUM 14:18 18 ‘The LORD is very patient and absolutely loyal, forgiving wrongs and disloyalty. Yet he doesn’t forgo all punishment, disciplining the grandchildren and great-grandchildren for their ancestors’ wrongs.’
NUM 14:19 19 Please forgive the wrongs of these people because of your absolute loyalty, just as you’ve forgiven these people from their time in Egypt until now.”
NUM 14:20 20 Then the LORD said, “I will forgive as you requested.
NUM 14:21 21 But as I live and as the LORD ’s glory fills the entire earth,
NUM 14:22 22 none of the men who saw my glory and the signs I did in Egypt and in the desert, but tested me these ten times and haven’t listened to my voice,
NUM 14:23 23 will see the land I promised to their ancestors. All who disrespected me won’t see it.
NUM 14:24 24 But I’ll bring my servant Caleb into the land that he explored, and his descendants will possess it because he has a different spirit, and he has remained true to me.
NUM 14:25 25 Since the Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valley, tomorrow turn and march into the desert by the route of the Reed Sea.”
NUM 14:26 26 The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
NUM 14:27 27 How long will this wicked community complain against me? I’ve heard the Israelites’ dissent as they continue to complain against me.
NUM 14:28 28 Say to them, “As I live,” says the LORD , “just as I’ve heard you say, so I’ll do to you.
NUM 14:29 29 Your dead bodies will fall in this desert. None of you who were enlisted and were registered from 20 years old and above, who complained against me,
NUM 14:30 30 will enter the land in which I promised to settle you, with the exception of Caleb, Jephunneh’s son, and Joshua, Nun’s son.
NUM 14:31 31 But your children, whom you said would be taken by force, I’ll bring them in and they will know the land that you rejected.
NUM 14:32 32 Your bodies, however, will fall in this desert,
NUM 14:33 33 and your children will be shepherds in the desert for forty years. They will suffer for your unfaithfulness, until the last of your bodies fall in the desert.
NUM 14:34 34 For as many days as you explored the land, that is, forty days, just as many years you’ll bear your guilt, that is, forty years. This is how you will understand my frustration.”
NUM 14:35 35 I the LORD have spoken. I will do this to the entire wicked community who gathered against me. They will die in this desert. There they’ll meet their end.
NUM 14:36 36 The men whom Moses sent out to explore the land had returned and caused the entire community to complain against him by starting a rumor about the land.
NUM 14:37 37 These men died by a plague in the LORD ’s presence on account of their false rumor.
NUM 14:38 38 But Joshua, Nun’s son, and Caleb, Jephunneh’s son, survived from those men who went to explore the land.
NUM 14:39 39 Moses spoke these words to all the Israelites, and the people mourned bitterly.
NUM 14:40 40 They rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain range, saying, “Let’s go up to the place the LORD told us to, for we have sinned.”
NUM 14:41 41 But Moses said, “Why do you disobey the LORD ’s command? It won’t succeed.
NUM 14:42 42 Don’t go up, for the LORD isn’t with you. Don’t be struck down before your enemies.
NUM 14:43 43 The Amalekites and the Canaanites will be there in front of you and you will fall by the sword because you turned away from the LORD , and the LORD is no longer with you.”
NUM 14:44 44 Yet they recklessly ascended toward the top of the mountains, even though Moses and the LORD ’s chest containing the covenant didn’t depart from the camp.
NUM 14:45 45 Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites, who lived in those mountains, descended, struck them down, and beat them all the way to Hormah.
NUM 15:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 15:2 2 Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land where you will live, which I am giving you,
NUM 15:3 3 and you make a food gift to the LORD as a soothing smell for the LORD from the herd or the flock—whether an entirely burned offering, or a sacrifice to fulfill a solemn promise, or a spontaneous gift, or at your sacred seasons—
NUM 15:4 4 the one presenting the offering to the LORD will bring a grain offering of one-tenth of a measure of fine flour mixed with one-fourth of a hin of oil.
NUM 15:5 5 You will also offer one-fourth of a hin of wine as a drink offering with either the entirely burned offering or the sacrifice, for each lamb.
NUM 15:6 6 For a ram you will offer a grain offering of two-tenths of a measure of fine flour mixed with one-third of a hin of oil.
NUM 15:7 7 You will also present one-third of a hin of wine for a drink offering as a soothing smell for the LORD .
NUM 15:8 8 When you offer a bull for an entirely burned offering, or a sacrifice to fulfill a solemn promise, or a well-being sacrifice to the LORD ,
NUM 15:9 9 you will present with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of a measure of fine flour mixed with a half hin of oil.
NUM 15:10 10 You will present a half hin of wine for a drink offering as a food gift that is a soothing smell to the LORD .
NUM 15:11 11 So will it be done with each ox, each ram, or for any sheep or goat.
NUM 15:12 12 However many you offer, you will do the same for each one.
NUM 15:13 13 Every citizen will perform these rituals in bringing a food gift that is a soothing smell to the LORD .
NUM 15:14 14 If an immigrant lives with you or has settled among you for many years and would also like to offer a food gift that is a soothing smell to the LORD , that person must do just as you do.
NUM 15:15 15 The assembly will have the same regulation for you and for the immigrant. The regulation will be permanent for all time. You and the immigrant will be the same in the LORD ’s presence.
NUM 15:16 16 There will be one set of instructions and one legal norm for the immigrant and for you.
NUM 15:17 17 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 15:18 18 Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land to which I’m bringing you,
NUM 15:19 19 whenever you eat the land’s food you will present a gift offering to the LORD .
NUM 15:20 20 You will present a gift offering from the first bread you bake just like you present a gift offering from the threshing floor.
NUM 15:21 21 You will give a gift offering from the first bread you bake for all time.
NUM 15:22 22 If by accident you don’t obey all these commands that the LORD spoke to Moses,
NUM 15:23 23 or everything that the LORD commanded you through Moses from the day of the LORD ’s command onward for all time,
NUM 15:24 24 then if it was done unintentionally without the knowledge of the community, the entire community must offer one bull from the herd as an entirely burned offering, a soothing smell to the LORD , with its grain and drink offering according to the specific instruction, and one male goat for a purification offering.
NUM 15:25 25 The priest will seek reconciliation for the entire Israelite community. They will be forgiven, because it was unintentional and because they brought their food gift to the LORD , along with their purification offering in the LORD ’s presence for their accidental error.
NUM 15:26 26 The entire Israelite community and the immigrant residing among them will be forgiven, because all the people acted unintentionally.
NUM 15:27 27 If an individual sins unintentionally, that person must present a one-year-old female goat for a purification offering.
NUM 15:28 28 The priest will seek reconciliation in the LORD ’s presence for the person who sinned unintentionally, when the sin is an accident, seeking reconciliation so that person will be forgiven.
NUM 15:29 29 There will be one set of instructions for the Israelite citizen and the immigrant residing with you for anyone who commits an unintentional sin.
NUM 15:30 30 But the person who acts deliberately, whether a citizen or an immigrant, and insults the LORD , that person will be cut off from the people
NUM 15:31 31 for despising the LORD ’s word and breaking his commands. That person will be completely cut off and bear the guilt.
NUM 15:32 32 When the Israelites were in the desert, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
NUM 15:33 33 Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the entire community.
NUM 15:34 34 They placed him in custody, because it wasn’t clear what should be done to him.
NUM 15:35 35 Then the LORD said to Moses: The man should be put to death. The entire community should stone him outside the camp.
NUM 15:36 36 The entire community took him outside the camp and stoned him. He died as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NUM 15:37 37 The LORD said to Moses:
NUM 15:38 38 Speak to the Israelites and say to them: Make fringes on the edges of your clothing for all time. Have them put blue cords on the fringe on the edges.
NUM 15:39 39 This will be your fringe. You will see it and remember all the LORD ’s commands and do them. Then you won’t go exploring the lusts of your own heart or your eyes.
NUM 15:40 40 In this way you’ll remember to do all my commands. Then you will be holy to your God.
NUM 15:41 41 I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.
NUM 16:1 1 Korah—Izhar’s son, Kohath’s grandson, and Levi’s great-grandson—with Dathan and Abiram, Eliab’s sons, and On, Peleth’s son, descendants of Reuben,
NUM 16:2 2 rose up against Moses, along with two hundred fifty Israelite men, leaders of the community, chosen by the assembly, men of reputation.
NUM 16:3 3 They assembled against Moses and Aaron and said to them, “You’ve gone too far, because the entire community is holy, every last one of them, and the LORD is with them. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the LORD ’s assembly?”
NUM 16:4 4 When Moses heard this, he fell on his face.
NUM 16:5 5 He spoke to Korah and all his community, “In the morning the LORD will make known who is his, who is holy, and who is able to approach him. The one he chooses for himself is the one who will be able to approach him.
NUM 16:6 6 This is what must be done. Korah and your entire community: Take censers for yourselves.
NUM 16:7 7 Tomorrow put fire in them and place incense on them in the LORD ’s presence. The man whom the LORD chooses, that one is holy. You Levites have gone too far!”
NUM 16:8 8 Moses said to Korah, “Listen, you Levites,
NUM 16:9 9 isn’t it enough for you that Israel’s God has separated you from the Israelite community to allow you to approach him, to perform the service of the LORD ’s dwelling, and to serve before the community by ministering for them?
NUM 16:10 10 He has allowed you and all your fellow Levites with you to approach him. Yet you also seek the priesthood?
NUM 16:11 11 Thus you and your entire community have assembled against the LORD . But Aaron, what is he that you complain about him?”
NUM 16:12 12 Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, Eliab’s sons. But they said, “We won’t come up!
NUM 16:13 13 Isn’t it enough that you’ve brought us up from a land full of milk and honey to kill us in the desert so that you’d also dominate us?
NUM 16:14 14 Moreover, you haven’t brought us to a land full of milk and honey, nor given us the inheritance of field and vineyard. Would you also gouge out the eyes of these men? We won’t come up!”
NUM 16:15 15 Moses became very angry and he said to the LORD , “Pay no attention to their offering. I haven’t taken a single donkey from them, nor have I wronged any one of them.”
NUM 16:16 16 Moses said to Korah, “You and your entire community should appear before the LORD tomorrow, you, they, and Aaron.
NUM 16:17 17 Every person should take his censer, place incense on it, and present it before the LORD . Each person will carry his censer, two hundred fifty censers in all, including you and Aaron.”
NUM 16:18 18 Then every person took his censer, placed fire on it, put incense on it, and stood at the entrance of the meeting tent with Moses and Aaron.
NUM 16:19 19 Korah gathered the entire community with them to the entrance of the meeting tent. Then the LORD ’s glory appeared to the entire community.
NUM 16:20 20 The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron,
NUM 16:21 21 “Separate yourselves from this community so that I may consume them in a moment.”
NUM 16:22 22 They fell on their faces and said, “God, the God of all living things. If one person sins, should you become angry with the entire community?”
NUM 16:23 23 The LORD said to Moses,
NUM 16:24 24 “Speak to the community and say, ‘Withdraw from around the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’”
NUM 16:25 25 Moses rose and went to Dathan and Abiram. Israel’s elders followed him.
NUM 16:26 26 He spoke to the community: “Move away from the tents of these wicked men and don’t touch anything of theirs, lest you too be wiped out for all their sins.”
NUM 16:27 27 They withdrew from around the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Then Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrance of their tents with their wives, children, and little ones.
NUM 16:28 28 Moses said, “By this you will know that the LORD sent me to do these deeds and that it wasn’t my own desire.
NUM 16:29 29 If all these people die a natural death, or if their fate be that of all humans, then the LORD hasn’t sent me.
NUM 16:30 30 But if the LORD performs an act of creation, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them and everything that belongs to them, so that they descend alive to their graves, then you’ll know that these men disrespected the LORD .”
NUM 16:31 31 As soon as he finished speaking these words, the ground under them split open.
NUM 16:32 32 The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, including every human that belonged to Korah and all their possessions.
NUM 16:33 33 They along with all their possessions descended alive to their graves, and the earth closed over them. They perished in the middle of the assembly.
NUM 16:34 34 All the Israelites who were around them fled at their cry, for they said, “The earth may swallow us.”
NUM 16:35 35 Then fire went out from the LORD and consumed the two hundred fifty men offering incense.
NUM 16:36 36 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 16:37 37 Tell Eleazar, Aaron the priest’s son, to raise the censers from the fire and scatter the ashes about, because they are holy.
NUM 16:38 38 Hammer the censers of those who sinned and lost their lives into thin plates for the altar. Since they presented them in the LORD ’s presence, they had become holy. They will be a sign for the Israelites.
NUM 16:39 39 Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers presented by those who had been consumed by fire and hammered them into a covering for the altar,
NUM 16:40 40 just as the LORD instructed him through Moses. This was a reminder for the Israelites that no outsider who isn’t one of Aaron’s descendants should approach to burn incense in the LORD ’s presence, so as not to be like Korah and his community.
NUM 16:41 41 On the next day the entire Israelite community complained to Moses and Aaron, “You killed the LORD ’s people.”
NUM 16:42 42 When the community assembled against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the meeting tent. At that moment the cloud covered it, and the LORD ’s glory appeared.
NUM 16:43 43 Moses and Aaron came to the front of the meeting tent,
NUM 16:44 44 and the LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 16:45 45 Get away from this community, so that I may consume them in an instant. They fell on their faces,
NUM 16:46 46 and Moses said to Aaron, “Take the censer, put fire from the altar on it, place incense on it, go quickly to the community, and seek reconciliation for them. Indeed, the LORD ’s anger has gone out. The plague has begun.”
NUM 16:47 47 Aaron took it as Moses said and ran into the middle of the assembly, for the plague had already begun among the people. He burned incense and sought reconciliation for the people.
NUM 16:48 48 He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague stopped.
NUM 16:49 49 Those who died from the plague were fourteen thousand seven hundred, in addition to those who died because of Korah.
NUM 16:50 50 Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the meeting tent once the plague stopped.
NUM 17:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 17:2 2 Speak to the Israelites and take from them a staff from each household, from each of the chiefs of their households, twelve staffs. Write each person’s name on his staff.
NUM 17:3 3 Write Aaron’s name on Levi’s staff, for there will be one staff for the leader of each household.
NUM 17:4 4 Then you will place them in the meeting tent in front of the chest containing the covenant, where I meet you.
NUM 17:5 5 The staff of the person I choose will sprout. Then I will rid myself of the Israelites’ complaints that they make against you.
NUM 17:6 6 Moses spoke to the Israelites, and each of their chiefs gave him a staff, one staff for each chief and his household, twelve staffs, and the staff of Aaron was with their staffs.
NUM 17:7 7 Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the meeting tent.
NUM 17:8 8 The next day Moses entered the covenant tent, and Aaron’s staff of Levi’s household had sprouted. It grew shoots, produced blossoms, and bore almonds.
NUM 17:9 9 Moses brought out all the staffs from the LORD ’s presence to the Israelites. They saw what happened, and each person took back his staff.
NUM 17:10 10 Then the LORD said to Moses, “Return Aaron’s staff in front of the chest containing the covenant to serve as a sign to the rebels so that their complaints against me end and they don’t die.”
NUM 17:11 11 Moses did exactly as the LORD commanded him.
NUM 17:12 12 The Israelites said to Moses, “We are perishing. We are being destroyed. All of us are being destroyed.
NUM 17:13 13 Anyone who approaches the LORD ’s dwelling will die. Are we doomed to perish?”
NUM 18:1 1 The LORD said to Aaron: You, your sons, and your household will bear the guilt of offenses connected with the sanctuary. You and your sons will bear the guilt of offenses connected with your priesthood.
NUM 18:2 2 Bring with you your brothers from the tribe of Levi, your father’s tribe, so that they can assist you and serve you and your sons before the covenant tent.
NUM 18:3 3 They will perform their duties for you and the service for the entire tent. But they will not approach the holy equipment of the sanctuary or the altar, lest both they and you die.
NUM 18:4 4 They will assist you and they will perform the duties of the meeting tent with regard to all the work of the tent. But no outsider may accompany you.
NUM 18:5 5 You will perform the duties of the sanctuary and the altar. Then there will no longer be any anger against the Israelites.
NUM 18:6 6 I have taken your brothers, the Levites, from the Israelites. They are a gift to you, dedicated to the LORD to perform the service of the meeting tent.
NUM 18:7 7 You and your sons must perform the duties of your priesthood for all the matters of the altar and the area behind the curtain. I give you your priestly service as a gift. But an outsider who approaches will die.
NUM 18:8 8 The LORD spoke to Aaron: I now place you in charge of my gifts, including all the Israelites’ sacred offerings. I have given them to you and your sons as an allowance. This is a permanent regulation.
NUM 18:9 9 This is what belongs to you from the most holy offerings, from the offerings by fire: all their offerings, including their grain offerings, their purification offerings, and their compensation offerings. The most holy offerings that they bring to me will be yours and your sons’.
NUM 18:10 10 You will eat it as a most holy thing. Every male may eat it. It will be holy to you.
NUM 18:11 11 This will also belong to you, your sons, and your daughters: I’m giving you the gift offerings and all the Israelites’ uplifted offerings. This is a permanent regulation. Anyone who is clean in your household may eat it.
NUM 18:12 12 All the choice oil, new wine, and the grain’s first harvest that they give to the LORD , I’m giving to you.
NUM 18:13 13 The early produce of everything in their land, which they bring to the LORD , will be yours. Anyone who is clean in your household may eat it.
NUM 18:14 14 Everything that is devoted to the LORD in Israel will be yours.
NUM 18:15 15 Any oldest male from the womb of any living thing that is presented to the LORD , whether human or animal, will be yours. However, you will redeem the oldest males of humans and of unclean animals.
NUM 18:16 16 Their redemption price from one month of age you will calculate at five shekels of silver according to the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.
NUM 18:17 17 But the oldest offspring of a cow, sheep, or goat you may not redeem. They are holy. You must dash their blood on the altar and turn their fat into smoke for a soothing smell to the LORD .
NUM 18:18 18 But their meat is yours. It will be yours just as the breast of the uplifted offering and the right thigh are yours.
NUM 18:19 19 All the holy gift offerings that the Israelites raise to the LORD I have given to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is a permanent regulation. It is a covenant of salt forever in the LORD ’s presence, for you and your descendants.
NUM 18:20 20 The LORD said to Aaron: You will have no inheritance in their land, nor will you have a share among them. I am your share and your inheritance among the Israelites.
NUM 18:21 21 I have given all the one-tenth portions in Israel to the Levites as an inheritance. They are a reward for performing their service in the meeting tent.
NUM 18:22 22 The Israelites will no longer be able to approach the meeting tent, or they will be responsible for their sin and die.
NUM 18:23 23 The Levites will perform the service of the meeting tent, and they will be responsible for their own sins. This is a permanent regulation for all time. But they will not inherit land among the Israelites
NUM 18:24 24 because I’ve given the Israelites’ one-tenth portion, which they have raised to the LORD as a gift offering, as an inheritance to the Levites. Therefore, I’ve said to them, “They won’t inherit land among the Israelites.”
NUM 18:25 25 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 18:26 26 Speak to the Levites and say to them: When you receive from the Israelites the one-tenth portion that I have given you from them as your inheritance, you also must present a gift offering to the LORD from it, a tenth from the one-tenth portion.
NUM 18:27 27 It will be considered your gift offering, like the grain of the threshing floor and what fills the winepress.
NUM 18:28 28 In this way you will also present a gift offering to the LORD from all the one-tenth portions that you take from the Israelites. You will provide from it a gift offering to the LORD for Aaron the priest.
NUM 18:29 29 You will present each gift offering to the LORD from all your gifts, from its best portions and its holiest parts.
NUM 18:30 30 You will say to them: When you have presented the best portion, it will be considered for the Levites equivalent to the produce of the grain and the produce of the winepress.
NUM 18:31 31 You and your household may eat it anywhere, because it is payment for your service in the meeting tent.
NUM 18:32 32 You will not bear guilt after you have presented the best portion. But you must not make the sacred gifts of the Israelites impure, on penalty of death.
NUM 19:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
NUM 19:2 2 This is the regulation in the Instruction that the LORD commanded. Tell the Israelites that they must bring you a red cow without defect, which is flawless and on which no yoke has been laid.
NUM 19:3 3 You will give it to Eleazar the priest, and he will take it outside the camp and slaughter it in front of him.
NUM 19:4 4 Eleazar the priest will take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle it seven times in front of the meeting tent.
NUM 19:5 5 Then he will burn the cow in front of him, its skin, flesh, and blood, with its dung.
NUM 19:6 6 The priest will take cedarwood, hyssop, and crimson cloth and throw them into the fire where the cow is burning.
NUM 19:7 7 Then the priest will wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Afterward the priest will enter the camp, but he will be unclean until evening.
NUM 19:8 8 The one who burned the cow will wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, but he will be unclean until evening.
NUM 19:9 9 A person who is clean will gather the ashes of the cow and place them outside the camp in a clean place. They will be kept for the water of purification for the Israelite community as a purification offering.
NUM 19:10 10 The one who gathers the ashes of the cow will wash his clothes but will be unclean until evening. This will be a permanent regulation for the Israelites and for the immigrant who lives among them.
NUM 19:11 11 The person who touches the dead body of any human will be unclean for seven days.
NUM 19:12 12 That person must be cleansed with water on the third and seventh days to be clean. If he fails to be cleansed with water on the third and seventh days, he will not be clean.
NUM 19:13 13 Anyone who touches the body of a human who has died and doesn’t cleanse himself defiles the LORD ’s dwelling. Such persons must be cut off from Israel because the water of purification wasn’t sprinkled on them. They remain unclean.
NUM 19:14 14 This is the instruction: When anyone dies in a tent, all who go into the tent and all who are in the tent are unclean for seven days.
NUM 19:15 15 Any open jar without a sealed cover on it is unclean.
NUM 19:16 16 Anyone in the open field who touches a person slain by the sword, or who died naturally, or a human bone or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
NUM 19:17 17 For the unclean person, they will take some of the ashes of the purification offering and place fresh water with it in a jar.
NUM 19:18 18 Then a clean person will take hyssop, dip it into the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the jars, on the people who were there, and on anyone who touched bone, the slain, the dead, or the grave.
NUM 19:19 19 On the third day and the seventh day the clean person will sprinkle it on the unclean, so that he will have purified him on the seventh day. He will then wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be clean at evening.
NUM 19:20 20 Any person who is unclean and didn’t cleanse himself will be cut off from the assembly, because he has defiled the LORD ’s sanctuary. He didn’t have the water of purification sprinkled on him. He is unclean.
NUM 19:21 21 This will be a permanent regulation for them. The one who sprinkles the water of purification will wash his own clothes. Anyone who touches the water of purification will be unclean until evening.
NUM 19:22 22 Whoever the unclean person touches will be unclean, and the one who touches the unclean will be unclean until evening.
NUM 20:1 1 In the first month, the entire Israelite community entered the Zin desert and the people stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died and was buried there.
NUM 20:2 2 Now there was no water for the community, and they assembled against Moses and Aaron.
NUM 20:3 3 Then the people confronted Moses and said to him, “If only we too had died when our brothers perished in the LORD ’s presence!
NUM 20:4 4 Why have you brought the LORD ’s assembly into this desert to kill us and our animals here?
NUM 20:5 5 Why have you led us up from Egypt to bring us to this evil place without grain, figs, vines, or pomegranates? And there’s no water to drink!”
NUM 20:6 6 Moses and Aaron went away from the assembly to the entrance of the meeting tent and they fell on their faces. Then the LORD ’s glory appeared to them.
NUM 20:7 7 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 20:8 8 “You and Aaron your brother, take the staff and assemble the community. In their presence, tell the rock to provide water. You will produce water from the rock for them and allow the community and their animals to drink.”
NUM 20:9 9 Moses took the staff from the LORD ’s presence, as the LORD had commanded him.
NUM 20:10 10 Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly before the rock. He said to them, “Listen, you rebels! Should we produce water from the rock for you?”
NUM 20:11 11 Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock with his staff twice. Out flooded water so that the community and their animals could drink.
NUM 20:12 12 The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you didn’t trust me to show my holiness before the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land that I am giving them.”
NUM 20:13 13 These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites confronted the LORD with controversy and he showed his holiness to them.
NUM 20:14 14 Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: “This is what your brother Israel says: ‘You know all the adversity that has happened to us.
NUM 20:15 15 How our ancestors went down to Egypt and lived in Egypt for a long time. The Egyptians oppressed us as they had our ancestors,
NUM 20:16 16 and we cried out to the LORD . He heard our voice, sent a messenger, and brought us out of Egypt. Now here we are in Kadesh, a city on the edge of your border.
NUM 20:17 17 Please let us cross through your land. We won’t pass through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will walk on the King’s Highway and not turn to the right or to the left until we have crossed your border.’”
NUM 20:18 18 Edom said to him, “You won’t cross through, or I will come out against you with a sword.”
NUM 20:19 19 The Israelites said to him, “We’ll go up by the road. If we drink from your water, either we or our livestock, we’ll pay for it. It’s a small matter. We would only ask to cross on foot.”
NUM 20:20 20 But he said, “You won’t cross.” Then Edom came out against them with a powerful army and a strong hand.
NUM 20:21 21 Edom refused to allow Israel to cross his border. And Israel turned away from him.
NUM 20:22 22 They marched from Kadesh. The entire Israelite community came to Mount Hor.
NUM 20:23 23 The LORD said to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor on the border of the land of Edom:
NUM 20:24 24 Aaron will join his ancestors, for he may not enter the land that I’ve given to the Israelites, because you rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah.
NUM 20:25 25 Take Aaron and his son Eleazar, and bring them up Mount Hor.
NUM 20:26 26 Strip Aaron of his clothes and put them on Eleazar his son. Then Aaron will die there.
NUM 20:27 27 Moses did as the LORD commanded. They went up Mount Hor in the sight of the entire community.
NUM 20:28 28 Moses stripped Aaron of his clothes and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron died there at the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar descended from the mountain.
NUM 20:29 29 When the entire community saw that Aaron had died, the entire household of Israel wept thirty days for Aaron.
NUM 21:1 1 When the Canaanite king of Arad, who ruled in the arid southern plain, heard that the Israelites were coming on the Atharim road, he fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
NUM 21:2 2 Then Israel made a solemn promise to the LORD and said, “If you give this people into our hands, we will completely destroy their city.”
NUM 21:3 3 The LORD heard the voice of Israel and handed the Canaanites over. They completely destroyed them and their cities, so the name of the place is called Hormah.
NUM 21:4 4 They marched from Mount Hor on the Reed Sea road around the land of Edom. The people became impatient on the road.
NUM 21:5 5 The people spoke against God and Moses: “Why did you bring us up from Egypt to kill us in the desert, where there is no food or water. And we detest this miserable bread!”
NUM 21:6 6 So the LORD sent poisonous snakes among the people and they bit the people. Many of the Israelites died.
NUM 21:7 7 The people went to Moses and said, “We’ve sinned, for we spoke against the LORD and you. Pray to the LORD so that he will send the snakes away from us.” So Moses prayed for the people.
NUM 21:8 8 The LORD said to Moses, “Make a poisonous snake and place it on a pole. Whoever is bitten can look at it and live.”
NUM 21:9 9 Moses made a bronze snake and placed it on a pole. If a snake bit someone, that person could look at the bronze snake and live.
NUM 21:10 10 Then the Israelites marched and they camped at Oboth.
NUM 21:11 11 They marched from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the desert on the border of Moab toward the east.
NUM 21:12 12 From there they marched and camped in the Zered ravine.
NUM 21:13 13 From there they marched and camped across the Arnon in the desert that extends from the border of the Amorites, for the Arnon was the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
NUM 21:14 14 For this reason the scroll of the LORD ’s wars says: Waheb in Suphah and the ravines. The Arnon
NUM 21:15 15 and the ravines that extend to the settlement of Ar and lie along the border of Moab.
NUM 21:16 16 From there they marched to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people, and I’ll give them water.”
NUM 21:17 17 Then the Israelites sang this song: “Well, flow up! Sing about it!
NUM 21:18 18 The well that the officials dug, that the officials of the people hollowed out with the ruler’s scepter and their staffs.” They marched from the desert to Mattanah;
NUM 21:19 19 from Mattanah to Nahaliel; from Nahaliel to Bamoth;
NUM 21:20 20 from Bamoth to the valley in the Moabite countryside, to the top of Pisgah overlooking Jeshimon.
NUM 21:21 21 Then the Israelites sent messengers to Sihon the Amorite king:
NUM 21:22 22 “Let us pass through your land. We won’t turn aside into a field or vineyard. We won’t drink water from a well. We will walk on the King’s Highway until we cross your border.”
NUM 21:23 23 But Sihon wouldn’t allow the Israelites to cross his border. Sihon gathered all his people and went out to meet the Israelites in the desert. When he came to Jahaz, he attacked the Israelites.
NUM 21:24 24 The Israelites struck him down with their swords and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for the border of the Ammonites was fortified.
NUM 21:25 25 The Israelites took all these cities. Then the Israelites settled in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its villages.
NUM 21:26 26 Now Heshbon was the city of Sihon the Amorite king who had fought against the former king of Moab. He had taken all his land from him as far as the Arnon.
NUM 21:27 27 Therefore, the poets say: “Come to Heshbon, let it be built. Let the city of Sihon be established.
NUM 21:28 28 Fire went out from Heshbon, flame from Sihon’s city. It consumed Ar of Moab and swallowed up the shrines of the Arnon.
NUM 21:29 29 You are doomed, Moab! You are destroyed, people of Chemosh! He gave his sons as fugitives, and his daughters as captives to the Amorite king Sihon.
NUM 21:30 30 Yet we have thrown them down, destroying them from Heshbon to Dibon. We brought ruin until Nophah, which is by Medeba.”
NUM 21:31 31 Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
NUM 21:32 32 Moses sent spies to Jazer. They captured its villages and took possession of the Amorites who were there.
NUM 21:33 33 Then they turned and ascended the road of Bashan. Og, Bashan’s king, came out at Edrei to meet them in battle, he and all his people.
NUM 21:34 34 The LORD said to Moses: Don’t be afraid of him, for I have handed over all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon the Amorite king who ruled in Heshbon.
NUM 21:35 35 They slaughtered Og, his sons, and all his people until there were no survivors. Then they took possession of his land.
NUM 22:1 1 The Israelites marched and camped in the plains of Moab across the Jordan from Jericho.
NUM 22:2 2 Balak, Zippor’s son, saw everything that the Israelites did to the Amorites.
NUM 22:3 3 The Moabites greatly feared the people, for they were so numerous. The Moabites were terrified of the Israelites.
NUM 22:4 4 The Moabites said to the elders of Midian, “Now this assembly will devour everything around us, as an ox eats up the grass in the field.” Balak, Zippor’s son, was king of Moab at that time.
NUM 22:5 5 He sent messengers to Balaam, Beor’s son, at Pethor, which is by the river in the land of his people, to summon him: “A people has come out of Egypt, and they have now covered the land. They have settled next to me.
NUM 22:6 6 Now please come and curse this people for me because they are stronger than I am. Perhaps I’ll be able to destroy them and drive them from the land, for I know that whomever you bless is blessed and whomever you curse is cursed.”
NUM 22:7 7 So the elders of Moab and Midian went with the payment for divination in their hands. They came to Balaam and told him Balak’s words.
NUM 22:8 8 He said to them, “Spend the night here and I’ll bring back to you a word exactly as the LORD speaks to me.” So the officials of Moab stayed with Balaam.
NUM 22:9 9 God came to Balaam and said, “Who are these men with you?”
NUM 22:10 10 Balaam said to God, “Moab’s King Balak, Zippor’s son, sent them to me with the message,
NUM 22:11 11 ‘A people has come out of Egypt and covered the land. Now come and curse them for me. Perhaps I’ll be able to fight against them and drive them out.’”
NUM 22:12 12 God said to Balaam, “Don’t go with them. Don’t curse the people, because they are blessed.”
NUM 22:13 13 Then Balaam arose in the morning and said to Balak’s officials, “Go to your land, for the LORD has refused to allow me to go with you.”
NUM 22:14 14 The officials of Moab arose, they went to Balak, and they said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”
NUM 22:15 15 Balak continued to send other officials more numerous and important than these.
NUM 22:16 16 They came to Balaam and said to him, “This is what Balak, Zippor’s son, says: ‘Please let nothing hold you back from coming to me,
NUM 22:17 17 for I’ll greatly honor you and I’ll do anything you ask of me. Please come and curse this people for me.’”
NUM 22:18 18 Balaam answered and said to Balak’s servants, “If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I wouldn’t be able to do anything, small or great, to break the command of the LORD my God.
NUM 22:19 19 Now you also must remain the night here so that I may know what else the LORD may say to me.”
NUM 22:20 20 God came to Balaam in the night and said to him, “If the men have come to summon you, arise and go with them. But you must do only what I tell you to do.”
NUM 22:21 21 So Balaam arose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
NUM 22:22 22 Then God became angry because he went. So while he was riding on his donkey accompanied by his two servants, the LORD ’s messenger stood in the road as his adversary.
NUM 22:23 23 The donkey saw the LORD ’s messenger standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand, so the donkey turned from the road and went into the field. Balaam struck the donkey in order to turn him back onto the road.
NUM 22:24 24 Then the LORD ’s messenger stood in the narrow path between vineyards with a stone wall on each side.
NUM 22:25 25 When the donkey saw the LORD ’s messenger, it leaned against the wall and squeezed Balaam’s foot against the wall, so he continued to beat it.
NUM 22:26 26 The LORD ’s messenger persisted and crossed over and stood in a narrow place, where it wasn’t possible to turn either right or left.
NUM 22:27 27 The donkey saw the LORD ’s messenger and lay down underneath Balaam. Balaam became angry and beat the donkey with the rod.
NUM 22:28 28 Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth and it said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you’ve beaten me these three times?”
NUM 22:29 29 Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you’ve tormented me. If I had a sword in my hand, I’d kill you now.”
NUM 22:30 30 The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, on whom you’ve often ridden to this day? Have I been in the habit of doing this to you?” Balaam said, “No.”
NUM 22:31 31 Then the LORD uncovered Balaam’s eyes, and Balaam saw the LORD ’s messenger standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. Then he bowed low and worshipped.
NUM 22:32 32 The LORD ’s messenger said to him, “Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? I’ve come out here as an adversary, because you took the road recklessly in front of me.
NUM 22:33 33 The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If it hadn’t turned away from me, I would just now have killed you and let it live.”
NUM 22:34 34 Balaam said to the LORD ’s messenger, “I’ve sinned, because I didn’t know that you were standing against me in the road. Now, if you think it’s wrong, I’ll go back.”
NUM 22:35 35 The LORD ’s messenger said to Balaam, “Go with the men. But don’t say anything. Say only that which I tell you.” So Balaam went with Balak’s officials.
NUM 22:36 36 When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at Ir-moab, which is on the border of the Arnon at the farthest point of the border.
NUM 22:37 37 Balak said to Balaam, “Didn’t I send urgently and summon you? Why didn’t you come to me? Am I really not able to honor you?”
NUM 22:38 38 Balaam said to Balak, “I’ve now come to you. But I’m only able to speak whatever word God gives me to say. That is what I will speak.”
NUM 22:39 39 Then Balaam went with Balak and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
NUM 22:40 40 Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep and sent them to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
NUM 22:41 41 In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal, where he could see part of the people.
NUM 23:1 1 Balaam said to Balak, “Build me seven altars here and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”
NUM 23:2 2 Balak did as Balaam had said. Then Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
NUM 23:3 3 Balaam said to Balak, “Stay by your entirely burned offering. I will go and perhaps the LORD will grant me an appearance and speak. Whatever he shows me, I will tell you.” Then he went off to a high outlook.
NUM 23:4 4 God granted Balaam an appearance. Balaam said to him, “I have arranged seven altars and I have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.”
NUM 23:5 5 The LORD gave Balaam something to say, and said to him, “Return to Balak and say this.”
NUM 23:6 6 Balaam returned to him, while he and all the officials of Moab were standing next to his entirely burned offering.
NUM 23:7 7 Then he raised his voice and made his address: “From Aram Balak led me, the king of Moab, from the eastern mountains. Come, curse Jacob for me; come, denounce Israel.
NUM 23:8 8 How can I curse whom God hasn’t cursed? How can I denounce whom God hasn’t denounced?
NUM 23:9 9 From the top of the rocks I see him; from the hills I gaze on him. Here is a people living alone; it doesn’t consider itself among the nations.
NUM 23:10 10 Who can count the dust of Jacob, or number a fourth of Israel? Let me die the death of those who do right, and let my end be like his.”
NUM 23:11 11 Then Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemy. But now you’ve blessed him.”
NUM 23:12 12 He answered and said, “Don’t I have to take care to speak whatever the LORD gives me to say?”
NUM 23:13 13 Then Balak said to Balaam, “Come with me, please, to another place where you’ll see them. You’ll see only part of them. You won’t see all of them. Then curse them for me from there.”
NUM 23:14 14 He took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah. He built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
NUM 23:15 15 Then Balaam said to Balak, “Stand here by your entirely burned offering, while I seek an appearance over there.”
NUM 23:16 16 The LORD granted Balaam an appearance and gave him a message. He said, “Return to Balak and say this.”
NUM 23:17 17 Balaam approached Balak, who was standing by his entirely burned offering with the officials of Moab. Balak said to him, “What did the LORD say?”
NUM 23:18 18 Then Balaam raised his voice and made his address: “Arise, Balak, and listen; hear me out, Zippor’s son.
NUM 23:19 19 God isn’t a man that he would lie, or a human being that he would change his mind. Has he ever spoken and not done it, or promised and not fulfilled it?
NUM 23:20 20 I received a blessing, and he blessed. I can’t take it back.
NUM 23:21 21 He hasn’t envisioned misfortune for Jacob, nor has he seen trouble for Israel. The LORD his God is with him, proclaimed as his king.
NUM 23:22 22 God, who brought them out of Egypt, is like a magnificent wild bull for him.
NUM 23:23 23 There is no omen against Jacob, no divination against Israel. Instantly it is told to Jacob, and to Israel, what God performs.
NUM 23:24 24 A people now rises like a lioness, like a lion it stands up. It doesn’t lie down until it eats the prey and drinks the blood of the slain.”
NUM 23:25 25 Then Balak said to Balaam, “Don’t curse them or bless them.”
NUM 23:26 26 But Balaam answered and said to Balak, “Didn’t I say to you, ‘I’ll do whatever the LORD tells me to’?”
NUM 23:27 27 Balak said to Balaam, “Please come and I’ll take you to another place. Perhaps God will prefer it, so that you could curse him for me from there.”
NUM 23:28 28 So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks Jeshimon.
NUM 23:29 29 Balaam said to Balak, “Build me seven altars here and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”
NUM 23:30 30 Balak did just as Balaam said. He offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
NUM 24:1 1 Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless the Israelites, so he didn’t go as the other times to seek omens. Instead, he turned toward the desert.
NUM 24:2 2 Balaam looked up and saw Israel camping by tribes. Then God’s spirit came on him.
NUM 24:3 3 He raised his voice and made his address: “The oracle of Balaam, Beor’s son; the oracle of a man whose eye is open.
NUM 24:4 4 The oracle of one who hears God’s speech, who perceives the Almighty’s visions, who falls down with eyes uncovered.
NUM 24:5 5 How beautiful are your tents, Jacob, your camps, Israel!
NUM 24:6 6 Like palm groves that stretch out, like gardens next to a river, like eaglewood trees that the LORD has planted, like cedar trees next to water.
NUM 24:7 7 Water will drip from his branches; his seed will have plenty of water; his king will be higher than Agag, and his kingdom will be lifted up.
NUM 24:8 8 God, who brought him from Egypt, is like a magnificent wild bull for him. He will devour enemy nations and break their bones; he will strike with his arrows.
NUM 24:9 9 He crouched and lay down like a lion; like a lioness, who can make her rise? The one blessing you will be blessed, and the one cursing you will be cursed.”
NUM 24:10 10 Balak was angry with Balaam. He pounded his fists. Balak said to Balaam, “I summoned you to curse my enemies, but now you’ve given a blessing these three times.
NUM 24:11 11 Now get out of here and go home. I told you I’d greatly honor you, but the LORD has denied you any honor.”
NUM 24:12 12 Balaam said to Balak, “Didn’t I tell your messengers, whom you sent to me,
NUM 24:13 13 ‘If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I wouldn’t be able to break the LORD ’s command for good or ill by my own will. I’ll say whatever the LORD says’?
NUM 24:14 14 So now I’m going to my people. Let me advise you what this people will do to your people in the days to come.”
NUM 24:15 15 He raised his voice and made his address: “The oracle of Balaam, Beor’s son, the oracle of a man whose eye is open.
NUM 24:16 16 The oracle of one who hears God’s speech, and understands the Most High’s knowledge, who perceives the Almighty’s visions, who falls down with eyes uncovered.
NUM 24:17 17 I see him, but not now; I look at him, but not nearby. A star comes from Jacob; a scepter arises from Israel, smashing Moab’s forehead, the head of all the Sethites.
NUM 24:18 18 Edom will become a possession, Seir a possession of its enemies. But Israel acts powerfully.
NUM 24:19 19 Someone from Jacob will rule and destroy the survivors from Ir.”
NUM 24:20 20 He looked at Amalek and raised his voice and gave his address: “Amalek is foremost among the nations, but its end is to perish forever.”
NUM 24:21 21 He looked at the Kenites and raised his voice and gave his address: “Your dwelling is secure; your nest is set in the rock.
NUM 24:22 22 Yet Kain will burn when Asshur takes you away captive.”
NUM 24:23 23 He raised his voice and made his address: “How terrible! Who will live when God does this?
NUM 24:24 24 Ships from Kittim will attack Asshur; they will attack Eber, and even he will perish forever.”
NUM 24:25 25 Then Balaam arose, set out, and returned home. Balak also went on his way.
NUM 25:1 1 When the Israelites lived at Shittim, the people made themselves impure by having illicit sex with Moabite women.
NUM 25:2 2 The Moabite women invited the people to the sacrifices for their god. So the people ate a meal, and they worshipped their god.
NUM 25:3 3 Israel became attached to the Baal of Peor, and the LORD was angry at the Israelites.
NUM 25:4 4 The LORD said to Moses: Take all the leaders of the people and kill them on behalf of the LORD in broad daylight, so that the LORD ’s anger turns away from Israel.
NUM 25:5 5 Then Moses said to Israel’s officials, “Each of you: kill your men who are attached to the Baal of Peor.”
NUM 25:6 6 An Israelite man brought a Midianite woman to his brothers in the sight of Moses and the entire Israelite community, who were weeping at the entrance of the meeting tent.
NUM 25:7 7 When Phinehas (Eleazar’s son and Aaron the priest’s grandson) saw this, he arose in the middle of the community, took a spear in his hand,
NUM 25:8 8 went after the Israelite man into the chamber, and stabbed the two of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through the stomach. Then the plague stopped spreading among the Israelites.
NUM 25:9 9 Yet those who died by the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.

NUM 25:11 11 Phinehas (Eleazar’s son and Aaron the priest’s grandson) has turned back my rage toward the Israelites. Because he was jealous for me among you, I didn’t consume the Israelites due to my jealousy.
NUM 25:12 12 Therefore, say: I’m now giving him my covenant of well-being.
NUM 25:13 13 It will be for him and his descendants a covenant of permanent priesthood, because he was jealous for his God and sought reconciliation for the Israelites.

NUM 27:4 4 Why should our father’s name be taken away from his clan because he didn’t have a son? Give us property among our father’s brothers.”
NUM 27:5 5 Moses brought their case before the LORD .
NUM 27:6 6 The LORD said to Moses:
NUM 27:7 7 Zelophehad’s daughters are right in what they are saying. By all means, give them property as an inheritance among their father’s brothers. Hand over their father’s inheritance to them.
NUM 27:8 8 Speak to the Israelites and say: If a man dies and doesn’t have a son, you must hand his inheritance over to his daughters.
NUM 27:9 9 If he doesn’t have a daughter, you will give his inheritance to his brothers.
NUM 27:10 10 If he doesn’t have any brothers, you should give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.
NUM 27:11 11 If his father had no brothers, you should give his inheritance to his nearest relative from his clan. He will take possession of it. This will be a regulation and a case law for the Israelites, as the LORD commanded Moses.

NUM 28:2 2 Command the Israelites and say to them: Make sure to offer to me my offering, my food, my food gift as a soothing smell to me at its appointed time.
NUM 28:3 3 You will say to them: This is the food gift that you must present to the LORD : two flawless one-year-old lambs as the regular entirely burned offering every day.
NUM 28:4 4 One lamb you will offer in the morning and the second at twilight,
NUM 28:5 5 with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering mixed with a fourth of a hin of beaten oil.
NUM 28:6 6 It is the regular entirely burned offering begun at Mount Sinai, a food gift that is a soothing smell to the LORD .
NUM 28:7 7 Their drink offering will be a fourth of a hin for each lamb. In the sanctuary a drink offering of brandy will be poured out for the LORD .
NUM 28:8 8 The second lamb you will offer at twilight like the grain offering and the drink offering in the morning. You will offer a food gift that is a soothing smell to the LORD .
NUM 28:9 9 On the Sabbath day: two flawless one-year-old male lambs and two-tenths of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with oil, and its drink offering.
NUM 28:10 10 This is the entirely burned offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular entirely burned offering and its drink offering.

NUM 28:13 13 and one-tenth of fine flour for a grain offering mixed with oil for each lamb. It is an entirely burned offering with a soothing smell, a food gift to the LORD .
NUM 28:14 14 Their drink offerings will be half a hin of wine for a bull, a third a hin of wine for a ram, and a fourth a hin of wine for a lamb. This is the monthly entirely burned offering for every month through the months of the year.
NUM 28:15 15 There will be one male goat for a purification offering to the LORD in addition to the regular entirely burned offering and its drink offering.
NUM 28:16 16 On the fourteenth day of the first month there will be a Passover offering to the LORD .
NUM 28:17 17 On the fifteenth day of this month there will be a festival. For seven days unleavened bread will be eaten.
NUM 28:18 18 The first day will be a holy occasion. You will not do any job-related work.
NUM 28:19 19 You will bring a food gift, an entirely burned offering to the LORD : two bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven male lambs one year old. They will be flawless.
NUM 28:20 20 Their grain offering will be fine flour mixed with oil. You will offer three-tenths for the bull, two-tenths for the ram,
NUM 28:21 21 and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs,
NUM 28:22 22 along with one male goat for a purification offering to seek reconciliation for yourselves.
NUM 28:23 23 You will offer these in addition to the entirely burned offering of the morning, which is the regular entirely burned offering.
NUM 28:24 24 Like these, you will also offer each day for seven days a food gift as a soothing smell to the LORD . It will be offered in addition to the regular entirely burned offering and its drink offering.
NUM 28:25 25 The seventh day will be a holy occasion for you. You will not do any job-related work.

NUM 28:28 28 Their grain offering will be fine flour mixed with oil: three-tenths for each bull, two-tenths for the one ram,
NUM 28:29 29 and one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
NUM 28:30 30 Offer one male goat to seek reconciliation for yourselves.
NUM 28:31 31 You will offer these in addition to the regular entirely burned offering, its grain offering and drink offerings. They will be flawless.
