NUM 29:24 24 The grain offering and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs will be as prescribed for their number.

NUM 29:27 27 The grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs will be as prescribed for their number.
NUM 29:28 28 There will be one male goat for a purification offering in addition to the regular entirely burned offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
NUM 29:29 29 On the sixth day: eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs one year old, all flawless.
NUM 29:30 30 The grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs will be as prescribed for their number.
NUM 29:31 31 There will be one male goat for a purification offering in addition to the regular entirely burned offering with its grain offering and its drink offerings.

NUM 29:33 33 The grain offering and their drink offering for the bulls, rams, and lambs will be as prescribed for their number.
NUM 29:34 34 There will be one male goat for a purification offering in addition to the regular entirely burned offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
NUM 29:35 35 On the eighth day you will have a holiday. You will not do any job-related work.
NUM 29:36 36 You will present an entirely burned offering, a food gift as a soothing smell to the LORD : one bull, one ram, and seven male lambs one year old, all without blemish.
NUM 29:37 37 The grain offering and their drink offerings for the bull, ram, and lambs will be as prescribed for their number.
NUM 29:38 38 There will be one male goat for a purification offering in addition to the regular entirely burned offering with its grain offering and its drink offering.
NUM 29:39 39 These you will offer to the LORD at your appointed times in addition to your payments for solemn promises, your spontaneous gifts, your entirely burned offerings, your grain offerings, your drink offerings, and your well-being sacrifices.
NUM 29:40 40 Moses told the Israelites everything that the LORD commanded Moses.
NUM 30:1 1 Moses spoke to the leaders of the tribes of the Israelites: This is what the LORD has commanded:
NUM 30:2 2 When a man makes a solemn promise to the LORD or swears a solemn pledge of binding obligation for himself, he cannot break his word. He must do everything he said.
NUM 30:3 3 When a woman makes a solemn promise to the LORD or a binding obligation while she is young and in her father’s household,
NUM 30:4 4 and her father hears her solemn promise or her binding obligation for herself and keeps silent —then all her solemn promises and any of her binding obligations for herself will stand.
NUM 30:5 5 But if her father expresses disapproval to her on the day that he hears her, none of her solemn promises nor any of her binding obligations for herself will stand. The LORD will forgive her, because her father expressed disapproval to her.
NUM 30:6 6 If she marries while her solemn promise is in effect or makes a statement by which she binds herself,
NUM 30:7 7 and her husband hears it and on the day he hears it keeps silent—her solemn promises will stand as well as her binding obligations for herself.
NUM 30:8 8 But if on the day that her husband hears it he expresses disapproval to her, he can break her solemn promise and the statement by which she bound herself. Then the LORD will forgive her.
NUM 30:9 9 Every solemn promise of a widow or a divorced woman who makes a binding obligation for herself will stand.
NUM 30:10 10 If a woman makes a solemn promise in her husband’s household or makes a binding obligation for herself with a solemn pledge,
NUM 30:11 11 and her husband hears, keeps silent, and doesn’t express disapproval to her—then all her solemn promises will stand and all her binding obligations for herself will stand.
NUM 30:12 12 If her husband breaks them on the day he hears them, then whatever she said with regard to her solemn promises or the binding obligations for herself will not stand. Her husband has broken them. The LORD will forgive her.
NUM 30:13 13 Her husband may allow any solemn promise or any binding pledge of self-denial to stand or be broken.
NUM 30:14 14 But if her husband keeps silent from one day to the next, he has upheld all her solemn promises, or all her binding obligations. He has upheld them because he remained silent on the day he heard them.
NUM 30:15 15 If he breaks them after he has heard them, he will assume her guilt.
NUM 30:16 16 These are the regulations that the LORD commanded Moses concerning a husband and his wife and between a father and his daughter while she is young and in her father’s household.
NUM 31:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 31:2 2 Take just reparations for the Israelites from the Midianites. Afterward you will join your ancestors.
NUM 31:3 3 Moses spoke to the people: “Equip some of your men for battle so that they may go against Midian and execute the LORD ’s just punishment against Midian.
NUM 31:4 4 You will send out for battle one thousand from each of the tribes of Israel.”
NUM 31:5 5 From the thousands of Israel, one thousand from each tribe were selected. Twelve thousand were equipped for battle.
NUM 31:6 6 Moses sent them to battle, one thousand from each tribe, along with Phinehas, Eleazar the priest’s son, who carried the sanctuary equipment and the trumpets for sounding the alarm in his hand.
NUM 31:7 7 They battled against Midian as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they killed every male.
NUM 31:8 8 They killed the kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian, along with others slain. They also killed Balaam, Beor’s son, with the sword.
NUM 31:9 9 The Israelites took captive the Midianite women, their little ones, all their cattle, their herds, and their possessions.
NUM 31:10 10 They burned all the cities where they lived and their encampments.
NUM 31:11 11 They took all the spoils of war and the valuable property, both human and animal,
NUM 31:12 12 and they brought the captives, the valuable property, and the spoils of war to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the Israelite community, at the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
NUM 31:13 13 Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chiefs of the community went to meet them outside the camp.
NUM 31:14 14 Moses became angry with the commanders of the army, the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds, who came back from the battle.
NUM 31:15 15 Moses said to them, “Have you let all the women live?
NUM 31:16 16 These very women, on Balaam’s advice, made the Israelites break faith with the LORD in the affair at Peor, so there was a plague among the LORD ’s community.
NUM 31:17 17 Now kill every male child and every female who has known a man intimately by sleeping with him.
NUM 31:18 18 But all the young girls who have not known a man intimately by sleeping with him, spare for yourselves.
NUM 31:19 19 You will remain outside the camp for seven days. Everyone among you or your captives who has killed a person or touched a corpse must purify themselves on the third and seventh days.
NUM 31:20 20 You must also purify every garment, and everything made of leather, goats’ hair, or wood.”
NUM 31:21 21 Eleazar the priest said to the men of battle who had gone out to war, “This is the regulation in the Instruction that the LORD commanded Moses:
NUM 31:22 22 Gold, silver, copper, iron, tin, and lead—
NUM 31:23 23 anything that can withstand fire—you will put through the fire and it will be clean. It will also be purified with the water of purification. Anything that isn’t able to withstand fire, you will immerse in water.
NUM 31:24 24 You must wash your clothes on the seventh day and you will be clean. Afterward you may enter the camp.”
NUM 31:25 25 The LORD said to Moses:
NUM 31:26 26 You, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the community’s households must take an inventory of the valuable property and the captives, both human and animals,
NUM 31:27 27 and divide the valuable property between the warriors who went into battle and the entire community.
NUM 31:28 28 You will offer as tribute to the LORD from each warrior who went into battle one living being in five hundred, whether human, oxen, donkeys, or flocks.
NUM 31:29 29 Take it from the warriors’ half and give it to Eleazar the priest as a gift offering to the LORD .
NUM 31:30 30 But from the Israelites’ half you will take one out of every fifty, whether from human, oxen, donkeys, or flock—all the animals. You will give them to the Levites who carry out the duties of the LORD ’s dwelling.
NUM 31:31 31 Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.
NUM 31:32 32 The valuable property remaining from the spoils of war that the people of the army had taken was 675,000 sheep,
NUM 31:33 33 72,000 oxen,
NUM 31:34 34 61,000 donkeys,
NUM 31:35 35 and 32,000 women who hadn’t known a man intimately by sleeping with him.
NUM 31:36 36 The half-share of those who had gone out to battle numbered 337,500 sheep,
NUM 31:37 37 of which the LORD ’s tribute was 675.
NUM 31:38 38 The oxen were 36,000, of which the LORD ’s tribute was 72.
NUM 31:39 39 The donkeys were 30,500, of which the LORD ’s tribute was 61.
NUM 31:40 40 Humans were 16,000, of which the LORD ’s tribute was 32 persons.
NUM 31:41 41 Moses gave the tribute, a gift offering for the LORD , to Eleazar the priest as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NUM 31:42 42 As for the half-share of the Israelites that Moses divided from those who had gone out to battle:
NUM 31:43 43 the community’s half-share was 337,500 sheep,
NUM 31:44 44 36,000 oxen,
NUM 31:45 45 30,500 donkeys,
NUM 31:46 46 and 16,000 humans.
NUM 31:47 47 Moses took from the Israelites’ half one out of every fifty, from humans and animals. He gave them to the Levites who carry out the duties of the LORD ’s dwelling, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
NUM 31:48 48 The commanders over the thousands of the army, officers over thousands and officers over hundreds, approached Moses
NUM 31:49 49 and said to Moses, “Your servants have counted the warriors in our charge and not one of us is missing.
NUM 31:50 50 We have brought the LORD ’s offering that each found, gold articles—anklets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces—to seek reconciliation for ourselves before the LORD .”
NUM 31:51 51 Moses and Eleazar the priest took all the gold articles from them.
NUM 31:52 52 All the gold for the gift offering that was presented to the LORD from the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds was sixteen thousand seven hundred fifty shekels.
NUM 31:53 53 Each of the men of battle took spoils of war for himself.
NUM 31:54 54 Yet Moses and Eleazar the priest also received the gold from the officers of thousands and of hundreds, and they brought it to the meeting tent as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD .
NUM 32:1 1 The livestock owned by the Reubenites and the Gadites were unusually vast and numerous. They saw that the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead were exactly the place for livestock.
NUM 32:2 2 So the Gadites and the Reubenites came and said to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chiefs of the community:
NUM 32:3 3 “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon is
NUM 32:4 4 the land that the LORD struck down before the Israelite community. It is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock.”
NUM 32:5 5 They said, “If you approve our request, give this land to your servants as property. Don’t make us cross the Jordan.”
NUM 32:6 6 Moses said to the Gadites and the Reubenites, “Should your brothers go to war, while you stay here?
NUM 32:7 7 Why would you destroy the Israelites’ resolve to cross into the land that the LORD gave them?
NUM 32:8 8 Your ancestors did this, when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to inspect the land.
NUM 32:9 9 They went up to the Cluster ravine, saw the land, and destroyed the Israelites’ resolve to enter the land that the LORD had given them.
NUM 32:10 10 The LORD became angry on that day and promised,
NUM 32:11 11 ‘None of the persons that went up from Egypt, those 20 years old and above, will see the fertile ground that I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they didn’t remain true to me,
NUM 32:12 12 except Caleb, Jephunneh the Kenizzite’s son, and Joshua, Nun’s son, because they remained true to the LORD .’
NUM 32:13 13 The LORD became angry with the Israelites and made them wander in the desert for forty years until the entire generation had died, which had done evil in the LORD ’s eyes.
NUM 32:14 14 Now you’ve taken the place of your ancestors, a group of sinful men, to intensify the LORD ’s anger against Israel.
NUM 32:15 15 If you turn away from him, he will turn away again to abandon Israel in the desert. Then you will destroy this entire people.”
NUM 32:16 16 So they approached him and said, “We will build walled enclosures here for our livestock and towns for our children.
NUM 32:17 17 Then we will eagerly fight in front of the Israelites until we have brought them into their place. Our children will live in the fortified cities because of the land’s inhabitants.
NUM 32:18 18 And we won’t return to our homes until each one of the Israelites takes possession of his property.
NUM 32:19 19 We won’t inherit land with them there across the Jordan, because we’ve received our property on the east side of the Jordan.”
NUM 32:20 20 Moses said to them, “Do this and fight before the LORD in war.
NUM 32:21 21 All of you who are equipped for war, cross the Jordan before the LORD until he has driven his enemies out before him
NUM 32:22 22 and the land is subdued in the LORD ’s presence. Then you may return innocently before the LORD and Israel, and this land will be your property before the LORD .
NUM 32:23 23 But if you don’t do this, you’ve sinned against the LORD . Know that your sin will find you.
NUM 32:24 24 So build towns for your children and walled enclosures for your flocks, but do what you have promised.”
NUM 32:25 25 The Gadites and the Reubenites said to Moses, “Your servants will do as my master has commanded.
NUM 32:26 26 Our children, wives, livestock, and all of our animals will remain in the cities of Gilead.
NUM 32:27 27 But your servants, everyone equipped for war before the LORD , will go over to do battle as my master said.”
NUM 32:28 28 Moses made demands for them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua, Nun’s son, and to the leaders of the households of the Israelite tribes.
NUM 32:29 29 Moses said to them, “If the Gadites and the Reubenites cross the Jordan with you, each equipped for battle before the LORD , and the land is subdued before you, then you will give them the land of Gilead as a possession.
NUM 32:30 30 If, however, they don’t cross with you, equipped for war, they will take possession of property with you in the land of Canaan.”
NUM 32:31 31 The Gadites and the Reubenites answered, “We’ll do just as the LORD has spoken to your servants.
NUM 32:32 32 We’ll cross into the land of Canaan before the LORD , equipped for war. But the property we inherit will be across the Jordan.”
NUM 32:33 33 So Moses gave to them—to the Gadites, the Reubenites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, Joseph’s son—the kingdom of Sihon the king of the Amorites, and the kingdom of Og the king of Bashan, including the land, its cities, and the territory surrounding the land’s cities.
NUM 32:34 34 The Gadites built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
NUM 32:35 35 Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
NUM 32:36 36 Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran, fortified cities and walled enclosures for flocks.
NUM 32:37 37 The Reubenites built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
NUM 32:38 38 Nebo, and Baal-meon (whose names were changed), and Sibmah. They named the cities that they built.
NUM 32:39 39 The descendants of Machir, Manasseh’s son, went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.
NUM 32:40 40 So Moses gave Gilead to Machir, Manasseh’s son, and he lived there.
NUM 32:41 41 Manasseh’s son Jair went and captured their villages and named them Havvoth-jair.
NUM 32:42 42 Nobah went and captured Kenath and its surrounding villages. He renamed it Nobah after himself.

NUM 33:39 39 Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.

NUM 33:53 53 You will take possession of the land and live in it, because I’ve given the land to you to possess.
NUM 33:54 54 You will divide up the land by lot according to your clans. To the large you will make its inheritance large, and to the small you will make its inheritance small. To whomever the lot falls, that place will be his. You will inherit land according to your ancestral tribes.
NUM 33:55 55 But if you don’t drive out the inhabitants of the land before you, then those you allow to remain will prick your eyes and be thorns in your side. They will harass you in the land in which you are living.
NUM 33:56 56 Then what I intended to do to them, I’ll do to you.
NUM 34:1 1 The LORD said to Moses:
NUM 34:2 2 Command the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that will fall to you as an inheritance. The land of Canaan according to its boundaries:
NUM 34:3 3 Your southern boundary extends from the Zin desert alongside Edom. Your southern border extends from the edge of the Dead Sea on the east.

NUM 35:1 1 The LORD spoke to Moses in the Moab plains by the Jordan across from Jericho:
NUM 35:2 2 Command the Israelites that they give cities from their inherited property to the Levites in which to live. You will also give the Levites pastures around their cities.
NUM 35:3 3 The cities will be theirs in which to live. Their pastures will be for their cattle, their possessions, and all their animals.
NUM 35:4 4 The pastures of the cities that you must give to the Levites will extend from the wall of the city outward for one thousand five hundred feet in all directions.
NUM 35:5 5 You will measure outside the city on the east side three thousand feet, on the south side three thousand feet, on the west side three thousand feet, and on the north side three thousand feet, with the city in the middle. These will be their cities’ pastures.
NUM 35:6 6 Six of the cities that you give to the Levites will be refuge cities. You will allow the person who kills someone to flee there. In addition to these you will give them forty-two cities.
NUM 35:7 7 All the cities that you give to the Levites will total forty-eight, along with their pastures.
NUM 35:8 8 As for the cities that you give from the property of the Israelites, you will take more from the larger tribes and less from the smaller. Each in proportion to its inheritance will give cities to the Levites.
NUM 35:9 9 The LORD spoke to Moses:
NUM 35:10 10 Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
NUM 35:11 11 identify for yourselves cities to be refuge cities, where a person who kills someone by accident may flee.
NUM 35:12 12 The cities will be for you a place of refuge from the close relative of the dead. The person who killed someone may not be put to death until he stands before the community for judgment.
NUM 35:13 13 You will establish six refuge cities for yourselves.
NUM 35:14 14 You will establish three cities across the Jordan and three cities in the land of Canaan. They will be the refuge cities.
NUM 35:15 15 These six cities will be refuge for Israelites, immigrants, and temporary residents, as a place to flee for anyone who kills a person by accident.
NUM 35:16 16 But if someone strikes a person with an iron object and he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must definitely be put to death.
NUM 35:17 17 If someone strikes another with a stone in hand that could cause death and he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must definitely be put to death.
NUM 35:18 18 Or if someone strikes with a wood object in hand that could cause death, he is a murderer. The murderer must definitely be put to death.
NUM 35:19 19 The close relative responsible for the blood of the dead is the one who will put the murderer to death. When he meets him, he will execute him.
NUM 35:20 20 If in hatred someone hits another or throws something at him with premeditation, he will be put to death.
NUM 35:21 21 Or if in hostility someone strikes another with his hand and he dies, the one who struck is a murderer and he will be put to death. The close relative will put the murderer to death when he meets him.
NUM 35:22 22 But if suddenly and without hostility someone hits another or throws any object at him without premeditation,
NUM 35:23 23 or accidentally drops any stone on him that could cause death and he dies—even though they weren’t enemies and no evil was intended—
NUM 35:24 24 then the community must come to a verdict between the killer and the close relative in accordance with these case laws.
NUM 35:25 25 The community will protect the killer from the hand of the close relative and return him to the refuge city where he fled. He will live there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with holy oil.
NUM 35:26 26 But if the killer ever goes outside the boundaries of the refuge city where he fled
NUM 35:27 27 and the close relative finds him outside the boundary of his refuge city and kills him, he will not be responsible for his blood.
NUM 35:28 28 The killer must live in his refuge city until the high priest’s death. After the high priest’s death the killer may return to the land he owns.
NUM 35:29 29 These will be the regulations and case laws for all time in all your settlements.
NUM 35:30 30 Anyone who kills another will be executed on the evidence of witnesses. But one witness alone cannot testify against a person for a death sentence.
NUM 35:31 31 You may not accept a ransom for the life of a killer, who is guilty of a capital crime, for he must definitely be put to death.
NUM 35:32 32 You may not accept a ransom for someone who has fled to his refuge city so that he can return and live in the land before the priest’s death.
NUM 35:33 33 You may not pollute the land in which you live, for the blood pollutes the land. There can be no recovery for the land from the blood that is shed in it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
NUM 35:34 34 You will not make the land in which you live unclean, the land in the middle of which I reside, for I the LORD reside among the Israelites.
NUM 36:1 1 The leaders of the households of the clans of Gilead, Machir’s son and Manasseh’s grandson, of Joseph’s clans, approached and spoke before Moses and the chiefs, who were the leaders of the Israelite households.
NUM 36:2 2 They said, “The LORD commanded my master to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the Israelites. But my master was also commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.
NUM 36:3 3 If they are married to someone from another Israelite tribe, their inheritance will be taken away from our household and given to another tribe into which they marry. Then it will be taken away from the lot of our inheritance.
NUM 36:4 4 At the Israelite Jubilee, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe into which they married. Then their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe.”
NUM 36:5 5 Then Moses commanded the Israelites according to the LORD ’s word: “The tribe of Joseph’s descendants are correct in what they’re saying.
NUM 36:6 6 This is the word that the LORD commands to Zelophehad’s daughters: They may marry whomever seems best to them, but they may only marry into one of the clans of their ancestral tribe,
NUM 36:7 7 so that the inheritance of the Israelites doesn’t transfer from one tribe to another. The Israelites will each retain the tribal inheritance of his ancestral tribe.
NUM 36:8 8 Every daughter who inherits land from an Israelite tribe must marry into one of the clans of her father’s tribe. In this way each Israelite will own the land of his ancestors.
NUM 36:9 9 An inheritance of land may not be transferred from one tribe to another, for the Israelite tribes will each retain its own inheritance.”
NUM 36:10 10 Zelophehad’s daughters did as the LORD commanded Moses.
NUM 36:11 11 Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, Zelophehad’s daughters, married their cousins.
NUM 36:12 12 They married into the clan of Manasseh, Joseph’s son. Their inheritance remained in the tribe of their father’s clan.
NUM 36:13 13 These are the commandments and the case laws that the LORD commanded the Israelites through Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.
DEU 1:1 1 These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel across the Jordan River, in the desert, on the plain across from Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Di-zahab. (
DEU 1:2 2 It is eleven days from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea along the Mount Seir route.)
DEU 1:3 3 It was in the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, that Moses spoke to the Israelites precisely what the LORD had commanded him for them. (
DEU 1:4 4 This was after the defeat of Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled in Heshbon, and Og, Bashan’s king, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei.)
DEU 1:5 5 Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this Instruction. He said the following:
DEU 1:6 6 At Horeb, the LORD our God told us: You’ve been at this mountain long enough.
DEU 1:7 7 Get going! Enter the hills of the Amorites and the surrounding areas in the desert, the highlands, the lowlands, the arid southern region, and the seacoast—the land of the Canaanites—and the Lebanon range, all the way to the great Euphrates River.
DEU 1:8 8 Look, I have laid the land before you. Go and possess the land that I promised to give to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as well as to their descendants after them.
DEU 1:9 9 At that same time, I told you: I can’t handle all of you by myself.
DEU 1:10 10 The LORD your God has multiplied your number—you are now as countless as the stars in the sky.
DEU 1:11 11 May the LORD , your ancestors’ God, continue to multiply you—a thousand times more! And may God bless you, just as he promised.
DEU 1:12 12 But how can I handle all your troubles, burdens, and disputes by myself?
DEU 1:13 13 Now, for each of your tribes, choose wise, discerning, and well-regarded individuals. I will appoint them as your leaders.
DEU 1:14 14 You answered me: “What you have proposed is a good idea.”
DEU 1:15 15 So I took leading individuals from your tribes, people who were wise and well-regarded, and I set them up as your leaders. There were commanders over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, as well as officials for each of your tribes.
DEU 1:16 16 At that same time, I commanded your judges: Listen to your fellow tribe members and judge fairly, whether the dispute is between one fellow tribe member or between a tribe member and an immigrant.
DEU 1:17 17 Don’t show favoritism in a decision. Hear both sides out, whether the person is important or not. Don’t be afraid of anyone because the ruling belongs to God. Any dispute that is too difficult for you to decide, bring to me and I will take care of it.
DEU 1:18 18 So at that time, I commanded you concerning everything you were to do.
DEU 1:19 19 We left Horeb and journeyed through that vast and terrifying desert you saw, on the way to the hills of the Amorites, exactly as the LORD our God commanded us. Then we arrived at Kadesh-barnea.
DEU 1:20 20 I said to you: You have come to the hills of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving to us.
DEU 1:21 21 Look! The LORD your God has laid out the land before you. Go up and take it, just as the LORD , your ancestors’ God, has promised you. Don’t be afraid! Don’t be frightened!
DEU 1:22 22 Then all of you approached me, saying, “Let’s send spies ahead of us—they can check out the land for us. Then they can return with word about the route we should use and bring a report about the cities that we’ll be entering.”
DEU 1:23 23 This idea seemed good to me, so I selected twelve men, one from each tribe.
DEU 1:24 24 These set out and went up into the hills, going as far as the Cluster ravine. They walked all around that area.
DEU 1:25 25 They took some of the land’s fruit and then came back down to us. They reported to us: “The land that the LORD our God is giving to us is wonderful!”
DEU 1:26 26 But you weren’t willing to go up. You rejected the LORD your God’s instruction.
DEU 1:27 27 You complained in your tents, saying things like, “The LORD hates us! That’s why he brought us out of Egypt—to hand us over to the Amorites, to destroy us!
DEU 1:28 28 What are we doing? Our brothers have made our hearts sick by saying, ‘People far stronger and much taller than we live there, and the cities are huge, with walls sky-high! Worse still, we saw the descendants of the Anakites there!’”
DEU 1:29 29 But I said to you: Don’t be terrified! Don’t be afraid of them!
DEU 1:30 30 The LORD your God is going before you. He will fight for you just as he fought for you in Egypt while you watched,
DEU 1:31 31 and as you saw him do in the desert. Throughout your entire journey, until you reached this very place, the LORD your God has carried you just as a parent carries a child.
DEU 1:32 32 But you had no faith in the LORD your God about this matter,
DEU 1:33 33 even though he went ahead of you, scouting places where you should camp, in fire by night, so you could see the road you were taking, and in cloud during the daytime.
DEU 1:34 34 The LORD heard what you said. He was angry and he swore:
DEU 1:35 35 Not even one of these people—this wicked generation!—will see the wonderful land that I promised to give to your ancestors.
DEU 1:36 36 The only exception is Caleb, Jephunneh’s son. He will see it. I will give the land he walked on to him and his children for this reason: he was completely devoted to the LORD . (
DEU 1:37 37 The LORD was even angry with me because of what you did. “You won’t enter the land either,” God said.
DEU 1:38 38 “But Nun’s son Joshua, your assistant, will enter it. Strengthen him because he’s the one who will help Israel inherit the land.”)
DEU 1:39 39 Now as for your toddlers, those you said would be taken in war, and your young children who don’t yet know right and wrong—they will enter the land. I will give it to them. They will possess it!
DEU 1:40 40 But you all must now turn around. Head back toward the wilderness along the route of the Reed Sea.
DEU 1:41 41 You replied to me: “We’ve sinned against the LORD ! We will go up! We will fight, just as the LORD our God commanded.” Each one of you grabbed your weapons. You thought it would be easy to go up into the hills.
DEU 1:42 42 But the LORD told me: Tell them: Don’t go up! Don’t fight because I will not be with you. You will be defeated by your enemies.
DEU 1:43 43 I reported this to you but you wouldn’t listen. You disobeyed the LORD ’s instruction. Hotheadedly, you went up into the hills.
DEU 1:44 44 And the Amorites who lived in those hills came out to meet you in battle. They chased you like bees give chase! They gave you a beating from Seir all the way to Hormah.
DEU 1:45 45 When you came back, you cried before the LORD , but he wouldn’t respond to your tears or give you a hearing.
DEU 1:46 46 And so you stayed in Kadesh-barnea for quite some time.
DEU 2:1 1 Next, we turned around and headed back toward the wilderness along the Reed Sea road, exactly as the LORD instructed me. We traveled all around Mount Seir for a long time.
DEU 2:2 2 Eventually the LORD said:
DEU 2:3 3 You’ve been traveling around this mountain long enough. Head north.
DEU 2:4 4 Command the people as follows: You are about to enter into the territory of your relatives who live in Seir: Esau’s descendants. They will be afraid of you, so watch yourselves most carefully.
DEU 2:5 5 Don’t fight with them because I will not give the tiniest parcel of their land to you. I have given Mount Seir to Esau’s family as their property.
DEU 2:6 6 Of course you may buy food from them with money so you can eat, and also water with money so you can drink.
DEU 2:7 7 No doubt about it: the LORD your God has blessed you in all that you have done. He watched over your journey through that vast desert. Throughout these forty years the LORD your God has been with you. You haven’t needed a thing.
DEU 2:8 8 So we passed through the territory of our relatives who live in Seir, Esau’s descendants, leaving the desert road from Elath and from Ezion-geber. Next we turned and went along the Moab wilderness route.
DEU 2:9 9 The LORD said to me: Don’t aggravate Moab. Don’t fight them in battle because I won’t give any part of their land to you as your own. I have given Ar to Lot’s descendants as their property. (
DEU 2:10 10 Now the Emim had lived there before. They were big and numerous and tall—just like the Anakim.
DEU 2:11 11 Most people thought the Emim were Rephaim, like the Anakim were. But the Moabites called them “Emim.”
DEU 2:12 12 Additionally, the Horim had lived in Seir previously, but Esau’s descendants took possession of their area, eliminating them altogether and settling in their place. That is exactly what Israel did in the land it took possession of, which the LORD gave to them.)
DEU 2:13 13 “So then, get going. Cross the Zered ravine.” So we crossed the Zered ravine.
DEU 2:14 14 It took us a total of thirty-eight years to go from Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Zered ravine. It was at that point that the last of the previous generation, every one of fighting age in the camp, had died, just as the LORD had sworn about them.
DEU 2:15 15 In fact, the LORD ’s power was against them, to rid the camp of them, until they were all gone.
DEU 2:16 16 Now as soon as all those of fighting age had died,
DEU 2:17 17 the LORD said to me:
DEU 2:18 18 Today you are crossing through the territory of Moab and Ar
DEU 2:19 19 and you will come close to the Ammonites. Don’t aggravate them. Don’t fight with them because I won’t give any part of the Ammonites’ land to you as your own. I’ve given it to Lot’s descendants as their property.
DEU 2:20 20 Now people thought that land was Rephaim territory as well. The Rephaim had lived there previously. But the Ammonites called them “Zamzummim.”
DEU 2:21 21 They were large, numerous, and tall, just like the Anakim. But the LORD completely destroyed the Zamzummim before the Ammonites, and they took possession of that area, settling in their place.
DEU 2:22 22 That is exactly what God did for Esau’s descendants, who live in Seir, when he completely destroyed the Horites in their presence, and they took possession of the Horites’ area, settling in their place to this very day.
DEU 2:23 23 The Avvim, who had lived in settlements around Gaza, were completely destroyed by the Caphtorim, who had come from Caphtor. They replaced the Avvim there.
DEU 2:24 24 “So get going. Cross the Arnon ravine. I have handed Sihon the Amorite king of Heshbon and his land over to you. It’s time to possess the area! It’s time to fight him in battle!
DEU 2:25 25 Starting right now, I am making everyone everywhere afraid of you and scared of you. Once they hear news of you, they will be shaking and worrying because of you.”
DEU 2:26 26 I then sent messengers from the Kedemoth desert to Sihon, Heshbon’s king, with words of peace:
DEU 2:27 27 “Please let us pass through your land. We promise to stay on the road. We won’t step off it, right or left.
DEU 2:28 28 Please sell us food for money so we can eat; sell us water for money so we can drink. Let us pass through on foot—
DEU 2:29 29 just as Esau’s descendants who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me—until we cross the Jordan River into the land that the LORD our God is giving to us.”
DEU 2:30 30 But Sihon, Heshbon’s king, wasn’t willing to let us pass through his land because the LORD your God had made his spirit hard and his heart inflexible so that God could hand him over to you, which is exactly how it happened.
DEU 2:31 31 The LORD said to me: Look! Right now I’m laying Sihon and his land before you. It’s time to take possession of his land!
DEU 2:32 32 Sihon and all his forces came out to meet us in battle at Jahaz.
DEU 2:33 33 But the LORD our God gave him to us. We struck him down, along with his sons, and all his forces.
DEU 2:34 34 At that time, we captured all of Sihon’s cities, and we placed every town—men, women, and children—under the ban. We left no survivors.
DEU 2:35 35 The only things we kept for ourselves were the animals and the plunder from the towns we had taken.
DEU 2:36 36 From Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Ravine, to the town that is in the valley there, even as far as Gilead, there wasn’t a city that could resist us. The LORD our God laid everything out before us.
DEU 2:37 37 But you didn’t go near the Ammonite lands or hillside cities alongside the Jabbok River, in compliance with all that the LORD our God had commanded.
DEU 3:1 1 Next we turned and went up along the road to Bashan. Og, Bashan’s king, came out with all his forces to meet us in battle at Edrei.
DEU 3:2 2 The LORD said to me: Don’t be afraid of him! I have handed him, all his forces, and his land over to you. Do the same thing to him that you did to Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled in Heshbon.
DEU 3:3 3 And so the LORD our God also handed Og, Bashan’s king, along with his forces, over to us. We struck them down until no survivor was left.
DEU 3:4 4 We also captured all of Og’s towns at that time. There wasn’t a single city that we didn’t take from them—a total of sixty towns, the entire region of Argob, the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan.
DEU 3:5 5 Each of these towns was fortified with high walls, double gates, and crossbars. Outside the towns there were also a great number of villages.
DEU 3:6 6 We placed them under the ban, just as we did with Sihon, Heshbon’s king. Every town—men, women, and children—was under the ban.
DEU 3:7 7 The only things we kept for ourselves were the animals and the plunder from the towns.
DEU 3:8 8 So at that time, we took the land that had belonged to the two Amorite kings beyond the Jordan, all the way from the Arnon Ravine to Mount Hermon (
DEU 3:9 9 Sidonians call Hermon “Sirion,” but the Amorites call it “Senir”),
DEU 3:10 10 including all the towns on the plateau, in the regions of Gilead and Bashan, and all the way to Salecah and Edrei—all the towns that belonged to Og’s kingdom in Bashan. (
DEU 3:11 11 By the way, Bashan’s King Og was the last of the Rephaim. His bed was made of iron. Isn’t it still in the Ammonite town of Rabbah? By standard measurements, it was thirteen and a half feet long and six feet wide.)
DEU 3:12 12 So this is the land we possessed at that time. I gave some of it, from Aroer, which is beside the Arnon River, up through half of the Gilead highlands, along with its cities, to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
DEU 3:13 13 The rest of the Gilead region and all of Bashan, Og’s kingdom, I gave to half the tribe of Manasseh. (Now the whole Argob area, including all of Bashan, was often called Rephaim Country.
DEU 3:14 14 Jair, from the tribe of Manasseh, took possession of the entire Argob region, as far as the border with the Geshurites and the Maacathites. He named the Bashan area after himself, Jair’s Settlement. That’s what it’s still called today.)
DEU 3:15 15 I also gave Gilead to Machir.
DEU 3:16 16 To the Reubenites and the Gadites, I gave land from the Gilead, as far as the Arnon River—the middle of the river being the boundary line—to the Jabbok River, which is the boundary line with the Ammonites.
DEU 3:17 17 Also the desert plain, with the Jordan River as the boundary, from the Galilee Sea down to the desert sea (the Dead Sea ) below the slopes of Mount Pisgah on the east.
DEU 3:18 18 Then I commanded you: Although the LORD your God has given you this land to possess, you must now cross over before the rest of your Israelite relatives as a fighting force ready for battle!
DEU 3:19 19 However, your wives, children, and herds—I know you have lots of herds!—may remain in the towns that I have given to you.
DEU 3:20 20 Once the LORD settles your relatives, as you have been settled, and they also possess the land that the LORD your God is giving them across the Jordan River, each of you can return to the property that I have given to you.
DEU 3:21 21 It was at that same time that I commanded Joshua: You saw everything that the LORD your God did to these two kings. That is exactly what the LORD will do to all the kingdoms where you’re going!
DEU 3:22 22 Don’t be afraid of them because the LORD your God is the one who will be fighting for you.
DEU 3:23 23 It was also at that same time that I begged the LORD :
DEU 3:24 24 Please, LORD God! You have only begun to show your servant your greatness and your mighty hand. What god in heaven or on earth can act as you do or can perform your deeds and powerful acts?
DEU 3:25 25 Please let me cross over the Jordan River so I can see the wonderful land that lies beyond it: those beautiful highlands, even the Lebanon region.
DEU 3:26 26 But the LORD was angry with me because of you! He wouldn’t listen to me. He said to me: That’s enough from you! Don’t ever ask me about this again!
DEU 3:27 27 Go up to the top of Mount Pisgah. Look west, north, south, and east. Have a good look, but you will not cross the Jordan River.
DEU 3:28 28 Instead, command Joshua, strengthen him, and encourage him because he’s the one who will cross the river before this people. He’s the one who will make sure they inherit the land you will see.
DEU 3:29 29 After that, we stayed in the valley across from Beth-peor.
DEU 4:1 1 Now, Israel, in light of all that, listen to the regulations and the case laws that I am teaching you to follow, so that you may live, enter, and possess the land that the LORD , your ancestors’ God, is giving to you.
DEU 4:2 2 Don’t add anything to the word that I am commanding you, and don’t take anything away from it. Instead, keep the commands of the LORD your God that I am commanding all of you.
DEU 4:3 3 You saw with your own eyes what the LORD did concerning the Baal of Peor. The LORD your God destroyed everyone who followed the Baal of Peor,
DEU 4:4 4 but all of you who stayed true to the LORD your God are alive today.
DEU 4:5 5 So pay attention! I am teaching all of you the regulations and the case laws exactly as the LORD my God commanded me. You must do these in the land you are entering to possess.
DEU 4:6 6 Keep them faithfully because that will show your wisdom and insight to the nations who will hear about all these regulations. They will say, “Surely this great nation is a wise and insightful people!”
DEU 4:7 7 After all, is there any great nation that has gods as close to it as the LORD our God is close to us whenever we call to him?
DEU 4:8 8 Or does any great nation have regulations and case laws as righteous as all this Instruction that I am setting before you today?
DEU 4:9 9 But be on guard and watch yourselves closely so that you don’t forget the things your eyes saw and so they never leave your mind as long as you live. Teach them to your children and your grandchildren.
DEU 4:10 10 Remember that day when you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me: “Gather the people to me. I will declare my words to them so that they will learn to fear me every day of their lives on the fertile land, and teach their children to do the same.”
DEU 4:11 11 Then you all came close and stood at the foot of the mountain. The mountain was blazing with fire up to the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick smoke!
DEU 4:12 12 The LORD spoke to you out of the very fire itself. You heard the sound of words, but you didn’t see any form. There was only a voice.
DEU 4:13 13 The LORD declared his covenant to you, which he commanded you to do—the Ten Commandments —and wrote them on two stone tablets.
DEU 4:14 14 At that time, the LORD commanded me to teach you all the regulations and the case laws that you must keep in the land that you are entering to possess.
DEU 4:15 15 So watch your conduct closely, because you didn’t see any form on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb out of the very fire itself.
DEU 4:16 16 Don’t ruin everything and make an idol for yourself: a form of any image, any likeness—male or female—
DEU 4:17 17 or any likeness whatsoever, whether of a land animal, a bird that flies in the sky,
DEU 4:18 18 an insect that crawls on the earth, or a fish that lives in the sea.
DEU 4:19 19 Don’t look to the skies, to the sun or the moon or the stars, all the heavenly bodies, and be led astray, worshipping and serving them. The LORD your God has granted these things to all the nations who live under heaven.
DEU 4:20 20 But the LORD took you and brought you out of that iron furnace, out of Egypt, so that you might be his own treasured people, which is what you are right now.
DEU 4:21 21 The LORD was angry with me because of your deeds and swore that I couldn’t cross the Jordan River or enter the wonderful land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
DEU 4:22 22 I will die here in this land. I won’t cross the Jordan River. But you will, and you will take possession of that wonderful land.
DEU 4:23 23 So all of you, watch yourselves! Don’t forget the covenant that the LORD your God made with you by making an idol or an image of any kind or anything the LORD your God forbids,
DEU 4:24 24 because the LORD your God is an all-consuming fire. He is a passionate God.
DEU 4:25 25 Once you have had children and grandchildren and have grown old on the land, if you ruin things by making an idol, in any form whatsoever, and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God and anger him,
DEU 4:26 26 I call heaven and earth as my witnesses against you today: You will definitely disappear—and quickly—from the land that you are crossing over the Jordan River to possess. You won’t extend your time there but will instead be totally destroyed.
DEU 4:27 27 The LORD will scatter you among the nations. Only a very few of you will survive in the countries where the LORD will drag you.
DEU 4:28 28 There you will worship other gods, made of wood and stone by human hands—gods that cannot see, listen, eat, or smell.
DEU 4:29 29 You will seek the LORD your God from there, and you will find him if you seek him with all your heart and with all your being.
DEU 4:30 30 In your distress, when all these things happen to you in the future, you will return to the LORD your God and you will obey his voice,
DEU 4:31 31 because the LORD your God is a compassionate God. He won’t let you go, he won’t destroy you, and he won’t forget the covenant that he swore to your ancestors.
DEU 4:32 32 Now look into it: into days long past, before your time—all the way back to the day God first created human beings on earth, from one end of heaven to the other. Has anything this amazing ever happened? Has anything like it ever been heard of before?
DEU 4:33 33 Has any people ever listened to a god’s voice speaking out of fire, as each of you have, and survived?
DEU 4:34 34 Or has any god ever tried to take one nation out of another nation using tests, miracles, wonders, war, a strong hand and outstretched arm, or awesome power like all that the LORD your God did for you in Egypt while you watched?
DEU 4:35 35 You were shown these things so that you would know this: The LORD is the only God. There’s no other god except him.
DEU 4:36 36 From heaven he made you hear his voice in order to discipline you. On earth he showed you his great fire. You heard his words from that very fire.
DEU 4:37 37 And because he loved your ancestors and chose their descendants after them, God brought you out of Egypt with his own presence, by his own great power,
DEU 4:38 38 in order to remove larger and stronger nations from before you and bring you into their land, giving it to you as an inheritance. That’s where things stand right now.
DEU 4:39 39 Know then today and keep in mind that the LORD is the only God in heaven above or on earth below. There is no other.
DEU 4:40 40 Keep the Lord’s regulations and his commandments. I’m commanding them to you today for your well-being and for the well-being of your children after you, so that you may extend your time on the fertile land that the LORD your God is giving you forever.
DEU 4:41 41 Then Moses set aside three cities on the eastern side of the Jordan River
DEU 4:42 42 so that anyone who killed someone accidentally and without prior hatred could flee to one of these cities and be safe:
DEU 4:43 43 Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau for the Reubenites, Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites, and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
DEU 4:44 44 Now this is the Instruction that Moses set before the Israelites.
DEU 4:45 45 These are the laws and the regulations and the case laws that Moses spoke to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
DEU 4:46 46 This took place across the Jordan River, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon the Amorite king who ruled in Heshbon, whom Moses and the Israelites defeated when they came out of Egypt.
DEU 4:47 47 They took possession of his land and the land of Og, Bashan’s king—the two Amorite kings across the Jordan River to the east—
DEU 4:48 48 from Aroer, which is on the banks of the Arnon River, all the way to Mount Sion, also known as Hermon,
DEU 4:49 49 and all the desert regions across the Jordan River, on the east, down to the Dead Sea, beneath the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
DEU 5:1 1 Moses called out to all Israel, saying to them: “Israel! Listen to the regulations and the case laws that I’m recounting in your hearing right now. Learn them and carefully do them.
DEU 5:2 2 The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Mount Horeb.
DEU 5:3 3 The LORD didn’t make this covenant with our ancestors but with us—all of us who are here and alive right now.
DEU 5:4 4 The LORD spoke with you face-to-face on the mountain from the very fire itself.
DEU 5:5 5 At that time, I was standing between the LORD and you, declaring to you the LORD ’s word, because you were terrified of the fire and didn’t go up on the mountain.” The LORD said:
DEU 5:6 6 I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
DEU 5:7 7 You must have no other gods before me.
DEU 5:8 8 Do not make an idol for yourself—no form whatsoever—of anything in the sky above or on the earth below or in the waters under the earth.
DEU 5:9 9 Do not bow down to them or worship them because I, the LORD your God, am a passionate God. I punish children for their parents’ sins—even to the third and fourth generations of those who hate me.
DEU 5:10 10 But I am loyal and gracious to the thousandth generation of those who love me and keep my commandments.
DEU 5:11 11 Do not use the LORD your God’s name as if it were of no significance; the LORD won’t forgive anyone who uses his name that way.
DEU 5:12 12 Keep the Sabbath day and treat it as holy, exactly as the LORD your God commanded:
DEU 5:13 13 Six days you may work and do all your tasks,
DEU 5:14 14 but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. Don’t do any work on it—not you, your sons or daughters, your male or female servants, your oxen or donkeys or any of your animals, or the immigrant who is living among you—so that your male and female servants can rest just like you.
DEU 5:15 15 Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, but the LORD your God brought you out of there with a strong hand and an outstretched arm. That’s why the LORD your God commands you to keep the Sabbath day.
DEU 5:16 16 Honor your father and your mother, exactly as the LORD your God requires, so that your life will be long and so that things will go well for you on the fertile land that the LORD your God is giving you.
DEU 5:17 17 Do not kill.
DEU 5:18 18 Do not commit adultery.
DEU 5:19 19 Do not steal.
DEU 5:20 20 Do not testify falsely against your neighbor.
DEU 5:21 21 Do not desire and try to take your neighbor’s wife. Do not crave your neighbor’s house, field, male or female servant, ox, donkey, or anything else that belongs to your neighbor.
DEU 5:22 22 Those are the words the LORD spoke to your entire assembly with a loud voice while on the mountain, from the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick smoke. He added no more. God wrote them on two stone tablets, then gave them to me.
DEU 5:23 23 Now once you heard the voice from the darkness while the mountain was blazing with fire, you came to me—more specifically, all the chiefs of your tribes and your elders came—
DEU 5:24 24 and you said: “Look here! The LORD our God has shown us his glory and greatness. We’ve heard his voice come out of the very fire itself. We’ve seen firsthand that God can speak to a human being and they can survive!
DEU 5:25 25 But why should we die? Surely this massive fire will consume us! If we hear any more of the LORD our God’s voice, we will die.
DEU 5:26 26 Is there anyone who has heard the living God’s voice speaking out of the very fire itself, like we have, and survived?
DEU 5:27 27 You go and listen to all that the LORD our God says. Then tell us all that the LORD our God speaks to you. We’ll listen and we’ll do it.”
DEU 5:28 28 The LORD heard what you said, when you said this to me. The LORD then told me: I heard what the people said when they spoke with you. Everything they suggest is good.
DEU 5:29 29 If only their minds were like this: always fearing me and keeping all my commandments so that things would go well for them and their children forever!
DEU 5:30 30 Go and tell them: You may go back to your tents.
DEU 5:31 31 But you, Moses, must stay here with me. I will tell you all the commandments, the regulations, and the case laws that you must teach the Israelites to do in the land that I am giving them to possess.
DEU 5:32 32 So you must carefully do exactly what the LORD your God commands you. Don’t deviate even a bit!
DEU 5:33 33 You must walk the precise path that the LORD your God indicates for you so that you will live, and so that things will go well for you, and so you will extend your time on the land that you will possess.
DEU 6:1 1 Now these are the commandments, the regulations, and the case laws that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you to follow in the land you are entering to possess,
DEU 6:2 2 so that you will fear the LORD your God by keeping all his regulations and his commandments that I am commanding you—both you and your sons and daughters—all the days of your life and so that you will lengthen your life.
DEU 6:3 3 Listen to them, Israel! Follow them carefully so that things will go well for you and so that you will continue to multiply exactly as the LORD , your ancestors’ God, promised you, in a land full of milk and honey.
DEU 6:4 4 Israel, listen! Our God is the LORD ! Only the LORD !
DEU 6:5 5 Love the LORD your God with all your heart, all your being, and all your strength.
DEU 6:6 6 These words that I am commanding you today must always be on your minds.
DEU 6:7 7 Recite them to your children. Talk about them when you are sitting around your house and when you are out and about, when you are lying down and when you are getting up.
DEU 6:8 8 Tie them on your hand as a sign. They should be on your forehead as a symbol.
DEU 6:9 9 Write them on your house’s doorframes and on your city’s gates.
DEU 6:10 10 Now once the LORD your God has brought you into the land that he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give to you—a land that will be full of large and wonderful towns that you didn’t build,
DEU 6:11 11 houses stocked with all kinds of goods that you didn’t stock, cisterns that you didn’t make, vineyards and olive trees that you didn’t plant—and you eat and get stuffed,
DEU 6:12 12 watch yourself! Don’t forget the LORD , who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
DEU 6:13 13 Revere the LORD your God, serve him, and take your solemn pledges in his name!
DEU 6:14 14 Don’t follow other gods, those gods of the people around you—
DEU 6:15 15 because the LORD your God, who is with you and among you, is a passionate God. The LORD your God’s anger will burn against you, and he will wipe you off the fertile land.
DEU 6:16 16 Don’t test the LORD your God the way you frustrated him at Massah.
DEU 6:17 17 You must carefully follow the LORD your God’s commands along with the laws and regulations he has given you.
DEU 6:18 18 Do what is right and good in the LORD ’s sight so that things will go well for you and so you will enter and take possession of the wonderful land that the LORD swore to your ancestors,
DEU 6:19 19 and so the LORD will drive out all your enemies from before you, just as he promised.
DEU 6:20 20 In the future, your children will ask you, “What is the meaning of the laws, the regulations, and the case laws that the LORD our God commanded you?”
DEU 6:21 21 Tell them: We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt. But the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
DEU 6:22 22 Before our own eyes, the LORD performed great and awesome deeds of power against Egypt, Pharaoh, and his entire dynasty.
DEU 6:23 23 But the Lord brought us out from there so that he could bring us in, giving us the land that he swore to our ancestors.
DEU 6:24 24 Then the LORD commanded us to perform all these regulations, revering the LORD our God, so that things go well for us always and so we continue to live, as we’re doing right now.
DEU 6:25 25 What’s more, we will be considered righteous if we are careful to do all this commandment before the LORD our God, just as he commanded us.
DEU 7:1 1 Now once the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to take possession of, and he drives out numerous nations before you—the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites: seven nations that are larger and stronger than you—
DEU 7:2 2 once the LORD your God lays them before you, you must strike them down, placing them under the ban. Don’t make any covenants with them, and don’t be merciful to them.
DEU 7:3 3 Don’t intermarry with them. Don’t give your daughter to one of their sons to marry, and don’t take one of their daughters to marry your son,
DEU 7:4 4 because they will turn your child away from following me so that they end up serving other gods. That will make the LORD ’s anger burn against you, and he will quickly annihilate you.
DEU 7:5 5 Instead, this is what you must do with these nations: rip down their altars, smash their sacred stones, cut down their sacred poles, and burn their idols
DEU 7:6 6 because you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God chose you to be his own treasured people beyond all others on the fertile land.
DEU 7:7 7 It was not because you were greater than all other people that the LORD loved you and chose you. In fact, you were the smallest of peoples!
DEU 7:8 8 No, it is because the LORD loved you and because he kept the solemn pledge he swore to your ancestors that the LORD brought you out with a strong hand and saved you from the house of slavery, from the power of Pharaoh, Egypt’s king.
DEU 7:9 9 Know now then that the LORD your God is the only true God! He is the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and proves loyal to everyone who loves him and keeps his commands—even to the thousandth generation!
DEU 7:10 10 He is the God who personally repays anyone who hates him, ultimately destroying that kind of person. The LORD does not waste time with anyone who hates him; he repays them personally.
DEU 7:11 11 So make sure you carefully keep the commandment, the regulations, and the case laws that I am commanding you right now.
DEU 7:12 12 If you listen to these case laws and follow them carefully, the LORD your God will keep the covenant and display the loyalty that he promised your ancestors.
DEU 7:13 13 He will love you, bless you, and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your wombs and the fruit of your fertile land—all your grain, your wine, your oil, and the offspring of your cattle and flocks—upon the very fertile land that he swore to your ancestors to give to you.
DEU 7:14 14 You will be more blessed than any other group of people. No one will be sterile or infertile—not among you or your animals.
DEU 7:15 15 The LORD will remove all sickness from you. As for all those dreadful Egyptian diseases you experienced, the Lord won’t put them on you but will inflict them on all who hate you.
DEU 7:16 16 You will destroy all the peoples that the LORD your God is handing over to you. Show them no pity. And don’t serve their gods because that would be a trap for you.
DEU 7:17 17 If you happen to think to yourself, These nations are greater than we are; how can we possibly possess their land?
DEU 7:18 18 don’t be afraid of them! Remember, instead, what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and all Egypt:
DEU 7:19 19 the great trials that you saw with your own eyes, the signs and wonders, and the strong hand and outstretched arm the LORD your God used to rescue you. That’s what the LORD your God will do to any people you fear.
DEU 7:20 20 The LORD your God will send terror on them until even the survivors and those hiding from you are destroyed.
DEU 7:21 21 Don’t dread these nations because the LORD your God, the great and awesome God, is with you and among you. (
DEU 7:22 22 The LORD your God will drive out these nations before you bit by bit. You won’t be able to finish them off quickly; otherwise, the wild animals would become too much for you to handle.)
DEU 7:23 23 The LORD your God will lay these nations before you, throwing them into a huge panic until they are destroyed.
DEU 7:24 24 He will hand their kings over to you, and you will wipe their names out from under the skies. No one will be able to stand before you; you will crush them.
DEU 7:25 25 Burn the images of their gods. Don’t desire the silver or the gold that is on them and take it for yourself, or you will be trapped by it. That is detestable to the LORD your God.
DEU 7:26 26 Don’t bring any detestable thing into your house, or you will be placed under the ban too, just like it is! You must utterly detest these kinds of things, despising them completely, because they are under the ban.
DEU 8:1 1 You must carefully perform all of the commandment that I am commanding you right now so you can live and multiply and enter and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors.
DEU 8:2 2 Remember the long road on which the LORD your God led you during these forty years in the desert so he could humble you, testing you to find out what was in your heart: whether you would keep his commandments or not.
DEU 8:3 3 He humbled you by making you hungry and then feeding you the manna that neither you nor your ancestors had ever experienced, so he could teach you that people don’t live on bread alone. No, they live based on whatever the LORD says.
DEU 8:4 4 During these forty years, your clothes didn’t wear out and your feet didn’t swell up.
DEU 8:5 5 Know then in your heart that the LORD your God has been disciplining you just as a father disciplines his children.
DEU 8:6 6 Keep the commandments of the LORD your God by walking in his ways and by fearing him,
DEU 8:7 7 because the LORD your God is bringing you to a wonderful land, a land with streams of water, springs, and wells that gush up in the valleys and on the hills;
DEU 8:8 8 a land of wheat and barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of olive oil and honey;
DEU 8:9 9 a land where you will eat food without any shortage—you won’t lack a thing there—a land where stone is hard as iron and where you will mine copper from the hills.
DEU 8:10 10 You will eat, you will be satisfied, and you will bless the LORD your God in the wonderful land that he’s given you.
DEU 8:11 11 But watch yourself! Don’t forget the LORD your God by not keeping his commands or his case laws or his regulations that I am commanding you right now.
DEU 8:12 12 When you eat, get full, build nice houses, and settle down,
DEU 8:13 13 and when your herds and your flocks are growing large, your silver and gold are multiplying, and everything you have is thriving,
DEU 8:14 14 don’t become arrogant, forgetting the LORD your God: the one who rescued you from Egypt, from the house of slavery;
DEU 8:15 15 the one who led you through this vast and terrifying desert of poisonous snakes and scorpions, of cracked ground with no water; the one who made water flow for you out of a hard rock;
DEU 8:16 16 the one who fed you manna in the wilderness, which your ancestors had never experienced, in order to humble and test you, but in order to do good to you in the end.
DEU 8:17 17 Don’t think to yourself, My own strength and abilities have produced all this prosperity for me.
DEU 8:18 18 Remember the LORD your God! He’s the one who gives you the strength to be prosperous in order to establish the covenant he made with your ancestors—and that’s how things stand right now.
DEU 8:19 19 But if you do, in fact, forget the LORD your God and follow other gods, serving and bowing down to them, I swear to you right now that you will be completely destroyed.
DEU 8:20 20 Just like the nations that the LORD is destroying before you, that’s exactly how you will be destroyed—all because you didn’t obey the LORD your God’s voice.
DEU 9:1 1 Listen, Israel! Today you will cross the Jordan River to enter and take possession of nations larger and more powerful than you, along with huge cities with fortifications that reach to the sky.
DEU 9:2 2 These people are large and tall—they are the Anakim. You know and have heard what people say: “Who can stand up to the Anakim?”
DEU 9:3 3 Know right now that the LORD your God, who is crossing over before you, is an all-consuming fire! He will wipe them out! He will subdue them before you! Then you will take possession of their land, eliminating them quickly, exactly as the LORD told you.
DEU 9:4 4 Once the LORD your God has driven them out before you, don’t think to yourself, It’s because I’m righteous that the LORD brought me in to possess this land. It is instead because of these nations’ wickedness that the LORD is removing them before you.
DEU 9:5 5 You aren’t entering and taking possession of their land because you are righteous or because your heart is especially virtuous; rather, it is because these nations are wicked—that’s why the LORD your God is removing them before you, and because he wishes to establish the promise he made to your ancestors: to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
DEU 9:6 6 Know then that the LORD your God isn’t giving you this excellent land for you to possess on account of your righteousness—because you are a stubborn people!
DEU 9:7 7 Remember—don’t ever forget!—how you made the LORD your God furious in the wilderness. From the very first day you stepped out of Egypt until you arrived at this place, you have been rebels against the LORD .
DEU 9:8 8 Even at Horeb you angered the LORD ! He was so enraged by you that he threatened to wipe you out.
DEU 9:9 9 When I went up on the mountain to get the stone tablets, the covenant tablets that the LORD made with you, I was up there forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread, drank no water.
DEU 9:10 10 The LORD gave me the two stone tablets, written by God’s finger, and on them were all the words that the LORD had said to you on the mountain, out of the very fire itself, on the day we assembled.
DEU 9:11 11 At the end of those forty days and nights, the LORD gave me the two stone tablets—the covenant tablets.
DEU 9:12 12 Then the LORD said to me, “Get going! Get down from here quickly because your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have ruined everything! They couldn’t wait to turn from the path I commanded them! They’ve made themselves an idol out of cast metal.”
DEU 9:13 13 The LORD said more to me: “I have seen this people. Look! What a stubborn people they are!
DEU 9:14 14 Now stand back. I am going to wipe them out. I will erase their name from under heaven, then I will make a nation out of you—one stronger and larger than they were.”
DEU 9:15 15 So I went down the mountain while it was blazing with fire. The two covenant tablets were in my two hands.
DEU 9:16 16 It was then that I saw how you sinned against the LORD your God: you made yourselves a calf, an idol made of cast metal! You couldn’t wait to turn from the path the LORD commanded you!
DEU 9:17 17 I grabbed the two tablets and threw them down with my own hands, shattering them while you watched.
DEU 9:18 18 Then I fell before the LORD as I had done the previous forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water, all because of the sin that you had committed by doing such evil in the LORD ’s sight, infuriating him.
DEU 9:19 19 I was afraid of the massive anger and rage the LORD had for you—he was going to wipe you out! However, the LORD listened to me again in that moment.
DEU 9:20 20 But the LORD was furious with Aaron—he was going to wipe him out! So I also prayed hard for Aaron at that time.
DEU 9:21 21 And as for that sinful thing you made, that calf, I took it and I burned it with fire. Then I smashed it, grinding it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust. Then I dumped the dust into the stream that ran down the mountain.
DEU 9:22 22 Also at Taberah, again at Massah, and then again at Kibroth-hattaavah, you have been the kind of people who make the LORD angry.
DEU 9:23 23 And then, when the LORD sent you from Kadesh-barnea, telling you: “Go up and take possession of the land that I’m giving you,” you disobeyed the LORD your God’s command. You didn’t trust him. You didn’t obey God’s voice.
DEU 9:24 24 You’ve been rebellious toward the LORD from the day I met you.
DEU 9:25 25 But I fell on my knees in the LORD ’s presence forty days and forty nights, lying flat out, because the LORD planned on wiping you out.
DEU 9:26 26 But I prayed to the LORD ! I said: LORD , my Lord! Don’t destroy your people, your own possession, whom you saved by your own power, whom you brought out of Egypt with a strong hand!
DEU 9:27 27 Remember your servants: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob! Don’t focus on this people’s stubbornness, wickedness, and sin.
DEU 9:28 28 Otherwise, that land out of which you brought us will say: The LORD wasn’t strong enough to bring them into the land he’d promised them. Because he didn’t care for them in the least, he brought them out to die in the desert.
DEU 9:29 29 But these are your people! Your own possession! The people you brought out by your great power and by your outstretched arm!
DEU 10:1 1 At that time the LORD told me: Carve two stone tablets, just like the first ones, and hike up the mountain to me. Construct a wooden chest as well.
DEU 10:2 2 I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets—the ones you smashed—then you will place them in the chest.
DEU 10:3 3 So I built a chest out of acacia wood and carved two stone tablets just like the first ones. Then I hiked up the mountain holding the two tablets in my hands.
DEU 10:4 4 God wrote on the new tablets what had been written on the first set: the Ten Commandments that the LORD spoke to you on the mountain, from the very fire itself, on the day we assembled there. Then the LORD gave them to me.
DEU 10:5 5 So I came back down the mountain. I put the tablets in the chest that I’d made, and that’s where they are now, exactly as the LORD commanded me. (
DEU 10:6 6 Now, the Israelites had set out from Beeroth-bene-jaakan to Moserah. It was there that Aaron died and was buried. His son Eleazar succeeded him in the priestly role.
DEU 10:7 7 From there the Israelites traveled to Gudgodah, then from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, which is a land with flowing streams.
DEU 10:8 8 At that time, the LORD selected the tribe of Levi to carry the chest containing the LORD ’s covenant, to minister before the LORD , to serve him, and to offer blessings in his name. That’s the way things are right now.
DEU 10:9 9 That’s why the Levites don’t have a stake or inheritance with the rest of their relatives. The LORD is the Levites’ inheritance, just as the LORD your God promised them.)
DEU 10:10 10 Just as the first time, I remained on the mountain forty days and nights. And the LORD listened to me again in this instance. The LORD wasn’t willing to destroy you.
DEU 10:11 11 Then the LORD told me: Get going. Lead the people so they can enter and take possession of the land that I promised I’d give to their ancestors.
DEU 10:12 12 Now in light of all that, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you? Only this: to revere the LORD your God by walking in all his ways, by loving him, by serving the LORD your God with all your heart and being,
DEU 10:13 13 and by keeping the LORD ’s commandments and his regulations that I’m commanding you right now. It’s for your own good!
DEU 10:14 14 Clearly, the LORD owns the sky, the highest heavens, the earth, and everything in it.
DEU 10:15 15 But the LORD adored your ancestors, loving them and choosing the descendants that followed them—you!—from all other people. That’s how things still stand now.
DEU 10:16 16 So circumcise your hearts and stop being so stubborn,
DEU 10:17 17 because the LORD your God is the God of all gods and Lord of all lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God who doesn’t play favorites and doesn’t take bribes.
DEU 10:18 18 He enacts justice for orphans and widows, and he loves immigrants, giving them food and clothing.
DEU 10:19 19 That means you must also love immigrants because you were immigrants in Egypt.
DEU 10:20 20 Revere the LORD your God, serve him, cling to him, swear by his name alone!
DEU 10:21 21 He is your praise, and he is your God—the one who performed these great and awesome acts that you witnessed with your very own eyes.
DEU 10:22 22 Your ancestors went down to Egypt with a total of seventy people, but now look! The LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars in the nighttime sky!
DEU 11:1 1 So love the LORD your God and follow his instruction, his regulations, his case laws, and his commandments always.
DEU 11:2 2 And know right now what your children haven’t known or yet witnessed: The LORD your God’s discipline, his power, his mighty hand and outstretched arm;
DEU 11:3 3 the signs and the acts that he performed in the heart of Egyptian territory, against Egypt’s King Pharaoh and all his land;
DEU 11:4 4 what God did to the Egyptian army, to its horses and chariots—how he made the water of the Reed Sea flow over their heads when they chased after you, but the LORD destroyed them, and that’s how things stand right now;
DEU 11:5 5 what the Lord did for you in the desert, until you arrived at this place;
DEU 11:6 6 and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the descendants of Eliab the Reubenite, when the ground opened up its mouth and swallowed them, their families, their tents, and every living thing they possessed in the presence of all Israel.
DEU 11:7 7 Your own eyes witnessed each of these powerful acts the LORD performed.
DEU 11:8 8 So keep every part of the commandment that I am giving you today so that you stay strong to enter and take possession of the land that you are crossing over to possess,
DEU 11:9 9 and so that you might prolong your life on the fertile land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give to them and their descendants—a land full of milk and honey.
DEU 11:10 10 The land you are about to enter and possess is definitely not like the land of Egypt, where you came from, where you sowed your seed and irrigated it by hand like a vegetable garden.
DEU 11:11 11 No, the land you are entering to possess is a land of hills and valleys, where your drinking water will be rain from heaven.
DEU 11:12 12 It’s a land that the LORD cares for: the LORD ’s eyes are on it constantly from the first of the year until the very end of the year.
DEU 11:13 13 Now, if you completely obey God’s commandments that I am giving you right now, by loving the LORD your God and by serving him with all your heart and all your being,
DEU 11:14 14 then he will provide rain for your land at the right time—early rain and late rain—so you can stock up your grain, wine, and oil.
DEU 11:15 15 He will also make your fields lush for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
DEU 11:16 16 But watch yourselves! Otherwise, your heart might be led astray so you stray away, serving other gods and worshipping them.
DEU 11:17 17 Then the LORD ’s anger would burn against you. He will close the sky up tight. There won’t be any rain, and the ground won’t yield any of its crops. You will quickly disappear off the wonderful land the LORD is giving to you.
DEU 11:18 18 Place these words I’m speaking on your heart and in your very being. Tie them on your hand as a sign. They should be on your forehead as a symbol.
DEU 11:19 19 Teach them to your children, by talking about them when you are sitting around your house and when you are out and about, when you are lying down and when you are getting up.
DEU 11:20 20 Write them on your house’s doorframes and on your city’s gates.
DEU 11:21 21 Do all that so your days and your children’s days on the fertile land the LORD swore to give to your ancestors are many—indeed, as many as the number of days that the sky’s been over the earth!
DEU 11:22 22 It’s true: if you carefully keep all this commandment that I’m giving you, by doing it, by loving the LORD your God, by walking in all his ways, and by clinging to him,
DEU 11:23 23 then the LORD will clear out all these nations before you. You will inherit what belonged to nations that are larger and stronger than you are.
DEU 11:24 24 Every place you set foot on will be yours: your territory will run from the wilderness all the way to the Lebanon range, and from the Euphrates River all the way to the Mediterranean Sea.
DEU 11:25 25 No one will be able to stand up to you. Just as he promised, the LORD your God will make the entire land deathly afraid of you wherever you advance in it.
DEU 11:26 26 Pay attention! I am setting blessing and curse before you right now:
DEU 11:27 27 the blessing if you obey the LORD your God’s commandments that I am giving you right now,
DEU 11:28 28 but the curse if you don’t obey the LORD your God’s commandments and stray from the path that I am giving you today by following other gods that you have not known.
DEU 11:29 29 Now when the LORD your God brings you into the land that you are entering to take possession of, put the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal. (
DEU 11:30 30 Aren’t both of these mountains across the Jordan River, down along the western road in the region of the Canaanites who live in the desert plain, across from Gilgal, next to the Moreh Oak Grove?)
DEU 11:31 31 So then, once you cross the Jordan River to enter and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you, and you take possession of it, settling down in it,
DEU 11:32 32 you must carefully follow the regulations and the case laws that I am laying out before you right now.
DEU 12:1 1 These are the regulations and the case laws that you must carefully keep in the fertile land the LORD , your ancestors’ God, has given to you to possess for as long as you live on that land:
DEU 12:2 2 You must completely destroy every place where the nations that you are displacing worshipped their gods—whether on high mountains or hills or under leafy green trees.
DEU 12:3 3 Rip down their altars and shatter their sacred stones. Burn their sacred poles with fire. Hack their gods’ idols into pieces. Wipe out their names from that place.
DEU 12:4 4 Don’t act like they did toward the LORD your God!
