DEU 31:7 7 Then Moses called Joshua and, with all Israel watching, said to him: “Be strong and fearless because you are the one who will lead this people to the land the LORD swore to their ancestors to give to them; you are the one who will divide up the land for them.
DEU 31:8 8 But the LORD is the one who is marching before you! He is the one who will be with you! He won’t let you down. He won’t abandon you. So don’t be afraid or scared!”
DEU 31:9 9 Then Moses wrote this Instruction down and gave it to the priests—the Levites who carry the chest containing the LORD ’s covenant—and to all of the Israelite elders.
DEU 31:10 10 Moses then commanded them: At the end of seven years, at the appointed time in the year of debt cancellation, during the Festival of Booths,
DEU 31:11 11 when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God at the location he selects, you must read this Instruction aloud, in the hearing of all the people.
DEU 31:12 12 Gather everyone—men, women, children, and the immigrants who live in your cities—in order that they hear it, learn it, and revere the LORD your God, carefully doing all the words of this Instruction,
DEU 31:13 13 and so that their children, who don’t yet know the Instruction, may hear it and learn to revere the LORD your God for as long as you live on the ground you are crossing the Jordan River to possess.
DEU 31:14 14 Then the LORD said to Moses: “It’s almost time for you to die. Summon Joshua. The two of you must present yourselves at the meeting tent so I can command him.” So Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the meeting tent.
DEU 31:15 15 The LORD appeared in the tent in a pillar of cloud; the cloud pillar stood at the tent’s entrance.
DEU 31:16 16 The LORD then said to Moses: “Soon you will rest with your ancestors, and the people will rise up and act unfaithfully, going after strange gods of the land they are entering. They will abandon me, breaking my covenant that I made with them.
DEU 31:17 17 At that point my anger will burn against them, and I’ll be the one who abandons them! I’ll hide my face from them. They will become nothing but food for their enemies, and all sorts of bad things and misfortunes will happen to them. Then they will say: ‘Haven’t these terrible things happened to us because our God is no longer with us?’
DEU 31:18 18 But I will hide my face at that time because of the many wrong things they have done, because they have turned to other gods!
DEU 31:19 19 So in light of all that, you must write down this poem and teach it to the Israelites. Put it in their mouths so that the poem becomes a witness for me against them.
DEU 31:20 20 When I bring the Israelites to the land I swore to their ancestors, which is full of milk and honey, and they eat, get full, then fat, and then turn toward other gods, serving them and disrespecting me and breaking my covenant,
DEU 31:21 21 then, when all kinds of bad things and misfortunes happen to them, this poem will witness against them, giving its testimony, because it won’t be lost from the mouths of their descendants. Yes, I know right now what they are inclined to do, even before I’ve brought them into the land I swore.”
DEU 31:22 22 So Moses wrote this poem down that very day, and he taught it to the Israelites.
DEU 31:23 23 Then the Lord commissioned Joshua, Nun’s son: “Be strong and fearless because you are the one who will bring the Israelites to the land I swore to them. I myself will be with you.”
DEU 31:24 24 Once Moses had finished writing in their entirety all the words of this Instruction scroll,
DEU 31:25 25 he commanded the Levites who carry the chest containing the LORD ’s covenant as follows:
DEU 31:26 26 “Take this Instruction scroll and put it next to the chest containing the LORD your God’s covenant. It must remain there as a witness against you
DEU 31:27 27 because I know how rebellious and hardheaded you are. If you are this rebellious toward the LORD while I’m still alive, it’s bound to get worse once I’m dead!
DEU 31:28 28 Assemble all of your tribes’ elders and your officials in front of me, so I can speak these words in their hearing, and so I can call heaven and earth as my witnesses against them,
DEU 31:29 29 because I know that after I’m dead, you will ruin everything, departing from the path I’ve commanded you. Terrible things will happen to you in the future because you will do evil in the LORD ’s eyes, aggravating him with the things your hands have made.”
DEU 31:30 30 Then Moses recited in their entirety the words of this poem in the hearing of the entire assembly of Israel:
DEU 32:1 1 Heaven! Pay attention and I will speak; Earth! Listen to the words of my mouth.
DEU 32:2 2 My teaching will fall like raindrops; my speech will settle like dew— like gentle rains on grass, like spring showers on all that is green—
DEU 32:3 3 because I proclaim the LORD ’s name: Give praise to our God!
DEU 32:4 4 The rock: his acts are perfection! No doubt about it: all his ways are right! He’s the faithful God, never deceiving; altogether righteous and true is he.
DEU 32:5 5 But children who weren’t his own sinned against him with their defects; they are a twisted and perverse generation.
DEU 32:6 6 Is this how you thank the LORD , you stupid, senseless people? Isn’t he your father, your creator? Didn’t he make you and establish you?
DEU 32:7 7 Remember the days long past; consider the years long gone. Ask your father, he will tell you about it; ask your elders, they will give you the details:
DEU 32:8 8 When God Most High divided up the nations— when he divided up humankind— he decided the people’s boundaries based on the number of the gods.
DEU 32:9 9 Surely the LORD ’s property was his people; Jacob was his part of the inheritance.
DEU 32:10 10 God found Israel in a wild land— in a howling desert wasteland— he protected him, cared for him, watched over him with his very own eye.
DEU 32:11 11 Like an eagle protecting its nest, hovering over its young, God spread out his wings, took hold of Israel, carried him on his back.
DEU 32:12 12 The LORD alone led Israel; no foreign god assisted.
DEU 32:13 13 God made Israel glide over the highlands; he fed him with food from the field, nursed him with honey from a boulder, with oil from a hard rock:
DEU 32:14 14 curds from the herd, milk from the flock, along with the best of lambs, rams from Bashan, he-goats too, along with the finest wheat— and for drink, wine from the juiciest grapes!
DEU 32:15 15 Jacob ate until he was stuffed; Jeshurun got fat, then rebellious. It was you who got fat, thick, stubborn! Jeshurun gave up on the God who made him, thought the rock of his salvation was worthless.
DEU 32:16 16 They made God jealous with strange gods, aggravated him with detestable things.
DEU 32:17 17 They sacrificed to demons, not to God, to deities of which they had no knowledge— new gods only recently on the scene, ones about which your ancestors had never heard.
DEU 32:18 18 You deserted the rock that sired you; you forgot the God who gave birth to you!
DEU 32:19 19 The LORD saw this and rejected out of aggravation his sons and his daughters.
DEU 32:20 20 He said: I will hide my face from them— I will see what becomes of them— because they are a confused generation; they are children lacking loyalty.
DEU 32:21 21 They provoked me with “no-gods,” aggravated me with their pieces of junk. So I am going to provoke them with “No-People,” aggravate them with a nation of fools.
DEU 32:22 22 A fire burns in me— it will blaze to the depths of the grave; it will destroy the land and its crops; it will blacken the base of the mountains.
DEU 32:23 23 I’ll throw on them disaster after disaster; I’ll destroy them with my arrows:
DEU 32:24 24 devastating hunger, consuming plague, bitter sickness. I’ll send animal fangs after them, venom from dust crawlers too.
DEU 32:25 25 Outside, in the streets, the sword will bereave! Inside, in the safest room, there will be terror for young men and women, nursing baby and senior citizen.
DEU 32:26 26 I thought about it: I could have struck them down, erased them from human memory,
DEU 32:27 27 but their enemies’ rage concerned me; their opponents might misunderstand. They might say, “Our strong hands, not the LORD ’s, did all this,”
DEU 32:28 28 because they are not a thoughtful nation; they lack any insight.
DEU 32:29 29 If they had any wisdom, they would understand this; they would discern what will become of them.
DEU 32:30 30 How could one person chase off a thousand in battle? How could two people make ten thousand flee for their lives? Only because their rock sold them off, only because the LORD handed them over!
DEU 32:31 31 But, no, their rocks can’t compare to our rock! Our enemies are completely stupid.
DEU 32:32 32 Their roots run straight from Sodom— from the fields of Gomorrah! Their grapes are pure poison; their grape clusters, nothing but bitter;
DEU 32:33 33 their wine is snake poison, venom from a cruel cobra.
DEU 32:34 34 Don’t I have this stored up, sealed in my vaults?
DEU 32:35 35 Revenge is my domain, so is punishment-in-kind, at the exact moment their step slips up, because the day of their destruction is just around the corner; their final destiny is speeding on its way!
DEU 32:36 36 But the LORD will acquit his people, will have compassion on those who serve him, once he sees that their strength is all gone, that both prisoners and free people are wiped out.
DEU 32:37 37 The Lord will ask, “Where are their gods— the rocks they trusted in—
DEU 32:38 38 who ate up the fat of their sacrifices, who drank their sacred wine? They should stand up and help you! They should protect you now!
DEU 32:39 39 Now, look here: I myself, I’m the one; there are no other gods with me. I’m the one who deals death and gives life; I’m the one who wounded, but now I will heal. There’s no escaping my hand.
DEU 32:40 40 But now I’m lifting my hand to heaven— I swear by my own eternity:
DEU 32:41 41 when I sharpen my blazing sword and my hand grabs hold of justice, I’ll pay my enemies back; I’ll punish in kind everyone who hates me.
DEU 32:42 42 I’ll make my arrows drink much blood, while my sword devours flesh, the blood of the dead and captured, flowing from the heads of enemy generals.”
DEU 32:43 43 Heavens: Rejoice with God! All you gods: bow down to the Lord! Because he will avenge his children’s blood; he will pay back his enemies; he will punish in kind those who hate him; he will cleanse his people’s land.
DEU 32:44 44 So Moses came and recited all the words of this poem in everyone’s hearing; Joshua, Nun’s son, joined him.
DEU 32:45 45 When Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
DEU 32:46 46 he told them: Set your mind on all these words I’m testifying against you right now, because you must command your children to perform carefully all the words of this Instruction.
DEU 32:47 47 This is no trivial matter for you—this is your very life! It is by this means alone that you will prolong your life on the fertile land you are crossing the Jordan River to possess.
DEU 32:48 48 The LORD spoke to Moses that very same day:
DEU 32:49 49 “Hike up the Abarim mountains, to Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab opposite Jericho. Take a good look at the land of Canaan, which I’m giving to the Israelites as their property.
DEU 32:50 50 You will die on the mountain you have hiked up, and you will be gathered to your people just like your brother Aaron, who died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,
DEU 32:51 51 because the two of you were unfaithful toward me in front of the Israelites at the waters of Meribath-kadesh, in the Zin wilderness, because you didn’t treat me with proper respect before the Israelites.
DEU 32:52 52 You can look at the land from the other side of the river, but you won’t enter there.”
DEU 33:1 1 This is the blessing that Moses the man of God gave the Israelites before he died.
DEU 33:2 2 He said: The LORD came from Sinai: from Seir he shone like the dawn on us, from Paran Mountain he beamed down. Thousands of holy ones were with him; his warriors were next to him, ready.
DEU 33:3 3 Yes, those who love the nations— all his holy ones—were at your command; they followed your footsteps; they got moving when you said so.
DEU 33:4 4 Moses gave the Instruction to us— it’s the prized possession of Jacob’s assembly.
DEU 33:5 5 A king came to rule in Jeshurun, when the people’s leaders gathered together, when Israel’s tribes were one.
DEU 33:6 6 “I pray that Reuben lives, doesn’t die, though his numbers are so few.”
DEU 33:7 7 Moses said this to Judah: “ LORD , listen to Judah’s voice! Bring him back to his own people, strengthen his hands; be his help against every enemy.”
DEU 33:8 8 Then he told Levi: “Give your Thummim to Levi, your Urim to your faithful one— the one you tested at Massah, the one you challenged by Meribah’s waters;
DEU 33:9 9 the one who said of his own mother and father: ‘I don’t consider them as such’; of their siblings: ‘I don’t recognize them’; of their own children, ‘I don’t know them’— but who obeyed your words and who guarded your covenant!
DEU 33:10 10 They teach your case laws to Jacob, your Instruction to Israel. They hold sweet incense to your nose; put the entirely burned offering on your altar.
DEU 33:11 11 I pray that the LORD blesses Levi’s strength, favors his hard work, and crushes the insides of his enemies so that those who hate him can’t fight anymore.”
DEU 33:12 12 He said to Benjamin: “The LORD ’s dearest one rests safely on him. The Lord always shields him; he rests on God’s chest.”
DEU 33:13 13 Then he told Joseph: “I pray that his land is blessed by God: with heaven’s gifts from above, with the deep waters stretching out underneath;
DEU 33:14 14 with the gifts produced by the sun, with the gifts generated by the moon;
DEU 33:15 15 with the best fruit from ancient mountains, with the gifts of eternal hills;
DEU 33:16 16 with the gifts of the earth and all that fills it, and the favor of the one who lives on Sinai. I pray that all these rest on Joseph’s head, on the crown of that prince among brothers.
DEU 33:17 17 A firstborn bull —that’s how majestic he is! A wild ox’s horns—those are his horns! With them he gores all peoples completely, to the far ends of the earth! His horns are Ephraim’s tens of thousands. His horns are Manasseh’s thousands.”
DEU 33:18 18 Then he told Zebulun: “Zebulun: celebrate when you are out and about; Issachar: celebrate when you are at home in your tents!
DEU 33:19 19 They call all sorts of people to the mountain, where they offer right sacrifices. It’s true: They’re nourished on the sea’s abundance; they are nourished on buried treasures in the sand.”
DEU 33:20 20 Then he told Gad: “May Gad’s broad lands be blessed! He lives like a lion: he rips an arm, even a head!
DEU 33:21 21 He chose the best part for himself because there, where the commander’s portion was, the leaders of the people gathered together. Gad executed the LORD ’s justice and the Lord’s judgments for Israel.”
DEU 33:22 22 Then he told Dan: “Dan is a lion cub. He jumps up from Bashan.”
DEU 33:23 23 Then he told Naphtali: “Naphtali—you are full of favor, overflowing with the LORD ’s blessing— go possess the west and the south!”
DEU 33:24 24 Finally, he told Asher: “Asher is the most blessed of sons. I pray that he’s his brothers’ favorite— one who dips his foot in fine oil.
DEU 33:25 25 I pray that your dead bolts are iron and copper, and that your strength lasts all your days.”
DEU 33:26 26 Jeshurun! No one compares to God! He rides through heaven to help you, rides majestically through the clouds.
DEU 33:27 27 The most ancient God is a place of safety; the eternal arms are a support. He drove out the enemy before you. He commanded: “Destroy them!”
DEU 33:28 28 So Israel now lives in safety— Jacob’s residence is secure— in a land full of grain and wine, where the heavens drip dew.
DEU 33:29 29 Happy are you, Israel! Who is like you? You are a people saved by the LORD ! He’s the shield that helps you, your majestic sword! Your enemies will come crawling on their knees to you, but you will stomp on their backs!
DEU 34:1 1 Then Moses hiked up from the Moabite plains to Mount Nebo, the peak of the Pisgah slope, which faces Jericho. The LORD showed him the whole land: the Gilead region as far as Dan’s territory;
DEU 34:2 2 all the parts belonging to Naphtali along with the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, as well as the entirety of Judah as far as the Mediterranean Sea;
DEU 34:3 3 also the arid southern plain, and the plain—including the Jericho Valley, Palm City—as far as Zoar.
DEU 34:4 4 Then the LORD said to Moses: “This is the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I promised: ‘I will give it to your descendants.’ I have shown it to you with your own eyes; however, you will not cross over into it.”
DEU 34:5 5 Then Moses, the LORD ’s servant, died—right there in the land of Moab, according to the LORD ’s command.
DEU 34:6 6 The Lord buried him in a valley in Moabite country across from Beth-peor. Even now, no one knows where Moses’ grave is.
DEU 34:7 7 Moses was 120 years old when he died. His eyesight wasn’t impaired, and his vigor hadn’t diminished a bit.
DEU 34:8 8 Back down in the Moabite plains, the Israelites mourned Moses’ death for thirty days. At that point, the time for weeping and for mourning Moses was over.
DEU 34:9 9 Joshua, Nun’s son, was filled with wisdom because Moses had placed his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to Joshua, and they did exactly what the LORD commanded Moses.
DEU 34:10 10 No prophet like Moses has yet emerged in Israel; Moses knew the LORD face-to-face!
DEU 34:11 11 That’s not even to mention all those signs and wonders that the LORD sent Moses to do in Egypt—to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to his entire land—
DEU 34:12 12 as well as all the extraordinary power that Moses displayed before Israel’s own eyes!
MAT 1:1 1 A record of the ancestors of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham:
MAT 1:2 2 Abraham was the father of Isaac. Isaac was the father of Jacob. Jacob was the father of Judah and his brothers.
MAT 1:3 3 Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah, whose mother was Tamar. Perez was the father of Hezron. Hezron was the father of Aram.
MAT 1:4 4 Aram was the father of Amminadab. Amminadab was the father of Nahshon. Nahshon was the father of Salmon.
MAT 1:5 5 Salmon was the father of Boaz, whose mother was Rahab. Boaz was the father of Obed, whose mother was Ruth. Obed was the father of Jesse.
MAT 1:6 6 Jesse was the father of David the king. David was the father of Solomon, whose mother had been the wife of Uriah.
MAT 1:7 7 Solomon was the father of Rehoboam. Rehoboam was the father of Abijah. Abijah was the father of Asaph.
MAT 1:8 8 Asaph was the father of Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat was the father of Joram. Joram was the father of Uzziah.
MAT 1:9 9 Uzziah was the father of Jotham. Jotham was the father of Ahaz. Ahaz was the father of Hezekiah.
MAT 1:10 10 Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh. Manasseh was the father of Amos. Amos was the father of Josiah.
MAT 1:11 11 Josiah was the father of Jechoniah and his brothers. This was at the time of the exile to Babylon.
MAT 1:12 12 After the exile to Babylon: Jechoniah was the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel was the father of Zerubbabel.
MAT 1:13 13 Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud. Abiud was the father of Eliakim. Eliakim was the father of Azor.
MAT 1:14 14 Azor was the father of Zadok. Zadok was the father of Achim. Achim was the father of Eliud.
MAT 1:15 15 Eliud was the father of Eleazar. Eleazar was the father of Matthan. Matthan was the father of Jacob.
MAT 1:16 16 Jacob was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary—of whom Jesus was born, who is called the Christ.
MAT 1:17 17 So there were fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen generations from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen generations from the exile to Babylon to the Christ.
MAT 1:18 18 This is how the birth of Jesus Christ took place. When Mary his mother was engaged to Joseph, before they were married, she became pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
MAT 1:19 19 Joseph her husband was a righteous man. Because he didn’t want to humiliate her, he decided to call off their engagement quietly.
MAT 1:20 20 As he was thinking about this, an angel from the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph son of David, don’t be afraid to take Mary as your wife, because the child she carries was conceived by the Holy Spirit.
MAT 1:21 21 She will give birth to a son, and you will call him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”
MAT 1:22 22 Now all of this took place so that what the Lord had spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled:
MAT 1:23 23 Look! A virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son, And they will call him, Emmanuel. ( Emmanuel means “God with us.”)
MAT 1:24 24 When Joseph woke up, he did just as an angel from God commanded and took Mary as his wife.
MAT 1:25 25 But he didn’t have sexual relations with her until she gave birth to a son. Joseph called him Jesus.
MAT 2:1 1 After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in the territory of Judea during the rule of King Herod, magi came from the east to Jerusalem.
MAT 2:2 2 They asked, “Where is the newborn king of the Jews? We’ve seen his star in the east, and we’ve come to honor him.”
MAT 2:3 3 When King Herod heard this, he was troubled, and everyone in Jerusalem was troubled with him.
MAT 2:4 4 He gathered all the chief priests and the legal experts and asked them where the Christ was to be born.
MAT 2:5 5 They said, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is what the prophet wrote:
MAT 2:6 6 You, Bethlehem, land of Judah, by no means are you least among the rulers of Judah, because from you will come one who governs, who will shepherd my people Israel.
MAT 2:7 7 Then Herod secretly called for the magi and found out from them the time when the star had first appeared.
MAT 2:8 8 He sent them to Bethlehem, saying, “Go and search carefully for the child. When you’ve found him, report to me so that I too may go and honor him.”
MAT 2:9 9 When they heard the king, they went; and look, the star they had seen in the east went ahead of them until it stood over the place where the child was.
MAT 2:10 10 When they saw the star, they were filled with joy.
MAT 2:11 11 They entered the house and saw the child with Mary his mother. Falling to their knees, they honored him. Then they opened their treasure chests and presented him with gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
MAT 2:12 12 Because they were warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own country by another route.
MAT 2:13 13 When the magi had departed, an angel from the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream and said, “Get up. Take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod will soon search for the child in order to kill him.”
MAT 2:14 14 Joseph got up and, during the night, took the child and his mother to Egypt.
MAT 2:15 15 He stayed there until Herod died. This fulfilled what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: I have called my son out of Egypt .
MAT 2:16 16 When Herod knew the magi had fooled him, he grew very angry. He sent soldiers to kill all the children in Bethlehem and in all the surrounding territory who were two years old and younger, according to the time that he had learned from the magi.
MAT 2:17 17 This fulfilled the word spoken through Jeremiah the prophet:
MAT 2:18 18 A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and much grieving. Rachel weeping for her children, and she did not want to be comforted, because they were no more.
MAT 2:19 19 After King Herod died, an angel from the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt.
MAT 2:20 20 “Get up,” the angel said, “and take the child and his mother and go to the land of Israel. Those who were trying to kill the child are dead.”
MAT 2:21 21 Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and went to the land of Israel.
MAT 2:22 22 But when he heard that Archelaus ruled over Judea in place of his father Herod, Joseph was afraid to go there. Having been warned in a dream, he went to the area of Galilee.
MAT 2:23 23 He settled in a city called Nazareth so that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: He will be called a Nazarene.
MAT 3:1 1 In those days John the Baptist appeared in the desert of Judea announcing,
MAT 3:2 2 “Change your hearts and lives! Here comes the kingdom of heaven!”
MAT 3:3 3 He was the one of whom Isaiah the prophet spoke when he said: The voice of one shouting in the wilderness, “ Prepare the way for the Lord; make his paths straight. ”
MAT 3:4 4 John wore clothes made of camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
MAT 3:5 5 People from Jerusalem, throughout Judea, and all around the Jordan River came to him.
MAT 3:6 6 As they confessed their sins, he baptized them in the Jordan River.
MAT 3:7 7 Many Pharisees and Sadducees came to be baptized by John. He said to them, “You children of snakes! Who warned you to escape from the angry judgment that is coming soon?
MAT 3:8 8 Produce fruit that shows you have changed your hearts and lives.
MAT 3:9 9 And don’t even think about saying to yourselves, Abraham is our father. I tell you that God is able to raise up Abraham’s children from these stones.
MAT 3:10 10 The ax is already at the root of the trees. Therefore, every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit will be chopped down and tossed into the fire.
MAT 3:11 11 I baptize with water those of you who have changed your hearts and lives. The one who is coming after me is stronger than I am. I’m not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and with fire.
MAT 3:12 12 The shovel he uses to sift the wheat from the husks is in his hands. He will clean out his threshing area and bring the wheat into his barn. But he will burn the husks with a fire that can’t be put out.”
MAT 3:13 13 At that time Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan River so that John would baptize him.
MAT 3:14 14 John tried to stop him and said, “I need to be baptized by you, yet you come to me?”
MAT 3:15 15 Jesus answered, “ Allow me to be baptized now. This is necessary to fulfill all righteousness. ” So John agreed to baptize Jesus.
MAT 3:16 16 When Jesus was baptized, he immediately came up out of the water. Heaven was opened to him, and he saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove and resting on him.
MAT 3:17 17 A voice from heaven said, “This is my Son whom I dearly love; I find happiness in him.”
MAT 4:1 1 Then the Spirit led Jesus up into the wilderness so that the devil might tempt him.
MAT 4:2 2 After Jesus had fasted for forty days and forty nights, he was starving.
MAT 4:3 3 The tempter came to him and said, “Since you are God’s Son, command these stones to become bread.”
MAT 4:4 4 Jesus replied, “ It’s written, People won’t live only by bread, but by every word spoken by God . ”
MAT 4:5 5 After that the devil brought him into the holy city and stood him at the highest point of the temple. He said to him,
MAT 4:6 6 “Since you are God’s Son, throw yourself down; for it is written, I will command my angels concerning you, and they will take you up in their hands so that you won’t hit your foot on a stone. ”
MAT 4:7 7 Jesus replied, “ Again it’s written, Don’t test the Lord your God . ”
MAT 4:8 8 Then the devil brought him to a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
MAT 4:9 9 He said, “I’ll give you all these if you bow down and worship me.”
MAT 4:10 10 Jesus responded, “ Go away, Satan, because it’s written, You will worship the Lord your God and serve only him . ”
MAT 4:11 11 The devil left him, and angels came and took care of him.
MAT 4:12 12 Now when Jesus heard that John was arrested, he went to Galilee.
MAT 4:13 13 He left Nazareth and settled in Capernaum, which lies alongside the sea in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali.
MAT 4:14 14 This fulfilled what Isaiah the prophet said:
MAT 4:15 15 Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, alongside the sea, across the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,
MAT 4:16 16 the people who lived in the dark have seen a great light, and a light has come upon those who lived in the region and in shadow of death.
MAT 4:17 17 From that time Jesus began to announce, “ Change your hearts and lives! Here comes the kingdom of heaven! ”
MAT 4:18 18 As Jesus walked alongside the Galilee Sea, he saw two brothers, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, throwing fishing nets into the sea, because they were fishermen.
MAT 4:19 19 “Come, follow me,” he said, “and I’ll show you how to fish for people.”
MAT 4:20 20 Right away, they left their nets and followed him.
MAT 4:21 21 Continuing on, he saw another set of brothers, James the son of Zebedee and his brother John. They were in a boat with Zebedee their father repairing their nets. Jesus called them and
MAT 4:22 22 immediately they left the boat and their father and followed him.
MAT 4:23 23 Jesus traveled throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues. He announced the good news of the kingdom and healed every disease and sickness among the people.
MAT 4:24 24 News about him spread throughout Syria. People brought to him all those who had various kinds of diseases, those in pain, those possessed by demons, those with epilepsy, and those who were paralyzed, and he healed them.
MAT 4:25 25 Large crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and from the areas beyond the Jordan River.
MAT 5:1 1 Now when Jesus saw the crowds, he went up a mountain. He sat down and his disciples came to him.
MAT 5:2 2 He taught them, saying:
MAT 5:3 3 “Happy are people who are hopeless, because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
MAT 5:4 4 “Happy are people who grieve, because they will be made glad.
MAT 5:5 5 “Happy are people who are humble, because they will inherit the earth.
MAT 5:6 6 “Happy are people who are hungry and thirsty for righteousness, because they will be fed until they are full.
MAT 5:7 7 “Happy are people who show mercy, because they will receive mercy.
MAT 5:8 8 “Happy are people who have pure hearts, because they will see God.
MAT 5:9 9 “Happy are people who make peace, because they will be called God’s children.
MAT 5:10 10 “Happy are people whose lives are harassed because they are righteous, because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
MAT 5:11 11 “Happy are you when people insult you and harass you and speak all kinds of bad and false things about you, all because of me.
MAT 5:12 12 Be full of joy and be glad, because you have a great reward in heaven. In the same way, people harassed the prophets who came before you.
MAT 5:13 13 “You are the salt of the earth. But if salt loses its saltiness, how will it become salty again? It’s good for nothing except to be thrown away and trampled under people’s feet.
MAT 5:14 14 You are the light of the world. A city on top of a hill can’t be hidden.
MAT 5:15 15 Neither do people light a lamp and put it under a basket. Instead, they put it on top of a lampstand, and it shines on all who are in the house.
MAT 5:16 16 In the same way, let your light shine before people, so they can see the good things you do and praise your Father who is in heaven.
MAT 5:17 17 “Don’t even begin to think that I have come to do away with the Law and the Prophets. I haven’t come to do away with them but to fulfill them.
MAT 5:18 18 I say to you very seriously that as long as heaven and earth exist, neither the smallest letter nor even the smallest stroke of a pen will be erased from the Law until everything there becomes a reality.
MAT 5:19 19 Therefore, whoever ignores one of the least of these commands and teaches others to do the same will be called the lowest in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever keeps these commands and teaches people to keep them will be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
MAT 5:20 20 I say to you that unless your righteousness is greater than the righteousness of the legal experts and the Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
MAT 5:21 21 “You have heard that it was said to those who lived long ago, Don’t commit murder, and all who commit murder will be in danger of judgment.
MAT 5:22 22 But I say to you that everyone who is angry with their brother or sister will be in danger of judgment. If they say to their brother or sister, ‘You idiot,’ they will be in danger of being condemned by the governing council. And if they say, ‘You fool,’ they will be in danger of fiery hell.
MAT 5:23 23 Therefore, if you bring your gift to the altar and there remember that your brother or sister has something against you,
MAT 5:24 24 leave your gift at the altar and go. First make things right with your brother or sister and then come back and offer your gift.
MAT 5:25 25 Be sure to make friends quickly with your opponents while you are with them on the way to court. Otherwise, they will haul you before the judge, the judge will turn you over to the officer of the court, and you will be thrown into prison.
MAT 5:26 26 I say to you in all seriousness that you won’t get out of there until you’ve paid the very last penny.
MAT 5:27 27 “You have heard that it was said, Don’t commit adultery.
MAT 5:28 28 But I say to you that every man who looks at a woman lustfully has already committed adultery in his heart.
MAT 5:29 29 And if your right eye causes you to fall into sin, tear it out and throw it away. It’s better that you lose a part of your body than that your whole body be thrown into hell.
MAT 5:30 30 And if your right hand causes you to fall into sin, chop it off and throw it away. It’s better that you lose a part of your body than that your whole body go into hell.
MAT 5:31 31 “It was said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a divorce certificate.’
MAT 5:32 32 But I say to you that whoever divorces his wife except for sexual unfaithfulness forces her to commit adultery. And whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
MAT 5:33 33 “Again you have heard that it was said to those who lived long ago: Don’t make a false solemn pledge, but you should follow through on what you have pledged to the Lord.
MAT 5:34 34 But I say to you that you must not pledge at all. You must not pledge by heaven, because it’s God’s throne.
MAT 5:35 35 You must not pledge by the earth, because it’s God’s footstool. You must not pledge by Jerusalem, because it’s the city of the great king.
MAT 5:36 36 And you must not pledge by your head, because you can’t turn one hair white or black.
MAT 5:37 37 Let your yes mean yes, and your no mean no. Anything more than this comes from the evil one.
MAT 5:38 38 “You have heard that it was said, An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth .
MAT 5:39 39 But I say to you that you must not oppose those who want to hurt you. If people slap you on your right cheek, you must turn the left cheek to them as well.
MAT 5:40 40 When they wish to haul you to court and take your shirt, let them have your coat too.
MAT 5:41 41 When they force you to go one mile, go with them two.
MAT 5:42 42 Give to those who ask, and don’t refuse those who wish to borrow from you.
MAT 5:43 43 “You have heard that it was said, You must love your neighbor and hate your enemy.
MAT 5:44 44 But I say to you, love your enemies and pray for those who harass you
MAT 5:45 45 so that you will be acting as children of your Father who is in heaven. He makes the sun rise on both the evil and the good and sends rain on both the righteous and the unrighteous.
MAT 5:46 46 If you love only those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
MAT 5:47 47 And if you greet only your brothers and sisters, what more are you doing? Don’t even the Gentiles do the same?
MAT 5:48 48 Therefore, just as your heavenly Father is complete in showing love to everyone, so also you must be complete.
MAT 6:1 1 “Be careful that you don’t practice your religion in front of people to draw their attention. If you do, you will have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.
MAT 6:2 2 “Whenever you give to the poor, don’t blow your trumpet as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets so that they may get praise from people. I assure you, that’s the only reward they’ll get.
MAT 6:3 3 But when you give to the poor, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand is doing
MAT 6:4 4 so that you may give to the poor in secret. Your Father who sees what you do in secret will reward you.
MAT 6:5 5 “When you pray, don’t be like hypocrites. They love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the street corners so that people will see them. I assure you, that’s the only reward they’ll get.
MAT 6:6 6 But when you pray, go to your room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is present in that secret place. Your Father who sees what you do in secret will reward you.
MAT 6:7 7 “When you pray, don’t pour out a flood of empty words, as the Gentiles do. They think that by saying many words they’ll be heard.
MAT 6:8 8 Don’t be like them, because your Father knows what you need before you ask.
MAT 6:9 9 Pray like this: Our Father who is in heaven, uphold the holiness of your name.
MAT 6:10 10 Bring in your kingdom so that your will is done on earth as it’s done in heaven.
MAT 6:11 11 Give us the bread we need for today.
MAT 6:12 12 Forgive us for the ways we have wronged you, just as we also forgive those who have wronged us.
MAT 6:13 13 And don’t lead us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.
MAT 6:14 14 “If you forgive others their sins, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
MAT 6:15 15 But if you don’t forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your sins.
MAT 6:16 16 “And when you fast, don’t put on a sad face like the hypocrites. They distort their faces so people will know they are fasting. I assure you that they have their reward.
MAT 6:17 17 When you fast, brush your hair and wash your face.
MAT 6:18 18 Then you won’t look like you are fasting to people, but only to your Father who is present in that secret place. Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
MAT 6:19 19 “Stop collecting treasures for your own benefit on earth, where moth and rust eat them and where thieves break in and steal them.
MAT 6:20 20 Instead, collect treasures for yourselves in heaven, where moth and rust don’t eat them and where thieves don’t break in and steal them.
MAT 6:21 21 Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
MAT 6:22 22 “The eye is the lamp of the body. Therefore, if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.
MAT 6:23 23 But if your eye is bad, your whole body will be full of darkness. If then the light in you is darkness, how terrible that darkness will be!
MAT 6:24 24 No one can serve two masters. Either you will hate the one and love the other, or you will be loyal to the one and have contempt for the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
MAT 6:25 25 “Therefore, I say to you, don’t worry about your life, what you’ll eat or what you’ll drink, or about your body, what you’ll wear. Isn’t life more than food and the body more than clothes?
MAT 6:26 26 Look at the birds in the sky. They don’t sow seed or harvest grain or gather crops into barns. Yet your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you worth much more than they are?
MAT 6:27 27 Who among you by worrying can add a single moment to your life?
MAT 6:28 28 And why do you worry about clothes? Notice how the lilies in the field grow. They don’t wear themselves out with work, and they don’t spin cloth.
MAT 6:29 29 But I say to you that even Solomon in all of his splendor wasn’t dressed like one of these.
MAT 6:30 30 If God dresses grass in the field so beautifully, even though it’s alive today and tomorrow it’s thrown into the furnace, won’t God do much more for you, you people of weak faith?
MAT 6:31 31 Therefore, don’t worry and say, ‘What are we going to eat?’ or ‘What are we going to drink?’ or ‘What are we going to wear?’
MAT 6:32 32 Gentiles long for all these things. Your heavenly Father knows that you need them.
MAT 6:33 33 Instead, desire first and foremost God’s kingdom and God’s righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
MAT 6:34 34 Therefore, stop worrying about tomorrow, because tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
MAT 7:1 1 “Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.
MAT 7:2 2 You’ll receive the same judgment you give. Whatever you deal out will be dealt out to you.
MAT 7:3 3 Why do you see the splinter that’s in your brother’s or sister’s eye, but don’t notice the log in your own eye?
MAT 7:4 4 How can you say to your brother or sister, ‘Let me take the splinter out of your eye,’ when there’s a log in your eye?
MAT 7:5 5 You deceive yourself! First take the log out of your eye, and then you’ll see clearly to take the splinter out of your brother’s or sister’s eye.
MAT 7:6 6 Don’t give holy things to dogs, and don’t throw your pearls in front of pigs. They will stomp on the pearls, then turn around and attack you.
MAT 7:7 7 “Ask, and you will receive. Search, and you will find. Knock, and the door will be opened to you.
MAT 7:8 8 For everyone who asks, receives. Whoever seeks, finds. And to everyone who knocks, the door is opened.
MAT 7:9 9 Who among you will give your children a stone when they ask for bread?
MAT 7:10 10 Or give them a snake when they ask for fish?
MAT 7:11 11 If you who are evil know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your heavenly Father give good things to those who ask him.
MAT 7:12 12 Therefore, you should treat people in the same way that you want people to treat you; this is the Law and the Prophets.
MAT 7:13 13 “Go in through the narrow gate. The gate that leads to destruction is broad and the road wide, so many people enter through it.
MAT 7:14 14 But the gate that leads to life is narrow and the road difficult, so few people find it.
MAT 7:15 15 “Watch out for false prophets. They come to you dressed like sheep, but inside they are vicious wolves.
MAT 7:16 16 You will know them by their fruit. Do people get bunches of grapes from thorny weeds, or do they get figs from thistles?
MAT 7:17 17 In the same way, every good tree produces good fruit, and every rotten tree produces bad fruit.
MAT 7:18 18 A good tree can’t produce bad fruit. And a rotten tree can’t produce good fruit.
MAT 7:19 19 Every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit is chopped down and thrown into the fire.
MAT 7:20 20 Therefore, you will know them by their fruit.
MAT 7:21 21 “Not everybody who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will get into the kingdom of heaven. Only those who do the will of my Father who is in heaven will enter.
MAT 7:22 22 On the Judgment Day, many people will say to me, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name and expel demons in your name and do lots of miracles in your name?’
MAT 7:23 23 Then I’ll tell them, ‘I’ve never known you. Get away from me, you people who do wrong.’
MAT 7:24 24 “ Everybody who hears these words of mine and puts them into practice is like a wise builder who built a house on bedrock.
MAT 7:25 25 The rain fell, the floods came, and the wind blew and beat against that house. It didn’t fall because it was firmly set on bedrock.
MAT 7:26 26 But everybody who hears these words of mine and doesn’t put them into practice will be like a fool who built a house on sand.
MAT 7:27 27 The rain fell, the floods came, and the wind blew and beat against that house. It fell and was completely destroyed. ”
MAT 7:28 28 When Jesus finished these words, the crowds were amazed at his teaching
MAT 7:29 29 because he was teaching them like someone with authority and not like their legal experts.
MAT 8:1 1 Now when Jesus had come down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
MAT 8:2 2 A man with a skin disease came, kneeled before him, and said, “Lord, if you want, you can make me clean.”
MAT 8:3 3 Jesus reached out his hand and touched him, saying, “ I do want to. Become clean. ” Instantly his skin disease was cleansed.
MAT 8:4 4 Jesus said to him, “ Don’t say anything to anyone. Instead, go and show yourself to the priest and offer the gift that Moses commanded. This will be a testimony to them. ”
MAT 8:5 5 When Jesus went to Capernaum, a centurion approached,
MAT 8:6 6 pleading with him, “Lord, my servant is flat on his back at home, paralyzed, and his suffering is awful.”
MAT 8:7 7 Jesus responded, “ I’ll come and heal him. ”
MAT 8:8 8 But the centurion replied, “Lord, I don’t deserve to have you come under my roof. Just say the word and my servant will be healed.
MAT 8:9 9 I’m a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to one, ‘Go,’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes. I say to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and the servant does it.”
MAT 8:10 10 When Jesus heard this, he was impressed and said to the people following him, “ I say to you with all seriousness that even in Israel I haven’t found faith like this.
MAT 8:11 11 I say to you that there are many who will come from east and west and sit down to eat with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
MAT 8:12 12 But the children of the kingdom will be thrown outside into the darkness. People there will be weeping and grinding their teeth. ”
MAT 8:13 13 Jesus said to the centurion, “ Go; it will be done for you just as you have believed. ” And his servant was healed that very moment.
MAT 8:14 14 Jesus went home with Peter and saw Peter’s mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.
MAT 8:15 15 He touched her hand, and the fever left her. Then she got up and served them.
MAT 8:16 16 That evening people brought to Jesus many who were demon-possessed. He threw the spirits out with just a word. He healed everyone who was sick.
MAT 8:17 17 This happened so that what Isaiah the prophet said would be fulfilled: He is the one who took our illnesses and carried away our diseases.
MAT 8:18 18 Now when Jesus saw the crowd, he ordered his disciples to go over to the other side of the lake.
MAT 8:19 19 A legal expert came and said to him, “Teacher, I’ll follow you wherever you go.”
MAT 8:20 20 Jesus replied, “ Foxes have dens, and the birds in the sky have nests, but the Human One has no place to lay his head. ”
MAT 8:21 21 Another man, one of his disciples, said to him, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
MAT 8:22 22 But Jesus said to him, “ Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead. ”
MAT 8:23 23 When Jesus got into a boat, his disciples followed him.
MAT 8:24 24 A huge storm arose on the lake so that waves were sloshing over the boat. But Jesus was asleep.
MAT 8:25 25 They came and woke him, saying, “Lord, rescue us! We’re going to drown!”
MAT 8:26 26 He said to them, “ Why are you afraid, you people of weak faith? ” Then he got up and gave orders to the winds and the lake, and there was a great calm.
MAT 8:27 27 The people were amazed and said, “What kind of person is this? Even the winds and the lake obey him!”
MAT 8:28 28 When Jesus arrived on the other side of the lake in the country of the Gadarenes, two men who were demon-possessed came from among the tombs to meet him. They were so violent that nobody could travel on that road.
MAT 8:29 29 They cried out, “What are you going to do with us, Son of God? Have you come to torture us before the time of judgment?”
MAT 8:30 30 Far off in the distance a large herd of pigs was feeding.
MAT 8:31 31 The demons pleaded with him, “If you throw us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”
MAT 8:32 32 Then he said to the demons, “ Go away, ” and they came out and went into the pigs. The whole herd rushed down the cliff into the lake and drowned.
MAT 8:33 33 Those who tended the pigs ran into the city and told everything that had happened to the demon-possessed men.
MAT 8:34 34 Then the whole city came out and met Jesus. When they saw him, they pleaded with him to leave their region.
MAT 9:1 1 Boarding a boat, Jesus crossed to the other side of the lake and went to his own city.
MAT 9:2 2 People brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a cot. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the man who was paralyzed, “ Be encouraged, my child, your sins are forgiven. ”
MAT 9:3 3 Some legal experts said among themselves, “This man is insulting God.”
MAT 9:4 4 But Jesus knew what they were thinking and said, “ Why do you fill your minds with evil things?
MAT 9:5 5 Which is easier—to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
MAT 9:6 6 But so you will know that the Human One has authority on the earth to forgive sins ”—he said to the man who was paralyzed—“ Get up, take your cot, and go home. ”
MAT 9:7 7 The man got up and went home.
MAT 9:8 8 When the crowds saw what had happened, they were afraid and praised God, who had given such authority to human beings.
MAT 9:9 9 As Jesus continued on from there, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at a kiosk for collecting taxes. He said to him, “ Follow me, ” and he got up and followed him.
MAT 9:10 10 As Jesus sat down to eat in Matthew’s house, many tax collectors and sinners joined Jesus and his disciples at the table.
MAT 9:11 11 But when the Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
MAT 9:12 12 When Jesus heard it, he said, “ Healthy people don’t need a doctor, but sick people do.
MAT 9:13 13 Go and learn what this means: I want mercy and not sacrifice . I didn’t come to call righteous people, but sinners. ”
MAT 9:14 14 At that time John’s disciples came and asked Jesus, “Why do we and the Pharisees frequently fast, but your disciples never fast?”
MAT 9:15 15 Jesus responded, “The wedding guests can’t mourn while the groom is still with them, can they? But the days will come when the groom will be taken away from them, and then they’ll fast.
MAT 9:16 16 “ No one sews a piece of new, unshrunk cloth on old clothes because the patch tears away the cloth and makes a worse tear.
MAT 9:17 17 No one pours new wine into old wineskins. If they did, the wineskins would burst, the wine would spill, and the wineskins would be ruined. Instead, people pour new wine into new wineskins so that both are kept safe. ”
MAT 9:18 18 While Jesus was speaking to them, a ruler came and knelt in front of him, saying, “My daughter has just died. But come and place your hand on her, and she’ll live.”
MAT 9:19 19 So Jesus and his disciples got up and went with him.
MAT 9:20 20 Then a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years came up behind Jesus and touched the hem of his clothes.
MAT 9:21 21 She thought, If I only touch his robe I’ll be healed.
MAT 9:22 22 When Jesus turned and saw her, he said, “ Be encouraged, daughter. Your faith has healed you. ” And the woman was healed from that time on.
MAT 9:23 23 When Jesus went into the ruler’s house, he saw the flute players and the distressed crowd.
MAT 9:24 24 He said, “ Go away, because the little girl isn’t dead but is asleep ”; but they laughed at him.

MAT 9:26 26 News about this spread throughout that whole region.
MAT 9:27 27 As Jesus departed, two blind men followed him, crying out, “Show us mercy, Son of David.”
MAT 9:28 28 When he came into the house, the blind men approached him. Jesus said to them, “ Do you believe I can do this? ” “Yes, Lord,” they replied.
MAT 9:29 29 Then Jesus touched their eyes and said, “ It will happen for you just as you have believed. ”
MAT 9:30 30 Their eyes were opened. Then Jesus sternly warned them, “ Make sure nobody knows about this. ”
MAT 9:31 31 But they went out and spread the word about him throughout that whole region.
MAT 9:32 32 As they were leaving, people brought to him a man who was demon-possessed and unable to speak.
MAT 9:33 33 When Jesus had thrown out the demon, the man who couldn’t speak began to talk. The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel.”
MAT 9:34 34 But the Pharisees said, “He throws out demons with the authority of the ruler of demons.”

MAT 9:36 36 Now when Jesus saw the crowds, he had compassion for them because they were troubled and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
MAT 9:37 37 Then he said to his disciples, “ The size of the harvest is bigger than you can imagine, but there are few workers.
MAT 9:38 38 Therefore, plead with the Lord of the harvest to send out workers for his harvest. ”
MAT 10:1 1 He called his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits to throw them out and to heal every disease and every sickness.
MAT 10:2 2 Here are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, who is called Peter; and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee; and John his brother;
MAT 10:3 3 Philip; and Bartholomew; Thomas; and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus; and Thaddaeus;
MAT 10:4 4 Simon the Cananaean; and Judas, who betrayed Jesus.
MAT 10:5 5 Jesus sent these twelve out and commanded them, “Don’t go among the Gentiles or into a Samaritan city.
MAT 10:6 6 Go instead to the lost sheep, the people of Israel.
MAT 10:7 7 As you go, make this announcement: ‘The kingdom of heaven has come near.’
MAT 10:8 8 Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those with skin diseases, and throw out demons. You received without having to pay. Therefore, give without demanding payment.
MAT 10:9 9 Workers deserve to be fed, so don’t gather gold or silver or copper coins for your money belts to take on your trips.
MAT 10:10 10 Don’t take a backpack for the road or two shirts or sandals or a walking stick.
MAT 10:11 11 Whatever city or village you go into, find somebody in it who is worthy and stay there until you go on your way.
MAT 10:12 12 When you go into a house, say, ‘Peace!’
MAT 10:13 13 If the house is worthy, give it your blessing of peace. But if the house isn’t worthy, take back your blessing.
MAT 10:14 14 If anyone refuses to welcome you or listen to your words, shake the dust off your feet as you leave that house or city.
MAT 10:15 15 I assure you that it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on Judgment Day than it will be for that city.
MAT 10:16 16 “Look, I’m sending you as sheep among wolves. Therefore, be wise as snakes and innocent as doves.
MAT 10:17 17 Watch out for people—because they will hand you over to councils and they will beat you in their synagogues.
MAT 10:18 18 They will haul you in front of governors and even kings because of me so that you may give your testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
MAT 10:19 19 Whenever they hand you over, don’t worry about how to speak or what you will say, because what you can say will be given to you at that moment.
MAT 10:20 20 You aren’t doing the talking, but the Spirit of my Father is doing the talking through you.
MAT 10:21 21 Brothers and sisters will hand each other over to be executed. A father will turn his child in. Children will defy their parents and have them executed.
MAT 10:22 22 Everyone will hate you on account of my name. But whoever stands firm until the end will be saved.
MAT 10:23 23 Whenever they harass you in one city, escape to the next, because I assure that you will not go through all the cities of Israel before the Human One comes.
MAT 10:24 24 “Disciples aren’t greater than their teacher, and slaves aren’t greater than their master.
MAT 10:25 25 It’s enough for disciples to be like their teacher and slaves like their master. If they have called the head of the house Beelzebul, it’s certain that they will call the members of his household by even worse names.
MAT 10:26 26 “Therefore, don’t be afraid of those people because nothing is hidden that won’t be revealed, and nothing secret that won’t be brought out into the open.
MAT 10:27 27 What I say to you in the darkness, tell in the light; and what you hear whispered, announce from the rooftops.
MAT 10:28 28 Don’t be afraid of those who kill the body but can’t kill the soul. Instead, be afraid of the one who can destroy both body and soul in hell.
MAT 10:29 29 Aren’t two sparrows sold for a small coin? But not one of them will fall to the ground without your Father knowing about it already.
MAT 10:30 30 Even the hairs of your head are all counted.
MAT 10:31 31 Don’t be afraid. You are worth more than many sparrows.
MAT 10:32 32 “Therefore, everyone who acknowledges me before people, I also will acknowledge before my Father who is in heaven.
MAT 10:33 33 But everyone who denies me before people, I also will deny before my Father who is in heaven.
MAT 10:34 34 “Don’t think that I’ve come to bring peace to the earth. I haven’t come to bring peace but a sword.
MAT 10:35 35 I’ve come to turn a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law .
MAT 10:36 36 People’s enemies are members of their own households .
MAT 10:37 37 “Those who love father or mother more than me aren’t worthy of me. Those who love son or daughter more than me aren’t worthy of me.
MAT 10:38 38 Those who don’t pick up their crosses and follow me aren’t worthy of me.
MAT 10:39 39 Those who find their lives will lose them, and those who lose their lives because of me will find them.
MAT 10:40 40 “ Those who receive you are also receiving me, and those who receive me are receiving the one who sent me.
MAT 10:41 41 Those who receive a prophet as a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward. Those who receive a righteous person as a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward.
MAT 10:42 42 I assure you that everybody who gives even a cup of cold water to these little ones because they are my disciples will certainly be rewarded. ”

MAT 11:29 29 Put on my yoke, and learn from me. I’m gentle and humble. And you will find rest for yourselves.
MAT 11:30 30 My yoke is easy to bear, and my burden is light. ”
MAT 12:1 1 At that time Jesus went through the wheat fields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry so they were picking heads of wheat and eating them.
MAT 12:2 2 When the Pharisees saw this, they said to him, “Look, your disciples are breaking the Sabbath law.”
MAT 12:3 3 But he said to them, “ Haven’t you read what David did when he and those with him were hungry?
MAT 12:4 4 He went into God’s house and broke the law by eating the bread of the presence, which only the priests were allowed to eat.
MAT 12:5 5 Or haven’t you read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple treat the Sabbath as any other day and are still innocent?
MAT 12:6 6 But I tell you that something greater than the temple is here.
MAT 12:7 7 If you had known what this means, I want mercy and not sacrifice , you wouldn’t have condemned the innocent.
MAT 12:8 8 The Human One is Lord of the Sabbath. ”
MAT 12:9 9 Jesus left that place and went into their synagogue.
MAT 12:10 10 A man with a withered hand was there. Wanting to bring charges against Jesus, they asked, “Does the Law allow a person to heal on the Sabbath?”
MAT 12:11 11 Jesus replied, “ Who among you has a sheep that falls into a pit on the Sabbath and will not take hold of it and pull it out?
MAT 12:12 12 How much more valuable is a person than a sheep! So the Law allows a person to do what is good on the Sabbath. ”
MAT 12:13 13 Then Jesus said to the man, “ Stretch out your hand. ” So he did and it was made healthy, just like the other one.
MAT 12:14 14 The Pharisees went out and met in order to find a way to destroy Jesus.
MAT 12:15 15 Jesus knew what they intended to do, so he went away from there. Large crowds followed him, and he healed them all.
MAT 12:16 16 But he ordered them not to spread the word about him,
MAT 12:17 17 so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:
MAT 12:18 18 Look, my Servant whom I chose, the one I love, in whom I find great pleasure . I’ll put my Spirit upon him, and he’ll announce judgment to the Gentiles.
MAT 12:19 19 He won’t argue or shout, and nobody will hear his voice in the streets.
MAT 12:20 20 He won’t break a bent stalk, and he won’t snuff out a smoldering wick, until he makes justice win.
MAT 12:21 21 And the Gentiles will put their hope in his name.
MAT 12:22 22 They brought to Jesus a demon-possessed man who was blind and unable to speak. Jesus healed him so that he could both speak and see.
MAT 12:23 23 All the crowds were amazed and said, “This man couldn’t be the Son of David, could he?”
MAT 12:24 24 When the Pharisees heard, they said, “This man throws out demons only by the authority of Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”
MAT 12:25 25 Because Jesus knew what they were thinking, he replied, “Every kingdom involved in civil war becomes a wasteland. Every city or house torn apart by divisions will collapse.
MAT 12:26 26 If Satan throws out Satan, he is at war with himself. How then can his kingdom endure?
MAT 12:27 27 And if I throw out demons by the authority of Beelzebul, then by whose authority do your followers throw them out? Therefore, they will be your judges.
MAT 12:28 28 But if I throw out demons by the power of God’s Spirit, then God’s kingdom has already overtaken you.
MAT 12:29 29 Can people go into a house that belongs to a strong man and steal his possessions, unless they first tie up the strong man? Then they can rob his house.
MAT 12:30 30 Whoever isn’t with me is against me, and whoever doesn’t gather with me scatters.
MAT 12:31 31 “Therefore, I tell you that people will be forgiven for every sin and insult to God. But insulting the Holy Spirit won’t be forgiven.
MAT 12:32 32 And whoever speaks a word against the Human One will be forgiven. But whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit won’t be forgiven, not in this age or in the age that is coming.
MAT 12:33 33 “ Either consider the tree good and its fruit good, or consider the tree rotten and its fruit rotten. A tree is known by its fruit.
MAT 12:34 34 Children of snakes! How can you speak good things while you are evil? What fills the heart comes out of the mouth.
MAT 12:35 35 Good people bring out good things from their good treasure. But evil people bring out evil things from their evil treasure.
MAT 12:36 36 I tell you that people will have to answer on Judgment Day for every useless word they speak.
MAT 12:37 37 By your words you will be either judged innocent or condemned as guilty. ”
MAT 12:38 38 At that time some of the legal experts and the Pharisees requested of Jesus, “Teacher, we would like to see a sign from you.”
MAT 12:39 39 But he replied, “An evil and unfaithful generation searches for a sign, but it won’t receive any sign except Jonah’s sign.
MAT 12:40 40 Just as Jonah was in the whale’s belly for three days and three nights , so the Human One will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.
MAT 12:41 41 The citizens of Nineveh will stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it as guilty, because they changed their hearts and lives in response to Jonah’s preaching. And look, someone greater than Jonah is here.
MAT 12:42 42 The queen of the South will be raised up by God at the judgment with this generation and condemn it because she came from a distant land to hear Solomon’s wisdom. And look, someone greater than Solomon is here.
MAT 12:43 43 “ When an unclean spirit leaves a person, it wanders through dry places looking for a place to rest. But it doesn’t find any.
MAT 12:44 44 Then it says, ‘I’ll go back to the house I left.’ When it arrives, it finds the place vacant, cleaned up, and decorated.
MAT 12:45 45 Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more evil than itself. They go in and make their home there. That person is worse off at the end than at the beginning. This is the way it will be also for this evil generation. ”
MAT 12:46 46 While Jesus was speaking to the crowds, his mother and brothers stood outside trying to speak with him.
MAT 12:47 47 Someone said to him, “Look, your mother and brothers are outside wanting to speak with you.”
MAT 12:48 48 Jesus replied, “ Who is my mother? Who are my brothers? ”
MAT 12:49 49 He stretched out his hand toward his disciples and said, “ Look, here are my mother and my brothers.
MAT 12:50 50 Whoever does the will of my Father who is in heaven is my brother, sister, and mother. ”
MAT 13:1 1 That day Jesus went out of the house and sat down beside the lake.
MAT 13:2 2 Such large crowds gathered around him that he climbed into a boat and sat down. The whole crowd was standing on the shore.
MAT 13:3 3 He said many things to them in parables: “ A farmer went out to scatter seed.
MAT 13:4 4 As he was scattering seed, some fell on the path, and birds came and ate it.
MAT 13:5 5 Other seed fell on rocky ground where the soil was shallow. They sprouted immediately because the soil wasn’t deep.
MAT 13:6 6 But when the sun came up, it scorched the plants, and they dried up because they had no roots.
MAT 13:7 7 Other seed fell among thorny plants. The thorny plants grew and choked them.
MAT 13:8 8 Other seed fell on good soil and bore fruit, in one case a yield of one hundred to one, in another case a yield of sixty to one, and in another case a yield of thirty to one.
MAT 13:9 9 Everyone who has ears should pay attention. ”
MAT 13:10 10 Jesus’ disciples came and said to him, “Why do you use parables when you speak to the crowds?”
MAT 13:11 11 Jesus replied, “Because they haven’t received the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but you have.
MAT 13:12 12 For those who have will receive more and they will have more than enough. But as for those who don’t have, even the little they have will be taken away from them.
MAT 13:13 13 This is why I speak to the crowds in parables: although they see, they don’t really see; and although they hear, they don’t really hear or understand.
MAT 13:14 14 What Isaiah prophesied has become completely true for them: You will hear, to be sure, but never understand; and you will certainly see but never recognize what you are seeing .
MAT 13:15 15 For this people’s senses have become calloused, and they’ve become hard of hearing, and they’ve shut their eyes so that they won’t see with their eyes or hear with their ears or understand with their minds, and change their hearts and lives that I may heal them .
MAT 13:16 16 “Happy are your eyes because they see. Happy are your ears because they hear.
MAT 13:17 17 I assure you that many prophets and righteous people wanted to see what you see and hear what you hear, but they didn’t.
MAT 13:18 18 “ Consider then the parable of the farmer.
MAT 13:19 19 Whenever people hear the word about the kingdom and don’t understand it, the evil one comes and carries off what was planted in their hearts. This is the seed that was sown on the path.
MAT 13:20 20 As for the seed that was spread on rocky ground, this refers to people who hear the word and immediately receive it joyfully.
MAT 13:21 21 Because they have no roots, they last for only a little while. When they experience distress or abuse because of the word, they immediately fall away.
MAT 13:22 22 As for the seed that was spread among thorny plants, this refers to those who hear the word, but the worries of this life and the false appeal of wealth choke the word, and it bears no fruit.
MAT 13:23 23 As for what was planted on good soil, this refers to those who hear and understand, and bear fruit and produce—in one case a yield of one hundred to one, in another case a yield of sixty to one, and in another case a yield of thirty to one. ”
MAT 13:24 24 Jesus told them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like someone who planted good seed in his field.
MAT 13:25 25 While people were sleeping, an enemy came and planted weeds among the wheat and went away.
MAT 13:26 26 When the stalks sprouted and bore grain, then the weeds also appeared.
MAT 13:27 27 “The servants of the landowner came and said to him, ‘Master, didn’t you plant good seed in your field? Then how is it that it has weeds?’
MAT 13:28 28 “‘An enemy has done this,’ he answered. “The servants said to him, ‘Do you want us to go and gather them?’
MAT 13:29 29 “ But the landowner said, ‘No, because if you gather the weeds, you’ll pull up the wheat along with them.
MAT 13:30 30 Let both grow side by side until the harvest. And at harvesttime I’ll say to the harvesters, “ First gather the weeds and tie them together in bundles to be burned. But bring the wheat into my barn. ” ’ ”
MAT 13:31 31 He told another parable to them: “ The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that someone took and planted in his field.
MAT 13:32 32 It’s the smallest of all seeds. But when it’s grown, it’s the largest of all vegetable plants. It becomes a tree so that the birds in the sky come and nest in its branches. ”
MAT 13:33 33 He told them another parable: “ The kingdom of heaven is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in a bushel of wheat flour until the yeast had worked its way through all the dough. ”
MAT 13:34 34 Jesus said all these things to the crowds in parables, and he spoke to them only in parables.
MAT 13:35 35 This was to fulfill what the prophet spoke: I’ll speak in parables; I’ll declare what has been hidden since the beginning of the world.
MAT 13:36 36 Jesus left the crowds and went into the house. His disciples came to him and said, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”
MAT 13:37 37 Jesus replied, “ The one who plants the good seed is the Human One.
MAT 13:38 38 The field is the world. And the good seeds are the followers of the kingdom. But the weeds are the followers of the evil one.
MAT 13:39 39 The enemy who planted them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the present age. The harvesters are the angels.
MAT 13:40 40 Just as people gather weeds and burn them in the fire, so it will be at the end of the present age.
MAT 13:41 41 The Human One will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all things that cause people to fall away and all people who sin.
MAT 13:42 42 He will throw them into a burning furnace. People there will be weeping and grinding their teeth.
MAT 13:43 43 Then the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father’s kingdom. Those who have ears should hear. ”
MAT 13:44 44 “The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure that somebody hid in a field, which someone else found and covered up. Full of joy, the finder sold everything and bought that field.
MAT 13:45 45 “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls.
MAT 13:46 46 When he found one very precious pearl, he went and sold all that he owned and bought it.
MAT 13:47 47 “Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that people threw into the lake and gathered all kinds of fish.
MAT 13:48 48 When it was full, they pulled it to the shore, where they sat down and put the good fish together into containers. But the bad fish they threw away.
MAT 13:49 49 That’s the way it will be at the end of the present age. The angels will go out and separate the evil people from the righteous people,
MAT 13:50 50 and will throw the evil ones into a burning furnace. People there will be weeping and grinding their teeth.
MAT 13:51 51 “ Have you understood all these things? ” Jesus asked. They said to him, “Yes.”
MAT 13:52 52 Then he said to them, “ Therefore, every legal expert who has been trained as a disciple for the kingdom of heaven is like the head of a household who brings old and new things out of their treasure chest. ”
MAT 13:53 53 When Jesus finished these parables, he departed.
MAT 13:54 54 When he came to his hometown, he taught the people in their synagogue. They were surprised and said, “Where did he get this wisdom? Where did he get the power to work miracles?
MAT 13:55 55 Isn’t he the carpenter’s son? Isn’t his mother named Mary? Aren’t James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas his brothers?
MAT 13:56 56 And his sisters, aren’t they here with us? Where did this man get all this?”
MAT 13:57 57 They were repulsed by him and fell into sin. But Jesus said to them, “ Prophets are honored everywhere except in their own hometowns and in their own households. ”
MAT 13:58 58 He was unable to do many miracles there because of their disbelief.
MAT 14:1 1 At that time Herod the ruler heard the news about Jesus.
MAT 14:2 2 He said to his servants, “This is John the Baptist. He’s been raised from the dead. This is why these miraculous powers are at work through him.”
MAT 14:3 3 Herod had arrested John, bound him, and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Herod’s brother Philip.
MAT 14:4 4 That’s because John told Herod, “It’s against the law for you to marry her.”
MAT 14:5 5 Although Herod wanted to kill him, he feared the crowd because they thought John was a prophet.
MAT 14:6 6 But at Herod’s birthday party Herodias’ daughter danced in front of the guests and thrilled Herod.
MAT 14:7 7 Then he swore to give her anything she asked.
MAT 14:8 8 At her mother’s urging, the girl said, “Give me the head of John the Baptist here on a plate.”
MAT 14:9 9 Although the king was upset, because of his solemn pledge and his guests he commanded that they give it to her.
MAT 14:10 10 Then he had John beheaded in prison.
MAT 14:11 11 They brought his head on a plate and gave it to the young woman, and she brought it to her mother.
MAT 14:12 12 But John’s disciples came and took his body and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus what had happened.
MAT 14:13 13 When Jesus heard about John, he withdrew in a boat to a deserted place by himself. When the crowds learned this, they followed him on foot from the cities.
MAT 14:14 14 When Jesus arrived and saw a large crowd, he had compassion for them and healed those who were sick.
MAT 14:15 15 That evening his disciples came and said to him, “This is an isolated place and it’s getting late. Send the crowds away so they can go into the villages and buy food for themselves.”
MAT 14:16 16 But Jesus said to them, “ There’s no need to send them away. You give them something to eat. ”
MAT 14:17 17 They replied, “We have nothing here except five loaves of bread and two fish.”
MAT 14:18 18 He said, “ Bring them here to me. ”
MAT 14:19 19 He ordered the crowds to sit down on the grass. He took the five loaves of bread and the two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them and broke the loaves apart and gave them to his disciples. Then the disciples gave them to the crowds.
MAT 14:20 20 Everyone ate until they were full, and they filled twelve baskets with the leftovers.
MAT 14:21 21 About five thousand men plus women and children had eaten.
MAT 14:22 22 Right then, Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead to the other side of the lake while he dismissed the crowds.
MAT 14:23 23 When he sent them away, he went up onto a mountain by himself to pray. Evening came and he was alone.
MAT 14:24 24 Meanwhile, the boat, fighting a strong headwind, was being battered by the waves and was already far away from land.
MAT 14:25 25 Very early in the morning he came to his disciples, walking on the lake.
MAT 14:26 26 When the disciples saw him walking on the lake, they were terrified and said, “It’s a ghost!” They were so frightened they screamed.
MAT 14:27 27 Just then Jesus spoke to them, “ Be encouraged! It’s me. Don’t be afraid. ”
MAT 14:28 28 Peter replied, “Lord, if it’s you, order me to come to you on the water.”
MAT 14:29 29 And Jesus said, “ Come. ” Then Peter got out of the boat and was walking on the water toward Jesus.
MAT 14:30 30 But when Peter saw the strong wind, he became frightened. As he began to sink, he shouted, “Lord, rescue me!”
MAT 14:31 31 Jesus immediately reached out and grabbed him, saying, “ You man of weak faith! Why did you begin to have doubts? ”
MAT 14:32 32 When they got into the boat, the wind settled down.
MAT 14:33 33 Then those in the boat worshipped Jesus and said, “You must be God’s Son!”
MAT 14:34 34 When they had crossed the lake, they landed at Gennesaret.
MAT 14:35 35 When the people who lived in that place recognized him, they sent word throughout that whole region, and they brought to him everyone who was sick.
MAT 14:36 36 Then they begged him that they might just touch the edge of his clothes. Everyone who touched him was cured.
MAT 15:1 1 Then Pharisees and legal experts came to Jesus from Jerusalem and said,
MAT 15:2 2 “Why are your disciples breaking the elders’ rules handed down to us? They don’t ritually purify their hands by washing before they eat.”
MAT 15:3 3 Jesus replied, “ Why do you break the command of God by keeping the rules handed down to you?
MAT 15:4 4 For God said, Honor your father and your mother, and The person who speaks against father or mother will certainly be put to death .
MAT 15:5 5 But you say, ‘If you tell your father or mother, “ Everything I’m expected to contribute to you I’m giving to God as a gift, ” then you don’t have to honor your father.’
MAT 15:6 6 So you do away with God’s Law for the sake of the rules that have been handed down to you.
MAT 15:7 7 Hypocrites! Isaiah really knew what he was talking about when he prophesied about you,
MAT 15:8 8 This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far away from me.
MAT 15:9 9 Their worship of me is empty since they teach instructions that are human rules . ”
MAT 15:10 10 Jesus called the crowd near and said to them, “ Listen and understand.
MAT 15:11 11 It’s not what goes into the mouth that contaminates a person in God’s sight. It’s what comes out of the mouth that contaminates the person. ”
MAT 15:12 12 Then the disciples came and said to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended by what you just said?”
MAT 15:13 13 Jesus replied, “ Every plant that my heavenly Father didn’t plant will be pulled up.
MAT 15:14 14 Leave the Pharisees alone. They are blind people who are guides to blind people. But if a blind person leads another blind person, they will both fall into a ditch. ”
MAT 15:15 15 Then Peter spoke up, “Explain this riddle to us.”
MAT 15:16 16 Jesus said, “ Don’t you understand yet?
MAT 15:17 17 Don’t you know that everything that goes into the mouth enters the stomach and goes out into the sewer?
MAT 15:18 18 But what goes out of the mouth comes from the heart. And that’s what contaminates a person in God’s sight.
MAT 15:19 19 Out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adultery, sexual sins, thefts, false testimonies, and insults.
MAT 15:20 20 These contaminate a person in God’s sight. But eating without washing hands doesn’t contaminate in God’s sight. ”
MAT 15:21 21 From there, Jesus went to the regions of Tyre and Sidon.
MAT 15:22 22 A Canaanite woman from those territories came out and shouted, “Show me mercy, Son of David. My daughter is suffering terribly from demon possession.”
MAT 15:23 23 But he didn’t respond to her at all. His disciples came and urged him, “Send her away; she keeps shouting out after us.”
MAT 15:24 24 Jesus replied, “ I’ve been sent only to the lost sheep, the people of Israel. ”
MAT 15:25 25 But she knelt before him and said, “Lord, help me.”
MAT 15:26 26 He replied, “ It is not good to take the children’s bread and toss it to dogs. ”
MAT 15:27 27 She said, “Yes, Lord. But even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall off their masters’ table.”
MAT 15:28 28 Jesus answered, “ Woman, you have great faith. It will be just as you wish. ” And right then her daughter was healed.
MAT 15:29 29 Jesus moved on from there along the shore of the Galilee Sea. He went up a mountain and sat down.
MAT 15:30 30 Large crowds came to him, including those who were paralyzed, blind, injured, and unable to speak, and many others. They laid them at his feet, and he healed them.
MAT 15:31 31 So the crowd was amazed when they saw those who had been unable to speak talking, and the paralyzed cured, and the injured walking, and the blind seeing. And they praised the God of Israel.
