MAT 15:32 32 Now Jesus called his disciples and said, “ I feel sorry for the crowd because they have been with me for three days and have nothing to eat. I don’t want to send them away hungry for fear they won’t have enough strength to travel. ”
MAT 15:33 33 His disciples replied, “Where are we going to get enough food in this wilderness to satisfy such a big crowd?”
MAT 15:34 34 Jesus said, “ How much bread do you have? ” They responded, “Seven loaves and a few fish.”
MAT 15:35 35 He told the crowd to sit on the ground.
MAT 15:36 36 He took the seven loaves of bread and the fish. After he gave thanks, he broke them into pieces and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.
MAT 15:37 37 Everyone ate until they were full. The disciples collected seven baskets full of leftovers.
MAT 15:38 38 Four thousand men ate, plus women and children.
MAT 15:39 39 After dismissing the crowds, Jesus got into the boat and came to the region of Magadan.
MAT 16:1 1 The Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus. In order to test him they asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
MAT 16:2 2 But he replied, “ At evening you say, ‘It will be nice weather because the sky is bright red.’
MAT 16:3 3 And in the morning you say, ‘There will be bad weather today because the sky is cloudy.’ You know how to make sense of the sky’s appearance. But you are unable to recognize the signs that point to what the time is.
MAT 16:4 4 An evil and unfaithful generation searches for a sign. But it won’t receive any sign except Jonah’s sign. ” Then he left them and went away.
MAT 16:5 5 When the disciples arrived on the other side of the lake, they had forgotten to bring bread.
MAT 16:6 6 Jesus said to them, “ Watch out and be on your guard for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees. ”
MAT 16:7 7 They discussed this among themselves and said, “We didn’t bring any bread.”
MAT 16:8 8 Jesus knew what they were discussing and said, “ You people of weak faith! Why are you discussing among yourselves the fact that you don’t have any bread?
MAT 16:9 9 Don’t you understand yet? Don’t you remember the five loaves that fed the five thousand and how many baskets of leftovers you gathered?
MAT 16:10 10 And the seven loaves that fed the four thousand and how many large baskets of leftovers you gathered?
MAT 16:11 11 Don’t you know that I wasn’t talking about bread? But be on your guard for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees. ”
MAT 16:12 12 Then they understood that he wasn’t telling them to be on their guard for yeast used in making bread. No, he was telling them to watch out for the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
MAT 16:13 13 Now when Jesus came to the area of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, “ Who do people say the Human One is? ”
MAT 16:14 14 They replied, “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and still others Jeremiah or one of the other prophets.”
MAT 16:15 15 He said, “ And what about you? Who do you say that I am? ”
MAT 16:16 16 Simon Peter said, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
MAT 16:17 17 Then Jesus replied, “ Happy are you, Simon son of Jonah, because no human has shown this to you. Rather my Father who is in heaven has shown you.
MAT 16:18 18 I tell you that you are Peter. And I’ll build my church on this rock. The gates of the underworld won’t be able to stand against it.
MAT 16:19 19 I’ll give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Anything you fasten on earth will be fastened in heaven. Anything you loosen on earth will be loosened in heaven. ”
MAT 16:20 20 Then he ordered the disciples not to tell anybody that he was the Christ.
MAT 16:21 21 From that time Jesus began to show his disciples that he had to go to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders, chief priests, and legal experts, and that he had to be killed and raised on the third day.
MAT 16:22 22 Then Peter took hold of Jesus and, scolding him, began to correct him: “God forbid, Lord! This won’t happen to you.”
MAT 16:23 23 But he turned to Peter and said, “ Get behind me, Satan. You are a stone that could make me stumble, for you are not thinking God’s thoughts but human thoughts. ”
MAT 16:24 24 Then Jesus said to his disciples, “ All who want to come after me must say no to themselves, take up their cross, and follow me.
MAT 16:25 25 All who want to save their lives will lose them. But all who lose their lives because of me will find them.
MAT 16:26 26 Why would people gain the whole world but lose their lives? What will people give in exchange for their lives?
MAT 16:27 27 For the Human One is about to come with the majesty of his Father with his angels. And then he will repay each one for what that person has done.
MAT 16:28 28 I assure you that some standing here won’t die before they see the Human One coming in his kingdom. ”
MAT 17:1 1 Six days later Jesus took Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them to the top of a very high mountain.
MAT 17:2 2 He was transformed in front of them. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became as white as light.
MAT 17:3 3 Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with Jesus.
MAT 17:4 4 Peter reacted to all of this by saying to Jesus, “Lord, it’s good that we’re here. If you want, I’ll make three shrines: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
MAT 17:5 5 While he was still speaking, look, a bright cloud overshadowed them. A voice from the cloud said, “This is my Son whom I dearly love. I am very pleased with him. Listen to him!”
MAT 17:6 6 Hearing this, the disciples fell on their faces, filled with awe.
MAT 17:7 7 But Jesus came and touched them. “ Get up, ” he said. “ Don’t be afraid. ”
MAT 17:8 8 When they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.
MAT 17:9 9 As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus commanded them, “ Don’t tell anybody about the vision until the Human One is raised from the dead. ”
MAT 17:10 10 The disciples asked, “Then why do the legal experts say that Elijah must first come?”
MAT 17:11 11 Jesus responded, “ Elijah does come first and will restore all things.
MAT 17:12 12 In fact, I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they didn’t know him. But they did to him whatever they wanted. In the same way the Human One is also going to suffer at their hands. ”
MAT 17:13 13 Then the disciples realized he was telling them about John the Baptist.
MAT 17:14 14 When they came to the crowd, a man met Jesus. He knelt before him,
MAT 17:15 15 saying, “Lord, show mercy to my son. He is epileptic and suffers terribly, for he often falls into the fire or the water.
MAT 17:16 16 I brought him to your disciples, but they couldn’t heal him.”
MAT 17:17 17 Jesus answered, “ You faithless and crooked generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring the boy here to me. ”
MAT 17:18 18 Then Jesus spoke harshly to the demon. And it came out of the child, who was healed from that time on.
MAT 17:19 19 Then the disciples came to Jesus in private and said, “Why couldn’t we throw the demon out?”
MAT 17:20 20 “ Because you have little faith, ” he said. “ I assure you that if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you could say to this mountain, ‘Go from here to there,’ and it will go. There will be nothing that you can’t do. ”
MAT 17:21 22 When the disciples came together in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “ The Human One is about to be delivered over into human hands.
MAT 17:22 23 They will kill him. But he will be raised on the third day. ” And they were heartbroken.
MAT 17:23 24 When they came to Capernaum, the people who collected the half-shekel temple tax came to Peter and said, “Doesn’t your teacher pay the temple tax?”
MAT 17:24 25 “Yes,” he said. But when they came into the house, Jesus spoke to Peter first.“ What do you think, Simon? From whom do earthly kings collect taxes, from their children or from strangers? ”
MAT 17:25 26 “From strangers,” he said. Jesus said to him, “ Then the children don’t have to pay.
MAT 17:26 27 But just so we don’t offend them, go to the lake, throw out a fishing line and hook, and take the first fish you catch. When you open its mouth, you will find a shekel coin. Take it and pay the tax for both of us. ”
MAT 18:1 1 At that time the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
MAT 18:2 2 Then he called a little child over to sit among the disciples,
MAT 18:3 3 and said, “I assure you that if you don’t turn your lives around and become like this little child, you will definitely not enter the kingdom of heaven.
MAT 18:4 4 Those who humble themselves like this little child will be the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
MAT 18:5 5 Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me.
MAT 18:6 6 “As for whoever causes these little ones who believe in me to trip and fall into sin, it would be better for them to have a huge stone hung around their necks and be drowned in the bottom of the lake.
MAT 18:7 7 How terrible it is for the world because of the things that cause people to trip and fall into sin! Such things have to happen, but how terrible it is for the person who causes those things to happen!
MAT 18:8 8 If your hand or your foot causes you to fall into sin, chop it off and throw it away. It’s better to enter into life crippled or lame than to be thrown into the eternal fire with two hands or two feet.
MAT 18:9 9 If your eye causes you to fall into sin, tear it out and throw it away. It’s better to enter into life with one eye than to be cast into a burning hell with two eyes.
MAT 18:10 10 “Be careful that you don’t look down on one of these little ones. I say to you that their angels in heaven are always looking into the face of my Father who is in heaven.
MAT 18:11 12 What do you think? If someone had one hundred sheep and one of them wandered off, wouldn’t he leave the ninety-nine on the hillsides and go in search for the one that wandered off?
MAT 18:12 13 If he finds it, I assure you that he is happier about having that one sheep than about the ninety-nine who didn’t wander off.
MAT 18:13 14 In the same way, my Father who is in heaven doesn’t want to lose one of these little ones.
MAT 18:14 15 “ If your brother or sister sins against you, go and correct them when you are alone together. If they listen to you, then you’ve won over your brother or sister.
MAT 18:15 16 But if they won’t listen, take with you one or two others so that every word may be established by the mouth of two or three witnesses .
MAT 18:16 17 But if they still won’t pay attention, report it to the church. If they won’t pay attention even to the church, treat them as you would a Gentile and tax collector.
MAT 18:17 18 I assure you that whatever you fasten on earth will be fastened in heaven. And whatever you loosen on earth will be loosened in heaven.
MAT 18:18 19 Again I assure you that if two of you agree on earth about anything you ask, then my Father who is in heaven will do it for you.
MAT 18:19 20 For where two or three are gathered in my name, I’m there with them. ”
MAT 18:20 21 Then Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, how many times should I forgive my brother or sister who sins against me? Should I forgive as many as seven times?”
MAT 18:21 22 Jesus said, “Not just seven times, but rather as many as seventy-seven times.
MAT 18:22 23 Therefore, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.
MAT 18:23 24 When he began to settle accounts, they brought to him a servant who owed him ten thousand bags of gold.
MAT 18:24 25 Because the servant didn’t have enough to pay it back, the master ordered that he should be sold, along with his wife and children and everything he had, and that the proceeds should be used as payment.
MAT 18:25 26 But the servant fell down, kneeled before him, and said, ‘Please, be patient with me, and I’ll pay you back.’
MAT 18:26 27 The master had compassion on that servant, released him, and forgave the loan.
MAT 18:27 28 “When that servant went out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him one hundred coins. He grabbed him around the throat and said, ‘Pay me back what you owe me.’
MAT 18:28 29 “Then his fellow servant fell down and begged him, ‘Be patient with me, and I’ll pay you back.’
MAT 18:29 30 But he refused. Instead, he threw him into prison until he paid back his debt.
MAT 18:30 31 “When his fellow servants saw what happened, they were deeply offended. They came and told their master all that happened.
MAT 18:31 32 His master called the first servant and said, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you appealed to me.
MAT 18:32 33 Shouldn’t you also have mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had mercy on you?’
MAT 18:33 34 His master was furious and handed him over to the guard responsible for punishing prisoners, until he had paid the whole debt.
MAT 18:34 35 “ My heavenly Father will also do the same to you if you don’t forgive your brother or sister from your heart. ”
MAT 19:1 1 When Jesus finished saying these things, he left Galilee and came to the area of Judea on the east side of the Jordan.
MAT 19:2 2 Large crowds followed him, and he healed them.
MAT 19:3 3 Some Pharisees came to him. In order to test him, they said, “Does the Law allow a man to divorce his wife for just any reason?”
MAT 19:4 4 Jesus answered, “ Haven’t you read that at the beginning the creator made them male and female?
MAT 19:5 5 And God said, ‘Because of this a man should leave his father and mother and be joined together with his wife, and the two will be one flesh .’
MAT 19:6 6 So they are no longer two but one flesh. Therefore, humans must not pull apart what God has put together. ”
MAT 19:7 7 The Pharisees said to him, “Then why did Moses command us to give a divorce certificate and divorce her? ”
MAT 19:8 8 Jesus replied, “ Moses allowed you to divorce your wives because your hearts are unyielding. But it wasn’t that way from the beginning.
MAT 19:9 9 I say to you that whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual unfaithfulness, and marries another woman commits adultery. ”
MAT 19:10 10 His disciples said to him, “If that’s the way things are between a man and his wife, then it’s better not to marry.”
MAT 19:11 11 He replied, “ Not everybody can accept this teaching, but only those who have received the ability to accept it.
MAT 19:12 12 For there are eunuchs who have been eunuchs from birth. And there are eunuchs who have been made eunuchs by other people. And there are eunuchs who have made themselves eunuchs because of the kingdom of heaven. Those who can accept it should accept it. ”
MAT 19:13 13 Some people brought children to Jesus so that he would place his hands on them and pray. But the disciples scolded them.
MAT 19:14 14 “ Allow the children to come to me, ” Jesus said. “ Don’t forbid them, because the kingdom of heaven belongs to people like these children. ”
MAT 19:15 15 Then he blessed the children and went away from there.
MAT 19:16 16 A man approached him and said, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to have eternal life?”
MAT 19:17 17 Jesus said, “ Why do you ask me about what is good? There’s only one who is good. If you want to enter eternal life, keep the commandments. ”
MAT 19:18 18 The man said, “Which ones?” Then Jesus said, “ Don’t commit murder. Don’t commit adultery. Don’t steal. Don’t give false testimony .
MAT 19:19 19 Honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as you love yourself . ”
MAT 19:20 20 The young man replied, “I’ve kept all these. What am I still missing?”
MAT 19:21 21 Jesus said, “ If you want to be complete, go, sell what you own, and give the money to the poor. Then you will have treasure in heaven. And come follow me. ”
MAT 19:22 22 But when the young man heard this, he went away saddened, because he had many possessions.
MAT 19:23 23 Then Jesus said to his disciples, “ I assure you that it will be very hard for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.
MAT 19:24 24 In fact, it’s easier for a camel to squeeze through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter God’s kingdom. ”
MAT 19:25 25 When his disciples heard this, they were stunned. “Then who can be saved?” they asked.
MAT 19:26 26 Jesus looked at them carefully and said, “ It’s impossible for human beings. But all things are possible for God. ”
MAT 19:27 27 Then Peter replied, “Look, we’ve left everything and followed you. What will we have?”
MAT 19:28 28 Jesus said to them, “I assure you who have followed me that, when everything is made new, when the Human One sits on his magnificent throne, you also will sit on twelve thrones overseeing the twelve tribes of Israel.
MAT 19:29 29 And all who have left houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, children, or farms because of my name will receive one hundred times more and will inherit eternal life.
MAT 19:30 30 But many who are first will be last. And many who are last will be first.
MAT 20:1 1 “The kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
MAT 20:2 2 After he agreed with the workers to pay them a denarion, he sent them into his vineyard.
MAT 20:3 3 “Then he went out around nine in the morning and saw others standing around the marketplace doing nothing.
MAT 20:4 4 He said to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and I’ll pay you whatever is right.’
MAT 20:5 5 And they went. “Again around noon and then at three in the afternoon, he did the same thing.
MAT 20:6 6 Around five in the afternoon he went and found others standing around, and he said to them, ‘Why are you just standing around here doing nothing all day long?’
MAT 20:7 7 “‘Because nobody has hired us,’ they replied. “He responded, ‘You also go into the vineyard.’
MAT 20:8 8 “When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his manager, ‘Call the workers and give them their wages, beginning with the last ones hired and moving on finally to the first.’
MAT 20:9 9 When those who were hired at five in the afternoon came, each one received a denarion.
MAT 20:10 10 Now when those hired first came, they thought they would receive more. But each of them also received a denarion.
MAT 20:11 11 When they received it, they grumbled against the landowner,
MAT 20:12 12 ‘These who were hired last worked one hour, and they received the same pay as we did even though we had to work the whole day in the hot sun.’
MAT 20:13 13 “ But he replied to one of them, ‘Friend, I did you no wrong. Didn’t I agree to pay you a denarion?
MAT 20:14 14 Take what belongs to you and go. I want to give to this one who was hired last the same as I give to you.
MAT 20:15 15 Don’t I have the right to do what I want with what belongs to me? Or are you resentful because I’m generous?’
MAT 20:16 16 So those who are last will be first. And those who are first will be last. ”
MAT 20:17 17 As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the Twelve aside by themselves on the road. He told them,
MAT 20:18 18 “ Look, we are going up to Jerusalem. The Human One will be handed over to the chief priests and legal experts. They will condemn him to death.
MAT 20:19 19 They will hand him over to the Gentiles to be ridiculed, tortured, and crucified. But he will be raised on the third day. ”
MAT 20:20 20 Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus along with her sons. Bowing before him, she asked a favor of him.
MAT 20:21 21 “ What do you want? ” he asked. She responded, “Say that these two sons of mine will sit, one on your right hand and one on your left, in your kingdom.”
MAT 20:22 22 Jesus replied, “ You don’t know what you’re asking! Can you drink from the cup that I’m about to drink from? ” They said to him, “We can.”
MAT 20:23 23 He said to them, “ You will drink from my cup, but to sit at my right or left hand isn’t mine to give. It belongs to those for whom my Father prepared it. ”
MAT 20:24 24 Now when the other ten disciples heard about this, they became angry with the two brothers.
MAT 20:25 25 But Jesus called them over and said, “ You know that those who rule the Gentiles show off their authority over them and their high-ranking officials order them around.
MAT 20:26 26 But that’s not the way it will be with you. Whoever wants to be great among you will be your servant.
MAT 20:27 27 Whoever wants to be first among you will be your slave—
MAT 20:28 28 just as the Human One didn’t come to be served but rather to serve and to give his life to liberate many people. ”
MAT 20:29 29 As Jesus and his disciples were going out of Jericho a large crowd followed him.
MAT 20:30 30 When two blind men sitting along the road heard that Jesus was passing by, they shouted, “Show us mercy, Lord, Son of David!”
MAT 20:31 31 Now the crowd scolded them and told them to be quiet. But they shouted even louder, “Show us mercy, Lord, Son of David!”
MAT 20:32 32 Jesus stopped in his tracks and called to them. “ What do you want me to do for you? ” he asked.
MAT 20:33 33 “Lord, we want to see,” they replied.
MAT 20:34 34 Jesus had compassion on them and touched their eyes. Immediately they were able to see, and they followed him.
MAT 21:1 1 When they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus gave two disciples a task.
MAT 21:2 2 He said to them, “ Go into the village over there. As soon as you enter, you will find a donkey tied up and a colt with it. Untie them and bring them to me.
MAT 21:3 3 If anyone says anything to you, say that their master needs them. ” He sent them off right away.
MAT 21:4 4 Now this happened to fulfill what the prophet said,
MAT 21:5 5 Say to Daughter Zion, “ Look, your king is coming to you, humble and riding on a donkey, and on a colt the donkey’s offspring. ”
MAT 21:6 6 The disciples went and did just as Jesus had ordered them.
MAT 21:7 7 They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their clothes on them. Then he sat on them.
MAT 21:8 8 Now a large crowd spread their clothes on the road. Others cut palm branches off the trees and spread them on the road.
MAT 21:9 9 The crowds in front of him and behind him shouted, “ Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessings on the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
MAT 21:10 10 And when Jesus entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred up. “Who is this?” they asked.
MAT 21:11 11 The crowds answered, “It’s the prophet Jesus from Nazareth in Galilee.”
MAT 21:12 12 Then Jesus went into the temple and threw out all those who were selling and buying there. He pushed over the tables used for currency exchange and the chairs of those who sold doves.
MAT 21:13 13 He said to them, “ It’s written, My house will be called a house of prayer. But you’ve made it a hideout for crooks. ”
MAT 21:14 14 People who were blind and lame came to Jesus in the temple, and he healed them.
MAT 21:15 15 But when the chief priests and legal experts saw the amazing things he was doing and the children shouting in the temple, “ Hosanna to the Son of David!” they were angry.
MAT 21:16 16 They said to Jesus, “Do you hear what these children are saying?” “ Yes, ” he answered. “ Haven’t you ever read, From the mouths of babies and infants you’ve arranged praise for yourself? ”
MAT 21:17 17 Then he left them and went out of the city to Bethany and spent the night there.
MAT 21:18 18 Early in the morning as Jesus was returning to the city, he was hungry.
MAT 21:19 19 He saw a fig tree along the road, but when he came to it, he found nothing except leaves. Then he said to it, “ You’ll never again bear fruit! ” The fig tree dried up at once.
MAT 21:20 20 When the disciples saw it, they were amazed. “How did the fig tree dry up so fast?” they asked.
MAT 21:21 21 Jesus responded, “ I assure you that if you have faith and don’t doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree. You will even say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the lake.’ And it will happen.
MAT 21:22 22 If you have faith, you will receive whatever you pray for. ”
MAT 21:23 23 When Jesus entered the temple, the chief priests and elders of the people came to him as he was teaching. They asked, “What kind of authority do you have for doing these things? Who gave you this authority?”
MAT 21:24 24 Jesus replied, “ I have a question for you. If you tell me the answer, I’ll tell you what kind of authority I have to do these things.
MAT 21:25 25 Where did John get his authority to baptize? Did he get it from heaven or from humans? ” They argued among themselves, “If we say ‘from heaven,’ he’ll say to us, ‘Then why didn’t you believe him?’
MAT 21:26 26 But we can’t say ‘from humans’ because we’re afraid of the crowd, since everyone thinks John was a prophet.”
MAT 21:27 27 Then they replied, “We don’t know.” Jesus also said to them, “Neither will I tell you what kind of authority I have to do these things.
MAT 21:28 28 “What do you think? A man had two sons. Now he came to the first and said, ‘Son, go and work in the vineyard today.’
MAT 21:29 29 “‘No, I don’t want to,’ he replied. But later he changed his mind and went.
MAT 21:30 30 “The father said the same thing to the other son, who replied, ‘Yes, sir.’ But he didn’t go.
MAT 21:31 31 “ Which one of these two did his father’s will? ” They said, “The first one.” Jesus said to them, “I assure you that tax collectors and prostitutes are entering God’s kingdom ahead of you.
MAT 21:32 32 For John came to you on the righteous road, and you didn’t believe him. But tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. Yet even after you saw this, you didn’t change your hearts and lives and you didn’t believe him.
MAT 21:33 33 “Listen to another parable. There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. Then he rented it to tenant farmers and took a trip.
MAT 21:34 34 When it was time for harvest, he sent his servants to the tenant farmers to collect his fruit.
MAT 21:35 35 But the tenant farmers grabbed his servants. They beat some of them, and some of them they killed. Some of them they stoned to death.
MAT 21:36 36 “Again he sent other servants, more than the first group. They treated them in the same way.
MAT 21:37 37 Finally he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.
MAT 21:38 38 “But when the tenant farmers saw the son, they said to each other, ‘This is the heir. Come on, let’s kill him and we’ll have his inheritance.’
MAT 21:39 39 They grabbed him, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
MAT 21:40 40 “ When the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenant farmers? ”
MAT 21:41 41 They said, “He will totally destroy those wicked farmers and rent the vineyard to other tenant farmers who will give him the fruit when it’s ready.”
MAT 21:42 42 Jesus said to them, “ Haven’t you ever read in the scriptures, The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. The Lord has done this, and it’s amazing in our eyes?
MAT 21:43 43 Therefore, I tell you that God’s kingdom will be taken away from you and will be given to a people who produce its fruit.
MAT 21:44 44 Whoever falls on this stone will be crushed. And the stone will crush the person it falls on. ”
MAT 21:45 45 Now when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard the parable, they knew Jesus was talking about them.
MAT 21:46 46 They were trying to arrest him, but they feared the crowds, who thought he was a prophet.
MAT 22:1 1 Jesus responded by speaking again in parables:
MAT 22:2 2 “The kingdom of heaven is like a king who prepared a wedding party for his son.
MAT 22:3 3 He sent his servants to call those invited to the wedding party. But they didn’t want to come.
MAT 22:4 4 Again he sent other servants and said to them, ‘Tell those who have been invited, “ Look, the meal is all prepared. I’ve butchered the oxen and the fattened cattle. Now everything’s ready. Come to the wedding party! ” ’
MAT 22:5 5 But they paid no attention and went away—some to their fields, others to their businesses.
MAT 22:6 6 The rest of them grabbed his servants, abused them, and killed them.
MAT 22:7 7 “The king was angry. He sent his soldiers to destroy those murderers and set their city on fire.
MAT 22:8 8 Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding party is prepared, but those who were invited weren’t worthy.
MAT 22:9 9 Therefore, go to the roads on the edge of town and invite everyone you find to the wedding party.’
MAT 22:10 10 “Then those servants went to the roads and gathered everyone they found, both evil and good. The wedding party was full of guests.
MAT 22:11 11 Now when the king came in and saw the guests, he spotted a man who wasn’t wearing wedding clothes.
MAT 22:12 12 He said to him, ‘Friend, how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ But he was speechless.
MAT 22:13 13 Then the king said to his servants, ‘Tie his hands and feet and throw him out into the farthest darkness. People there will be weeping and grinding their teeth.’
MAT 22:14 14 “ Many people are invited, but few people are chosen. ”
MAT 22:15 15 Then the Pharisees met together to find a way to trap Jesus in his words.
MAT 22:16 16 They sent their disciples, along with the supporters of Herod, to him. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that you are genuine and that you teach God’s way as it really is. We know that you are not swayed by people’s opinions, because you don’t show favoritism.
MAT 22:17 17 So tell us what you think: Does the Law allow people to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
MAT 22:18 18 Knowing their evil motives, Jesus replied, “ Why do you test me, you hypocrites?
MAT 22:19 19 Show me the coin used to pay the tax. ” And they brought him a denarion.
MAT 22:20 20 “ Whose image and inscription is this? ” he asked.
MAT 22:21 21 “Caesar’s,” they replied. Then he said, “ Give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God what belongs to God. ”
MAT 22:22 22 When they heard this they were astonished, and they departed.
MAT 22:23 23 That same day Sadducees, who deny that there is a resurrection, came to Jesus.
MAT 22:24 24 They asked, “Teacher, Moses said, If a man who doesn’t have children dies, his brother must marry his wife and produce children for his brother.
MAT 22:25 25 Now there were seven brothers among us. The first one married, then died. Because he had no children he left his widow to his brother.
MAT 22:26 26 The same thing happened with the second brother and the third, and in fact with all seven brothers.
MAT 22:27 27 Finally, the woman died.
MAT 22:28 28 At the resurrection, which of the seven brothers will be her husband? They were all married to her.”
MAT 22:29 29 Jesus responded, “ You are wrong because you don’t know either the scriptures or God’s power.
MAT 22:30 30 At the resurrection people won’t marry nor will they be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like angels from God.
MAT 22:31 31 As for the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read what God told you,
MAT 22:32 32 I’m the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? He isn’t the God of the dead but of the living. ”
MAT 22:33 33 Now when the crowd heard this, they were astonished at his teaching.
MAT 22:34 34 When the Pharisees heard that Jesus had left the Sadducees speechless, they met together.
MAT 22:35 35 One of them, a legal expert, tested him.
MAT 22:36 36 “Teacher, what is the greatest commandment in the Law?”
MAT 22:37 37 He replied, “ You must love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your being, and with all your mind.
MAT 22:38 38 This is the first and greatest commandment.
MAT 22:39 39 And the second is like it: You must love your neighbor as you love yourself .
MAT 22:40 40 All the Law and the Prophets depend on these two commands. ”
MAT 22:41 41 Now as the Pharisees were gathering, Jesus asked them,
MAT 22:42 42 “ What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he? ” “David’s son,” they replied.
MAT 22:43 43 He said, “ Then how is it that David, inspired by the Holy Spirit, called him Lord when he said,
MAT 22:44 44 The Lord said to my lord, ‘Sit at my right side until I turn your enemies into your footstool’?
MAT 22:45 45 If David calls him Lord, how can he be David’s son? ”
MAT 22:46 46 Nobody was able to answer him. And from that day forward nobody dared to ask him anything.
MAT 23:1 1 Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and his disciples,
MAT 23:2 2 “The legal experts and the Pharisees sit on Moses’ seat.
MAT 23:3 3 Therefore, you must take care to do everything they say. But don’t do what they do.
MAT 23:4 4 For they tie together heavy packs that are impossible to carry. They put them on the shoulders of others, but are unwilling to lift a finger to move them.
MAT 23:5 5 Everything they do, they do to be noticed by others. They make extra-wide prayer bands for their arms and long tassels for their clothes.
MAT 23:6 6 They love to sit in places of honor at banquets and in the synagogues.
MAT 23:7 7 They love to be greeted with honor in the markets and to be addressed as ‘Rabbi.’
MAT 23:8 8 “But you shouldn’t be called Rabbi , because you have one teacher, and all of you are brothers and sisters.
MAT 23:9 9 Don’t call anybody on earth your father, because you have one Father, who is heavenly.
MAT 23:10 10 Don’t be called teacher , because Christ is your one teacher.
MAT 23:11 11 But the one who is greatest among you will be your servant.
MAT 23:12 12 All who lift themselves up will be brought low. But all who make themselves low will be lifted up.
MAT 23:13 13 “How terrible it will be for you legal experts and Pharisees! Hypocrites! You shut people out of the kingdom of heaven. You don’t enter yourselves, and you won’t allow those who want to enter to do so.
MAT 23:14 15 “How terrible it will be for you, legal experts and Pharisees! Hypocrites! You travel over sea and land to make one convert. But when they’ve been converted, they become twice the child of hell you are.
MAT 23:15 16 “How terrible it will be for you blind guides who say, ‘If people swear by the temple, it’s nothing. But if people swear by the gold in the temple, they are obligated to do what they swore.’
MAT 23:16 17 You foolish and blind people! Which is greater, the gold or the temple that makes the gold holy?
MAT 23:17 18 You say, ‘If people swear by the altar, it’s nothing. But if they swear by the gift on the altar, they are obligated to do what they swore.’
MAT 23:18 19 You blind people! Which is greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift holy?
MAT 23:19 20 Therefore, those who swear by the altar swear by it and by everything that’s on it.
MAT 23:20 21 Those who swear by the temple swear by it and by everything that’s part of it.
MAT 23:21 22 Those who swear by heaven swear by God’s throne and by the one who sits on it.
MAT 23:22 23 “How terrible it will be for you legal experts and Pharisees! Hypocrites! You give to God a tenth of mint, dill, and cumin, but you forget about the more important matters of the Law: justice, peace, and faith. You ought to give a tenth but without forgetting about those more important matters.
MAT 23:23 24 You blind guides! You filter out an ant but swallow a camel.
MAT 23:24 25 “How terrible it will be for you legal experts and Pharisees! Hypocrites! You clean the outside of the cup and plate, but inside they are full of violence and pleasure seeking.
MAT 23:25 26 Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup so that the outside of the cup will be clean too.
MAT 23:26 27 “How terrible it will be for you legal experts and Pharisees! Hypocrites! You are like whitewashed tombs. They look beautiful on the outside. But inside they are full of dead bones and all kinds of filth.
MAT 23:27 28 In the same way you look righteous to people. But inside you are full of pretense and rebellion.
MAT 23:28 29 “How terrible it will be for you legal experts and Pharisees! Hypocrites! You build tombs for the prophets and decorate the graves of the righteous.
MAT 23:29 30 You say, ‘If we had lived in our ancestors’ days, we wouldn’t have joined them in killing the prophets.’
MAT 23:30 31 You testify against yourselves that you are children of those who murdered the prophets.
MAT 23:31 32 Go ahead, complete what your ancestors did.
MAT 23:32 33 You snakes! You children of snakes! How will you be able to escape the judgment of hell?
MAT 23:33 34 Therefore, look, I’m sending you prophets, wise people, and legal experts. Some of them you will kill and crucify. And some you will beat in your synagogues and chase from city to city.
MAT 23:34 35 Therefore, upon you will come all the righteous blood that has been poured out on the earth, from the blood of that righteous man Abel to the blood of Zechariah the son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.
MAT 23:35 36 I assure you that all these things will come upon this generation.
MAT 23:36 37 “ Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You who kill the prophets and stone those who were sent to you. How often I wanted to gather your people together, just as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings. But you didn’t want that.
MAT 23:37 38 Look, your house is left to you deserted.
MAT 23:38 39 I tell you, you won’t see me until you say, Blessings on the one who comes in the Lord’s name . ”
MAT 24:1 1 Now Jesus left the temple and was going away. His disciples came to point out to him the temple buildings.
MAT 24:2 2 He responded, “ Do you see all these things? I assure that no stone will be left on another. Everything will be demolished. ”
MAT 24:3 3 Now while Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately and said, “Tell us, when will these things happen? What will be the sign of your coming and the end of the age?”
MAT 24:4 4 Jesus replied, “Watch out that no one deceives you.
MAT 24:5 5 Many will come in my name, saying, ‘I’m the Christ.’ They will deceive many people.
MAT 24:6 6 You will hear about wars and reports of wars. Don’t be alarmed. These things must happen, but this isn’t the end yet.
MAT 24:7 7 Nations and kingdoms will fight against each other, and there will be famines and earthquakes in all sorts of places.
MAT 24:8 8 But all these things are just the beginning of the sufferings associated with the end.
MAT 24:9 9 They will arrest you, abuse you, and they will kill you. All nations will hate you on account of my name.
MAT 24:10 10 At that time many will fall away. They will betray each other and hate each other.
MAT 24:11 11 Many false prophets will appear and deceive many people.
MAT 24:12 12 Because disobedience will expand, the love of many will grow cold.
MAT 24:13 13 But the one who endures to the end will be delivered.
MAT 24:14 14 This gospel of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the world as a testimony to all the nations. Then the end will come.
MAT 24:15 15 “When you see the disgusting and destructive thing that Daniel talked about standing in the holy place (the reader should understand this),
MAT 24:16 16 then those in Judea must escape to the mountains.
MAT 24:17 17 Those on the roof shouldn’t come down to grab things from their houses.
MAT 24:18 18 Those in the field shouldn’t come back to grab their clothes.
MAT 24:19 19 How terrible it will be at that time for women who are pregnant and for women who are nursing their children.
MAT 24:20 20 Pray that it doesn’t happen in winter or on the Sabbath day.
MAT 24:21 21 There will be great suffering such as the world has never before seen and will never again see.
MAT 24:22 22 If that time weren’t shortened, nobody would be rescued. But for the sake of the ones whom God chose, that time will be cut short.
MAT 24:23 23 “Then if somebody says to you, ‘Look, here’s the Christ,’ or ‘He’s over here,’ don’t believe it.
MAT 24:24 24 False christs and false prophets will appear, and they will offer great signs and wonders in order to deceive, if possible, even those whom God has chosen.
MAT 24:25 25 Look, I’ve told you ahead of time.
MAT 24:26 26 So if they say to you, ‘Look, he’s in the desert,’ don’t go out. And if they say, ‘Look, he’s in the rooms deep inside the house,’ don’t believe it.
MAT 24:27 27 Just as the lightning flashes from the east to the west, so it will be with the coming of the Human One.
MAT 24:28 28 The vultures gather wherever there’s a dead body.
MAT 24:29 29 “Now immediately after the suffering of that time the sun will become dark, and the moon won’t give its light. The stars will fall from the sky and the planets and other heavenly bodies will be shaken.
MAT 24:30 30 Then the sign of the Human One will appear in the sky. At that time all the tribes of the earth will be full of sadness, and they will see the Human One coming in the heavenly clouds with power and great splendor.
MAT 24:31 31 He will send his angels with the sound of a great trumpet, and they will gather his chosen ones from the four corners of the earth, from one end of the sky to the other.
MAT 24:32 32 “Learn this parable from the fig tree. After its branch becomes tender and it sprouts new leaves, you know that summer is near.
MAT 24:33 33 In the same way, when you see all these things, you know that the Human One is near, at the door.
MAT 24:34 34 I assure you that this generation won’t pass away until all these things happen.
MAT 24:35 35 Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
MAT 24:36 36 “But nobody knows when that day or hour will come, not the heavenly angels and not the Son. Only the Father knows.
MAT 24:37 37 As it was in the time of Noah, so it will be at the coming of the Human One.
MAT 24:38 38 In those days before the flood, people were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark.
MAT 24:39 39 They didn’t know what was happening until the flood came and swept them all away. The coming of the Human One will be like that.
MAT 24:40 40 At that time there will be two men in the field. One will be taken and the other left.
MAT 24:41 41 Two women will be grinding at the mill. One will be taken and the other left.
MAT 24:42 42 Therefore, stay alert! You don’t know what day the Lord is coming.
MAT 24:43 43 But you understand that if the head of the house knew at what time the thief would come, he would keep alert and wouldn’t allow the thief to break into his house.
MAT 24:44 44 Therefore, you also should be prepared, because the Human One will come at a time you don’t know.
MAT 24:45 45 “Who then are the faithful and wise servants whom their master puts in charge of giving food at the right time to those who live in his house?
MAT 24:46 46 Happy are those servants whom the master finds fulfilling their responsibilities when he comes.
MAT 24:47 47 I assure you that he will put them in charge of all his possessions.
MAT 24:48 48 But suppose those bad servants should say to themselves, My master won’t come until later.
MAT 24:49 49 And suppose they began to beat their fellow servants and to eat and drink with the drunks?
MAT 24:50 50 The master of those servants will come on a day when they are not expecting him, at a time they couldn’t predict.
MAT 24:51 51 He will cut them in pieces and put them in a place with the hypocrites. People there will be weeping and grinding their teeth.
MAT 25:1 1 “At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten young bridesmaids who took their lamps and went out to meet the groom.
MAT 25:2 2 Now five of them were wise, and the other five were foolish.
MAT 25:3 3 The foolish ones took their lamps but didn’t bring oil for them.
MAT 25:4 4 But the wise ones took their lamps and also brought containers of oil.
MAT 25:5 5 “When the groom was late in coming, they all became drowsy and went to sleep.
MAT 25:6 6 But at midnight there was a cry, ‘Look, the groom! Come out to meet him.’
MAT 25:7 7 “Then all those bridesmaids got up and prepared their lamps.
MAT 25:8 8 But the foolish bridesmaids said to the wise ones, ‘Give us some of your oil, because our lamps have gone out.’
MAT 25:9 9 “But the wise bridesmaids replied, ‘No, because if we share with you, there won’t be enough for our lamps and yours. We have a better idea. You go to those who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.’
MAT 25:10 10 But while they were gone to buy oil, the groom came. Those who were ready went with him into the wedding. Then the door was shut.
MAT 25:11 11 “Later the other bridesmaids came and said, ‘Lord, lord, open the door for us.’
MAT 25:12 12 “But he replied, ‘I tell you the truth, I don’t know you.’
MAT 25:13 13 “Therefore, keep alert, because you don’t know the day or the hour.
MAT 25:14 14 “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who was leaving on a trip. He called his servants and handed his possessions over to them.
MAT 25:15 15 To one he gave five valuable coins, and to another he gave two, and to another he gave one. He gave to each servant according to that servant’s ability. Then he left on his journey.
MAT 25:16 16 “After the man left, the servant who had five valuable coins took them and went to work doing business with them. He gained five more.
MAT 25:17 17 In the same way, the one who had two valuable coins gained two more.
MAT 25:18 18 But the servant who had received the one valuable coin dug a hole in the ground and buried his master’s money.
MAT 25:19 19 “Now after a long time the master of those servants returned and settled accounts with them.
MAT 25:20 20 The one who had received five valuable coins came forward with five additional coins. He said, ‘Master, you gave me five valuable coins. Look, I’ve gained five more.’
MAT 25:21 21 “His master replied, ‘Excellent! You are a good and faithful servant! You’ve been faithful over a little. I’ll put you in charge of much. Come, celebrate with me.’
MAT 25:22 22 “The second servant also came forward and said, ‘Master, you gave me two valuable coins. Look, I’ve gained two more.’
MAT 25:23 23 “His master replied, ‘Well done! You are a good and faithful servant. You’ve been faithful over a little. I’ll put you in charge of much. Come, celebrate with me.’
MAT 25:24 24 “Now the one who had received one valuable coin came and said, ‘Master, I knew that you are a hard man. You harvest grain where you haven’t sown. You gather crops where you haven’t spread seed.
MAT 25:25 25 So I was afraid. And I hid my valuable coin in the ground. Here, you have what’s yours.’
MAT 25:26 26 “His master replied, ‘You evil and lazy servant! You knew that I harvest grain where I haven’t sown and that I gather crops where I haven’t spread seed?
MAT 25:27 27 In that case, you should have turned my money over to the bankers so that when I returned, you could give me what belonged to me with interest.
MAT 25:28 28 Therefore, take from him the valuable coin and give it to the one who has ten coins.
MAT 25:29 29 Those who have much will receive more, and they will have more than they need. But as for those who don’t have much, even the little bit they have will be taken away from them.
MAT 25:30 30 Now take the worthless servant and throw him out into the farthest darkness.’ “People there will be weeping and grinding their teeth.
MAT 25:31 31 “Now when the Human One comes in his majesty and all his angels are with him, he will sit on his majestic throne.
MAT 25:32 32 All the nations will be gathered in front of him. He will separate them from each other, just as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
MAT 25:33 33 He will put the sheep on his right side. But the goats he will put on his left.
MAT 25:34 34 “Then the king will say to those on his right, ‘Come, you who will receive good things from my Father. Inherit the kingdom that was prepared for you before the world began.
MAT 25:35 35 I was hungry and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty and you gave me a drink. I was a stranger and you welcomed me.
MAT 25:36 36 I was naked and you gave me clothes to wear. I was sick and you took care of me. I was in prison and you visited me.’
MAT 25:37 37 “Then those who are righteous will reply to him, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?
MAT 25:38 38 When did we see you as a stranger and welcome you, or naked and give you clothes to wear?
MAT 25:39 39 When did we see you sick or in prison and visit you?’
MAT 25:40 40 “Then the king will reply to them, ‘I assure you that when you have done it for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you have done it for me.’
MAT 25:41 41 “Then he will say to those on his left, ‘Get away from me, you who will receive terrible things. Go into the unending fire that has been prepared for the devil and his angels.
MAT 25:42 42 I was hungry and you didn’t give me food to eat. I was thirsty and you didn’t give me anything to drink.
MAT 25:43 43 I was a stranger and you didn’t welcome me. I was naked and you didn’t give me clothes to wear. I was sick and in prison, and you didn’t visit me.’
MAT 25:44 44 “ Then they will reply, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and didn’t do anything to help you?’
MAT 25:45 45 Then he will answer, ‘I assure you that when you haven’t done it for one of the least of these, you haven’t done it for me.’
MAT 25:46 46 And they will go away into eternal punishment. But the righteous ones will go into eternal life. ”
MAT 26:1 1 When Jesus finished speaking all these words, he said to his disciples,
MAT 26:2 2 “ You know that the Passover is two days from now. And the Human One will be handed over to be crucified. ”
MAT 26:3 3 Then the chief priests and elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of Caiaphas the high priest.
MAT 26:4 4 They were plotting to arrest Jesus by cunning tricks and to kill him.
MAT 26:5 5 But they agreed that it shouldn’t happen during the feast so there wouldn’t be an uproar among the people.
MAT 26:6 6 When Jesus was at Bethany visiting the house of Simon, who had a skin disease,
MAT 26:7 7 a woman came to him with a vase made of alabaster containing very expensive perfume. She poured it on Jesus’ head while he was sitting at dinner.
MAT 26:8 8 Now when the disciples saw it they were angry and said, “Why this waste?
MAT 26:9 9 This perfume could have been sold for a lot of money and given to the poor.”
MAT 26:10 10 But Jesus knew what they were thinking. He said, “ Why do you make trouble for the woman? She’s done a good thing for me.
MAT 26:11 11 You always have the poor with you, but you won’t always have me.
MAT 26:12 12 By pouring this perfume over my body she’s prepared me to be buried.
MAT 26:13 13 I tell you the truth that wherever in the whole world this good news is announced, what she’s done will also be told in memory of her. ”
MAT 26:14 14 Then one of the Twelve, who was called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
MAT 26:15 15 and said, “What will you give me if I turn Jesus over to you?” They paid him thirty pieces of silver.
MAT 26:16 16 From that time on he was looking for an opportunity to turn him in.
MAT 26:17 17 On the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and said, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover meal?”
MAT 26:18 18 He replied, “ Go into the city, to a certain man, and say, ‘The teacher says, “ My time is near. I’m going to celebrate the Passover with my disciples at your house. ” ’ ”
MAT 26:19 19 The disciples did just as Jesus instructed them. They prepared the Passover.
MAT 26:20 20 That evening he took his place at the table with the twelve disciples.
MAT 26:21 21 As they were eating he said, “ I assure you that one of you will betray me. ”
MAT 26:22 22 Deeply saddened, each one said to him, “I’m not the one, am I, Lord?”
MAT 26:23 23 He replied, “ The one who will betray me is the one who dips his hand with me into this bowl.
MAT 26:24 24 The Human One goes to his death just as it is written about him. But how terrible it is for that person who betrays the Human One! It would have been better for him if he had never been born. ”
MAT 26:25 25 Now Judas, who would betray him, replied, “It’s not me, is it, Rabbi?” Jesus answered, “ You said it. ”
MAT 26:26 26 While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to the disciples and said, “ Take and eat. This is my body. ”
MAT 26:27 27 He took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, “ Drink from this, all of you.
MAT 26:28 28 This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many so that their sins may be forgiven.
MAT 26:29 29 I tell you, I won’t drink wine again until that day when I drink it in a new way with you in my Father’s kingdom. ”
MAT 26:30 30 Then, after singing songs of praise, they went to the Mount of Olives.
MAT 26:31 31 Then Jesus said to his disciples, “ Tonight you will all fall away because of me. This is because it is written, I will hit the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will go off in all directions .
MAT 26:32 32 But after I’m raised up, I’ll go before you to Galilee. ”
MAT 26:33 33 Peter replied, “If everyone else stumbles because of you, I’ll never stumble.”
MAT 26:34 34 Jesus said to him, “ I assure you that, before the rooster crows tonight, you will deny me three times. ”
MAT 26:35 35 Peter said, “Even if I must die alongside you, I won’t deny you.” All the disciples said the same thing.
MAT 26:36 36 Then Jesus went with his disciples to a place called Gethsemane. He said to the disciples, “ Stay here while I go and pray over there. ”
MAT 26:37 37 When he took Peter and Zebedee’s two sons, he began to feel sad and anxious.
MAT 26:38 38 Then he said to them, “ I’m very sad. It’s as if I’m dying. Stay here and keep alert with me. ”
MAT 26:39 39 Then he went a short distance farther and fell on his face and prayed, “ My Father, if it’s possible, take this cup of suffering away from me. However—not what I want but what you want. ”
MAT 26:40 40 He came back to the disciples and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “ Couldn’t you stay alert one hour with me?
MAT 26:41 41 Stay alert and pray so that you won’t give in to temptation. The spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak. ”
MAT 26:42 42 A second time he went away and prayed, “ My Father, if it’s not possible that this cup be taken away unless I drink it, then let it be what you want. ”
MAT 26:43 43 Again he came and found them sleeping. Their eyes were heavy with sleep.
MAT 26:44 44 But he left them and again went and prayed the same words for the third time.
MAT 26:45 45 Then he came to his disciples and said to them, “ Will you sleep and rest all night? Look, the time has come for the Human One to be betrayed into the hands of sinners.
MAT 26:46 46 Get up. Let’s go. Look, here comes my betrayer. ”
MAT 26:47 47 While Jesus was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, came. With him was a large crowd carrying swords and clubs. They had been sent by the chief priests and elders of the people.
MAT 26:48 48 His betrayer had given them a sign: “Arrest the man I kiss.”
MAT 26:49 49 Just then he came to Jesus and said, “Hello, Rabbi.” Then he kissed him.
MAT 26:50 50 But Jesus said to him, “ Friend, do what you came to do. ” Then they came and grabbed Jesus and arrested him.
MAT 26:51 51 One of those with Jesus reached for his sword. Striking the high priest’s slave, he cut off his ear.
MAT 26:52 52 Then Jesus said to him, “ Put the sword back into its place. All those who use the sword will die by the sword.
MAT 26:53 53 Or do you think that I’m not able to ask my Father and he will send to me more than twelve battle groups of angels right away?
MAT 26:54 54 But if I did that, how would the scriptures be fulfilled that say this must happen? ”
MAT 26:55 55 Then Jesus said to the crowds, “ Have you come with swords and clubs to arrest me, like a thief? Day after day, I sat in the temple teaching, but you didn’t arrest me.
MAT 26:56 56 But all this has happened so that what the prophets said in the scriptures might be fulfilled. ” Then all the disciples left Jesus and ran away.
MAT 26:57 57 Those who arrested Jesus led him to Caiaphas the high priest. The legal experts and the elders had gathered there.
MAT 26:58 58 Peter followed him from a distance until he came to the high priest’s courtyard. He entered that area and sat outside with the officers to see how it would turn out.
MAT 26:59 59 The chief priests and the whole council were looking for false testimony against Jesus so that they could put him to death.
MAT 26:60 60 They didn’t find anything they could use from the many false witnesses who were willing to come forward. But finally they found two
MAT 26:61 61 who said, “This man said, ‘I can destroy God’s temple and rebuild it in three days.’”
MAT 26:62 62 Then the high priest stood and said to Jesus, “Aren’t you going to respond to the testimony these people have brought against you?”
MAT 26:63 63 But Jesus was silent. The high priest said, “By the living God, I demand that you tell us whether you are the Christ, God’s Son.”
MAT 26:64 64 “ You said it, ” Jesus replied. “ But I say to you that from now on you’ll see the Human One sitting on the right side of the Almighty and coming on the heavenly clouds . ”
MAT 26:65 65 Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, “He’s insulting God! Why do we need any more witnesses? Look, you’ve heard his insult against God.
MAT 26:66 66 What do you think?” And they answered, “He deserves to die!”
MAT 26:67 67 Then they spit in his face and beat him. They hit him
MAT 26:68 68 and said, “Prophesy for us, Christ! Who hit you?”
MAT 26:69 69 Meanwhile, Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A servant woman came and said to him, “You were also with Jesus the Galilean.”
MAT 26:70 70 But he denied it in front of all of them, saying, “I don’t know what you are talking about.”
MAT 26:71 71 When he went over to the gate, another woman saw him and said to those who were there, “This man was with Jesus, the man from Nazareth.”
MAT 26:72 72 With a solemn pledge, he denied it again, saying, “I don’t know the man.”
MAT 26:73 73 A short time later those standing there came and said to Peter, “You must be one of them. The way you talk gives you away.”
MAT 26:74 74 Then he cursed and swore, “I don’t know the man!” At that very moment the rooster crowed.
MAT 26:75 75 Peter remembered Jesus’ words, “ Before the rooster crows you will deny me three times. ” And Peter went out and cried uncontrollably.
MAT 27:1 1 Early in the morning all the chief priests and the elders of the people reached the decision to have Jesus put to death.
MAT 27:2 2 They bound him, led him away, and turned him over to Pilate the governor.
MAT 27:3 3 When Judas, who betrayed Jesus, saw that Jesus was condemned to die, he felt deep regret. He returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, and
MAT 27:4 4 said, “I did wrong because I betrayed an innocent man.” But they said, “What is that to us? That’s your problem.”
MAT 27:5 5 Judas threw the silver pieces into the temple and left. Then he went and hanged himself.
MAT 27:6 6 The chief priests picked up the silver pieces and said, “According to the Law it’s not right to put this money in the treasury. Since it was used to pay for someone’s life, it’s unclean.”
MAT 27:7 7 So they decided to use it to buy the potter’s field where strangers could be buried.
MAT 27:8 8 That’s why that field is called “Field of Blood” to this very day.
MAT 27:9 9 This fulfilled the words of Jeremiah the prophet: And I took the thirty pieces of silver, the price for the one whose price had been set by some of the Israelites,
MAT 27:10 10 and I gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord commanded me .
MAT 27:11 11 Jesus was brought before the governor. The governor said, “Are you the king of the Jews?” Jesus replied, “ That’s what you say. ”
MAT 27:12 12 But he didn’t answer when the chief priests and elders accused him.
MAT 27:13 13 Then Pilate said, “Don’t you hear the testimony they bring against you?”
MAT 27:14 14 But he didn’t answer, not even a single word. So the governor was greatly amazed.
MAT 27:15 15 It was customary during the festival for the governor to release to the crowd one prisoner, whomever they might choose.
MAT 27:16 16 At that time there was a well-known prisoner named Jesus Barabbas.
MAT 27:17 17 When the crowd had come together, Pilate asked them, “Whom would you like me to release to you, Jesus Barabbas or Jesus who is called Christ?”
MAT 27:18 18 He knew that the leaders of the people had handed him over because of jealousy.
MAT 27:19 19 While he was serving as judge, his wife sent this message to him, “Leave that righteous man alone. I’ve suffered much today in a dream because of him.”
MAT 27:20 20 But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and kill Jesus.
MAT 27:21 21 The governor said, “Which of the two do you want me to release to you?” “Barabbas,” they replied.
MAT 27:22 22 Pilate said, “Then what should I do with Jesus who is called Christ?” They all said, “Crucify him!”
MAT 27:23 23 But he said, “Why? What wrong has he done?” They shouted even louder, “Crucify him!”
MAT 27:24 24 Pilate saw that he was getting nowhere and that a riot was starting. So he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd. “I’m innocent of this man’s blood,” he said. “It’s your problem.”
MAT 27:25 25 All the people replied, “Let his blood be on us and on our children.”
MAT 27:26 26 Then he released Barabbas to them. He had Jesus whipped, then handed him over to be crucified.
MAT 27:27 27 The governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the governor’s house, and they gathered the whole company of soldiers around him.
MAT 27:28 28 They stripped him and put a red military coat on him.
MAT 27:29 29 They twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on his head. They put a stick in his right hand. Then they bowed down in front of him and mocked him, saying, “Hey! King of the Jews!”
MAT 27:30 30 After they spit on him, they took the stick and struck his head again and again.
MAT 27:31 31 When they finished mocking him, they stripped him of the military coat and put his own clothes back on him. They led him away to crucify him.
MAT 27:32 32 As they were going out, they found Simon, a man from Cyrene. They forced him to carry his cross.
MAT 27:33 33 When they came to a place called Golgotha, which means Skull Place,
MAT 27:34 34 they gave Jesus wine mixed with vinegar to drink. But after tasting it, he didn’t want to drink it.
MAT 27:35 35 After they crucified him, they divided up his clothes among them by drawing lots.
MAT 27:36 36 They sat there, guarding him.
MAT 27:37 37 They placed above his head the charge against him. It read, “This is Jesus, the king of the Jews.”
MAT 27:38 38 They crucified with him two outlaws, one on his right side and one on his left.
MAT 27:39 39 Those who were walking by insulted Jesus, shaking their heads
MAT 27:40 40 and saying, “So you were going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, were you? Save yourself! If you are God’s Son, come down from the cross.”
MAT 27:41 41 In the same way, the chief priests, along with the legal experts and the elders, were making fun of him, saying,
MAT 27:42 42 “He saved others, but he can’t save himself. He’s the king of Israel, so let him come down from the cross now. Then we’ll believe in him.
MAT 27:43 43 He trusts in God, so let God deliver him now if he wants to. He said, ‘I’m God’s Son.’”
MAT 27:44 44 The outlaws who were crucified with him insulted him in the same way.
MAT 27:45 45 From noon until three in the afternoon the whole earth was dark.
MAT 27:46 46 At about three Jesus cried out with a loud shout, “ Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani ,” which means, “ My God, my God, why have you left me? ”
MAT 27:47 47 After hearing him, some standing there said, “He’s calling Elijah.”
MAT 27:48 48 One of them ran over, took a sponge full of vinegar, and put it on a pole. He offered it to Jesus to drink.
MAT 27:49 49 But the rest of them said, “Let’s see if Elijah will come and save him.”
MAT 27:50 50 Again Jesus cried out with a loud shout. Then he died.
MAT 27:51 51 Look, the curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, the rocks split,
MAT 27:52 52 and the bodies of many holy people who had died were raised.
MAT 27:53 53 After Jesus’ resurrection they came out of their graves and went into the holy city where they appeared to many people.
MAT 27:54 54 When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and what had just happened, they were filled with awe and said, “This was certainly God’s Son.”
MAT 27:55 55 Many women were watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee to serve him.
MAT 27:56 56 Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.
MAT 27:57 57 That evening a man named Joseph came. He was a rich man from Arimathea who had become a disciple of Jesus.
MAT 27:58 58 He came to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Pilate gave him permission to take it.
MAT 27:59 59 Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean linen cloth,
MAT 27:60 60 and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had carved out of the rock. After he rolled a large stone at the door of the tomb, he went away.
MAT 27:61 61 Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting in front of the tomb.
MAT 27:62 62 The next day, which was the day after Preparation Day, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate.
MAT 27:63 63 They said, “Sir, we remember that while that deceiver was still alive he said, ‘After three days I will arise.’
MAT 27:64 64 Therefore, order the grave to be sealed until the third day. Otherwise, his disciples may come and steal the body and tell the people, ‘He’s been raised from the dead.’ This last deception will be worse than the first.”
MAT 27:65 65 Pilate replied, “You have soldiers for guard duty. Go and make it as secure as you know how.”
MAT 27:66 66 Then they went and secured the tomb by sealing the stone and posting the guard.
MAT 28:1 1 After the Sabbath, at dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to look at the tomb.
MAT 28:2 2 Look, there was a great earthquake, for an angel from the Lord came down from heaven. Coming to the stone, he rolled it away and sat on it.
MAT 28:3 3 Now his face was like lightning and his clothes as white as snow.
MAT 28:4 4 The guards were so terrified of him that they shook with fear and became like dead men.
MAT 28:5 5 But the angel said to the women, “Don’t be afraid. I know that you are looking for Jesus who was crucified.
MAT 28:6 6 He isn’t here, because he’s been raised from the dead, just as he said. Come, see the place where they laid him.
MAT 28:7 7 Now hurry, go and tell his disciples, ‘He’s been raised from the dead. He’s going on ahead of you to Galilee. You will see him there.’ I’ve given the message to you.”
MAT 28:8 8 With great fear and excitement, they hurried away from the tomb and ran to tell his disciples.
MAT 28:9 9 But Jesus met them and greeted them. They came and grabbed his feet and worshipped him.
MAT 28:10 10 Then Jesus said to them, “ Don’t be afraid. Go and tell my brothers that I am going into Galilee. They will see me there. ”
MAT 28:11 11 Now as the women were on their way, some of the guards came into the city and told the chief priests everything that had happened.
MAT 28:12 12 They met with the elders and decided to give a large sum of money to the soldiers.
MAT 28:13 13 They told them, “Say that Jesus’ disciples came at night and stole his body while you were sleeping.
MAT 28:14 14 And if the governor hears about this, we will take care of it with him so you will have nothing to worry about.”
MAT 28:15 15 So the soldiers took the money and did as they were told. And this report has spread throughout all Judea to this very day.
MAT 28:16 16 Now the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus told them to go.
MAT 28:17 17 When they saw him, they worshipped him, but some doubted.
MAT 28:18 18 Jesus came near and spoke to them, “ I’ve received all authority in heaven and on earth.
MAT 28:19 19 Therefore, go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
MAT 28:20 20 teaching them to obey everything that I’ve commanded you. Look, I myself will be with you every day until the end of this present age. ”
MRK 1:1 1 The beginning of the good news about Jesus Christ, God’s Son,
MRK 1:2 2 happened just as it was written about in the prophecy of Isaiah: Look, I am sending my messenger before you . He will prepare your way,
MRK 1:3 3 a voice shouting in the wilderness: “ Prepare the way for the Lord; make his paths straight .”
MRK 1:4 4 John the Baptist was in the wilderness calling for people to be baptized to show that they were changing their hearts and lives and wanted God to forgive their sins.
MRK 1:5 5 Everyone in Judea and all the people of Jerusalem went out to the Jordan River and were being baptized by John as they confessed their sins.
MRK 1:6 6 John wore clothes made of camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
MRK 1:7 7 He announced, “One stronger than I am is coming after me. I’m not even worthy to bend over and loosen the strap of his sandals.
MRK 1:8 8 I baptize you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
MRK 1:9 9 About that time, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and John baptized him in the Jordan River.
MRK 1:10 10 While he was coming up out of the water, Jesus saw heaven splitting open and the Spirit, like a dove, coming down on him.
MRK 1:11 11 And there was a voice from heaven: “You are my Son, whom I dearly love; in you I find happiness.”
MRK 1:12 12 At once the Spirit forced Jesus out into the wilderness.
MRK 1:13 13 He was in the wilderness for forty days, tempted by Satan. He was among the wild animals, and the angels took care of him.
MRK 1:14 14 After John was arrested, Jesus came into Galilee announcing God’s good news,
MRK 1:15 15 saying, “ Now is the time! Here comes God’s kingdom! Change your hearts and lives, and trust this good news! ”
MRK 1:16 16 As Jesus passed alongside the Galilee Sea, he saw two brothers, Simon and Andrew, throwing fishing nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
MRK 1:17 17 “ Come, follow me, ” he said, “ and I’ll show you how to fish for people. ”
MRK 1:18 18 Right away, they left their nets and followed him.
MRK 1:19 19 After going a little farther, he saw James and John, Zebedee’s sons, in their boat repairing the fishing nets.
MRK 1:20 20 At that very moment he called them. They followed him, leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired workers.
MRK 1:21 21 Jesus and his followers went into Capernaum. Immediately on the Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and started teaching.
MRK 1:22 22 The people were amazed by his teaching, for he was teaching them with authority, not like the legal experts.
MRK 1:23 23 Suddenly, there in the synagogue, a person with an evil spirit screamed,
MRK 1:24 24 “What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are. You are the holy one from God.”
MRK 1:25 25 “ Silence! ” Jesus said, speaking harshly to the demon. “ Come out of him! ”
MRK 1:26 26 The unclean spirit shook him and screamed, then it came out.
MRK 1:27 27 Everyone was shaken and questioned among themselves, “What’s this? A new teaching with authority! He even commands unclean spirits and they obey him!”
MRK 1:28 28 Right away the news about him spread throughout the entire region of Galilee.
MRK 1:29 29 After leaving the synagogue, Jesus, James, and John went home with Simon and Andrew.
MRK 1:30 30 Simon’s mother-in-law was in bed, sick with a fever, and they told Jesus about her at once.
MRK 1:31 31 He went to her, took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she served them.
MRK 1:32 32 That evening, at sunset, people brought to Jesus those who were sick or demon-possessed.
MRK 1:33 33 The whole town gathered near the door.
MRK 1:34 34 He healed many who were sick with all kinds of diseases, and he threw out many demons. But he didn’t let the demons speak, because they recognized him.
MRK 1:35 35 Early in the morning, well before sunrise, Jesus rose and went to a deserted place where he could be alone in prayer.
MRK 1:36 36 Simon and those with him tracked him down.
MRK 1:37 37 When they found him, they told him, “Everyone’s looking for you!”
MRK 1:38 38 He replied, “ Let’s head in the other direction, to the nearby villages, so that I can preach there too. That’s why I’ve come. ”
MRK 1:39 39 He traveled throughout Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and throwing out demons.
MRK 1:40 40 A man with a skin disease approached Jesus, fell to his knees, and begged, “If you want, you can make me clean.”
MRK 1:41 41 Incensed, Jesus reached out his hand, touched him, and said, “ I do want to. Be clean. ”
MRK 1:42 42 Instantly, the skin disease left him, and he was clean.
MRK 1:43 43 Sternly, Jesus sent him away,
MRK 1:44 44 saying, “ Don’t say anything to anyone. Instead, go and show yourself to the priest and offer the sacrifice for your cleansing that Moses commanded. This will be a testimony to them. ”
MRK 1:45 45 Instead, he went out and started talking freely and spreading the news so that Jesus wasn’t able to enter a town openly. He remained outside in deserted places, but people came to him from everywhere.
MRK 2:1 1 After a few days, Jesus went back to Capernaum, and people heard that he was at home.
MRK 2:2 2 So many gathered that there was no longer space, not even near the door. Jesus was speaking the word to them.
MRK 2:3 3 Some people arrived, and four of them were bringing to him a man who was paralyzed.
MRK 2:4 4 They couldn’t carry him through the crowd, so they tore off part of the roof above where Jesus was. When they had made an opening, they lowered the mat on which the paralyzed man was lying.
MRK 2:5 5 When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “ Child, your sins are forgiven! ”
MRK 2:6 6 Some legal experts were sitting there, muttering among themselves,
MRK 2:7 7 “Why does he speak this way? He’s insulting God. Only the one God can forgive sins.”
MRK 2:8 8 Jesus immediately recognized what they were discussing, and he said to them, “ Why do you fill your minds with these questions?
MRK 2:9 9 Which is easier—to say to a paralyzed person, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, take up your bed, and walk’?
MRK 2:10 10 But so you will know that the Human One has authority on the earth to forgive sins ” —he said to the man who was paralyzed,
MRK 2:11 11 “ Get up, take your mat, and go home. ”
MRK 2:12 12 Jesus raised him up, and right away he picked up his mat and walked out in front of everybody. They were all amazed and praised God, saying, “We’ve never seen anything like this!”
MRK 2:13 13 Jesus went out beside the lake again. The whole crowd came to him, and he began to teach them.
MRK 2:14 14 As he continued along, he saw Levi, Alphaeus’ son, sitting at a kiosk for collecting taxes. Jesus said to him, “ Follow me. ” Levi got up and followed him.
MRK 2:15 15 Jesus sat down to eat at Levi’s house. Many tax collectors and sinners were eating with Jesus and his disciples. Indeed, many of them had become his followers.
MRK 2:16 16 When some of the legal experts from among the Pharisees saw that he was eating with sinners and tax collectors, they asked his disciples, “Why is he eating with sinners and tax collectors?”
MRK 2:17 17 When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “ Healthy people don’t need a doctor, but sick people do. I didn’t come to call righteous people, but sinners. ”
MRK 2:18 18 John’s disciples and the Pharisees had a habit of fasting. Some people asked Jesus, “Why do John’s disciples and the Pharisees’ disciples fast, but yours don’t?”
MRK 2:19 19 Jesus said, “The wedding guests can’t fast while the groom is with them, can they? As long as they have the groom with them, they can’t fast.
MRK 2:20 20 But the days will come when the groom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast.
MRK 2:21 21 “ No one sews a piece of new, unshrunk cloth on old clothes; otherwise, the patch tears away from it, the new from the old, and makes a worse tear.
MRK 2:22 22 No one pours new wine into old leather wineskins; otherwise, the wine would burst the wineskins and the wine would be lost and the wineskins destroyed. But new wine is for new wineskins. ”
MRK 2:23 23 Jesus went through the wheat fields on the Sabbath. As the disciples made their way, they were picking the heads of wheat.
MRK 2:24 24 The Pharisees said to Jesus, “Look! Why are they breaking the Sabbath law?”
MRK 2:25 25 He said to them, “ Haven’t you ever read what David did when he was in need, when he and those with him were hungry?
MRK 2:26 26 During the time when Abiathar was high priest, David went into God’s house and ate the bread of the presence, which only the priests were allowed to eat. He also gave bread to those who were with him. ”
MRK 2:27 27 Then he said, “ The Sabbath was created for humans; humans weren’t created for the Sabbath.
MRK 2:28 28 This is why the Human One is Lord even over the Sabbath. ”
MRK 3:1 1 Jesus returned to the synagogue. A man with a withered hand was there.
MRK 3:2 2 Wanting to bring charges against Jesus, they were watching Jesus closely to see if he would heal on the Sabbath.
MRK 3:3 3 He said to the man with the withered hand, “ Step up where people can see you. ”
MRK 3:4 4 Then he said to them, “ Is it legal on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save life or to kill? ” But they said nothing.
MRK 3:5 5 Looking around at them with anger, deeply grieved at their unyielding hearts, he said to the man, “ Stretch out your hand. ” So he did, and his hand was made healthy.
MRK 3:6 6 At that, the Pharisees got together with the supporters of Herod to plan how to destroy Jesus.
MRK 3:7 7 Jesus left with his disciples and went to the lake. A large crowd followed him because they had heard what he was doing. They were from Galilee,
MRK 3:8 8 Judea, Jerusalem, Idumea, beyond the Jordan, and the area surrounding Tyre and Sidon.
MRK 3:9 9 Jesus told his disciples to get a small boat ready for him so the crowd wouldn’t crush him.
MRK 3:10 10 He had healed so many people that everyone who was sick pushed forward so that they could touch him.
MRK 3:11 11 Whenever the evil spirits saw him, they fell down at his feet and shouted, “You are God’s Son!”
MRK 3:12 12 But he strictly ordered them not to reveal who he was.
MRK 3:13 13 Jesus went up on a mountain and called those he wanted, and they came to him.
MRK 3:14 14 He appointed twelve and called them apostles. He appointed them to be with him, to be sent out to preach,
MRK 3:15 15 and to have authority to throw out demons.
MRK 3:16 16 He appointed twelve: Peter, a name he gave Simon;
MRK 3:17 17 James and John, Zebedee’s sons, whom he nicknamed Boanerges, which means “sons of Thunder”;
MRK 3:18 18 and Andrew; Philip; Bartholomew; Matthew; Thomas; James, Alphaeus’ son; Thaddaeus; Simon the Cananaean;
MRK 3:19 19 and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus.
MRK 3:20 20 Jesus entered a house. A crowd gathered again so that it was impossible for him and his followers even to eat.
MRK 3:21 21 When his family heard what was happening, they came to take control of him. They were saying, “He’s out of his mind!”
MRK 3:22 22 The legal experts came down from Jerusalem. Over and over they charged, “He’s possessed by Beelzebul. He throws out demons with the authority of the ruler of demons.”
MRK 3:23 23 When Jesus called them together he spoke to them in a parable: “ How can Satan throw Satan out?
MRK 3:24 24 A kingdom involved in civil war will collapse.
MRK 3:25 25 And a house torn apart by divisions will collapse.
MRK 3:26 26 If Satan rebels against himself and is divided, then he can’t endure. He’s done for.
