MRK 3:27 27 No one gets into the house of a strong person and steals anything without first tying up the strong person. Only then can the house be burglarized.
MRK 3:28 28 I assure you that human beings will be forgiven for everything, for all sins and insults of every kind.
MRK 3:29 29 But whoever insults the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven. That person is guilty of a sin with consequences that last forever. ”
MRK 3:30 30 He said this because the legal experts were saying, “He’s possessed by an evil spirit.”
MRK 3:31 31 His mother and brothers arrived. They stood outside and sent word to him, calling for him.
MRK 3:32 32 A crowd was seated around him, and those sent to him said, “Look, your mother, brothers, and sisters are outside looking for you.”
MRK 3:33 33 He replied, “ Who is my mother? Who are my brothers? ”
MRK 3:34 34 Looking around at those seated around him in a circle, he said, “ Look, here are my mother and my brothers.
MRK 3:35 35 Whoever does God’s will is my brother, sister, and mother. ”
MRK 4:1 1 Jesus began to teach beside the lake again. Such a large crowd gathered that he climbed into a boat there on the lake. He sat in the boat while the whole crowd was nearby on the shore.
MRK 4:2 2 He said many things to them in parables. While teaching them, he said,
MRK 4:3 3 “ Listen to this! A farmer went out to scatter seed.
MRK 4:4 4 As he was scattering seed, some fell on the path; and the birds came and ate it.
MRK 4:5 5 Other seed fell on rocky ground where the soil was shallow. They sprouted immediately because the soil wasn’t deep.
MRK 4:6 6 When the sun came up, it scorched the plants; and they dried up because they had no roots.
MRK 4:7 7 Other seed fell among thorny plants. The thorny plants grew and choked the seeds, and they produced nothing.
MRK 4:8 8 Other seed fell into good soil and bore fruit. Upon growing and increasing, the seed produced in one case a yield of thirty to one, in another case a yield of sixty to one, and in another case a yield of one hundred to one. ”
MRK 4:9 9 He said, “ Whoever has ears to listen should pay attention! ”
MRK 4:10 10 When they were alone, the people around Jesus, along with the Twelve, asked him about the parables.
MRK 4:11 11 He said to them, “The secret of God’s kingdom has been given to you, but to those who are outside everything comes in parables.
MRK 4:12 12 This is so that they can look and see but have no insight, and they can hear but not understand. Otherwise, they might turn their lives around and be forgiven.
MRK 4:13 13 “ Don’t you understand this parable? Then how will you understand all the parables?
MRK 4:14 14 The farmer scatters the word.
MRK 4:15 15 This is the meaning of the seed that fell on the path: When the word is scattered and people hear it, right away Satan comes and steals the word that was planted in them.
MRK 4:16 16 Here’s the meaning of the seed that fell on rocky ground: When people hear the word, they immediately receive it joyfully.
MRK 4:17 17 Because they have no roots, they last for only a little while. When they experience distress or abuse because of the word, they immediately fall away.
MRK 4:18 18 Others are like the seed scattered among the thorny plants. These are the ones who have heard the word;
MRK 4:19 19 but the worries of this life, the false appeal of wealth, and the desire for more things break in and choke the word, and it bears no fruit.
MRK 4:20 20 The seed scattered on good soil are those who hear the word and embrace it. They bear fruit, in one case a yield of thirty to one, in another case sixty to one, and in another case one hundred to one. ”
MRK 4:21 21 Jesus said to them, “ Does anyone bring in a lamp in order to put it under a basket or a bed? Shouldn’t it be placed on a lampstand?
MRK 4:22 22 Everything hidden will be revealed, and everything secret will come out into the open.
MRK 4:23 23 Whoever has ears to listen should pay attention! ”
MRK 4:24 24 He said to them, “ Listen carefully! God will evaluate you with the same standard you use to evaluate others. Indeed, you will receive even more.
MRK 4:25 25 Those who have will receive more, but as for those who don’t have, even what they don’t have will be taken away from them. ”
MRK 4:26 26 Then Jesus said, “ This is what God’s kingdom is like. It’s as though someone scatters seed on the ground,
MRK 4:27 27 then sleeps and wakes night and day. The seed sprouts and grows, but the farmer doesn’t know how.
MRK 4:28 28 The earth produces crops all by itself, first the stalk, then the head, then the full head of grain.
MRK 4:29 29 Whenever the crop is ready, the farmer goes out to cut the grain because it’s harvesttime. ”
MRK 4:30 30 He continued, “ What’s a good image for God’s kingdom? What parable can I use to explain it?
MRK 4:31 31 Consider a mustard seed. When scattered on the ground, it’s the smallest of all the seeds on the earth;
MRK 4:32 32 but when it’s planted, it grows and becomes the largest of all vegetable plants. It produces such large branches that the birds in the sky are able to nest in its shade. ”
MRK 4:33 33 With many such parables he continued to give them the word, as much as they were able to hear.
MRK 4:34 34 He spoke to them only in parables, then explained everything to his disciples when he was alone with them.
MRK 4:35 35 Later that day, when evening came, Jesus said to them, “ Let’s cross over to the other side of the lake. ”
MRK 4:36 36 They left the crowd and took him in the boat just as he was. Other boats followed along.
MRK 4:37 37 Gale-force winds arose, and waves crashed against the boat so that the boat was swamped.
MRK 4:38 38 But Jesus was in the rear of the boat, sleeping on a pillow. They woke him up and said, “Teacher, don’t you care that we’re drowning?”
MRK 4:39 39 He got up and gave orders to the wind, and he said to the lake, “ Silence! Be still! ” The wind settled down and there was a great calm.
MRK 4:40 40 Jesus asked them, “ Why are you frightened? Don’t you have faith yet? ”
MRK 4:41 41 Overcome with awe, they said to each other, “Who then is this? Even the wind and the sea obey him!”
MRK 5:1 1 Jesus and his disciples came to the other side of the lake, to the region of the Gerasenes.
MRK 5:2 2 As soon as Jesus got out of the boat, a man possessed by an evil spirit came out of the tombs.
MRK 5:3 3 This man lived among the tombs, and no one was ever strong enough to restrain him, even with a chain.
MRK 5:4 4 He had been secured many times with leg irons and chains, but he broke the chains and smashed the leg irons. No one was tough enough to control him.
MRK 5:5 5 Night and day in the tombs and the hills, he would howl and cut himself with stones.
MRK 5:6 6 When he saw Jesus from far away, he ran and knelt before him,
MRK 5:7 7 shouting, “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? Swear to God that you won’t torture me!”
MRK 5:8 8 He said this because Jesus had already commanded him, “ Unclean spirit, come out of the man! ”
MRK 5:9 9 Jesus asked him, “ What is your name? ” He responded, “Legion is my name, because we are many.”
MRK 5:10 10 They pleaded with Jesus not to send them out of that region.
MRK 5:11 11 A large herd of pigs was feeding on the hillside.
MRK 5:12 12 “Send us into the pigs!” they begged. “Let us go into the pigs!”
MRK 5:13 13 Jesus gave them permission, so the unclean spirits left the man and went into the pigs. Then the herd of about two thousand pigs rushed down the cliff into the lake and drowned.
MRK 5:14 14 Those who tended the pigs ran away and told the story in the city and in the countryside. People came to see what had happened.
MRK 5:15 15 They came to Jesus and saw the man who used to be demon-possessed. They saw the very man who had been filled with many demons sitting there fully dressed and completely sane, and they were filled with awe.
MRK 5:16 16 Those who had actually seen what had happened to the demon-possessed man told the others about the pigs.
MRK 5:17 17 Then they pleaded with Jesus to leave their region.
MRK 5:18 18 While he was climbing into the boat, the one who had been demon-possessed pleaded with Jesus to let him come along as one of his disciples.
MRK 5:19 19 But Jesus wouldn’t allow it. “ Go home to your own people, ” Jesus said, “ and tell them what the Lord has done for you and how he has shown you mercy. ”
MRK 5:20 20 The man went away and began to proclaim in the Ten Cities all that Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.
MRK 5:21 21 Jesus crossed the lake again, and on the other side a large crowd gathered around him on the shore.
MRK 5:22 22 Jairus, one of the synagogue leaders, came forward. When he saw Jesus, he fell at his feet
MRK 5:23 23 and pleaded with him, “My daughter is about to die. Please, come and place your hands on her so that she can be healed and live.”
MRK 5:24 24 So Jesus went with him. A swarm of people were following Jesus, crowding in on him.
MRK 5:25 25 A woman was there who had been bleeding for twelve years.
MRK 5:26 26 She had suffered a lot under the care of many doctors, and had spent everything she had without getting any better. In fact, she had gotten worse.
MRK 5:27 27 Because she had heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his clothes.
MRK 5:28 28 She was thinking, If I can just touch his clothes, I’ll be healed.
MRK 5:29 29 Her bleeding stopped immediately, and she sensed in her body that her illness had been healed.
MRK 5:30 30 At that very moment, Jesus recognized that power had gone out from him. He turned around in the crowd and said, “ Who touched my clothes? ”
MRK 5:31 31 His disciples said to him, “Don’t you see the crowd pressing against you? Yet you ask, ‘Who touched me?’”
MRK 5:32 32 But Jesus looked around carefully to see who had done it.
MRK 5:33 33 The woman, full of fear and trembling, came forward. Knowing what had happened to her, she fell down in front of Jesus and told him the whole truth.
MRK 5:34 34 He responded, “ Daughter, your faith has healed you; go in peace, healed from your disease. ”
MRK 5:35 35 While Jesus was still speaking with her, messengers came from the synagogue leader’s house, saying to Jairus, “Your daughter has died. Why bother the teacher any longer?”
MRK 5:36 36 But Jesus overheard their report and said to the synagogue leader, “ Don’t be afraid; just keep trusting. ”
MRK 5:37 37 He didn’t allow anyone to follow him except Peter, James, and John, James’ brother.
MRK 5:38 38 They came to the synagogue leader’s house, and he saw a commotion, with people crying and wailing loudly.
MRK 5:39 39 He went in and said to them, “ What’s all this commotion and crying about? The child isn’t dead. She’s only sleeping. ”
MRK 5:40 40 They laughed at him, but he threw them all out. Then, taking the child’s parents and his disciples with him, he went to the room where the child was.
MRK 5:41 41 Taking her hand, he said to her, “ Talitha koum ,” which means, “Young woman, get up.”
MRK 5:42 42 Suddenly the young woman got up and began to walk around. She was 12 years old. They were shocked!
MRK 5:43 43 He gave them strict orders that no one should know what had happened. Then he told them to give her something to eat.
MRK 6:1 1 Jesus left that place and came to his hometown. His disciples followed him.
MRK 6:2 2 On the Sabbath, he began to teach in the synagogue. Many who heard him were surprised. “Where did this man get all this? What’s this wisdom he’s been given? What about the powerful acts accomplished through him?
MRK 6:3 3 Isn’t this the carpenter? Isn’t he Mary’s son and the brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? Aren’t his sisters here with us?” They were repulsed by him and fell into sin.
MRK 6:4 4 Jesus said to them, “ Prophets are honored everywhere except in their own hometowns, among their relatives, and in their own households. ”
MRK 6:5 5 He was unable to do any miracles there, except that he placed his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
MRK 6:6 6 He was appalled by their disbelief. Then Jesus traveled through the surrounding villages teaching.
MRK 6:7 7 He called for the Twelve and sent them out in pairs. He gave them authority over unclean spirits.
MRK 6:8 8 He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a walking stick—no bread, no bags, and no money in their belts.
MRK 6:9 9 He told them to wear sandals but not to put on two shirts.
MRK 6:10 10 He said, “ Whatever house you enter, remain there until you leave that place.
MRK 6:11 11 If a place doesn’t welcome you or listen to you, as you leave, shake the dust off your feet as a witness against them. ”
MRK 6:12 12 So they went out and proclaimed that people should change their hearts and lives.
MRK 6:13 13 They cast out many demons, and they anointed many sick people with olive oil and healed them.
MRK 6:14 14 Herod the king heard about these things, because the name of Jesus had become well-known. Some were saying, “John the Baptist has been raised from the dead, and this is why miraculous powers are at work through him.”
MRK 6:15 15 Others were saying, “He is Elijah.” Still others were saying, “He is a prophet like one of the ancient prophets.”
MRK 6:16 16 But when Herod heard these rumors, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has been raised to life.”
MRK 6:17 17 He said this because Herod himself had arranged to have John arrested and put in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Herod’s brother Philip. Herod had married her,
MRK 6:18 18 but John told Herod, “It’s against the law for you to marry your brother’s wife!”
MRK 6:19 19 So Herodias had it in for John. She wanted to kill him, but she couldn’t.
MRK 6:20 20 This was because Herod respected John. He regarded him as a righteous and holy person, so he protected him. John’s words greatly confused Herod, yet he enjoyed listening to him.
MRK 6:21 21 Finally, the time was right. It was on one of Herod’s birthdays, when he had prepared a feast for his high-ranking officials and military officers and Galilee’s leading residents.
MRK 6:22 22 Herod’s daughter Herodias came in and danced, thrilling Herod and his dinner guests. The king said to the young woman, “Ask me whatever you wish, and I will give it to you.”
MRK 6:23 23 Then he swore to her, “Whatever you ask I will give to you, even as much as half of my kingdom.”
MRK 6:24 24 She left the banquet hall and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” “John the Baptist’s head,” Herodias replied.
MRK 6:25 25 Hurrying back to the ruler, she made her request: “I want you to give me John the Baptist’s head on a plate, right this minute.”
MRK 6:26 26 Although the king was upset, because of his solemn pledge and his guests, he didn’t want to refuse her.
MRK 6:27 27 So he ordered a guard to bring John’s head. The guard went to the prison, cut off John’s head,
MRK 6:28 28 brought his head on a plate, and gave it to the young woman, and she gave it to her mother.
MRK 6:29 29 When John’s disciples heard what had happened, they came and took his dead body and laid it in a tomb.
MRK 6:30 30 The apostles returned to Jesus and told him everything they had done and taught.
MRK 6:31 31 Many people were coming and going, so there was no time to eat. He said to the apostles, “Come by yourselves to a secluded place and rest for a while.”
MRK 6:32 32 They departed in a boat by themselves for a deserted place.
MRK 6:33 33 Many people saw them leaving and recognized them, so they ran ahead from all the cities and arrived before them.
MRK 6:34 34 When Jesus arrived and saw a large crowd, he had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd. Then he began to teach them many things.
MRK 6:35 35 Late in the day, his disciples came to him and said, “This is an isolated place, and it’s already late in the day.
MRK 6:36 36 Send them away so that they can go to the surrounding countryside and villages and buy something to eat for themselves.”
MRK 6:37 37 He replied, “ You give them something to eat. ” But they said to him, “Should we go off and buy bread worth almost eight months’ pay and give it to them to eat?”
MRK 6:38 38 He said to them, “ How much bread do you have? Take a look. ” After checking, they said, “Five loaves of bread and two fish.”
MRK 6:39 39 He directed the disciples to seat all the people in groups as though they were having a banquet on the green grass.
MRK 6:40 40 They sat down in groups of hundreds and fifties.
MRK 6:41 41 He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke the loaves into pieces, and gave them to his disciples to set before the people. He also divided the two fish among them all.
MRK 6:42 42 Everyone ate until they were full.
MRK 6:43 43 They filled twelve baskets with the leftover pieces of bread and fish.
MRK 6:44 44 About five thousand had eaten.
MRK 6:45 45 Right then, Jesus made his disciples get into a boat and go ahead to the other side of the lake, toward Bethsaida, while he dismissed the crowd.
MRK 6:46 46 After saying good-bye to them, Jesus went up onto a mountain to pray.
MRK 6:47 47 Evening came and the boat was in the middle of the lake, but he was alone on the land.
MRK 6:48 48 He saw his disciples struggling. They were trying to row forward, but the wind was blowing against them. Very early in the morning, he came to them, walking on the lake. He intended to pass by them.
MRK 6:49 49 When they saw him walking on the lake, they thought he was a ghost and they screamed.
MRK 6:50 50 Seeing him was terrifying to all of them. Just then he spoke to them, “ Be encouraged! It’s me. Don’t be afraid. ”
MRK 6:51 51 He got into the boat, and the wind settled down. His disciples were so baffled they were beside themselves.
MRK 6:52 52 That’s because they hadn’t understood about the loaves. Their minds had been closed so that they resisted God’s ways.
MRK 6:53 53 When Jesus and his disciples had crossed the lake, they landed at Gennesaret, anchored the boat,
MRK 6:54 54 and came ashore. People immediately recognized Jesus
MRK 6:55 55 and ran around that whole region bringing sick people on their mats to wherever they heard he was.
MRK 6:56 56 Wherever he went—villages, cities, or farming communities—they would place the sick in the marketplaces and beg him to allow them to touch even the hem of his clothing. Everyone who touched him was healed.
MRK 7:1 1 The Pharisees and some legal experts from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus.
MRK 7:2 2 They saw some of his disciples eating food with unclean hands. (They were eating without first ritually purifying their hands through washing.
MRK 7:3 3 The Pharisees and all the Jews don’t eat without first washing their hands carefully. This is a way of observing the rules handed down by the elders.
MRK 7:4 4 Upon returning from the marketplace, they don’t eat without first immersing themselves. They observe many other rules that have been handed down, such as the washing of cups, jugs, pans, and sleeping mats.)
MRK 7:5 5 So the Pharisees and legal experts asked Jesus, “Why are your disciples not living according to the rules handed down by the elders but instead eat food with ritually unclean hands?”
MRK 7:6 6 He replied, “ Isaiah really knew what he was talking about when he prophesied about you hypocrites. He wrote, This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far away from me.
MRK 7:7 7 Their worship of me is empty since they teach instructions that are human words.
MRK 7:8 8 You ignore God’s commandment while holding on to rules created by humans and handed down to you. ”
MRK 7:9 9 Jesus continued, “ Clearly, you are experts at rejecting God’s commandment in order to establish these rules.
MRK 7:10 10 Moses said, Honor your father and your mother, and The person who speaks against father or mother will certainly be put to death .
MRK 7:11 11 But you say, ‘If you tell your father or mother, “ Everything I’m expected to contribute to you is corban (that is, a gift I’m giving to God), ”
MRK 7:12 12 then you are no longer required to care for your father or mother.’
MRK 7:13 13 In this way you do away with God’s word in favor of the rules handed down to you, which you pass on to others. And you do a lot of other things just like that. ”
MRK 7:14 14 Then Jesus called the crowd again and said, “ Listen to me, all of you, and understand.
MRK 7:15 15 Nothing outside of a person can enter and contaminate a person in God’s sight; rather, the things that come out of a person contaminate the person. ”
MRK 7:16 17 After leaving the crowd, he entered a house where his disciples asked him about that riddle.
MRK 7:17 18 He said to them, “ Don’t you understand either? Don’t you know that nothing from the outside that enters a person has the power to contaminate?
MRK 7:18 19 That’s because it doesn’t enter into the heart but into the stomach, and it goes out into the sewer. ” By saying this, Jesus declared that no food could contaminate a person in God’s sight.
MRK 7:19 20 “ It’s what comes out of a person that contaminates someone in God’s sight, ” he said.
MRK 7:20 21 “ It’s from the inside, from the human heart, that evil thoughts come: sexual sins, thefts, murders,
MRK 7:21 22 adultery, greed, evil actions, deceit, unrestrained immorality, envy, insults, arrogance, and foolishness.
MRK 7:22 23 All these evil things come from the inside and contaminate a person in God’s sight. ”
MRK 7:23 24 Jesus left that place and went into the region of Tyre. He didn’t want anyone to know that he had entered a house, but he couldn’t hide.
MRK 7:24 25 In fact, a woman whose young daughter was possessed by an unclean spirit heard about him right away. She came and fell at his feet.
MRK 7:25 26 The woman was Greek, Syrophoenician by birth. She begged Jesus to throw the demon out of her daughter.
MRK 7:26 27 He responded, “ The children have to be fed first. It isn’t right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs. ”
MRK 7:27 28 But she answered, “Lord, even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
MRK 7:28 29 “ Good answer! ” he said. “ Go on home. The demon has already left your daughter. ”
MRK 7:29 30 When she returned to her house, she found the child lying on the bed and the demon gone.
MRK 7:30 31 After leaving the region of Tyre, Jesus went through Sidon toward the Galilee Sea through the region of the Ten Cities.
MRK 7:31 32 Some people brought to him a man who was deaf and could hardly speak, and they begged him to place his hand on the man for healing.
MRK 7:32 33 Jesus took him away from the crowd by himself and put his fingers in the man’s ears. Then he spit and touched the man’s tongue.
MRK 7:33 34 Looking into heaven, Jesus sighed deeply and said, “ Ephphatha, ” which means, “Open up.”
MRK 7:34 35 At once, his ears opened, his twisted tongue was released, and he began to speak clearly.
MRK 7:35 36 Jesus gave the people strict orders not to tell anyone. But the more he tried to silence them, the more eagerly they shared the news.
MRK 7:36 37 People were overcome with wonder, saying, “He does everything well! He even makes the deaf to hear and gives speech to those who can’t speak.”
MRK 8:1 1 In those days there was another large crowd with nothing to eat. Jesus called his disciples and told them,
MRK 8:2 2 “ I feel sorry for the crowd because they have been with me for three days and have nothing to eat.
MRK 8:3 3 If I send them away hungry to their homes, they won’t have enough strength to travel, for some have come a long distance. ”
MRK 8:4 4 His disciples responded, “How can anyone get enough food in this wilderness to satisfy these people?”
MRK 8:5 5 Jesus asked, “ How much bread do you have? ” They said, “Seven loaves.”
MRK 8:6 6 He told the crowd to sit on the ground. He took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them apart, and gave them to his disciples to distribute; and they gave the bread to the crowd.
MRK 8:7 7 They also had a few fish. He said a blessing over them, then gave them to the disciples to hand out also.
MRK 8:8 8 They ate until they were full. They collected seven baskets full of leftovers.
MRK 8:9 9 This was a crowd of about four thousand people! Jesus sent them away,

MRK 8:11 11 The Pharisees showed up and began to argue with Jesus. To test him, they asked for a sign from heaven.
MRK 8:12 12 With an impatient sigh, Jesus said, “ Why does this generation look for a sign? I assure you that no sign will be given to it. ”
MRK 8:13 13 Leaving them, he got back in the boat and crossed to the other side of the lake.
MRK 8:14 14 Jesus’ disciples had forgotten to bring any bread, so they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
MRK 8:15 15 He gave them strict orders: “ Watch out and be on your guard for the yeast of the Pharisees as well as the yeast of Herod. ”
MRK 8:16 16 The disciples discussed this among themselves, “He said this because we have no bread.”
MRK 8:17 17 Jesus knew what they were discussing and said, “ Why are you talking about the fact that you don’t have any bread? Don’t you grasp what has happened? Don’t you understand? Are your hearts so resistant to what God is doing?
MRK 8:18 18 Don’t you have eyes? Why can’t you see? Don’t you have ears? Why can’t you hear? Don’t you remember?
MRK 8:19 19 When I broke five loaves of bread for those five thousand people, how many baskets full of leftovers did you gather? ” They answered, “Twelve.”
MRK 8:20 20 “ And when I broke seven loaves of bread for those four thousand people, how many baskets full of leftovers did you gather? ” They answered, “Seven.”
MRK 8:21 21 Jesus said to them, “ And you still don’t understand? ”
MRK 8:22 22 Jesus and his disciples came to Bethsaida. Some people brought a blind man to Jesus and begged him to touch and heal him.
MRK 8:23 23 Taking the blind man’s hand, Jesus led him out of the village. After spitting on his eyes and laying his hands on the man, he asked him, “ Do you see anything? ”
MRK 8:24 24 The man looked up and said, “I see people. They look like trees, only they are walking around.”
MRK 8:25 25 Then Jesus placed his hands on the man’s eyes again. He looked with his eyes wide open, his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly.
MRK 8:26 26 Then Jesus sent him home, saying, “ Don’t go into the village! ”
MRK 8:27 27 Jesus and his disciples went into the villages near Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “ Who do people say that I am? ”
MRK 8:28 28 They told him, “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, and still others one of the prophets.”
MRK 8:29 29 He asked them, “ And what about you? Who do you say that I am? ” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”
MRK 8:30 30 Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone about him.
MRK 8:31 31 Then Jesus began to teach his disciples: “ The Human One must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and the legal experts, and be killed, and then, after three days, rise from the dead. ”
MRK 8:32 32 He said this plainly. But Peter took hold of Jesus and, scolding him, began to correct him.
MRK 8:33 33 Jesus turned and looked at his disciples, then sternly corrected Peter: “ Get behind me, Satan. You are not thinking God’s thoughts but human thoughts. ”
MRK 8:34 34 After calling the crowd together with his disciples, Jesus said to them, “ All who want to come after me must say no to themselves, take up their cross, and follow me.
MRK 8:35 35 All who want to save their lives will lose them. But all who lose their lives because of me and because of the good news will save them.
MRK 8:36 36 Why would people gain the whole world but lose their lives?
MRK 8:37 37 What will people give in exchange for their lives?
MRK 8:38 38 Whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this unfaithful and sinful generation, the Human One will be ashamed of that person when he comes in the Father’s glory with the holy angels. ”
MRK 9:1 1 Jesus continued, “ I assure you that some standing here won’t die before they see God’s kingdom arrive in power. ”
MRK 9:2 2 Six days later Jesus took Peter, James, and John, and brought them to the top of a very high mountain where they were alone. He was transformed in front of them,
MRK 9:3 3 and his clothes were amazingly bright, brighter than if they had been bleached white.
MRK 9:4 4 Elijah and Moses appeared and were talking with Jesus.
MRK 9:5 5 Peter reacted to all of this by saying to Jesus, “Rabbi, it’s good that we’re here. Let’s make three shrines—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
MRK 9:6 6 He said this because he didn’t know how to respond, for the three of them were terrified.
MRK 9:7 7 Then a cloud overshadowed them, and a voice spoke from the cloud, “This is my Son, whom I dearly love. Listen to him!”
MRK 9:8 8 Suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus.
MRK 9:9 9 As they were coming down the mountain, he ordered them not to tell anyone what they had seen until after the Human One had risen from the dead.
MRK 9:10 10 So they kept it to themselves, wondering, “What’s this ‘rising from the dead’?”
MRK 9:11 11 They asked Jesus, “Why do the legal experts say that Elijah must come first?”
MRK 9:12 12 He answered, “ Elijah does come first to restore all things. Why was it written that the Human One would suffer many things and be rejected?
MRK 9:13 13 In fact, I tell you that Elijah has come, but they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it was written about him. ”
MRK 9:14 14 When Jesus, Peter, James, and John approached the other disciples, they saw a large crowd surrounding them and legal experts arguing with them.
MRK 9:15 15 Suddenly the whole crowd caught sight of Jesus. They ran to greet him, overcome with excitement.
MRK 9:16 16 Jesus asked them, “ What are you arguing about? ”
MRK 9:17 17 Someone from the crowd responded, “Teacher, I brought my son to you, since he has a spirit that doesn’t allow him to speak.
MRK 9:18 18 Wherever it overpowers him, it throws him into a fit. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and stiffens up. So I spoke to your disciples to see if they could throw it out, but they couldn’t.”
MRK 9:19 19 Jesus answered them, “ You faithless generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him to me. ”
MRK 9:20 20 They brought him. When the spirit saw Jesus, it immediately threw the boy into a fit. He fell on the ground and rolled around, foaming at the mouth.
MRK 9:21 21 Jesus asked his father, “ How long has this been going on? ” He said, “Since he was a child.
MRK 9:22 22 It has often thrown him into a fire or into water trying to kill him. If you can do anything, help us! Show us compassion!”
MRK 9:23 23 Jesus said to him, “ ‘If you can do anything’? All things are possible for the one who has faith. ”
MRK 9:24 24 At that the boy’s father cried out, “I have faith; help my lack of faith!”
MRK 9:25 25 Noticing that the crowd had surged together, Jesus spoke harshly to the unclean spirit, “ Mute and deaf spirit, I command you to come out of him and never enter him again. ”
MRK 9:26 26 After screaming and shaking the boy horribly, the spirit came out. The boy seemed to be dead; in fact, several people said that he had died.
MRK 9:27 27 But Jesus took his hand, lifted him up, and he arose.
MRK 9:28 28 After Jesus went into a house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why couldn’t we throw this spirit out?”
MRK 9:29 29 Jesus answered, “ Throwing this kind of spirit out requires prayer. ”
MRK 9:30 30 From there Jesus and his followers went through Galilee, but he didn’t want anyone to know it.

MRK 9:40 40 Whoever isn’t against us is for us.

MRK 9:43 43 If your hand causes you to fall into sin, chop it off. It’s better for you to enter into life crippled than to go away with two hands into the fire of hell, which can’t be put out.
MRK 9:44 45 If your foot causes you to fall into sin, chop it off. It’s better for you to enter life lame than to be thrown into hell with two feet.
MRK 9:45 47 If your eye causes you to fall into sin, tear it out. It’s better for you to enter God’s kingdom with one eye than to be thrown into hell with two.
MRK 9:46 48 That’s a place where worms don’t die and the fire never goes out .
MRK 9:47 49 Everyone will be salted with fire.
MRK 9:48 50 Salt is good; but if salt loses its saltiness, how will it become salty again? Maintain salt among yourselves and keep peace with each other. ”

MRK 12:7 7 But those tenant farmers said to each other, ‘This is the heir. Let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

MRK 14:47 47 One of the bystanders drew a sword and struck the high priest’s slave and cut off his ear.
MRK 14:48 48 Jesus responded, “ Have you come with swords and clubs to arrest me, like an outlaw?
MRK 14:49 49 Day after day, I was with you, teaching in the temple, but you didn’t arrest me. But let the scriptures be fulfilled. ”
MRK 14:50 50 And all his disciples left him and ran away.
MRK 14:51 51 One young man, a disciple, was wearing nothing but a linen cloth. They grabbed him,
MRK 14:52 52 but he left the linen cloth behind and ran away naked.
MRK 14:53 53 They led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests, elders, and legal experts gathered.
MRK 14:54 54 Peter followed him from a distance, right into the high priest’s courtyard. He was sitting with the guards, warming himself by the fire.
MRK 14:55 55 The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were looking for testimony against Jesus in order to put him to death, but they couldn’t find any.
MRK 14:56 56 Many brought false testimony against him, but they contradicted each other.
MRK 14:57 57 Some stood to offer false witness against him, saying,
MRK 14:58 58 “We heard him saying, ‘I will destroy this temple, constructed by humans, and within three days I will build another, one not made by humans.’”
MRK 14:59 59 But their testimonies didn’t agree even on this point.
MRK 14:60 60 Then the high priest stood up in the middle of the gathering and examined Jesus. “Aren’t you going to respond to the testimony these people have brought against you?”
MRK 14:61 61 But Jesus was silent and didn’t answer. Again, the high priest asked, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the blessed one?”
MRK 14:62 62 Jesus said, “ I am. And you will see the Human One sitting on the right side of the Almighty and coming on the heavenly clouds. ”
MRK 14:63 63 Then the high priest tore his clothes and said, “Why do we need any more witnesses?
MRK 14:64 64 You’ve heard his insult against God. What do you think?” They all condemned him. “He deserves to die!”
MRK 14:65 65 Some began to spit on him. Some covered his face and hit him, saying, “Prophesy!” Then the guards took him and beat him.
MRK 14:66 66 Meanwhile, Peter was below in the courtyard. A woman, one of the high priest’s servants, approached
MRK 14:67 67 and saw Peter warming himself by the fire. She stared at him and said, “You were also with the Nazarene, Jesus.”
MRK 14:68 68 But he denied it, saying, “I don’t know what you’re talking about. I don’t understand what you’re saying.” And he went outside into the outer courtyard. A rooster crowed.
MRK 14:69 69 The female servant saw him and began a second time to say to those standing around, “This man is one of them.”
MRK 14:70 70 But he denied it again. A short time later, those standing around again said to Peter, “You must be one of them, because you are also a Galilean.”
MRK 14:71 71 But he cursed and swore, “I don’t know this man you’re talking about.”
MRK 14:72 72 At that very moment, a rooster crowed a second time. Peter remembered what Jesus told him, “ Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times. ” And he broke down, sobbing.
MRK 15:1 1 At daybreak, the chief priests—with the elders, legal experts, and the whole Sanhedrin—formed a plan. They bound Jesus, led him away, and turned him over to Pilate.
MRK 15:2 2 Pilate questioned him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” Jesus replied, “ That’s what you say. ”
MRK 15:3 3 The chief priests were accusing him of many things.
MRK 15:4 4 Pilate asked him again, “Aren’t you going to answer? What about all these accusations?”
MRK 15:5 5 But Jesus gave no more answers, so that Pilate marveled.
MRK 15:6 6 During the festival, Pilate released one prisoner to them, whomever they requested.
MRK 15:7 7 A man named Barabbas was locked up with the rebels who had committed murder during an uprising.
MRK 15:8 8 The crowd pushed forward and asked Pilate to release someone, as he regularly did.
MRK 15:9 9 Pilate answered them, “Do you want me to release to you the king of the Jews?”
MRK 15:10 10 He knew that the chief priests had handed him over because of jealousy.
MRK 15:11 11 But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead.
MRK 15:12 12 Pilate replied, “Then what do you want me to do with the one you call king of the Jews?”
MRK 15:13 13 They shouted back, “Crucify him!”
MRK 15:14 14 Pilate said to them, “Why? What wrong has he done?” They shouted even louder, “Crucify him!”
MRK 15:15 15 Pilate wanted to satisfy the crowd, so he released Barabbas to them. He had Jesus whipped, then handed him over to be crucified.
MRK 15:16 16 The soldiers led Jesus away into the courtyard of the palace known as the governor’s headquarters, and they called together the whole company of soldiers.
MRK 15:17 17 They dressed him up in a purple robe and twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on him.
MRK 15:18 18 They saluted him, “Hey! King of the Jews!”
MRK 15:19 19 Again and again, they struck his head with a stick. They spit on him and knelt before him to honor him.
MRK 15:20 20 When they finished mocking him, they stripped him of the purple robe and put his own clothes back on him. Then they led him out to crucify him.
MRK 15:21 21 Simon, a man from Cyrene, Alexander and Rufus’ father, was coming in from the countryside. They forced him to carry his cross.
MRK 15:22 22 They brought Jesus to the place called Golgotha, which means Skull Place.
MRK 15:23 23 They tried to give him wine mixed with myrrh, but he didn’t take it.
MRK 15:24 24 They crucified him. They divided up his clothes, drawing lots for them to determine who would take what.
MRK 15:25 25 It was nine in the morning when they crucified him.
MRK 15:26 26 The notice of the formal charge against him was written, “The king of the Jews.”
MRK 15:27 27 They crucified two outlaws with him, one on his right and one on his left.
MRK 15:28 29 People walking by insulted him, shaking their heads and saying, “Ha! So you were going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, were you?
MRK 15:29 30 Save yourself and come down from that cross!”
MRK 15:30 31 In the same way, the chief priests were making fun of him among themselves, together with the legal experts. “He saved others,” they said, “but he can’t save himself.
MRK 15:31 32 Let the Christ, the king of Israel, come down from the cross. Then we’ll see and believe.” Even those who had been crucified with Jesus insulted him.
MRK 15:32 33 From noon until three in the afternoon the whole earth was dark.
MRK 15:33 34 At three, Jesus cried out with a loud shout, “ Eloi, eloi, lama sabachthani, ” which means, “My God, my God, why have you left me?”
MRK 15:34 35 After hearing him, some standing there said, “Look! He’s calling Elijah!”
MRK 15:35 36 Someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, and put it on a pole. He offered it to Jesus to drink, saying, “Let’s see if Elijah will come to take him down.”
MRK 15:36 37 But Jesus let out a loud cry and died.
MRK 15:37 38 The curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom.
MRK 15:38 39 When the centurion, who stood facing Jesus, saw how he died, he said, “This man was certainly God’s Son.”
MRK 15:39 40 Some women were watching from a distance, including Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James (the younger one) and Joses, and Salome.
MRK 15:40 41 When Jesus was in Galilee, these women had followed and supported him, along with many other women who had come to Jerusalem with him.
MRK 15:41 42 Since it was late in the afternoon on Preparation Day, just before the Sabbath,
MRK 15:42 43 Joseph from Arimathea dared to approach Pilate and ask for Jesus’ body. (Joseph was a prominent council member who also eagerly anticipated the coming of God’s kingdom.)
MRK 15:43 44 Pilate wondered if Jesus was already dead. He called the centurion and asked him whether Jesus had already died.
MRK 15:44 45 When he learned from the centurion that Jesus was dead, Pilate gave the dead body to Joseph.
MRK 15:45 46 He bought a linen cloth, took Jesus down from the cross, wrapped him in the cloth, and laid him in a tomb that had been carved out of rock. He rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.
MRK 15:46 47 Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where he was buried.

LUK 1:1 1 Many people have already applied themselves to the task of compiling an account of the events that have been fulfilled among us.
LUK 1:2 2 They used what the original eyewitnesses and servants of the word handed down to us.
LUK 1:3 3 Now, after having investigated everything carefully from the beginning, I have also decided to write a carefully ordered account for you, most honorable Theophilus.
LUK 1:4 4 I want you to have confidence in the soundness of the instruction you have received.
LUK 1:5 5 During the rule of King Herod of Judea there was a priest named Zechariah who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah. His wife Elizabeth was a descendant of Aaron.
LUK 1:6 6 They were both righteous before God, blameless in their observance of all the Lord’s commandments and regulations.
LUK 1:7 7 They had no children because Elizabeth was unable to become pregnant and they both were very old.
LUK 1:8 8 One day Zechariah was serving as a priest before God because his priestly division was on duty.
LUK 1:9 9 Following the customs of priestly service, he was chosen by lottery to go into the Lord’s sanctuary and burn incense.
LUK 1:10 10 All the people who gathered to worship were praying outside during this hour of incense offering.
LUK 1:11 11 An angel from the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the altar of incense.
LUK 1:12 12 When Zechariah saw the angel, he was startled and overcome with fear.
LUK 1:13 13 The angel said, “Don’t be afraid, Zechariah. Your prayers have been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will give birth to your son and you must name him John.
LUK 1:14 14 He will be a joy and delight to you, and many people will rejoice at his birth,
LUK 1:15 15 for he will be great in the Lord’s eyes. He must not drink wine and liquor. He will be filled with the Holy Spirit even before his birth.
LUK 1:16 16 He will bring many Israelites back to the Lord their God.
LUK 1:17 17 He will go forth before the Lord, equipped with the spirit and power of Elijah. He will turn the hearts of fathers back to their children, and he will turn the disobedient to righteous patterns of thinking. He will make ready a people prepared for the Lord.”
LUK 1:18 18 Zechariah said to the angel, “How can I be sure of this? My wife and I are very old.”
LUK 1:19 19 The angel replied, “I am Gabriel. I stand in God’s presence. I was sent to speak to you and to bring this good news to you.
LUK 1:20 20 Know this: What I have spoken will come true at the proper time. But because you didn’t believe, you will remain silent, unable to speak until the day when these things happen.”
LUK 1:21 21 Meanwhile, the people were waiting for Zechariah, and they wondered why he was in the sanctuary for such a long time.
LUK 1:22 22 When he came out, he was unable to speak to them. They realized he had seen a vision in the temple, for he gestured to them and couldn’t speak.
LUK 1:23 23 When he completed the days of his priestly service, he returned home.
LUK 1:24 24 Afterward, his wife Elizabeth became pregnant. She kept to herself for five months, saying,
LUK 1:25 25 “This is the Lord’s doing. He has shown his favor to me by removing my disgrace among other people.”
LUK 1:26 26 When Elizabeth was six months pregnant, God sent the angel Gabriel to Nazareth, a city in Galilee,
LUK 1:27 27 to a virgin who was engaged to a man named Joseph, a descendant of David’s house. The virgin’s name was Mary.
LUK 1:28 28 When the angel came to her, he said, “Rejoice, favored one! The Lord is with you!”
LUK 1:29 29 She was confused by these words and wondered what kind of greeting this might be.
LUK 1:30 30 The angel said, “Don’t be afraid, Mary. God is honoring you.
LUK 1:31 31 Look! You will conceive and give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus.
LUK 1:32 32 He will be great and he will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of David his father.
LUK 1:33 33 He will rule over Jacob’s house forever, and there will be no end to his kingdom.”
LUK 1:34 34 Then Mary said to the angel, “How will this happen since I haven’t had sexual relations with a man?”
LUK 1:35 35 The angel replied, “The Holy Spirit will come over you and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore, the one who is to be born will be holy. He will be called God’s Son.
LUK 1:36 36 Look, even in her old age, your relative Elizabeth has conceived a son. This woman who was labeled ‘unable to conceive’ is now six months pregnant.
LUK 1:37 37 Nothing is impossible for God.”
LUK 1:38 38 Then Mary said, “I am the Lord’s servant. Let it be with me just as you have said.” Then the angel left her.
LUK 1:39 39 Mary got up and hurried to a city in the Judean highlands.
LUK 1:40 40 She entered Zechariah’s home and greeted Elizabeth.
LUK 1:41 41 When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the child leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
LUK 1:42 42 With a loud voice she blurted out, “God has blessed you above all women, and he has blessed the child you carry.
LUK 1:43 43 Why do I have this honor, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
LUK 1:44 44 As soon as I heard your greeting, the baby in my womb jumped for joy.
LUK 1:45 45 Happy is she who believed that the Lord would fulfill the promises he made to her.”
LUK 1:46 46 Mary said, “With all my heart I glorify the Lord!
LUK 1:47 47 In the depths of who I am I rejoice in God my savior.
LUK 1:48 48 He has looked with favor on the low status of his servant. Look! From now on, everyone will consider me highly favored
LUK 1:49 49 because the mighty one has done great things for me. Holy is his name.
LUK 1:50 50 He shows mercy to everyone, from one generation to the next, who honors him as God.
LUK 1:51 51 He has shown strength with his arm. He has scattered those with arrogant thoughts and proud inclinations.
LUK 1:52 52 He has pulled the powerful down from their thrones and lifted up the lowly.
LUK 1:53 53 He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty-handed.
LUK 1:54 54 He has come to the aid of his servant Israel, remembering his mercy,
LUK 1:55 55 just as he promised to our ancestors, to Abraham and to Abraham’s descendants forever.”
LUK 1:56 56 Mary stayed with Elizabeth about three months, and then returned to her home.
LUK 1:57 57 When the time came for Elizabeth to have her child, she gave birth to a boy.
LUK 1:58 58 Her neighbors and relatives celebrated with her because they had heard that the Lord had shown her great mercy.
LUK 1:59 59 On the eighth day, it came time to circumcise the child. They wanted to name him Zechariah because that was his father’s name.
LUK 1:60 60 But his mother replied, “No, his name will be John.”
LUK 1:61 61 They said to her, “None of your relatives have that name.”
LUK 1:62 62 Then they began gesturing to his father to see what he wanted to call him.
LUK 1:63 63 After asking for a tablet, he surprised everyone by writing, “His name is John.”
LUK 1:64 64 At that moment, Zechariah was able to speak again, and he began praising God.
LUK 1:65 65 All their neighbors were filled with awe, and everyone throughout the Judean highlands talked about what had happened.
LUK 1:66 66 All who heard about this considered it carefully. They said, “What then will this child be?” Indeed, the Lord’s power was with him.
LUK 1:67 67 John’s father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied,
LUK 1:68 68 “Bless the Lord God of Israel because he has come to help and has delivered his people.
LUK 1:69 69 He has raised up a mighty savior for us in his servant David’s house,
LUK 1:70 70 just as he said through the mouths of his holy prophets long ago.
LUK 1:71 71 He has brought salvation from our enemies and from the power of all those who hate us.
LUK 1:72 72 He has shown the mercy promised to our ancestors, and remembered his holy covenant,
LUK 1:73 73 the solemn pledge he made to our ancestor Abraham. He has granted
LUK 1:74 74 that we would be rescued from the power of our enemies so that we could serve him without fear,
LUK 1:75 75 in holiness and righteousness in God’s eyes, for as long as we live.
LUK 1:76 76 You, child, will be called a prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare his way.
LUK 1:77 77 You will tell his people how to be saved through the forgiveness of their sins.
LUK 1:78 78 Because of our God’s deep compassion, the dawn from heaven will break upon us,
LUK 1:79 79 to give light to those who are sitting in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide us on the path of peace.”
LUK 1:80 80 The child grew up, becoming strong in character. He was in the wilderness until he began his public ministry to Israel.
LUK 2:1 1 In those days Caesar Augustus declared that everyone throughout the empire should be enrolled in the tax lists.
LUK 2:2 2 This first enrollment occurred when Quirinius governed Syria.
LUK 2:3 3 Everyone went to their own cities to be enrolled.
LUK 2:4 4 Since Joseph belonged to David’s house and family line, he went up from the city of Nazareth in Galilee to David’s city, called Bethlehem, in Judea.
LUK 2:5 5 He went to be enrolled together with Mary, who was promised to him in marriage and who was pregnant.
LUK 2:6 6 While they were there, the time came for Mary to have her baby.
LUK 2:7 7 She gave birth to her firstborn child, a son, wrapped him snugly, and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the guestroom.
LUK 2:8 8 Nearby shepherds were living in the fields, guarding their sheep at night.
LUK 2:9 9 The Lord’s angel stood before them, the Lord’s glory shone around them, and they were terrified.
LUK 2:10 10 The angel said, “Don’t be afraid! Look! I bring good news to you—wonderful, joyous news for all people.
LUK 2:11 11 Your savior is born today in David’s city. He is Christ the Lord.
LUK 2:12 12 This is a sign for you: you will find a newborn baby wrapped snugly and lying in a manger.”
LUK 2:13 13 Suddenly a great assembly of the heavenly forces was with the angel praising God. They said,
LUK 2:14 14 “Glory to God in heaven, and on earth peace among those whom he favors.”
LUK 2:15 15 When the angels returned to heaven, the shepherds said to each other, “Let’s go right now to Bethlehem and see what’s happened. Let’s confirm what the Lord has revealed to us.”
LUK 2:16 16 They went quickly and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in the manger.
LUK 2:17 17 When they saw this, they reported what they had been told about this child.
LUK 2:18 18 Everyone who heard it was amazed at what the shepherds told them.
LUK 2:19 19 Mary committed these things to memory and considered them carefully.
LUK 2:20 20 The shepherds returned home, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen. Everything happened just as they had been told.
LUK 2:21 21 When eight days had passed, Jesus’ parents circumcised him and gave him the name Jesus. This was the name given to him by the angel before he was conceived.
LUK 2:22 22 When the time came for their ritual cleansing, in accordance with the Law from Moses, they brought Jesus up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord. (
LUK 2:23 23 It’s written in the Law of the Lord, “Every firstborn male will be dedicated to the Lord.”)
LUK 2:24 24 They offered a sacrifice in keeping with what’s stated in the Law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons .
LUK 2:25 25 A man named Simeon was in Jerusalem. He was righteous and devout. He eagerly anticipated the restoration of Israel, and the Holy Spirit rested on him.
LUK 2:26 26 The Holy Spirit revealed to him that he wouldn’t die before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
LUK 2:27 27 Led by the Spirit, he went into the temple area. Meanwhile, Jesus’ parents brought the child to the temple so that they could do what was customary under the Law.
LUK 2:28 28 Simeon took Jesus in his arms and praised God. He said,
LUK 2:29 29 “Now, master, let your servant go in peace according to your word,
LUK 2:30 30 because my eyes have seen your salvation.
LUK 2:31 31 You prepared this salvation in the presence of all peoples.
LUK 2:32 32 It’s a light for revelation to the Gentiles and a glory for your people Israel.”
LUK 2:33 33 His father and mother were amazed by what was said about him.
LUK 2:34 34 Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother, “This boy is assigned to be the cause of the falling and rising of many in Israel and to be a sign that generates opposition
LUK 2:35 35 so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed. And a sword will pierce your innermost being too.”
LUK 2:36 36 There was also a prophet, Anna the daughter of Phanuel, who belonged to the tribe of Asher. She was very old. After she married, she lived with her husband for seven years.
LUK 2:37 37 She was now an 84-year-old widow. She never left the temple area but worshipped God with fasting and prayer night and day.
LUK 2:38 38 She approached at that very moment and began to praise God and to speak about Jesus to everyone who was looking forward to the redemption of Jerusalem.
LUK 2:39 39 When Mary and Joseph had completed everything required by the Law of the Lord, they returned to their hometown, Nazareth in Galilee.
LUK 2:40 40 The child grew up and became strong. He was filled with wisdom, and God’s favor was on him.
LUK 2:41 41 Each year his parents went to Jerusalem for the Passover Festival.
LUK 2:42 42 When he was 12 years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to their custom.
LUK 2:43 43 After the festival was over, they were returning home, but the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem. His parents didn’t know it.
LUK 2:44 44 Supposing that he was among their band of travelers, they journeyed on for a full day while looking for him among their family and friends.
LUK 2:45 45 When they didn’t find Jesus, they returned to Jerusalem to look for him.
LUK 2:46 46 After three days they found him in the temple. He was sitting among the teachers, listening to them and putting questions to them.
LUK 2:47 47 Everyone who heard him was amazed by his understanding and his answers.
LUK 2:48 48 When his parents saw him, they were shocked. His mother said, “Child, why have you treated us like this? Listen! Your father and I have been worried. We’ve been looking for you!”
LUK 2:49 49 Jesus replied, “ Why were you looking for me? Didn’t you know that it was necessary for me to be in my Father’s house? ”
LUK 2:50 50 But they didn’t understand what he said to them.
LUK 2:51 51 Jesus went down to Nazareth with them and was obedient to them. His mother cherished every word in her heart.
LUK 2:52 52 Jesus matured in wisdom and years, and in favor with God and with people.
LUK 3:1 1 In the fifteenth year of the rule of the emperor Tiberius—when Pontius Pilate was governor over Judea and Herod was ruler over Galilee, his brother Philip was ruler over Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was ruler over Abilene,
LUK 3:2 2 during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas—God’s word came to John son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
LUK 3:3 3 John went throughout the region of the Jordan River, calling for people to be baptized to show that they were changing their hearts and lives and wanted God to forgive their sins.
LUK 3:4 4 This is just as it was written in the scroll of the words of Isaiah the prophet, A voice crying out in the wilderness: “ Prepare the way for the Lord; make his paths straight.
LUK 3:5 5 Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be leveled. The crooked will be made straight and the rough places made smooth.
LUK 3:6 6 All humanity will see God’s salvation. ”
LUK 3:7 7 Then John said to the crowds who came to be baptized by him, “You children of snakes! Who warned you to escape from the angry judgment that is coming soon?
LUK 3:8 8 Produce fruit that shows you have changed your hearts and lives. And don’t even think about saying to yourselves, Abraham is our father. I tell you that God is able to raise up Abraham’s children from these stones.
LUK 3:9 9 The ax is already at the root of the trees. Therefore, every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit will be chopped down and tossed into the fire.”
LUK 3:10 10 The crowds asked him, “What then should we do?”
LUK 3:11 11 He answered, “Whoever has two shirts must share with the one who has none, and whoever has food must do the same.”
LUK 3:12 12 Even tax collectors came to be baptized. They said to him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
LUK 3:13 13 He replied, “Collect no more than you are authorized to collect.”
LUK 3:14 14 Soldiers asked, “What about us? What should we do?” He answered, “Don’t cheat or harass anyone, and be satisfied with your pay.”
LUK 3:15 15 The people were filled with expectation, and everyone wondered whether John might be the Christ.
LUK 3:16 16 John replied to them all, “I baptize you with water, but the one who is more powerful than me is coming. I’m not worthy to loosen the strap of his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
LUK 3:17 17 The shovel he uses to sift the wheat from the husks is in his hands. He will clean out his threshing area and bring the wheat into his barn. But he will burn the husks with a fire that can’t be put out.”
LUK 3:18 18 With many other words John appealed to them, proclaiming good news to the people.
LUK 3:19 19 But Herod the ruler had been criticized harshly by John because of Herodias, Herod’s brother’s wife, and because of all the evil he had done.
LUK 3:20 20 He added this to the list of his evil deeds: he locked John up in prison.
LUK 3:21 21 When everyone was being baptized, Jesus also was baptized. While he was praying, heaven was opened
LUK 3:22 22 and the Holy Spirit came down on him in bodily form like a dove. And there was a voice from heaven: “You are my Son, whom I dearly love; in you I find happiness.”
