LUK 4:1 1 Jesus returned from the Jordan River full of the Holy Spirit, and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness.
LUK 4:2 2 There he was tempted for forty days by the devil. He ate nothing during those days and afterward Jesus was starving.
LUK 4:3 3 The devil said to him, “Since you are God’s Son, command this stone to become a loaf of bread.”
LUK 4:4 4 Jesus replied, “ It’s written, People won’t live only by bread .”
LUK 4:5 5 Next the devil led him to a high place and showed him in a single instant all the kingdoms of the world.
LUK 4:6 6 The devil said, “I will give you this whole domain and the glory of all these kingdoms. It’s been entrusted to me and I can give it to anyone I want.
LUK 4:7 7 Therefore, if you will worship me, it will all be yours.”
LUK 4:8 8 Jesus answered, “ It’s written, You will worship the Lord your God and serve only him. ”
LUK 4:9 9 The devil brought him into Jerusalem and stood him at the highest point of the temple. He said to him, “Since you are God’s Son, throw yourself down from here;
LUK 4:10 10 for it’s written: He will command his angels concerning you, to protect you
LUK 4:11 11 and they will take you up in their hands so that you won’t hit your foot on a stone. ”
LUK 4:12 12 Jesus answered, “ It’s been said, Don’t test the Lord your God. ”
LUK 4:13 13 After finishing every temptation, the devil departed from him until the next opportunity.
LUK 4:14 14 Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit to Galilee, and news about him spread throughout the whole countryside.
LUK 4:15 15 He taught in their synagogues and was praised by everyone.
LUK 4:16 16 Jesus went to Nazareth, where he had been raised. On the Sabbath he went to the synagogue as he normally did and stood up to read.
LUK 4:17 17 The synagogue assistant gave him the scroll from the prophet Isaiah. He unrolled the scroll and found the place where it was written:
LUK 4:18 18 The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me . He has sent me to preach good news to the poor, to proclaim release to the prisoners and recovery of sight to the blind, to liberate the oppressed,
LUK 4:19 19 and to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.
LUK 4:20 20 He rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the synagogue assistant, and sat down. Every eye in the synagogue was fixed on him.
LUK 4:21 21 He began to explain to them, “ Today, this scripture has been fulfilled just as you heard it. ”
LUK 4:22 22 Everyone was raving about Jesus, so impressed were they by the gracious words flowing from his lips. They said, “This is Joseph’s son, isn’t it?”
LUK 4:23 23 Then Jesus said to them, “ Undoubtedly, you will quote this saying to me: ‘Doctor, heal yourself. Do here in your hometown what we’ve heard you did in Capernaum.’ ”
LUK 4:24 24 He said, “ I assure you that no prophet is welcome in the prophet’s hometown.
LUK 4:25 25 And I can assure you that there were many widows in Israel during Elijah’s time, when it didn’t rain for three and a half years and there was a great food shortage in the land.
LUK 4:26 26 Yet Elijah was sent to none of them but only to a widow in the city of Zarephath in the region of Sidon.
LUK 4:27 27 There were also many persons with skin diseases in Israel during the time of the prophet Elisha, but none of them were cleansed. Instead, Naaman the Syrian was cleansed. ”
LUK 4:28 28 When they heard this, everyone in the synagogue was filled with anger.
LUK 4:29 29 They rose up and ran him out of town. They led him to the crest of the hill on which their town had been built so that they could throw him off the cliff.
LUK 4:30 30 But he passed through the crowd and went on his way.
LUK 4:31 31 Jesus went down to the city of Capernaum in Galilee and taught the people each Sabbath.
LUK 4:32 32 They were amazed by his teaching because he delivered his message with authority.
LUK 4:33 33 A man in the synagogue had the spirit of an unclean demon. He screamed,
LUK 4:34 34 “Hey! What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are. You are the holy one from God.”
LUK 4:35 35 “ Silence! ” Jesus said, speaking harshly to the demon. “ Come out of him! ” The demon threw the man down before them, then came out of him without harming him.
LUK 4:36 36 They were all shaken and said to each other, “What kind of word is this, that he can command unclean spirits with authority and power, and they leave?”
LUK 4:37 37 Reports about him spread everywhere in the surrounding region.
LUK 4:38 38 After leaving the synagogue, Jesus went home with Simon. Simon’s mother-in-law was sick with a high fever, and the family asked Jesus to help her.
LUK 4:39 39 He bent over her and spoke harshly to the fever, and it left her. She got up at once and served them.
LUK 4:40 40 When the sun was setting, everyone brought to Jesus relatives and acquaintances with all kinds of diseases. Placing his hands on each of them, he healed them.
LUK 4:41 41 Demons also came out of many people. They screamed, “You are God’s Son.” But he spoke harshly to them and wouldn’t allow them to speak because they recognized that he was the Christ.
LUK 4:42 42 When daybreak arrived, Jesus went to a deserted place. The crowds were looking for him. When they found him, they tried to keep him from leaving them.
LUK 4:43 43 But he said to them, “ I must preach the good news of God’s kingdom in other cities too, for this is why I was sent. ”
LUK 4:44 44 So he continued preaching in the Judean synagogues.
LUK 5:1 1 One day Jesus was standing beside Lake Gennesaret when the crowd pressed in around him to hear God’s word.
LUK 5:2 2 Jesus saw two boats sitting by the lake. The fishermen had gone ashore and were washing their nets.
LUK 5:3 3 Jesus boarded one of the boats, the one that belonged to Simon, then asked him to row out a little distance from the shore. Jesus sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
LUK 5:4 4 When he finished speaking to the crowds, he said to Simon, “ Row out farther, into the deep water, and drop your nets for a catch. ”
LUK 5:5 5 Simon replied, “Master, we’ve worked hard all night and caught nothing. But because you say so, I’ll drop the nets.”
LUK 5:6 6 So they dropped the nets and their catch was so huge that their nets were splitting.
LUK 5:7 7 They signaled for their partners in the other boat to come and help them. They filled both boats so full that they were about to sink.
LUK 5:8 8 When Simon Peter saw the catch, he fell at Jesus’ knees and said, “Leave me, Lord, for I’m a sinner!”
LUK 5:9 9 Peter and those with him were overcome with amazement because of the number of fish they caught.
LUK 5:10 10 James and John, Zebedee’s sons, were Simon’s partners and they were amazed too. Jesus said to Simon, “ Don’t be afraid. From now on, you will be fishing for people. ”
LUK 5:11 11 As soon as they brought the boats to the shore, they left everything and followed Jesus.
LUK 5:12 12 Jesus was in one of the towns where there was also a man covered with a skin disease. When he saw Jesus, he fell on his face and begged, “Lord, if you want, you can make me clean.”
LUK 5:13 13 Jesus reached out his hand, touched him, and said, “ I do want to. Be clean. ” Instantly, the skin disease left him.
LUK 5:14 14 Jesus ordered him not to tell anyone. “ Instead, ” Jesus said, “ go and show yourself to the priest and make an offering for your cleansing, as Moses instructed. This will be a testimony to them. ”
LUK 5:15 15 News of him spread even more and huge crowds gathered to listen and to be healed from their illnesses.
LUK 5:16 16 But Jesus would withdraw to deserted places for prayer.
LUK 5:17 17 One day when Jesus was teaching, Pharisees and legal experts were sitting nearby. They had come from every village in Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem. Now the power of the Lord was with Jesus to heal.
LUK 5:18 18 Some men were bringing a man who was paralyzed, lying on a cot. They wanted to carry him in and place him before Jesus,
LUK 5:19 19 but they couldn’t reach him because of the crowd. So they took him up on the roof and lowered him—cot and all—through the roof tiles into the crowded room in front of Jesus.
LUK 5:20 20 When Jesus saw their faith, he said, “ Friend, your sins are forgiven. ”
LUK 5:21 21 The legal experts and Pharisees began to mutter among themselves, “Who is this who insults God? Only God can forgive sins!”
LUK 5:22 22 Jesus recognized what they were discussing and responded, “ Why do you fill your minds with these questions?
LUK 5:23 23 Which is easier—to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
LUK 5:24 24 But so that you will know that the Human One has authority on the earth to forgive sins ” —Jesus now spoke to the man who was paralyzed, “ I say to you, get up, take your cot, and go home. ”
LUK 5:25 25 Right away, the man stood before them, picked up his cot, and went home, praising God.
LUK 5:26 26 All the people were beside themselves with wonder. Filled with awe, they glorified God, saying, “We’ve seen unimaginable things today.”
LUK 5:27 27 Afterward, Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at a kiosk for collecting taxes. Jesus said to him, “ Follow me. ”
LUK 5:28 28 Levi got up, left everything behind, and followed him.
LUK 5:29 29 Then Levi threw a great banquet for Jesus in his home. A large number of tax collectors and others sat down to eat with them.
LUK 5:30 30 The Pharisees and their legal experts grumbled against his disciples. They said, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
LUK 5:31 31 Jesus answered, “ Healthy people don’t need a doctor, but sick people do.
LUK 5:32 32 I didn’t come to call righteous people but sinners to change their hearts and lives. ”
LUK 5:33 33 Some people said to Jesus, “The disciples of John fast often and pray frequently. The disciples of the Pharisees do the same, but your disciples are always eating and drinking.”
LUK 5:34 34 Jesus replied, “ You can’t make the wedding guests fast while the groom is with them, can you?
LUK 5:35 35 The days will come when the groom will be taken from them, and then they will fast. ”
LUK 5:36 36 Then he told them a parable. “ No one tears a patch from a new garment to patch an old garment. Otherwise, the new garment would be ruined, and the new patch wouldn’t match the old garment.
LUK 5:37 37 Nobody pours new wine into old wineskins. If they did, the new wine would burst the wineskins, the wine would spill, and the wineskins would be ruined.
LUK 5:38 38 Instead, new wine must be put into new wineskins.
LUK 5:39 39 No one who drinks a well-aged wine wants new wine, but says, ‘The well-aged wine is better.’ ”
LUK 6:1 1 One Sabbath, as Jesus was going through the wheat fields, his disciples were picking the heads of wheat, rubbing them in their hands, and eating them.
LUK 6:2 2 Some Pharisees said, “Why are you breaking the Sabbath law?”
LUK 6:3 3 Jesus replied, “ Haven’t you read what David and his companions did when they were hungry?
LUK 6:4 4 He broke the Law by going into God’s house and eating the bread of the presence, which only the priests can eat. He also gave some of the bread to his companions. ”
LUK 6:5 5 Then he said to them, “ The Human One is Lord of the Sabbath. ”
LUK 6:6 6 On another Sabbath, Jesus entered a synagogue to teach. A man was there whose right hand was withered.
LUK 6:7 7 The legal experts and the Pharisees were watching him closely to see if he would heal on the Sabbath. They were looking for a reason to bring charges against him.
LUK 6:8 8 Jesus knew their thoughts, so he said to the man with the withered hand, “ Get up and stand in front of everyone. ” He got up and stood there.
LUK 6:9 9 Jesus said to the legal experts and Pharisees, “ Here’s a question for you: Is it legal on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it? ”
LUK 6:10 10 Looking around at them all, he said to the man, “ Stretch out your hand. ” So he did and his hand was made healthy.
LUK 6:11 11 They were furious and began talking with each other about what to do to Jesus.
LUK 6:12 12 During that time, Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and he prayed to God all night long.
LUK 6:13 13 At daybreak, he called together his disciples. He chose twelve of them whom he called apostles:
LUK 6:14 14 Simon, whom he named Peter; his brother Andrew; James; John; Philip; Bartholomew;
LUK 6:15 15 Matthew; Thomas; James the son of Alphaeus; Simon, who was called a zealot;
LUK 6:16 16 Judas the son of James; and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
LUK 6:17 17 Jesus came down from the mountain with them and stood on a large area of level ground. A great company of his disciples and a huge crowd of people from all around Judea and Jerusalem and the area around Tyre and Sidon joined him there.
LUK 6:18 18 They came to hear him and to be healed from their diseases, and those bothered by unclean spirits were healed.
LUK 6:19 19 The whole crowd wanted to touch him, because power was going out from him and he was healing everyone.
LUK 6:20 20 Jesus raised his eyes to his disciples and said: “Happy are you who are poor, because God’s kingdom is yours.
LUK 6:21 21 Happy are you who hunger now, because you will be satisfied. Happy are you who weep now, because you will laugh.
LUK 6:22 22 Happy are you when people hate you, reject you, insult you, and condemn your name as evil because of the Human One.
LUK 6:23 23 Rejoice when that happens! Leap for joy because you have a great reward in heaven. Their ancestors did the same things to the prophets.
LUK 6:24 24 But how terrible for you who are rich, because you have already received your comfort.
LUK 6:25 25 How terrible for you who have plenty now, because you will be hungry. How terrible for you who laugh now, because you will mourn and weep.
LUK 6:26 26 How terrible for you when all speak well of you. Their ancestors did the same things to the false prophets.
LUK 6:27 27 “But I say to you who are willing to hear: Love your enemies. Do good to those who hate you.
LUK 6:28 28 Bless those who curse you. Pray for those who mistreat you.
LUK 6:29 29 If someone slaps you on the cheek, offer the other one as well. If someone takes your coat, don’t withhold your shirt either.
LUK 6:30 30 Give to everyone who asks and don’t demand your things back from those who take them.
LUK 6:31 31 Treat people in the same way that you want them to treat you.
LUK 6:32 32 “If you love those who love you, why should you be commended? Even sinners love those who love them.
LUK 6:33 33 If you do good to those who do good to you, why should you be commended? Even sinners do that.
LUK 6:34 34 If you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, why should you be commended? Even sinners lend to sinners expecting to be paid back in full.
LUK 6:35 35 Instead, love your enemies, do good, and lend expecting nothing in return. If you do, you will have a great reward. You will be acting the way children of the Most High act, for he is kind to ungrateful and wicked people.
LUK 6:36 36 Be compassionate just as your Father is compassionate.
LUK 6:37 37 “ Don’t judge, and you won’t be judged. Don’t condemn, and you won’t be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
LUK 6:38 38 Give, and it will be given to you. A good portion—packed down, firmly shaken, and overflowing—will fall into your lap. The portion you give will determine the portion you receive in return. ”
LUK 6:39 39 Jesus also told them a riddle. “ A blind person can’t lead another blind person, right? Won’t they both fall into a ditch?
LUK 6:40 40 Disciples aren’t greater than their teacher, but whoever is fully prepared will be like their teacher.
LUK 6:41 41 Why do you see the splinter in your brother’s or sister’s eye but don’t notice the log in your own eye?
LUK 6:42 42 How can you say to your brother or sister, ‘Brother, Sister, let me take the splinter out of your eye,’ when you don’t see the log in your own eye? You deceive yourselves! First take the log out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to take the splinter out of your brother’s or sister’s eye.
LUK 6:43 43 “A good tree doesn’t produce bad fruit, nor does a bad tree produce good fruit.
LUK 6:44 44 Each tree is known by its own fruit. People don’t gather figs from thorny plants, nor do they pick grapes from prickly bushes.
LUK 6:45 45 A good person produces good from the good treasury of the inner self, while an evil person produces evil from the evil treasury of the inner self. The inner self overflows with words that are spoken.
LUK 6:46 46 “ Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord’ and don’t do what I say?
LUK 6:47 47 I’ll show what it’s like when someone comes to me, hears my words, and puts them into practice.
LUK 6:48 48 It’s like a person building a house by digging deep and laying the foundation on bedrock. When the flood came, the rising water smashed against that house, but the water couldn’t shake the house because it was well built.
LUK 6:49 49 But those who don’t put into practice what they hear are like a person who built a house without a foundation. The floodwater smashed against it and it collapsed instantly. It was completely destroyed. ”
LUK 7:1 1 After Jesus finished presenting all his words among the people, he entered Capernaum.
LUK 7:2 2 A centurion had a servant who was very important to him, but the servant was ill and about to die.
LUK 7:3 3 When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to Jesus to ask him to come and heal his servant.
LUK 7:4 4 When they came to Jesus, they earnestly pleaded with Jesus. “He deserves to have you do this for him,” they said.
LUK 7:5 5 “He loves our people and he built our synagogue for us.”
LUK 7:6 6 Jesus went with them. He had almost reached the house when the centurion sent friends to say to Jesus, “Lord, don’t be bothered. I don’t deserve to have you come under my roof.
LUK 7:7 7 In fact, I didn’t even consider myself worthy to come to you. Just say the word and my servant will be healed.
LUK 7:8 8 I’m also a man appointed under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to one, ‘Go,’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes. I say to my servant, ‘Do this,’ and the servant does it.”
LUK 7:9 9 When Jesus heard these words, he was impressed with the centurion. He turned to the crowd following him and said, “ I tell you, even in Israel I haven’t found faith like this. ”
LUK 7:10 10 When the centurion’s friends returned to his house, they found the servant restored to health.
LUK 7:11 11 A little later Jesus went to a city called Nain. His disciples and a great crowd traveled with him.
LUK 7:12 12 As he approached the city gate, a dead man was being carried out. He was his mother’s only son, and she was a widow. A large crowd from the city was with her.
LUK 7:13 13 When he saw her, the Lord had compassion for her and said, “ Don’t cry. ”
LUK 7:14 14 He stepped forward and touched the stretcher on which the dead man was being carried. Those carrying him stood still. Jesus said, “ Young man, I say to you, get up. ”
LUK 7:15 15 The dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother.
LUK 7:16 16 Awestruck, everyone praised God. “A great prophet has appeared among us,” they said. “God has come to help his people.”
LUK 7:17 17 This news about Jesus spread throughout Judea and the surrounding region.
LUK 7:18 18 John’s disciples informed him about all these things. John called two of his disciples
LUK 7:19 19 and sent them to the Lord. They were to ask him, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for someone else?”
LUK 7:20 20 When they reached Jesus, they said, “John the Baptist sent us to you. He asks, ‘Are you the one who is coming, or should we look for someone else?’”
LUK 7:21 21 Right then, Jesus healed many of their diseases, illnesses, and evil spirits, and he gave sight to a number of blind people.
LUK 7:22 22 Then he replied to John’s disciples, “ Go, report to John what you have seen and heard. Those who were blind are able to see. Those who were crippled now walk. People with skin diseases are cleansed. Those who were deaf now hear. Those who were dead are raised up. And good news is preached to the poor.
LUK 7:23 23 Happy is anyone who doesn’t stumble along the way because of me. ”
LUK 7:24 24 After John’s messengers were gone, Jesus spoke to the crowds about John. “ What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A stalk blowing in the wind?
LUK 7:25 25 What did you go out to see? A man dressed up in refined clothes? Look, those who dress in fashionable clothes and live in luxury are in royal palaces.
LUK 7:26 26 What did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
LUK 7:27 27 He is the one of whom it’s written: Look, I’m sending my messenger before you, who will prepare your way before you .
LUK 7:28 28 I tell you that no greater human being has ever been born than John. Yet whoever is least in God’s kingdom is greater than he. ”
LUK 7:29 29 Everyone who heard this, including the tax collectors, acknowledged God’s justice because they had been baptized by John.
LUK 7:30 30 But the Pharisees and legal experts rejected God’s will for themselves because they hadn’t been baptized by John.
LUK 7:31 31 “ To what will I compare the people of this generation? ” Jesus asked. “ What are they like?
LUK 7:32 32 They are like children sitting in the marketplace calling out to each other, ‘We played the flute for you and you didn’t dance. We sang a funeral song and you didn’t cry.’
LUK 7:33 33 John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’
LUK 7:34 34 Yet the Human One came eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunk, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’
LUK 7:35 35 But wisdom is proved to be right by all her descendants. ”
LUK 7:36 36 One of the Pharisees invited Jesus to eat with him. After he entered the Pharisee’s home, he took his place at the table.
LUK 7:37 37 Meanwhile, a woman from the city, a sinner, discovered that Jesus was dining in the Pharisee’s house. She brought perfumed oil in a vase made of alabaster.
LUK 7:38 38 Standing behind him at his feet and crying, she began to wet his feet with her tears. She wiped them with her hair, kissed them, and poured the oil on them.
LUK 7:39 39 When the Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw what was happening, he said to himself, If this man were a prophet, he would know what kind of woman is touching him. He would know that she is a sinner.
LUK 7:40 40 Jesus replied, “ Simon, I have something to say to you. ” “Teacher, speak,” he said.
LUK 7:41 41 “ A certain lender had two debtors. One owed enough money to pay five hundred people for a day’s work. The other owed enough money for fifty.
LUK 7:42 42 When they couldn’t pay, the lender forgave the debts of them both. Which of them will love him more? ”
LUK 7:43 43 Simon replied, “I suppose the one who had the largest debt canceled.” Jesus said, “ You have judged correctly. ”
LUK 7:44 44 Jesus turned to the woman and said to Simon, “ Do you see this woman? When I entered your home, you didn’t give me water for my feet, but she wet my feet with tears and wiped them with her hair.
LUK 7:45 45 You didn’t greet me with a kiss, but she hasn’t stopped kissing my feet since I came in.
LUK 7:46 46 You didn’t anoint my head with oil, but she has poured perfumed oil on my feet.
LUK 7:47 47 This is why I tell you that her many sins have been forgiven; so she has shown great love. The one who is forgiven little loves little. ”
LUK 7:48 48 Then Jesus said to her, “ Your sins are forgiven. ”
LUK 7:49 49 The other table guests began to say among themselves, “Who is this person that even forgives sins?”
LUK 7:50 50 Jesus said to the woman, “ Your faith has saved you. Go in peace. ”
LUK 8:1 1 Soon afterward, Jesus traveled through the cities and villages, preaching and proclaiming the good news of God’s kingdom. The Twelve were with him,
LUK 8:2 2 along with some women who had been healed of evil spirits and sicknesses. Among them were Mary Magdalene (from whom seven demons had been thrown out),
LUK 8:3 3 Joanna (the wife of Herod’s servant Chuza), Susanna, and many others who provided for them out of their resources.
LUK 8:4 4 When a great crowd was gathering and people were coming to Jesus from one city after another, he spoke to them in a parable:
LUK 8:5 5 “ A farmer went out to scatter his seed. As he was scattering it, some fell on the path where it was crushed, and the birds in the sky came and ate it.
LUK 8:6 6 Other seed fell on rock. As it grew, it dried up because it had no moisture.
LUK 8:7 7 Other seed fell among thorny plants. The thorns grew with the plants and choked them.
LUK 8:8 8 Still other seed landed on good soil. When it grew, it produced one hundred times more grain than was scattered. ” As he said this, he called out, “ Everyone who has ears should pay attention. ”
LUK 8:9 9 His disciples asked him what this parable meant.
LUK 8:10 10 He said, “You have been given the mysteries of God’s kingdom, but these mysteries come to everyone else in parables so that when they see, they can’t see, and when they hear, they can’t understand .
LUK 8:11 11 “The parable means this: The seed is God’s word.
LUK 8:12 12 The seed on the path are those who hear, but then the devil comes and steals the word from their hearts so that they won’t believe and be saved.
LUK 8:13 13 The seed on the rock are those who receive the word joyfully when they hear it, but they have no root. They believe for a while but fall away when they are tempted.
LUK 8:14 14 As for the seed that fell among thorny plants, these are the ones who, as they go about their lives, are choked by the concerns, riches, and pleasures of life, and their fruit never matures.
LUK 8:15 15 The seed that fell on good soil are those who hear the word and commit themselves to it with a good and upright heart. Through their resolve, they bear fruit.
LUK 8:16 16 “ No one lights a lamp and then covers it with a bowl or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it on top of a lampstand so that those who enter can see the light.
LUK 8:17 17 Nothing is hidden that won’t be exposed. Nor is anything concealed that won’t be made known and brought to the light.
LUK 8:18 18 Therefore, listen carefully. Those who have will receive more, but as for those who don’t have, even what they seem to have will be taken away from them. ”
LUK 8:19 19 Jesus’ mother and brothers came to him but were unable to reach him because of the crowd.
LUK 8:20 20 Someone told him, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you.”
LUK 8:21 21 He replied, “ My mother and brothers are those who listen to God’s word and do it. ”
LUK 8:22 22 One day Jesus and his disciples boarded a boat. He said to them, “ Let’s cross over to the other side of the lake. ” So they set sail.
LUK 8:23 23 While they were sailing, he fell asleep. Gale-force winds swept down on the lake. The boat was filling up with water and they were in danger.
LUK 8:24 24 So they went and woke Jesus, shouting, “Master, Master, we’re going to drown!” But he got up and gave orders to the wind and the violent waves. The storm died down and it was calm.
LUK 8:25 25 He said to his disciples, “ Where is your faith? ” Filled with awe and wonder, they said to each other, “Who is this? He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him!”
LUK 8:26 26 Jesus and his disciples sailed to the Gerasenes’ land, which is across the lake from Galilee.
LUK 8:27 27 As soon as Jesus got out of the boat, a certain man met him. The man was from the city and was possessed by demons. For a long time, he had lived among the tombs, naked and homeless.
LUK 8:28 28 When he saw Jesus, he shrieked and fell down before him. Then he shouted, “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, don’t torture me!”
LUK 8:29 29 He said this because Jesus had already commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had taken possession of him, so he would be bound with leg irons and chains and placed under guard. But he would break his restraints, and the demon would force him into the wilderness.
LUK 8:30 30 Jesus asked him, “ What is your name? ” “Legion,” he replied, because many demons had entered him.
LUK 8:31 31 They pleaded with him not to order them to go back into the abyss.

LUK 8:56 56 Her parents were beside themselves with joy, but he ordered them to tell no one what had happened.

LUK 13:1 1 Some who were present on that occasion told Jesus about the Galileans whom Pilate had killed while they were offering sacrifices.
LUK 13:2 2 He replied, “ Do you think the suffering of these Galileans proves that they were more sinful than all the other Galileans?
LUK 13:3 3 No, I tell you, but unless you change your hearts and lives, you will die just as they did.
LUK 13:4 4 What about those eighteen people who were killed when the tower of Siloam fell on them? Do you think that they were more guilty of wrongdoing than everyone else who lives in Jerusalem?
LUK 13:5 5 No, I tell you, but unless you change your hearts and lives, you will die just as they did. ”
LUK 13:6 6 Jesus told this parable: “ A man owned a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit on it and found none.
LUK 13:7 7 He said to his gardener, ‘Look, I’ve come looking for fruit on this fig tree for the past three years, and I’ve never found any. Cut it down! Why should it continue depleting the soil’s nutrients?’
LUK 13:8 8 The gardener responded, ‘Lord, give it one more year, and I will dig around it and give it fertilizer.
LUK 13:9 9 Maybe it will produce fruit next year; if not, then you can cut it down.’ ”
LUK 13:10 10 Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
LUK 13:11 11 A woman was there who had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was bent over and couldn’t stand up straight.
LUK 13:12 12 When he saw her, Jesus called her to him and said, “ Woman, you are set free from your sickness. ”
LUK 13:13 13 He placed his hands on her and she straightened up at once and praised God.
LUK 13:14 14 The synagogue leader, incensed that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, responded, “There are six days during which work is permitted. Come and be healed on those days, not on the Sabbath day.”
LUK 13:15 15 The Lord replied, “ Hypocrites! Don’t each of you on the Sabbath untie your ox or donkey from its stall and lead it out to get a drink?
LUK 13:16 16 Then isn’t it necessary that this woman, a daughter of Abraham, bound by Satan for eighteen long years, be set free from her bondage on the Sabbath day? ”
LUK 13:17 17 When he said these things, all his opponents were put to shame, but all those in the crowd rejoiced at all the extraordinary things he was doing.
LUK 13:18 18 Jesus asked, “ What is God’s kingdom like? To what can I compare it?

LUK 13:20 20 Again he said, “ To what can I compare God’s kingdom?
LUK 13:21 21 It’s like yeast, which a woman took and hid in a bushel of wheat flour until the yeast had worked its way through the whole. ”

LUK 13:26 26 Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’

LUK 13:28 28 There will be weeping and grinding of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in God’s kingdom, but you yourselves will be thrown out.
LUK 13:29 29 People will come from east and west, north and south, and sit down to eat in God’s kingdom.
LUK 13:30 30 Look! Those who are last will be first and those who are first will be last.”

LUK 13:32 32 Jesus said to them, “Go, tell that fox, ‘Look, I’m throwing out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will complete my work.
LUK 13:33 33 However, it’s necessary for me to travel today, tomorrow, and the next day because it’s impossible for a prophet to be killed outside of Jerusalem.’

LUK 14:1 1 One Sabbath, when Jesus went to share a meal in the home of one of the leaders of the Pharisees, they were watching him closely.
LUK 14:2 2 A man suffering from an abnormal swelling of the body was there.
LUK 14:3 3 Jesus asked the lawyers and Pharisees, “ Does the Law allow healing on the Sabbath or not? ”
LUK 14:4 4 But they said nothing. Jesus took hold of the sick man, cured him, and then let him go.
LUK 14:5 5 He said to them, “ Suppose your child or ox fell into a ditch on the Sabbath day. Wouldn’t you immediately pull it out? ”
LUK 14:6 6 But they had no response.
LUK 14:7 7 When Jesus noticed how the guests sought out the best seats at the table, he told them a parable.
LUK 14:8 8 “ When someone invites you to a wedding celebration, don’t take your seat in the place of honor. Someone more highly regarded than you could have been invited by your host.
LUK 14:9 9 The host who invited both of you will come and say to you, ‘Give your seat to this other person.’ Embarrassed, you will take your seat in the least important place.
LUK 14:10 10 Instead, when you receive an invitation, go and sit in the least important place. When your host approaches you, he will say, ‘Friend, move up here to a better seat.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all your fellow guests.
LUK 14:11 11 All who lift themselves up will be brought low, and those who make themselves low will be lifted up. ”
LUK 14:12 12 Then Jesus said to the person who had invited him, “ When you host a lunch or dinner, don’t invite your friends, your brothers and sisters, your relatives, or rich neighbors. If you do, they will invite you in return and that will be your reward.
LUK 14:13 13 Instead, when you give a banquet, invite the poor, crippled, lame, and blind.
LUK 14:14 14 And you will be blessed because they can’t repay you. Instead, you will be repaid when the just are resurrected. ”
LUK 14:15 15 When one of the dinner guests heard Jesus’ remarks, he said to Jesus, “Happy are those who will feast in God’s kingdom.”
LUK 14:16 16 Jesus replied, “ A certain man hosted a large dinner and invited many people.
LUK 14:17 17 When it was time for the dinner to begin, he sent his servant to tell the invited guests, ‘Come! The dinner is now ready.’
LUK 14:18 18 One by one, they all began to make excuses. The first one told him, ‘I bought a farm and must go and see it. Please excuse me.’
LUK 14:19 19 Another said, ‘I bought five teams of oxen, and I’m going to check on them. Please excuse me.’
LUK 14:20 20 Another said, ‘I just got married, so I can’t come.’
LUK 14:21 21 When he returned, the servant reported these excuses to his master. The master of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go quickly to the city’s streets, the busy ones and the side streets, and bring the poor, crippled, blind, and lame.’
LUK 14:22 22 The servant said, ‘Master, your instructions have been followed and there is still room.’
LUK 14:23 23 The master said to the servant, ‘Go to the highways and back alleys and urge people to come in so that my house will be filled.
LUK 14:24 24 I tell you, not one of those who were invited will taste my dinner.’ ”
LUK 14:25 25 Large crowds were traveling with Jesus. Turning to them, he said,
LUK 14:26 26 “Whoever comes to me and doesn’t hate father and mother, spouse and children, and brothers and sisters—yes, even one’s own life—cannot be my disciple.
LUK 14:27 27 Whoever doesn’t carry their own cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
LUK 14:28 28 “If one of you wanted to build a tower, wouldn’t you first sit down and calculate the cost, to determine whether you have enough money to complete it?
LUK 14:29 29 Otherwise, when you have laid the foundation but couldn’t finish the tower, all who see it will begin to belittle you.
LUK 14:30 30 They will say, ‘Here’s the person who began construction and couldn’t complete it!’
LUK 14:31 31 Or what king would go to war against another king without first sitting down to consider whether his ten thousand soldiers could go up against the twenty thousand coming against him?
LUK 14:32 32 And if he didn’t think he could win, he would send a representative to discuss terms of peace while his enemy was still a long way off.
LUK 14:33 33 In the same way, none of you who are unwilling to give up all of your possessions can be my disciple.
LUK 14:34 34 “ Salt is good. But if salt loses its flavor, how will it become salty again?
LUK 14:35 35 It has no value, neither for the soil nor for the manure pile. People throw it away. Whoever has ears to hear should pay attention. ”

LUK 15:6 6 When he arrives home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, ‘Celebrate with me because I’ve found my lost sheep.’

LUK 19:2 2 A man there named Zacchaeus, a ruler among tax collectors, was rich.
LUK 19:3 3 He was trying to see who Jesus was, but, being a short man, he couldn’t because of the crowd.
LUK 19:4 4 So he ran ahead and climbed up a sycamore tree so he could see Jesus, who was about to pass that way.

LUK 19:7 7 Everyone who saw this grumbled, saying, “He has gone to be the guest of a sinner.”

LUK 19:13 13 He called together ten servants and gave each of them money worth four months’ wages. He said, ‘Do business with this until I return.’
LUK 19:14 14 His citizens hated him, so they sent a representative after him who said, ‘We don’t want this man to be our king.’
LUK 19:15 15 After receiving his kingdom, he returned and called the servants to whom he had given the money to find out how much they had earned.
LUK 19:16 16 The first servant came forward and said, ‘Your money has earned a return of one thousand percent.’
LUK 19:17 17 The king replied, ‘Excellent! You are a good servant. Because you have been faithful in a small matter, you will have authority over ten cities.’
LUK 19:18 18 “The second servant came and said, ‘Master, your money has made a return of five hundred percent.’
LUK 19:19 19 To this one, the king said, ‘You will have authority over five cities.’
LUK 19:20 20 “Another servant came and said, ‘Master, here is your money. I wrapped it up in a scarf for safekeeping.
LUK 19:21 21 I was afraid of you because you are a stern man. You withdraw what you haven’t deposited and you harvest what you haven’t planted.’
LUK 19:22 22 The king replied, ‘I will judge you by the words of your own mouth, you worthless servant! You knew, did you, that I’m a stern man, withdrawing what I didn’t deposit, and harvesting what I didn’t plant?
LUK 19:23 23 Why then didn’t you put my money in the bank? Then when I arrived, at least I could have gotten it back with interest.’
LUK 19:24 24 “ He said to his attendants, ‘Take his money and give it to the one who has ten times as much.’
LUK 19:25 25 ‘But Master,’ they said, ‘he already has ten times as much!’
LUK 19:26 26 He replied, ‘I say to you that everyone who has will be given more, but from those who have nothing, even what they have will be taken away.

LUK 19:28 28 After Jesus said this, he continued on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
LUK 19:29 29 As Jesus came to Bethphage and Bethany on the Mount of Olives, he gave two disciples a task.
LUK 19:30 30 He said, “ Go into the village over there. When you enter it, you will find tied up there a colt that no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
LUK 19:31 31 If anyone asks, ‘Why are you untying it?’ just say, ‘Its master needs it.’ ”

LUK 19:34 34 They replied, “Its master needs it.”

LUK 19:36 36 As Jesus rode along, they spread their clothes on the road.

LUK 19:38 38 They said, “Blessings on the king who comes in the name of the Lord. Peace in heaven and glory in the highest heavens.”

LUK 19:40 40 He answered, “ I tell you, if they were silent, the stones would shout. ”
LUK 19:41 41 As Jesus came to the city and observed it, he wept over it.
LUK 19:42 42 He said, “ If only you knew on this of all days the things that lead to peace. But now they are hidden from your eyes.
LUK 19:43 43 The time will come when your enemies will build fortifications around you, encircle you, and attack you from all sides.
LUK 19:44 44 They will crush you completely, you and the people within you. They won’t leave one stone on top of another within you, because you didn’t recognize the time of your gracious visit from God. ”

LUK 19:48 48 However, they couldn’t find a way to do it because all the people were enthralled with what they heard.
LUK 20:1 1 On one of the days when Jesus was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the good news, the chief priests, legal experts, and elders approached him.
LUK 20:2 2 They said, “Tell us: What kind of authority do you have for doing these things? Who gave you this authority?”
LUK 20:3 3 He replied, “ I have a question for you. Tell me:
LUK 20:4 4 Was John’s baptism of heavenly or of human origin? ”
LUK 20:5 5 They discussed among themselves, “If we say, ‘It’s of heavenly origin,’ he’ll say, ‘Why didn’t you believe him?’
LUK 20:6 6 But if we say, ‘It’s of human origin,’ all the people will stone us to death because they are convinced that John was a prophet.”
LUK 20:7 7 They answered that they didn’t know where it came from.
LUK 20:8 8 Then Jesus replied, “ Neither will I tell you what kind of authority I have to do these things. ”
LUK 20:9 9 Jesus told the people this parable: “ A certain man planted a vineyard, rented it to tenant farmers, and went on a trip for a long time.
LUK 20:10 10 When it was time, he sent a servant to collect from the tenants his share of the fruit of the vineyard. But the tenants sent him away, beaten and empty-handed.
LUK 20:11 11 The man sent another servant. But they beat him, treated him disgracefully, and sent him away empty-handed as well.
LUK 20:12 12 He sent a third servant. They wounded this servant and threw him out.
LUK 20:13 13 The owner of the vineyard said, ‘What should I do? I’ll send my son, whom I love dearly. Perhaps they will respect him.’
LUK 20:14 14 But when they saw him, they said to each other, ‘This is the heir. Let’s kill him so the inheritance will be ours.’
LUK 20:15 15 They threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
LUK 20:16 16 He will come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others. ” When the people heard this, they said, “May this never happen!”
LUK 20:17 17 Staring at them, Jesus said, “ Then what is the meaning of this text of scripture: The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone?
LUK 20:18 18 Everyone who falls on that stone will be crushed. And the stone will crush the person it falls on. ”
LUK 20:19 19 The legal experts and chief priests wanted to arrest him right then because they knew he had told this parable against them. But they feared the people.
LUK 20:20 20 The legal experts and chief priests were watching Jesus closely and sent spies who pretended to be sincere. They wanted to trap him in his words so they could hand him over to the jurisdiction and authority of the governor.
LUK 20:21 21 They asked him, “Teacher, we know that you are correct in what you say and teach. You don’t show favoritism but teach God’s way as it really is.
LUK 20:22 22 Does the Law allow people to pay taxes to Caesar or not?”
LUK 20:23 23 Since Jesus recognized their deception, he said to them,
LUK 20:24 24 “ Show me a coin. Whose image and inscription does it have on it? ” “Caesar’s,” they replied.
LUK 20:25 25 He said to them, “ Give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar and to God what belongs to God. ”
LUK 20:26 26 They couldn’t trap him in his words in front of the people. Astonished by his answer, they were speechless.
LUK 20:27 27 Some Sadducees, who deny that there’s a resurrection, came to Jesus and asked,
LUK 20:28 28 “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies leaving a widow but no children, the brother must marry the widow and raise up children for his brother .
LUK 20:29 29 Now there were seven brothers. The first man married a woman and then died childless.
LUK 20:30 30 The second
LUK 20:31 31 and then the third brother married her. Eventually all seven married her, and they all died without leaving any children.
LUK 20:32 32 Finally, the woman died too.
LUK 20:33 33 In the resurrection, whose wife will she be? All seven were married to her.”
LUK 20:34 34 Jesus said to them, “ People who belong to this age marry and are given in marriage.
LUK 20:35 35 But those who are considered worthy to participate in that age, that is, in the age of the resurrection from the dead, won’t marry nor will they be given in marriage.
LUK 20:36 36 They can no longer die, because they are like angels and are God’s children since they share in the resurrection.
LUK 20:37 37 Even Moses demonstrated that the dead are raised—in the passage about the burning bush, when he speaks of the Lord as the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob .
LUK 20:38 38 He isn’t the God of the dead but of the living. To him they are all alive. ”
LUK 20:39 39 Some of the legal experts responded, “Teacher, you have answered well.”
LUK 20:40 40 No one dared to ask him anything else.
LUK 20:41 41 Jesus said to them, “ Why do they say that the Christ is David’s son?
LUK 20:42 42 David himself says in the scroll of Psalms, The Lord said to my lord, ‘Sit at my right side
LUK 20:43 43 until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.’
LUK 20:44 44 Since David calls him ‘Lord,’ how can he be David’s son? ”
LUK 20:45 45 In the presence of all the people, Jesus said to his disciples,
LUK 20:46 46 “ Watch out for the legal experts. They like to walk around in long robes. They love being greeted with honor in the markets. They long for the places of honor in the synagogues and at banquets.
LUK 20:47 47 They are the ones who cheat widows out of their homes, and to show off they say long prayers. They will be judged most harshly. ”
LUK 21:1 1 Looking up, Jesus saw rich people throwing their gifts into the collection box for the temple treasury.

LUK 21:3 3 He said, “ I assure you that this poor widow has put in more than them all.
LUK 21:4 4 All of them are giving out of their spare change. But she from her hopeless poverty has given everything she had to live on. ”

LUK 21:17 17 Everyone will hate you because of my name.
LUK 21:18 18 Still, not a hair on your heads will be lost.
LUK 21:19 19 By holding fast, you will gain your lives.

LUK 21:30 30 When they sprout leaves, you can see for yourselves and know that summer is near.
LUK 21:31 31 In the same way, when you see these things happening, you know that God’s kingdom is near.
LUK 21:32 32 I assure you that this generation won’t pass away until everything has happened.
LUK 21:33 33 Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will certainly not pass away.
LUK 21:34 34 “ Take care that your hearts aren’t dulled by drinking parties, drunkenness, and the anxieties of day-to-day life. Don’t let that day fall upon you unexpectedly,
LUK 21:35 35 like a trap. It will come upon everyone who lives on the face of the whole earth.
LUK 21:36 36 Stay alert at all times, praying that you are strong enough to escape everything that is about to happen and to stand before the Human One. ”

LUK 23:48 49 And everyone who knew him, including the women who had followed him from Galilee, stood at a distance observing these things.
LUK 23:49 50 Now there was a man named Joseph who was a member of the council. He was a good and righteous man.
LUK 23:50 51 He hadn’t agreed with the plan and actions of the council. He was from the Jewish city of Arimathea and eagerly anticipated God’s kingdom.
LUK 23:51 52 This man went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body.
LUK 23:52 53 Taking it down, he wrapped it in a linen cloth and laid it in a tomb carved out of the rock, in which no one had ever been buried.
LUK 23:53 54 It was the Preparation Day for the Sabbath, and the Sabbath was quickly approaching.
LUK 23:54 55 The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed Joseph. They saw the tomb and how Jesus’ body was laid in it,
LUK 23:55 56 then they went away and prepared fragrant spices and perfumed oils. They rested on the Sabbath, in keeping with the commandment.
LUK 24:1 1 Very early in the morning on the first day of the week, the women went to the tomb, bringing the fragrant spices they had prepared.
LUK 24:2 2 They found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
LUK 24:3 3 but when they went in, they didn’t find the body of the Lord Jesus.
LUK 24:4 4 They didn’t know what to make of this. Suddenly, two men were standing beside them in gleaming bright clothing.
LUK 24:5 5 The women were frightened and bowed their faces toward the ground, but the men said to them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?
LUK 24:6 6 He isn’t here, but has been raised. Remember what he told you while he was still in Galilee,
LUK 24:7 7 that the Human One must be handed over to sinners, be crucified, and on the third day rise again.”
LUK 24:8 8 Then they remembered his words.
LUK 24:9 9 When they returned from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and all the others.
LUK 24:10 10 It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told these things to the apostles.
LUK 24:11 11 Their words struck the apostles as nonsense, and they didn’t believe the women.
LUK 24:12 12 But Peter ran to the tomb. When he bent over to look inside, he saw only the linen cloth. Then he returned home, wondering what had happened.
LUK 24:13 13 On that same day, two disciples were traveling to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.
LUK 24:14 14 They were talking to each other about everything that had happened.
LUK 24:15 15 While they were discussing these things, Jesus himself arrived and joined them on their journey.
LUK 24:16 16 They were prevented from recognizing him.
LUK 24:17 17 He said to them, “ What are you talking about as you walk along? ” They stopped, their faces downcast.
LUK 24:18 18 The one named Cleopas replied, “Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who is unaware of the things that have taken place there over the last few days?”
LUK 24:19 19 He said to them, “ What things? ” They said to him, “The things about Jesus of Nazareth. Because of his powerful deeds and words, he was recognized by God and all the people as a prophet.
LUK 24:20 20 But our chief priests and our leaders handed him over to be sentenced to death, and they crucified him.
LUK 24:21 21 We had hoped he was the one who would redeem Israel. All these things happened three days ago.
LUK 24:22 22 But there’s more: Some women from our group have left us stunned. They went to the tomb early this morning
LUK 24:23 23 and didn’t find his body. They came to us saying that they had even seen a vision of angels who told them he is alive.
LUK 24:24 24 Some of those who were with us went to the tomb and found things just as the women said. They didn’t see him.”
LUK 24:25 25 Then Jesus said to them, “ You foolish people! Your dull minds keep you from believing all that the prophets talked about.
LUK 24:26 26 Wasn’t it necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and then enter into his glory? ”
LUK 24:27 27 Then he interpreted for them the things written about himself in all the scriptures, starting with Moses and going through all the Prophets.
LUK 24:28 28 When they came to Emmaus, he acted as if he was going on ahead.
LUK 24:29 29 But they urged him, saying, “Stay with us. It’s nearly evening, and the day is almost over.” So he went in to stay with them.
LUK 24:30 30 After he took his seat at the table with them, he took the bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them.
LUK 24:31 31 Their eyes were opened and they recognized him, but he disappeared from their sight.
LUK 24:32 32 They said to each other, “Weren’t our hearts on fire when he spoke to us along the road and when he explained the scriptures for us?”
LUK 24:33 33 They got up right then and returned to Jerusalem. They found the eleven and their companions gathered together.
LUK 24:34 34 They were saying to each other, “The Lord really has risen! He appeared to Simon!”
LUK 24:35 35 Then the two disciples described what had happened along the road and how Jesus was made known to them as he broke the bread.
LUK 24:36 36 While they were saying these things, Jesus himself stood among them and said, “ Peace be with you! ”
LUK 24:37 37 They were terrified and afraid. They thought they were seeing a ghost.
LUK 24:38 38 He said to them, “ Why are you startled? Why are doubts arising in your hearts?
LUK 24:39 39 Look at my hands and my feet. It’s really me! Touch me and see, for a ghost doesn’t have flesh and bones like you see I have. ”
LUK 24:40 40 As he said this, he showed them his hands and feet.
LUK 24:41 41 Because they were wondering and questioning in the midst of their happiness, he said to them, “ Do you have anything to eat? ”
LUK 24:42 42 They gave him a piece of baked fish.
LUK 24:43 43 Taking it, he ate it in front of them.
LUK 24:44 44 Jesus said to them, “ These are my words that I spoke to you while I was still with you—that everything written about me in the Law from Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled. ”
LUK 24:45 45 Then he opened their minds to understand the scriptures.
LUK 24:46 46 He said to them, “ This is what is written: the Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
LUK 24:47 47 and a change of heart and life for the forgiveness of sins must be preached in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
LUK 24:48 48 You are witnesses of these things.
LUK 24:49 49 Look, I’m sending to you what my Father promised, but you are to stay in the city until you have been furnished with heavenly power. ”
LUK 24:50 50 He led them out as far as Bethany, where he lifted his hands and blessed them.
LUK 24:51 51 As he blessed them, he left them and was taken up to heaven.
LUK 24:52 52 They worshipped him and returned to Jerusalem overwhelmed with joy.
LUK 24:53 53 And they were continuously in the temple praising God.
JHN 1:1 1 In the beginning was the Word and the Word was with God and the Word was God.
JHN 1:2 2 The Word was with God in the beginning.
JHN 1:3 3 Everything came into being through the Word, and without the Word nothing came into being. What came into being
JHN 1:4 4 through the Word was life, and the life was the light for all people.
JHN 1:5 5 The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness doesn’t extinguish the light.
JHN 1:6 6 A man named John was sent from God.
JHN 1:7 7 He came as a witness to testify concerning the light, so that through him everyone would believe in the light.
JHN 1:8 8 He himself wasn’t the light, but his mission was to testify concerning the light.
JHN 1:9 9 The true light that shines on all people was coming into the world.
JHN 1:10 10 The light was in the world, and the world came into being through the light, but the world didn’t recognize the light.
JHN 1:11 11 The light came to his own people, and his own people didn’t welcome him.
JHN 1:12 12 But those who did welcome him, those who believed in his name, he authorized to become God’s children,
JHN 1:13 13 born not from blood nor from human desire or passion, but born from God.
JHN 1:14 14 The Word became flesh and made his home among us. We have seen his glory, glory like that of a father’s only son, full of grace and truth.
JHN 1:15 15 John testified about him, crying out, “This is the one of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me is greater than me because he existed before me.’”
JHN 1:16 16 From his fullness we have all received grace upon grace;
JHN 1:17 17 as the Law was given through Moses, so grace and truth came into being through Jesus Christ.
JHN 1:18 18 No one has ever seen God. God the only Son, who is at the Father’s side, has made God known.
JHN 1:19 19 This is John’s testimony when the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, “Who are you?”
JHN 1:20 20 John confessed (he didn’t deny but confessed), “I’m not the Christ.”
JHN 1:21 21 They asked him, “Then who are you? Are you Elijah?” John said, “I’m not.” “Are you the prophet?” John answered, “No.”
JHN 1:22 22 They asked, “Who are you? We need to give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
JHN 1:23 23 John replied, “ I am a voice crying out in the wilderness, Make the Lord’s path straight, just as the prophet Isaiah said.”
JHN 1:24 24 Those sent by the Pharisees
JHN 1:25 25 asked, “Why do you baptize if you aren’t the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the prophet?”
JHN 1:26 26 John answered, “I baptize with water. Someone greater stands among you, whom you don’t recognize.
JHN 1:27 27 He comes after me, but I’m not worthy to untie his sandal straps.”
JHN 1:28 28 This encounter took place across the Jordan in Bethany where John was baptizing.
JHN 1:29 29 The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look! The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
JHN 1:30 30 This is the one about whom I said, ‘He who comes after me is really greater than me because he existed before me.’
JHN 1:31 31 Even I didn’t recognize him, but I came baptizing with water so that he might be made known to Israel.”
JHN 1:32 32 John testified, “I saw the Spirit coming down from heaven like a dove, and it rested on him.
JHN 1:33 33 Even I didn’t recognize him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water said to me, ‘The one on whom you see the Spirit coming down and resting is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.’
JHN 1:34 34 I have seen and testified that this one is God’s Son.”
JHN 1:35 35 The next day John was standing again with two of his disciples.
JHN 1:36 36 When he saw Jesus walking along he said, “Look! The Lamb of God!”
JHN 1:37 37 The two disciples heard what he said, and they followed Jesus.
JHN 1:38 38 When Jesus turned and saw them following, he asked, “ What are you looking for? ” They said, “Rabbi (which is translated Teacher ), where are you staying?”
JHN 1:39 39 He replied, “ Come and see. ” So they went and saw where he was staying, and they remained with him that day. It was about four o’clock in the afternoon.
JHN 1:40 40 One of the two disciples who heard what John said and followed Jesus was Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter.
JHN 1:41 41 He first found his own brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated Christ ).
JHN 1:42 42 He led him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “ You are Simon, son of John. You will be called Cephas ” (which is translated Peter ).
JHN 1:43 43 The next day Jesus wanted to go into Galilee, and he found Philip. Jesus said to him, “ Follow me. ”
JHN 1:44 44 Philip was from Bethsaida, the hometown of Andrew and Peter.
JHN 1:45 45 Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found the one Moses wrote about in the Law and the Prophets: Jesus, Joseph’s son, from Nazareth.”
JHN 1:46 46 Nathanael responded, “Can anything from Nazareth be good?” Philip said, “Come and see.”
JHN 1:47 47 Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said about him, “ Here is a genuine Israelite in whom there is no deceit. ”
JHN 1:48 48 Nathanael asked him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered, “ Before Philip called you, I saw you under the fig tree. ”
JHN 1:49 49 Nathanael replied, “Rabbi, you are God’s Son. You are the king of Israel.”
JHN 1:50 50 Jesus answered, “ Do you believe because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree? You will see greater things than these!
JHN 1:51 51 I assure you that you will see heaven open and God’s angels going up to heaven and down to earth on the Human One. ”
JHN 2:1 1 On the third day there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there, and
JHN 2:2 2 Jesus and his disciples were also invited to the celebration.
JHN 2:3 3 When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They don’t have any wine.”
JHN 2:4 4 Jesus replied, “ Woman, what does that have to do with me? My time hasn’t come yet. ”
JHN 2:5 5 His mother told the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
JHN 2:6 6 Nearby were six stone water jars used for the Jewish cleansing ritual, each able to hold about twenty or thirty gallons.
JHN 2:7 7 Jesus said to the servants, “ Fill the jars with water, ” and they filled them to the brim.
JHN 2:8 8 Then he told them, “ Now draw some from them and take it to the headwaiter, ” and they did.
JHN 2:9 9 The headwaiter tasted the water that had become wine. He didn’t know where it came from, though the servants who had drawn the water knew. The headwaiter called the groom
JHN 2:10 10 and said, “Everyone serves the good wine first. They bring out the second-rate wine only when the guests are drinking freely. You kept the good wine until now.”
JHN 2:11 11 This was the first miraculous sign that Jesus did in Cana of Galilee. He revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
JHN 2:12 12 After this, Jesus and his mother, his brothers, and his disciples went down to Capernaum and stayed there for a few days.
JHN 2:13 13 It was nearly time for the Jewish Passover, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
JHN 2:14 14 He found in the temple those who were selling cattle, sheep, and doves, as well as those involved in exchanging currency sitting there.
JHN 2:15 15 He made a whip from ropes and chased them all out of the temple, including the cattle and the sheep. He scattered the coins and overturned the tables of those who exchanged currency.
JHN 2:16 16 He said to the dove sellers, “ Get these things out of here! Don’t make my Father’s house a place of business. ”
JHN 2:17 17 His disciples remembered that it is written, Passion for your house consumes me.
JHN 2:18 18 Then the Jewish leaders asked him, “By what authority are you doing these things? What miraculous sign will you show us?”
JHN 2:19 19 Jesus answered, “ Destroy this temple and in three days I’ll raise it up. ”
JHN 2:20 20 The Jewish leaders replied, “It took forty-six years to build this temple, and you will raise it up in three days?”
JHN 2:21 21 But the temple Jesus was talking about was his body.
JHN 2:22 22 After he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered what he had said, and they believed the scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.
JHN 2:23 23 While Jesus was in Jerusalem for the Passover Festival, many believed in his name because they saw the miraculous signs that he did.
JHN 2:24 24 But Jesus didn’t trust himself to them because he knew all people.
JHN 2:25 25 He didn’t need anyone to tell him about human nature, for he knew what human nature was.
JHN 3:1 1 There was a Pharisee named Nicodemus, a Jewish leader.
JHN 3:2 2 He came to Jesus at night and said to him, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God, for no one could do these miraculous signs that you do unless God is with him.”
JHN 3:3 3 Jesus answered, “ I assure you, unless someone is born anew, it’s not possible to see God’s kingdom. ”
JHN 3:4 4 Nicodemus asked, “How is it possible for an adult to be born? It’s impossible to enter the mother’s womb for a second time and be born, isn’t it?”
JHN 3:5 5 Jesus answered, “ I assure you, unless someone is born of water and the Spirit, it’s not possible to enter God’s kingdom.
JHN 3:6 6 Whatever is born of the flesh is flesh, and whatever is born of the Spirit is spirit.
JHN 3:7 7 Don’t be surprised that I said to you, ‘You must be born anew.’
JHN 3:8 8 God’s Spirit blows wherever it wishes. You hear its sound, but you don’t know where it comes from or where it is going. It’s the same with everyone who is born of the Spirit. ”
JHN 3:9 9 Nicodemus said, “How are these things possible?”
JHN 3:10 10 “Jesus answered, “You are a teacher of Israel and you don’t know these things?
JHN 3:11 11 I assure you that we speak about what we know and testify about what we have seen, but you don’t receive our testimony.
JHN 3:12 12 If I have told you about earthly things and you don’t believe, how will you believe if I tell you about heavenly things?
JHN 3:13 13 No one has gone up to heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Human One.
JHN 3:14 14 Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so must the Human One be lifted up
JHN 3:15 15 so that everyone who believes in him will have eternal life.
JHN 3:16 16 God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him won’t perish but will have eternal life.
JHN 3:17 17 God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world might be saved through him.
JHN 3:18 18 Whoever believes in him isn’t judged; whoever doesn’t believe in him is already judged, because they don’t believe in the name of God’s only Son.
JHN 3:19 19 “ This is the basis for judgment: The light came into the world, and people loved darkness more than the light, for their actions are evil.
JHN 3:20 20 All who do wicked things hate the light and don’t come to the light for fear that their actions will be exposed to the light.
JHN 3:21 21 Whoever does the truth comes to the light so that it can be seen that their actions were done in God. ”
JHN 3:22 22 After this Jesus and his disciples went into Judea, where he spent some time with them and was baptizing.
JHN 3:23 23 John was baptizing at Aenon near Salem because there was a lot of water there, and people were coming to him and being baptized. (
JHN 3:24 24 John hadn’t yet been thrown into prison.)
JHN 3:25 25 A debate started between John’s disciples and a certain Jew about cleansing rituals.
JHN 3:26 26 They came to John and said, “Rabbi, look! The man who was with you across the Jordan, the one about whom you testified, is baptizing and everyone is flocking to him.”
JHN 3:27 27 John replied, “No one can receive anything unless it is given from heaven.
JHN 3:28 28 You yourselves can testify that I said that I’m not the Christ but that I’m the one sent before him.
JHN 3:29 29 The groom is the one who is getting married. The friend of the groom stands close by and, when he hears him, is overjoyed at the groom’s voice. Therefore, my joy is now complete.
JHN 3:30 30 He must increase and I must decrease.
JHN 3:31 31 The one who comes from above is above all things. The one who is from the earth belongs to the earth and speaks as one from the earth. The one who comes from heaven is above all things.
JHN 3:32 32 He testifies to what he has seen and heard, but no one accepts his testimony.
JHN 3:33 33 Whoever accepts his testimony confirms that God is true.
JHN 3:34 34 The one whom God sent speaks God’s words because God gives the Spirit generously.
JHN 3:35 35 The Father loves the Son and gives everything into his hands.
JHN 3:36 36 Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. Whoever doesn’t believe in the Son won’t see life, but the angry judgment of God remains on them.”
JHN 4:1 1 Jesus learned that the Pharisees had heard that he was making more disciples and baptizing more than John (
JHN 4:2 2 although Jesus’ disciples were baptizing, not Jesus himself).
JHN 4:3 3 Therefore, he left Judea and went back to Galilee.
JHN 4:4 4 Jesus had to go through Samaria.
JHN 4:5 5 He came to a Samaritan city called Sychar, which was near the land Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
JHN 4:6 6 Jacob’s well was there. Jesus was tired from his journey, so he sat down at the well. It was about noon.
JHN 4:7 7 A Samaritan woman came to the well to draw water. Jesus said to her, “ Give me some water to drink. ”
JHN 4:8 8 His disciples had gone into the city to buy him some food.
JHN 4:9 9 The Samaritan woman asked, “Why do you, a Jewish man, ask for something to drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (Jews and Samaritans didn’t associate with each other.)
JHN 4:10 10 Jesus responded, “ If you recognized God’s gift and who is saying to you, ‘Give me some water to drink,’ you would be asking him and he would give you living water. ”
JHN 4:11 11 The woman said to him, “Sir, you don’t have a bucket and the well is deep. Where would you get this living water?
JHN 4:12 12 You aren’t greater than our father Jacob, are you? He gave this well to us, and he drank from it himself, as did his sons and his livestock.”
JHN 4:13 13 Jesus answered, “ Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again,
JHN 4:14 14 but whoever drinks from the water that I will give will never be thirsty again. The water that I give will become in those who drink it a spring of water that bubbles up into eternal life. ”
JHN 4:15 15 The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water, so that I will never be thirsty and will never need to come here to draw water!”
JHN 4:16 16 Jesus said to her, “ Go, get your husband, and come back here. ”
JHN 4:17 17 The woman replied, “I don’t have a husband.” “ You are right to say, ‘I don’t have a husband,’ ” Jesus answered.
JHN 4:18 18 “ You’ve had five husbands, and the man you are with now isn’t your husband. You’ve spoken the truth. ”
JHN 4:19 19 The woman said, “Sir, I see that you are a prophet.
JHN 4:20 20 Our ancestors worshipped on this mountain, but you and your people say that it is necessary to worship in Jerusalem.”
