JHN 4:23 23 But the time is coming—and is here!—when true worshippers will worship in spirit and truth. The Father looks for those who worship him this way.
JHN 4:24 24 God is spirit, and it is necessary to worship God in spirit and truth. ”
JHN 4:25 25 The woman said, “I know that the Messiah is coming, the one who is called the Christ. When he comes, he will teach everything to us.”
JHN 4:26 26 Jesus said to her, “ I Am—the one who speaks with you. ”
JHN 4:27 27 Just then, Jesus’ disciples arrived and were shocked that he was talking with a woman. But no one asked, “What do you want?” or “Why are you talking with her?”
JHN 4:28 28 The woman put down her water jar and went into the city. She said to the people,
JHN 4:29 29 “Come and see a man who has told me everything I’ve done! Could this man be the Christ?”
JHN 4:30 30 They left the city and were on their way to see Jesus.
JHN 4:31 31 In the meantime the disciples spoke to Jesus, saying, “Rabbi, eat.”
JHN 4:32 32 Jesus said to them, “ I have food to eat that you don’t know about. ”
JHN 4:33 33 The disciples asked each other, “Has someone brought him food?”
JHN 4:34 34 Jesus said to them, “ I am fed by doing the will of the one who sent me and by completing his work.
JHN 4:35 35 Don’t you have a saying, ‘Four more months and then it’s time for harvest’? Look, I tell you: open your eyes and notice that the fields are already ripe for the harvest.
JHN 4:36 36 Those who harvest are receiving their pay and gathering fruit for eternal life so that those who sow and those who harvest can celebrate together.
JHN 4:37 37 This is a true saying, that one sows and another harvests.
JHN 4:38 38 I have sent you to harvest what you didn’t work hard for; others worked hard, and you will share in their hard work. ”
JHN 4:39 39 Many Samaritans in that city believed in Jesus because of the woman’s word when she testified, “He told me everything I’ve ever done.”
JHN 4:40 40 So when the Samaritans came to Jesus, they asked him to stay with them, and he stayed there two days.
JHN 4:41 41 Many more believed because of his word,
JHN 4:42 42 and they said to the woman, “We no longer believe because of what you said, for we have heard for ourselves and know that this one is truly the savior of the world.”
JHN 4:43 43 After two days Jesus left for Galilee. (
JHN 4:44 44 Jesus himself had testified that prophets have no honor in their own country.)
JHN 4:45 45 When he came to Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him because they had seen all the things he had done in Jerusalem during the festival, for they also had been at the festival.
JHN 4:46 46 He returned to Cana in Galilee where he had turned the water into wine. In Capernaum there was a certain royal official whose son was sick.
JHN 4:47 47 When he heard that Jesus was coming from Judea to Galilee, he went out to meet him and asked Jesus if he would come and heal his son, for his son was about to die.
JHN 4:48 48 Jesus said to him, “ Unless you see miraculous signs and wonders, you won’t believe. ”
JHN 4:49 49 The royal official said to him, “Lord, come before my son dies.”
JHN 4:50 50 Jesus replied, “ Go home. Your son lives. ” The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and set out for his home.
JHN 4:51 51 While he was on his way, his servants were already coming to meet him. They said, “Your son lives!”
JHN 4:52 52 So he asked them at what time his son had started to get better. And they said, “The fever left him yesterday at about one o’clock in the afternoon.”
JHN 4:53 53 Then the father realized that this was the hour when Jesus had said to him, “ Your son lives. ” And he and his entire household believed in Jesus.
JHN 4:54 54 This was the second miraculous sign Jesus did while going from Judea to Galilee.
JHN 5:1 1 After this there was a Jewish festival, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
JHN 5:2 2 In Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate in the north city wall is a pool with the Aramaic name Bethsaida. It had five covered porches,
JHN 5:3 3 and a crowd of people who were sick, blind, lame, and paralyzed sat there.
JHN 5:4 5 A certain man was there who had been sick for thirty-eight years.
JHN 5:5 6 When Jesus saw him lying there, knowing that he had already been there a long time, he asked him, “ Do you want to get well? ”
JHN 5:6 7 The sick man answered him, “Sir, I don’t have anyone who can put me in the water when it is stirred up. When I’m trying to get to it, someone else has gotten in ahead of me.”
JHN 5:7 8 Jesus said to him, “ Get up! Pick up your mat and walk. ”
JHN 5:8 9 Immediately the man was well, and he picked up his mat and walked. Now that day was the Sabbath.
JHN 5:9 10 The Jewish leaders said to the man who had been healed, “It’s the Sabbath; you aren’t allowed to carry your mat.”
JHN 5:10 11 He answered, “The man who made me well said to me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’”
JHN 5:11 12 They inquired, “Who is this man who said to you, ‘Pick it up and walk’?”
JHN 5:12 13 The man who had been cured didn’t know who it was, because Jesus had slipped away from the crowd gathered there.
JHN 5:13 14 Later Jesus found him in the temple and said, “See! You have been made well. Don’t sin anymore in case something worse happens to you.”
JHN 5:14 15 The man went and proclaimed to the Jewish leaders that Jesus was the man who had made him well.
JHN 5:15 16 As a result, the Jewish leaders were harassing Jesus, since he had done these things on the Sabbath.
JHN 5:16 17 Jesus replied, “ My Father is still working, and I am working too. ”
JHN 5:17 18 For this reason the Jewish leaders wanted even more to kill him—not only because he was doing away with the Sabbath but also because he called God his own Father, thereby making himself equal with God.
JHN 5:18 19 Jesus responded to the Jewish leaders, “I assure you that the Son can’t do anything by himself except what he sees the Father doing. Whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.
JHN 5:19 20 The Father loves the Son and shows him everything that he does. He will show him greater works than these so that you will marvel.
JHN 5:20 21 As the Father raises the dead and gives life, so too does the Son give life to whomever he wishes.
JHN 5:21 22 The Father doesn’t judge anyone, but he has given all judgment to the Son
JHN 5:22 23 so that everyone will honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever doesn’t honor the Son doesn’t honor the Father who sent him.
JHN 5:23 24 “I assure you that whoever hears my word and believes in the one who sent me has eternal life and won’t come under judgment but has passed from death into life.
JHN 5:24 25 “I assure you that the time is coming—and is here!—when the dead will hear the voice of God’s Son, and those who hear it will live.
JHN 5:25 26 Just as the Father has life in himself, so he has granted the Son to have life in himself.
JHN 5:26 27 He gives the Son authority to judge, because he is the Human One.
JHN 5:27 28 Don’t be surprised by this, because the time is coming when all who are in their graves will hear his voice.
JHN 5:28 29 Those who did good things will come out into the resurrection of life, and those who did wicked things into the resurrection of judgment.
JHN 5:29 30 I can’t do anything by myself. Whatever I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just. I don’t seek my own will but the will of the one who sent me.
JHN 5:30 31 “If I testify about myself, my testimony isn’t true.
JHN 5:31 32 There is someone else who testifies about me, and I know his testimony about me is true.
JHN 5:32 33 You sent a delegation to John, and he testified to the truth.
JHN 5:33 34 Although I don’t accept human testimony, I say these things so that you can be saved.
JHN 5:34 35 John was a burning and shining lamp, and, at least for a while, you were willing to celebrate in his light.
JHN 5:35 36 “I have a witness greater than John’s testimony. The Father has given me works to do so that I might complete them. These works I do testify about me that the Father sent me.
JHN 5:36 37 And the Father who sent me testifies about me. You have never even heard his voice or seen his form,
JHN 5:37 38 and you don’t have his word dwelling with you because you don’t believe the one whom he has sent.
JHN 5:38 39 Examine the scriptures, since you think that in them you have eternal life. They also testify about me,
JHN 5:39 40 yet you don’t want to come to me so that you can have life.
JHN 5:40 41 “I don’t accept praise from people,
JHN 5:41 42 but I know you, that you don’t have God’s love in you.
JHN 5:42 43 I have come in my Father’s name, and you don’t receive me. If others come in their own name, you receive them.
JHN 5:43 44 How can you believe when you receive praise from each other but don’t seek the praise that comes from the only God?
JHN 5:44 45 “ Don’t think that I will accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses, the one in whom your hope rests.
JHN 5:45 46 If you believed Moses, you would believe me, because Moses wrote about me.
JHN 5:46 47 If you don’t believe the writings of Moses, how will you believe my words? ”
JHN 6:1 1 After this Jesus went across the Galilee Sea (that is, the Tiberias Sea).
JHN 6:2 2 A large crowd followed him, because they had seen the miraculous signs he had done among the sick.
JHN 6:3 3 Jesus went up a mountain and sat there with his disciples.
JHN 6:4 4 It was nearly time for Passover, the Jewish festival.
JHN 6:5 5 Jesus looked up and saw the large crowd coming toward him. He asked Philip, “ Where will we buy food to feed these people? ”
JHN 6:6 6 Jesus said this to test him, for he already knew what he was going to do.
JHN 6:7 7 Philip replied, “More than a half year’s salary worth of food wouldn’t be enough for each person to have even a little bit.”
JHN 6:8 8 One of his disciples, Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, said,
JHN 6:9 9 “A youth here has five barley loaves and two fish. But what good is that for a crowd like this?”
JHN 6:10 10 Jesus said, “Have the people sit down.” There was plenty of grass there. They sat down, about five thousand of them.
JHN 6:11 11 Then Jesus took the bread. When he had given thanks, he distributed it to those who were sitting there. He did the same with the fish, each getting as much as they wanted.
JHN 6:12 12 When they had plenty to eat, he said to his disciples, “ Gather up the leftover pieces, so that nothing will be wasted. ”
JHN 6:13 13 So they gathered them and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves that had been left over by those who had eaten.
JHN 6:14 14 When the people saw that he had done a miraculous sign, they said, “This is truly the prophet who is coming into the world.”
JHN 6:15 15 Jesus understood that they were about to come and force him to be their king, so he took refuge again, alone on a mountain.
JHN 6:16 16 When evening came, Jesus’ disciples went down to the lake.
JHN 6:17 17 They got into a boat and were crossing the lake to Capernaum. It was already getting dark and Jesus hadn’t come to them yet.
JHN 6:18 18 The water was getting rough because a strong wind was blowing.
JHN 6:19 19 When the wind had driven them out for about three or four miles, they saw Jesus walking on the water. He was approaching the boat and they were afraid.
JHN 6:20 20 He said to them, “I Am. Don’t be afraid.”
JHN 6:21 21 Then they wanted to take him into the boat, and just then the boat reached the land where they had been heading.
JHN 6:22 22 The next day the crowd that remained on the other side of the lake realized that only one boat had been there. They knew Jesus hadn’t gone with his disciples, but that the disciples had gone alone.
JHN 6:23 23 Some boats came from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread over which the Lord had given thanks.
JHN 6:24 24 When the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor his disciples were there, they got into the boats and came to Capernaum looking for Jesus.
JHN 6:25 25 When they found him on the other side of the lake, they asked him, “Rabbi, when did you get here?”
JHN 6:26 26 Jesus replied, “ I assure you that you are looking for me not because you saw miraculous signs but because you ate all the food you wanted.
JHN 6:27 27 Don’t work for the food that doesn’t last but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Human One will give you. God the Father has confirmed him as his agent to give life. ”
JHN 6:28 28 They asked, “What must we do in order to accomplish what God requires?”
JHN 6:29 29 Jesus replied, “ This is what God requires, that you believe in him whom God sent. ”
JHN 6:30 30 They asked, “What miraculous sign will you do, that we can see and believe you? What will you do?
JHN 6:31 31 Our ancestors ate manna in the wilderness, just as it is written, He gave them bread from heaven to eat .”
JHN 6:32 32 Jesus told them, “ I assure you, it wasn’t Moses who gave the bread from heaven to you, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.
JHN 6:33 33 The bread of God is the one who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world. ”
JHN 6:34 34 They said, “Sir, give us this bread all the time!”
JHN 6:35 35 Jesus replied, “ I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never go hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
JHN 6:36 36 But I told you that you have seen me and still don’t believe.
JHN 6:37 37 Everyone whom the Father gives to me will come to me, and I won’t send away anyone who comes to me.
JHN 6:38 38 I have come down from heaven not to do my will, but the will of him who sent me.
JHN 6:39 39 This is the will of the one who sent me, that I won’t lose anything he has given me, but I will raise it up at the last day.
JHN 6:40 40 This is my Father’s will: that all who see the Son and believe in him will have eternal life, and I will raise them up at the last day. ”
JHN 6:41 41 The Jewish opposition grumbled about him because he said, “ I am the bread that came down from heaven. ”
JHN 6:42 42 They asked, “Isn’t this Jesus, Joseph’s son, whose mother and father we know? How can he now say, ‘I have come down from heaven’?”
JHN 6:43 43 Jesus responded, “ Don’t grumble among yourselves.
JHN 6:44 44 No one can come to me unless they are drawn to me by the Father who sent me, and I will raise them up at the last day.
JHN 6:45 45 It is written in the Prophets, And they will all be taught by God. Everyone who has listened to the Father and learned from him comes to me.
JHN 6:46 46 No one has seen the Father except the one who is from God. He has seen the Father.
JHN 6:47 47 I assure you, whoever believes has eternal life.
JHN 6:48 48 I am the bread of life.
JHN 6:49 49 Your ancestors ate manna in the wilderness and they died.
JHN 6:50 50 This is the bread that comes down from heaven so that whoever eats from it will never die.
JHN 6:51 51 I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats this bread will live forever, and the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh. ”
JHN 6:52 52 Then the Jews debated among themselves, asking, “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”
JHN 6:53 53 Jesus said to them, “ I assure you, unless you eat the flesh of the Human One and drink his blood, you have no life in you.
JHN 6:54 54 Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise them up at the last day.
JHN 6:55 55 My flesh is true food and my blood is true drink.
JHN 6:56 56 Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me and I in them.
JHN 6:57 57 As the living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father, so whoever eats me lives because of me.
JHN 6:58 58 This is the bread that came down from heaven. It isn’t like the bread your ancestors ate, and then they died. Whoever eats this bread will live forever. ”
JHN 6:59 59 Jesus said these things while he was teaching in the synagogue in Capernaum.
JHN 6:60 60 Many of his disciples who heard this said, “This message is harsh. Who can hear it?”
JHN 6:61 61 Jesus knew that the disciples were grumbling about this and he said to them, “ Does this offend you?
JHN 6:62 62 What if you were to see the Human One going up where he was before?
JHN 6:63 63 The Spirit is the one who gives life and the flesh doesn’t help at all. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and life.
JHN 6:64 64 Yet some of you don’t believe. ” Jesus knew from the beginning who wouldn’t believe and the one who would betray him.
JHN 6:65 65 He said, “ For this reason I said to you that none can come to me unless the Father enables them to do so. ”
JHN 6:66 66 At this, many of his disciples turned away and no longer accompanied him.
JHN 6:67 67 Jesus asked the Twelve, “ Do you also want to leave? ”
JHN 6:68 68 Simon Peter answered, “Lord, where would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
JHN 6:69 69 We believe and know that you are God’s holy one.”
JHN 6:70 70 Jesus replied, “ Didn’t I choose you twelve? Yet one of you is a devil. ”
JHN 6:71 71 He was speaking of Judas, Simon Iscariot’s son, for he, one of the Twelve, was going to betray him.
JHN 7:1 1 After this Jesus traveled throughout Galilee. He didn’t want to travel in Judea, because the Jewish authorities wanted to kill him.
JHN 7:2 2 When it was almost time for the Jewish Festival of Booths,
JHN 7:3 3 Jesus’ brothers said to him, “Leave Galilee. Go to Judea so that your disciples can see the amazing works that you do.
JHN 7:4 4 Those who want to be known publicly don’t do things secretly. Since you can do these things, show yourself to the world.”
JHN 7:5 5 His brothers said this because even they didn’t believe in him.
JHN 7:6 6 Jesus replied, “ For you, anytime is fine. But my time hasn’t come yet.
JHN 7:7 7 The world can’t hate you. It hates me, though, because I testify that its works are evil.
JHN 7:8 8 You go up to the festival. I’m not going to this one because my time hasn’t yet come. ”
JHN 7:9 9 Having said this, he stayed in Galilee.
JHN 7:10 10 However, after his brothers left for the festival, he went too—not openly but in secret.
JHN 7:11 11 The Jewish leaders were looking for Jesus at the festival. They kept asking, “Where is he?”
JHN 7:12 12 The crowds were murmuring about him. “He’s a good man,” some said, but others were saying, “No, he tricks the people.”
JHN 7:13 13 No one spoke about him publicly, though, for fear of the Jewish authorities.
JHN 7:14 14 Halfway through the festival, Jesus went up to the temple and started to teach.
JHN 7:15 15 Astonished, the Jewish leaders asked, “He’s never been taught! How has he mastered the Law?”
JHN 7:16 16 Jesus responded, “ My teaching isn’t mine but comes from the one who sent me.
JHN 7:17 17 Whoever wants to do God’s will can tell whether my teaching is from God or whether I speak on my own.
JHN 7:18 18 Those who speak on their own seek glory for themselves. Those who seek the glory of him who sent me are people of truth; there’s no falsehood in them.
JHN 7:19 19 Didn’t Moses give you the Law? Yet none of you keep the Law. Why do you want to kill me? ”
JHN 7:20 20 The crowd answered, “You have a demon. Who wants to kill you?”
JHN 7:21 21 Jesus replied, “ I did one work, and you were all astonished.
JHN 7:22 22 Because Moses gave you the commandment about circumcision (although it wasn’t Moses but the patriarchs), you circumcise a man on the Sabbath.
JHN 7:23 23 If a man can be circumcised on the Sabbath without breaking Moses’ Law, why are you angry with me because I made an entire man well on the Sabbath?
JHN 7:24 24 Don’t judge according to appearances. Judge with right judgment. ”
JHN 7:25 25 Some people from Jerusalem said, “Isn’t he the one they want to kill?
JHN 7:26 26 Here he is, speaking in public, yet they aren’t saying anything to him. Could it be that our leaders actually think he is the Christ?
JHN 7:27 27 We know where he is from, but when the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from.”
JHN 7:28 28 While Jesus was teaching in the temple, he exclaimed, “ You know me and where I am from. I haven’t come on my own. The one who sent me is true, and you don’t know him.
JHN 7:29 29 I know him because I am from him and he sent me. ”
JHN 7:30 30 So they wanted to seize Jesus, but they couldn’t because his time hadn’t yet come.
JHN 7:31 31 Many from that crowd believed in Jesus. They said, “When the Christ comes, will he do more miraculous signs than this man does?”
JHN 7:32 32 The Pharisees heard the crowd whispering such things about Jesus, and the chief priests and Pharisees sent guards to arrest him.
JHN 7:33 33 Therefore, Jesus said, “ I’m still with you for a little while before I go to the one who sent me.
JHN 7:34 34 You will look for me, but you won’t find me, and where I am you can’t come. ”
JHN 7:35 35 The Jewish opposition asked each other, “Where does he intend to go that we can’t find him? Surely he doesn’t intend to go where our people have been scattered and are living among the Greeks! He isn’t going to teach the Greeks, is he?
JHN 7:36 36 What does he mean when he says, ‘You will look for me, but you won’t find me, and where I am you can’t come’?”
JHN 7:37 37 On the last and most important day of the festival, Jesus stood up and shouted, “ All who are thirsty should come to me!
JHN 7:38 38 All who believe in me should drink! As the scriptures said concerning me, Rivers of living water will flow out from within him. ”
JHN 7:39 39 Jesus said this concerning the Spirit. Those who believed in him would soon receive the Spirit, but they hadn’t experienced the Spirit yet since Jesus hadn’t yet been glorified.
JHN 7:40 40 When some in the crowd heard these words, they said, “This man is truly the prophet.”
JHN 7:41 41 Others said, “He’s the Christ.” But others said, “The Christ can’t come from Galilee, can he?
JHN 7:42 42 Didn’t the scripture say that the Christ comes from David’s family and from Bethlehem, David’s village?”
JHN 7:43 43 So the crowd was divided over Jesus.
JHN 7:44 44 Some wanted to arrest him, but no one grabbed him.
JHN 7:45 45 The guards returned to the chief priests and Pharisees, who asked, “Why didn’t you bring him?”
JHN 7:46 46 The guards answered, “No one has ever spoken the way he does.”
JHN 7:47 47 The Pharisees replied, “Have you too been deceived?
JHN 7:48 48 Have any of the leaders believed in him? Has any Pharisee?
JHN 7:49 49 No, only this crowd, which doesn’t know the Law. And they are under God’s curse!”
JHN 7:50 50 Nicodemus, who was one of them and had come to Jesus earlier, said,
JHN 7:51 51 “Our Law doesn’t judge someone without first hearing him and learning what he is doing, does it?”
JHN 7:52 52 They answered him, “You are not from Galilee too, are you? Look it up and you will see that the prophet doesn’t come from Galilee.”
JHN 7:53 53 They each went to their own homes,
JHN 8:1 1 And Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
JHN 8:2 2 Early in the morning he returned to the temple. All the people gathered around him, and he sat down and taught them.
JHN 8:3 3 The legal experts and Pharisees brought a woman caught in adultery. Placing her in the center of the group,
JHN 8:4 4 they said to Jesus, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of committing adultery.
JHN 8:5 5 In the Law, Moses commanded us to stone women like this. What do you say?”
JHN 8:6 6 They said this to test him, because they wanted a reason to bring an accusation against him. Jesus bent down and wrote on the ground with his finger.
JHN 8:7 7 They continued to question him, so he stood up and replied, “Whoever hasn’t sinned should throw the first stone.”
JHN 8:8 8 Bending down again, he wrote on the ground.
JHN 8:9 9 Those who heard him went away, one by one, beginning with the elders. Finally, only Jesus and the woman were left in the middle of the crowd.
JHN 8:10 10 Jesus stood up and said to her, “Woman, where are they? Is there no one to condemn you?”
JHN 8:11 11 She said, “No one, sir.” Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go, and from now on, don’t sin anymore.”
JHN 8:12 12 Jesus spoke to the people again, saying, “ I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me won’t walk in darkness but will have the light of life. ”
JHN 8:13 13 Then the Pharisees said to him, “Because you are testifying about yourself, your testimony isn’t valid.”
JHN 8:14 14 Jesus replied, “ Even if I testify about myself, my testimony is true, since I know where I came from and where I’m going. You don’t know where I come from or where I’m going.
JHN 8:15 15 You judge according to human standards, but I judge no one.
JHN 8:16 16 Even if I do judge, my judgment is truthful, because I’m not alone. My judgments come from me and from the Father who sent me.
JHN 8:17 17 In your Law it is written that the witness of two people is true.
JHN 8:18 18 I am one witness concerning myself, and the Father who sent me is the other. ”
JHN 8:19 19 They asked him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered, “ You don’t know me and you don’t know my Father. If you knew me, you would also know my Father. ”
JHN 8:20 20 He spoke these words while he was teaching in the temple area known as the treasury. No one arrested him, because his time hadn’t yet come.
JHN 8:21 21 Jesus continued, “ I’m going away. You will look for me, and you will die in your sin. Where I’m going, you can’t come. ”
JHN 8:22 22 The Jewish leaders said, “He isn’t going to kill himself, is he? Is that why he said, ‘Where I’m going, you can’t come’?”
JHN 8:23 23 He said to them, “ You are from below; I’m from above. You are from this world; I’m not from this world.
JHN 8:24 24 This is why I told you that you would die in your sins. If you don’t believe that I Am, you will die in your sins. ”
JHN 8:25 25 “Who are you?” they asked. Jesus replied, “ I’m exactly who I have claimed to be from the beginning.
JHN 8:26 26 I have many things to say in judgment concerning you. The one who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him I tell the world. ”
JHN 8:27 27 They didn’t know he was speaking about his Father.
JHN 8:28 28 So Jesus said to them, “ When the Human One is lifted up, then you will know that I Am. Then you will know that I do nothing on my own, but I say just what the Father has taught me.
JHN 8:29 29 He who sent me is with me. He doesn’t leave me by myself, because I always do what makes him happy. ”
JHN 8:30 30 While Jesus was saying these things, many people came to believe in him.
JHN 8:31 31 Jesus said to the Jews who believed in him, “ You are truly my disciples if you remain faithful to my teaching.
JHN 8:32 32 Then you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free. ”
JHN 8:33 33 They responded, “We are Abraham’s children; we’ve never been anyone’s slaves. How can you say that we will be set free?”
JHN 8:34 34 Jesus answered, “ I assure you that everyone who sins is a slave to sin.
JHN 8:35 35 A slave isn’t a permanent member of the household, but a son is.
JHN 8:36 36 Therefore, if the Son makes you free, you really will be free.
JHN 8:37 37 I know that you are Abraham’s children, yet you want to kill me because you don’t welcome my teaching.
JHN 8:38 38 I’m telling you what I’ve seen when I am with the Father, but you are doing what you’ve heard from your father. ”
JHN 8:39 39 They replied, “Our father is Abraham.” Jesus responded, “ If you were Abraham’s children, you would do Abraham’s works.
JHN 8:40 40 Instead, you want to kill me, though I am the one who has spoken the truth I heard from God. Abraham didn’t do this.
JHN 8:41 41 You are doing your father’s works. ” They said, “Our ancestry isn’t in question! The only Father we have is God!”
JHN 8:42 42 Jesus replied, “ If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came from God. Here I am. I haven’t come on my own. God sent me.
JHN 8:43 43 Why don’t you understand what I’m saying? It’s because you can’t really hear my words.
JHN 8:44 44 Your father is the devil. You are his children, and you want to do what your father wants. He was a murderer from the beginning. He has never stood for the truth, because there’s no truth in him. Whenever that liar speaks, he speaks according to his own nature, because he’s a liar and the father of liars.
JHN 8:45 45 Because I speak the truth, you don’t believe me.
JHN 8:46 46 Who among you can show I’m guilty of sin? Since I speak the truth, why don’t you believe me?
JHN 8:47 47 God’s children listen to God’s words. You don’t listen to me because you aren’t God’s children. ”
JHN 8:48 48 The Jewish opposition answered, “We were right to say that you are a Samaritan and have a demon, weren’t we?”
JHN 8:49 49 “ I don’t have a demon, ” Jesus replied. “ But I honor my Father and you dishonor me.
JHN 8:50 50 I’m not trying to bring glory to myself. There’s one who is seeking to glorify me, and he’s the judge.
JHN 8:51 51 I assure you that whoever keeps my word will never die. ”
JHN 8:52 52 The Jewish opposition said to Jesus, “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham and the prophets died, yet you say, ‘Whoever keeps my word will never die.’
JHN 8:53 53 Are you greater than our father Abraham? He died and the prophets died, so who do you make yourself out to be?”
JHN 8:54 54 Jesus answered, “ If I glorify myself, my glory is meaningless. My Father, who you say is your God, is the one who glorifies me.
JHN 8:55 55 You don’t know him, but I do. If I said I didn’t know him, I would be like you, a liar. But I do know him, and I keep his word.
JHN 8:56 56 Your father Abraham was overjoyed that he would see my day. He saw it and was happy. ”
JHN 8:57 57 “You aren’t even 50 years old!” the Jewish opposition replied. “How can you say that you have seen Abraham?”
JHN 8:58 58 “ I assure you, ” Jesus replied, “ before Abraham was, I Am. ”
JHN 8:59 59 So they picked up stones to throw at him, but Jesus hid himself and left the temple.
JHN 9:1 1 As Jesus walked along, he saw a man who was blind from birth.
JHN 9:2 2 Jesus’ disciples asked, “Rabbi, who sinned so that he was born blind, this man or his parents?”
JHN 9:3 3 Jesus answered, “ Neither he nor his parents. This happened so that God’s mighty works might be displayed in him.
JHN 9:4 4 While it’s daytime, we must do the works of him who sent me. Night is coming when no one can work.
JHN 9:5 5 While I am in the world, I am the light of the world. ”
JHN 9:6 6 After he said this, he spit on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and smeared the mud on the man’s eyes.
JHN 9:7 7 Jesus said to him, “ Go, wash in the pool of Siloam ” (this word means sent ). So the man went away and washed. When he returned, he could see.
JHN 9:8 8 The man’s neighbors and those who used to see him when he was a beggar said, “Isn’t this the man who used to sit and beg?”
JHN 9:9 9 Some said, “It is,” and others said, “No, it’s someone who looks like him.” But the man said, “Yes, it’s me!”
JHN 9:10 10 So they asked him, “How are you now able to see?”
JHN 9:11 11 He answered, “The man they call Jesus made mud, smeared it on my eyes, and said, ‘Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.’ So I went and washed, and then I could see.”
JHN 9:12 12 They asked, “Where is this man?” He replied, “I don’t know.”
JHN 9:13 13 Then they led the man who had been born blind to the Pharisees.
JHN 9:14 14 Now Jesus made the mud and smeared it on the man’s eyes on a Sabbath day.
JHN 9:15 15 So Pharisees also asked him how he was able to see. The man told them, “He put mud on my eyes, I washed, and now I see.”
JHN 9:16 16 Some Pharisees said, “This man isn’t from God, because he breaks the Sabbath law.” Others said, “How can a sinner do miraculous signs like these?” So they were divided.
JHN 9:17 17 Some of the Pharisees questioned the man who had been born blind again: “What do you have to say about him, since he healed your eyes?” He replied, “He’s a prophet.”
JHN 9:18 18 The Jewish leaders didn’t believe the man had been blind and received his sight until they called for his parents.
JHN 9:19 19 The Jewish leaders asked them, “Is this your son? Are you saying he was born blind? How can he now see?”
JHN 9:20 20 His parents answered, “We know he is our son. We know he was born blind.
JHN 9:21 21 But we don’t know how he now sees, and we don’t know who healed his eyes. Ask him. He’s old enough to speak for himself.”
JHN 9:22 22 His parents said this because they feared the Jewish authorities. This is because the Jewish authorities had already decided that whoever confessed Jesus to be the Christ would be expelled from the synagogue.
JHN 9:23 23 That’s why his parents said, “He’s old enough. Ask him.”
JHN 9:24 24 Therefore, they called a second time for the man who had been born blind and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know this man is a sinner.”
JHN 9:25 25 The man answered, “I don’t know whether he’s a sinner. Here’s what I do know: I was blind and now I see.”
JHN 9:26 26 They questioned him: “What did he do to you? How did he heal your eyes?”
JHN 9:27 27 He replied, “I already told you, and you didn’t listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you want to become his disciples too?”
JHN 9:28 28 They insulted him: “You are his disciple, but we are Moses’ disciples.
JHN 9:29 29 We know that God spoke to Moses, but we don’t know where this man is from.”
JHN 9:30 30 The man answered, “This is incredible! You don’t know where he is from, yet he healed my eyes!
JHN 9:31 31 We know that God doesn’t listen to sinners. God listens to anyone who is devout and does God’s will.
JHN 9:32 32 No one has ever heard of a healing of the eyes of someone born blind.
JHN 9:33 33 If this man wasn’t from God, he couldn’t do this.”
JHN 9:34 34 They responded, “You were born completely in sin! How is it that you dare to teach us?” Then they expelled him.
JHN 9:35 35 Jesus heard they had expelled the man born blind. Finding him, Jesus said, “ Do you believe in the Human One? ”
JHN 9:36 36 He answered, “Who is he, sir? I want to believe in him.”
JHN 9:37 37 Jesus said, “ You have seen him. In fact, he is the one speaking with you. ”
JHN 9:38 38 The man said, “Lord, I believe.” And he worshipped Jesus.
JHN 9:39 39 Jesus said, “ I have come into the world to exercise judgment so that those who don’t see can see and those who see will become blind. ”
JHN 9:40 40 Some Pharisees who were with him heard what he said and asked, “Surely we aren’t blind, are we?”
JHN 9:41 41 Jesus said to them, “ If you were blind, you wouldn’t have any sin, but now that you say, ‘We see,’ your sin remains.
JHN 10:1 1 I assure you that whoever doesn’t enter into the sheep pen through the gate but climbs over the wall is a thief and an outlaw.
JHN 10:2 2 The one who enters through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
JHN 10:3 3 The guard at the gate opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
JHN 10:4 4 Whenever he has gathered all of his sheep, he goes before them and they follow him, because they know his voice.
JHN 10:5 5 They won’t follow a stranger but will run away because they don’t know the stranger’s voice. ”
JHN 10:6 6 Those who heard Jesus use this analogy didn’t understand what he was saying.
JHN 10:7 7 So Jesus spoke again, “I assure you that I am the gate of the sheep.
JHN 10:8 8 All who came before me were thieves and outlaws, but the sheep didn’t listen to them.
JHN 10:9 9 I am the gate. Whoever enters through me will be saved. They will come in and go out and find pasture.
JHN 10:10 10 The thief enters only to steal, kill, and destroy. I came so that they could have life—indeed, so that they could live life to the fullest.
JHN 10:11 11 “I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
JHN 10:12 12 When the hired hand sees the wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and runs away. That’s because he isn’t the shepherd; the sheep aren’t really his. So the wolf attacks the sheep and scatters them.
JHN 10:13 13 He’s only a hired hand and the sheep don’t matter to him.
JHN 10:14 14 “I am the good shepherd. I know my own sheep and they know me,
JHN 10:15 15 just as the Father knows me and I know the Father. I give up my life for the sheep.
JHN 10:16 16 I have other sheep that don’t belong to this sheep pen. I must lead them too. They will listen to my voice and there will be one flock, with one shepherd.
JHN 10:17 17 “ This is why the Father loves me: I give up my life so that I can take it up again.
JHN 10:18 18 No one takes it from me, but I give it up because I want to. I have the right to give it up, and I have the right to take it up again. I received this commandment from my Father. ”
JHN 10:19 19 There was another division among the Jews because of Jesus’ words.
JHN 10:20 20 Many of them said, “He has a demon and has lost his mind. Why listen to him?”
JHN 10:21 21 Others said, “These aren’t the words of someone who has a demon. Can a demon heal the eyes of people who are blind?”
JHN 10:22 22 The time came for the Festival of Dedication in Jerusalem. It was winter,
JHN 10:23 23 and Jesus was in the temple, walking in the covered porch named for Solomon.
JHN 10:24 24 The Jewish opposition circled around him and asked, “How long will you test our patience? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”
JHN 10:25 25 Jesus answered, “ I have told you, but you don’t believe. The works I do in my Father’s name testify about me,
JHN 10:26 26 but you don’t believe because you don’t belong to my sheep.
JHN 10:27 27 My sheep listen to my voice. I know them and they follow me.
JHN 10:28 28 I give them eternal life. They will never die, and no one will snatch them from my hand.
JHN 10:29 29 My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them from my Father’s hand.
JHN 10:30 30 I and the Father are one. ”
JHN 10:31 31 Again the Jewish opposition picked up stones in order to stone him.
JHN 10:32 32 Jesus responded, “ I have shown you many good works from the Father. For which of those works do you stone me? ”
JHN 10:33 33 The Jewish opposition answered, “We don’t stone you for a good work but for insulting God. You are human, yet you make yourself out to be God.”
JHN 10:34 34 Jesus replied, “ Isn’t it written in your Law, I have said, you are gods?
JHN 10:35 35 Scripture calls those to whom God’s word came gods , and scripture can’t be abolished.
JHN 10:36 36 So how can you say that the one whom the Father has made holy and sent into the world insults God because he said, ‘I am God’s Son’?
JHN 10:37 37 If I don’t do the works of my Father, don’t believe me.
JHN 10:38 38 But if I do them, and you don’t believe me, believe the works so that you can know and recognize that the Father is in me and I am in the Father.”
JHN 10:39 39 Again, they wanted to arrest him, but he escaped from them.
JHN 10:40 40 Jesus went back across the Jordan to the place where John had baptized at first, and he stayed there.
JHN 10:41 41 Many people came to him. “John didn’t do any miraculous signs,” they said, “but everything John said about this man was true.”
JHN 10:42 42 Many believed in Jesus there.
JHN 11:1 1 A certain man, Lazarus, was ill. He was from Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha. (
JHN 11:2 2 This was the Mary who anointed the Lord with fragrant oil and wiped his feet with her hair. Her brother Lazarus was ill.)
JHN 11:3 3 So the sisters sent word to Jesus, saying, “Lord, the one whom you love is ill.”
JHN 11:4 4 When he heard this, Jesus said, “ This illness isn’t fatal. It’s for the glory of God so that God’s Son can be glorified through it. ”
JHN 11:5 5 Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus.
JHN 11:6 6 When he heard that Lazarus was ill, he stayed where he was. After two days,
JHN 11:7 7 he said to his disciples, “ Let’s return to Judea again. ”
JHN 11:8 8 The disciples replied, “Rabbi, the Jewish opposition wants to stone you, but you want to go back?”
JHN 11:9 9 Jesus answered, “ Aren’t there twelve hours in the day? Whoever walks in the day doesn’t stumble because they see the light of the world.
JHN 11:10 10 But whoever walks in the night does stumble because the light isn’t in them. ”
JHN 11:11 11 He continued, “ Our friend Lazarus is sleeping, but I am going in order to wake him up. ”
JHN 11:12 12 The disciples said, “Lord, if he’s sleeping, he will get well.”
JHN 11:13 13 They thought Jesus meant that Lazarus was in a deep sleep, but Jesus had spoken about Lazarus’ death.
JHN 11:14 14 Jesus told them plainly, “ Lazarus has died.
JHN 11:15 15 For your sakes, I’m glad I wasn’t there so that you can believe. Let’s go to him. ”
JHN 11:16 16 Then Thomas (the one called Didymus) said to the other disciples, “Let us go too so that we may die with Jesus.”
JHN 11:17 17 When Jesus arrived, he found that Lazarus had already been in the tomb for four days.
JHN 11:18 18 Bethany was a little less than two miles from Jerusalem.
JHN 11:19 19 Many Jews had come to comfort Martha and Mary after their brother’s death.
JHN 11:20 20 When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went to meet him, while Mary remained in the house.
JHN 11:21 21 Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.
JHN 11:22 22 Even now I know that whatever you ask God, God will give you.”
JHN 11:23 23 Jesus told her, “ Your brother will rise again. ”
JHN 11:24 24 Martha replied, “I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.”
JHN 11:25 25 Jesus said to her, “ I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me will live, even though they die.
JHN 11:26 26 Everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this? ”
JHN 11:27 27 She replied, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Christ, God’s Son, the one who is coming into the world.”
JHN 11:28 28 After she said this, she went and spoke privately to her sister Mary, “The teacher is here and he’s calling for you.”
JHN 11:29 29 When Mary heard this, she got up quickly and went to Jesus.
JHN 11:30 30 He hadn’t entered the village but was still in the place where Martha had met him.
JHN 11:31 31 When the Jews who were comforting Mary in the house saw her get up quickly and leave, they followed her. They assumed she was going to mourn at the tomb.
JHN 11:32 32 When Mary arrived where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.”
JHN 11:33 33 When Jesus saw her crying and the Jews who had come with her crying also, he was deeply disturbed and troubled.
JHN 11:34 34 He asked, “ Where have you laid him? ” They replied, “Lord, come and see.”
JHN 11:35 35 Jesus began to cry.
JHN 11:36 36 The Jews said, “See how much he loved him!”
JHN 11:37 37 But some of them said, “He healed the eyes of the man born blind. Couldn’t he have kept Lazarus from dying?”
JHN 11:38 38 Jesus was deeply disturbed again when he came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone covered the entrance.
JHN 11:39 39 Jesus said, “ Remove the stone. ” Martha, the sister of the dead man, said, “Lord, the smell will be awful! He’s been dead four days.”
JHN 11:40 40 Jesus replied, “ Didn’t I tell you that if you believe, you will see God’s glory? ”
JHN 11:41 41 So they removed the stone. Jesus looked up and said, “ Father, thank you for hearing me.
JHN 11:42 42 I know you always hear me. I say this for the benefit of the crowd standing here so that they will believe that you sent me. ”
JHN 11:43 43 Having said this, Jesus shouted with a loud voice, “ Lazarus, come out! ”
JHN 11:44 44 The dead man came out, his feet bound and his hands tied, and his face covered with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “ Untie him and let him go. ”
JHN 11:45 45 Therefore, many of the Jews who came with Mary and saw what Jesus did believed in him.
JHN 11:46 46 But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
JHN 11:47 47 Then the chief priests and Pharisees called together the council and said, “What are we going to do? This man is doing many miraculous signs!
JHN 11:48 48 If we let him go on like this, everyone will believe in him. Then the Romans will come and take away both our temple and our people.”
JHN 11:49 49 One of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, told them, “You don’t know anything!
JHN 11:50 50 You don’t see that it is better for you that one man die for the people rather than the whole nation be destroyed.”
JHN 11:51 51 He didn’t say this on his own. As high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus would soon die for the nation—
JHN 11:52 52 and not only for the nation. Jesus would also die so that God’s children scattered everywhere would be gathered together as one.
JHN 11:53 53 From that day on they plotted to kill him.
JHN 11:54 54 Therefore, Jesus was no longer active in public ministry among the Jewish leaders. Instead, he left Jerusalem and went to a place near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim, where he stayed with his disciples.
JHN 11:55 55 It was almost time for the Jewish Passover, and many people went from the countryside up to Jerusalem to purify themselves through ritual washing before the Passover.
JHN 11:56 56 They were looking for Jesus. As they spoke to each other in the temple, they said, “What do you think? He won’t come to the festival, will he?”
JHN 11:57 57 The chief priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where he was should report it, so they could arrest him.
JHN 12:1 1 Six days before Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, home of Lazarus, whom Jesus had raised from the dead.
JHN 12:2 2 Lazarus and his sisters hosted a dinner for him. Martha served and Lazarus was among those who joined him at the table.
JHN 12:3 3 Then Mary took an extraordinary amount, almost three-quarters of a pound, of very expensive perfume made of pure nard. She anointed Jesus’ feet with it, then wiped his feet dry with her hair. The house was filled with the aroma of the perfume.
JHN 12:4 4 Judas Iscariot, one of his disciples (the one who was about to betray him), complained,
JHN 12:5 5 “This perfume was worth a year’s wages! Why wasn’t it sold and the money given to the poor?” (
JHN 12:6 6 He said this not because he cared about the poor but because he was a thief. He carried the money bag and would take what was in it.)
JHN 12:7 7 Then Jesus said, “ Leave her alone. This perfume was to be used in preparation for my burial, and this is how she has used it.
JHN 12:8 8 You will always have the poor among you, but you won’t always have me. ”
JHN 12:9 9 Many Jews learned that he was there. They came not only because of Jesus but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.
JHN 12:10 10 The chief priests decided that they would kill Lazarus too.
JHN 12:11 11 It was because of Lazarus that many of the Jews had deserted them and come to believe in Jesus.
JHN 12:12 12 The next day the great crowd that had come for the festival heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
JHN 12:13 13 They took palm branches and went out to meet him. They shouted, “Hosanna! Blessings on the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessings on the king of Israel!”
JHN 12:14 14 Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, just as it is written,
JHN 12:15 15 Don’t be afraid, Daughter Zion. Look! Your king is coming , sitting on a donkey’s colt .
JHN 12:16 16 His disciples didn’t understand these things at first. After he was glorified, they remembered that these things had been written about him and that they had done these things to him.
JHN 12:17 17 The crowd who had been with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead were testifying about him.
JHN 12:18 18 That’s why the crowd came to meet him, because they had heard about this miraculous sign that he had done.
JHN 12:19 19 Therefore, the Pharisees said to each other, “See! You’ve accomplished nothing! Look! The whole world is following him!”
JHN 12:20 20 Some Greeks were among those who had come up to worship at the festival.
JHN 12:21 21 They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and made a request: “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
JHN 12:22 22 Philip told Andrew, and Andrew and Philip told Jesus.
JHN 12:23 23 Jesus replied, “The time has come for the Human One to be glorified.
JHN 12:24 24 I assure you that unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it can only be a single seed. But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
JHN 12:25 25 Those who love their lives will lose them, and those who hate their lives in this world will keep them forever.
JHN 12:26 26 Whoever serves me must follow me. Wherever I am, there my servant will also be. My Father will honor whoever serves me.
JHN 12:27 27 “ Now I am deeply troubled. What should I say? ‘Father, save me from this time’? No, for this is the reason I have come to this time.
JHN 12:28 28 Father, glorify your name! ” Then a voice came from heaven, “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”
JHN 12:29 29 The crowd standing there heard and said, “It’s thunder.” Others said, “An angel spoke to him.”
JHN 12:30 30 Jesus replied, “ This voice wasn’t for my benefit but for yours.
JHN 12:31 31 Now is the time for judgment of this world. Now this world’s ruler will be thrown out.
JHN 12:32 32 When I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw everyone to me. ” (
JHN 12:33 33 He said this to show how he was going to die.)
JHN 12:34 34 The crowd responded, “We have heard from the Law that the Christ remains forever. How can you say that the Human One must be lifted up? Who is this Human One?”
JHN 12:35 35 Jesus replied, “ The light is with you for only a little while. Walk while you have the light so that darkness doesn’t overtake you. Those who walk in the darkness don’t know where they are going.
JHN 12:36 36 As long as you have the light, believe in the light so that you might become people whose lives are determined by the light. ” After Jesus said these things, he went away and hid from them.
JHN 12:37 37 Jesus had done many miraculous signs before the people, but they didn’t believe in him.
JHN 12:38 38 This was to fulfill the word of the prophet Isaiah: Lord, who has believed through our message? To whom is the arm of the Lord fully revealed?
JHN 12:39 39 Isaiah explains why they couldn’t believe:
JHN 12:40 40 He made their eyes blind and closed their minds so that they might not see with their eyes, understand with their minds, and turn their lives around— and I would heal them.
JHN 12:41 41 Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus’ glory; he spoke about Jesus.
JHN 12:42 42 Even so, many leaders believed in him, but they wouldn’t acknowledge their faith because they feared that the Pharisees would expel them from the synagogue.
JHN 12:43 43 They believed, but they loved human praise more than God’s glory.
JHN 12:44 44 Jesus shouted, “ Whoever believes in me doesn’t believe in me but in the one who sent me.
JHN 12:45 45 Whoever sees me sees the one who sent me.
JHN 12:46 46 I have come as a light into the world so that everyone who believes in me won’t live in darkness.
JHN 12:47 47 If people hear my words and don’t keep them, I don’t judge them. I didn’t come to judge the world but to save it.
JHN 12:48 48 Whoever rejects me and doesn’t receive my words will be judged at the last day by the word I have spoken.
JHN 12:49 49 I don’t speak on my own, but the Father who sent me commanded me regarding what I should speak and say.
JHN 12:50 50 I know that his commandment is eternal life. Therefore, whatever I say is just as the Father has said to me. ”
JHN 13:1 1 Before the Festival of Passover, Jesus knew that his time had come to leave this world and go to the Father. Having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them fully.
JHN 13:2 2 Jesus and his disciples were sharing the evening meal. The devil had already provoked Judas, Simon Iscariot’s son, to betray Jesus.
JHN 13:3 3 Jesus knew the Father had given everything into his hands and that he had come from God and was returning to God.
JHN 13:4 4 So he got up from the table and took off his robes. Picking up a linen towel, he tied it around his waist.
JHN 13:5 5 Then he poured water into a washbasin and began to wash the disciples’ feet, drying them with the towel he was wearing.
JHN 13:6 6 When Jesus came to Simon Peter, Peter said to him, “Lord, are you going to wash my feet?”
JHN 13:7 7 Jesus replied, “ You don’t understand what I’m doing now, but you will understand later. ”
JHN 13:8 8 “No!” Peter said. “You will never wash my feet!” Jesus replied, “ Unless I wash you, you won’t have a place with me. ”
JHN 13:9 9 Simon Peter said, “Lord, not only my feet but also my hands and my head!”
JHN 13:10 10 Jesus responded, “ Those who have bathed need only to have their feet washed, because they are completely clean. You disciples are clean, but not every one of you. ”
JHN 13:11 11 He knew who would betray him. That’s why he said, “ Not every one of you is clean. ”

JHN 13:14 14 If I, your Lord and teacher, have washed your feet, you too must wash each other’s feet.
JHN 13:15 15 I have given you an example: Just as I have done, you also must do.
JHN 13:16 16 I assure you, servants aren’t greater than their master, nor are those who are sent greater than the one who sent them.
JHN 13:17 17 Since you know these things, you will be happy if you do them.
JHN 13:18 18 I’m not speaking about all of you. I know those whom I’ve chosen. But this is to fulfill the scripture, The one who eats my bread has turned against me.

JHN 13:22 22 His disciples looked at each other, confused about which of them he was talking about.
JHN 13:23 23 One of the disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was at Jesus’ side.
JHN 13:24 24 Simon Peter nodded at him to get him to ask Jesus who he was talking about.
JHN 13:25 25 Leaning back toward Jesus, this disciple asked, “Lord, who is it?”
JHN 13:26 26 Jesus answered, “ It’s the one to whom I will give this piece of bread once I have dipped into the bowl. ” Then he dipped the piece of bread and gave it to Judas, Simon Iscariot’s son.
JHN 13:27 27 After Judas took the bread, Satan entered into him. Jesus told him, “ What you are about to do, do quickly. ”
JHN 13:28 28 No one sitting at the table understood why Jesus said this to him.
JHN 13:29 29 Some thought that, since Judas kept the money bag, Jesus told him, “Go, buy what we need for the feast,” or that he should give something to the poor.
JHN 13:30 30 So when Judas took the bread, he left immediately. And it was night.

JHN 13:32 32 If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify the Human One in himself and will glorify him immediately.

JHN 13:38 38 Jesus replied, “Will you give up your life for me? I assure you that you will deny me three times before the rooster crows.

JHN 15:27 27 You will testify too, because you have been with me from the beginning.
JHN 16:1 1 I have said these things to you so that you won’t fall away.
JHN 16:2 2 They will expel you from the synagogue. The time is coming when those who kill you will think that they are doing a service to God.
JHN 16:3 3 They will do these things because they don’t know the Father or me.
JHN 16:4 4 But I have said these things to you so that when their time comes, you will remember that I told you about them. “I didn’t say these things to you from the beginning, because I was with you.
JHN 16:5 5 But now I go away to the one who sent me. None of you ask me, ‘Where are you going?’
JHN 16:6 6 Yet because I have said these things to you, you are filled with sorrow.
JHN 16:7 7 I assure you that it is better for you that I go away. If I don’t go away, the Companion won’t come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you.
JHN 16:8 8 When he comes, he will show the world it was wrong about sin, righteousness, and judgment.
JHN 16:9 9 He will show the world it was wrong about sin because they don’t believe in me.
JHN 16:10 10 He will show the world it was wrong about righteousness because I’m going to the Father and you won’t see me anymore.
JHN 16:11 11 He will show the world it was wrong about judgment because this world’s ruler stands condemned.
JHN 16:12 12 “ I have much more to say to you, but you can’t handle it now.
JHN 16:13 13 However, when the Spirit of Truth comes, he will guide you in all truth. He won’t speak on his own, but will say whatever he hears and will proclaim to you what is to come.
JHN 16:14 14 He will glorify me, because he will take what is mine and proclaim it to you.
JHN 16:15 15 Everything that the Father has is mine. That’s why I said that the Spirit takes what is mine and will proclaim it to you.
JHN 16:16 16 Soon you won’t be able to see me; soon after that, you will see me. ”
JHN 16:17 17 Some of Jesus’ disciples said to each other, “What does he mean: ‘Soon you won’t see me, and soon after that you will see me’ and ‘Because I’m going to the Father’?
JHN 16:18 18 What does he mean by ‘soon’? We don’t understand what he’s talking about.”
JHN 16:19 19 Jesus knew they wanted to ask him, so he said, “Are you trying to find out from each other what I meant when I said, ‘Soon you won’t see me, and soon after that you will see me’?
JHN 16:20 20 I assure you that you will cry and lament, and the world will be happy. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy.
JHN 16:21 21 When a woman gives birth, she has pain because her time has come. But when the child is born, she no longer remembers her distress because of her joy that a child has been born into the world.
JHN 16:22 22 In the same way, you have sorrow now; but I will see you again, and you will be overjoyed. No one takes away your joy.
JHN 16:23 23 In that day, you won’t ask me anything. I assure you that the Father will give you whatever you ask in my name.
JHN 16:24 24 Up to now, you have asked nothing in my name. Ask and you will receive so that your joy will be complete.
JHN 16:25 25 “ I’ve been using figures of speech with you. The time is coming when I will no longer speak to you in such analogies. Instead, I will tell you plainly about the Father.
JHN 16:26 26 In that day you will ask in my name. I’m not saying that I will ask the Father on your behalf.
JHN 16:27 27 The Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and believed that I came from God.
JHN 16:28 28 I left the Father and came into the world. I tell you again: I am leaving the world and returning to the Father. ”
JHN 16:29 29 His disciples said, “See! Now you speak plainly; you aren’t using figures of speech.
JHN 16:30 30 Now we know that you know everything and you don’t need anyone to ask you. Because of this we believe you have come from God.”
JHN 16:31 31 Jesus replied, “ Now you believe?
JHN 16:32 32 Look! A time is coming—and is here!—when each of you will be scattered to your own homes and you will leave me alone. I’m not really alone, for the Father is with me.
JHN 16:33 33 I’ve said these things to you so that you will have peace in me. In the world you have distress. But be encouraged! I have conquered the world. ”
JHN 17:1 1 When Jesus finished saying these things, he looked up to heaven and said, “Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son, so that the Son can glorify you.
JHN 17:2 2 You gave him authority over everyone so that he could give eternal life to everyone you gave him.
JHN 17:3 3 This is eternal life: to know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent.
JHN 17:4 4 I have glorified you on earth by finishing the work you gave me to do.
JHN 17:5 5 Now, Father, glorify me in your presence with the glory I shared with you before the world was created.
JHN 17:6 6 “I have revealed your name to the people you gave me from this world. They were yours and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
JHN 17:7 7 Now they know that everything you have given me comes from you.
JHN 17:8 8 This is because I gave them the words that you gave me, and they received them. They truly understood that I came from you, and they believed that you sent me.
JHN 17:9 9 “I’m praying for them. I’m not praying for the world but for those you gave me, because they are yours.
JHN 17:10 10 Everything that is mine is yours and everything that is yours is mine; I have been glorified in them.
JHN 17:11 11 I’m no longer in the world, but they are in the world, even as I’m coming to you. Holy Father, watch over them in your name, the name you gave me, that they will be one just as we are one.
JHN 17:12 12 When I was with them, I watched over them in your name, the name you gave to me, and I kept them safe. None of them were lost, except the one who was destined for destruction, so that scripture would be fulfilled.
JHN 17:13 13 Now I’m coming to you and I say these things while I’m in the world so that they can share completely in my joy.
JHN 17:14 14 I gave your word to them and the world hated them, because they don’t belong to this world, just as I don’t belong to this world.
JHN 17:15 15 I’m not asking that you take them out of this world but that you keep them safe from the evil one.
JHN 17:16 16 They don’t belong to this world, just as I don’t belong to this world.
JHN 17:17 17 Make them holy in the truth; your word is truth.
JHN 17:18 18 As you sent me into the world, so I have sent them into the world.
JHN 17:19 19 I made myself holy on their behalf so that they also would be made holy in the truth.
JHN 17:20 20 “I’m not praying only for them but also for those who believe in me because of their word.
JHN 17:21 21 I pray they will be one, Father, just as you are in me and I am in you. I pray that they also will be in us, so that the world will believe that you sent me.
JHN 17:22 22 I’ve given them the glory that you gave me so that they can be one just as we are one.
JHN 17:23 23 I’m in them and you are in me so that they will be made perfectly one. Then the world will know that you sent me and that you have loved them just as you loved me.
JHN 17:24 24 “Father, I want those you gave me to be with me where I am. Then they can see my glory, which you gave me because you loved me before the creation of the world.
JHN 17:25 25 “ Righteous Father, even the world didn’t know you, but I’ve known you, and these believers know that you sent me.
JHN 17:26 26 I’ve made your name known to them and will continue to make it known so that your love for me will be in them, and I myself will be in them. ”
JHN 18:1 1 After he said these things, Jesus went out with his disciples and crossed over to the other side of the Kidron Valley. He and his disciples entered a garden there.
JHN 18:2 2 Judas, his betrayer, also knew the place because Jesus often gathered there with his disciples.
JHN 18:3 3 Judas brought a company of soldiers and some guards from the chief priests and Pharisees. They came there carrying lanterns, torches, and weapons.
JHN 18:4 4 Jesus knew everything that was to happen to him, so he went out and asked, “ Who are you looking for? ”
JHN 18:5 5 They answered, “Jesus the Nazarene.” He said to them, “ I Am. ” (Judas, his betrayer, was standing with them.)
JHN 18:6 6 When he said, “I Am,” they shrank back and fell to the ground.
JHN 18:7 7 He asked them again, “ Who are you looking for? ” They said, “Jesus the Nazarene.”
JHN 18:8 8 Jesus answered, “ I told you, ‘I Am.’ If you are looking for me, then let these people go. ”
JHN 18:9 9 This was so that the word he had spoken might be fulfilled: “ I didn’t lose anyone of those whom you gave me. ”
JHN 18:10 10 Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, drew it and struck the high priest’s servant, cutting off his right ear. (The servant’s name was Malchus.)
JHN 18:11 11 Jesus told Peter, “ Put your sword away! Am I not to drink the cup the Father has given me? ”
JHN 18:12 12 Then the company of soldiers, the commander, and the guards from the Jewish leaders took Jesus into custody. They bound him
JHN 18:13 13 and led him first to Annas. He was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year. (
JHN 18:14 14 Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jewish leaders that it was better for one person to die for the people.)
JHN 18:15 15 Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus. Because this other disciple was known to the high priest, he went with Jesus into the high priest’s courtyard.
JHN 18:16 16 However, Peter stood outside near the gate. Then the other disciple (the one known to the high priest) came out and spoke to the woman stationed at the gate, and she brought Peter in.
JHN 18:17 17 The servant woman stationed at the gate asked Peter, “Aren’t you one of this man’s disciples?” “I’m not,” he replied.
JHN 18:18 18 The servants and the guards had made a fire because it was cold. They were standing around it, warming themselves. Peter joined them there, standing by the fire and warming himself.
JHN 18:19 19 Meanwhile, the chief priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching.
JHN 18:20 20 Jesus answered, “ I’ve spoken openly to the world. I’ve always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where all the Jews gather. I’ve said nothing in private.
JHN 18:21 21 Why ask me? Ask those who heard what I told them. They know what I said. ”
JHN 18:22 22 After Jesus spoke, one of the guards standing there slapped Jesus in the face. “Is that how you would answer the high priest?” he asked.
JHN 18:23 23 Jesus replied, “ If I speak wrongly, testify about what was wrong. But if I speak correctly, why do you strike me? ”
JHN 18:24 24 Then Annas sent him, bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
JHN 18:25 25 Meanwhile, Simon Peter was still standing with the guards, warming himself. They asked, “Aren’t you one of his disciples?” Peter denied it, saying, “I’m not.”
JHN 18:26 26 A servant of the high priest, a relative of the one whose ear Peter had cut off, said to him, “Didn’t I see you in the garden with him?”
JHN 18:27 27 Peter denied it again, and immediately a rooster crowed.
JHN 18:28 28 The Jewish leaders led Jesus from Caiaphas to the Roman governor’s palace. It was early in the morning. So that they could eat the Passover, the Jewish leaders wouldn’t enter the palace; entering the palace would have made them ritually impure.
JHN 18:29 29 So Pilate went out to them and asked, “What charge do you bring against this man?”
JHN 18:30 30 They answered, “If he had done nothing wrong, we wouldn’t have handed him over to you.”
JHN 18:31 31 Pilate responded, “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your Law.” The Jewish leaders replied, “The Law doesn’t allow us to kill anyone.” (
JHN 18:32 32 This was so that Jesus’ word might be fulfilled when he indicated how he was going to die.)
JHN 18:33 33 Pilate went back into the palace. He summoned Jesus and asked, “Are you the king of the Jews?”
JHN 18:34 34 Jesus answered, “ Do you say this on your own or have others spoken to you about me? ”
JHN 18:35 35 Pilate responded, “I’m not a Jew, am I? Your nation and its chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?”
JHN 18:36 36 Jesus replied, “ My kingdom doesn’t originate from this world. If it did, my guards would fight so that I wouldn’t have been arrested by the Jewish leaders. My kingdom isn’t from here. ”
JHN 18:37 37 “So you are a king?” Pilate said. Jesus answered, “ You say that I am a king. I was born and came into the world for this reason: to testify to the truth. Whoever accepts the truth listens to my voice. ”
JHN 18:38 38 “What is truth?” Pilate asked. After Pilate said this, he returned to the Jewish leaders and said, “I find no grounds for any charge against him.
JHN 18:39 39 You have a custom that I release one prisoner for you at Passover. Do you want me to release for you the king of the Jews?”
JHN 18:40 40 They shouted, “Not this man! Give us Barabbas!” (Barabbas was an outlaw.)
JHN 19:1 1 Then Pilate had Jesus taken and whipped.
JHN 19:2 2 The soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple robe.
JHN 19:3 3 Over and over they went up to him and said, “Greetings, king of the Jews!” And they slapped him in the face.
JHN 19:4 4 Pilate came out of the palace again and said to the Jewish leaders, “Look! I’m bringing him out to you to let you know that I find no grounds for a charge against him.”
JHN 19:5 5 When Jesus came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, Pilate said to them, “Here’s the man.”
JHN 19:6 6 When the chief priests and their deputies saw him, they shouted out, “Crucify, crucify!” Pilate told them, “You take him and crucify him. I don’t find any grounds for a charge against him.”
JHN 19:7 7 The Jewish leaders replied, “We have a Law, and according to this Law he ought to die because he made himself out to be God’s Son.”
JHN 19:8 8 When Pilate heard this word, he was even more afraid.
JHN 19:9 9 He went back into the residence and spoke to Jesus, “Where are you from?” Jesus didn’t answer.
JHN 19:10 10 So Pilate said, “You won’t speak to me? Don’t you know that I have authority to release you and also to crucify you?”
JHN 19:11 11 Jesus replied, “ You would have no authority over me if it had not been given to you from above. That’s why the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin. ”
JHN 19:12 12 From that moment on, Pilate wanted to release Jesus. However, the Jewish leaders cried out, saying, “If you release this man, you aren’t a friend of the emperor! Anyone who makes himself out to be a king opposes the emperor!”
JHN 19:13 13 When Pilate heard these words, he led Jesus out and seated him on the judge’s bench at the place called Stone Pavement (in Aramaic, Gabbatha ).
JHN 19:14 14 It was about noon on the Preparation Day for the Passover. Pilate said to the Jewish leaders, “Here’s your king.”
JHN 19:15 15 The Jewish leaders cried out, “Take him away! Take him away! Crucify him!” Pilate responded, “What? Do you want me to crucify your king?” “We have no king except the emperor,” the chief priests answered.
JHN 19:16 16 Then Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified. The soldiers took Jesus prisoner.
JHN 19:17 17 Carrying his cross by himself, he went out to a place called Skull Place (in Aramaic, Golgotha ).
JHN 19:18 18 That’s where they crucified him—and two others with him, one on each side and Jesus in the middle.
JHN 19:19 19 Pilate had a public notice written and posted on the cross. It read “Jesus the Nazarene, the king of the Jews.”
JHN 19:20 20 Many of the Jews read this sign, for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city and it was written in Aramaic, Latin, and Greek.
JHN 19:21 21 Therefore, the Jewish chief priests complained to Pilate, “Don’t write, ‘The king of the Jews’ but ‘This man said, “I am the king of the Jews.”’”
JHN 19:22 22 Pilate answered, “What I’ve written, I’ve written.”
JHN 19:23 23 When the soldiers crucified Jesus, they took his clothes and his sandals, and divided them into four shares, one for each soldier. His shirt was seamless, woven as one piece from the top to the bottom.
JHN 19:24 24 They said to each other, “Let’s not tear it. Let’s cast lots to see who will get it.” This was to fulfill the scripture, They divided my clothes among themselves, and they cast lots for my clothing. That’s what the soldiers did.
JHN 19:25 25 Jesus’ mother and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene stood near the cross.
JHN 19:26 26 When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing nearby, he said to his mother, “ Woman, here is your son. ”
JHN 19:27 27 Then he said to the disciple, “ Here is your mother. ” And from that time on, this disciple took her into his home.
JHN 19:28 28 After this, knowing that everything was already completed, in order to fulfill the scripture, Jesus said, “ I am thirsty. ”
JHN 19:29 29 A jar full of sour wine was nearby, so the soldiers soaked a sponge in it, placed it on a hyssop branch, and held it up to his lips.
JHN 19:30 30 When he had received the sour wine, Jesus said, “ It is completed. ” Bowing his head, he gave up his life.
JHN 19:31 31 It was the Preparation Day and the Jewish leaders didn’t want the bodies to remain on the cross on the Sabbath, especially since that Sabbath was an important day. So they asked Pilate to have the legs of those crucified broken and the bodies taken down.
JHN 19:32 32 Therefore, the soldiers came and broke the legs of the two men who were crucified with Jesus.
JHN 19:33 33 When they came to Jesus, they saw that he was already dead so they didn’t break his legs.
JHN 19:34 34 However, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
JHN 19:35 35 The one who saw this has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he speaks the truth, and he has testified so that you also can believe.
JHN 19:36 36 These things happened to fulfill the scripture, They won’t break any of his bones .
JHN 19:37 37 And another scripture says, They will look at him whom they have pierced.
JHN 19:38 38 After this Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate if he could take away the body of Jesus. Joseph was a disciple of Jesus, but a secret one because he feared the Jewish authorities. Pilate gave him permission, so he came and took the body away.
JHN 19:39 39 Nicodemus, the one who at first had come to Jesus at night, was there too. He brought a mixture of myrrh and aloe, nearly seventy-five pounds in all.
JHN 19:40 40 Following Jewish burial customs, they took Jesus’ body and wrapped it, with the spices, in linen cloths.
JHN 19:41 41 There was a garden in the place where Jesus was crucified, and in the garden was a new tomb in which no one had ever been laid.
JHN 19:42 42 Because it was the Jewish Preparation Day and the tomb was nearby, they laid Jesus in it.
JHN 20:1 1 Early in the morning of the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and saw that the stone had been taken away from the tomb.
JHN 20:2 2 She ran to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved, and said, “They have taken the Lord from the tomb, and we don’t know where they’ve put him.”
JHN 20:3 3 Peter and the other disciple left to go to the tomb.
JHN 20:4 4 They were running together, but the other disciple ran faster than Peter and was the first to arrive at the tomb.
JHN 20:5 5 Bending down to take a look, he saw the linen cloths lying there, but he didn’t go in.
JHN 20:6 6 Following him, Simon Peter entered the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there.
JHN 20:7 7 He also saw the face cloth that had been on Jesus’ head. It wasn’t with the other clothes but was folded up in its own place.
JHN 20:8 8 Then the other disciple, the one who arrived at the tomb first, also went inside. He saw and believed.
JHN 20:9 9 They didn’t yet understand the scripture that Jesus must rise from the dead.
JHN 20:10 10 Then the disciples returned to the place where they were staying.
JHN 20:11 11 Mary stood outside near the tomb, crying. As she cried, she bent down to look into the tomb.
JHN 20:12 12 She saw two angels dressed in white, seated where the body of Jesus had been, one at the head and one at the foot.
JHN 20:13 13 The angels asked her, “Woman, why are you crying?” She replied, “They have taken away my Lord, and I don’t know where they’ve put him.”
JHN 20:14 14 As soon as she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, but she didn’t know it was Jesus.
JHN 20:15 15 Jesus said to her, “ Woman, why are you crying? Who are you looking for? ” Thinking he was the gardener, she replied, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have put him and I will get him.”
JHN 20:16 16 Jesus said to her, “ Mary. ” She turned and said to him in Aramaic, “Rabbouni” (which means Teacher ).
JHN 20:17 17 Jesus said to her, “ Don’t hold on to me, for I haven’t yet gone up to my Father. Go to my brothers and sisters and tell them, ‘I’m going up to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’ ”
JHN 20:18 18 Mary Magdalene left and announced to the disciples, “I’ve seen the Lord.” Then she told them what he said to her.
JHN 20:19 19 It was still the first day of the week. That evening, while the disciples were behind closed doors because they were afraid of the Jewish authorities, Jesus came and stood among them. He said, “ Peace be with you. ”
JHN 20:20 20 After he said this, he showed them his hands and his side. When the disciples saw the Lord, they were filled with joy.
JHN 20:21 21 Jesus said to them again, “ Peace be with you. As the Father sent me, so I am sending you. ”
JHN 20:22 22 Then he breathed on them and said, “ Receive the Holy Spirit.
JHN 20:23 23 If you forgive anyone’s sins, they are forgiven; if you don’t forgive them, they aren’t forgiven. ”
JHN 20:24 24 Thomas, the one called Didymus, one of the Twelve, wasn’t with the disciples when Jesus came.
JHN 20:25 25 The other disciples told him, “We’ve seen the Lord!” But he replied, “Unless I see the nail marks in his hands, put my finger in the wounds left by the nails, and put my hand into his side, I won’t believe.”
JHN 20:26 26 After eight days his disciples were again in a house and Thomas was with them. Even though the doors were locked, Jesus entered and stood among them. He said, “ Peace be with you. ”
JHN 20:27 27 Then he said to Thomas, “ Put your finger here. Look at my hands. Put your hand into my side. No more disbelief. Believe! ”
JHN 20:28 28 Thomas responded to Jesus, “My Lord and my God!”
JHN 20:29 29 Jesus replied, “ Do you believe because you see me? Happy are those who don’t see and yet believe. ”
JHN 20:30 30 Then Jesus did many other miraculous signs in his disciples’ presence, signs that aren’t recorded in this scroll.
JHN 20:31 31 But these things are written so that you will believe that Jesus is the Christ, God’s Son, and that believing, you will have life in his name.
JHN 21:1 1 Later, Jesus himself appeared again to his disciples at the Sea of Tiberias. This is how it happened:
JHN 21:2 2 Simon Peter, Thomas (called Didymus ), Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, Zebedee’s sons, and two other disciples were together.
JHN 21:3 3 Simon Peter told them, “I’m going fishing.” They said, “We’ll go with you.” They set out in a boat, but throughout the night they caught nothing.
JHN 21:4 4 Early in the morning, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples didn’t realize it was Jesus.
JHN 21:5 5 Jesus called to them, “ Children, have you caught anything to eat? ” They answered him, “No.”
JHN 21:6 6 He said, “ Cast your net on the right side of the boat and you will find some. ” So they did, and there were so many fish that they couldn’t haul in the net.
JHN 21:7 7 Then the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It’s the Lord!” When Simon Peter heard it was the Lord, he wrapped his coat around himself (for he was naked) and jumped into the water.
JHN 21:8 8 The other disciples followed in the boat, dragging the net full of fish, for they weren’t far from shore, only about one hundred yards.
JHN 21:9 9 When they landed, they saw a fire there, with fish on it, and some bread.
JHN 21:10 10 Jesus said to them, “ Bring some of the fish that you’ve just caught. ”
JHN 21:11 11 Simon Peter got up and pulled the net to shore. It was full of large fish, one hundred fifty-three of them. Yet the net hadn’t torn, even with so many fish.
JHN 21:12 12 Jesus said to them, “ Come and have breakfast. ” None of the disciples could bring themselves to ask him, “Who are you?” They knew it was the Lord.
JHN 21:13 13 Jesus came, took the bread, and gave it to them. He did the same with the fish.
JHN 21:14 14 This was now the third time Jesus appeared to his disciples after he was raised from the dead.
JHN 21:15 15 When they finished eating, Jesus asked Simon Peter, “ Simon son of John, do you love me more than these? ” Simon replied, “Yes, Lord, you know I love you.” Jesus said to him, “ Feed my lambs. ”
JHN 21:16 16 Jesus asked a second time, “ Simon son of John, do you love me? ” Simon replied, “Yes, Lord, you know I love you.” Jesus said to him, “ Take care of my sheep. ”
JHN 21:17 17 He asked a third time, “ Simon son of John, do you love me? ” Peter was sad that Jesus asked him a third time, “Do you love me?” He replied, “Lord, you know everything; you know I love you.” Jesus said to him, “ Feed my sheep.
