JHN 21:18 18 I assure you that when you were younger you tied your own belt and walked around wherever you wanted. When you grow old, you will stretch out your hands and another will tie your belt and lead you where you don’t want to go. ”
JHN 21:19 19 He said this to show the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God. After saying this, Jesus said to Peter, “ Follow me. ”
JHN 21:20 20 Peter turned around and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them. This was the one who had leaned against Jesus at the meal and asked him, “Lord, who is going to betray you?”
JHN 21:21 21 When Peter saw this disciple, he said to Jesus, “Lord, what about him?”
JHN 21:22 22 Jesus replied, “ If I want him to remain until I come, what difference does that make to you? You must follow me. ”
JHN 21:23 23 Therefore, the word spread among the brothers and sisters that this disciple wouldn’t die. However, Jesus didn’t say he wouldn’t die, but only, “If I want him to remain until I come, what difference does that make to you?”
JHN 21:24 24 This is the disciple who testifies concerning these things and who wrote them down. We know that his testimony is true.
JHN 21:25 25 Jesus did many other things as well. If all of them were recorded, I imagine the world itself wouldn’t have enough room for the scrolls that would be written.
ACT 1:1 1 Theophilus, the first scroll I wrote concerned everything Jesus did and taught from the beginning,
ACT 1:2 2 right up to the day when he was taken up into heaven. Before he was taken up, working in the power of the Holy Spirit, Jesus instructed the apostles he had chosen.
ACT 1:3 3 After his suffering, he showed them that he was alive with many convincing proofs. He appeared to them over a period of forty days, speaking to them about God’s kingdom.
ACT 1:4 4 While they were eating together, he ordered them not to leave Jerusalem but to wait for what the Father had promised. He said, “This is what you heard from me:
ACT 1:5 5 John baptized with water, but in only a few days you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.”
ACT 1:6 6 As a result, those who had gathered together asked Jesus, “Lord, are you going to restore the kingdom to Israel now?”
ACT 1:7 7 Jesus replied, “It isn’t for you to know the times or seasons that the Father has set by his own authority.
ACT 1:8 8 Rather, you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.”
ACT 1:9 9 After Jesus said these things, as they were watching, he was lifted up and a cloud took him out of their sight.
ACT 1:10 10 While he was going away and as they were staring toward heaven, suddenly two men in white robes stood next to them.
ACT 1:11 11 They said, “Galileans, why are you standing here, looking toward heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way that you saw him go into heaven.”
ACT 1:12 12 Then they returned to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives, which is near Jerusalem—a sabbath day’s journey away.
ACT 1:13 13 When they entered the city, they went to the upstairs room where they were staying. Peter, John, James, and Andrew; Philip and Thomas; Bartholomew and Matthew; James, Alphaeus’ son; Simon the zealot; and Judas, James’ son—
ACT 1:14 14 all were united in their devotion to prayer, along with some women, including Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.
ACT 1:15 15 During this time, the family of believers was a company of about one hundred twenty persons. Peter stood among them and said,
ACT 1:16 16 “Brothers and sisters, the scripture that the Holy Spirit announced beforehand through David had to be fulfilled. This was the scripture concerning Judas, who became a guide for those who arrested Jesus.
ACT 1:17 17 This happened even though he was one of us and received a share of this ministry.” (
ACT 1:18 18 In fact, he bought a field with the payment he received for his injustice. Falling headfirst, he burst open in the middle and all his intestines spilled out.
ACT 1:19 19 This became known to everyone living in Jerusalem, so they called that field in their own language Hakeldama, or “Field of Blood.”)
ACT 1:20 20 “It is written in the Psalms scroll, “ Let his home become deserted and let there be no one living in it; ” and “ Give his position of leadership to another. ”
ACT 1:21 21 “Therefore, we must select one of those who have accompanied us during the whole time the Lord Jesus lived among us,
ACT 1:22 22 beginning from the baptism of John until the day when Jesus was taken from us. This person must become along with us a witness to his resurrection.”
ACT 1:23 23 So they nominated two: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also known as Justus, and Matthias.
ACT 1:24 24 They prayed, “Lord, you know everyone’s deepest thoughts and desires. Show us clearly which one you have chosen from among these two
ACT 1:25 25 to take the place of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas turned away to go to his own place.”
ACT 1:26 26 When they cast lots, the lot fell on Matthias. He was added to the eleven apostles.
ACT 2:1 1 When Pentecost Day arrived, they were all together in one place.
ACT 2:2 2 Suddenly a sound from heaven like the howling of a fierce wind filled the entire house where they were sitting.
ACT 2:3 3 They saw what seemed to be individual flames of fire alighting on each one of them.
ACT 2:4 4 They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages as the Spirit enabled them to speak.
ACT 2:5 5 There were pious Jews from every nation under heaven living in Jerusalem.
ACT 2:6 6 When they heard this sound, a crowd gathered. They were mystified because everyone heard them speaking in their native languages.
ACT 2:7 7 They were surprised and amazed, saying, “Look, aren’t all the people who are speaking Galileans, every one of them?
ACT 2:8 8 How then can each of us hear them speaking in our native language?
ACT 2:9 9 Parthians, Medes, and Elamites; as well as residents of Mesopotamia, Judea, and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
ACT 2:10 10 Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the regions of Libya bordering Cyrene; and visitors from Rome (both Jews and converts to Judaism),
ACT 2:11 11 Cretans and Arabs—we hear them declaring the mighty works of God in our own languages!”
ACT 2:12 12 They were all surprised and bewildered. Some asked each other, “What does this mean?”
ACT 2:13 13 Others jeered at them, saying, “They’re full of new wine!”
ACT 2:14 14 Peter stood with the other eleven apostles. He raised his voice and declared, “Judeans and everyone living in Jerusalem! Know this! Listen carefully to my words!
ACT 2:15 15 These people aren’t drunk, as you suspect; after all, it’s only nine o’clock in the morning!
ACT 2:16 16 Rather, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
ACT 2:17 17 “ In the last days, God says, ” “ I will pour out my Spirit on all people. ” “ Your sons and daughters will prophesy. ” “ Your young will see visions. ” “ Your elders will dream dreams. ”
ACT 2:18 18 “ Even upon my servants, men and women, ” “ I will pour out my Spirit in those days, ” “ and they will prophesy. ”
ACT 2:19 19 “ I will cause wonders to occur in the heavens above ” “ and signs on the earth below, ” “ blood and fire and a cloud of smoke. ”
ACT 2:20 20 “ The sun will be changed into darkness, ” “ and the moon will be changed into blood, ” “ before the great and spectacular day of the Lord comes. ”
ACT 2:21 21 “ And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. ”
ACT 2:22 22 “Fellow Israelites, listen to these words! Jesus the Nazarene was a man whose credentials God proved to you through miracles, wonders, and signs, which God performed through him among you. You yourselves know this.
ACT 2:23 23 In accordance with God’s established plan and foreknowledge, he was betrayed. You, with the help of wicked men, had Jesus killed by nailing him to a cross.
ACT 2:24 24 God raised him up! God freed him from death’s dreadful grip, since it was impossible for death to hang on to him.
ACT 2:25 25 David says about him, “ I foresaw that the Lord was always with me; ” “ because he is at my right hand I won’t be shaken. ”
ACT 2:26 26 “ Therefore, my heart was glad ” “ and my tongue rejoiced. ” “ Moreover, my body will live in hope, ”
ACT 2:27 27 “ because you won’t abandon me to the grave, ” “ nor permit your holy one to experience decay. ”
ACT 2:28 28 “ You have shown me the paths of life; ” “ your presence will fill me with happiness. ”
ACT 2:29 29 “Brothers and sisters, I can speak confidently about the patriarch David. He died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this very day.
ACT 2:30 30 Because he was a prophet, he knew that God promised him with a solemn pledge to seat one of his descendants on his throne.
ACT 2:31 31 Having seen this beforehand, David spoke about the resurrection of Christ, that “ he wasn’t abandoned to the grave, nor did his body experience decay ”.
ACT 2:32 32 This Jesus God raised up. We are all witnesses to that fact.
ACT 2:33 33 He was exalted to God’s right side and received from the Father the promised Holy Spirit. He poured out this Spirit, and you are seeing and hearing the results of his having done so.
ACT 2:34 34 David didn’t ascend into heaven. Yet he says, “ The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right side, ”
ACT 2:35 35 “ until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.’ ”
ACT 2:36 36 “Therefore, let all Israel know beyond question that God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Christ.”
ACT 2:37 37 When the crowd heard this, they were deeply troubled. They said to Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what should we do?”
ACT 2:38 38 Peter replied, “Change your hearts and lives. Each of you must be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins. Then you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
ACT 2:39 39 This promise is for you, your children, and for all who are far away—as many as the Lord our God invites.”
ACT 2:40 40 With many other words he testified to them and encouraged them, saying, “Be saved from this perverse generation.”
ACT 2:41 41 Those who accepted Peter’s message were baptized. God brought about three thousand people into the community on that day.
ACT 2:42 42 The believers devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching, to the community, to their shared meals, and to their prayers.
ACT 2:43 43 A sense of awe came over everyone. God performed many wonders and signs through the apostles.
ACT 2:44 44 All the believers were united and shared everything.
ACT 2:45 45 They would sell pieces of property and possessions and distribute the proceeds to everyone who needed them.
ACT 2:46 46 Every day, they met together in the temple and ate in their homes. They shared food with gladness and simplicity.
ACT 2:47 47 They praised God and demonstrated God’s goodness to everyone. The Lord added daily to the community those who were being saved.
ACT 3:1 1 Peter and John were going up to the temple at three o’clock in the afternoon, the established prayer time.
ACT 3:2 2 Meanwhile, a man crippled since birth was being carried in. Every day, people would place him at the temple gate known as the Beautiful Gate so he could ask for money from those entering the temple.
ACT 3:3 3 When he saw Peter and John about to enter, he began to ask them for a gift.
ACT 3:4 4 Peter and John stared at him. Peter said, “Look at us!”
ACT 3:5 5 So the man gazed at them, expecting to receive something from them.
ACT 3:6 6 Peter said, “I don’t have any money, but I will give you what I do have. In the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, rise up and walk!”
ACT 3:7 7 Then he grasped the man’s right hand and raised him up. At once his feet and ankles became strong.
ACT 3:8 8 Jumping up, he began to walk around. He entered the temple with them, walking, leaping, and praising God.
ACT 3:9 9 All the people saw him walking and praising God.
ACT 3:10 10 They recognized him as the same one who used to sit at the temple’s Beautiful Gate asking for money. They were filled with amazement and surprise at what had happened to him.
ACT 3:11 11 While the healed man clung to Peter and John, all the people rushed toward them at Solomon’s Porch, completely amazed.
ACT 3:12 12 Seeing this, Peter addressed the people: “You Israelites, why are you amazed at this? Why are you staring at us as if we made him walk by our own power or piety?
ACT 3:13 13 The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the God of our ancestors—has glorified his servant Jesus. This is the one you handed over and denied in Pilate’s presence, even though he had already decided to release him.
ACT 3:14 14 You rejected the holy and righteous one, and asked that a murderer be released to you instead.
ACT 3:15 15 You killed the author of life, the very one whom God raised from the dead. We are witnesses of this.
ACT 3:16 16 His name itself has made this man strong. That is, because of faith in Jesus’ name, God has strengthened this man whom you see and know. The faith that comes through Jesus gave him complete health right before your eyes.
ACT 3:17 17 “Brothers and sisters, I know you acted in ignorance. So did your rulers.
ACT 3:18 18 But this is how God fulfilled what he foretold through all the prophets: that his Christ would suffer.
ACT 3:19 19 Change your hearts and lives! Turn back to God so that your sins may be wiped away.
ACT 3:20 20 Then the Lord will provide a season of relief from the distress of this age and he will send Jesus, whom he handpicked to be your Christ.
ACT 3:21 21 Jesus must remain in heaven until the restoration of all things, about which God spoke long ago through his holy prophets.
ACT 3:22 22 Moses said, “ The Lord your God will raise up from your own people a prophet like me. Listen to whatever he tells you. ”
ACT 3:23 23 “ Whoever doesn’t listen to that prophet will be totally cut off from the people. ”
ACT 3:24 24 All the prophets who spoke—from Samuel forward—announced these days.
ACT 3:25 25 You are the heirs of the prophets and the covenant that God made with your ancestors when he told Abraham, “ Through your descendants, all the families on earth will be blessed. ”
ACT 3:26 26 After God raised his servant, he sent him to you first—to bless you by enabling each of you to turn from your evil ways.”
ACT 4:1 1 While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple guard, and the Sadducees confronted them.
ACT 4:2 2 They were incensed that the apostles were teaching the people and announcing that the resurrection of the dead was happening because of Jesus.
ACT 4:3 3 They seized Peter and John and put them in prison until the next day. (It was already evening.)
ACT 4:4 4 Many who heard the word became believers, and their number grew to about five thousand.
ACT 4:5 5 The next day the leaders, elders, and legal experts gathered in Jerusalem,
ACT 4:6 6 along with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and others from the high priest’s family.
ACT 4:7 7 They had Peter and John brought before them and asked, “By what power or in what name did you do this?”
ACT 4:8 8 Then Peter, inspired by the Holy Spirit, answered, “Leaders of the people and elders,
ACT 4:9 9 are we being examined today because something good was done for a sick person, a good deed that healed him?
ACT 4:10 10 If so, then you and all the people of Israel need to know that this man stands healthy before you because of the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene—whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead.
ACT 4:11 11 This Jesus is the stone you builders rejected; he has become the cornerstone!
ACT 4:12 12 Salvation can be found in no one else. Throughout the whole world, no other name has been given among humans through which we must be saved.”
ACT 4:13 13 The council was caught by surprise by the confidence with which Peter and John spoke. After all, they understood that these apostles were uneducated and inexperienced. They also recognized that they had been followers of Jesus.
ACT 4:14 14 However, since the healed man was standing with Peter and John before their own eyes, they had no rebuttal.
ACT 4:15 15 After ordering them to wait outside, the council members began to confer with each other.
ACT 4:16 16 “What should we do with these men? Everyone living in Jerusalem is aware of the sign performed through them. It’s obvious to everyone and we can’t deny it.
ACT 4:17 17 To keep it from spreading further among the people, we need to warn them not to speak to anyone in this name.”
ACT 4:18 18 When they called Peter and John back, they demanded that they stop all speaking and teaching in the name of Jesus.
ACT 4:19 19 Peter and John responded, “It’s up to you to determine whether it’s right before God to obey you rather than God.
ACT 4:20 20 As for us, we can’t stop speaking about what we have seen and heard.”
ACT 4:21 21 They threatened them further, then released them. Because of public support for Peter and John, they couldn’t find a way to punish them. Everyone was praising God for what had happened,
ACT 4:22 22 because the man who had experienced this sign of healing was over 40 years old.
ACT 4:23 23 After their release, Peter and John returned to the brothers and sisters and reported everything the chief priests and elders had said.
ACT 4:24 24 They listened, then lifted their voices in unison to God, “Master, you are the one who created the heaven, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
ACT 4:25 25 You are the one who spoke by the Holy Spirit through our ancestor David, your servant: “ Why did the Gentiles rage ”, “ and the peoples plot in vain? ”
ACT 4:26 26 “ The kings of the earth took their stand ” “ and the rulers gathered together as one ” “ against the Lord and against his Christ. ”
ACT 4:27 27 Indeed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with Gentiles and Israelites, did gather in this city against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed.
ACT 4:28 28 They did what your power and plan had already determined would happen.
ACT 4:29 29 Now, Lord, take note of their threats and enable your servants to speak your word with complete confidence.
ACT 4:30 30 Stretch out your hand to bring healing and enable signs and wonders to be performed through the name of Jesus, your holy servant.”
ACT 4:31 31 After they prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began speaking God’s word with confidence.
ACT 4:32 32 The community of believers was one in heart and mind. None of them would say, “This is mine!” about any of their possessions, but held everything in common.
ACT 4:33 33 The apostles continued to bear powerful witness to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and an abundance of grace was at work among them all.
ACT 4:34 34 There were no needy persons among them. Those who owned properties or houses would sell them, bring the proceeds from the sales,
ACT 4:35 35 and place them in the care and under the authority of the apostles. Then it was distributed to anyone who was in need.
ACT 4:36 36 Joseph, whom the apostles nicknamed Barnabas (that is, “one who encourages”), was a Levite from Cyprus.
ACT 4:37 37 He owned a field, sold it, brought the money, and placed it in the care and under the authority of the apostles.
ACT 5:1 1 However, a man named Ananias, along with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property.
ACT 5:2 2 With his wife’s knowledge, he withheld some of the proceeds from the sale. He brought the rest and placed it in the care and under the authority of the apostles.
ACT 5:3 3 Peter asked, “Ananias, how is it that Satan has influenced you to lie to the Holy Spirit by withholding some of the proceeds from the sale of your land?
ACT 5:4 4 Wasn’t that property yours to keep? After you sold it, wasn’t the money yours to do with whatever you wanted? What made you think of such a thing? You haven’t lied to other people but to God!”
ACT 5:5 5 When Ananias heard these words, he dropped dead. Everyone who heard this conversation was terrified.
ACT 5:6 6 Some young men stood up, wrapped up his body, carried him out, and buried him.
ACT 5:7 7 About three hours later, his wife entered, but she didn’t know what had happened to her husband.
ACT 5:8 8 Peter asked her, “Tell me, did you and your husband receive this price for the field?” She responded, “Yes, that’s the amount.”
ACT 5:9 9 He replied, “How could you scheme with each other to challenge the Lord’s Spirit? Look! The feet of those who buried your husband are at the door. They will carry you out too.”
ACT 5:10 10 At that very moment, she dropped dead at his feet. When the young men entered and found her dead, they carried her out and buried her with her husband.
ACT 5:11 11 Trepidation and dread seized the whole church and all who heard what had happened.
ACT 5:12 12 The apostles performed many signs and wonders among the people. They would come together regularly at Solomon’s Porch.
ACT 5:13 13 No one from outside the church dared to join them, even though the people spoke highly of them.
ACT 5:14 14 Indeed, more and more believers in the Lord, large numbers of both men and women, were added to the church.
ACT 5:15 15 As a result, they would even bring the sick out into the main streets and lay them on cots and mats so that at least Peter’s shadow could fall on some of them as he passed by.
ACT 5:16 16 Even large numbers of persons from towns around Jerusalem would gather, bringing the sick and those harassed by unclean spirits. Everyone was healed.
ACT 5:17 17 The high priest, together with his allies, the Sadducees, was overcome with jealousy.
ACT 5:18 18 They seized the apostles and made a public show of putting them in prison.
ACT 5:19 19 An angel from the Lord opened the prison doors during the night and led them out. The angel told them,
ACT 5:20 20 “Go, take your place in the temple, and tell the people everything about this new life.”
ACT 5:21 21 Early in the morning, they went into the temple as they had been told and began to teach. When the high priest and his colleagues gathered, they convened the Jerusalem Council, that is, the full assembly of Israel’s elders. They sent word to the prison to have the apostles brought before them.
ACT 5:22 22 However, the guards didn’t find them in the prison. They returned and reported,
ACT 5:23 23 “We found the prison locked and well-secured, with guards standing at the doors, but when we opened the doors we found no one inside!”
ACT 5:24 24 When they received this news, the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests were baffled and wondered what might be happening.
ACT 5:25 25 Just then, someone arrived and announced, “Look! The people you put in prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people!”
ACT 5:26 26 Then the captain left with his guards and brought the apostles back. They didn’t use force because they were afraid the people would stone them.
ACT 5:27 27 The apostles were brought before the council where the high priest confronted them:
ACT 5:28 28 “In no uncertain terms, we demanded that you not teach in this name. And look at you! You have filled Jerusalem with your teaching. And you are determined to hold us responsible for this man’s death.”
ACT 5:29 29 Peter and the apostles replied, “We must obey God rather than humans!
ACT 5:30 30 The God of our ancestors raised Jesus from the dead—whom you killed by hanging him on a tree.
ACT 5:31 31 God has exalted Jesus to his right side as leader and savior so that he could enable Israel to change its heart and life and to find forgiveness for sins.
ACT 5:32 32 We are witnesses of such things, as is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him.”
ACT 5:33 33 When the council members heard this, they became furious and wanted to kill the apostles.
ACT 5:34 34 One council member, a Pharisee and teacher of the Law named Gamaliel, well-respected by all the people, stood up and ordered that the men be taken outside for a few moments.
ACT 5:35 35 He said, “Fellow Israelites, consider carefully what you intend to do to these people.
ACT 5:36 36 Some time ago, Theudas appeared, claiming to be somebody, and some four hundred men joined him. After he was killed, all of his followers scattered, and nothing came of that.
ACT 5:37 37 Afterward, at the time of the census, Judas the Galilean appeared and got some people to follow him in a revolt. He was killed too, and all his followers scattered far and wide.
ACT 5:38 38 Here’s my recommendation in this case: Distance yourselves from these men. Let them go! If their plan or activity is of human origin, it will end in ruin.
ACT 5:39 39 If it originates with God, you won’t be able to stop them. Instead, you would actually find yourselves fighting God!” The council was convinced by his reasoning.
ACT 5:40 40 After calling the apostles back, they had them beaten. They ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, then let them go.
ACT 5:41 41 The apostles left the council rejoicing because they had been regarded as worthy to suffer disgrace for the sake of the name.
ACT 5:42 42 Every day they continued to teach and proclaim the good news that Jesus is the Christ, both in the temple and in houses.
ACT 6:1 1 About that time, while the number of disciples continued to increase, a complaint arose. Greek-speaking disciples accused the Aramaic-speaking disciples because their widows were being overlooked in the daily food service.
ACT 6:2 2 The Twelve called a meeting of all the disciples and said, “It isn’t right for us to set aside proclamation of God’s word in order to serve tables.
ACT 6:3 3 Brothers and sisters, carefully choose seven well-respected men from among you. They must be well-respected and endowed by the Spirit with exceptional wisdom. We will put them in charge of this concern.
ACT 6:4 4 As for us, we will devote ourselves to prayer and the service of proclaiming the word.”
ACT 6:5 5 This proposal pleased the entire community. They selected Stephen, a man endowed by the Holy Spirit with exceptional faith, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolaus from Antioch, a convert to Judaism.
ACT 6:6 6 The community presented these seven to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
ACT 6:7 7 God’s word continued to grow. The number of disciples in Jerusalem increased significantly. Even a large group of priests embraced the faith.
ACT 6:8 8 Stephen, who stood out among the believers for the way God’s grace was at work in his life and for his exceptional endowment with divine power, was doing great wonders and signs among the people.
ACT 6:9 9 Opposition arose from some who belonged to the so-called Synagogue of Former Slaves. Members from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia entered into debate with Stephen.
ACT 6:10 10 However, they couldn’t resist the wisdom the Spirit gave him as he spoke.
ACT 6:11 11 Then they secretly enticed some people to claim, “We heard him insult Moses and God.”
ACT 6:12 12 They stirred up the people, the elders, and the legal experts. They caught Stephen, dragged him away, and brought him before the Jerusalem Council.
ACT 6:13 13 Before the council, they presented false witnesses who testified, “This man never stops speaking against this holy place and the Law.
ACT 6:14 14 In fact, we heard him say that this man Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and alter the customary practices Moses gave us.”
ACT 6:15 15 Everyone seated in the council stared at Stephen, and they saw that his face was radiant, just like an angel’s.
ACT 7:1 1 The high priest asked, “Are these accusations true?”
ACT 7:2 2 Stephen responded, “Brothers and fathers, listen to me. Our glorious God appeared to our ancestor Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran.
ACT 7:3 3 God told him, ‘Leave your homeland and kin, and go to the land that I will show you.’
ACT 7:4 4 So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. After Abraham’s father died, God had him resettle in this land where you now live.
ACT 7:5 5 God didn’t give him an inheritance here, not even a square foot of land. However, God did promise to give the land as his possession to him and to his descendants, even though Abraham had no child.
ACT 7:6 6 God put it this way: “ His descendants will be strangers in a land that belongs to others, who will enslave them and abuse them for four hundred years. ”
ACT 7:7 7 “ And I will condemn the nation they serve as slaves, ”God said, “ and afterward they will leave ” that land and serve me in this place.
ACT 7:8 8 God gave him the covenant confirmed through circumcision. Accordingly, eight days after Isaac’s birth, Abraham circumcised him. Isaac did the same with Jacob, and Jacob with the twelve patriarchs.
ACT 7:9 9 “Because the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph, they sold him into slavery in Egypt. God was with him, however,
ACT 7:10 10 and rescued him from all his troubles. The grace and wisdom he gave Joseph were recognized by Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who appointed him ruler over Egypt and over his whole palace.
ACT 7:11 11 A famine came upon all Egypt and Canaan, and great hardship came with it. Our ancestors had nothing to eat.
ACT 7:12 12 When Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt, he sent our ancestors there for the first time.
ACT 7:13 13 During their second visit, Joseph told his brothers who he was, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph’s family.
ACT 7:14 14 Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his relatives—seventy-five in all—and invited them to live with him.
ACT 7:15 15 So Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our ancestors died.
ACT 7:16 16 Their bodies were brought back to Shechem and placed in the tomb that Abraham had purchased for a certain sum of money from Hamor’s children, who lived in Shechem.
ACT 7:17 17 “When it was time for God to keep the promise he made to Abraham, the number of our people in Egypt had greatly expanded.
ACT 7:18 18 But then “ another king rose to power over Egypt who didn’t know anything about Joseph. ”
ACT 7:19 19 He exploited our people and abused our ancestors. He even forced them to abandon their newly born babies so they would die.
ACT 7:20 20 That’s when Moses was born. He was highly favored by God, and for three months his parents cared for him in their home.
ACT 7:21 21 After he was abandoned, Pharaoh’s daughter adopted and cared for him as though he were her own son.
ACT 7:22 22 Moses learned everything Egyptian wisdom had to offer, and he was a man of powerful words and deeds.
ACT 7:23 23 “When Moses was 40 years old, he decided to visit his family, the Israelites.
ACT 7:24 24 He saw one of them being wronged so he came to his rescue and evened the score by killing the Egyptian.
ACT 7:25 25 He expected his own kin to understand that God was using him to rescue them, but they didn’t.
ACT 7:26 26 The next day he came upon some Israelites who were caught up in an argument. He tried to make peace between them by saying, ‘You are brothers! Why are you harming each other?’
ACT 7:27 27 The one who started the fight against his neighbor pushed Moses aside and said, “ ‘Who appointed you as our leader and judge? ”
ACT 7:28 28 “ Are you planning to kill me like you killed that Egyptian yesterday?’ ”
ACT 7:29 29 When Moses heard this, he fled to Midian, where he lived as an immigrant and had two sons.
ACT 7:30 30 “Forty years later, an angel appeared to Moses in the flame of a burning bush in the wilderness near Mount Sinai.
ACT 7:31 31 Enthralled by the sight, Moses approached to get a closer look and he heard the Lord’s voice:
ACT 7:32 32 ‘“ I am the God of your ancestors, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. ”’ Trembling with fear, Moses didn’t dare to investigate any further.
ACT 7:33 33 The Lord continued, ‘“ Remove the sandals from your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground. ”
ACT 7:34 34 “ I have clearly seen the oppression my people have experienced in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning. I have come down to rescue them. Come! I am sending you to Egypt ”.’
ACT 7:35 35 “This is the same Moses whom they rejected when they asked, ‘Who appointed you as our leader and judge?’ This is the Moses whom God sent as leader and deliverer. God did this with the help of the angel who appeared before him in the bush.
ACT 7:36 36 This man led them out after he performed wonders and signs in Egypt at the Red Sea and for forty years in the wilderness.
ACT 7:37 37 This is the Moses who told the Israelites, ‘“ God will raise up for you a prophet like me from your own people. ”’
ACT 7:38 38 This is the one who was in the assembly in the wilderness with our ancestors and with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai. He is the one who received life-giving words to give to us.
ACT 7:39 39 He’s also the one whom our ancestors refused to obey. Instead, they pushed him aside and, in their thoughts and desires, returned to Egypt.
ACT 7:40 40 They told Aaron, ‘“ Make us gods that will lead us. As for this Moses who led us out of Egypt, we don’t know what’s happened to him! ”’
ACT 7:41 41 That’s when they made an idol in the shape of a calf, offered a sacrifice to it, and began to celebrate what they had made with their own hands.
ACT 7:42 42 So God turned away from them and handed them over to worship the stars in the sky, just as it is written in the scroll of the Prophets: “ Did you bring sacrifices and offerings to me ” “ for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel? ”
ACT 7:43 43 “ No! Instead, you took the tent of Moloch with you, ” “ and the star of your god Rephan, ” “ the images that you made in order to worship them. ” “ Therefore, I will send you far away, farther than Babylon. ”
ACT 7:44 44 “The tent of testimony was with our ancestors in the wilderness. Moses built it just as he had been instructed by the one who spoke to him and according to the pattern he had seen.
ACT 7:45 45 In time, when they had received the tent, our ancestors carried it with them when, under Joshua’s leadership, they took possession of the land from the nations whom God expelled. This tent remained in the land until the time of David.
ACT 7:46 46 God approved of David, who asked that he might provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
ACT 7:47 47 But it was Solomon who actually built a house for God.
ACT 7:48 48 However, the Most High doesn’t live in houses built by human hands. As the prophet says,
ACT 7:49 49 “ Heaven is my throne, ” “ and the earth is my footstool. ” “ ‘What kind of house will you build for me,’ says the Lord, ” “ ‘or where is my resting place? ”
ACT 7:50 50 “ Didn’t I make all these things with my own hand?’ ”
ACT 7:51 51 “You stubborn people! In your thoughts and hearing, you are like those who have had no part in God’s covenant! You continuously set yourself against the Holy Spirit, just like your ancestors did.
ACT 7:52 52 Was there a single prophet your ancestors didn’t harass? They even killed those who predicted the coming of the righteous one, and you’ve betrayed and murdered him!
ACT 7:53 53 You received the Law given by angels, but you haven’t kept it.”
ACT 7:54 54 Once the council members heard these words, they were enraged and began to grind their teeth at Stephen.
ACT 7:55 55 But Stephen, enabled by the Holy Spirit, stared into heaven and saw God’s majesty and Jesus standing at God’s right side.
ACT 7:56 56 He exclaimed, “Look! I can see heaven on display and the Human One standing at God’s right side!”
ACT 7:57 57 At this, they shrieked and covered their ears. Together, they charged at him,
ACT 7:58 58 threw him out of the city, and began to stone him. The witnesses placed their coats in the care of a young man named Saul.
ACT 7:59 59 As they battered him with stones, Stephen prayed, “Lord Jesus, accept my life!”
ACT 7:60 60 Falling to his knees, he shouted, “Lord, don’t hold this sin against them!” Then he died.
ACT 8:1 1 Saul was in full agreement with Stephen’s murder. At that time, the church in Jerusalem began to be subjected to vicious harassment. Everyone except the apostles was scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria.
ACT 8:2 2 Some pious men buried Stephen and deeply grieved over him.
ACT 8:3 3 Saul began to wreak havoc against the church. Entering one house after another, he would drag off both men and women and throw them into prison.
ACT 8:4 4 Those who had been scattered moved on, preaching the good news along the way.
ACT 8:5 5 Philip went down to a city in Samaria and began to preach Christ to them.
ACT 8:6 6 The crowds were united by what they heard Philip say and the signs they saw him perform, and they gave him their undivided attention.
ACT 8:7 7 With loud shrieks, unclean spirits came out of many people, and many who were paralyzed or crippled were healed.
ACT 8:8 8 There was great rejoicing in that city.
ACT 8:9 9 Before Philip’s arrival, a certain man named Simon had practiced sorcery in that city and baffled the people of Samaria. He claimed to be a great person.
ACT 8:10 10 Everyone, from the least to the greatest, gave him their undivided attention and referred to him as “the power of God called Great.”
ACT 8:11 11 He had their attention because he had baffled them with sorcery for a long time.
ACT 8:12 12 After they came to believe Philip, who preached the good news about God’s kingdom and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized.
ACT 8:13 13 Even Simon himself came to believe and was baptized. Afterward, he became one of Philip’s supporters. As he saw firsthand the signs and great miracles that were happening, he was astonished.
ACT 8:14 14 When word reached the apostles in Jerusalem that Samaria had accepted God’s word, they commissioned Peter and John to go to Samaria.
ACT 8:15 15 Peter and John went down to Samaria where they prayed that the new believers would receive the Holy Spirit. (
ACT 8:16 16 This was because the Holy Spirit had not yet fallen on any of them; they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)
ACT 8:17 17 So Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
ACT 8:18 18 When Simon perceived that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money.
ACT 8:19 19 He said, “Give me this authority too so that anyone on whom I lay my hands will receive the Holy Spirit.”
ACT 8:20 20 Peter responded, “May your money be condemned to hell along with you because you believed you could buy God’s gift with money!
ACT 8:21 21 You can have no part or share in God’s word because your heart isn’t right with God.
ACT 8:22 22 Therefore, change your heart and life! Turn from your wickedness! Plead with the Lord in the hope that your wicked intent can be forgiven,
ACT 8:23 23 for I see that your bitterness has poisoned you and evil has you in chains.”
ACT 8:24 24 Simon replied, “All of you, please, plead to the Lord for me so that nothing of what you have said will happen to me!”
ACT 8:25 25 After the apostles had testified and proclaimed the Lord’s word, they returned to Jerusalem, preaching the good news to many Samaritan villages along the way.
ACT 8:26 26 An angel from the Lord spoke to Philip, “At noon, take the road that leads from Jerusalem to Gaza.” (This is a desert road.)
ACT 8:27 27 So he did. Meanwhile, an Ethiopian man was on his way home from Jerusalem, where he had come to worship. He was a eunuch and an official responsible for the entire treasury of Candace. (Candace is the title given to the Ethiopian queen.)
ACT 8:28 28 He was reading the prophet Isaiah while sitting in his carriage.
ACT 8:29 29 The Spirit told Philip, “Approach this carriage and stay with it.”
ACT 8:30 30 Running up to the carriage, Philip heard the man reading the prophet Isaiah. He asked, “Do you really understand what you are reading?”
ACT 8:31 31 The man replied, “Without someone to guide me, how could I?” Then he invited Philip to climb up and sit with him.
ACT 8:32 32 This was the passage of scripture he was reading: “ Like a sheep he was led to the slaughter ” “ and like a lamb before its shearer is silent ” “ so he didn’t open his mouth. ”
ACT 8:33 33 “ In his humiliation justice was taken away from him. ” “ Who can tell the story of his descendants ” “ because his life was taken from the earth? ”
ACT 8:34 34 The eunuch asked Philip, “Tell me, about whom does the prophet say this? Is he talking about himself or someone else?”
ACT 8:35 35 Starting with that passage, Philip proclaimed the good news about Jesus to him.
ACT 8:36 36 As they went down the road, they came to some water. The eunuch said, “Look! Water! What would keep me from being baptized?”
ACT 8:37 38 He ordered that the carriage halt. Both Philip and the eunuch went down to the water, where Philip baptized him.
ACT 8:38 39 When they came up out of the water, the Lord’s Spirit suddenly took Philip away. The eunuch never saw him again but went on his way rejoicing.
ACT 8:39 40 Philip found himself in Azotus. He traveled through that area, preaching the good news in all the cities until he reached Caesarea.
ACT 9:1 1 Meanwhile, Saul was still spewing out murderous threats against the Lord’s disciples. He went to the high priest,
ACT 9:2 2 seeking letters to the synagogues in Damascus. If he found persons who belonged to the Way, whether men or women, these letters would authorize him to take them as prisoners to Jerusalem.
ACT 9:3 3 During the journey, as he approached Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven encircled him.
ACT 9:4 4 He fell to the ground and heard a voice asking him, “Saul, Saul, why are you harassing me?”
ACT 9:5 5 Saul asked, “Who are you, Lord?” “I am Jesus, whom you are harassing,” came the reply.
ACT 9:6 6 “Now get up and enter the city. You will be told what you must do.”
ACT 9:7 7 Those traveling with him stood there speechless; they heard the voice but saw no one.
ACT 9:8 8 After they picked Saul up from the ground, he opened his eyes but he couldn’t see. So they led him by the hand into Damascus.
ACT 9:9 9 For three days he was blind and neither ate nor drank anything.
ACT 9:10 10 In Damascus there was a certain disciple named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision, “Ananias!” He answered, “Yes, Lord.”
ACT 9:11 11 The Lord instructed him, “Go to Judas’ house on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul. He is praying.
ACT 9:12 12 In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias enter and put his hands on him to restore his sight.”
ACT 9:13 13 Ananias countered, “Lord, I have heard many reports about this man. People say he has done horrible things to your holy people in Jerusalem.
ACT 9:14 14 He’s here with authority from the chief priests to arrest everyone who calls on your name.”
ACT 9:15 15 The Lord replied, “Go! This man is the agent I have chosen to carry my name before Gentiles, kings, and Israelites.
ACT 9:16 16 I will show him how much he must suffer for the sake of my name.”
ACT 9:17 17 Ananias went to the house. He placed his hands on Saul and said, “Brother Saul, the Lord sent me—Jesus, who appeared to you on the way as you were coming here. He sent me so that you could see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
ACT 9:18 18 Instantly, flakes fell from Saul’s eyes and he could see again. He got up and was baptized.
ACT 9:19 19 After eating, he regained his strength. He stayed with the disciples in Damascus for several days.
ACT 9:20 20 Right away, he began to preach about Jesus in the synagogues. “He is God’s Son,” he declared.
ACT 9:21 21 Everyone who heard him was baffled. They questioned each other, “Isn’t he the one who was wreaking havoc among those in Jerusalem who called on this name? Hadn’t he come here to take those same people as prisoners to the chief priests?”
ACT 9:22 22 But Saul grew stronger and stronger. He confused the Jews who lived in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ.
ACT 9:23 23 After this had gone on for some time, the Jews hatched a plot to kill Saul.
ACT 9:24 24 However, he found out about their scheme. They were keeping watch at the city gates around the clock so they could assassinate him.
ACT 9:25 25 But his disciples took him by night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the city wall.
ACT 9:26 26 When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him. They didn’t believe he was really a disciple.
ACT 9:27 27 Then Barnabas brought Saul to the apostles and told them the story about how Saul saw the Lord on the way and that the Lord had spoken to Saul. He also told them about the confidence with which Saul had preached in the name of Jesus in Damascus.
ACT 9:28 28 After this, Saul moved freely among the disciples in Jerusalem and was speaking with confidence in the name of the Lord.
ACT 9:29 29 He got into debates with the Greek-speaking Jews as well, but they tried to kill him.
ACT 9:30 30 When the family of believers learned about this, they escorted him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.
ACT 9:31 31 Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria enjoyed a time of peace. God strengthened the church, and its life was marked by reverence for the Lord. Encouraged by the Holy Spirit, the church continued to grow in numbers.
ACT 9:32 32 As Peter toured the whole region, he went to visit God’s holy people in Lydda.
ACT 9:33 33 There he found a man named Aeneas who was paralyzed and had been confined to his bed for eight years.
ACT 9:34 34 Peter said to him, “Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you! Get up and make your bed.” At once he got up.
ACT 9:35 35 Everyone who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.
ACT 9:36 36 In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (in Greek her name is Dorcas). Her life overflowed with good works and compassionate acts on behalf of those in need.
ACT 9:37 37 About that time, though, she became so ill that she died. After they washed her body, they laid her in an upstairs room.
ACT 9:38 38 Since Lydda was near Joppa, when the disciples heard that Peter was there, they sent two people to Peter. They urged, “Please come right away!”
ACT 9:39 39 Peter went with them. Upon his arrival, he was taken to the upstairs room. All the widows stood beside him, crying as they showed the tunics and other clothing Dorcas made when she was alive.
ACT 9:40 40 Peter sent everyone out of the room, then knelt and prayed. He turned to the body and said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, saw Peter, and sat up.
ACT 9:41 41 He gave her his hand and raised her up. Then he called God’s holy people, including the widows, and presented her alive to them.
ACT 9:42 42 The news spread throughout Joppa, and many put their faith in the Lord.
ACT 9:43 43 Peter stayed for some time in Joppa with a certain tanner named Simon.
ACT 10:1 1 There was a man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion in the Italian Company.
ACT 10:2 2 He and his whole household were pious, Gentile God-worshippers. He gave generously to those in need among the Jewish people and prayed to God constantly.
ACT 10:3 3 One day at nearly three o’clock in the afternoon, he clearly saw an angel from God in a vision. The angel came to him and said, “Cornelius!”
ACT 10:4 4 Startled, he stared at the angel and replied, “What is it, Lord?” The angel said, “Your prayers and your compassionate acts are like a memorial offering to God.
ACT 10:5 5 Send messengers to Joppa at once and summon a certain Simon, the one known as Peter.
ACT 10:6 6 He is a guest of Simon the tanner, whose house is near the seacoast.”
ACT 10:7 7 When the angel who was speaking to him had gone, Cornelius summoned two of his household servants along with a pious soldier from his personal staff.
ACT 10:8 8 He explained everything to them, then sent them to Joppa.
ACT 10:9 9 At noon on the following day, as their journey brought them close to the city, Peter went up on the roof to pray.
ACT 10:10 10 He became hungry and wanted to eat. While others were preparing the meal, he had a visionary experience.
ACT 10:11 11 He saw heaven opened up and something like a large linen sheet being lowered to the earth by its four corners.
ACT 10:12 12 Inside the sheet were all kinds of four-legged animals, reptiles, and wild birds.
ACT 10:13 13 A voice told him, “Get up, Peter! Kill and eat!”
ACT 10:14 14 Peter exclaimed, “Absolutely not, Lord! I have never eaten anything impure or unclean.”
ACT 10:15 15 The voice spoke a second time, “Never consider unclean what God has made pure.”
ACT 10:16 16 This happened three times, then the object was suddenly pulled back into heaven.
ACT 10:17 17 Peter was bewildered about the meaning of the vision. Just then, the messengers sent by Cornelius discovered the whereabouts of Simon’s house and arrived at the gate.
ACT 10:18 18 Calling out, they inquired whether the Simon known as Peter was a guest there.
ACT 10:19 19 While Peter was brooding over the vision, the Spirit interrupted him, “Look! Three people are looking for you.
ACT 10:20 20 Go downstairs. Don’t ask questions; just go with them because I have sent them.”
ACT 10:21 21 So Peter went downstairs and told them, “I’m the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”
ACT 10:22 22 They replied, “We’ve come on behalf of Cornelius, a centurion and righteous man, a God-worshipper who is well-respected by all Jewish people. A holy angel directed him to summon you to his house and to hear what you have to say.”
ACT 10:23 23 Peter invited them into the house as his guests. The next day he got up and went with them, together with some of the believers from Joppa.
ACT 10:24 24 They arrived in Caesarea the following day. Anticipating their arrival, Cornelius had gathered his relatives and close friends.
ACT 10:25 25 As Peter entered the house, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet in order to honor him.
ACT 10:26 26 But Peter lifted him up, saying, “Get up! Like you, I’m just a human.”
ACT 10:27 27 As they continued to talk, Peter went inside and found a large gathering of people.
ACT 10:28 28 He said to them, “You all realize that it is forbidden for a Jew to associate or visit with outsiders. However, God has shown me that I should never call a person impure or unclean.
ACT 10:29 29 For this reason, when you sent for me, I came without objection. I want to know, then, why you sent for me.”
ACT 10:30 30 Cornelius answered, “Four days ago at this same time, three o’clock in the afternoon, I was praying at home. Suddenly a man in radiant clothing stood before me.
ACT 10:31 31 He said, ‘Cornelius, God has heard your prayers, and your compassionate acts are like a memorial offering to him.
ACT 10:32 32 Therefore, send someone to Joppa and summon Simon, who is known as Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, located near the seacoast.’
ACT 10:33 33 I sent for you right away, and you were kind enough to come. Now, here we are, gathered in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has directed you to say.”
ACT 10:34 34 Peter said, “I really am learning that God doesn’t show partiality to one group of people over another.
ACT 10:35 35 Rather, in every nation, whoever worships him and does what is right is acceptable to him.
ACT 10:36 36 This is the message of peace he sent to the Israelites by proclaiming the good news through Jesus Christ: He is Lord of all!
ACT 10:37 37 You know what happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee after the baptism John preached.
ACT 10:38 38 You know about Jesus of Nazareth, whom God anointed with the Holy Spirit and endowed with power. Jesus traveled around doing good and healing everyone oppressed by the devil because God was with him.
ACT 10:39 39 We are witnesses of everything he did, both in Judea and in Jerusalem. They killed him by hanging him on a tree,
ACT 10:40 40 but God raised him up on the third day and allowed him to be seen,
ACT 10:41 41 not by everyone but by us. We are witnesses whom God chose beforehand, who ate and drank with him after God raised him from the dead.
ACT 10:42 42 He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one whom God appointed as judge of the living and the dead.
ACT 10:43 43 All the prophets testify about him that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name.”
ACT 10:44 44 While Peter was still speaking, the Holy Spirit fell on everyone who heard the word.
ACT 10:45 45 The circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles.
ACT 10:46 46 They heard them speaking in other languages and praising God. Peter asked,
ACT 10:47 47 “These people have received the Holy Spirit just as we have. Surely no one can stop them from being baptized with water, can they?”
ACT 10:48 48 He directed that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they invited Peter to stay for several days.
ACT 11:1 1 The apostles and the brothers and sisters throughout Judea heard that even the Gentiles had welcomed God’s word.
ACT 11:2 2 When Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers criticized him.
ACT 11:3 3 They accused him, “You went into the home of the uncircumcised and ate with them!”
ACT 11:4 4 Step-by-step, Peter explained what had happened.
ACT 11:5 5 “I was in the city of Joppa praying when I had a visionary experience. In my vision, I saw something like a large linen sheet being lowered from heaven by its four corners. It came all the way down to me.
ACT 11:6 6 As I stared at it, wondering what it was, I saw four-legged animals—including wild beasts—as well as reptiles and wild birds.
ACT 11:7 7 I heard a voice say, ‘Get up, Peter! Kill and eat!’
ACT 11:8 8 I responded, ‘Absolutely not, Lord! Nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’
ACT 11:9 9 The voice from heaven spoke a second time, ‘Never consider unclean what God has made pure.’
ACT 11:10 10 This happened three times, then everything was pulled back into heaven.
ACT 11:11 11 At that moment three men who had been sent to me from Caesarea arrived at the house where we were staying.
ACT 11:12 12 The Spirit told me to go with them even though they were Gentiles. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered that man’s house.
ACT 11:13 13 He reported to us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is known as Peter.
ACT 11:14 14 He will tell you how you and your entire household can be saved.’
ACT 11:15 15 When I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, just as the Spirit fell on us in the beginning.
ACT 11:16 16 I remembered the Lord’s words: ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
ACT 11:17 17 If God gave them the same gift he gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, then who am I? Could I stand in God’s way?”
ACT 11:18 18 Once the apostles and other believers heard this, they calmed down. They praised God and concluded, “So then God has enabled Gentiles to change their hearts and lives so that they might have new life.”
ACT 11:19 19 Now those who were scattered as a result of the trouble that occurred because of Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They proclaimed the word only to Jews.
ACT 11:20 20 Among them were some people from Cyprus and Cyrene. They entered Antioch and began to proclaim the good news about the Lord Jesus also to Gentiles.
ACT 11:21 21 The Lord’s power was with them, and a large number came to believe and turned to the Lord.
ACT 11:22 22 When the church in Jerusalem heard about this, they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
ACT 11:23 23 When he arrived and saw evidence of God’s grace, he was overjoyed and encouraged everyone to remain fully committed to the Lord.
ACT 11:24 24 Barnabas responded in this way because he was a good man, whom the Holy Spirit had endowed with exceptional faith. A considerable number of people were added to the Lord.
ACT 11:25 25 Barnabas went to Tarsus in search of Saul.
ACT 11:26 26 When he found him, he brought him to Antioch. They were there for a whole year, meeting with the church and teaching large numbers of people. It was in Antioch where the disciples were first labeled “Christians.”
ACT 11:27 27 About that time, some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
ACT 11:28 28 One of them, Agabus, stood up and, inspired by the Spirit, predicted that a severe famine would overtake the entire Roman world. (This occurred during Claudius’ rule.)
ACT 11:29 29 The disciples decided they would send support to the brothers and sisters in Judea, with everyone contributing to this ministry according to each person’s abundance.
ACT 11:30 30 They sent Barnabas and Saul to take this gift to the elders.
ACT 12:1 1 About that time King Herod began to harass some who belonged to the church.
ACT 12:2 2 He had James, John’s brother, killed with a sword.
ACT 12:3 3 When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he arrested Peter as well. This happened during the Festival of Unleavened Bread.
ACT 12:4 4 He put Peter in prison, handing him over to four squads of soldiers, sixteen in all, who guarded him. He planned to charge him publicly after the Passover.
ACT 12:5 5 While Peter was held in prison, the church offered earnest prayer to God for him.
ACT 12:6 6 The night before Herod was going to bring Peter’s case forward, Peter was asleep between two soldiers and bound with two chains, with soldiers guarding the prison entrance.
ACT 12:7 7 Suddenly an angel from the Lord appeared and a light shone in the prison cell. After nudging Peter on his side to awaken him, the angel raised him up and said, “Quick! Get up!” The chains fell from his wrists.
ACT 12:8 8 The angel continued, “Get dressed. Put on your sandals.” Peter did as he was told. The angel said, “Put on your coat and follow me.”
ACT 12:9 9 Following the angel, Peter left the prison. However, he didn’t realize the angel had actually done all this. He thought he was seeing a vision.
ACT 12:10 10 They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city. It opened for them by itself. After leaving the prison, they proceeded the length of one street, when abruptly the angel was gone.
ACT 12:11 11 At that, Peter came to his senses and remarked, “Now I’m certain that the Lord sent his angel and rescued me from Herod and from everything the Jewish people expected.”
ACT 12:12 12 Realizing this, he made his way to Mary’s house. (Mary was John’s mother; he was also known as Mark.) Many believers had gathered there and were praying.
ACT 12:13 13 When Peter knocked at the outer gate, a female servant named Rhoda went to answer.
ACT 12:14 14 She was so overcome with joy when she recognized Peter’s voice that she didn’t open the gate. Instead, she ran back in and announced that Peter was standing at the gate.
ACT 12:15 15 “You’ve lost your mind!” they responded. She stuck by her story with such determination that they began to say, “It must be his guardian angel.”
ACT 12:16 16 Meanwhile, Peter remained outside, knocking at the gate. They finally opened the gate and saw him there, and they were astounded.
ACT 12:17 17 He gestured with his hand to quiet them down, then recounted how the Lord led him out of prison. He said, “Tell this to James and the brothers and sisters.” Then he left for another place.
ACT 12:18 18 The next morning the soldiers were flustered about what had happened to Peter.
ACT 12:19 19 Herod called for a thorough search. When Peter didn’t turn up, Herod interrogated the guards and had them executed. Afterward, Herod left Judea in order to spend some time in Caesarea.
ACT 12:20 20 Herod had been furious with the people of Tyre and Sidon for some time. They made a pact to approach him together, since their region depended on the king’s realm for its food supply. They persuaded Blastus, the king’s personal attendant, to join their cause, then appealed for an end to hostilities.
ACT 12:21 21 On the scheduled day Herod dressed himself in royal attire, seated himself on the throne, and gave a speech to the people.
ACT 12:22 22 Those assembled kept shouting, over and over, “This is a god’s voice, not the voice of a mere human!”
ACT 12:23 23 Immediately an angel from the Lord struck Herod down, because he didn’t give the honor to God. He was eaten by worms and died.
ACT 12:24 24 God’s word continued to grow and increase.
ACT 12:25 25 Barnabas and Saul returned to Antioch from Jerusalem after completing their mission, bringing with them John, who was also known as Mark.
ACT 13:1 1 The church at Antioch included prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon (nicknamed Niger), Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen (a childhood friend of Herod the ruler), and Saul.
ACT 13:2 2 As they were worshipping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Appoint Barnabas and Saul to the work I have called them to undertake.”
ACT 13:3 3 After they fasted and prayed, they laid their hands on these two and sent them off.
ACT 13:4 4 After the Holy Spirit sent them on their way, they went down to Seleucia. From there they sailed to Cyprus.
ACT 13:5 5 In Salamis they proclaimed God’s word in the Jewish synagogues. John was with them as their assistant.
ACT 13:6 6 They traveled throughout the island until they arrived at Paphos. There they found a certain man named Bar-Jesus, a Jew who was a false prophet and practiced sorcery.
ACT 13:7 7 He kept company with the governor of that province, an intelligent man named Sergius Paulus. The governor sent for Barnabas and Saul since he wanted to hear God’s word.
ACT 13:8 8 But Elymas the sorcerer (for that’s what people understood his name meant) opposed them, trying to steer the governor away from the faith.
ACT 13:9 9 Empowered by the Holy Spirit, Saul, also known as Paul, glared at Bar-Jesus and
ACT 13:10 10 said, “You are a deceiver and trickster! You devil! You attack anything that is right! Will you never stop twisting the straight ways of the Lord into crooked paths?
ACT 13:11 11 Listen! The Lord’s power is set against you. You will be blind for a while, unable even to see the daylight.” At once, Bar-Jesus’ eyes were darkened, and he began to grope about for someone to lead him around by the hand.
ACT 13:12 12 When the governor saw what had taken place, he came to believe, for he was astonished by the teaching about the Lord.
ACT 13:13 13 Paul and his companions sailed from Paphos to Perga in Pamphylia. John deserted them there and returned to Jerusalem.
ACT 13:14 14 They went on from Perga and arrived at Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath, they entered and found seats in the synagogue there.
ACT 13:15 15 After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders invited them, “Brothers, if one of you has a sermon for the people, please speak.”
ACT 13:16 16 Standing up, Paul gestured with his hand and said, “Fellow Israelites and Gentile God-worshippers, please listen to me.
ACT 13:17 17 The God of this people Israel chose our ancestors. God made them a great people while they lived as strangers in the land of Egypt. With his great power, he led them out of that country.
ACT 13:18 18 For about forty years, God put up with them in the wilderness.
ACT 13:19 19 God conquered seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave the Israelites their land as an inheritance.
ACT 13:20 20 This happened over a period of about four hundred fifty years. “After this, he gave them judges until the time of the prophet Samuel.
ACT 13:21 21 The Israelites requested a king, so God gave them Saul, Kish’s son, from the tribe of Benjamin, and he served as their king for forty years.
ACT 13:22 22 After God removed him, he raised up David to be their king. God testified concerning him, ‘“ I have found ” David, Jesse’s son, “ a man who shares my desires. ” Whatever my will is, he will do.’
ACT 13:23 23 From this man’s descendants, God brought to Israel a savior, Jesus, just as he promised.
ACT 13:24 24 Before Jesus’ appearance, John proclaimed to all the Israelites a baptism to show they were changing their hearts and lives.
ACT 13:25 25 As John was completing his mission, he said, ‘Who do you think I am? I’m not the one you think I am, but he is coming after me. I’m not worthy to loosen his sandals.’
ACT 13:26 26 “Brothers, children of Abraham’s family, and you Gentile God-worshippers, the message about this salvation has been sent to us.
ACT 13:27 27 The people in Jerusalem and their leaders didn’t recognize Jesus. By condemning him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
ACT 13:28 28 Even though they didn’t find a single legal basis for the death penalty, they asked Pilate to have him executed.
ACT 13:29 29 When they finished doing everything that had been written about him, they took him down from the cross and laid him in a tomb.
ACT 13:30 30 But God raised him from the dead!
ACT 13:31 31 He appeared over many days to those who had traveled with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses to the people.
ACT 13:32 32 “We proclaim to you the good news. What God promised to our ancestors,
ACT 13:33 33 he has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it was written in the second psalm, “ You are my son; today I have become your father. ”
ACT 13:34 34 “God raised Jesus from the dead, never again to be subjected to death’s decay. Therefore, God said, “ I will give to you the holy and firm promises I made to David. ”
ACT 13:35 35 In another place it is said, “ You will not let your holy one experience death’s decay. ”
ACT 13:36 36 David served God’s purpose in his own generation, then he died and was buried with his ancestors. He experienced death’s decay,
ACT 13:37 37 but the one whom God has raised up didn’t experience death’s decay.
ACT 13:38 38 “Therefore, brothers and sisters, know this: Through Jesus we proclaim forgiveness of sins to you. From all those sins from which you couldn’t be put in right relationship with God through Moses’ Law,
ACT 13:39 39 through Jesus everyone who believes is put in right relationship with God.
ACT 13:40 40 Take care that the prophets’ words don’t apply to you:
ACT 13:41 41 “ Look, you scoffers ”, “ marvel and die ”. “ I’m going to do work in your day — ” “ a work you won’t believe ” “ even if someone told you ”.”
ACT 13:42 42 As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people urged them to speak about these things again on the next Sabbath.
ACT 13:43 43 When the people in the synagogue were dismissed, many Jews and devout converts to Judaism accompanied Paul and Barnabas, who urged them to remain faithful to the message of God’s grace.
ACT 13:44 44 On the next Sabbath, almost everyone in the city gathered to hear the Lord’s word.
ACT 13:45 45 When the Jews saw the crowds, they were overcome with jealousy. They argued against what Paul was saying by slandering him.
ACT 13:46 46 Speaking courageously, Paul and Barnabas said, “We had to speak God’s word to you first. Since you reject it and show that you are unworthy to receive eternal life, we will turn to the Gentiles.
ACT 13:47 47 This is what the Lord commanded us: “ I have made you a light for the Gentiles, ” “ so that you could bring salvation to the end of the earth ”.”
ACT 13:48 48 When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and honored the Lord’s word. Everyone who was appointed for eternal life believed,
ACT 13:49 49 and the Lord’s word was broadcast throughout the entire region.
ACT 13:50 50 However, the Jews provoked the prominent women among the Gentile God-worshippers, as well as the city’s leaders. They instigated others to harass Paul and Barnabas, and threw them out of their district.
ACT 13:51 51 Paul and Barnabas shook the dust from their feet and went to Iconium.
ACT 13:52 52 Because of the abundant presence of the Holy Spirit in their lives, the disciples were overflowing with happiness.
ACT 14:1 1 The same thing happened in Iconium. Paul and Barnabas entered the Jewish synagogue and spoke as they had before. As a result, a huge number of Jews and Greeks believed.
ACT 14:2 2 However, the Jews who rejected the faith stirred up the Gentiles, poisoning their minds against the brothers.
ACT 14:3 3 Nevertheless, Paul and Barnabas stayed there for quite some time, confidently speaking about the Lord. And the Lord confirmed the word about his grace by the signs and wonders he enabled them to perform.
ACT 14:4 4 The people of the city were divided—some siding with the Jews, others with the Lord’s messengers.
ACT 14:5 5 Then some Gentiles and Jews, including their leaders, hatched a plot to mistreat and stone Paul and Barnabas.
ACT 14:6 6 When they learned of it, these two messengers fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and the surrounding area,
ACT 14:7 7 where they continued to proclaim the good news.
ACT 14:8 8 In Lystra there was a certain man who lacked strength in his legs. He had been crippled since birth and had never walked. Sitting there, he
ACT 14:9 9 heard Paul speaking. Paul stared at him and saw that he believed he could be healed.
ACT 14:10 10 Raising his voice, Paul said, “Stand up straight on your feet!” He jumped up and began to walk.
ACT 14:11 11 Seeing what Paul had done, the crowd shouted in the Lycaonian language, “The gods have taken human form and come down to visit us!”
ACT 14:12 12 They referred to Barnabas as Zeus and to Paul as Hermes, since Paul was the main speaker.
ACT 14:13 13 The priest of Zeus, whose temple was located just outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates. Along with the crowds, he wanted to offer sacrifices to them.
ACT 14:14 14 When the Lord’s messengers Barnabas and Paul found out about this, they tore their clothes in protest and rushed out into the crowd. They shouted,
ACT 14:15 15 “People, what are you doing? We are humans too, just like you! We are proclaiming the good news to you: turn to the living God and away from such worthless things. He “ made the heaven, the earth, the sea, and everything in them. ”
ACT 14:16 16 In the past, he permitted every nation to go its own way.
ACT 14:17 17 Nevertheless, he hasn’t left himself without a witness. He has blessed you by giving you rain from above as well as seasonal harvests, and satisfying you with food and happiness.”
ACT 14:18 18 Even with these words, they barely kept the crowds from sacrificing to them.
ACT 14:19 19 Jews from Antioch and Iconium arrived and won the crowds over. They stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, supposing he was dead.
ACT 14:20 20 When the disciples surrounded him, he got up and entered the city again. The following day he left with Barnabas for Derbe.
ACT 14:21 21 Paul and Barnabas proclaimed the good news to the people in Derbe and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch, where
ACT 14:22 22 they strengthened the disciples and urged them to remain firm in the faith. They told them, “If we are to enter God’s kingdom, we must pass through many troubles.”
ACT 14:23 23 They appointed elders for each church. With prayer and fasting, they committed these elders to the Lord, in whom they had placed their trust.
ACT 14:24 24 After Paul and Barnabas traveled through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
ACT 14:25 25 They proclaimed the word in Perga, then went down to Attalia.
ACT 14:26 26 From there they sailed to Antioch, where they had been entrusted by God’s grace to the work they had now completed.
ACT 14:27 27 On their arrival, they gathered the church together and reported everything that God had accomplished through their activity, and how God had opened a door of faith for the Gentiles.
ACT 14:28 28 They stayed with the disciples a long time.
ACT 15:1 1 Some people came down from Judea teaching the family of believers, “Unless you are circumcised according to the custom we’ve received from Moses, you can’t be saved.”
ACT 15:2 2 Paul and Barnabas took sides against these Judeans and argued strongly against their position. The church at Antioch appointed Paul, Barnabas, and several others from Antioch to go up to Jerusalem to set this question before the apostles and the elders.
ACT 15:3 3 The church sent this delegation on their way. They traveled through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling stories about the conversion of the Gentiles to everyone. Their reports thrilled the brothers and sisters.
ACT 15:4 4 When they arrived in Jerusalem, the church, the apostles, and the elders all welcomed them. They gave a full report of what God had accomplished through their activity.
ACT 15:5 5 Some believers from among the Pharisees stood up and claimed, “The Gentiles must be circumcised. They must be required to keep the Law from Moses.”
ACT 15:6 6 The apostles and the elders gathered to consider this matter.
ACT 15:7 7 After much debate, Peter stood and addressed them, “Fellow believers, you know that, early on, God chose me from among you as the one through whom the Gentiles would hear the word of the gospel and come to believe.
ACT 15:8 8 God, who knows people’s deepest thoughts and desires, confirmed this by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us.
ACT 15:9 9 He made no distinction between us and them, but purified their deepest thoughts and desires through faith.
ACT 15:10 10 Why then are you now challenging God by placing a burden on the shoulders of these disciples that neither we nor our ancestors could bear?
ACT 15:11 11 On the contrary, we believe that we and they are saved in the same way, by the grace of the Lord Jesus.”
ACT 15:12 12 The entire assembly fell quiet as they listened to Barnabas and Paul describe all the signs and wonders God did among the Gentiles through their activity.
ACT 15:13 13 When Barnabas and Paul also fell silent, James responded, “Fellow believers, listen to me.
ACT 15:14 14 Simon reported how, in his kindness, God came to the Gentiles in the first place, to raise up from them a people of God.
ACT 15:15 15 The prophets’ words agree with this; as it is written,
ACT 15:16 16 “ After this I will return, ” “ and I will rebuild David’s fallen tent; ” “ I will rebuild what has been torn down. ” “ I will restore it ”
ACT 15:17 17 “ so that the rest of humanity will seek the Lord, ” “ even all the Gentiles who belong to me. ” “ The Lord says this, the one who does these things ”
ACT 15:18 18 known from earliest times.
ACT 15:19 19 “Therefore, I conclude that we shouldn’t create problems for Gentiles who turn to God.
ACT 15:20 20 Instead, we should write a letter, telling them to avoid the pollution associated with idols, sexual immorality, eating meat from strangled animals, and consuming blood.
ACT 15:21 21 After all, Moses has been proclaimed in every city for a long time, and is read aloud every Sabbath in every synagogue.”
ACT 15:22 22 The apostles and the elders, along with the entire church, agreed to send some delegates chosen from among themselves to Antioch, together with Paul and Barnabas. They selected Judas Barsabbas and Silas, who were leaders among the brothers and sisters.
ACT 15:23 23 They were to carry this letter: The apostles and the elders, to the Gentile brothers and sisters in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia. Greetings!
ACT 15:24 24 We’ve heard that some of our number have disturbed you with unsettling words we didn’t authorize.
ACT 15:25 25 We reached a united decision to select some delegates and send them to you along with our dear friends Barnabas and Paul.
ACT 15:26 26 These people have devoted their lives to the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
ACT 15:27 27 Therefore, we are sending Judas and Silas. They will confirm what we have written.
ACT 15:28 28 The Holy Spirit has led us to the decision that no burden should be placed on you other than these essentials:
ACT 15:29 29 refuse food offered to idols, blood, the meat from strangled animals, and sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid such things. Farewell.
ACT 15:30 30 When Barnabas, Paul, and the delegates were sent on their way, they went down to Antioch. They gathered the believers and delivered the letter.
ACT 15:31 31 The people read it, delighted with its encouraging message.
ACT 15:32 32 Judas and Silas were prophets, and they said many things that encouraged and strengthened the brothers and sisters.
ACT 15:33 33 Judas and Silas stayed there awhile, then were sent back with a blessing of peace from the brothers and sisters to those who first sent them.
ACT 15:34 35 Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch, where, together with many others, they taught and proclaimed the good news of the Lord’s word.
ACT 15:35 36 Some time later, Paul said to Barnabas, “Let’s go back and visit all the brothers and sisters in every city where we preached the Lord’s word. Let’s see how they are doing.”
ACT 15:36 37 Barnabas wanted to take John Mark with them.
ACT 15:37 38 Paul insisted that they shouldn’t take him along, since he had deserted them in Pamphylia and hadn’t continued with them in their work.
ACT 15:38 39 Their argument became so intense that they went their separate ways. Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus.
ACT 15:39 40 Paul chose Silas and left, entrusted by the brothers and sisters to the Lord’s grace.
ACT 15:40 41 He traveled through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
ACT 16:1 1 Paul reached Derbe, and then Lystra, where there was a disciple named Timothy. He was the son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father.
ACT 16:2 2 The brothers and sisters in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
ACT 16:3 3 Paul wanted to take Timothy with him, so he circumcised him. This was because of the Jews who lived in those areas, for they all knew Timothy’s father was Greek.
ACT 16:4 4 As Paul and his companions traveled through the cities, they instructed Gentile believers to keep the regulations put in place by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.
ACT 16:5 5 So the churches were strengthened in the faith and every day their numbers flourished.
ACT 16:6 6 Paul and his companions traveled throughout the regions of Phrygia and Galatia because the Holy Spirit kept them from speaking the word in the province of Asia.
ACT 16:7 7 When they approached the province of Mysia, they tried to enter the province of Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus wouldn’t let them.
ACT 16:8 8 Passing by Mysia, they went down to Troas instead.
ACT 16:9 9 A vision of a man from Macedonia came to Paul during the night. He stood urging Paul, “Come over to Macedonia and help us!”
ACT 16:10 10 Immediately after he saw the vision, we prepared to leave for the province of Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to proclaim the good news to them.
ACT 16:11 11 We sailed from Troas straight for Samothrace and came to Neapolis the following day.
ACT 16:12 12 From there we went to Philippi, a city of Macedonia’s first district and a Roman colony. We stayed in that city several days.
ACT 16:13 13 On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate to the riverbank, where we thought there might be a place for prayer. We sat down and began to talk with the women who had gathered.
ACT 16:14 14 One of those women was Lydia, a Gentile God-worshipper from the city of Thyatira, a dealer in purple cloth. As she listened, the Lord enabled her to embrace Paul’s message.
ACT 16:15 15 Once she and her household were baptized, she urged, “Now that you have decided that I am a believer in the Lord, come and stay in my house.” And she persuaded us.
ACT 16:16 16 One day, when we were on the way to the place for prayer, we met a slave woman. She had a spirit that enabled her to predict the future. She made a lot of money for her owners through fortune-telling.
ACT 16:17 17 She began following Paul and us, shouting, “These people are servants of the Most High God! They are proclaiming a way of salvation to you!”
ACT 16:18 18 She did this for many days. This annoyed Paul so much that he finally turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I command you to leave her!” It left her at that very moment.
