ACT 16:19 19 Her owners realized that their hope for making money was gone. They grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them before the officials in the city center.
ACT 16:20 20 When her owners approached the legal authorities, they said, “These people are causing an uproar in our city. They are Jews
ACT 16:21 21 who promote customs that we Romans can’t accept or practice.”
ACT 16:22 22 The crowd joined in the attacks against Paul and Silas, so the authorities ordered that they be stripped of their clothes and beaten with a rod.
ACT 16:23 23 When Paul and Silas had been severely beaten, the authorities threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to secure them with great care.
ACT 16:24 24 When he received these instructions, he threw them into the innermost cell and secured their feet in stocks.
ACT 16:25 25 Around midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
ACT 16:26 26 All at once there was such a violent earthquake that it shook the prison’s foundations. The doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.
ACT 16:27 27 When the jailer awoke and saw the open doors of the prison, he thought the prisoners had escaped, so he drew his sword and was about to kill himself.
ACT 16:28 28 But Paul shouted loudly, “Don’t harm yourself! We’re all here!”
ACT 16:29 29 The jailer called for some lights, rushed in, and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.
ACT 16:30 30 He led them outside and asked, “Honorable masters, what must I do to be rescued?”
ACT 16:31 31 They replied, “Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved—you and your entire household.”
ACT 16:32 32 They spoke the Lord’s word to him and everyone else in his house.
ACT 16:33 33 Right then, in the middle of the night, the jailer welcomed them and washed their wounds. He and everyone in his household were immediately baptized.
ACT 16:34 34 He brought them into his home and gave them a meal. He was overjoyed because he and everyone in his household had come to believe in God.
ACT 16:35 35 The next morning the legal authorities sent the police to the jailer with the order “Release those people.”
ACT 16:36 36 So the jailer reported this to Paul, informing him, “The authorities sent word that you both are to be released. You can leave now. Go in peace.”
ACT 16:37 37 Paul told the police, “Even though we are Roman citizens, they beat us publicly without first finding us guilty of a crime, and they threw us into prison. And now they want to send us away secretly? No way! They themselves will have to come and escort us out.”
ACT 16:38 38 The police reported this to the legal authorities, who were alarmed to learn that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
ACT 16:39 39 They came and consoled Paul and Silas, escorting them out of prison and begging them to leave the city.
ACT 16:40 40 Paul and Silas left the prison and made their way to Lydia’s house where they encouraged the brothers and sisters. Then they left Philippi.
ACT 17:1 1 Paul and Silas journeyed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, then came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.
ACT 17:2 2 As was Paul’s custom, he entered the synagogue and for three Sabbaths interacted with them on the basis of the scriptures.
ACT 17:3 3 Through his interpretation of the scriptures, he demonstrated that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. He declared, “This Jesus whom I proclaim to you is the Christ.”
ACT 17:4 4 Some were convinced and joined Paul and Silas, including a larger number of Greek God-worshippers and quite a few prominent women.
ACT 17:5 5 But the Jews became jealous and brought along some thugs who were hanging out in the marketplace. They formed a mob and started a riot in the city. They attacked Jason’s house, intending to bring Paul and Silas before the people.
ACT 17:6 6 When they didn’t find them, they dragged Jason and some believers before the city officials. They were shouting, “These people who have been disturbing the peace throughout the empire have also come here.
ACT 17:7 7 What is more, Jason has welcomed them into his home. Every one of them does what is contrary to Caesar’s decrees by naming someone else as king: Jesus.”
ACT 17:8 8 This provoked the crowd and the city officials even more.
ACT 17:9 9 After Jason and the others posted bail, they released them.
ACT 17:10 10 As soon as it was dark, the brothers and sisters sent Paul and Silas on to Beroea. When they arrived, they went to the Jewish synagogue.
ACT 17:11 11 The Beroean Jews were more honorable than those in Thessalonica. This was evident in the great eagerness with which they accepted the word and examined the scriptures each day to see whether Paul and Silas’ teaching was true.
ACT 17:12 12 Many came to believe, including a number of reputable Greek women and many Greek men.
ACT 17:13 13 The Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul also proclaimed God’s word in Beroea, so they went there too and were upsetting and disturbing the crowds.
ACT 17:14 14 The brothers and sisters sent Paul away to the seacoast at once, but Silas and Timothy remained at Beroea.
ACT 17:15 15 Those who escorted Paul led him as far as Athens, then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to come to him as quickly as possible.
ACT 17:16 16 While Paul waited for them in Athens, he was deeply distressed to find that the city was flooded with idols.
ACT 17:17 17 He began to interact with the Jews and Gentile God-worshippers in the synagogue. He also addressed whoever happened to be in the marketplace each day.
ACT 17:18 18 Certain Epicurean and Stoic philosophers engaged him in discussion too. Some said, “What an amateur! What’s he trying to say?” Others remarked, “He seems to be a proclaimer of foreign gods.” (They said this because he was preaching the good news about Jesus and the resurrection.)
ACT 17:19 19 They took him into custody and brought him to the council on Mars Hill. “What is this new teaching? Can we learn what you are talking about?
ACT 17:20 20 You’ve told us some strange things and we want to know what they mean.” (
ACT 17:21 21 They said this because all Athenians as well as the foreigners who live in Athens used to spend their time doing nothing but talking about or listening to the newest thing.)
ACT 17:22 22 Paul stood up in the middle of the council on Mars Hill and said, “People of Athens, I see that you are very religious in every way.
ACT 17:23 23 As I was walking through town and carefully observing your objects of worship, I even found an altar with this inscription: ‘To an unknown God.’ What you worship as unknown, I now proclaim to you.
ACT 17:24 24 God, who made the world and everything in it, is Lord of heaven and earth. He doesn’t live in temples made with human hands.
ACT 17:25 25 Nor is God served by human hands, as though he needed something, since he is the one who gives life, breath, and everything else.
ACT 17:26 26 From one person God created every human nation to live on the whole earth, having determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands.
ACT 17:27 27 God made the nations so they would seek him, perhaps even reach out to him and find him. In fact, God isn’t far away from any of us.
ACT 17:28 28 In God we live, move, and exist. As some of your own poets said, ‘We are his offspring.’
ACT 17:29 29 “Therefore, as God’s offspring, we have no need to imagine that the divine being is like a gold, silver, or stone image made by human skill and thought.
ACT 17:30 30 God overlooks ignorance of these things in times past, but now directs everyone everywhere to change their hearts and lives.
ACT 17:31 31 This is because God has set a day when he intends to judge the world justly by a man he has appointed. God has given proof of this to everyone by raising him from the dead.”
ACT 17:32 32 When they heard about the resurrection from the dead, some began to ridicule Paul. However, others said, “We’ll hear from you about this again.”
ACT 17:33 33 At that, Paul left the council.
ACT 17:34 34 Some people joined him and came to believe, including Dionysius, a member of the council on Mars Hill, a woman named Damaris, and several others.
ACT 18:1 1 After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.
ACT 18:2 2 There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus. He had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all Jews to leave Rome. Paul visited with them.
ACT 18:3 3 Because they practiced the same trade, he stayed and worked with them. They all worked with leather.
ACT 18:4 4 Every Sabbath he interacted with people in the synagogue, trying to convince both Jews and Greeks.
ACT 18:5 5 Once Silas and Timothy arrived from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus was the Christ.
ACT 18:6 6 When they opposed and slandered him, he shook the dust from his clothes in protest and said to them, “You are responsible for your own fates! I’m innocent! From now on I’ll go to the Gentiles!”
ACT 18:7 7 He left the synagogue and went next door to the home of Titius Justus, a Gentile God-worshipper.
ACT 18:8 8 Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his entire household came to believe in the Lord. Many Corinthians believed and were baptized after listening to Paul.
ACT 18:9 9 One night the Lord said to Paul in a vision, “Don’t be afraid. Continue speaking. Don’t be silent.
ACT 18:10 10 I’m with you and no one who attacks you will harm you, for I have many people in this city.”
ACT 18:11 11 So he stayed there for eighteen months, teaching God’s word among them.
ACT 18:12 12 Now when Gallio was the governor of the province of Achaia, the Jews united in their opposition against Paul and brought him before the court.
ACT 18:13 13 “This man is persuading others to worship God unlawfully,” they declared.
ACT 18:14 14 Just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio said to the Jews, “If there had been some sort of injury or criminal behavior, I would have reason to accept your complaint.
ACT 18:15 15 However, since these are squabbles about a message, names, and your own Law, deal with them yourselves. I have no desire to sit in judgment over such things.”
ACT 18:16 16 He expelled them from the court,
ACT 18:17 17 but everyone seized Sosthenes, the synagogue leader, and gave him a beating in the presence of the governor. None of this mattered to Gallio.
ACT 18:18 18 After Paul stayed in Corinth for some time, he said good-bye to the brothers and sisters. At the Corinthian seaport of Cenchreae he had his head shaved, since he had made a solemn promise. Then, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila, he sailed away to Syria.
ACT 18:19 19 After they arrived in Ephesus, he left Priscilla and Aquila and entered the synagogue and interacted with the Jews.
ACT 18:20 20 They asked him to stay longer, but he declined.
ACT 18:21 21 As he said farewell to them, though, he added, “God willing, I will return.” Then he sailed off from Ephesus.
ACT 18:22 22 He arrived in Caesarea, went up to Jerusalem and greeted the church, and then went down to Antioch.
ACT 18:23 23 After some time there he left and traveled from place to place in the region of Galatia and the district of Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
ACT 18:24 24 Meanwhile, a certain Jew named Apollos arrived in Ephesus. He was a native of Alexandria and was well-educated and effective in his use of the scriptures.
ACT 18:25 25 He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and spoke as one stirred up by the Spirit. He taught accurately the things about Jesus, even though he was aware only of the baptism John proclaimed and practiced.
ACT 18:26 26 He began speaking with confidence in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they received him into their circle of friends and explained to him God’s way more accurately.
ACT 18:27 27 When he wanted to travel to Achaia, the brothers and sisters encouraged him and wrote to the disciples so they would open their homes to him. Once he arrived, he was of great help to those who had come to believe through grace.
ACT 18:28 28 He would vigorously defeat Jewish arguments in public debate, using the scriptures to prove that Jesus was the Christ.
ACT 19:1 1 While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul took a route through the interior and came to Ephesus, where he found some disciples.
ACT 19:2 2 He asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you came to believe?” They replied, “We’ve not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
ACT 19:3 3 Then he said, “What baptism did you receive, then?” They answered, “John’s baptism.”
ACT 19:4 4 Paul explained, “John baptized with a baptism by which people showed they were changing their hearts and lives. It was a baptism that told people about the one who was coming after him. This is the one in whom they were to believe. This one is Jesus.”
ACT 19:5 5 After they listened to Paul, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
ACT 19:6 6 When Paul placed his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they began speaking in other languages and prophesying.
ACT 19:7 7 Altogether, there were about twelve people.
ACT 19:8 8 Paul went to the synagogue and spoke confidently for the next three months. He interacted with those present and offered convincing arguments concerning the nature of God’s kingdom.
ACT 19:9 9 Some people had closed their minds, though. They refused to believe and publicly slandered the Way. As a result, Paul left them, took the disciples with him, and continued his daily interactions in Tyrannus’ lecture hall.
ACT 19:10 10 This went on for two years, so that everyone living in the province of Asia—both Jews and Greeks—heard the Lord’s word.
ACT 19:11 11 God was doing unusual miracles through Paul.
ACT 19:12 12 Even the small towels and aprons that had touched his skin were taken to the sick, and their diseases were cured and the evil spirits left them.
ACT 19:13 13 There were some Jews who traveled around throwing out evil spirits. They tried to use the power of the name of the Lord Jesus against some people with evil spirits. They said, “In the name of the Jesus whom Paul preaches, I command you!”
ACT 19:14 14 The seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
ACT 19:15 15 The evil spirit replied, “I know Jesus and I’m familiar with Paul, but who are you?”
ACT 19:16 16 The person who had an evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all with such force that they ran out of that house naked and wounded.
ACT 19:17 17 This became known to the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus. Everyone was seized with fear and they held the name of the Lord Jesus in the highest regard.
ACT 19:18 18 Many of those who had come to believe came, confessing their past practices.
ACT 19:19 19 This included a number of people who practiced sorcery. They collected their sorcery texts and burned them publicly. The value of those materials was calculated at more than someone might make if they worked for one hundred sixty-five years.
ACT 19:20 20 In this way the Lord’s word grew abundantly and strengthened powerfully.
ACT 19:21 21 Once these things had come to an end, Paul, guided by the Spirit, decided to return to Jerusalem, taking a route that would carry him through the provinces of Macedonia and Achaia. He said, “After I have been there, I must visit Rome as well.”
ACT 19:22 22 He sent two of his assistants, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he remained awhile in the province of Asia.
ACT 19:23 23 At that time a great disturbance erupted about the Way.
ACT 19:24 24 There was a silversmith named Demetrius. He made silver models of Artemis’ temple, and his business generated a lot of profit for the craftspeople.
ACT 19:25 25 He called a meeting with these craftspeople and others working in related trades and said, “Friends, you know that we make an easy living from this business.
ACT 19:26 26 And you can see and hear that this Paul has convinced and misled a lot of people, not only in Ephesus but also throughout most of the province of Asia. He says that gods made by human hands aren’t really gods.
ACT 19:27 27 This poses a danger not only by discrediting our trade but also by completely dishonoring the great goddess Artemis. The whole province of Asia—indeed, the entire civilized world—worships her, but her splendor will soon be extinguished.”
ACT 19:28 28 Once they heard this, they were beside themselves with anger and began to shout, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
ACT 19:29 29 The city was thrown into turmoil. They rushed as one into the theater. They seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s traveling companions from the province of Macedonia.
ACT 19:30 30 Paul wanted to appear before the assembly, but the disciples wouldn’t allow him.
ACT 19:31 31 Even some officials of the province of Asia, who were Paul’s friends, sent word to him, urging him not to risk going into the theater.
ACT 19:32 32 Meanwhile, the assembly was in a state of confusion. Some shouted one thing, others shouted something else, and most of the crowd didn’t know why they had gathered.
ACT 19:33 33 The Jews sent Alexander to the front, and some of the crowd directed their words toward him. He gestured that he wanted to offer a defense before the assembly,
ACT 19:34 34 but when they realized he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!” This continued for about two hours.
ACT 19:35 35 The city manager brought order to the crowd and said, “People of Ephesus, doesn’t everyone know that the city of Ephesus is guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?
ACT 19:36 36 Therefore, since these facts are undeniable, you must calm down. Don’t be reckless.
ACT 19:37 37 The men you brought here have neither robbed the temple nor slandered our goddess.
ACT 19:38 38 Therefore, if Demetrius and the craftspeople with him have a charge against anyone, the courts are in session and governors are available. They can press charges against each other there.
ACT 19:39 39 Additional disputes can be resolved in a legal assembly.
ACT 19:40 40 As for us, we are in danger of being charged with rioting today, since we can’t justify this unruly gathering.”
ACT 19:41 41 After he said this, he dismissed the assembly.
ACT 20:1 1 When the riot was over, Paul sent for the disciples, encouraged them, said good-bye, and left for the province of Macedonia.
ACT 20:2 2 He traveled through that region with a message of encouragement. When he came to Greece,
ACT 20:3 3 he stayed for three months. Because the Jews hatched a plot against Paul as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided instead to return through Macedonia.
ACT 20:4 4 He was accompanied by Sopater, Pyrrhus’ son from Beroea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.
ACT 20:5 5 They went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.
ACT 20:6 6 We sailed from Philippi after the Festival of Unleavened Bread and met them five days later in Troas, where we stayed for a week.
ACT 20:7 7 On the first day of the week, as we gathered together for a meal, Paul was holding a discussion with them. Since he was leaving the next day, he continued talking until midnight.
ACT 20:8 8 There were many lamps in the upstairs room where we had gathered.
ACT 20:9 9 A young man named Eutychus was sitting in the window. He was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third floor and died.
ACT 20:10 10 Paul went down, fell on him and embraced him, then said, “Don’t be alarmed. He’s alive!”
ACT 20:11 11 Then Paul went back upstairs and ate. He talked for a long time—right up until daybreak—then he left.
ACT 20:12 12 They took the young man away alive, and they were greatly comforted.
ACT 20:13 13 We went on to the ship and sailed for Assos, where we intended to take Paul on board. Paul had arranged this, since he intended to make his way there by land.
ACT 20:14 14 When he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.
ACT 20:15 15 The next day we sailed from there and arrived opposite Chios. On the day after, we sailed to Samos, and on the following day we came to Miletus.
ACT 20:16 16 Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus so that he wouldn’t need to spend too much time in the province of Asia. He was hurrying to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by Pentecost Day.
ACT 20:17 17 From Miletus he sent a message to Ephesus calling for the church’s elders to meet him.
ACT 20:18 18 When they arrived, he said to them, “You know how I lived among you the whole time I was with you, beginning with the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.
ACT 20:19 19 I served the Lord with great humility and with tears in the midst of trials that came upon me because of the Jews’ schemes.
ACT 20:20 20 You know I held back nothing that would be helpful so that I could proclaim to you and teach you both publicly and privately in your homes.
ACT 20:21 21 You know I have testified to both Jews and Greeks that they must change their hearts and lives as they turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
ACT 20:22 22 Now, compelled by the Spirit, I’m going to Jerusalem. I don’t know what will happen to me there.
ACT 20:23 23 What I do know is that the Holy Spirit testifies to me from city to city that prisons and troubles await me.
ACT 20:24 24 But nothing, not even my life, is more important than my completing my mission. This is nothing other than the ministry I received from the Lord Jesus: to testify about the good news of God’s grace.
ACT 20:25 25 “I know that none of you will see me again—you among whom I traveled and proclaimed the kingdom.
ACT 20:26 26 Therefore, today I testify to you that I’m not responsible for anyone’s fate.
ACT 20:27 27 I haven’t avoided proclaiming the entire plan of God to you.
ACT 20:28 28 Watch yourselves and the whole flock, in which the Holy Spirit has placed you as supervisors, to shepherd God’s church, which he obtained with the death of his own Son.
ACT 20:29 29 I know that, after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and won’t spare the flock.
ACT 20:30 30 Some of your own people will distort the word in order to lure followers after them.
ACT 20:31 31 Stay alert! Remember that for three years I constantly and tearfully warned each one of you. I never stopped warning you!
ACT 20:32 32 Now I entrust you to God and the message of his grace, which is able to build you up and give you an inheritance among all whom God has made holy.
ACT 20:33 33 I haven’t craved anyone’s silver, gold, or clothing.
ACT 20:34 34 You yourselves know that I have provided for my own needs and for those of my companions with my own hands.
ACT 20:35 35 In everything I have shown you that, by working hard, we must help the weak. In this way we remember the Lord Jesus’ words: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
ACT 20:36 36 After he said these things, he knelt down with all of them to pray.
ACT 20:37 37 They cried uncontrollably as everyone embraced and kissed Paul.
ACT 20:38 38 They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see him again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
ACT 21:1 1 After we tore ourselves away from them, we set sail on a straight course to Cos, reaching Rhodes the next day, and then Patara.
ACT 21:2 2 We found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, boarded, and put out to sea.
ACT 21:3 3 We spotted Cyprus, but passed by it on our left. We sailed on to the province of Syria and landed in Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.
ACT 21:4 4 We found the disciples there and stayed with them for a week. Compelled by the Spirit, they kept telling Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
ACT 21:5 5 When our time had come to an end, we departed. All of them, including women and children, accompanied us out of town where we knelt on the beach and prayed.
ACT 21:6 6 We said good-bye to each other, then we boarded the ship and they returned to their homes.
ACT 21:7 7 Continuing our voyage, we sailed from Tyre and arrived in Ptolemais. We greeted the brothers and sisters there and spent a day with them.
ACT 21:8 8 The next day we left and came to Caesarea. We went to the house of Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven, and stayed with him.
ACT 21:9 9 He had four unmarried daughters who were involved in the work of prophecy.
ACT 21:10 10 After staying there for several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
ACT 21:11 11 He came to us, took Paul’s belt, tied his own feet and hands, and said, “This is what the Holy Spirit says: ‘In Jerusalem the Jews will bind the man who owns this belt, and they will hand him over to the Gentiles.’”
ACT 21:12 12 When we heard this, we and the local believers urged Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
ACT 21:13 13 Paul replied, “Why are you doing this? Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I’m ready not only to be arrested but even to die in Jerusalem for the sake of the name of the Lord Jesus.”
ACT 21:14 14 Since we couldn’t talk him out of it, the only thing we could say was, “The Lord’s will be done.”
ACT 21:15 15 After this, we got ready and made our way up to Jerusalem.
ACT 21:16 16 Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us and led us to Mnason’s home, where we were guests. He was from Cyprus and had been a disciple a long time.
ACT 21:17 17 When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers and sisters welcomed us warmly.
ACT 21:18 18 On the next day Paul and the rest of us went to see James. All of the elders were present.
ACT 21:19 19 After greeting them, he gave them a detailed report of what God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
ACT 21:20 20 Those who heard this praised God. Then they said to him, “Brother, you see how many thousands of Jews have become believers, and all of them keep the Law passionately.
ACT 21:21 21 They have been informed that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to reject Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children nor to live according to our customs.
ACT 21:22 22 What about this? Without a doubt, they will hear that you have arrived.
ACT 21:23 23 You must therefore do what we tell you. Four men among us have made a solemn promise.
ACT 21:24 24 Take them with you, go through the purification ritual with them, and pay the cost of having their heads shaved. Everyone will know there is nothing to those reports about you but that you too live a life in keeping with the Law.
ACT 21:25 25 As for the Gentile believers, we wrote a letter about what we decided, that they avoid food offered to idols, blood, the meat from strangled animals, and sexual immorality.”
ACT 21:26 26 The following day Paul took the men with him and went through the purification ritual with them. He entered the temple and publicly announced the completion of the days of purification, when the offering would be presented for each one of them.
ACT 21:27 27 When the seven days of purification were almost over, the Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul in the temple. Grabbing him, they threw the whole crowd into confusion by shouting,
ACT 21:28 28 “Fellow Israelites! Help! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people, the Law, and this place. Not only that, he has even brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.” (
ACT 21:29 29 They said this because they had seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him earlier, and they assumed Paul had brought him into the temple.)
ACT 21:30 30 The entire city was stirred up. The people came rushing, seized Paul, and dragged him out of the temple. Immediately the gates were closed.
ACT 21:31 31 While they were trying to kill him, a report reached the commander of a company of soldiers that all Jerusalem was in a state of confusion.
ACT 21:32 32 Without a moment’s hesitation, he took some soldiers and officers and ran down to the mob. When the mob saw the commander and his soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
ACT 21:33 33 When the commander arrived, he arrested Paul and ordered him to be bound with two chains. Only then did he begin to ask who Paul was and what he had done.
ACT 21:34 34 Some in the crowd shouted one thing, others shouted something else. Because of the commotion, he couldn’t learn the truth, so he ordered that Paul be taken to the military headquarters.
ACT 21:35 35 When Paul reached the steps, he had to be carried by the soldiers in order to protect him from the violence of the crowd.
ACT 21:36 36 The mob that followed kept screaming, “Away with him!”
ACT 21:37 37 As Paul was about to be taken into the military headquarters, he asked the commander, “May I speak with you?” He answered, “Do you know Greek?
ACT 21:38 38 Aren’t you the Egyptian who started a revolt and led four thousand terrorists into the desert some time ago?”
ACT 21:39 39 Paul replied, “I’m a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of an important city. Please, let me speak to the people.”
ACT 21:40 40 With the commander’s permission, Paul stood on the steps and gestured to the people. When they were quiet, he addressed them in Aramaic.
ACT 22:1 1 “Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense.”
ACT 22:2 2 When they heard him address them in Aramaic, they became even more quiet.
ACT 22:3 3 Paul continued, “I’m a Jew, born in Tarsus in Cilicia but raised in this city. Under Gamaliel’s instruction, I was trained in the strict interpretation of our ancestral Law. I am passionately loyal to God, just like you who are gathered here today.
ACT 22:4 4 I harassed those who followed this Way to their death, arresting and delivering both men and women into prison.
ACT 22:5 5 The high priest and the whole Jerusalem Council can testify about me. I received letters from them, addressed to our associates in Damascus, then went there to bring those who were arrested to Jerusalem so they could be punished.
ACT 22:6 6 “During that journey, about noon, as I approached Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven encircled me.
ACT 22:7 7 I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you harassing me?’
ACT 22:8 8 I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ ‘I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you are harassing,’ he replied.
ACT 22:9 9 My traveling companions saw the light, but they didn’t hear the voice of the one who spoke to me.
ACT 22:10 10 I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ ‘Get up,’ the Lord replied, ‘and go into Damascus. There you will be told everything you have been appointed to do.’
ACT 22:11 11 I couldn’t see because of the brightness of that light, so my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.
ACT 22:12 12 “There was a certain man named Ananias. According to the standards of the Law, he was a pious man who enjoyed the respect of all the Jews living there.
ACT 22:13 13 He came and stood beside me. ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ he said. Instantly, I regained my sight and I could see him.
ACT 22:14 14 He said, ‘The God of our ancestors has selected you to know his will, to see the righteous one, and to hear his voice.
ACT 22:15 15 You will be his witness to everyone concerning what you have seen and heard.
ACT 22:16 16 What are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and wash away your sins as you call on his name.’
ACT 22:17 17 “When I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, I had a visionary experience.
ACT 22:18 18 I saw the Lord speaking to me. ‘Hurry!’ he said. ‘Leave Jerusalem at once because they won’t accept your testimony about me.’
ACT 22:19 19 I responded, ‘Lord, these people know I used to go from one synagogue to the next, beating those who believe in you and throwing them into prison.
ACT 22:20 20 When Stephen your witness was being killed, I stood there giving my approval, even watching the clothes that belonged to those who were killing him.’
ACT 22:21 21 Then the Lord said to me, ‘Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’”
ACT 22:22 22 The crowd listened to Paul until he said this. Then they shouted, “Away with this man! He’s not fit to live!”
ACT 22:23 23 As they were screaming, throwing off their garments, and flinging dust into the air,
ACT 22:24 24 the commander directed that Paul be taken into the military headquarters. He ordered that Paul be questioned under the whip so that he could find out why they were shouting at him like this.
ACT 22:25 25 As they were stretching him out and tying him down with straps, Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Can you legally whip a Roman citizen who hasn’t been found guilty in court?”
ACT 22:26 26 When the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and reported it. He asked, “What are you about to do? This man is a Roman citizen!”
ACT 22:27 27 The commander went to Paul and demanded, “Tell me! Are you a Roman citizen?” He said, “Yes.”
ACT 22:28 28 The commander replied, “It cost me a lot of money to buy my citizenship.” Paul said, “I’m a citizen by birth.”
ACT 22:29 29 At once those who were about to examine him stepped away. The commander was alarmed when he realized he had bound a Roman citizen.
ACT 22:30 30 The commander still wanted to know the truth about why Paul was being accused by the Jews. Therefore, the next day he ordered the chief priests and the entire Jerusalem Council to assemble. Then he took Paul out of prison and had him stand before them.
ACT 23:1 1 Paul stared at the council and said, “Brothers, I have lived my life with an altogether clear conscience right up to this very day.”
ACT 23:2 2 The high priest Ananias ordered those standing beside Paul to strike him in the mouth.
ACT 23:3 3 Then Paul said to him, “God is about to strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit and judge me according to the Law, yet disobey the Law by ordering that I be struck.”
ACT 23:4 4 Those standing near him asked, “You dare to insult God’s high priest?”
ACT 23:5 5 Paul replied, “Brothers, I wasn’t aware that he was the high priest. It is written, “ You will not speak evil about a ruler of your people ”.”
ACT 23:6 6 Knowing that some of them were Sadducees and the others Pharisees, Paul exclaimed in the council, “Brothers, I’m a Pharisee and a descendant of Pharisees. I am on trial because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead!”
ACT 23:7 7 These words aroused a dispute between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.
ACT 23:8 8 This is because Sadducees say that there’s no resurrection, angel, or spirit, but Pharisees affirm them all.
ACT 23:9 9 Council members were shouting loudly. Some Pharisees who were legal experts stood up and insisted forcefully, “We find nothing wrong with this man! What if a spirit or angel has spoken to him?”
ACT 23:10 10 The dispute became so heated that the commander feared they might tear Paul to pieces. He ordered soldiers to go down and remove him by force from their midst. Then they took him back to the military headquarters.
ACT 23:11 11 The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, “Be encouraged! Just as you have testified about me in Jerusalem, so too you must testify in Rome.”
ACT 23:12 12 The next morning some Jewish leaders formulated a plot and solemnly promised that they wouldn’t eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
ACT 23:13 13 More than forty people were involved in the conspiracy.
ACT 23:14 14 They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have solemnly promised to eat nothing until we have killed Paul.
ACT 23:15 15 You and the council must explain to the commander that you need Paul brought down to you. Pretend that you want to examine his case more closely. We’re prepared to kill him before he arrives.”
ACT 23:16 16 Paul’s sister had a son who heard about the ambush and he came to the military headquarters and reported it to Paul.
ACT 23:17 17 Paul called for one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander because he has something to report to him.”
ACT 23:18 18 He took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner Paul asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”
ACT 23:19 19 The commander took him by the hand and withdrew to a place where they could speak privately. He asked, “What do you have to report to me?”
ACT 23:20 20 He replied, “The Jewish leaders have conspired to ask that you bring Paul down to the council tomorrow. They will pretend that they want to investigate his case more closely.
ACT 23:21 21 Don’t fall for it! More than forty of them are waiting to ambush him. They have solemnly promised not to eat or drink until they have killed him. They are ready now, awaiting your consent.”
ACT 23:22 22 The commander dismissed the young man, ordering him, “Don’t tell anyone that you brought this to my attention.”
ACT 23:23 23 The commander called two centurions and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to leave for Caesarea at nine o’clock tonight.
ACT 23:24 24 Have horses ready for Paul to ride, so they may take him safely to Governor Felix.”
ACT 23:25 25 He wrote the following letter:
ACT 23:26 26 Claudius Lysias, to the most honorable Governor Felix: Greetings.
ACT 23:27 27 This man was seized by the Jews and was almost killed by them. I was nearby with a unit of soldiers, and I rescued him when I discovered that he was a Roman citizen.
ACT 23:28 28 I wanted to find out why they were accusing him, so I brought him to their council.
ACT 23:29 29 I discovered that they were accusing him about questions related to their Law. I found no charge deserving of death or imprisonment.
ACT 23:30 30 When I was informed of a conspiracy against his life, I sent him to you at once and ordered his accusers to bring their case against him before you.
ACT 23:31 31 Following their orders, the soldiers took Paul during the night and brought him to Antipatris.
ACT 23:32 32 The following day they let the horsemen continue on with Paul while they returned to the military headquarters in Jerusalem.
ACT 23:33 33 The horsemen entered Caesarea, delivered the letter to the governor, and brought Paul before him.
ACT 23:34 34 After he read the letter, he asked Paul about his home province. When he learned that he was from Cilicia,
ACT 23:35 35 the governor said, “I will hear your case when your accusers arrive.” Then he ordered that Paul be kept in custody in Herod’s palace.
ACT 24:1 1 Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus. They pressed charges against Paul before the governor.
ACT 24:2 2 After the governor summoned Paul, Tertullus began to make his case against him. He declared, “Under your leadership, we have experienced substantial peace, and your administration has brought reforms to our nation.
ACT 24:3 3 Always and everywhere, most honorable Felix, we acknowledge this with deep gratitude.
ACT 24:4 4 I don’t want to take too much of your time, so I ask that you listen with your usual courtesy to our brief statement of the facts.
ACT 24:5 5 We have found this man to be a troublemaker who stirs up riots among all the Jews throughout the empire. He’s a ringleader of the Nazarene faction
ACT 24:6 6 and even tried to defile the temple. That’s when we arrested him.
ACT 24:7 8 By examining him yourself, you will be able to verify the allegations we are bringing against him.”
ACT 24:8 9 The Jews reinforced the action against Paul, affirming the truth of these accusations.
ACT 24:9 10 The governor nodded at Paul, giving him permission to speak. He responded, “I know that you have been judge over this nation for many years, so I gladly offer my own defense.
ACT 24:10 11 You can verify that I went up to worship in Jerusalem no more than twelve days ago.
ACT 24:11 12 They didn’t find me arguing with anyone in the temple or stirring up a crowd, whether in the synagogue or anywhere else in the city.
ACT 24:12 13 Nor can they prove to you the allegations they are now bringing against me.
ACT 24:13 14 I do admit this to you, that I am a follower of the Way, which they call a faction. Accordingly, I worship the God of our ancestors and believe everything set out in the Law and written in the Prophets.
ACT 24:14 15 The hope I have in God I also share with my accusers, that there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the unrighteous.
ACT 24:15 16 On account of this, I have committed myself to maintaining a clear conscience before God and with all people.
ACT 24:16 17 After an absence of several years, I came to Jerusalem to bring gifts for the poor of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
ACT 24:17 18 When they found me in the temple, I was ritually pure. There was no crowd and no disturbance.
ACT 24:18 19 But there were some Jews from the province of Asia. They should be here making their accusations, if indeed they have something against me.
ACT 24:19 20 In their absence, have these people who are here declare what crime they found when I stood before the Jerusalem Council.
ACT 24:20 21 Perhaps it concerns this one statement that I blurted out when I was with them: ‘I am on trial before you today because of the resurrection of the dead.’”
ACT 24:21 22 Felix, who had an accurate understanding of the Way, adjourned the meeting. He said, “When Lysias the commander arrives from Jerusalem, I will decide this case.”
ACT 24:22 23 He arranged for a centurion to guard Paul. He was to give Paul some freedom, and his friends were not to be hindered in their efforts to provide for him.
ACT 24:23 24 After several days, Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, and summoned Paul. He listened to him talk about faith in Christ Jesus.
ACT 24:24 25 When he spoke about upright behavior, self-control, and the coming judgment, Felix became fearful and said, “Go away for now! When I have time, I’ll send for you.”
ACT 24:25 26 At the same time, he was hoping that Paul would offer him some money, so he often sent for him and talked with him.
ACT 24:26 27 When two years had passed, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. Since Felix wanted to grant a favor to the Jews, he left Paul in prison.
ACT 25:1 1 Three days after arriving in the province, Festus went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.
ACT 25:2 2 The chief priests and Jewish leaders presented their case against Paul. Appealing to him,
ACT 25:3 3 they asked as a favor from Festus that he summon Paul to Jerusalem. They were planning to ambush and kill him along the way.
ACT 25:4 4 But Festus responded by keeping Paul in Caesarea, since he was to return there very soon himself.
ACT 25:5 5 “Some of your leaders can come down with me,” he said. “If he’s done anything wrong, they can bring charges against him.”
ACT 25:6 6 He stayed with them for no more than eight or ten days, then went down to Caesarea. The following day he took his seat in the court and ordered that Paul be brought in.
ACT 25:7 7 When he arrived, many Jews who had come down from Jerusalem surrounded him. They brought serious charges against him, but they couldn’t prove them.
ACT 25:8 8 In his own defense, Paul said, “I’ve done nothing wrong against the Jewish Law, against the temple, or against Caesar.”
ACT 25:9 9 Festus, wanting to put the Jews in his debt, asked Paul, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me concerning these things?”
ACT 25:10 10 Paul replied, “I’m standing before Caesar’s court. I ought to be tried here. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you well know.
ACT 25:11 11 If I’m guilty and have done something that deserves death, then I won’t try to avoid death. But if there is nothing to their accusations against me, no one has the authority to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!”
ACT 25:12 12 After Festus conferred with his advisors, he responded, “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go.”
ACT 25:13 13 After several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived in Caesarea to welcome Festus.
ACT 25:14 14 Since they were staying there for many days, Festus discussed the case against Paul with the king. He said, “There is a man whom Felix left in prison.
ACT 25:15 15 When I was in Jerusalem, the Jewish chief priests and elders brought charges against him and requested a guilty verdict in his case.
ACT 25:16 16 I told them it is contrary to Roman practice to hand someone over before they have faced their accusers and had opportunity to offer a defense against the charges.
ACT 25:17 17 When they came here, I didn’t put them off. The very next day I took my seat in the court and ordered that the man be brought before me.
ACT 25:18 18 When the accusers took the floor, they didn’t charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.
ACT 25:19 19 Instead, they quibbled with him about their own religion and about some dead man named Jesus, who Paul claimed was alive.
ACT 25:20 20 Since I had no idea how to investigate these matters, I asked if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem to stand trial there on these issues.
ACT 25:21 21 However, Paul appealed that he be held in custody pending a decision from His Majesty the emperor, so I ordered that he be held until I could send him to Caesar.”
ACT 25:22 22 Agrippa said to Festus, “I want to hear the man myself.” “Tomorrow,” Festus replied, “you will hear him.”
ACT 25:23 23 The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great fanfare. They entered the auditorium with the military commanders and the city’s most prominent men. Festus then ordered that Paul be brought in.
ACT 25:24 24 Festus said, “King Agrippa and everyone present with us: You see this man! The entire Jewish community, both here and in Jerusalem, has appealed to me concerning him. They’ve been calling for his immediate death.
ACT 25:25 25 I’ve found that he has done nothing deserving death. When he appealed to His Majesty, I decided to send him to Rome.
ACT 25:26 26 I have nothing definite to write to our lord emperor. Therefore, I’ve brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after this investigation, I might have something to write.
ACT 25:27 27 After all, it would be foolish to send a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”
ACT 26:1 1 Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” So Paul gestured with his hand and began his defense.
ACT 26:2 2 “King Agrippa, I consider myself especially fortunate that I stand before you today as I offer my defense concerning all the accusations the Jews have brought against me.
ACT 26:3 3 This is because you understand well all the Jewish customs and controversies. Therefore, I ask you to listen to me patiently.
ACT 26:4 4 Every Jew knows the way of life I have followed since my youth because, from the beginning, I was among my people and in Jerusalem.
ACT 26:5 5 They have known me for a long time. If they wanted to, they could testify that I followed the way of life set out by the most exacting group of our religion. I am a Pharisee.
ACT 26:6 6 Today I am standing trial because of the hope in the promise God gave our ancestors.
ACT 26:7 7 This is the promise our twelve tribes hope to receive as they earnestly worship night and day. The Jews are accusing me, King Agrippa, because of this hope!
ACT 26:8 8 Why is it inconceivable to you that God raises the dead?
ACT 26:9 9 “I really thought that I ought to oppose the name of Jesus the Nazarene in every way possible.
ACT 26:10 10 And that’s exactly what I did in Jerusalem. I locked up many of God’s holy people in prison under the authority of the chief priests. When they were condemned to death, I voted against them.
ACT 26:11 11 In one synagogue after another—indeed, in all the synagogues—I would often torture them, compelling them to slander God. My rage bordered on the hysterical as I pursued them, even to foreign cities.
ACT 26:12 12 “On one such journey, I was going to Damascus with the full authority of the chief priests.
ACT 26:13 13 While on the road at midday, King Agrippa, I saw a light from heaven shining around me and my traveling companions. That light was brighter than the sun.
ACT 26:14 14 We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice that said to me in Aramaic, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you harassing me? It’s hard for you to kick against a spear.’
ACT 26:15 15 Then I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ The Lord replied, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are harassing.
ACT 26:16 16 Get up! Stand on your feet! I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you as my servant and witness of what you have seen and what I will show you.
ACT 26:17 17 I will rescue you from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you
ACT 26:18 18 to open their eyes. Then they can turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, and receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are made holy by faith in me.’
ACT 26:19 19 “So, King Agrippa, I wasn’t disobedient to that heavenly vision.
ACT 26:20 20 Instead, I proclaimed first to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, then to the whole region of Judea and to the Gentiles. My message was that they should change their hearts and lives and turn to God, and that they should demonstrate this change in their behavior.
ACT 26:21 21 Because of this, some Jews seized me in the temple and tried to murder me.
ACT 26:22 22 God has helped me up to this very day. Therefore, I stand here and bear witness to the lowly and the great. I’m saying nothing more than what the Prophets and Moses declared would happen:
ACT 26:23 23 that the Christ would suffer and that, as the first to rise from the dead, he would proclaim light both to my people and to the Gentiles.”
ACT 26:24 24 At this point in Paul’s defense, Festus declared with a loud voice, “You’ve lost your mind, Paul! Too much learning is driving you mad!”
ACT 26:25 25 But Paul replied, “I’m not mad, most honorable Festus! I’m speaking what is sound and true.
ACT 26:26 26 King Agrippa knows about these things, and I have been speaking openly to him. I’m certain that none of these things have escaped his attention. This didn’t happen secretly or in some out-of-the-way place.
ACT 26:27 27 King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do.”
ACT 26:28 28 Agrippa said to Paul, “Are you trying to convince me that, in such a short time, you’ve made me a Christian?”
ACT 26:29 29 Paul responded, “Whether it is a short or a long time, I pray to God that not only you but also all who are listening to me today will become like me, except for these chains.”
ACT 26:30 30 The king stood up, as did the governor, Bernice, and those sitting with them.
ACT 26:31 31 As they left, they were saying to each other, “This man is doing nothing that deserves death or imprisonment.”
ACT 26:32 32 Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been released if he hadn’t appealed to Caesar.”
ACT 27:1 1 When it was determined that we were to sail to Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were placed in the custody of a centurion named Julius of the Imperial Company.
ACT 27:2 2 We boarded a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail for ports along the coast of the province of Asia. So we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, came with us.
ACT 27:3 3 The next day we landed in Sidon. Julius treated Paul kindly and permitted him to go to some friends so they could take care of him.
ACT 27:4 4 From there we sailed off. We passed Cyprus, using the island to shelter us from the headwinds.
ACT 27:5 5 We sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, and landed in Myra in Lycia.
ACT 27:6 6 There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship headed for Italy and put us on board.
ACT 27:7 7 After many days of slow and difficult sailing, we arrived off the coast of Cnidus. The wind wouldn’t allow us to go farther, so we sailed under the shelter of Crete off Salmone.
ACT 27:8 8 We sailed along the coast only with difficulty until we came to a place called Good Harbors, near the city of Lasea.
ACT 27:9 9 Much time had been lost, and the voyage was now dangerous since the Day of Reconciliation had already passed. Paul warned them,
ACT 27:10 10 “Men, I see that our voyage will suffer damage and great loss, not only for the cargo and ship but also for our lives.”
ACT 27:11 11 But the centurion was persuaded more by the ship’s pilot and captain than by Paul’s advice.
ACT 27:12 12 Since the harbor was unsuitable for spending the winter, the majority supported a plan to put out to sea from there. They thought they might reach Phoenix in Crete and spend the winter in its harbor, which faced southwest and northwest.
ACT 27:13 13 When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they could carry out their plan. They pulled up anchor and sailed closely along the coast of Crete.
ACT 27:14 14 Before long, a hurricane-strength wind known as a northeaster swept down from Crete.
ACT 27:15 15 The ship was caught in the storm and couldn’t be turned into the wind. So we gave in to it, and it carried us along.
ACT 27:16 16 After sailing under the shelter of an island called Cauda, we were able to control the lifeboat only with difficulty.
ACT 27:17 17 They brought the lifeboat aboard, then began to wrap the ship with cables to hold it together. Fearing they might run aground on the sandbars of the Gulf of Syrtis, they lowered the anchor and let the ship be carried along.
ACT 27:18 18 We were so battered by the violent storm that the next day the men began throwing cargo overboard.
ACT 27:19 19 On the third day, they picked up the ship’s gear and hurled it into the sea.
ACT 27:20 20 When neither the sun nor the moon appeared for many days and the raging storm continued to pound us, all hope of our being saved from this peril faded.
ACT 27:21 21 For a long time no one had eaten. Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have complied with my instructions not to sail from Crete. Then we would have avoided this damage and loss.
ACT 27:22 22 Now I urge you to be encouraged. Not one of your lives will be lost, though we will lose the ship.
ACT 27:23 23 Last night an angel from the God to whom I belong and whom I worship stood beside me.
ACT 27:24 24 The angel said, ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul! You must stand before Caesar! Indeed, God has also graciously given you everyone sailing with you.’
ACT 27:25 25 Be encouraged, men! I have faith in God that it will be exactly as he told me.
ACT 27:26 26 However, we must run aground on some island.”
ACT 27:27 27 On the fourteenth night, we were being carried across the Adriatic Sea. Around midnight the sailors began to suspect that land was near.
ACT 27:28 28 They dropped a weighted line to take soundings and found the water to be about one hundred twenty feet deep. After proceeding a little farther, we took soundings again and found the water to be about ninety feet deep.
ACT 27:29 29 Afraid that we might run aground somewhere on the rocks, they hurled out four anchors from the stern and began to pray for daylight.
ACT 27:30 30 The sailors tried to abandon the ship by lowering the lifeboat into the sea, pretending they were going to lower anchors from the bow.
ACT 27:31 31 Paul said to the centurion and his soldiers, “Unless they stay in the ship, you can’t be saved from peril.”
ACT 27:32 32 The soldiers then cut the ropes to the lifeboat and let it drift away.
ACT 27:33 33 Just before daybreak, Paul urged everyone to eat. He said, “This is the fourteenth day you’ve lived in suspense, and you’ve not had even a bite to eat.
ACT 27:34 34 I urge you to take some food. Your health depends on it. None of you will lose a single hair from his head.”
ACT 27:35 35 After he said these things, he took bread, gave thanks to God in front of them all, then broke it and began to eat.
ACT 27:36 36 Everyone was encouraged and took some food. (
ACT 27:37 37 In all, there were two hundred seventy-six of us on the ship.)
ACT 27:38 38 When they had eaten as much as they wanted, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
ACT 27:39 39 In the morning light they saw a bay with a sandy beach. They didn’t know what land it was, but they thought they might possibly be able to run the ship aground.
ACT 27:40 40 They cut the anchors loose and left them in the sea. At the same time, they untied the ropes that ran back to the rudders. They raised the foresail to catch the wind and made for the beach.
ACT 27:41 41 But they struck a sandbar and the ship ran aground. The bow was stuck and wouldn’t move, and the stern was broken into pieces by the force of the waves.
ACT 27:42 42 The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming to shore and escaping.
ACT 27:43 43 However, the centurion wanted to save Paul, so he stopped them from carrying out their plan. He ordered those who could swim to jump overboard first and head for land.
ACT 27:44 44 He ordered the rest to grab hold of planks or debris from the ship. In this way, everyone reached land safely.
ACT 28:1 1 After reaching land safely, we learned that the island was called Malta.
ACT 28:2 2 The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. Because it was rainy and cold, they built a fire and welcomed all of us.
ACT 28:3 3 Paul gathered a bunch of dry sticks and put them on the fire. As he did, a poisonous snake, driven out by the heat, latched on to his hand.
ACT 28:4 4 When the islanders saw the snake hanging from his hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He was rescued from the sea, but the goddess Justice hasn’t let him live!”
ACT 28:5 5 Paul shook the snake into the fire and suffered no harm.
ACT 28:6 6 They expected him to swell up with fever or suddenly drop dead. After waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and began to claim that he was a god.
ACT 28:7 7 Publius, the island’s most prominent person, owned a large estate in that area. He welcomed us warmly into his home as his guests for three days.
ACT 28:8 8 Publius’ father was bedridden, sick with a fever and dysentery. Paul went to see him and prayed. He placed his hand on him and healed him.
ACT 28:9 9 Once this happened, the rest of the sick on the island came to him and were healed.
ACT 28:10 10 They honored us in many ways. When we were getting ready to sail again, they supplied us with what we needed.
ACT 28:11 11 After three months we put out to sea in a ship that had spent the winter at the island. It was an Alexandrian ship with carvings of the twin gods Castor and Pollux as its figurehead.
ACT 28:12 12 We landed in Syracuse where we stayed three days.
ACT 28:13 13 From there we sailed to Rhegium. After one day a south wind came up, and we arrived on the second day in Puteoli.
ACT 28:14 14 There we found brothers and sisters who urged us to stay with them for a week. In this way we came to Rome.
ACT 28:15 15 When the brothers and sisters there heard about us, they came as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he gave thanks to God and was encouraged.
ACT 28:16 16 When we entered Rome, Paul was permitted to live by himself, with a soldier guarding him.
ACT 28:17 17 Three days later, Paul called the Jewish leaders together. When they gathered, he said, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our ancestors, I’m a prisoner from Jerusalem. They handed me over to the Romans,
ACT 28:18 18 who intended to release me after they examined me, because they couldn’t find any reason for putting me to death.
ACT 28:19 19 When the Jews objected, I was forced to appeal to Caesar. Don’t think I appealed to Caesar because I had any reason to bring charges against my nation.
ACT 28:20 20 This is why I asked to see you and speak with you: it’s because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”
ACT 28:21 21 They responded, “We haven’t received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of our brothers come and reported or said anything bad about you.
ACT 28:22 22 But we think it’s important to hear what you think, for we know that people everywhere are speaking against this faction.”
ACT 28:23 23 On the day scheduled for this purpose, many people came to the place where he was staying. From morning until evening, he explained and testified concerning God’s kingdom and tried to convince them about Jesus through appealing to the Law from Moses and the Prophets.
ACT 28:24 24 Some were persuaded by what he said, but others refused to believe.
ACT 28:25 25 They disagreed with each other and were starting to leave when Paul made one more statement: “The Holy Spirit spoke correctly when he said to your ancestors through Isaiah the prophet,
ACT 28:26 26 “ Go to this people and say: ” “ You will hear, to be sure, but never understand; ” “ and you will certainly see but never recognize what you are seeing. ”
ACT 28:27 27 “ This people’s senses have become calloused, ” “ and they’ve become hard of hearing, ” “ and they’ve shut their eyes ” “ so that they won’t see with their eyes ” “ or hear with their ears ” “ or understand with their minds, ” “ and change their hearts and lives that I may heal them. ”
ACT 28:28 28 “Therefore, be certain of this: God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles. They will listen!”
ACT 28:29 30 Paul lived in his own rented quarters for two full years and welcomed everyone who came to see him.
ACT 28:30 31 Unhindered and with complete confidence, he continued to preach God’s kingdom and to teach about the Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM 1:1 1 From Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle and set apart for God’s good news.
ROM 1:2 2-3 God promised this good news about his Son ahead of time through his prophets in the holy scriptures. His Son was descended from David.
ROM 1:3 4 He was publicly identified as God’s Son with power through his resurrection from the dead, which was based on the Spirit of holiness. This Son is Jesus Christ our Lord.
ROM 1:4 5 Through him we have received God’s grace and our appointment to be apostles. This was to bring all Gentiles to faithful obedience for his name’s sake.
ROM 1:5 6 You who are called by Jesus Christ are also included among these Gentiles.
ROM 1:6 7 To those in Rome who are dearly loved by God and called to be God’s people. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM 1:7 8 First of all, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because the news about your faithfulness is being spread throughout the whole world.
ROM 1:8 9 I serve God in my spirit by preaching the good news about God’s Son, and God is my witness that I continually mention you
ROM 1:9 10 in all my prayers. I’m always asking that somehow, by God’s will, I might succeed in visiting you at last.
ROM 1:10 11 I really want to see you to pass along some spiritual gift to you so that you can be strengthened.
ROM 1:11 12 What I mean is that we can mutually encourage each other while I am with you. We can be encouraged by the faithfulness we find in each other, both your faithfulness and mine.
ROM 1:12 13 I want you to know, brothers and sisters, that I planned to visit you many times, although I have been prevented from coming until now. I want to harvest some fruit among you, just as I have done among the other Gentiles.
ROM 1:13 14 I have a responsibility both to Greeks and to those who don’t speak Greek, both to the wise and to the foolish.
ROM 1:14 15 That’s why I’m ready to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.
ROM 1:15 16 I’m not ashamed of the gospel: it is God’s own power for salvation to all who have faith in God, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
ROM 1:16 17 God’s righteousness is being revealed in the gospel, from faithfulness for faith, as it is written, “ The righteous person will live by faith. ”
ROM 1:17 18 God’s wrath is being revealed from heaven against all the ungodly behavior and the injustice of human beings who silence the truth with injustice.
ROM 1:18 19 This is because what is known about God should be plain to them because God made it plain to them.
ROM 1:19 20 Ever since the creation of the world, God’s invisible qualities—God’s eternal power and divine nature—have been clearly seen, because they are understood through the things God has made. So humans are without excuse.
ROM 1:20 21 Although they knew God, they didn’t honor God as God or thank him. Instead, their reasoning became pointless, and their foolish hearts were darkened.
ROM 1:21 22 While they were claiming to be wise, they made fools of themselves.
ROM 1:22 23 They exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images that look like mortal humans: birds, animals, and reptiles.
ROM 1:23 24 So God abandoned them to their hearts’ desires, which led to the moral corruption of degrading their own bodies with each other.
ROM 1:24 25 They traded God’s truth for a lie, and they worshipped and served the creation instead of the creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
ROM 1:25 26 That’s why God abandoned them to degrading lust. Their females traded natural sexual relations for unnatural sexual relations.
ROM 1:26 27 Also, in the same way, the males traded natural sexual relations with females, and burned with lust for each other. Males performed shameful actions with males, and they were paid back with the penalty they deserved for their mistake in their own bodies.
ROM 1:27 28 Since they didn’t think it was worthwhile to acknowledge God, God abandoned them to a defective mind to do inappropriate things.
ROM 1:28 29 So they were filled with all injustice, wicked behavior, greed, and evil behavior. They are full of jealousy, murder, fighting, deception, and malice. They are gossips,
ROM 1:29 30 they slander people, and they hate God. They are rude and proud, and they brag. They invent ways to be evil, and they are disobedient to their parents.
ROM 1:30 31 They are without understanding, disloyal, without affection, and without mercy.
ROM 1:31 32 Though they know God’s decision that those who persist in such practices deserve death, they not only keep doing these things but also approve others who practice them.
ROM 2:1 1 So every single one of you who judge others is without any excuse. You condemn yourself when you judge another person because the one who is judging is doing the same things.
ROM 2:2 2 We know that God’s judgment agrees with the truth, and his judgment is against those who do these kinds of things.
ROM 2:3 3 If you judge those who do these kinds of things while you do the same things yourself, think about this: Do you believe that you will escape God’s judgment?
ROM 2:4 4 Or do you have contempt for the riches of God’s generosity, tolerance, and patience? Don’t you realize that God’s kindness is supposed to lead you to change your heart and life?
ROM 2:5 5 You are storing up wrath for yourself because of your stubbornness and your heart that refuses to change. God’s just judgment will be revealed on the day of wrath.
ROM 2:6 6 “ God will repay everyone based on their works ”.
ROM 2:7 7 On the one hand, he will give eternal life to those who look for glory, honor, and immortality based on their patient good work.
ROM 2:8 8 But on the other hand, there will be wrath and anger for those who obey wickedness instead of the truth because they are acting out of selfishness and disobedience.
ROM 2:9 9 There will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, for the Jew first and also for the Greek.
ROM 2:10 10 But there will be glory, honor, and peace for everyone who does what is good, for the Jew first and also for the Greek.
ROM 2:11 11 God does not have favorites.
ROM 2:12 12 Those who have sinned outside the Law will also die outside the Law, and those who have sinned under the Law will be judged by the Law.
ROM 2:13 13 It isn’t the ones who hear the Law who are righteous in God’s eyes. It is the ones who do what the Law says who will be treated as righteous.
ROM 2:14 14 Gentiles don’t have the Law. But when they instinctively do what the Law requires they are a Law in themselves, though they don’t have the Law.
ROM 2:15 15 They show the proof of the Law written on their hearts, and their consciences affirm it. Their conflicting thoughts will accuse them, or even make a defense for them,
ROM 2:16 16 on the day when, according to my gospel, God will judge the hidden truth about human beings through Christ Jesus.
ROM 2:17 17 But, if you call yourself a Jew; if you rely on the Law; if you brag about your relationship to God;
ROM 2:18 18 if you know the will of God; if you are taught by the Law so that you can figure out the things that really matter;
ROM 2:19 19 if you have persuaded yourself that you are: a guide for the blind; a light to those who are in darkness;
ROM 2:20 20 an educator of the foolish; a teacher of infants (since you have the full content of knowledge and truth in the Law);
ROM 2:21 21 then why don’t you who are teaching others teach yourself? If you preach, “No stealing,” do you steal?
ROM 2:22 22 If you say, “No adultery,” do you commit adultery? If you hate idols, do you rob temples?
ROM 2:23 23 If you brag about the Law, do you shame God by breaking the Law?
ROM 2:24 24 As it is written: “ The name of God is discredited by the Gentiles because of you ”.
ROM 2:25 25 Circumcision is an advantage if you do what the Law says. But if you are a person who breaks the Law, your status of being circumcised has changed into not being circumcised.
ROM 2:26 26 So if the person who isn’t circumcised keeps the Law, won’t his status of not being circumcised be counted as if he were circumcised?
ROM 2:27 27 The one who isn’t physically circumcised but keeps the Law will judge you. You became a lawbreaker after you had the written Law and circumcision.
ROM 2:28 28 It isn’t the Jew who maintains outward appearances who will receive praise from God, and it isn’t people who are outwardly circumcised on their bodies.
ROM 2:29 29 Instead, it is the person who is a Jew inside, who is circumcised in spirit, not literally. That person’s praise doesn’t come from people but from God.
ROM 3:1 1 So what’s the advantage of being a Jew? Or what’s the benefit of circumcision?
ROM 3:2 2 Plenty in every way. First of all, the Jews were trusted with God’s revelations.
ROM 3:3 3 What does it matter, then, if some weren’t faithful? Their lack of faith won’t cancel God’s faithfulness, will it?
ROM 3:4 4 Absolutely not! God must be true, even if every human being is a liar, as it is written: “ So that it can show that you are right in your words; ” “ and you will triumph when you are judged. ”
ROM 3:5 5 But if our lack of righteousness confirms God’s justice, what will we say? That God, who brings wrath upon us, isn’t just (I’m speaking rhetorically)?
ROM 3:6 6 Absolutely not! If God weren’t just, how could he judge the world?
ROM 3:7 7 But if God’s truth is demonstrated by my lie and it increases his glory, why am I still judged as a sinner?
ROM 3:8 8 Why not say, “Let’s do evil things so that good things will come out of it”? (Some people who slander us accuse us of saying that, but these people deserve criticism.)
ROM 3:9 9 So what are we saying? Are we better off? Not at all. We have already stated the charge: both Jews and Greeks are all under the power of sin.
ROM 3:10 10 As it is written, “ There is no righteous person, not even one. ”
ROM 3:11 11 “ There is no one who understands. ” “ There is no one who looks for God. ”
ROM 3:12 12 “ They all turned away. ” “ They have become worthless together. ” “ There is no one who shows kindness. ” “ There is not even one. ”
ROM 3:13 13 “ Their throat is a grave that has been opened. ” “ They are deceitful with their tongues, ” “ and the poison of vipers is under their lips. ”
ROM 3:14 14 “ Their mouths are full of cursing and bitterness. ”
ROM 3:15 15 “ Their feet are quick to shed blood; ”
ROM 3:16 16 “ destruction and misery are in their ways; ”
ROM 3:17 17 “ and they don’t know the way of peace. ”
ROM 3:18 18 “ There is no fear of God in their view of the world. ”
ROM 3:19 19 Now we know that whatever the Law says, it speaks to those who are under the Law, in order to shut every mouth and make it so the whole world has to answer to God.
ROM 3:20 20 It follows that no human being will be treated as righteous in his presence by doing what the Law says, because the knowledge of sin comes through the Law.
ROM 3:21 21 But now God’s righteousness has been revealed apart from the Law, which is confirmed by the Law and the Prophets.
ROM 3:22 22 God’s righteousness comes through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ for all who have faith in him. There’s no distinction.
ROM 3:23 23 All have sinned and fall short of God’s glory,
ROM 3:24 24 but all are treated as righteous freely by his grace because of a ransom that was paid by Christ Jesus.
ROM 3:25 25 Through his faithfulness, God displayed Jesus as the place of sacrifice where mercy is found by means of his blood. He did this to demonstrate his righteousness in passing over sins that happened before,
ROM 3:26 26 during the time of God’s patient tolerance. He also did this to demonstrate that he is righteous in the present time, and to treat the one who has faith in Jesus as righteous.
ROM 3:27 27 What happens to our bragging? It’s thrown out. With which law? With what we have accomplished under the Law?
ROM 3:28 28 No, not at all, but through the law of faith. We consider that a person is treated as righteous by faith, apart from what is accomplished under the Law.
ROM 3:29 29 Or is God the God of Jews only? Isn’t God the God of Gentiles also? Yes, God is also the God of Gentiles.
ROM 3:30 30 Since God is one, then the one who makes the circumcised righteous by faith will also make the one who isn’t circumcised righteous through faith.
ROM 3:31 31 Do we then cancel the Law through this faith? Absolutely not! Instead, we confirm the Law.
ROM 4:1 1 So what are we going to say? Are we going to find that Abraham is our ancestor on the basis of genealogy?
ROM 4:2 2 Because if Abraham was made righteous because of his actions, he would have had a reason to brag, but not in front of God.
ROM 4:3 3 What does the scripture say? “ Abraham had faith in God, and it was credited to him as righteousness ”.
ROM 4:4 4 Workers’ salaries aren’t credited to them on the basis of an employer’s grace but rather on the basis of what they deserve.
ROM 4:5 5 But faith is credited as righteousness to those who don’t work, because they have faith in God who makes the ungodly righteous.
ROM 4:6 6 In the same way, David also pronounces a blessing on the person to whom God credits righteousness apart from actions:
ROM 4:7 7 “ Happy are those whose actions outside the Law are forgiven, ” “ and whose sins are covered. ”
ROM 4:8 8 “ Happy are those whose sin isn’t counted against them by the Lord ”.
ROM 4:9 9 Is this state of happiness only for the circumcised or is it also for those who aren’t circumcised? We say, “Faith was credited to Abraham as righteousness.”
ROM 4:10 10 So how was it credited? When he was circumcised, or when he wasn’t circumcised? In fact, it was credited while he still wasn’t circumcised, not after he was circumcised.
ROM 4:11 11 He received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness that comes from the faith he had while he still wasn’t circumcised. It happened this way so that Abraham could be the ancestor of all those people who aren’t circumcised, who have faith in God, and so are counted as righteous.
ROM 4:12 12 He could also be the ancestor of those circumcised people, who aren’t only circumcised but who also walk in the path of faith, like our ancestor Abraham did while he wasn’t circumcised.
ROM 4:13 13 The promise to Abraham and to his descendants, that he would inherit the world, didn’t come through the Law but through the righteousness that comes from faith.
ROM 4:14 14 If they inherit because of the Law, then faith has no effect and the promise has been canceled.
ROM 4:15 15 The Law brings about wrath. But when there isn’t any law, there isn’t any violation of the law.
ROM 4:16 16 That’s why the inheritance comes through faith, so that it will be on the basis of God’s grace. In that way, the promise is secure for all of Abraham’s descendants, not just for those who are related by Law but also for those who are related by the faith of Abraham, who is the father of all of us.
ROM 4:17 17 As it is written: “ I have appointed you to be the father of many nations. ” So Abraham is our father in the eyes of God in whom he had faith, the God who gives life to the dead and calls things that don’t exist into existence.
ROM 4:18 18 When it was beyond hope, he had faith in the hope that he would become the father of many nations, in keeping with the promise God spoke to him: “ That’s how many descendants you will have. ”
ROM 4:19 19 Without losing faith, Abraham, who was nearly 100 years old, took into account his own body, which was as good as dead, and Sarah’s womb, which was dead.
ROM 4:20 20 He didn’t hesitate with a lack of faith in God’s promise, but he grew strong in faith and gave glory to God.
ROM 4:21 21 He was fully convinced that God was able to do what he promised.
ROM 4:22 22 Therefore, it was credited to him as righteousness.
ROM 4:23 23 But the scripture that says “ it was credited to him ” wasn’t written only for Abraham’s sake.
ROM 4:24 24 It was written also for our sake, because it is going to be credited to us too. It will be credited to those of us who have faith in the one who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead.
ROM 4:25 25 He was handed over because of our mistakes, and he was raised to meet the requirements of righteousness for us.
ROM 5:1 1 Therefore, since we have been made righteous through his faithfulness, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM 5:2 2 We have access by faith into this grace in which we stand through him, and we boast in the hope of God’s glory.
ROM 5:3 3 But not only that! We even take pride in our problems, because we know that trouble produces endurance,
ROM 5:4 4 endurance produces character, and character produces hope.
ROM 5:5 5 This hope doesn’t put us to shame, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit, who has been given to us.
ROM 5:6 6 While we were still weak, at the right moment, Christ died for ungodly people.
ROM 5:7 7 It isn’t often that someone will die for a righteous person, though maybe someone might dare to die for a good person.
ROM 5:8 8 But God shows his love for us, because while we were still sinners Christ died for us.
ROM 5:9 9 So, now that we have been made righteous by his blood, we can be even more certain that we will be saved from God’s wrath through him.
ROM 5:10 10 If we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son while we were still enemies, now that we have been reconciled, how much more certain is it that we will be saved by his life?
ROM 5:11 11 And not only that: we even take pride in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, the one through whom we now have a restored relationship with God.
ROM 5:12 12 Just as through one human being sin came into the world, and death came through sin, so death has come to everyone, since everyone has sinned.
ROM 5:13 13 Although sin was in the world, since there was no Law, it wasn’t taken into account until the Law came.
ROM 5:14 14 But death ruled from Adam until Moses, even over those who didn’t sin in the same way Adam did—Adam was a type of the one who was coming.
ROM 5:15 15 But the free gift of Christ isn’t like Adam’s failure. If many people died through what one person did wrong, God’s grace is multiplied even more for many people with the gift—of the one person Jesus Christ—that comes through grace.
ROM 5:16 16 The gift isn’t like the consequences of one person’s sin. The judgment that came from one person’s sin led to punishment, but the free gift that came out of many failures led to the verdict of acquittal.
