ROM 5:17 17 If death ruled because of one person’s failure, those who receive the multiplied grace and the gift of righteousness will even more certainly rule in life through the one person Jesus Christ.
ROM 5:18 18 So now the righteous requirements necessary for life are met for everyone through the righteous act of one person, just as judgment fell on everyone through the failure of one person.
ROM 5:19 19 Many people were made righteous through the obedience of one person, just as many people were made sinners through the disobedience of one person.
ROM 5:20 20 The Law stepped in to amplify the failure, but where sin increased, grace multiplied even more.
ROM 5:21 21 The result is that grace will rule through God’s righteousness, leading to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord, just as sin ruled in death.
ROM 6:1 1 So what are we going to say? Should we continue sinning so grace will multiply?
ROM 6:2 2 Absolutely not! All of us died to sin. How can we still live in it?
ROM 6:3 3 Or don’t you know that all who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?
ROM 6:4 4 Therefore, we were buried together with him through baptism into his death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too can walk in newness of life.
ROM 6:5 5 If we were united together in a death like his, we will also be united together in a resurrection like his.
ROM 6:6 6 This is what we know: the person that we used to be was crucified with him in order to get rid of the corpse that had been controlled by sin. That way we wouldn’t be slaves to sin anymore,
ROM 6:7 7 because a person who has died has been freed from sin’s power.
ROM 6:8 8 But if we died with Christ, we have faith that we will also live with him.
ROM 6:9 9 We know that Christ has been raised from the dead and he will never die again. Death no longer has power over him.
ROM 6:10 10 He died to sin once and for all with his death, but he lives for God with his life.
ROM 6:11 11 In the same way, you also should consider yourselves dead to sin but alive for God in Christ Jesus.
ROM 6:12 12 So then, don’t let sin rule your body, so that you do what it wants.
ROM 6:13 13 Don’t offer parts of your body to sin, to be used as weapons to do wrong. Instead, present yourselves to God as people who have been brought back to life from the dead, and offer all the parts of your body to God to be used as weapons to do right.
ROM 6:14 14 Sin will have no power over you, because you aren’t under Law but under grace.
ROM 6:15 15 So what? Should we sin because we aren’t under Law but under grace? Absolutely not!
ROM 6:16 16 Don’t you know that if you offer yourselves to someone as obedient slaves, that you are slaves of the one whom you obey? That’s true whether you serve as slaves of sin, which leads to death, or as slaves of the kind of obedience that leads to righteousness.
ROM 6:17 17 But thank God that although you used to be slaves of sin, you gave wholehearted obedience to the teaching that was handed down to you, which provides a pattern.
ROM 6:18 18 Now that you have been set free from sin, you have become slaves of righteousness.
ROM 6:19 19 (I’m speaking with ordinary metaphors because of your limitations.) Once, you offered the parts of your body to be used as slaves to impurity and to lawless behavior that leads to still more lawless behavior. Now, you should present the parts of your body as slaves to righteousness, which makes your lives holy.
ROM 6:20 20 When you were slaves of sin, you were free from the control of righteousness.
ROM 6:21 21 What consequences did you get from doing things that you are now ashamed of? The outcome of those things is death.
ROM 6:22 22 But now that you have been set free from sin and become slaves to God, you have the consequence of a holy life, and the outcome is eternal life.
ROM 6:23 23 The wages that sin pays are death, but God’s gift is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
ROM 7:1 1 Brothers and sisters, I’m talking to you as people who know the Law. Don’t you know that the Law has power over someone only as long as he or she lives?
ROM 7:2 2 A married woman is united with her husband under the Law while he is alive. But if her husband dies, she is released from the Law concerning her husband.
ROM 7:3 3 So then, if she lives with another man while her husband is alive, she’s committing adultery. But if her husband dies, she’s free from the Law, so she won’t be committing adultery if she marries someone else.
ROM 7:4 4 Therefore, my brothers and sisters, you also died with respect to the Law through the body of Christ, so that you could be united with someone else. You are united with the one who was raised from the dead so that we can bear fruit for God.
ROM 7:5 5 When we were self-centered, the sinful passions aroused through the Law were at work in all the parts of our body, so that we bore fruit for death.
ROM 7:6 6 But now we have been released from the Law. We have died with respect to the thing that controlled us, so that we can be slaves in the new life under the Spirit, not in the old life under the written Law.
ROM 7:7 7 So what are we going to say? That the Law is sin? Absolutely not! But I wouldn’t have known sin except through the Law. I wouldn’t have known the desire for what others have if the Law had not said, “ Don’t desire to take what others have ”.
ROM 7:8 8 But sin seized the opportunity and used this commandment to produce all kinds of desires in me. Sin is dead without the Law.
ROM 7:9 9 I used to be alive without the Law, but when the commandment came, sin sprang to life,
ROM 7:10 10 and I died. So the commandment that was intended to give life brought death.
ROM 7:11 11 Sin seized the opportunity through the commandment, deceived me, and killed me.
ROM 7:12 12 So the Law itself is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good.
ROM 7:13 13 So did something good bring death to me? Absolutely not! But sin caused my death through something good so that sin would be exposed as sin. That way sin would become even more thoroughly sinful through the commandment.
ROM 7:14 14 We know that the Law is spiritual, but I’m made of flesh and blood, and I’m sold as a slave to sin.
ROM 7:15 15 I don’t know what I’m doing, because I don’t do what I want to do. Instead, I do the thing that I hate.
ROM 7:16 16 But if I’m doing the thing that I don’t want to do, I’m agreeing that the Law is right.
ROM 7:17 17 But now I’m not the one doing it anymore. Instead, it’s sin that lives in me.
ROM 7:18 18 I know that good doesn’t live in me—that is, in my body. The desire to do good is inside of me, but I can’t do it.
ROM 7:19 19 I don’t do the good that I want to do, but I do the evil that I don’t want to do.
ROM 7:20 20 But if I do the very thing that I don’t want to do, then I’m not the one doing it anymore. Instead, it is sin that lives in me that is doing it.
ROM 7:21 21 So I find that, as a rule, when I want to do what is good, evil is right there with me.
ROM 7:22 22 I gladly agree with the Law on the inside,
ROM 7:23 23 but I see a different law at work in my body. It wages a war against the law of my mind and takes me prisoner with the law of sin that is in my body.
ROM 7:24 24 I’m a miserable human being. Who will deliver me from this dead corpse?
ROM 7:25 25 Thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then I’m a slave to God’s Law in my mind, but I’m a slave to sin’s law in my body.
ROM 8:1 1 So now there isn’t any condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
ROM 8:2 2 The law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and death.
ROM 8:3 3 God has done what was impossible for the Law, since it was weak because of selfishness. God condemned sin in the body by sending his own Son to deal with sin in the same body as humans, who are controlled by sin.
ROM 8:4 4 He did this so that the righteous requirement of the Law might be fulfilled in us. Now the way we live is based on the Spirit, not based on selfishness.
ROM 8:5 5 People whose lives are based on selfishness think about selfish things, but people whose lives are based on the Spirit think about things that are related to the Spirit.
ROM 8:6 6 The attitude that comes from selfishness leads to death, but the attitude that comes from the Spirit leads to life and peace.
ROM 8:7 7 So the attitude that comes from selfishness is hostile to God. It doesn’t submit to God’s Law, because it can’t.
ROM 8:8 8 People who are self-centered aren’t able to please God.
ROM 8:9 9 But you aren’t self-centered. Instead you are in the Spirit, if in fact God’s Spirit lives in you. If anyone doesn’t have the Spirit of Christ, they don’t belong to him.
ROM 8:10 10 If Christ is in you, the Spirit is your life because of God’s righteousness, but the body is dead because of sin.
ROM 8:11 11 If the Spirit of the one who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you, the one who raised Christ from the dead will give life to your human bodies also, through his Spirit that lives in you.
ROM 8:12 12 So then, brothers and sisters, we have an obligation, but it isn’t an obligation to ourselves to live our lives on the basis of selfishness.
ROM 8:13 13 If you live on the basis of selfishness, you are going to die. But if by the Spirit you put to death the actions of the body, you will live.
ROM 8:14 14 All who are led by God’s Spirit are God’s sons and daughters.
ROM 8:15 15 You didn’t receive a spirit of slavery to lead you back again into fear, but you received a Spirit that shows you are adopted as his children. With this Spirit, we cry, “Abba, Father.”
ROM 8:16 16 The same Spirit agrees with our spirit, that we are God’s children.
ROM 8:17 17 But if we are children, we are also heirs. We are God’s heirs and fellow heirs with Christ, if we really suffer with him so that we can also be glorified with him.
ROM 8:18 18 I believe that the present suffering is nothing compared to the coming glory that is going to be revealed to us.
ROM 8:19 19 The whole creation waits breathless with anticipation for the revelation of God’s sons and daughters.
ROM 8:20 20 Creation was subjected to frustration, not by its own choice—it was the choice of the one who subjected it—but in the hope
ROM 8:21 21 that the creation itself will be set free from slavery to decay and brought into the glorious freedom of God’s children.
ROM 8:22 22 We know that the whole creation is groaning together and suffering labor pains up until now.
ROM 8:23 23 And it’s not only the creation. We ourselves who have the Spirit as the first crop of the harvest also groan inside as we wait to be adopted and for our bodies to be set free.
ROM 8:24 24 We were saved in hope. If we see what we hope for, that isn’t hope. Who hopes for what they already see?
ROM 8:25 25 But if we hope for what we don’t see, we wait for it with patience.
ROM 8:26 26 In the same way, the Spirit comes to help our weakness. We don’t know what we should pray, but the Spirit himself pleads our case with unexpressed groans.
ROM 8:27 27 The one who searches hearts knows how the Spirit thinks, because he pleads for the saints, consistent with God’s will.
ROM 8:28 28 We know that God works all things together for good for the ones who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
ROM 8:29 29 We know this because God knew them in advance, and he decided in advance that they would be conformed to the image of his Son. That way his Son would be the first of many brothers and sisters.
ROM 8:30 30 Those who God decided in advance would be conformed to his Son, he also called. Those whom he called, he also made righteous. Those whom he made righteous, he also glorified.
ROM 8:31 31 So what are we going to say about these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
ROM 8:32 32 He didn’t spare his own Son but gave him up for us all. Won’t he also freely give us all things with him?
ROM 8:33 33 Who will bring a charge against God’s elect people? It is God who acquits them.
ROM 8:34 34 Who is going to convict them? It is Christ Jesus who died, even more, who was raised, and who also is at God’s right side. It is Christ Jesus who also pleads our case for us.
ROM 8:35 35 Who will separate us from Christ’s love? Will we be separated by trouble, or distress, or harassment, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?
ROM 8:36 36 As it is written, “ We are being put to death all day long for your sake. ” “ We are treated like sheep for slaughter. ”
ROM 8:37 37 But in all these things we win a sweeping victory through the one who loved us.
ROM 8:38 38 I’m convinced that nothing can separate us from God’s love in Christ Jesus our Lord: not death or life, not angels or rulers, not present things or future things, not powers
ROM 8:39 39 or height or depth, or any other thing that is created.
ROM 9:1 1 I’m speaking the truth in Christ—I’m not lying, as my conscience assures me with the Holy Spirit:
ROM 9:2 2 I have great sadness and constant pain in my heart.
ROM 9:3 3 I wish I could be cursed, cut off from Christ if it helped my brothers and sisters, who are my flesh-and-blood relatives.
ROM 9:4 4 They are Israelites. The adoption as God’s children, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the Law, the worship, and the promises belong to them.
ROM 9:5 5 The Jewish ancestors are theirs, and the Christ descended from those ancestors. He is the one who rules over all things, who is God, and who is blessed forever. Amen.
ROM 9:6 6 But it’s not as though God’s word has failed. Not all who are descended from Israel are part of Israel.
ROM 9:7 7 Not all of Abraham’s children are called Abraham’s descendants, but instead “ your descendants will be named through Isaac. ”
ROM 9:8 8 That means it isn’t the natural children who are God’s children, but it is the children from the promise who are counted as descendants.
ROM 9:9 9 The words in the promise were: “ A year from now I will return, and Sarah will have a son ”.
ROM 9:10 10 Not only that, but also Rebecca conceived children with one man, our ancestor Isaac.
ROM 9:11 11 When they hadn’t been born yet and when they hadn’t yet done anything good or bad, it was shown that God’s purpose would continue because it was based on his choice.
ROM 9:12 12 It wasn’t because of what was done but because of God’s call. This was said to her: “ The older child will be a slave to the younger one ”.
ROM 9:13 13 As it is written, “ I loved Jacob, but I hated Esau ”.
ROM 9:14 14 So what are we going to say? Isn’t this unfair on God’s part? Absolutely not!
ROM 9:15 15 He says to Moses, “ I’ll have mercy on whomever I choose to have mercy, and I’ll show compassion to whomever I choose to show compassion ”.
ROM 9:16 16 So then, it doesn’t depend on a person’s desire or effort. It depends entirely on God, who shows mercy.
ROM 9:17 17 Scripture says to Pharaoh, “ I have put you in this position for this very thing: so I can show my power in you and so that my name can be spread through the entire earth. ”
ROM 9:18 18 So then, God has mercy on whomever he wants to, but he makes resistant whomever he wants to.
ROM 9:19 19 So you are going to say to me, “Then why does he still blame people? Who has ever resisted his will?”
ROM 9:20 20 You are only a human being. Who do you think you are to talk back to God? “ Does the clay say to the potter, ” “ Why did you make me like this? ”
ROM 9:21 21 Doesn’t the potter have the power over the clay to make one pot for special purposes and another for garbage from the same lump of clay?
ROM 9:22 22 What if God very patiently puts up with pots made for wrath that were designed for destruction, because he wanted to show his wrath and to make his power known?
ROM 9:23 23 What if he did this to make the wealth of his glory known toward pots made for mercy, which he prepared in advance for glory?
ROM 9:24 24 We are the ones God has called. We don’t come only from the Jews but we also come from the Gentiles.
ROM 9:25 25 As it says also in Hosea, “ I will call “my people” those who aren’t my people, ” “ and the one who isn’t well loved, I will call “loved one.” ”
ROM 9:26 26 And in the place where it was said to them, “ You aren’t my people, ” there they will be called “ the living God’s children ”.
ROM 9:27 27 But Isaiah cries out for Israel, “ Though the number of Israel’s children will be like the sand of the sea, ” “ only a remaining part will be saved, ”
ROM 9:28 28 “ because the Lord does what he says completely and quickly. ”
ROM 9:29 29 As Isaiah prophesied, “ If the Lord of the heavenly forces had not left descendants for us, ” “ we would have been like Sodom, ” “ and we would have become like Gomorrah. ”
ROM 9:30 30 So what are we going to say? Gentiles who weren’t striving for righteousness achieved righteousness, the righteousness that comes from faith.
ROM 9:31 31 But though Israel was striving for a Law of righteousness, they didn’t arrive.
ROM 9:32 32 Why? It’s because they didn’t go for it by faith but they went for it as if it could be reached by doing something. They have tripped over a stumbling block.
ROM 9:33 33 As it is written: “ Look! I’m putting a stumbling block in Zion, ” “ which is a rock that offends people. ” “ And the one who has faith in him will not be put to shame. ”
ROM 10:1 1 Brothers and sisters, my heart’s desire is for Israel’s salvation. That’s my prayer to God for them.
ROM 10:2 2 I can vouch for them: they are enthusiastic about God. However, it isn’t informed by knowledge.
ROM 10:3 3 They don’t submit to God’s righteousness because they don’t understand his righteousness, and they try to establish their own righteousness.
ROM 10:4 4 Christ is the goal of the Law, which leads to righteousness for all who have faith in God.
ROM 10:5 5 Moses writes about the righteousness that comes from the Law: “ The person who does these things will live by them. ”
ROM 10:6 6 But the righteousness that comes from faith talks like this: “ Don’t say in your heart ”, “ Who will go up into heaven? ” (that is, to bring Christ down)
ROM 10:7 7 or “ Who will go down into the region below? ” (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).
ROM 10:8 8 But what does it say? “ The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart ” (that is, the message of faith that we preach).
ROM 10:9 9 Because if you confess with your mouth “Jesus is Lord” and in your heart you have faith that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
ROM 10:10 10 Trusting with the heart leads to righteousness, and confessing with the mouth leads to salvation.
ROM 10:11 11 The scripture says, “ All who have faith in him won’t be put to shame ”.
ROM 10:12 12 There is no distinction between Jew and Greek, because the same Lord is Lord of all, who gives richly to all who call on him.
ROM 10:13 13 “ All who call on the Lord’s name will be saved. ”
ROM 10:14 14 So how can they call on someone they don’t have faith in? And how can they have faith in someone they haven’t heard of? And how can they hear without a preacher?
ROM 10:15 15 And how can they preach unless they are sent? As it is written, “ How beautiful are the feet of those who announce the good news. ”
ROM 10:16 16 But everyone hasn’t obeyed the good news. As Isaiah says, “ Lord, who has had faith in our message? ”
ROM 10:17 17 So, faith comes from listening, but it’s listening by means of Christ’s message.
ROM 10:18 18 But I ask you, didn’t they hear it? Definitely! “ Their voice has gone out into the entire earth, and their message has gone out to the corners of the inhabited world. ”
ROM 10:19 19 But I ask you again, didn’t Israel understand? First, Moses says, “ I will make you jealous of those who aren’t a people, of a people without understanding. ”
ROM 10:20 20 And Isaiah even dares to say, “ I was found by those who didn’t look for me; I revealed myself to those who didn’t ask for me. ”
ROM 10:21 21 But he says about Israel, “ All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people. ”
ROM 11:1 1 So I ask you, has God rejected his people? Absolutely not! I’m an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, from the tribe of Benjamin.
ROM 11:2 2 God hasn’t rejected his people, whom he knew in advance. Or don’t you know what the scripture says in the case of Elijah, when he pleads with God against Israel?
ROM 11:3 3 Lord, “ they have killed your prophets, and they have torn down your altars. I’m the only one left, and they are trying to take my life. ”
ROM 11:4 4 But what is God’s reply to him? “ I have kept for myself seven thousand people who haven’t bowed their knees to Baal. ”
ROM 11:5 5 So also in the present time there is a remaining group by the choice of God’s grace.
ROM 11:6 6 But if it is by grace, it isn’t by what’s done anymore. If it were, God’s grace wouldn’t be grace.
ROM 11:7 7 So what? Israel didn’t find what it was looking for. Those who were chosen found it, but the others were resistant.
ROM 11:8 8 As it is written, “ God gave them a dull spirit, so that their eyes would not see and their ears not hear, right up until the present day. ”
ROM 11:9 9 And David says, “ Their table should become a pitfall and a trap, ” “ a stumbling block and payback to them for what they have done. ”
ROM 11:10 10 “ Their eyes should be darkened so they can’t see, ” “ and their backs always bent. ”
ROM 11:11 11 So I’m asking you: They haven’t stumbled so that they’ve fallen permanently, have they? Absolutely not! But salvation has come to the Gentiles by their failure, in order to make Israel jealous.
ROM 11:12 12 But if their failure brings riches to the world, and their defeat brings riches to the Gentiles, how much more will come from the completion of their number!
ROM 11:13 13 I’m speaking to you Gentiles. Considering that I’m an apostle to the Gentiles, I publicize my own ministry
ROM 11:14 14 in the hope that somehow I might make my own people jealous and save some of them.
ROM 11:15 15 If their rejection has brought about a close relationship between God and the world, how can their acceptance mean anything less than life from the dead?
ROM 11:16 16 But if part of a batch of dough is offered to God as holy, the whole batch of dough is holy too. If a root is holy, the branches will be holy too.
ROM 11:17 17 If some of the branches were broken off, and you were a wild olive branch, and you were grafted in among the other branches and shared the root that produces the rich oil of the olive tree,
ROM 11:18 18 then don’t brag like you’re better than the other branches. If you do brag, be careful: it’s not you that sustains the root, but it’s the root that sustains you.
ROM 11:19 19 You will say then, “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.”
ROM 11:20 20 Fine. They were broken off because they weren’t faithful, but you stand only by your faithfulness. So don’t think in a proud way; instead be afraid.
ROM 11:21 21 If God didn’t spare the natural branches, he won’t spare you either.
ROM 11:22 22 So look at God’s kindness and harshness. It’s harshness toward those who fell, but it’s God’s kindness for you, provided you continue in his kindness; otherwise, you could be cut off too.
ROM 11:23 23 And even those who were cut off will be grafted back in if they don’t continue to be unfaithful, because God is able to graft them in again.
ROM 11:24 24 If you were naturally part of a wild olive tree and you were cut off from it, and then, contrary to nature, you were grafted into the cultivated olive tree, won’t these natural branches stand an even better chance of being grafted back onto their own olive tree?
ROM 11:25 25 I don’t want you to be unaware of this secret, brothers and sisters. That way you won’t think too highly of yourselves. A part of Israel has become resistant until the full number of the Gentiles comes in.
ROM 11:26 26 In this way, all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “ The deliverer will come from Zion. ” “ He will remove ungodly behavior from Jacob. ”
ROM 11:27 27 “ This is my covenant with them, ” “ when I take away their sins ”.
ROM 11:28 28 According to the gospel, they are enemies for your sake, but according to God’s choice, they are loved for the sake of their ancestors.
ROM 11:29 29 God’s gifts and calling can’t be taken back.
ROM 11:30 30 Once you were disobedient to God, but now you have mercy because they were disobedient.
ROM 11:31 31 In the same way, they have also been disobedient because of the mercy that you received, so now they can receive mercy too.
ROM 11:32 32 God has locked up all people in disobedience, in order to have mercy on all of them.
ROM 11:33 33 God’s riches, wisdom, and knowledge are so deep! They are as mysterious as his judgments, and they are as hard to track as his paths!
ROM 11:34 34 “ Who has known the Lord’s mind? ” “ Or who has been his mentor? ”
ROM 11:35 35 “ Or who has given him a gift ” “ and has been paid back by him? ”
ROM 11:36 36 All things are from him and through him and for him. May the glory be to him forever. Amen.
ROM 12:1 1 So, brothers and sisters, because of God’s mercies, I encourage you to present your bodies as a living sacrifice that is holy and pleasing to God. This is your appropriate priestly service.
ROM 12:2 2 Don’t be conformed to the patterns of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your minds so that you can figure out what God’s will is—what is good and pleasing and mature.
ROM 12:3 3 Because of the grace that God gave me, I can say to each one of you: don’t think of yourself more highly than you ought to think. Instead, be reasonable since God has measured out a portion of faith to each one of you.
ROM 12:4 4 We have many parts in one body, but the parts don’t all have the same function.
ROM 12:5 5 In the same way, though there are many of us, we are one body in Christ, and individually we belong to each other.
ROM 12:6 6 We have different gifts that are consistent with God’s grace that has been given to us. If your gift is prophecy, you should prophesy in proportion to your faith.
ROM 12:7 7 If your gift is service, devote yourself to serving. If your gift is teaching, devote yourself to teaching.
ROM 12:8 8 If your gift is encouragement, devote yourself to encouraging. The one giving should do it with no strings attached. The leader should lead with passion. The one showing mercy should be cheerful.
ROM 12:9 9 Love should be shown without pretending. Hate evil, and hold on to what is good.
ROM 12:10 10 Love each other like the members of your family. Be the best at showing honor to each other.
ROM 12:11 11 Don’t hesitate to be enthusiastic—be on fire in the Spirit as you serve the Lord!
ROM 12:12 12 Be happy in your hope, stand your ground when you’re in trouble, and devote yourselves to prayer.
ROM 12:13 13 Contribute to the needs of God’s people, and welcome strangers into your home.
ROM 12:14 14 Bless people who harass you—bless and don’t curse them.
ROM 12:15 15 Be happy with those who are happy, and cry with those who are crying.
ROM 12:16 16 Consider everyone as equal, and don’t think that you’re better than anyone else. Instead, associate with people who have no status. Don’t think that you’re so smart.
ROM 12:17 17 Don’t pay back anyone for their evil actions with evil actions, but show respect for what everyone else believes is good.
ROM 12:18 18 If possible, to the best of your ability, live at peace with all people.
ROM 12:19 19 Don’t try to get revenge for yourselves, my dear friends, but leave room for God’s wrath. It is written, “ Revenge belongs to me; I will pay it back, says the Lord ”.
ROM 12:20 20 Instead, “ If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. By doing this, you will pile burning coals of fire upon his head ”.
ROM 12:21 21 Don’t be defeated by evil, but defeat evil with good.
ROM 13:1 1 Every person should place themselves under the authority of the government. There isn’t any authority unless it comes from God, and the authorities that are there have been put in place by God.
ROM 13:2 2 So anyone who opposes the authority is standing against what God has established. People who take this kind of stand will get punished.
ROM 13:3 3 The authorities don’t frighten people who are doing the right thing. Rather, they frighten people who are doing wrong. Would you rather not be afraid of authority? Do what’s right, and you will receive its approval.
ROM 13:4 4 It is God’s servant given for your benefit. But if you do what’s wrong, be afraid because it doesn’t have weapons to enforce the law for nothing. It is God’s servant put in place to carry out his punishment on those who do what is wrong.
ROM 13:5 5 That is why it is necessary to place yourself under the government’s authority, not only to avoid God’s punishment but also for the sake of your conscience.
ROM 13:6 6 You should also pay taxes for the same reason, because the authorities are God’s assistants, concerned with this very thing.
ROM 13:7 7 So pay everyone what you owe them. Pay the taxes you owe, pay the duties you are charged, give respect to those you should respect, and honor those you should honor.
ROM 13:8 8 Don’t be in debt to anyone, except for the obligation to love each other. Whoever loves another person has fulfilled the Law.
ROM 13:9 9 The commandments, “ Don’t commit adultery, don’t murder, don’t steal, don’t desire what others have, ” and any other commandments, are all summed up in one word: “ You must love your neighbor as yourself. ”
ROM 13:10 10 Love doesn’t do anything wrong to a neighbor; therefore, love is what fulfills the Law.
ROM 13:11 11 As you do all this, you know what time it is. The hour has already come for you to wake up from your sleep. Now our salvation is nearer than when we first had faith.
ROM 13:12 12 The night is almost over, and the day is near. So let’s get rid of the actions that belong to the darkness and put on the weapons of light.
ROM 13:13 13 Let’s behave appropriately as people who live in the day, not in partying and getting drunk, not in sleeping around and obscene behavior, not in fighting and obsession.
ROM 13:14 14 Instead, dress yourself with the Lord Jesus Christ, and don’t plan to indulge your selfish desires.
ROM 14:1 1 Welcome the person who is weak in faith—but not in order to argue about differences of opinion.
ROM 14:2 2 One person believes in eating everything, while the weak person eats only vegetables.
ROM 14:3 3 Those who eat must not look down on the ones who don’t, and the ones who don’t eat must not judge the ones who do, because God has accepted them.
ROM 14:4 4 Who are you to judge someone else’s servants? They stand or fall before their own Lord (and they will stand, because the Lord has the power to make them stand).
ROM 14:5 5 One person considers some days to be more sacred than others, while another person considers all days to be the same. Each person must have their own convictions.
ROM 14:6 6 Someone who thinks that a day is sacred, thinks that way for the Lord. Those who eat, eat for the Lord, because they thank God. And those who don’t eat, don’t eat for the Lord, and they thank the Lord too.
ROM 14:7 7 We don’t live for ourselves and we don’t die for ourselves.
ROM 14:8 8 If we live, we live for the Lord, and if we die, we die for the Lord. Therefore, whether we live or die, we belong to God.
ROM 14:9 9 This is why Christ died and lived: so that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
ROM 14:10 10 But why do you judge your brother or sister? Or why do you look down on your brother or sister? We all will stand in front of the judgment seat of God.
ROM 14:11 11 Because it is written, “ As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow to me, ” “ and every tongue will give praise to God. ”
ROM 14:12 12 So then, each of us will give an account of ourselves to God.
ROM 14:13 13 So stop judging each other. Instead, this is what you should decide: never put a stumbling block or obstacle in the way of your brother or sister.
ROM 14:14 14 I know and I’m convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is wrong to eat in itself. But if someone thinks something is wrong to eat, it becomes wrong for that person.
ROM 14:15 15 If your brother or sister is upset by your food, you are no longer walking in love. Don’t let your food destroy someone for whom Christ died.
ROM 14:16 16 And don’t let something you consider to be good be criticized as wrong.
ROM 14:17 17 God’s kingdom isn’t about eating food and drinking but about righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
ROM 14:18 18 Whoever serves Christ this way pleases God and gets human approval.
ROM 14:19 19 So let’s strive for the things that bring peace and the things that build each other up.
ROM 14:20 20 Don’t destroy what God has done because of food. All food is acceptable, but it’s a bad thing if it trips someone else.
ROM 14:21 21 It’s a good thing not to eat meat or drink wine or to do anything that trips your brother or sister.
ROM 14:22 22 Keep the belief that you have to yourself—it’s between you and God. People are blessed who don’t convict themselves by the things they approve.
ROM 14:23 23 But those who have doubts are convicted if they go ahead and eat, because they aren’t acting on the basis of faith. Everything that isn’t based on faith is sin.
ROM 15:1 1 We who are powerful need to be patient with the weakness of those who don’t have power, and not please ourselves.
ROM 15:2 2 Each of us should please our neighbors for their good in order to build them up.
ROM 15:3 3 Christ didn’t please himself, but, as it is written, “ The insults of those who insulted you fell on me. ”
ROM 15:4 4 Whatever was written in the past was written for our instruction so that we could have hope through endurance and through the encouragement of the scriptures.
ROM 15:5 5 May the God of endurance and encouragement give you the same attitude toward each other, similar to Christ Jesus’ attitude.
ROM 15:6 6 That way you can glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ together with one voice.
ROM 15:7 7 So welcome each other, in the same way that Christ also welcomed you, for God’s glory.
ROM 15:8 8 I’m saying that Christ became a servant of those who are circumcised for the sake of God’s truth, in order to confirm the promises given to the ancestors,
ROM 15:9 9 and so that the Gentiles could glorify God for his mercy. As it is written, “ Because of this I will confess you among the Gentiles, ” “ and I will sing praises to your name ”.
ROM 15:10 10 And again, it says, “ Rejoice, Gentiles, with his people ”.
ROM 15:11 11 And again, “ Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, ” “ and all the people should sing his praises ”.
ROM 15:12 12 And again, Isaiah says, “ There will be a root of Jesse, ” “ who will also rise to rule the Gentiles. ” “ The Gentiles will place their hope in him ”.
ROM 15:13 13 May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in faith so that you overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
ROM 15:14 14 My brothers and sisters, I myself am convinced that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and are able to teach each other.
ROM 15:15 15 But I’ve written to you in a sort of daring way, partly to remind you of what you already know. I’m writing to you in this way because of the grace that was given to me by God.
ROM 15:16 16 It helps me to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles. I’m working as a priest of God’s gospel so that the offering of the Gentiles can be acceptable and made holy by the Holy Spirit.
ROM 15:17 17 So in Christ Jesus I brag about things that have to do with God.
ROM 15:18 18 I don’t dare speak about anything except what Christ has done through me to bring about the obedience of the Gentiles. He did it by what I’ve said and what I’ve done,
ROM 15:19 19 by the power of signs and wonders, and by the power of God’s Spirit. So I’ve completed the circuit of preaching Christ’s gospel from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum.
ROM 15:20 20 In this way, I have a goal to preach the gospel where they haven’t heard of Christ yet, so that I won’t be building on someone else’s foundation.
ROM 15:21 21 Instead, as it’s written, “ Those who hadn’t been told about him will see, and those who hadn’t heard will understand ”.
ROM 15:22 22 That’s why I’ve been stopped so many times from coming to see you.
ROM 15:23 23 But now, since I don’t have any place to work in these regions anymore, and since I’ve wanted to come to see you for many years,
ROM 15:24 24 I’ll visit you when I go to Spain. I hope to see you while I’m passing through. And I hope you will send me on my way there, after I have first been reenergized by some time in your company.
ROM 15:25 25 But now I’m going to Jerusalem, to serve God’s people.
ROM 15:26 26 Macedonia and Achaia have been happy to make a contribution for the poor among God’s people in Jerusalem.
ROM 15:27 27 They were happy to do this, and they are actually in debt to God’s people in Jerusalem. If the Gentiles got a share of the Jewish people’s spiritual resources, they ought to minister to them with material resources.
ROM 15:28 28 So then after I have finished this job and have safely delivered the final amount of the Gentiles’ offering to them, I will leave for Spain, visiting you on the way.
ROM 15:29 29 And I know that when I come to you I will come with the fullest blessing of Christ.
ROM 15:30 30 Brothers and sisters, I urge you, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to join me in my struggles in your prayers to God for me.
ROM 15:31 31 Pray that I will be rescued from the people in Judea who don’t believe. Also, pray that my service for Jerusalem will be acceptable to God’s people there
ROM 15:32 32 so that I can come to you with joy by God’s will and be reenergized with your company.

2CO 1:1 1 From Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God’s will, and Timothy our brother. To God’s church that is in Corinth, along with all of God’s people throughout Achaia.
2CO 1:2 2 Grace to you and peace from God our Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ.
2CO 1:3 3 May the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ be blessed! He is the compassionate Father and God of all comfort.
2CO 1:4 4 He’s the one who comforts us in all our trouble so that we can comfort other people who are in every kind of trouble. We offer the same comfort that we ourselves received from God.
2CO 1:5 5 That is because we receive so much comfort through Christ in the same way that we share so many of Christ’s sufferings.
2CO 1:6 6 So if we have trouble, it is to bring you comfort and salvation. If we are comforted, it is to bring you comfort from the experience of endurance while you go through the same sufferings that we also suffer.
2CO 1:7 7 Our hope for you is certain, because we know that as you are partners in suffering, so also you are partners in comfort.
2CO 1:8 8 Brothers and sisters, we don’t want you to be unaware of the troubles that we went through in Asia. We were weighed down with a load of suffering that was so far beyond our strength that we were afraid we might not survive.
2CO 1:9 9 It certainly seemed to us as if we had gotten the death penalty. This was so that we would have confidence in God, who raises the dead, instead of ourselves.
2CO 1:10 10 God rescued us from a terrible death, and he will rescue us. We have set our hope on him that he will rescue us again,
2CO 1:11 11 since you are helping with your prayer for us. Then many people can thank God on our behalf for the gift that was given to us through the prayers of many people.
2CO 1:12 12 We have conducted ourselves with godly sincerity and pure motives in the world, and especially toward you. This is why we are confident, and our conscience confirms this. We didn’t act with human wisdom but we relied on the grace of God.
2CO 1:13 13 We don’t write anything to you except what you can read and also understand. I hope that you will understand totally
2CO 1:14 14 since you have already understood us partly. Understand that in the day of our Lord Jesus, we will make you proud as you will also make us proud.
2CO 1:15 15 Because I was sure of this, I wanted to visit you first so that you could have a second opportunity to see me.
2CO 1:16 16 I wanted to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and then come to you again on my way back from Macedonia, at which point I was hoping you would help me on my way to Judea.
2CO 1:17 17 So I wasn’t unreliable when I planned to do this, was I? Or do I make decisions with a substandard human process so that I say “Yes, yes” and “No, no” at the same time?
2CO 1:18 18 But as God is faithful, our message to you isn’t both yes and no.
2CO 1:19 19 God’s Son, Jesus Christ, is the one who was preached among you by us—through me, Silvanus, and Timothy—he wasn’t yes and no. In him it is always yes.
2CO 1:20 20 All of God’s promises have their yes in him. That is why we say Amen through him to the glory of God.
2CO 1:21 21 God is the one who establishes us with you in Christ and who anointed us.
2CO 1:22 22 God also sealed us and gave the Spirit as a down payment in our hearts.
2CO 1:23 23 I call on God as my witness—I didn’t come again to Corinth because I wanted to spare you.
2CO 1:24 24 It isn’t that we are trying to control your faith, but we are working with you for your happiness, because you stand firm in your faith.
2CO 2:1 1 So I decided that, for my own sake, I wouldn’t visit you again while I was upset.
2CO 2:2 2 If I make you sad, who will be there to make me glad when you are sad because of me?
2CO 2:3 3 That’s why I wrote this very thing to you, so that when I came I wouldn’t be made sad by the ones who ought to make me happy. I have confidence in you, that my happiness means your happiness.
2CO 2:4 4 I wrote to you in tears, with a very troubled and anxious heart. I didn’t write to make you sad but so you would know the overwhelming love that I have for you.
2CO 2:5 5 But if someone has made anyone sad, that person hasn’t hurt me but all of you to some degree (not to exaggerate).
2CO 2:6 6 The punishment handed out by the majority is enough for this person.
2CO 2:7 7 This is why you should try your best to forgive and to comfort this person now instead, so that this person isn’t overwhelmed by too much sorrow.
2CO 2:8 8 So I encourage you to show your love for this person.
2CO 2:9 9 This is another reason why I wrote you. I wanted to test you and see if you are obedient in everything.
2CO 2:10 10 If you forgive anyone for anything, I do too. And whatever I’ve forgiven (if I’ve forgiven anything), I did it for you in the presence of Christ.
2CO 2:11 11 This is so that we won’t be taken advantage of by Satan, because we are well aware of his schemes.
2CO 2:12 12 When I came to Troas to preach Christ’s gospel, the Lord gave me an opportunity to preach.
2CO 2:13 13 But I was worried because I couldn’t find my brother Titus there. So I said good-bye to them and went on to Macedonia.
2CO 2:14 14 But thank God, who is always leading us around through Christ as if we were in a parade. He releases the fragrance of the knowledge of him everywhere through us.
2CO 2:15 15 We smell like the aroma of Christ’s offering to God, both to those who are being saved and to those who are on the road to destruction.
2CO 2:16 16 We smell like a contagious dead person to those who are dying, but we smell like the fountain of life to those who are being saved. Who is qualified for this kind of ministry?
2CO 2:17 17 We aren’t like so many people who hustle the word of God to make a profit. We are speaking through Christ in the presence of God, as those who are sincere and as those who are sent from God.
2CO 3:1 1 Are we starting to commend ourselves again? We don’t need letters of introduction to you or from you like other people, do we?
2CO 3:2 2 You are our letter, written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
2CO 3:3 3 You show that you are Christ’s letter, delivered by us. You weren’t written with ink but with the Spirit of the living God. You weren’t written on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
2CO 3:4 4 This is the confidence that we have through Christ in the presence of God.
2CO 3:5 5 It isn’t that we ourselves are qualified to claim that anything came from us. No, our qualification is from God.
2CO 3:6 6 He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not based on what is written but on the Spirit, because what is written kills, but the Spirit gives life.
2CO 3:7 7 The ministry that brought death was carved in letters on stone tablets. It came with such glory that the Israelites couldn’t look for long at Moses’ face because his face was shining with glory, even though it was a fading glory.
2CO 3:8 8 Won’t the ministry of the Spirit be much more glorious?
2CO 3:9 9 If the ministry that brought condemnation has glory, how much more glorious is the ministry that brings righteousness?
2CO 3:10 10 In fact, what was glorious isn’t glorious now, because of the glory that is brighter.
2CO 3:11 11 If the glory that fades away was glorious, how much more glorious is the one that lasts!
2CO 3:12 12 So, since we have such a hope, we act with great confidence.
2CO 3:13 13 We aren’t like Moses, who used to put a veil over his face so that the Israelites couldn’t watch the end of what was fading away.
2CO 3:14 14 But their minds were closed. Right up to the present day the same veil remains when the old covenant is read. The veil is not removed because it is taken away by Christ.
2CO 3:15 15 Even today, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their hearts.
2CO 3:16 16 But whenever someone turns back to the Lord, the veil is removed.
2CO 3:17 17 The Lord is the Spirit, and where the Lord’s Spirit is, there is freedom.
2CO 3:18 18 All of us are looking with unveiled faces at the glory of the Lord as if we were looking in a mirror. We are being transformed into that same image from one degree of glory to the next degree of glory. This comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
2CO 4:1 1 This is why we don’t get discouraged, given that we received this ministry in the same way that we received God’s mercy.
2CO 4:2 2 Instead, we reject secrecy and shameful actions. We don’t use deception, and we don’t tamper with God’s word. Instead, we commend ourselves to everyone’s conscience in the sight of God by the public announcement of the truth.
2CO 4:3 3 And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are on the road to destruction.
2CO 4:4 4 The god of this age has blinded the minds of those who don’t have faith so they couldn’t see the light of the gospel that reveals Christ’s glory. Christ is the image of God.
2CO 4:5 5 We don’t preach about ourselves. Instead, we preach about Jesus Christ as Lord, and we describe ourselves as your slaves for Jesus’ sake.
2CO 4:6 6 God said that light should shine out of the darkness. He is the same one who shone in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of God’s glory in the face of Jesus Christ.
2CO 4:7 7 But we have this treasure in clay pots so that the awesome power belongs to God and doesn’t come from us.
2CO 4:8 8 We are experiencing all kinds of trouble, but we aren’t crushed. We are confused, but we aren’t depressed.
2CO 4:9 9 We are harassed, but we aren’t abandoned. We are knocked down, but we aren’t knocked out.
2CO 4:10 10 We always carry Jesus’ death around in our bodies so that Jesus’ life can also be seen in our bodies.
2CO 4:11 11 We who are alive are always being handed over to death for Jesus’ sake so that Jesus’ life can also be seen in our bodies that are dying.
2CO 4:12 12 So death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
2CO 4:13 13 We have the same faithful spirit as what is written in scripture: “ I had faith, and so I spoke. ” We also have faith, and so we also speak.
2CO 4:14 14 We do this because we know that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus, and he will bring us into his presence along with you.
2CO 4:15 15 All these things are for your benefit. As grace increases to benefit more and more people, it will cause gratitude to increase, which results in God’s glory.
2CO 4:16 16 So we aren’t depressed. But even if our bodies are breaking down on the outside, the person that we are on the inside is being renewed every day.
2CO 4:17 17 Our temporary minor problems are producing an eternal stockpile of glory for us that is beyond all comparison.
2CO 4:18 18 We don’t focus on the things that can be seen but on the things that can’t be seen. The things that can be seen don’t last, but the things that can’t be seen are eternal.
2CO 5:1 1 We know that if the tent that we live in on earth is torn down, we have a building from God. It’s a house that isn’t handmade, which is eternal and located in heaven.
2CO 5:2 2 We groan while we live in this residence. We really want to dress ourselves with our building from heaven—
2CO 5:3 3 since we assume that when we take off this tent, we won’t find out that we are naked.
2CO 5:4 4 Yes, while we are in this tent we groan, because we are weighed down. We want to be dressed not undressed, so that what is dying can be swallowed up by life.
2CO 5:5 5 Now the one who prepared us for this very thing is God, and God gave us the Spirit as a down payment for our home.
2CO 5:6 6 So we are always confident, because we know that while we are living in the body, we are away from our home with the Lord.
2CO 5:7 7 We live by faith and not by sight.
2CO 5:8 8 We are confident, and we would prefer to leave the body and to be at home with the Lord.
2CO 5:9 9 So our goal is to be acceptable to him, whether we are at home or away from home.
2CO 5:10 10 We all must appear before Christ in court so that each person can be paid back for the things that were done while in the body, whether they were good or bad.
2CO 5:11 11 So we try to persuade people, since we know what it means to fear the Lord. We are well known by God, and I hope that in your heart we are well known by you as well.
2CO 5:12 12 We aren’t trying to commend ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you an opportunity to be proud of us so that you could answer those who take pride in superficial appearance, and not in what is in the heart.
2CO 5:13 13 If we are crazy, it’s for God’s sake. If we are rational, it’s for your sake.
2CO 5:14 14 The love of Christ controls us, because we have concluded this: one died for the sake of all; therefore, all died.
2CO 5:15 15 He died for the sake of all so that those who are alive should live not for themselves but for the one who died for them and was raised.
2CO 5:16 16 So then, from this point on we won’t recognize people by human standards. Even though we used to know Christ by human standards, that isn’t how we know him now.
2CO 5:17 17 So then, if anyone is in Christ, that person is part of the new creation. The old things have gone away, and look, new things have arrived!
2CO 5:18 18 All of these new things are from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and who gave us the ministry of reconciliation.
2CO 5:19 19 In other words, God was reconciling the world to himself through Christ, by not counting people’s sins against them. He has trusted us with this message of reconciliation.
2CO 5:20 20 So we are ambassadors who represent Christ. God is negotiating with you through us. We beg you as Christ’s representatives, “Be reconciled to God!”
2CO 5:21 21 God caused the one who didn’t know sin to be sin for our sake so that through him we could become the righteousness of God.

2CO 6:6 6 We displayed purity, knowledge, patience, and generosity. We served with the Holy Spirit, genuine love,

2CO 7:1 1 My dear friends, since we have these promises, let’s cleanse ourselves from anything that contaminates our body or spirit so that we make our holiness complete in the fear of God.
2CO 7:2 2 Make room in your hearts for us. We didn’t do anything wrong to anyone. We didn’t ruin anyone. We didn’t take advantage of anyone.
2CO 7:3 3 I’m not saying this to make you feel guilty. I’ve already said that you are in our hearts so that we die and live together with you.
2CO 7:4 4 I have every confidence in you. I’m terribly proud of you. I’m filled with encouragement. I’m overwhelmed with happiness while in the middle of our problems.
2CO 7:5 5 Even after we arrived in Macedonia, we couldn’t rest physically. We were surrounded by problems. There was external conflict, and there were internal fears.
2CO 7:6 6 However, God comforts people who are discouraged, and he comforted us by Titus’ arrival.
2CO 7:7 7 We weren’t comforted only by his arrival but also by the comfort he had received from you. He told us about your desire to see me, how you were sorry, and about your concern for me, so that I was even happier.
2CO 7:8 8 Even though my letter hurt you, I don’t regret it. Well—I did regret it just a bit because I see that that letter made you sad, though only for a short time.
2CO 7:9 9 Now I’m glad—not because you were sad but because you were made sad enough to change your hearts and lives. You felt godly sadness so that no one was harmed by us in any way.
2CO 7:10 10 Godly sadness produces a changed heart and life that leads to salvation and leaves no regrets, but sorrow under the influence of the world produces death.
2CO 7:11 11 Look at what this very experience of godly sadness has produced in you: such enthusiasm, what a desire to clear yourselves of blame, such indignation, what fear, what purpose, such concern, what justice! In everything you have shown yourselves to be innocent in the matter.
2CO 7:12 12 So although I wrote to you, it wasn’t for the sake of the one who did wrong, or for the sake of the one who was wronged, but to show you your own enthusiasm for us in the sight of God.
2CO 7:13 13 Because of this we have been encouraged. And in addition to our own encouragement, we were even more pleased at how happy Titus was. His mind has been put at rest by all of you.
2CO 7:14 14 If I’ve bragged about you to him in any way, I haven’t been embarrassed. Instead, our bragging to Titus has also been proven to be true, just like everything we said to you was true.
2CO 7:15 15 His devotion to you is growing even more as he remembers how all of you were obedient when you welcomed him with fear and trembling.
2CO 7:16 16 I’m happy, because I can completely depend on you.
2CO 8:1 1 Brothers and sisters, we want to let you know about the grace of God that was given to the churches of Macedonia.
2CO 8:2 2 While they were being tested by many problems, their extra amount of happiness and their extreme poverty resulted in a surplus of rich generosity.
2CO 8:3 3 I assure you that they gave what they could afford and even more than they could afford, and they did it voluntarily.
2CO 8:4 4 They urgently begged us for the privilege of sharing in this service for the saints.
2CO 8:5 5 They even exceeded our expectations, because they gave themselves to the Lord first and to us, consistent with God’s will.
2CO 8:6 6 As a result, we challenged Titus to finish this work of grace with you the way he had started it.
2CO 8:7 7 Be the best in this work of grace in the same way that you are the best in everything, such as faith, speech, knowledge, total commitment, and the love we inspired in you.
2CO 8:8 8 I’m not giving an order, but by mentioning the commitment of others, I’m trying to prove the authenticity of your love also.
2CO 8:9 9 You know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ. Although he was rich, he became poor for your sakes, so that you could become rich through his poverty.
2CO 8:10 10 I’m giving you my opinion about this. It’s to your advantage to do this, since you not only started to do it last year but you wanted to do it too.
2CO 8:11 11 Now finish the job as well so that you finish it with as much enthusiasm as you started, given what you can afford.
2CO 8:12 12 A gift is appreciated because of what a person can afford, not because of what that person can’t afford, if it’s apparent that it’s done willingly.
2CO 8:13 13 It isn’t that we want others to have financial ease and you financial difficulties, but it’s a matter of equality.
2CO 8:14 14 At the present moment, your surplus can fill their deficit so that in the future their surplus can fill your deficit. In this way there is equality.
2CO 8:15 15 As it is written, “ The one who gathered more didn’t have too much, and the one who gathered less didn’t have too little. ”
2CO 8:16 16 But thank God, who put the same commitment that I have for you in Titus’ heart.
2CO 8:17 17 Not only has he accepted our challenge but he’s on his way to see you voluntarily, and he’s excited.
2CO 8:18 18 We are sending the brother who is famous in all the churches because of his work for the gospel along with him.
2CO 8:19 19 In addition to this, he is chosen by the churches to be our traveling companion in this work of grace, which we are taking care of for the sake of the glory of the Lord himself, and to show our desire to help.
2CO 8:20 20 We are trying to avoid being blamed by anyone for the way we take care of this large amount of money.
2CO 8:21 21 We care about doing the right thing, not only in the Lord’s eyes but also in the eyes of other people.
2CO 8:22 22 We are sending our brother with them. We have tested his commitment in many ways and many times. Now he’s even more committed, because he has so much confidence in you.
2CO 8:23 23 If there is any question about Titus, he is my partner and coworker among you. If there is any question about our brothers, they are the churches’ apostles and an honor to Christ.
2CO 8:24 24 So show them the proof of your love and the reason we are so proud of you, in such a way that the churches can see it.
2CO 9:1 1 It’s unnecessary for me to write to you about this service for God’s people.
2CO 9:2 2 I know about your willingness to help. I brag about you to the Macedonians, saying, “Greece has been ready since last year,” and your enthusiasm has motivated most of them.
2CO 9:3 3 But I’m sending the brothers so that our bragging about you in this case won’t be empty words, and so that you can be prepared, just as I keep telling them you will be.
2CO 9:4 4 If some Macedonians should come with me and find out that you aren’t ready, we (not to mention you) would be embarrassed as far as this project goes.
2CO 9:5 5 This is why I thought it was necessary to encourage the brothers to go to you ahead of time and arrange in advance the generous gift you have already promised. I want it to be a real gift from you. I don’t want you to feel like you are being forced to give anything.
2CO 9:6 6 What I mean is this: the one who sows a small number of seeds will also reap a small crop, and the one who sows a generous amount of seeds will also reap a generous crop.
2CO 9:7 7 Everyone should give whatever they have decided in their heart. They shouldn’t give with hesitation or because of pressure. God loves a cheerful giver.
2CO 9:8 8 God has the power to provide you with more than enough of every kind of grace. That way, you will have everything you need always and in everything to provide more than enough for every kind of good work.
2CO 9:9 9 As it is written, “ He scattered everywhere; he gave to the needy; his righteousness remains forever. ”
2CO 9:10 10 The one who supplies seed for planting and bread for eating will supply and multiply your seed and will increase your crop, which is righteousness.
2CO 9:11 11 You will be made rich in every way so that you can be generous in every way. Such generosity produces thanksgiving to God through us.
2CO 9:12 12 Your ministry of this service to God’s people isn’t only fully meeting their needs but it is also multiplying in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.
2CO 9:13 13 They will give honor to God for your obedience to your confession of Christ’s gospel. They will do this because this service provides evidence of your obedience, and because of your generosity in sharing with them and with everyone.
2CO 9:14 14 They will also pray for you, and they will care deeply for you because of the outstanding grace that God has given to you.
2CO 9:15 15 Thank God for his gift that words can’t describe!
2CO 10:1 1 I, Paul, make a personal request to you with the gentleness and kindness of Christ. I’m shy when I’m with you, but I’m bossy when I’m away from you!
2CO 10:2 2 I beg you that when I’m with you in person, I won’t have to boss you around. I’m afraid that I may have to use that kind of behavior with those people who think we live by human standards.
2CO 10:3 3 Although we live in the world, we don’t fight our battles with human methods.
2CO 10:4 4 Our weapons that we fight with aren’t human, but instead they are powered by God for the destruction of fortresses. They destroy arguments,
2CO 10:5 5 and every defense that is raised up to oppose the knowledge of God. They capture every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
2CO 10:6 6 Once your obedience is complete, we are ready to punish any disobedience.
2CO 10:7 7 Look at what is right in front of you! If anyone is sure about belonging to Christ, that person should think again. We belong to Christ just like that person.
2CO 10:8 8 Even if I went on to brag about our authority, I wouldn’t be ashamed of it. The Lord gave us that authority to build you up and not to destroy you.
2CO 10:9 9 I don’t want it to seem like I’m trying to intimidate you with my letters.
2CO 10:10 10 I know what some people are saying: “His letters are severe and powerful, but in person he is weak and his speech is worth nothing.”
2CO 10:11 11 These people need to think about this—that when we are with you, our actions will show that we are the same as the words we wrote when we were away from you.
2CO 10:12 12 We won’t dare to place ourselves in the same league or to compare ourselves with some of those who are promoting themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves, and compare themselves with themselves, they have no understanding.
2CO 10:13 13 We won’t take pride in anything more than what is appropriate. Let’s look at the boundaries of our work area that God has assigned to us. It’s an area that includes you.
2CO 10:14 14 We aren’t going out of bounds, as if our work area doesn’t extend as far as you. We were the first ones to travel as far as Corinth with the gospel of Christ.
2CO 10:15 15 We don’t take pride in what other people do outside of our boundaries. We hope that our work will be extended even more by you as your faith grows, until it expands fully (within the boundaries, of course).
2CO 10:16 16 We hope that our work grows even to the point of the gospel being preached in places beyond Corinth, without bragging about what has already been done in another person’s work area.
2CO 10:17 17 But, “ the one who brags should brag in the Lord. ”
2CO 10:18 18 It isn’t the person who promotes himself or herself who is approved but the person whom the Lord commends.
2CO 11:1 1 I hope that you will put up with me while I act like a fool. Well, in fact, you are putting up with me!
2CO 11:2 2 I’m deeply concerned about you with the same concern that God has. As your father, I promised you in marriage to one husband. I promised to present you as an innocent virgin to Christ himself.
2CO 11:3 3 But I’m afraid that your minds might be seduced in the same way as the snake deceived Eve with his devious tricks. You might be unable to focus completely on a genuine and innocent commitment to Christ.
2CO 11:4 4 If a person comes and preaches some other Jesus than the one we preached, or if you receive a different Spirit than the one you had received, or a different gospel than the one you embraced, you put up with it so easily!
2CO 11:5 5 I don’t consider myself as second-rate in any way compared to the “super-apostles.”
2CO 11:6 6 But even if I’m uneducated in public speaking, I’m not uneducated in knowledge. We have shown this to you in every way and in everything we have done.
2CO 11:7 7 Did I commit a sin by humbling myself to give you an advantage because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?
2CO 11:8 8 I robbed other churches by taking a salary from them in order to serve you!
2CO 11:9 9 While I was with you, I didn’t burden any of you even though I needed things. The believers who came from Macedonia gave me everything I needed. I kept myself from being a financial drain on you in any way, and I will continue to keep myself from being a burden.
2CO 11:10 10 Since Christ’s truth is in me, I won’t stop telling the entire area of Greece that I’m proud of what I did.
2CO 11:11 11 Why? Is it because I don’t love you? God knows that I do!
2CO 11:12 12 But I’m going to continue to do what I’m doing. I want to contradict the claims of the people who want to be treated like they are the same as us because of what they brag about.
2CO 11:13 13 Such people are false apostles and dishonest workers who disguise themselves as apostles of Christ.
2CO 11:14 14 And no wonder! Even Satan disguises himself as an angel of light.
2CO 11:15 15 It is no great surprise then that his servants also disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will be what their actions deserve.
2CO 11:16 16 I repeat, no one should take me for a fool. But if you do, then allow me to be a fool so that I can brag like a fool for a bit.
2CO 11:17 17 I’m not saying what I’m saying because the Lord tells me to. I’m saying it like I’m a fool. I’m putting my confidence in this business of bragging.
2CO 11:18 18 Since so many people are bragging based on human standards, that is how I’m going to brag too.
2CO 11:19 19 Because you, who are so wise, are happy to put up with fools.
2CO 11:20 20 You put up with it if someone enslaves you, if someone exploits you, if someone takes advantage of you, if someone places themselves over you, or if someone hits you in the face.
2CO 11:21 21 I’m ashamed to say that we have been weak in comparison! But in whatever they challenge me, I challenge them (I’m speaking foolishly).
2CO 11:22 22 Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
2CO 11:23 23 Are they ministers of Christ? I’m speaking like a crazy person. What I’ve done goes well beyond what they’ve done. I’ve worked much harder. I’ve been imprisoned much more often. I’ve been beaten more times than I can count. I’ve faced death many times.
2CO 11:24 24 I received the “forty lashes minus one” from the Jews five times.
2CO 11:25 25 I was beaten with rods three times. I was stoned once. I was shipwrecked three times. I spent a day and a night on the open sea.
2CO 11:26 26 I’ve been on many journeys. I faced dangers from rivers, robbers, my people, and Gentiles. I faced dangers in the city, in the desert, on the sea, and from false brothers and sisters.
2CO 11:27 27 I faced these dangers with hard work and heavy labor, many sleepless nights, hunger and thirst, often without food, and in the cold without enough clothes.
2CO 11:28 28 Besides all the other things I could mention, there’s my daily stress because I’m concerned about all the churches.
2CO 11:29 29 Who is weak without me being weak? Who is led astray without me being furious about it?
2CO 11:30 30 If it’s necessary to brag, I’ll brag about my weaknesses.
2CO 11:31 31 The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, the one who is blessed forever, knows that I’m not lying.
2CO 11:32 32 At Damascus the governor under King Aretas was guarding the city of Damascus in order to capture me,
2CO 11:33 33 but I got away from him by being lowered in a basket through a window in the city wall.
2CO 12:1 1 It is necessary to brag, not that it does any good. I’ll move on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
2CO 12:2 2 I know a man in Christ who was caught up into the third heaven fourteen years ago. I don’t know whether it was in the body or out of the body. God knows.
2CO 12:3 3-4 I know that this man was caught up into paradise and that he heard unspeakable words that were things no one is allowed to repeat. I don’t know whether it was in the body or apart from the body. God knows.
2CO 12:4 5 I’ll brag about this man, but I won’t brag about myself, except to brag about my weaknesses.
2CO 12:5 6 If I did want to brag, I wouldn’t make a fool of myself because I’d tell the truth. I’m holding back from bragging so that no one will give me any more credit than what anyone sees or hears about me.
2CO 12:6 7 I was given a thorn in my body because of the outstanding revelations I’ve received so that I wouldn’t be conceited. It’s a messenger from Satan sent to torment me so that I wouldn’t be conceited.
2CO 12:7 8 I pleaded with the Lord three times for it to leave me alone.
2CO 12:8 9 He said to me, “My grace is enough for you, because power is made perfect in weakness.” So I’ll gladly spend my time bragging about my weaknesses so that Christ’s power can rest on me.
2CO 12:9 10 Therefore, I’m all right with weaknesses, insults, disasters, harassments, and stressful situations for the sake of Christ, because when I’m weak, then I’m strong.
2CO 12:10 11 I’ve become a fool! You made me do it. Actually, I should have been commended by you. I’m not inferior to the super-apostles in any way, even though I’m a nonentity.
2CO 12:11 12 The signs of an apostle were performed among you with continuous endurance through signs, wonders, and miracles.
2CO 12:12 13 How were you treated worse than the other churches, except that I myself wasn’t a financial burden on you? Forgive me for this wrong!
2CO 12:13 14 Look, I’m ready to visit you a third time, and I won’t be a burden on you. I don’t want your things; I want you. It isn’t the children’s responsibility to save up for their parents but parents for children.
2CO 12:14 15 I will very gladly spend and be spent for your sake. If I love you more, will you love me less?
2CO 12:15 16 We all know that I didn’t place a burden on you, but in spite of that you think I’m a con artist who fooled you with a trick.
2CO 12:16 17 I haven’t taken advantage of you through any of the people I sent to you, have I?
2CO 12:17 18 I strongly encouraged Titus to go to you and sent the brother with him. Titus didn’t take advantage of you, did he? Didn’t we live by the same Spirit? Didn’t we walk in the same footsteps?
2CO 12:18 19 Have you been thinking up to now that we are defending ourselves to you? Actually, we are speaking in the sight of God and in Christ. Dear friends, everything is meant to build you up.
2CO 12:19 20 I’m afraid that maybe when I come you will be different from the way I want you to be, and that I’ll be different from the way you want me to be. I’m afraid that there might be fighting, obsession, losing your temper, competitive opposition, backstabbing, gossip, conceit, and disorderly conduct.
2CO 12:20 21 I’m afraid that when I come again, my God may embarrass me in front of you. I might have to go into mourning over all the people who have sinned before and haven’t changed their hearts and lives from what they used to practice: moral corruption, sexual immorality, and doing whatever feels good.
2CO 13:1 1 This is the third time that I’m coming to visit you. Every matter is settled on the evidence of two or three witnesses.
2CO 13:2 2 When I was with you on my second visit, I already warned those who continued to sin. Now I’m repeating that warning to all the rest of you while I’m at a safe distance: if I come again, I won’t spare anyone.
2CO 13:3 3 Since you are demanding proof that Christ speaks through me, Christ isn’t weak in dealing with you but shows his power among you.
2CO 13:4 4 Certainly he was crucified because of weakness, but he lives by the power of God. Certainly we also are weak in him, but we will live together with him, because of God’s power that is directed toward you.
2CO 13:5 5 Examine yourselves to see if you are in the faith. Test yourselves. Don’t you understand that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless, of course, you fail the test.
2CO 13:6 6 But I hope that you will realize that we don’t fail the test.
2CO 13:7 7 We pray to God that you don’t do anything wrong, not because we want to appear to pass the test but so that you might do the right thing, even if we appear to fail.
2CO 13:8 8 We can’t do anything against the truth but only to help the truth.
2CO 13:9 9 We are happy when we are weak but you are strong. We pray for this: that you will be made complete.
2CO 13:10 10 This is why I’m writing these things while I’m away. I’m writing so that I won’t need to act harshly when I’m with you by using the authority that the Lord gave me. He gave it to me so that I could build you up, not tear you down.
2CO 13:11 11 Finally, brothers and sisters, good-bye. Put things in order, respond to my encouragement, be in harmony with each other, and live in peace—and the God of love and peace will be with you.
2CO 13:12 12 Say hello to each other with a holy kiss. All of God’s people say hello to you.
2CO 13:13 13 The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.
GAL 1:1 1 From Paul, an apostle who is not sent from human authority or commissioned through human agency, but sent through Jesus Christ and God the Father who raised him from the dead;
GAL 1:2 2 and from all the brothers and sisters with me. To the churches in Galatia.
GAL 1:3 3 Grace and peace to you from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
GAL 1:4 4 He gave himself for our sins, so he could deliver us from this present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father.
GAL 1:5 5 To God be the glory forever and always! Amen.
GAL 1:6 6 I’m amazed that you are so quickly deserting the one who called you by the grace of Christ to follow another gospel.
GAL 1:7 7 It’s not really another gospel, but certain people are confusing you and they want to change the gospel of Christ.
GAL 1:8 8 However, even if we ourselves or a heavenly angel should ever preach anything different from what we preached to you, they should be under a curse.
GAL 1:9 9 I’m repeating what we’ve said before: if anyone preaches something different from what you received, they should be under a curse!
GAL 1:10 10 Am I trying to win over human beings or God? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still trying to please people, I wouldn’t be Christ’s slave.
GAL 1:11 11 Brothers and sisters, I want you to know that the gospel I preached isn’t human in origin.
GAL 1:12 12 I didn’t receive it or learn it from a human. It came through a revelation from Jesus Christ.
GAL 1:13 13 You heard about my previous life in Judaism, how severely I harassed God’s church and tried to destroy it.
GAL 1:14 14 I advanced in Judaism beyond many of my peers, because I was much more militant about the traditions of my ancestors.
GAL 1:15 15 But God had set me apart from birth and called me through his grace. He was pleased
GAL 1:16 16 to reveal his Son to me, so that I might preach about him to the Gentiles. I didn’t immediately consult with any human being.
GAL 1:17 17 I didn’t go up to Jerusalem to see the men who were apostles before me either, but I went away into Arabia and I returned again to Damascus.
GAL 1:18 18 Then after three years I went up to Jerusalem to visit Cephas and stayed with him fifteen days.
GAL 1:19 19 But I didn’t see any other of the apostles except James the brother of the Lord.
GAL 1:20 20 Before God, I’m not lying about the things that I’m writing to you!
GAL 1:21 21 Then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia,
GAL 1:22 22 but I wasn’t known personally by the Christian churches in Judea.
GAL 1:23 23 They only heard a report about me: “The man who used to harass us now preaches the faith that he once tried to destroy.”
GAL 1:24 24 So they were glorifying God because of me.
GAL 2:1 1 Then after fourteen years I went up to Jerusalem again with Barnabas, and I took Titus along also.
GAL 2:2 2 I went there because of a revelation, and I laid out the gospel that I preach to the Gentiles for them. But I did it privately with the influential leaders to make sure that I wouldn’t be working or that I hadn’t worked for nothing.
GAL 2:3 3 However, not even Titus, who was with me and who was a Greek, was required to be circumcised.
GAL 2:4 4 But false brothers and sisters, who were brought in secretly, slipped in to spy on our freedom, which we have in Christ Jesus, and to make us slaves.
GAL 2:5 5 We didn’t give in and submit to them for a single moment, so that the truth of the gospel would continue to be with you.
GAL 2:6 6 The influential leaders didn’t add anything to what I was preaching—and whatever they were makes no difference to me, because God doesn’t show favoritism.
GAL 2:7 7 But on the contrary, they saw that I had been given the responsibility to preach the gospel to the people who aren’t circumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised.
GAL 2:8 8 The one who empowered Peter to become an apostle to the circumcised empowered me also to be one to the Gentiles.
GAL 2:9 9 James, Cephas, and John, who are considered to be key leaders, shook hands with me and Barnabas as equals when they recognized the grace that was given to me. So it was agreed that we would go to the Gentiles, while they continue to go to the people who were circumcised.
GAL 2:10 10 They asked only that we would remember the poor, which was certainly something I was willing to do.
GAL 2:11 11 But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he was wrong.
GAL 2:12 12 He had been eating with the Gentiles before certain people came from James. But when they came, he began to back out and separate himself, because he was afraid of the people who promoted circumcision.
GAL 2:13 13 And the rest of the Jews also joined him in this hypocrisy so that even Barnabas got carried away with them in their hypocrisy.
GAL 2:14 14 But when I saw that they weren’t acting consistently with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of everyone, “If you, though you’re a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you require the Gentiles to live like Jews?”
GAL 2:15 15 We are born Jews—we’re not Gentile sinners.
GAL 2:16 16 However, we know that a person isn’t made righteous by the works of the Law but rather through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ. We ourselves believed in Christ Jesus so that we could be made righteous by the faithfulness of Christ and not by the works of the Law—because no one will be made righteous by the works of the Law.
GAL 2:17 17 But if it is discovered that we ourselves are sinners while we are trying to be made righteous in Christ, then is Christ a servant of sin? Absolutely not!
GAL 2:18 18 If I rebuild the very things that I tore down, I show that I myself am breaking the Law.
GAL 2:19 19 I died to the Law through the Law, so that I could live for God.
GAL 2:20 20 I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. And the life that I now live in my body, I live by faith, indeed, by the faithfulness of God’s Son, who loved me and gave himself for me.
GAL 2:21 21 I don’t ignore the grace of God, because if we become righteous through the Law, then Christ died for no purpose.
GAL 3:1 1 You irrational Galatians! Who put a spell on you? Jesus Christ was put on display as crucified before your eyes!
GAL 3:2 2 I just want to know this from you: Did you receive the Spirit by doing the works of the Law or by believing what you heard?
GAL 3:3 3 Are you so irrational? After you started with the Spirit, are you now finishing up with your own human effort?
GAL 3:4 4 Did you experience so much for nothing? I wonder if it really was for nothing.
GAL 3:5 5 So does the one providing you with the Spirit and working miracles among you do this by you doing the works of the Law or by you believing what you heard?
