1TI 3:8 8 In the same way, servants in the church should be dignified, not two-faced, heavy drinkers, or greedy for money.
1TI 3:9 9 They should hold on to the faith that has been revealed with a clear conscience.
1TI 3:10 10 They should also be tested and then serve if they are without fault.
1TI 3:11 11 In the same way, women who are servants in the church should be dignified and not gossip. They should be sober and faithful in everything they do.
1TI 3:12 12 Servants must be faithful to their spouse and manage their children and their own households well.
1TI 3:13 13 Those who have served well gain a good standing and considerable confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
1TI 3:14 14 I hope to come to you quickly. But I’m writing these things to you so that
1TI 3:15 15 if I’m delayed, you’ll know how you should behave in God’s household. It is the church of the living God and the backbone and support of the truth.
1TI 3:16 16 Without question, the mystery of godliness is great: he was revealed as a human, declared righteous by the Spirit, seen by angels, preached throughout the nations, believed in around the world, and taken up in glory.
1TI 4:1 1 The Spirit clearly says that in latter times some people will turn away from the faith. They will pay attention to spirits that deceive and to the teaching of demons.
1TI 4:2 2 They will be controlled by the pretense of lying, and their own consciences will be seared.
1TI 4:3 3 They will prohibit marriage and eating foods that God created—and he intended them to be accepted with thanksgiving by those who are faithful and have come to know the truth.
1TI 4:4 4 Everything that has been created by God is good, and nothing that is received with thanksgiving should be rejected.
1TI 4:5 5 These things are made holy by God’s word and prayer.
1TI 4:6 6 If you point these things out to the believers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus who has been trained by the words of faith and the good teaching that you’ve carefully followed.
1TI 4:7 7 But stay away from the godless myths that are passed down from the older women. Train yourself for a holy life!
1TI 4:8 8 While physical training has some value, training in holy living is useful for everything. It has promise for this life now and the life to come.
1TI 4:9 9 This saying is reliable and deserves complete acceptance.
1TI 4:10 10 We work and struggle for this: “Our hope is set on the living God, who is the savior of all people, especially those who believe.”
1TI 4:11 11 Command these things. Teach them.
1TI 4:12 12 Don’t let anyone look down on you because you are young. Instead, set an example for the believers through your speech, behavior, love, faith, and by being sexually pure.
1TI 4:13 13 Until I arrive, pay attention to public reading, preaching, and teaching.
1TI 4:14 14 Don’t neglect the spiritual gift in you that was given through prophecy when the elders laid hands on you.
1TI 4:15 15 Practice these things, and live by them so that your progress will be visible to all.
1TI 4:16 16 Focus on working on your own development and on what you teach. If you do this, you will save yourself and those who hear you.
1TI 5:1 1 Don’t correct an older man, but encourage him like he’s your father; treat younger men like your brothers,
1TI 5:2 2 treat older women like your mother, and treat younger women like your sisters with appropriate respect.
1TI 5:3 3 Take care of widows who are truly needy.
1TI 5:4 4 But if a particular widow has children or grandchildren, they should first learn to respect their own family and repay their parents, because this pleases God.
1TI 5:5 5 A widow who is truly needy and all alone puts her hope in God and keeps on going with requests and prayers, night and day.
1TI 5:6 6 But a widow who tries to live a life of luxury is dead even while she is alive.
1TI 5:7 7 Teach these things so that the families will be without fault.
1TI 5:8 8 But if someone doesn’t provide for their own family, and especially for a member of their household, they have denied the faith. They are worse than those who have no faith.
1TI 5:9 9 Put a widow on the list who is older than 60 years old and who was faithful to her husband.
1TI 5:10 10 She should have a reputation for doing good: raising children, providing hospitality to strangers, washing the feet of the saints, helping those in distress, and dedicating herself to every kind of good thing.
1TI 5:11 11 But don’t accept younger widows for the list. When their physical desires distract them from Christ, they will want to get married.
1TI 5:12 12 Then they will be judged for setting aside their earlier commitment.
1TI 5:13 13 Also, they learn to be lazy by going from house to house. They are not only lazy, but they also become gossips and busybodies, talking about things they shouldn’t.
1TI 5:14 14 So I want younger widows to marry, have children, and manage their homes so that they won’t give the enemy any reason to slander us. (
1TI 5:15 15 Some have already turned away to follow Satan.)
1TI 5:16 16 If any woman who is a believer has widows in her family, she should take care of them and not burden the church, so that it can help other widows who are truly needy.
1TI 5:17 17 Elders who lead well should be paid double, especially those who work with public speaking and teaching.
1TI 5:18 18 The scripture says, “ Don’t put a muzzle on an ox while it treads grain ”, and “ Workers deserve their pay ”.
1TI 5:19 19 Don’t accept an accusation made against an elder unless it is confirmed by two or three witnesses.
1TI 5:20 20 Discipline those who are sinning in front of everyone so that all the others will be afraid.
1TI 5:21 21 I charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the elect angels to follow these practices without bias, and without playing favorites.
1TI 5:22 22 Don’t rush to commission anyone to leadership, and don’t participate in the sins of others. Keep yourself morally pure.
1TI 5:23 23 Don’t drink water anymore, but use a little wine because of your stomach problems and your frequent illnesses.
1TI 5:24 24 The sins of some people are obvious, and the sins are judged before the people must face judgment, but the sins of other people show up later.
1TI 5:25 25 In the same way, the good that people do is also obvious and can’t be hidden.
1TI 6:1 1 Those who are under the bondage of slavery should consider their own masters as worthy of full respect so that God’s name and our teaching won’t get a bad reputation.
1TI 6:2 2 And those who have masters who are believers shouldn’t look down on them because they are brothers. Instead, they should serve them more faithfully, because the people who benefit from your good service are believers who are loved. Teach and encourage these things.
1TI 6:3 3 If anyone teaches anything different and doesn’t agree with sound teaching about our Lord Jesus Christ and teaching that is consistent with godliness,
1TI 6:4 4 that person is conceited. They don’t understand anything but have a sick obsession with debates and arguments. This creates jealousy, conflict, verbal abuse, and evil suspicions.
1TI 6:5 5 There is constant bickering between people whose minds are ruined and who have been robbed of the truth. They think that godliness is a way to make money!
1TI 6:6 6 Actually, godliness is a great source of profit when it is combined with being happy with what you already have.
1TI 6:7 7 We didn’t bring anything into the world and so we can’t take anything out of it:
1TI 6:8 8 we’ll be happy with food and clothing.
1TI 6:9 9 But people who are trying to get rich fall into temptation. They are trapped by many stupid and harmful passions that plunge people into ruin and destruction.
1TI 6:10 10 The love of money is the root of all kinds of evil. Some have wandered away from the faith and have impaled themselves with a lot of pain because they made money their goal.
1TI 6:11 11 But as for you, man of God, run away from all these things. Instead, pursue righteousness, holy living, faithfulness, love, endurance, and gentleness.
1TI 6:12 12 Compete in the good fight of faith. Grab hold of eternal life—you were called to it, and you made a good confession of it in the presence of many witnesses.
1TI 6:13 13 I command you in the presence of God, who gives life to all things, and Christ Jesus, who made the good confession when testifying before Pontius Pilate.
1TI 6:14 14 Obey this order without fault or failure until the appearance of our Lord Jesus Christ.
1TI 6:15 15 The timing of this appearance is revealed by God alone, who is the blessed and only master, the King of kings and Lord of lords.
1TI 6:16 16 He alone has immortality and lives in light that no one can come near. No human being has ever seen or is able to see him. Honor and eternal power belong to him. Amen.
1TI 6:17 17 Tell people who are rich at this time not to become egotistical and not to place their hope on their finances, which are uncertain. Instead, they need to hope in God, who richly provides everything for our enjoyment.
1TI 6:18 18 Tell them to do good, to be rich in the good things they do, to be generous, and to share with others.
1TI 6:19 19 When they do these things, they will save a treasure for themselves that is a good foundation for the future. That way they can take hold of what is truly life.
1TI 6:20 20 Timothy, protect what has been given to you in trust. Avoid godless and pointless discussions and the contradictory claims of so-called “knowledge.”
1TI 6:21 21 When some people adopted this false knowledge, they missed the goal of faith. May grace be with you all.
2TI 1:1 1 From Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God’s will, to promote the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus.
2TI 1:2 2 To Timothy, my dear child. Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
2TI 1:3 3 I’m grateful to God, whom I serve with a good conscience as my ancestors did. I constantly remember you in my prayers day and night.
2TI 1:4 4 When I remember your tears, I long to see you so that I can be filled with happiness.
2TI 1:5 5 I’m reminded of your authentic faith, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice. I’m sure that this faith is also inside you.
2TI 1:6 6 Because of this, I’m reminding you to revive God’s gift that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
2TI 1:7 7 God didn’t give us a spirit that is timid but one that is powerful, loving, and self-controlled.
2TI 1:8 8 So don’t be ashamed of the testimony about the Lord or of me, his prisoner. Instead, share the suffering for the good news, depending on God’s power.
2TI 1:9 9 God is the one who saved and called us with a holy calling. This wasn’t based on what we have done, but it was based on his own purpose and grace that he gave us in Christ Jesus before time began.
2TI 1:10 10 Now his grace is revealed through the appearance of our savior, Christ Jesus. He destroyed death and brought life and immortality into clear focus through the good news.
2TI 1:11 11 I was appointed a messenger, apostle, and teacher of this good news.
2TI 1:12 12 This is also why I’m suffering the way I do, but I’m not ashamed. I know the one in whom I’ve placed my trust. I’m convinced that God is powerful enough to protect what he has placed in my trust until that day.
2TI 1:13 13 Hold on to the pattern of sound teaching that you heard from me with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
2TI 1:14 14 Protect this good thing that has been placed in your trust through the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
2TI 1:15 15 You know that everyone in Asia has turned away from me, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
2TI 1:16 16 May the Lord show mercy to Onesiphorus’ household, because he supported me many times and he wasn’t ashamed of my imprisonment.
2TI 1:17 17 After I arrived in Rome, he quickly looked for me and found me.
2TI 1:18 18 May the Lord allow him to find his mercy on that day (and you know very well how much he served me in Ephesus).
2TI 2:1 1 So, my child, draw your strength from the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
2TI 2:2 2 Take the things you heard me say in front of many other witnesses and pass them on to faithful people who are also capable of teaching others.
2TI 2:3 3 Accept your share of suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
2TI 2:4 4 Nobody who serves in the military gets tied up with civilian matters, so that they can please the one who recruited them.
2TI 2:5 5 Also in the same way, athletes don’t win unless they follow the rules.
2TI 2:6 6 A hardworking farmer should get the first share of the crop.
2TI 2:7 7 Think about what I’m saying; the Lord will give you understanding about everything.
2TI 2:8 8 Remember Jesus Christ, who was raised from the dead and descended from David. This is my good news.
2TI 2:9 9 This is the reason I’m suffering to the point that I’m in prison like a common criminal. But God’s word cannot be imprisoned.
2TI 2:10 10 This is why I endure everything for the sake of those who are chosen by God so that they too may experience salvation in Christ Jesus with eternal glory.
2TI 2:11 11 This saying is reliable: “If we have died together, we will also live together.
2TI 2:12 12 If we endure, we will also rule together. If we deny him, he will also deny us.
2TI 2:13 13 If we are disloyal, he stays faithful” because he can’t be anything else than what he is.
2TI 2:14 14 Remind them of these things and warn them in the sight of God not to engage in battles over words that aren’t helpful and only destroy those who hear them.
2TI 2:15 15 Make an effort to present yourself to God as a tried-and-true worker, who doesn’t need to be ashamed but is one who interprets the message of truth correctly.
2TI 2:16 16 Avoid their godless discussions, because they will lead many people into ungodly behavior,
2TI 2:17 17 and their ideas will spread like an infection. This includes Hymenaeus and Philetus,
2TI 2:18 18 who have deviated from the truth by claiming that the resurrection has already happened. This has undermined some people’s faith.
2TI 2:19 19 God’s solid foundation is still standing with this sign: “ The Lord knows the people who belong to him, ” and “ Everyone who confesses the Lord’s name must avoid wickedness. ”
2TI 2:20 20 In a mansion, there aren’t just gold and silver bowls but also some bowls that are made of wood and clay. Some are meant for special uses, some for garbage.
2TI 2:21 21 So if anyone washes filth off themselves, they will be set apart as a “special bowl.” They will be useful to the owner of the mansion for every sort of good work.
2TI 2:22 22 Run away from adolescent cravings. Instead, pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace together with those who confess the Lord with a clean heart.
2TI 2:23 23 Avoid foolish and thoughtless discussions, since you know that they produce conflicts.
2TI 2:24 24 God’s slave shouldn’t be argumentative but should be kind toward all people, able to teach, patient,
2TI 2:25 25 and should correct opponents with gentleness. Perhaps God will change their mind and give them a knowledge of the truth.
2TI 2:26 26 They may come to their senses and escape from the devil’s trap that holds them captive to do his will.
2TI 3:1 1 Understand that the last days will be dangerous times.
2TI 3:2 2 People will be selfish and love money. They will be the kind of people who brag and who are proud. They will slander others, and they will be disobedient to their parents. They will be ungrateful, unholy,
2TI 3:3 3 unloving, contrary, and critical. They will be without self-control and brutal, and they won’t love what is good.
2TI 3:4 4 They will be people who are disloyal, reckless, and conceited. They will love pleasure instead of loving God.
2TI 3:5 5 They will look like they are religious but deny God’s power. Avoid people like this.
2TI 3:6 6 Some will slither into households and control immature women who are burdened with sins and driven by all kinds of desires.
2TI 3:7 7 These women are always learning, but they can never arrive at an understanding of the truth.
2TI 3:8 8 These people oppose the truth in the same way that Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses. Their minds are corrupt and their faith is counterfeit.
2TI 3:9 9 But they won’t get very far. Their foolishness will become obvious to everyone like those others.
2TI 3:10 10 But you have paid attention to my teaching, conduct, purpose, faithfulness, patience, love, and endurance.
2TI 3:11 11 You have seen me experience physical abuse and ordeals in places such as Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. I put up with all sorts of abuse, and the Lord rescued me from it all!
2TI 3:12 12 In fact, anyone who wants to live a holy life in Christ Jesus will be harassed.
2TI 3:13 13 But evil people and swindlers will grow even worse, as they deceive others while being deceived themselves.
2TI 3:14 14 But you must continue with the things you have learned and found convincing. You know who taught you.
2TI 3:15 15 Since childhood you have known the holy scriptures that help you to be wise in a way that leads to salvation through faith that is in Christ Jesus.
2TI 3:16 16 Every scripture is inspired by God and is useful for teaching, for showing mistakes, for correcting, and for training character,
2TI 3:17 17 so that the person who belongs to God can be equipped to do everything that is good.
2TI 4:1 1 I’m giving you this commission in the presence of God and of Christ Jesus, who is coming to judge the living and the dead, and by his appearance and his kingdom.
2TI 4:2 2 Preach the word. Be ready to do it whether it is convenient or inconvenient. Correct, confront, and encourage with patience and instruction.
2TI 4:3 3 There will come a time when people will not tolerate sound teaching. They will collect teachers who say what they want to hear because they are self-centered.
2TI 4:4 4 They will turn their back on the truth and turn to myths.
2TI 4:5 5 But you must keep control of yourself in all circumstances. Endure suffering, do the work of a preacher of the good news, and carry out your service fully.
2TI 4:6 6 I’m already being poured out like a sacrifice to God, and the time of my death is near.
2TI 4:7 7 I have fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith.
2TI 4:8 8 At last the champion’s wreath that is awarded for righteousness is waiting for me. The Lord, who is the righteous judge, is going to give it to me on that day. He’s giving it not only to me but also to all those who have set their heart on waiting for his appearance.
2TI 4:9 9 Do your best to come to me quickly.
2TI 4:10 10 Demas has fallen in love with the present world and has deserted me and has gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus has gone to Dalmatia.
2TI 4:11 11 Only Luke is with me. Get Mark, and bring him with you. He has been a big help to me in the ministry.
2TI 4:12 12 I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
2TI 4:13 13 When you come, bring along the coat I left with Carpus in Troas. Also bring the scrolls and especially the parchments.
2TI 4:14 14 Alexander, the craftsman who works with metal, has really hurt me. The Lord will pay him back for what he has done.
2TI 4:15 15 But watch out for him, because he opposes our teaching.
2TI 4:16 16 No one took my side at my first court hearing. Everyone deserted me. I hope that God doesn’t hold it against them!
2TI 4:17 17 But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that the entire message would be preached through me and so all the nations could hear it. I was also rescued from the lion’s mouth!
2TI 4:18 18 The Lord will rescue me from every evil action and will save me for his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory forever and always. Amen.
2TI 4:19 19 Say hello to Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.
2TI 4:20 20 Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus in Miletus because of his illness.
2TI 4:21 21 Try hard to come to me before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers and sisters say hello.
2TI 4:22 22 The Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you all.
TIT 1:1 1 From Paul, a slave of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ. I’m sent to bring about the faith of God’s chosen people and a knowledge of the truth that agrees with godliness.
TIT 1:2 2 Their faith and this knowledge are based on the hope of eternal life that God, who doesn’t lie, promised before time began.
TIT 1:3 3 God revealed his message at the appropriate time through preaching, and I was trusted with preaching this message by the command of God our savior.
TIT 1:4 4 To Titus, my true child in a common faith. Grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our savior.
TIT 1:5 5 The reason I left you behind in Crete was to organize whatever needs to be done and to appoint elders in each city, as I told you.
TIT 1:6 6 Elders should be without fault. They should be faithful to their spouse, and have faithful children who can’t be accused of self-indulgence or rebelliousness.
TIT 1:7 7 This is because supervisors should be without fault as God’s managers: they shouldn’t be stubborn, irritable, addicted to alcohol, a bully, or greedy.
TIT 1:8 8 Instead, they should show hospitality, love what is good, and be reasonable, ethical, godly, and self-controlled.
TIT 1:9 9 They must pay attention to the reliable message as it has been taught to them so that they can encourage people with healthy instruction and refute those who speak against it.
TIT 1:10 10 In fact, there are many who are rebellious people, loudmouths, and deceivers, especially some of those who are Jewish believers.
TIT 1:11 11 They must be silenced because they upset entire households. They teach what they shouldn’t to make money dishonestly.
TIT 1:12 12 Someone who is one of their own prophets said, “People from Crete are always liars, wild animals, and lazy gluttons.”
TIT 1:13 13 This statement is true. Because of this, correct them firmly, so that they can be healthy in their faith.
TIT 1:14 14 They shouldn’t pay attention to Jewish myths and commands from people who reject the truth.
TIT 1:15 15 Everything is clean to those who are clean, but nothing is clean to those who are corrupt and without faith. Instead, their mind and conscience are corrupted.
TIT 1:16 16 They claim to know God, but they deny God by the things that they do. They are detestable, disobedient, and disqualified to do anything good.
TIT 2:1 1 But you should talk in a way that is consistent with sound teaching.
TIT 2:2 2 Tell the older men to be sober, dignified, sensible, and healthy in respect to their faith, love, and patience.
TIT 2:3 3 Likewise, tell the older women to be reverent in their behavior, teaching what is good, rather than being gossips or addicted to heavy drinking.
TIT 2:4 4 That way they can mentor young women to love their husbands and children,
TIT 2:5 5 and to be sensible, morally pure, working at home, kind and submissive to their own husbands, so that God’s word won’t be ridiculed.
TIT 2:6 6 Likewise, encourage the younger men to be sensible
TIT 2:7 7 in every way. Offer yourself as a role model of good actions. Show integrity, seriousness,
TIT 2:8 8 and a sound message that is above criticism when you teach, so that any opponent will be ashamed because they won’t find anything bad to say about us.
TIT 2:9 9 Tell slaves to submit to their own masters and please them in everything they do. They shouldn’t talk back
TIT 2:10 10 or steal. Instead, they should show that they are completely reliable in everything so that they might make the teaching about God our savior attractive in every way.
TIT 2:11 11 The grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people.
TIT 2:12 12 It educates us so that we can live sensible, ethical, and godly lives right now by rejecting ungodly lives and the desires of this world.
TIT 2:13 13 At the same time we wait for the blessed hope and the glorious appearance of our great God and savior Jesus Christ.
TIT 2:14 14 He gave himself for us in order to rescue us from every kind of lawless behavior, and cleanse a special people for himself who are eager to do good actions.
TIT 2:15 15 Talk about these things. Encourage and correct with complete authority. Don’t let anyone disrespect you.
TIT 3:1 1 Remind them to submit to rulers and authorities. They should be obedient and ready to do every good thing.
TIT 3:2 2 They shouldn’t speak disrespectfully about anyone, but they should be peaceful, kind, and show complete courtesy toward everyone.
TIT 3:3 3 We were once foolish, disobedient, deceived, and slaves to our desires and various pleasures too. We were spending our lives in evil behavior and jealousy. We were disgusting, and we hated other people.
TIT 3:4 4 But “when God our savior’s kindness and love appeared,
TIT 3:5 5 he saved us because of his mercy, not because of righteous things we had done. He did it through the washing of new birth and the renewing by the Holy Spirit,
TIT 3:6 6 which God poured out upon us generously through Jesus Christ our savior.
TIT 3:7 7 So, since we have been made righteous by his grace, we can inherit the hope for eternal life.”
TIT 3:8 8 This saying is reliable. And I want you to insist on these things, so that those who have come to believe in God might give careful attention to doing good. These things are good and useful for everyone.
TIT 3:9 9 Avoid stupid controversies, genealogies, and fights about the Law, because they are useless and worthless.
TIT 3:10 10 After a first and second warning, have nothing more to do with a person who causes conflict,
TIT 3:11 11 because you know that someone like this is twisted and sinful—so they condemn themselves.
TIT 3:12 12 When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, try to come to me in Nicopolis, because I’ve decided to spend the winter there.
TIT 3:13 13 Help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey with enthusiasm so that they won’t need anything.
TIT 3:14 14 But our people should also learn to devote themselves to doing good in order to meet pressing needs so they aren’t unproductive.
TIT 3:15 15 Everyone with me greets you; greet those who love us faithfully. Grace be with all of you.
PHM 1:1 1 From Paul, who is a prisoner for the cause of Christ Jesus, and our brother Timothy. To Philemon our dearly loved coworker,
PHM 1:2 2 Apphia our sister, Archippus our fellow soldier, and the church that meets in your house.
PHM 1:3 3 May the grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
PHM 1:4 4 Philemon, I thank my God every time I mention you in my prayers
PHM 1:5 5 because I’ve heard of your love and faithfulness, which you have both for the Lord Jesus and for all God’s people.
PHM 1:6 6 I pray that your partnership in the faith might become effective by an understanding of all that is good among us in Christ.
PHM 1:7 7 I have great joy and encouragement because of your love, since the hearts of God’s people are refreshed by your actions, my brother.
PHM 1:8 8 Therefore, though I have enough confidence in Christ to command you to do the right thing,
PHM 1:9 9 I would rather appeal to you through love. I, Paul—an old man, and now also a prisoner for Christ Jesus—
PHM 1:10 10 appeal to you for my child Onesimus. I became his father in the faith during my time in prison.
PHM 1:11 11 He was useless to you before, but now he is useful to both of us.
PHM 1:12 12 I’m sending him back to you, which is like sending you my own heart.
PHM 1:13 13 I considered keeping him with me so that he might serve me in your place during my time in prison because of the gospel.
PHM 1:14 14 However, I didn’t want to do anything without your consent so that your act of kindness would occur willingly and not under pressure.
PHM 1:15 15 Maybe this is the reason that Onesimus was separated from you for a while so that you might have him back forever—
PHM 1:16 16 no longer as a slave but more than a slave—that is, as a dearly loved brother. He is especially a dearly loved brother to me. How much more can he become a brother to you, personally and spiritually in the Lord!
PHM 1:17 17 So, if you really consider me a partner, welcome Onesimus as if you were welcoming me.
PHM 1:18 18 If he has harmed you in any way or owes you money, charge it to my account.
PHM 1:19 19 I, Paul, will pay it back to you (I’m writing this with my own hand). Of course, I won’t mention that you owe me your life.
PHM 1:20 20 Yes, brother, I want this favor from you in the Lord! Refresh my heart in Christ.
PHM 1:21 21 I’m writing to you, confident of your obedience and knowing that you will do more than what I ask.
PHM 1:22 22 Also, one more thing—prepare a guest room for me. I hope that I will be released from prison to be with you because of your prayers.
PHM 1:23 23 Epaphras, who is in prison with me for the cause of Christ Jesus, greets you,
PHM 1:24 24 as well as my coworkers Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke.
PHM 1:25 25 May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
HEB 1:1 1 In the past, God spoke through the prophets to our ancestors in many times and many ways.
HEB 1:2 2 In these final days, though, he spoke to us through a Son. God made his Son the heir of everything and created the world through him.
HEB 1:3 3 The Son is the light of God’s glory and the imprint of God’s being. He maintains everything with his powerful message. After he carried out the cleansing of people from their sins, he sat down at the right side of the highest majesty.
HEB 1:4 4 And the Son became so much greater than the other messengers, such as angels, that he received a more important title than theirs.
HEB 1:5 5 After all, when did God ever say to any of the angels: “ You are my Son. ” “ Today I have become your Father? ” Or, even, “ I will be his Father, ” “ and he will be my Son? ”
HEB 1:6 6 But then, when he brought his firstborn into the world, he said, “ All of God’s angels must worship him. ”
HEB 1:7 7 He talks about the angels: “ He’s the one who uses the spirits for his messengers ” “ and who uses flames of fire as ministers. ”
HEB 1:8 8 But he says to his Son, “ God, your throne is forever ” “ and your kingdom’s scepter is a rod of justice. ”
HEB 1:9 9 “ You loved righteousness and hated lawless behavior. ” “ That is why God, your God, ” “ has anointed you more than your companions with the oil of joy. ”
HEB 1:10 10 And he says, “ You, Lord, laid the earth’s foundations in the beginning, ” “ and the heavens are made by your hands. ”
HEB 1:11 11 “ They will pass away, ” “ but you remain. ” “ They will all wear out like old clothes. ”
HEB 1:12 12 “ You will fold them up like a coat. ” “ They will be changed like a person changes clothes, ” “ but you stay the same, ” “ and the years of your life won’t come to an end. ”
HEB 1:13 13 When has he ever said to any of the angels, “ Sit at my right side ” “ until I put your enemies under your feet like a footstool? ”
HEB 1:14 14 Aren’t all the angels ministering spirits who are sent to serve those who are going to inherit salvation?
HEB 2:1 1 This is why it’s necessary for us to pay more attention to what we have heard, or else we may drift away from it.
HEB 2:2 2 If the message that was spoken by angels was reliable, and every offense and act of disobedience received an appropriate consequence,
HEB 2:3 3 how will we escape if we ignore such a great salvation? It was first announced through the Lord, and then it was confirmed by those who heard him.
HEB 2:4 4 God also vouched for their message with signs, amazing things, various miracles, and gifts from the Holy Spirit, which were handed out the way he wanted.
HEB 2:5 5 God didn’t put the world that is coming (the world we are talking about) under the angels’ control.
HEB 2:6 6 Instead, someone declared somewhere, “ What is humanity that you think about them? ” “ Or what are human beings that you care about them? ”
HEB 2:7 7 “ For a while you made them lower than angels. ” “ You crowned human beings with glory and honor. ”
HEB 2:8 8 “ You put everything under their control. ” When he puts everything under their control, he doesn’t leave anything out of control. But right now, we don’t see everything under their control yet.
HEB 2:9 9 However, we do see the one who was made lower in order than the angels for a little while—it’s Jesus! He’s the one who is now crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of his death. He suffered death so that he could taste death for everyone through God’s grace.
HEB 2:10 10 It was appropriate for God, for whom and through whom everything exists, to use experiences of suffering to make perfect the pioneer of salvation. This salvation belongs to many sons and daughters whom he’s leading to glory.
HEB 2:11 11 This is because the one who makes people holy and the people who are being made holy all come from one source. That is why Jesus isn’t ashamed to call them brothers and sisters when he says,
HEB 2:12 12 “ I will publicly announce your name to my brothers and sisters. ” “ I will praise you in the middle of the assembly. ”
HEB 2:13 13 He also says, “ I will rely on him. ” And also, “ Here I am with the children whom God has given to me. ”
HEB 2:14 14 Therefore, since the children share in flesh and blood, he also shared the same things in the same way. He did this to destroy the one who holds the power over death—the devil—by dying.
HEB 2:15 15 He set free those who were held in slavery their entire lives by their fear of death.
HEB 2:16 16 Of course, he isn’t trying to help angels, but rather he’s helping Abraham’s descendants.
HEB 2:17 17 Therefore, he had to be made like his brothers and sisters in every way. This was so that he could become a merciful and faithful high priest in things relating to God, in order to wipe away the sins of the people.
HEB 2:18 18 He’s able to help those who are being tempted, since he himself experienced suffering when he was tempted.
HEB 3:1 1 Therefore, brothers and sisters who are partners in the heavenly calling, think about Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession.
HEB 3:2 2 Jesus was faithful to the one who appointed him just like Moses was faithful in God’s house.
HEB 3:3 3 But he deserves greater glory than Moses in the same way that the builder of the house deserves more honor than the house itself.
HEB 3:4 4 Every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.
HEB 3:5 5 Moses was faithful in all God’s house as a servant in order to affirm the things that would be spoken later.
HEB 3:6 6 But Jesus was faithful over God’s house as a Son. We are his house if we hold on to the confidence and the pride that our hope gives us.
HEB 3:7 7 So, as the Holy Spirit says, “ Today, if you hear his voice, ”
HEB 3:8 8 “ don’t have stubborn hearts ” “ as they did in the rebellion, ” “ on the day when they tested me in the desert. ”
HEB 3:9 9 “ That is where your ancestors challenged and tested me, ” “ though they had seen my work for forty years. ”
HEB 3:10 10 “ So I was angry with them. ” “ I said, ” “ Their hearts always go off course, ” “ and they don’t know my ways. ”
HEB 3:11 11 “ Because of my anger I swore: ” “ They will never enter my rest! ”
HEB 3:12 12 Watch out, brothers and sisters, so that none of you have an evil, unfaithful heart that abandons the living God.
HEB 3:13 13 Instead, encourage each other every day, as long as it’s called “today,” so that none of you become insensitive to God because of sin’s deception.
HEB 3:14 14 We are partners with Christ, but only if we hold on to the confidence we had in the beginning until the end.
HEB 3:15 15 When it says, “ Today, if you hear his voice, don’t have stubborn hearts ” “ as they did in the rebellion. ”
HEB 3:16 16 Who was it who rebelled when they heard his voice? Wasn’t it all of those who were brought out of Egypt by Moses?
HEB 3:17 17 And with whom was God angry for forty years? Wasn’t it with the ones who sinned, whose bodies fell in the desert?
HEB 3:18 18 And against whom did he swear that they would never enter his rest, if not against the ones who were disobedient?
HEB 3:19 19 We see that they couldn’t enter because of their lack of faith.
HEB 4:1 1 Therefore, since the promise that we can enter into rest is still open, let’s be careful so that none of you will appear to miss it.
HEB 4:2 2 We also had the good news preached to us, just as the Israelites did. However, the message they heard didn’t help them because they weren’t united in faith with the ones who listened to it.
HEB 4:3 3 We who have faith are entering the rest. As God said, “ And because of my anger I swore: ” “ They will never enter into my rest! ” And yet God’s works were completed at the foundation of the world.
HEB 4:4 4 Then somewhere he said this about the seventh day of creation: “ God rested on the seventh day from all his works. ”
HEB 4:5 5 But again, in the passage above, God said, “ They will never enter my rest! ”
HEB 4:6 6 Therefore, it’s left open for some to enter it, and the ones who had the good news preached to them before didn’t enter because of disobedience.
HEB 4:7 7 Just as it says in the passage above, God designates a certain day as “today,” when he says through David much later, “ Today, if you hear his voice, ” “ don’t have stubborn hearts. ”
HEB 4:8 8 If Joshua gave the Israelites rest, God wouldn’t have spoken about another day later on.
HEB 4:9 9 So you see that a sabbath rest is left open for God’s people.
HEB 4:10 10 The one who entered God’s rest also rested from his works, just as God rested from his own.
HEB 4:11 11 Therefore, let’s make every effort to enter that rest so that no one will fall by following the same example of disobedience,
HEB 4:12 12 because God’s word is living, active, and sharper than any two-edged sword. It penetrates to the point that it separates the soul from the spirit and the joints from the marrow. It’s able to judge the heart’s thoughts and intentions.
HEB 4:13 13 No creature is hidden from it, but rather everything is naked and exposed to the eyes of the one to whom we have to give an answer.
HEB 4:14 14 Also, let’s hold on to the confession since we have a great high priest who passed through the heavens, who is Jesus, God’s Son;
HEB 4:15 15 because we don’t have a high priest who can’t sympathize with our weaknesses but instead one who was tempted in every way that we are, except without sin.
HEB 4:16 16 Finally, let’s draw near to the throne of favor with confidence so that we can receive mercy and find grace when we need help.
HEB 5:1 1 Every high priest is taken from the people and put in charge of things that relate to God for their sake, in order to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
HEB 5:2 2 The high priest is able to deal gently with the ignorant and those who are misled since he himself is prone to weakness.
HEB 5:3 3 Because of his weakness, he must offer sacrifices for his own sins as well as for the people.
HEB 5:4 4 No one takes this honor for themselves but takes it only when they are called by God, just like Aaron.
HEB 5:5 5 In the same way Christ also didn’t promote himself to become high priest. Instead, it was the one who said to him, “ You are my Son. ” “ Today I have become your Father ”,
HEB 5:6 6 as he also says in another place, “ You are a priest forever, ” “ according to the order of Melchizedek. ”
HEB 5:7 7 During his days on earth, Christ offered prayers and requests with loud cries and tears as his sacrifices to the one who was able to save him from death. He was heard because of his godly devotion.
HEB 5:8 8 Although he was a Son, he learned obedience from what he suffered.
HEB 5:9 9 After he had been made perfect, he became the source of eternal salvation for everyone who obeys him.
HEB 5:10 10 He was appointed by God to be a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
HEB 5:11 11 We have a lot to say about this topic, and it’s difficult to explain, because you have been lazy and you haven’t been listening.
HEB 5:12 12 Although you should have been teachers by now, you need someone to teach you an introduction to the basics about God’s message. You have come to the place where you need milk instead of solid food.
HEB 5:13 13 Everyone who lives on milk is not used to the word of righteousness, because they are babies.
HEB 5:14 14 But solid food is for the mature, whose senses are trained by practice to distinguish between good and evil.
HEB 6:1 1 So let’s press on to maturity, by moving on from the basics about Christ’s word. Let’s not lay a foundation of turning away from dead works, of faith in God,
HEB 6:2 2 of teaching about ritual ways to wash with water, laying on of hands, the resurrection from the dead, and eternal judgment—all over again.
HEB 6:3 3 We’re going to press on, if God allows it.
HEB 6:4 4 Because it’s impossible to restore people to changed hearts and lives who turn away once they have seen the light, tasted the heavenly gift, become partners with the Holy Spirit,
HEB 6:5 5 and tasted God’s good word and the powers of the coming age.
HEB 6:6 6 They are crucifying God’s Son all over again and exposing him to public shame.
HEB 6:7 7 The ground receives a blessing from God when it drinks up the rain that regularly comes and falls on it and yields a useful crop for those people for whom it is being farmed.
HEB 6:8 8 But if it produces thorns and thistles, it’s useless and close to being cursed. It ends up being burned.
HEB 6:9 9 But we are convinced of better things in your case, brothers and sisters, even though we are talking this way—things that go together with salvation.
HEB 6:10 10 God isn’t unjust so that he forgets your efforts and the love you have shown for his name’s sake when you served and continue to serve God’s holy people.
HEB 6:11 11 But we desperately want each of you to show the same effort to make your hope sure until the end.
HEB 6:12 12 This is so you won’t be lazy but follow the example of the ones who inherit the promises through faith and patience.
HEB 6:13 13 When God gave Abraham his promise, he swore by himself since he couldn’t swear by anyone greater.
HEB 6:14 14 He said, “ I will certainly bless you and multiply your descendants. ”
HEB 6:15 15 So Abraham obtained the promise by showing patience.
HEB 6:16 16 People pledge by something greater than themselves. A solemn pledge guarantees what they say and shuts down any argument.
HEB 6:17 17 When God wanted to further demonstrate to the heirs of the promise that his purpose doesn’t change, he guaranteed it with a solemn pledge.
HEB 6:18 18 So these are two things that don’t change, because it’s impossible for God to lie. He did this so that we, who have taken refuge in him, can be encouraged to grasp the hope that is lying in front of us.
HEB 6:19 19 This hope, which is a safe and secure anchor for our whole being, enters the sanctuary behind the curtain.
HEB 6:20 20 That’s where Jesus went in advance and entered for us, since he became a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
HEB 7:1 1 This Melchizedek, who was king of Salem and priest of the Most High God, met Abraham as he returned from the defeat of the kings, and Melchizedek blessed him.
HEB 7:2 2 Abraham gave a tenth of everything to him. His name means first “king of righteousness,” and then “king of Salem,” that is, “king of peace.”
HEB 7:3 3 He is without father or mother or any family. He has no beginning or end of life, but he’s like God’s Son and remains a priest for all time.
HEB 7:4 4 See how great Melchizedek was! Abraham, the father of the people, gave him a tenth of everything he captured.
HEB 7:5 5 The descendants of Levi who receive the office of priest have a commandment under the Law to collect a tenth of everything from the people who are their brothers and sisters, though they also are descended from Abraham.
HEB 7:6 6 But Melchizedek, who isn’t related to them, received a tenth of everything from Abraham and blessed the one who had received the promises.
HEB 7:7 7 Without question, the less important person is blessed by the more important person.
HEB 7:8 8 In addition, in one case a tenth is received by people who die, and in the other case, the tenth is received by someone who continues to live, according to the record.
HEB 7:9 9 It could be said that Levi, who received a tenth, paid a tenth through Abraham
HEB 7:10 10 because he was still in his ancestor’s body when Abraham paid the tenth to Melchizedek.
HEB 7:11 11 So if perfection came through the levitical office of priest (for the people received the Law under the priests), why was there still a need to speak about raising up another priest according to the order of Melchizedek rather than one according to the order of Aaron?
HEB 7:12 12 When the order of the priest changes, there has to be a change in the Law as well.
HEB 7:13 13 The person we are talking about belongs to another tribe, and no one ever served at the altar from that tribe.
HEB 7:14 14 It’s clear that our Lord came from the tribe of Judah, but Moses never said anything about priests from that tribe.
HEB 7:15 15 And it’s even clearer if another priest appears who is like Melchizedek.
HEB 7:16 16 He has become a priest by the power of a life that can’t be destroyed, rather than a legal requirement about physical descent.
HEB 7:17 17 This is confirmed: “ You are a priest forever, ” “ according to the order of Melchizedek. ”
HEB 7:18 18 On the one hand, an earlier command is set aside because it was weak and useless
HEB 7:19 19 (because the Law made nothing perfect). On the other hand, a better hope is introduced, through which we draw near to God.
HEB 7:20 20 And this was not done without a solemn pledge! The others have become priests without a solemn pledge,
HEB 7:21 21 but this priest was affirmed with a solemn pledge by the one who said, “ The Lord has made a solemn pledge ” “ and will not change his mind: ” “ You are a priest forever. ”
HEB 7:22 22 As a result, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.
HEB 7:23 23 The others who became priests are numerous because death prevented them from continuing to serve.
HEB 7:24 24 In contrast, he holds the office of priest permanently because he continues to serve forever.
HEB 7:25 25 This is why he can completely save those who are approaching God through him, because he always lives to speak with God for them.
HEB 7:26 26 It’s appropriate for us to have this kind of high priest: holy, innocent, incorrupt, separate from sinners, and raised high above the heavens.
HEB 7:27 27 He doesn’t need to offer sacrifices every day like the other high priests, first for their own sins and then for the sins of the people. He did this once for all when he offered himself.
HEB 7:28 28 The Law appoints people who are prone to weakness as high priests, but the content of the solemn pledge, which came after the Law, appointed a Son who has been made perfect forever.
HEB 8:1 1 Now the main point of what we are saying is this: We have this kind of high priest. He sat down at the right side of the throne of the majesty in the heavens.
HEB 8:2 2 He’s serving as a priest in the holy place, which is the true meeting tent that God, not any human being, set up.
HEB 8:3 3 Every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices. So it’s necessary for this high priest also to have something to offer.
HEB 8:4 4 If he was located on earth, he wouldn’t be a priest because there are already others who offer gifts based on the Law.
HEB 8:5 5 They serve in a place that is a copy and shadow of the heavenly meeting tent. This is indicated when Moses was warned by God when he was about to set up the meeting tent: “ See that you follow the pattern that I showed you on the mountain in every detail ”.
HEB 8:6 6 But now, Jesus has received a superior priestly service just as he arranged a better covenant that is enacted with better promises.
HEB 8:7 7 If the first covenant had been without fault, it wouldn’t have made sense to expect a second.
HEB 8:8 8 But God did find fault with them, since he says, “ Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, ” “ when I will make a covenant with the house of Israel, ” “ and I will make a new covenant with the house of Judah. ”
HEB 8:9 9 “ It will not be like the covenant that I made with their ancestors ” “ on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, ” “ because they did not continue to keep my covenant, ” “ and I lost interest in them, says the Lord. ”
HEB 8:10 10 “ This is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel ” “ after those days, says the Lord. ” “ I will place my laws in their minds, ” “ and write them on their hearts. ” “ I will be their God, ” “ and they will be my people. ”
HEB 8:11 11 “ And each person won’t ever teach a neighbor ” “ or their brother or sister, saying, ” “ Know the Lord, ” “ because they will all know me, ” “ from the least important of them to the most important; ”
HEB 8:12 12 “ because I will be lenient toward their unjust actions, ” “ and I won’t remember their sins anymore. ”
HEB 8:13 13 When it says new, it makes the first obsolete. And if something is old and outdated, it’s close to disappearing.
HEB 9:1 1 So then the first covenant had regulations for the priests’ service and the holy place on earth.
HEB 9:2 2 They pitched the first tent called the holy place. It contained the lampstand, the table, and the loaves of bread presented to God.
HEB 9:3 3 There was a tent behind the second curtain called the holy of holies.
HEB 9:4 4 It had the gold altar for incense and the chest containing the covenant, which was covered with gold on all sides. In the chest there was a gold jar containing manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.
HEB 9:5 5 Above the chest there were magnificent winged creatures casting their shadow over the seat of the chest, where sin is taken care of. Right now we can’t talk about these things in detail.
HEB 9:6 6 When these things have been prepared in this way, priests enter the first tent all the time as they perform their service.
HEB 9:7 7 But only the high priest enters the second tent once a year. He never does this without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins the people committed in ignorance.
HEB 9:8 8 With this, the Holy Spirit is showing that the way into the holy place hadn’t been revealed yet while the first tent was standing.
HEB 9:9 9 This is a symbol for the present time. It shows that the gifts and sacrifices that are being offered can’t perfect the conscience of the one who is serving.
HEB 9:10 10 These are superficial regulations that are only about food, drink, and various ritual ways to wash with water. They are regulations that have been imposed until the time of the new order.
HEB 9:11 11 But Christ has appeared as the high priest of the good things that have happened. He passed through the greater and more perfect meeting tent, which isn’t made by human hands (that is, it’s not a part of this world).
HEB 9:12 12 He entered the holy of holies once for all by his own blood, not by the blood of goats or calves, securing our deliverance for all time.
HEB 9:13 13 If the blood of goats and bulls and the sprinkled ashes of cows made spiritually contaminated people holy and clean,
HEB 9:14 14 how much more will the blood of Jesus wash our consciences clean from dead works in order to serve the living God? He offered himself to God through the eternal Spirit as a sacrifice without any flaw.
HEB 9:15 15 This is why he’s the mediator of a new covenant (which is a will): so that those who are called might receive the promise of the eternal inheritance on the basis of his death. His death occurred to set them free from the offenses committed under the first covenant.
HEB 9:16 16 When there is a will, you need to confirm the death of the one who made the will.
HEB 9:17 17 This is because a will takes effect only after a death, since it’s not in force while the one who made the will is alive.
HEB 9:18 18 So not even the first covenant was put into effect without blood.
HEB 9:19 19 Moses took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the Law scroll itself and all the people after he had proclaimed every command of the Law to all the people.
HEB 9:20 20 While he did it, he said, “ This is the blood of the covenant that God established for you. ”
HEB 9:21 21 And in the same way he sprinkled the meeting tent and also all the equipment that would be used in the priests’ service with blood.
HEB 9:22 22 Almost everything is cleansed by blood, according to the Law’s regulations, and there is no forgiveness without blood being shed.
HEB 9:23 23 So it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be cleansed with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things had to be cleansed with better sacrifices than these.
HEB 9:24 24 Christ didn’t enter the holy place (which is a copy of the true holy place) made by human hands, but into heaven itself, so that he now appears in God’s presence for us.
HEB 9:25 25 He didn’t enter to offer himself over and over again, like the high priest enters the earthly holy place every year with blood that isn’t his.
HEB 9:26 26 If that were so, then Jesus would have to suffer many times since the foundation of the world. Instead, he has now appeared once at the end of the ages to get rid of sin by sacrificing himself.
HEB 9:27 27 People are destined to die once and then face judgment.
HEB 9:28 28 In the same way, Christ was also offered once to take on himself the sins of many people. He will appear a second time, not to take away sin but to save those who are eagerly waiting for him.
HEB 10:1 1 The Law is a shadow of the good things that are coming, not the real things themselves. It never can perfect the ones who are trying to draw near to God through the same sacrifices that are offered continually every year.
HEB 10:2 2 Otherwise, wouldn’t they have stopped being offered? If the people carrying out their religious duties had been completely cleansed once, no one would have been aware of sin anymore.
HEB 10:3 3 Instead, these sacrifices are a reminder of sin every year,
HEB 10:4 4 because it’s impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
HEB 10:5 5 Therefore, when he comes into the world he says, “ You didn’t want a sacrifice or an offering, ” “ but you prepared a body for me; ”
HEB 10:6 6 “ you weren’t pleased with entirely burned offerings or a sin offering. ”
HEB 10:7 7 “ So then I said, ” “ Look, I’ve come to do your will, God. ” “ This has been written about me in the scroll. ”
HEB 10:8 8 He says above, “ You didn’t want ”and “ you weren’t pleased with a sacrifice or an offering ”or “ with entirely burned offerings or a purification offering, ” which are offered because the Law requires them.
HEB 10:9 9 Then he said, “ Look, I’ve come to do your will ”. He puts an end to the first to establish the second.
HEB 10:10 10 We have been made holy by God’s will through the offering of Jesus Christ’s body once for all.
HEB 10:11 11 Every priest stands every day serving and offering the same sacrifices over and over, sacrifices that can never take away sins.
HEB 10:12 12 But when this priest offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, he sat down at the right side of God.
HEB 10:13 13 Since then, he’s waiting until his enemies are made into a footstool for his feet,
HEB 10:14 14 because he perfected the people who are being made holy with one offering for all time.
HEB 10:15 15 The Holy Spirit affirms this when saying,
HEB 10:16 16 “ This is the covenant that I will make with them. ” “ After these days, says the Lord, ” “ I will place my laws in their hearts ” “ and write them on their minds. ”
HEB 10:17 17 “ And I won’t remember their sins ” “ and their lawless behavior anymore. ”
HEB 10:18 18 When there is forgiveness for these things, there is no longer an offering for sin.
HEB 10:19 19 Brothers and sisters, we have confidence that we can enter the holy of holies by means of Jesus’ blood,
HEB 10:20 20 through a new and living way that he opened up for us through the curtain, which is his body,
HEB 10:21 21 and we have a great high priest over God’s house.
HEB 10:22 22 Therefore, let’s draw near with a genuine heart with the certainty that our faith gives us, since our hearts are sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies are washed with pure water.
HEB 10:23 23 Let’s hold on to the confession of our hope without wavering, because the one who made the promises is reliable.
HEB 10:24 24 And let us consider each other carefully for the purpose of sparking love and good deeds.
HEB 10:25 25 Don’t stop meeting together with other believers, which some people have gotten into the habit of doing. Instead, encourage each other, especially as you see the day drawing near.
HEB 10:26 26 If we make the decision to sin after we receive the knowledge of the truth, there isn’t a sacrifice for sins left any longer.
HEB 10:27 27 There’s only a scary expectation of judgment and of a burning fire that’s going to devour God’s opponents.
HEB 10:28 28 When someone rejected the Law from Moses, they were put to death without mercy on the basis of the testimony of two or three witnesses.
HEB 10:29 29 How much worse punishment do you think is deserved by the person who walks all over God’s Son, who acts as if the blood of the covenant that made us holy is just ordinary blood, and who insults the Spirit of grace?
HEB 10:30 30 We know the one who said, “ Judgment is mine; I will pay people back. ” And he also said, “ The Lord will judge his people. ”
HEB 10:31 31 It’s scary to fall into the hands of the living God!
HEB 10:32 32 But remember the earlier days, after you saw the light. You stood your ground while you were suffering from an enormous amount of pressure.
HEB 10:33 33 Sometimes you were exposed to insults and abuse in public. Other times you became partners with those who were treated that way.
HEB 10:34 34 You even showed sympathy toward people in prison and accepted the confiscation of your possessions with joy, since you knew that you had better and lasting possessions.
HEB 10:35 35 So don’t throw away your confidence—it brings a great reward.
HEB 10:36 36 You need to endure so that you can receive the promises after you do God’s will.
HEB 10:37 37 “ In a little while longer, ” “ the one who is coming will come and won’t delay; ”
HEB 10:38 38 “ but my righteous one will live by faith, ” “ and my whole being won’t be pleased with anyone who shrinks back. ”
HEB 10:39 39 But we aren’t the sort of people who timidly draw back and end up being destroyed. We’re the sort of people who have faith so that our whole beings are preserved.
HEB 11:1 1 Faith is the reality of what we hope for, the proof of what we don’t see.
HEB 11:2 2 The elders in the past were approved because they showed faith.
HEB 11:3 3 By faith we understand that the universe has been created by a word from God so that the visible came into existence from the invisible.
HEB 11:4 4 By faith Abel offered a better sacrifice to God than Cain, which showed that he was righteous, since God gave approval to him for his gift. Though he died, he’s still speaking through faith.
HEB 11:5 5 By faith Enoch was taken up so that he didn’t see death, and “ he wasn’t found because God took him up. ” He was given approval for having pleased God before he was taken up.
HEB 11:6 6 It’s impossible to please God without faith because the one who draws near to God must believe that he exists and that he rewards people who try to find him.
HEB 11:7 7 By faith Noah responded with godly fear when he was warned about events he hadn’t seen yet. He built an ark to deliver his household. With his faith, he criticized the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes from faith.
HEB 11:8 8 By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place that he was going to receive as an inheritance. He went out without knowing where he was going.
HEB 11:9 9 By faith he lived in the land he had been promised as a stranger. He lived in tents along with Isaac and Jacob, who were coheirs of the same promise.
HEB 11:10 10 He was looking forward to a city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God.
HEB 11:11 11 By faith even Sarah received the ability to have a child, though she herself was barren and past the age for having children, because she believed that the one who promised was faithful.
HEB 11:12 12 So descendants were born from one man (and he was as good as dead). They were as many as the number of the stars in the sky and as countless as the grains of sand on the seashore.
HEB 11:13 13 All these people died in faith without receiving the promises, but they saw the promises from a distance and welcomed them. They confessed that they were strangers and immigrants on earth.
HEB 11:14 14 People who say this kind of thing make it clear that they are looking for a homeland.
HEB 11:15 15 If they had been thinking about the country that they had left, they would have had the opportunity to return to it.
HEB 11:16 16 But at this point in time, they are longing for a better country, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore, God isn’t ashamed to be called their God—he has prepared a city for them.
HEB 11:17 17 By faith Abraham offered Isaac when he was tested. The one who received the promises was offering his only son.
HEB 11:18 18 He had been told concerning him, “ Your legitimate descendants will come from Isaac. ”
HEB 11:19 19 He figured that God could even raise him from the dead. So in a way he did receive him back from the dead.
HEB 11:20 20 By faith Isaac also blessed Jacob and Esau concerning their future.
HEB 11:21 21 By faith Jacob blessed each of Joseph’s sons as he was dying and “ bowed in worship over the head of his staff. ”
HEB 11:22 22 By faith Joseph recalled the exodus of the Israelites at the end of his life, and gave instructions about burying his bones.
HEB 11:23 23 By faith Moses was hidden by his parents for three months when he was born, because they saw that the child was beautiful and they weren’t afraid of the king’s orders.
HEB 11:24 24 By faith Moses refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter when he was grown up.
HEB 11:25 25 He chose to be mistreated with God’s people instead of having the temporary pleasures of sin.
HEB 11:26 26 He thought that the abuses he suffered for Christ were more valuable than the treasures of Egypt, since he was looking forward to the reward.
HEB 11:27 27 By faith he left Egypt without being afraid of the king’s anger. He kept on going as if he could see what is invisible.
HEB 11:28 28 By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, in order that the destroyer could not touch their firstborn children.
HEB 11:29 29 By faith they crossed the Red Sea as if they were on dry land, but when the Egyptians tried it, they were drowned.
HEB 11:30 30 By faith Jericho’s walls fell after the people marched around them for seven days.
HEB 11:31 31 By faith Rahab the prostitute wasn’t killed with the disobedient because she welcomed the spies in peace.
HEB 11:32 32 What more can I say? I would run out of time if I told you about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets.
HEB 11:33 33 Through faith they conquered kingdoms, brought about justice, realized promises, shut the mouths of lions,
HEB 11:34 34 put out raging fires, escaped from the edge of the sword, found strength in weakness, were mighty in war, and routed foreign armies.
HEB 11:35 35 Women received back their dead by resurrection. Others were tortured and refused to be released so they could gain a better resurrection.
HEB 11:36 36 But others experienced public shame by being taunted and whipped; they were even put in chains and in prison.
HEB 11:37 37 They were stoned to death, they were cut in two, and they died by being murdered with swords. They went around wearing the skins of sheep and goats, needy, oppressed, and mistreated.
HEB 11:38 38 The world didn’t deserve them. They wandered around in deserts, mountains, caves, and holes in the ground.
HEB 11:39 39 All these people didn’t receive what was promised, though they were given approval for their faith.
HEB 11:40 40 God provided something better for us so they wouldn’t be made perfect without us.
HEB 12:1 1 So then, with endurance, let’s also run the race that is laid out in front of us, since we have such a great cloud of witnesses surrounding us. Let’s throw off any extra baggage, get rid of the sin that trips us up,
HEB 12:2 2 and fix our eyes on Jesus, faith’s pioneer and perfecter. He endured the cross, ignoring the shame, for the sake of the joy that was laid out in front of him, and sat down at the right side of God’s throne.
HEB 12:3 3 Think about the one who endured such opposition from sinners so that you won’t be discouraged and you won’t give up.
HEB 12:4 4 In your struggle against sin, you haven’t resisted yet to the point of shedding blood,
HEB 12:5 5 and you have forgotten the encouragement that addresses you as sons and daughters: “ My child, don’t make light of the Lord’s discipline ” “ or give up when you are corrected by him, ”
HEB 12:6 6 “ because the Lord disciplines whomever he loves, ” “ and he punishes every son or daughter whom he accepts. ”
HEB 12:7 7 Bear hardship for the sake of discipline. God is treating you like sons and daughters! What child isn’t disciplined by his or her father?
HEB 12:8 8 But if you don’t experience discipline, which happens to all children, then you are illegitimate and not real sons and daughters.
HEB 12:9 9 What’s more, we had human parents who disciplined us, and we respected them for it. How much more should we submit to the Father of spirits and live?
HEB 12:10 10 Our human parents disciplined us for a little while, as it seemed best to them, but God does it for our benefit so that we can share his holiness.
HEB 12:11 11 No discipline is fun while it lasts, but it seems painful at the time. Later, however, it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness for those who have been trained by it.
HEB 12:12 12 So strengthen your drooping hands and weak knees!
HEB 12:13 13 Make straight paths for your feet so that if any part is lame, it will be healed rather than injured more seriously.
HEB 12:14 14 Pursue the goal of peace along with everyone—and holiness as well, because no one will see the Lord without it.
HEB 12:15 15 Make sure that no one misses out on God’s grace. Make sure that no root of bitterness grows up that might cause trouble and pollute many people.
HEB 12:16 16 Make sure that no one becomes sexually immoral or ungodly like Esau. He sold his inheritance as the oldest son for one meal.
HEB 12:17 17 You know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected because he couldn’t find a way to change his heart and life, though he looked for it with tears.
HEB 12:18 18 You haven’t drawn near to something that can be touched: a burning fire, darkness, shadow, a whirlwind,
HEB 12:19 19 a blast of a trumpet, and a sound of words that made the ones who heard it beg that there wouldn’t be one more word.
HEB 12:20 20 They couldn’t stand the command, “ If even a wild animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned. ”
HEB 12:21 21 The sight was so frightening that Moses said, “I’m terrified and shaking!”
HEB 12:22 22 But you have drawn near to Mount Zion, the city of the living God, heavenly Jerusalem, to countless angels in a festival gathering,
HEB 12:23 23 to the assembly of God’s firstborn children who are registered in heaven, to God the judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous who have been made perfect,
HEB 12:24 24 to Jesus the mediator of the new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks better than Abel’s blood.
HEB 12:25 25 See to it that you don’t resist the one who is speaking. If the people didn’t escape when they refused to listen to the one who warned them on earth, how will we escape if we reject the one who is warning from heaven?
HEB 12:26 26 His voice shook the earth then, but now he has made a promise: “ Still once more I will shake not only the earth but heaven also ”.
HEB 12:27 27 The words “still once more” reveal the removal of what is shaken—the things that are part of this creation—so that what isn’t shaken will remain.
HEB 12:28 28 Therefore, since we are receiving a kingdom that can’t be shaken, let’s continue to express our gratitude. With this gratitude, let’s serve in a way that is pleasing to God with respect and awe,
HEB 12:29 29 because our God really is a consuming fire.
HEB 13:1 1 Keep loving each other like family.
HEB 13:2 2 Don’t neglect to open up your homes to guests, because by doing this some have been hosts to angels without knowing it.
HEB 13:3 3 Remember prisoners as if you were in prison with them, and people who are mistreated as if you were in their place.
HEB 13:4 4 Marriage must be honored in every respect, with no cheating on the relationship, because God will judge the sexually immoral person and the person who commits adultery.
HEB 13:5 5 Your way of life should be free from the love of money, and you should be content with what you have. After all, he has said, “ I will never leave you or abandon you ”.
HEB 13:6 6 This is why we can confidently say, “ The Lord is my helper, ” “ and I won’t be afraid. ” “ What can people do to me? ”
HEB 13:7 7 Remember your leaders who spoke God’s word to you. Imitate their faith as you consider the way their lives turned out.
HEB 13:8 8 Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever!
HEB 13:9 9 Don’t be misled by the many strange teachings out there. It’s a good thing for the heart to be strengthened by grace rather than by food. Food doesn’t help those who live in this context.
HEB 13:10 10 We have an altar, and those who serve as priests in the meeting tent don’t have the right to eat from it.
HEB 13:11 11 The blood of the animals is carried into the holy of holies by the high priest as an offering for sin, and their bodies are burned outside the camp.
HEB 13:12 12 And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy with his own blood.
HEB 13:13 13 So now, let’s go to him outside the camp, bearing his shame.
HEB 13:14 14 We don’t have a permanent city here, but rather we are looking for the city that is still to come.
HEB 13:15 15 So let’s continually offer up a sacrifice of praise through him, which is the fruit from our lips that confess his name.
HEB 13:16 16 Don’t forget to do good and to share what you have because God is pleased with these kinds of sacrifices.
HEB 13:17 17 Rely on your leaders and defer to them, because they watch over your whole being as people who are going to be held responsible for you. They need to be able to do this with pleasure and not with complaints about you, because that wouldn’t help you.
HEB 13:18 18 Pray for us. We’re sure that we have a good conscience, and we want to do the right thing in every way.
HEB 13:19 19 I’m particularly asking you to do this so that I can be returned to you quickly.
HEB 13:20 20 May the God of peace, who brought back the great shepherd of the sheep, our Lord Jesus, from the dead by the blood of the eternal covenant,
HEB 13:21 21 equip you with every good thing to do his will, by developing in us what pleases him through Jesus Christ. To him be the glory forever and always. Amen.
HEB 13:22 22 I urge you, brothers and sisters, to put up with this message of encouragement, since I’ve only written a short letter to you!
HEB 13:23 23 You should know that our brother Timothy has been set free. If he comes soon, we will travel together to see you.
HEB 13:24 24 Greet your leaders and all of God’s holy people. The group from Italy greets you.
HEB 13:25 25 May grace be with all of you.
JAS 1:1 1 From James, a slave of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ. To the twelve tribes who are scattered outside the land of Israel. Greetings!
JAS 1:2 2 My brothers and sisters, think of the various tests you encounter as occasions for joy.
JAS 1:3 3 After all, you know that the testing of your faith produces endurance.
JAS 1:4 4 Let this endurance complete its work so that you may be fully mature, complete, and lacking in nothing.
JAS 1:5 5 But anyone who needs wisdom should ask God, whose very nature is to give to everyone without a second thought, without keeping score. Wisdom will certainly be given to those who ask.
JAS 1:6 6 Whoever asks shouldn’t hesitate. They should ask in faith, without doubting. Whoever doubts is like the surf of the sea, tossed and turned by the wind.
JAS 1:7 7 People like that should never imagine that they will receive anything from the Lord.
JAS 1:8 8 They are double-minded, unstable in all their ways.
JAS 1:9 9 Brothers and sisters who are poor should find satisfaction in their high status.
JAS 1:10 10 Those who are wealthy should find satisfaction in their low status, because they will die off like wildflowers.
JAS 1:11 11 The sun rises with its scorching heat and dries up the grass so that its flowers fall and its beauty is lost. Just like that, in the midst of their daily lives, the wealthy will waste away.
JAS 1:12 12 Those who stand firm during testing are blessed. They are tried and true. They will receive the life God has promised to those who love him as their reward.
JAS 1:13 13 No one who is tested should say, “God is tempting me!” This is because God is not tempted by any form of evil, nor does he tempt anyone.
JAS 1:14 14 Everyone is tempted by their own cravings; they are lured away and enticed by them.
JAS 1:15 15 Once those cravings conceive, they give birth to sin; and when sin grows up, it gives birth to death.
JAS 1:16 16 Don’t be misled, my dear brothers and sisters.
JAS 1:17 17 Every good gift, every perfect gift, comes from above. These gifts come down from the Father, the creator of the heavenly lights, in whose character there is no change at all.
JAS 1:18 18 He chose to give us birth by his true word, and here is the result: we are like the first crop from the harvest of everything he created.
JAS 1:19 19 Know this, my dear brothers and sisters: everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to grow angry.
JAS 1:20 20 This is because an angry person doesn’t produce God’s righteousness.
JAS 1:21 21 Therefore, with humility, set aside all moral filth and the growth of wickedness, and welcome the word planted deep inside you—the very word that is able to save you.
JAS 1:22 22 You must be doers of the word and not only hearers who mislead themselves.
JAS 1:23 23 Those who hear but don’t do the word are like those who look at their faces in a mirror.
JAS 1:24 24 They look at themselves, walk away, and immediately forget what they were like.
JAS 1:25 25 But there are those who study the perfect law, the law of freedom, and continue to do it. They don’t listen and then forget, but they put it into practice in their lives. They will be blessed in whatever they do.
JAS 1:26 26 If those who claim devotion to God don’t control what they say, they mislead themselves. Their devotion is worthless.
JAS 1:27 27 True devotion, the kind that is pure and faultless before God the Father, is this: to care for orphans and widows in their difficulties and to keep the world from contaminating us.
JAS 2:1 1 My brothers and sisters, when you show favoritism you deny the faithfulness of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has been resurrected in glory.
JAS 2:2 2 Imagine two people coming into your meeting. One has a gold ring and fine clothes, while the other is poor, dressed in filthy rags.
JAS 2:3 3 Then suppose that you were to take special notice of the one wearing fine clothes, saying, “Here’s an excellent place. Sit here.” But to the poor person you say, “Stand over there”; or, “Here, sit at my feet.”
JAS 2:4 4 Wouldn’t you have shown favoritism among yourselves and become evil-minded judges?
JAS 2:5 5 My dear brothers and sisters, listen! Hasn’t God chosen those who are poor by worldly standards to be rich in terms of faith? Hasn’t God chosen the poor as heirs of the kingdom he has promised to those who love him?
JAS 2:6 6 But you have dishonored the poor. Don’t the wealthy make life difficult for you? Aren’t they the ones who drag you into court?
JAS 2:7 7 Aren’t they the ones who insult the good name spoken over you at your baptism?
JAS 2:8 8 You do well when you really fulfill the royal law found in scripture, “ Love your neighbor as yourself. ”
JAS 2:9 9 But when you show favoritism, you are committing a sin, and by that same law you are exposed as a lawbreaker.
JAS 2:10 10 Anyone who tries to keep all of the Law but fails at one point is guilty of failing to keep all of it.
JAS 2:11 11 The one who said, “ Don’t commit adultery ”, also said, “ Don’t commit murder ”. So if you don’t commit adultery but do commit murder, you are a lawbreaker.
JAS 2:12 12 In every way, then, speak and act as people who will be judged by the law of freedom.
JAS 2:13 13 There will be no mercy in judgment for anyone who hasn’t shown mercy. Mercy overrules judgment.
JAS 2:14 14 My brothers and sisters, what good is it if people say they have faith but do nothing to show it? Claiming to have faith can’t save anyone, can it?
JAS 2:15 15 Imagine a brother or sister who is naked and never has enough food to eat.
JAS 2:16 16 What if one of you said, “Go in peace! Stay warm! Have a nice meal!”? What good is it if you don’t actually give them what their body needs?
JAS 2:17 17 In the same way, faith is dead when it doesn’t result in faithful activity.
JAS 2:18 18 Someone might claim, “You have faith and I have action.” But how can I see your faith apart from your actions? Instead, I’ll show you my faith by putting it into practice in faithful action.
JAS 2:19 19 It’s good that you believe that God is one. Ha! Even the demons believe this, and they tremble with fear.
JAS 2:20 20 Are you so slow? Do you need to be shown that faith without actions has no value at all?
JAS 2:21 21 What about Abraham, our father? Wasn’t he shown to be righteous through his actions when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
JAS 2:22 22 See, his faith was at work along with his actions. In fact, his faith was made complete by his faithful actions.
JAS 2:23 23 So the scripture was fulfilled that says, “ Abraham believed God, and God regarded him as righteous ”. What is more, Abraham was called God’s friend.
JAS 2:24 24 So you see that a person is shown to be righteous through faithful actions and not through faith alone.
JAS 2:25 25 In the same way, wasn’t Rahab the prostitute shown to be righteous when she received the messengers as her guests and then sent them on by another road?
JAS 2:26 26 As the lifeless body is dead, so faith without actions is dead.
JAS 3:1 1 My brothers and sisters, not many of you should become teachers, because we know that we teachers will be judged more strictly.
JAS 3:2 2 We all make mistakes often, but those who don’t make mistakes with their words have reached full maturity. Like a bridled horse, they can control themselves entirely.
JAS 3:3 3 When we bridle horses and put bits in their mouths to lead them wherever we want, we can control their whole bodies.
JAS 3:4 4 Consider ships: They are so large that strong winds are needed to drive them. But pilots direct their ships wherever they want with a little rudder.
JAS 3:5 5 In the same way, even though the tongue is a small part of the body, it boasts wildly. Think about this: A small flame can set a whole forest on fire.
JAS 3:6 6 The tongue is a small flame of fire, a world of evil at work in us. It contaminates our entire lives. Because of it, the circle of life is set on fire. The tongue itself is set on fire by the flames of hell.
JAS 3:7 7 People can tame and already have tamed every kind of animal, bird, reptile, and fish.
