JAS 3:8 8 No one can tame the tongue, though. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.
JAS 3:9 9 With it we both bless the Lord and Father and curse human beings made in God’s likeness.
JAS 3:10 10 Blessing and cursing come from the same mouth. My brothers and sisters, it just shouldn’t be this way!
JAS 3:11 11 Both fresh water and salt water don’t come from the same spring, do they?
JAS 3:12 12 My brothers and sisters, can a fig tree produce olives? Can a grapevine produce figs? Of course not, and fresh water doesn’t flow from a saltwater spring either.
JAS 3:13 13 Are any of you wise and understanding? Show that your actions are good with a humble lifestyle that comes from wisdom.
JAS 3:14 14 However, if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, then stop bragging and living in ways that deny the truth.
JAS 3:15 15 This is not the wisdom that comes down from above. Instead, it is from the earth, natural and demonic.
JAS 3:16 16 Wherever there is jealousy and selfish ambition, there is disorder and everything that is evil.
JAS 3:17 17 What of the wisdom from above? First, it is pure, and then peaceful, gentle, obedient, filled with mercy and good actions, fair, and genuine.
JAS 3:18 18 Those who make peace sow the seeds of justice by their peaceful acts.
JAS 4:1 1 What is the source of conflict among you? What is the source of your disputes? Don’t they come from your cravings that are at war in your own lives?
JAS 4:2 2 You long for something you don’t have, so you commit murder. You are jealous for something you can’t get, so you struggle and fight. You don’t have because you don’t ask.
JAS 4:3 3 You ask and don’t have because you ask with evil intentions, to waste it on your own cravings.
JAS 4:4 4 You unfaithful people! Don’t you know that friendship with the world means hostility toward God? So whoever wants to be the world's friend becomes God's enemy.
JAS 4:5 5 Or do you suppose that scripture is meaningless? Doesn’t God long for our faithfulness in the life he has given to us?
JAS 4:6 6 But he gives us more grace. This is why it says, “ God stands against the proud, but favors the humble ”.
JAS 4:7 7 Therefore, submit to God. Resist the devil, and he will run away from you.
JAS 4:8 8 Come near to God, and he will come near to you. Wash your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
JAS 4:9 9 Cry out in sorrow, mourn, and weep! Let your laughter become mourning and your joy become sadness.
JAS 4:10 10 Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up.
JAS 4:11 11 Brothers and sisters, don’t say evil things about each other. Whoever insults or criticizes a brother or sister insults and criticizes the Law. If you find fault with the Law, you are not a doer of the Law but a judge over it.
JAS 4:12 12 There is only one lawgiver and judge, and he is able to save and to destroy. But you who judge your neighbor, who are you?
JAS 4:13 13 Pay attention, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to such-and-such a town. We will stay there a year, buying and selling, and making a profit.”
JAS 4:14 14 You don’t really know about tomorrow. What is your life? You are a mist that appears for only a short while before it vanishes.
JAS 4:15 15 Here’s what you ought to say: “If the Lord wills, we will live and do this or that.”
JAS 4:16 16 But now you boast and brag, and all such boasting is evil.
JAS 4:17 17 It is a sin when someone knows the right thing to do and doesn’t do it.
JAS 5:1 1 Pay attention, you wealthy people! Weep and moan over the miseries coming upon you.
JAS 5:2 2 Your riches have rotted. Moths have destroyed your clothes.
JAS 5:3 3 Your gold and silver have rusted, and their rust will be evidence against you. It will eat your flesh like fire. Consider the treasure you have hoarded in the last days.
JAS 5:4 4 Listen! Hear the cries of the wages of your field hands. These are the wages you stole from those who harvested your fields. The cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of heavenly forces.
JAS 5:5 5 You have lived a self-satisfying life on this earth, a life of luxury. You have stuffed your hearts in preparation for the day of slaughter.
JAS 5:6 6 You have condemned and murdered the righteous one, who doesn’t oppose you.
JAS 5:7 7 Therefore, brothers and sisters, you must be patient as you wait for the coming of the Lord. Consider the farmer who waits patiently for the coming of rain in the fall and spring, looking forward to the precious fruit of the earth.
JAS 5:8 8 You also must wait patiently, strengthening your resolve, because the coming of the Lord is near.
JAS 5:9 9 Don’t complain about each other, brothers and sisters, so that you won’t be judged. Look! The judge is standing at the door!
JAS 5:10 10 Brothers and sisters, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord as an example of patient resolve and steadfastness.
JAS 5:11 11 Look at how we honor those who have practiced endurance. You have heard of the endurance of Job. And you have seen what the Lord has accomplished, for the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.
JAS 5:12 12 Most important, my brothers and sisters, never make a solemn pledge—neither by heaven nor earth, nor by anything else. Instead, speak with a simple “Yes” or “No,” or else you may fall under judgment.
JAS 5:13 13 If any of you are suffering, they should pray. If any of you are happy, they should sing.
JAS 5:14 14 If any of you are sick, they should call for the elders of the church, and the elders should pray over them, anointing them with oil in the name of the Lord.
JAS 5:15 15 Prayer that comes from faith will heal the sick, for the Lord will restore them to health. And if they have sinned, they will be forgiven.
JAS 5:16 16 For this reason, confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of the righteous person is powerful in what it can achieve.
JAS 5:17 17 Elijah was a person just like us. When he earnestly prayed that it wouldn’t rain, no rain fell for three and a half years.
JAS 5:18 18 He prayed again, God sent rain, and the earth produced its fruit.
JAS 5:19 19 My brothers and sisters, if any of you wander from the truth and someone turns back the wanderer,
JAS 5:20 20 recognize that whoever brings a sinner back from the wrong path will save them from death and will bring about the forgiveness of many sins.
1PE 1:1 1 Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, To God’s chosen strangers in the world of the diaspora, who live in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.
1PE 1:2 2 God the Father chose you because of what he knew beforehand. He chose you through the Holy Spirit’s work of making you holy and because of the faithful obedience and sacrifice of Jesus Christ. May God’s grace and peace be multiplied to you.
1PE 1:3 3 May the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ be blessed! On account of his vast mercy, he has given us new birth. You have been born anew into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
1PE 1:4 4 You have a pure and enduring inheritance that cannot perish—an inheritance that is presently kept safe in heaven for you.
1PE 1:5 5 Through his faithfulness, you are guarded by God’s power so that you can receive the salvation he is ready to reveal in the last time.
1PE 1:6 6 You now rejoice in this hope, even if it’s necessary for you to be distressed for a short time by various trials.
1PE 1:7 7 This is necessary so that your faith may be found genuine. (Your faith is more valuable than gold, which will be destroyed even though it is itself tested by fire.) Your genuine faith will result in praise, glory, and honor for you when Jesus Christ is revealed.
1PE 1:8 8 Although you’ve never seen him, you love him. Even though you don’t see him now, you trust him and so rejoice with a glorious joy that is too much for words.
1PE 1:9 9 You are receiving the goal of your faith: your salvation.
1PE 1:10 10 The prophets, who long ago foretold the grace that you’ve received, searched and explored, inquiring carefully about this salvation.
1PE 1:11 11 They wondered what the Spirit of Christ within them was saying when he bore witness beforehand about the suffering that would happen to Christ and the glory that would follow. They wondered what sort of person or what sort of time they were speaking about.
1PE 1:12 12 It was revealed to them that in their search they were not serving themselves but you. These things, which even angels long to examine, have now been proclaimed to you by those who brought you the good news. They did this in the power of the Holy Spirit, who was sent from heaven.
1PE 1:13 13 Therefore, once you have your minds ready for action and you are thinking clearly, place your hope completely on the grace that will be brought to you when Jesus Christ is revealed.
1PE 1:14 14 Don’t be conformed to your former desires, those that shaped you when you were ignorant. But, as obedient children,
1PE 1:15 15 you must be holy in every aspect of your lives, just as the one who called you is holy.
1PE 1:16 16 It is written, “ You will be holy, because I am holy. ”
1PE 1:17 17 Since you call upon a Father who judges all people according to their actions without favoritism, you should conduct yourselves with reverence during the time of your dwelling in a strange land.
1PE 1:18 18 Live in this way, knowing that you were not liberated by perishable things like silver or gold from the empty lifestyle you inherited from your ancestors.
1PE 1:19 19 Instead, you were liberated by the precious blood of Christ, like that of a flawless, spotless lamb.
1PE 1:20 20 Christ was chosen before the creation of the world, but was only revealed at the end of time. This was done for you,
1PE 1:21 21 who through Christ are faithful to the God who raised him from the dead and gave him glory. So now, your faith and hope should rest in God.
1PE 1:22 22 As you set yourselves apart by your obedience to the truth so that you might have genuine affection for your fellow believers, love each other deeply and earnestly.
1PE 1:23 23 Do this because you have been given new birth—not from the type of seed that decays but from seed that doesn’t. This seed is God’s life-giving and enduring word.
1PE 1:24 24 Thus, “ All human life on the earth is like grass, ” “ and all human glory is like a flower in a field. ” “ The grass dries up and its flower falls off, ”
1PE 1:25 25 “ but the Lord’s word endures forever. ” This is the word that was proclaimed to you as good news.
1PE 2:1 1 Therefore, get rid of all ill will and all deceit, pretense, envy, and slander.
1PE 2:2 2 Instead, like a newborn baby, desire the pure milk of the word. Nourished by it, you will grow into salvation,
1PE 2:3 3 since you have tasted that the Lord is good.
1PE 2:4 4 Now you are coming to him as to a living stone. Even though this stone was rejected by humans, from God’s perspective it is chosen, valuable.
1PE 2:5 5 You yourselves are being built like living stones into a spiritual temple. You are being made into a holy priesthood to offer up spiritual sacrifices that are acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
1PE 2:6 6 Thus it is written in scripture, “ Look! I am laying a cornerstone in Zion, chosen, valuable. The person who believes in him will never be shamed. ”
1PE 2:7 7 So God honors you who believe. For those who refuse to believe, though, the stone the builders tossed aside has become the capstone.
1PE 2:8 8 This is a stone that makes people stumble and a rock that makes them fall. Because they refuse to believe in the word, they stumble. Indeed, this is the end to which they were appointed.
1PE 2:9 9 But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people who are God’s own possession. You have become this people so that you may speak of the wonderful acts of the one who called you out of darkness into his amazing light.
1PE 2:10 10 Once you weren’t a people, but now you are God’s people. Once you hadn’t received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
1PE 2:11 11 Dear friends, since you are immigrants and strangers in the world, I urge that you avoid worldly desires that wage war against your lives.
1PE 2:12 12 Live honorably among the unbelievers. Today, they defame you, as if you were doing evil. But in the day when God visits to judge they will glorify him, because they have observed your honorable deeds.
1PE 2:13 13 For the sake of the Lord submit to every human institution. Do this whether it means submitting to the emperor as supreme ruler,
1PE 2:14 14 or to governors as those sent by the emperor. They are sent to punish those doing evil and to praise those doing good.
1PE 2:15 15 Submit to them because it’s God’s will that by doing good you will silence the ignorant talk of foolish people.
1PE 2:16 16 Do this as God’s slaves, and yet also as free people, not using your freedom as a cover-up for evil.
1PE 2:17 17 Honor everyone. Love the family of believers. Have respectful fear of God. Honor the emperor.
1PE 2:18 18 Household slaves, submit by accepting the authority of your masters with all respect. Do this not only to good and kind masters but also to those who are harsh.
1PE 2:19 19 Now, it is commendable if, because of one’s understanding of God, someone should endure pain through suffering unjustly.
1PE 2:20 20 But what praise comes from enduring patiently when you have sinned and are beaten for it? But if you endure steadfastly when you’ve done good and suffer for it, this is commendable before God.
1PE 2:21 21 You were called to this kind of endurance, because Christ suffered on your behalf. He left you an example so that you might follow in his footsteps.
1PE 2:22 22 He committed no sin, nor did he ever speak in ways meant to deceive.
1PE 2:23 23 When he was insulted, he did not reply with insults. When he suffered, he did not threaten revenge. Instead, he entrusted himself to the one who judges justly.
1PE 2:24 24 He carried in his own body on the cross the sins we committed. He did this so that we might live in righteousness, having nothing to do with sin. By his wounds you were healed.
1PE 2:25 25 Though you were like straying sheep, you have now returned to the shepherd and guardian of your lives.
1PE 3:1 1 Wives, likewise, submit to your own husbands. Do this so that even if some of them refuse to believe the word, they may be won without a word by their wives’ way of life.
1PE 3:2 2 After all, they will have observed the reverent and holy manner of your lives.
1PE 3:3 3 Don’t try to make yourselves beautiful on the outside, with stylish hair or by wearing gold jewelry or fine clothes.
1PE 3:4 4 Instead, make yourselves beautiful on the inside, in your hearts, with the enduring quality of a gentle, peaceful spirit. This type of beauty is very precious in God’s eyes.
1PE 3:5 5 For it was in this way that holy women who trusted in God used to make themselves beautiful, accepting the authority of their own husbands.
1PE 3:6 6 For example, Sarah accepted Abraham’s authority when she called him “ master ”. You have become her children when you do good and don’t respond to threats with fear.
1PE 3:7 7 Husbands, likewise, submit by living with your wife in ways that honor her, knowing that she is the weaker partner. Honor her all the more, as she is also a coheir of the gracious care of life. Do this so that your prayers won’t be hindered.
1PE 3:8 8 Finally, all of you be of one mind, sympathetic, lovers of your fellow believers, compassionate, and modest in your opinion of yourselves.
1PE 3:9 9 Don’t pay back evil for evil or insult for insult. Instead, give blessing in return. You were called to do this so that you might inherit a blessing.
1PE 3:10 10 For “ those who want to love life ” “ and see good days ” “ should keep their tongue from evil speaking ” “ and their lips from speaking lies. ”
1PE 3:11 11 “ They should shun evil and do good; ” “ seek peace and chase after it. ”
1PE 3:12 12 “ The Lord’s eyes are on the righteous ” “ and his ears are open to their prayers. ” “ But the Lord cannot tolerate those who do evil. ”
1PE 3:13 13 Who will harm you if you are zealous for good?
1PE 3:14 14 But happy are you, even if you suffer because of righteousness! Don’t be terrified or upset by them.
1PE 3:15 15 Instead, regard Christ the Lord as holy in your hearts. Whenever anyone asks you to speak of your hope, be ready to defend it.
1PE 3:16 16 Yet do this with respectful humility, maintaining a good conscience. Act in this way so that those who malign your good lifestyle in Christ may be ashamed when they slander you.
1PE 3:17 17 It is better to suffer for doing good (if this could possibly be God’s will) than for doing evil.
1PE 3:18 18 Christ himself suffered on account of sins, once for all, the righteous one on behalf of the unrighteous. He did this in order to bring you into the presence of God. Christ was put to death as a human, but made alive by the Spirit.
1PE 3:19 19 And it was by the Spirit that he went to preach to the spirits in prison.
1PE 3:20 20 In the past, these spirits were disobedient—when God patiently waited during the time of Noah. Noah built an ark in which a few (that is, eight) lives were rescued through water.
1PE 3:21 21 Baptism is like that. It saves you now—not because it removes dirt from your body but because it is the mark of a good conscience toward God. Your salvation comes through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
1PE 3:22 22 who is at God’s right side. Now that he has gone into heaven, he rules over all angels, authorities, and powers.
1PE 4:1 1 Therefore, since Christ suffered as a human, you should also arm yourselves with his way of thinking. This is because whoever suffers is finished with sin.
1PE 4:2 2 As a result, they don’t live the rest of their human lives in ways determined by human desires but in ways determined by God’s will.
1PE 4:3 3 You have wasted enough time doing what unbelievers desire—living in their unrestrained immorality and lust, their drunkenness and excessive feasting and wild parties, and their forbidden worship of idols.
1PE 4:4 4 They think it’s strange that you don’t join in these activities with the same flood of unrestrained wickedness. So they slander you.
1PE 4:5 5 They will have to reckon with the one who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
1PE 4:6 6 Indeed, this is the reason the good news was also preached to the dead. This happened so that, although they were judged as humans according to human standards, they could live by the Spirit according to divine standards.
1PE 4:7 7 The end of everything has come. Therefore, be self-controlled and clearheaded so you can pray.
1PE 4:8 8 Above all, show sincere love to each other, because love brings about the forgiveness of many sins.
1PE 4:9 9 Open your homes to each other without complaining.
1PE 4:10 10 And serve each other according to the gift each person has received, as good managers of God’s diverse gifts.
1PE 4:11 11 Whoever speaks should do so as those who speak God’s word. Whoever serves should do so from the strength that God furnishes. Do this so that in everything God may be honored through Jesus Christ. To him be honor and power forever and always. Amen.
1PE 4:12 12 Dear friends, don’t be surprised about the fiery trials that have come among you to test you. These are not strange happenings.
1PE 4:13 13 Instead, rejoice as you share Christ’s suffering. You share his suffering now so that you may also have overwhelming joy when his glory is revealed.
1PE 4:14 14 If you are mocked because of Christ’s name, you are blessed, for the Spirit of glory—indeed, the Spirit of God—rests on you.
1PE 4:15 15 Now none of you should suffer as a murderer or thief or evildoer or rebel.
1PE 4:16 16 But don’t be ashamed if you suffer as one who belongs to Christ. Rather, honor God as you bear Christ’s name. Give honor to God,
1PE 4:17 17 because it’s time for judgment to begin with God’s own household. But if judgment starts with us, what will happen to those who refuse to believe God’s good news?
1PE 4:18 18 If the righteous are barely rescued, what will happen to the godless and sinful?
1PE 4:19 19 So then, those who suffer because they follow God’s will should commit their lives to a trustworthy creator by doing what is right.
1PE 5:1 1 Therefore, I have a request for the elders among you. (I ask this as a fellow elder and a witness of Christ’s sufferings, and as one who shares in the glory that is about to be revealed.) I urge the elders:
1PE 5:2 2 Like shepherds, tend the flock of God among you. Watch over it. Don’t shepherd because you must, but do it voluntarily for God. Don’t shepherd greedily, but do it eagerly.
1PE 5:3 3 Don’t shepherd by ruling over those entrusted to your care, but become examples to the flock.
1PE 5:4 4 And when the chief shepherd appears, you will receive an unfading crown of glory.
1PE 5:5 5 In the same way, I urge you who are younger: accept the authority of the elders. And everyone, clothe yourselves with humility toward each other. God stands against the proud, but he gives favor to the humble.
1PE 5:6 6 Therefore, humble yourselves under God’s power so that he may raise you up in the last day.
1PE 5:7 7 Throw all your anxiety onto him, because he cares about you.
1PE 5:8 8 Be clearheaded. Keep alert. Your accuser, the devil, is on the prowl like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour.
1PE 5:9 9 Resist him, standing firm in the faith. Do so in the knowledge that your fellow believers are enduring the same suffering throughout the world.
1PE 5:10 10 After you have suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, the one who called you into his eternal glory in Christ Jesus, will himself restore, empower, strengthen, and establish you.
1PE 5:11 11 To him be power forever and always. Amen.
1PE 5:12 12 I have written and sent these few lines to you by Silvanus. I consider him to be a faithful brother. In these lines I have urged and affirmed that this is the genuine grace of God. Stand firm in it.
1PE 5:13 13 The fellow-elect church in Babylon greets you, and so does my son Mark.
1PE 5:14 14 Greet each other with the kiss of love. Peace to you all who are in Christ.
2PE 1:1 1 From Simon Peter, a slave and apostle of Jesus Christ. To those who received a faith equal to ours through the justice of our God and savior Jesus Christ.
2PE 1:2 2 May you have more and more grace and peace through the knowledge of God and Jesus our Lord.
2PE 1:3 3 By his divine power the Lord has given us everything we need for life and godliness through the knowledge of the one who called us by his own honor and glory.
2PE 1:4 4 Through his honor and glory he has given us his precious and wonderful promises, that you may share the divine nature and escape from the world’s immorality that sinful craving produces.
2PE 1:5 5 This is why you must make every effort to add moral excellence to your faith; and to moral excellence, knowledge;
2PE 1:6 6 and to knowledge, self-control; and to self-control, endurance; and to endurance, godliness;
2PE 1:7 7 and to godliness, affection for others; and to affection for others, love.
2PE 1:8 8 If all these are yours and they are growing in you, they’ll keep you from becoming inactive and unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
2PE 1:9 9 Whoever lacks these things is shortsighted and blind, forgetting that they were cleansed from their past sins.
2PE 1:10 10 Therefore, brothers and sisters, be eager to confirm your call and election. Do this and you will never ever be lost.
2PE 1:11 11 In this way you will receive a rich welcome into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and savior Jesus Christ.
2PE 1:12 12 So I’ll keep reminding you about these things, although you already know them and stand secure in the truth you have.
2PE 1:13 13 I think it’s right that I keep stirring up your memory, as long as I’m alive.
2PE 1:14 14 After all, our Lord Jesus Christ has shown me that I am about to depart from this life.
2PE 1:15 15 I’m eager for you always to remember these things after my death.
2PE 1:16 16 We didn’t repeat crafty myths when we told you about the powerful coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. Quite the contrary, we witnessed his majesty with our own eyes.
2PE 1:17 17 He received honor and glory from God the Father when a voice came to him from the magnificent glory, saying, “This is my dearly loved Son, with whom I am well-pleased.”
2PE 1:18 18 We ourselves heard this voice from heaven while we were with him on the holy mountain.
2PE 1:19 19 In addition, we have a most reliable prophetic word, and you would do well to pay attention to it, just as you would to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
2PE 1:20 20 Most important, you must know that no prophecy of scripture represents the prophet’s own understanding of things,
2PE 1:21 21 because no prophecy ever came by human will. Instead, men and women led by the Holy Spirit spoke from God.
2PE 2:1 1 But false prophets also arose among the people. In the same way, false teachers will come among you. They will introduce destructive opinions and deny the master who bought them, bringing quick destruction on themselves.
2PE 2:2 2 Many will follow them in their unrestrained immorality, and because of these false teachers the way of truth will be slandered.
2PE 2:3 3 In their greed they will take advantage of you with lies. The judgment pronounced against them long ago hasn’t fallen idle, nor is their destruction sleeping.
2PE 2:4 4 God didn’t spare the angels when they sinned but cast them into the lowest level of the underworld and committed them to chains of darkness, keeping them there until the judgment.
2PE 2:5 5 And he didn’t spare the ancient world when he brought a flood on the world of ungodly people, even though he protected Noah, a preacher of righteousness, along with seven others.
2PE 2:6 6 God condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to total destruction, reducing them to ashes as a warning to ungodly people.
2PE 2:7 7 And he rescued righteous Lot, who was made miserable by the unrestrained immorality of unruly people. (
2PE 2:8 8 While that righteous man lived among them he felt deep distress every day on account of the immoral actions he saw and heard.)
2PE 2:9 9 These things show that the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from their trials, and how to keep the unrighteous for punishment on the Judgment Day.
2PE 2:10 10 This is especially true for those who follow after the corrupt cravings of the sinful nature and defy the Lord’s authority. These reckless, brash people aren’t afraid to insult the glorious ones,
2PE 2:11 11 yet angels, who are stronger and more powerful, don’t use insults when pronouncing the Lord’s judgment on them.
2PE 2:12 12 These false teachers are like irrational animals, mere creatures of instinct, born to be captured and destroyed. They slander what they don’t understand and, like animals, they will be destroyed.
2PE 2:13 13 In this way, they will receive payment for their wrongdoing. They even enjoy unruly parties in broad daylight. They are blots and blemishes, taking delight in their seductive pleasures while feasting with you.
2PE 2:14 14 They are always looking for someone with whom to commit adultery. They are always on the lookout for opportunities to sin. They ensnare people whose faith is weak. They have hearts trained in greed. They are under God’s curse.
2PE 2:15 15 Leaving the straight path, they have gone off course, following the way of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the payment of doing wrong.
2PE 2:16 16 But Balaam was rebuked for his wrongdoing. A donkey, which has no voice, spoke with a human voice and put a stop to the prophet’s madness.
2PE 2:17 17 These false teachers are springs without water, mists driven by the wind. The underworld has been reserved for them.
2PE 2:18 18 With empty, self-important speech, they use sinful cravings and unrestrained immorality to ensnare people who have only just escaped life with those who have wandered from the truth.
2PE 2:19 19 These false teachers promise freedom, but they themselves are slaves of immorality; whatever overpowers you, enslaves you.
2PE 2:20 20 If people escape the moral filth of this world through the knowledge of our Lord and savior Jesus Christ, then get tangled up in it again and are overcome by it, they are worse off than they were before.
2PE 2:21 21 It would be better for them never to have known the way of righteousness than, having come to know it, to turn back from the holy commandment entrusted to them.
2PE 2:22 22 They demonstrate the truth of the proverb: “A dog returns to its own vomit, and a washed sow wallows in the mud.”
2PE 3:1 1 My dear friends, this is now my second letter to you. I have written both letters to stir up your sincere understanding with a reminder.
2PE 3:2 2 I want you to recall what the holy prophets foretold as well as what the Lord and savior commanded through your apostles.
2PE 3:3 3 Most important, know this: in the last days scoffers will come, jeering, living by their own cravings,
2PE 3:4 4 and saying, “Where is the promise of his coming? After all, nothing has changed—not since the beginning of creation, nor even since the ancestors died.”
2PE 3:5 5 But they fail to notice that, by God’s word, heaven and earth were formed long ago out of water and by means of water.
2PE 3:6 6 And it was through these that the world of that time was flooded and destroyed.
2PE 3:7 7 But by the same word, heaven and earth are now held in reserve for fire, kept for the Judgment Day and destruction of ungodly people.
2PE 3:8 8 Don’t let it escape your notice, dear friends, that with the Lord a single day is like a thousand years and a thousand years are like a single day.
2PE 3:9 9 The Lord isn’t slow to keep his promise, as some think of slowness, but he is patient toward you, not wanting anyone to perish but all to change their hearts and lives.
2PE 3:10 10 But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a dreadful noise, the elements will be consumed by fire, and the earth and all the works done on it will be exposed.
2PE 3:11 11 Since everything will be destroyed in this way, what sort of people ought you to be? You must live holy and godly lives,
2PE 3:12 12 waiting for and hastening the coming day of God. Because of that day, the heavens will be destroyed by fire and the elements will melt away in the flames.
2PE 3:13 13 But according to his promise we are waiting for a new heaven and a new earth, where righteousness is at home.
2PE 3:14 14 Therefore, dear friends, while you are waiting for these things to happen, make every effort to be found by him in peace—pure and faultless.
2PE 3:15 15 Consider the patience of our Lord to be salvation, just as our dear friend and brother Paul wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him,
2PE 3:16 16 speaking of these things in all his letters. Some of his remarks are hard to understand, and people who are ignorant and whose faith is weak twist them to their own destruction, just as they do the other scriptures.
2PE 3:17 17 Therefore, dear friends, since you have been warned in advance, be on guard so that you aren’t led off course into the error of sinful people, and lose your own safe position.
2PE 3:18 18 Instead, grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and savior Jesus Christ. To him belongs glory now and forever. Amen.
1JN 1:1 1 We announce to you what existed from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have seen and our hands handled, about the word of life.
1JN 1:2 2 The life was revealed, and we have seen, and we testify and announce to you the eternal life that was with the Father and was revealed to us.
1JN 1:3 3 What we have seen and heard, we also announce it to you so that you can have fellowship with us. Our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son, Jesus Christ.
1JN 1:4 4 We are writing these things so that our joy can be complete.
1JN 1:5 5 This is the message that we have heard from him and announce to you: “God is light and there is no darkness in him at all.”
1JN 1:6 6 If we claim, “We have fellowship with him,” and live in the darkness, we are lying and do not act truthfully.
1JN 1:7 7 But if we live in the light in the same way as he is in the light, we have fellowship with each other, and the blood of Jesus, his Son, cleanses us from every sin.
1JN 1:8 8 If we claim, “We don’t have any sin,” we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.
1JN 1:9 9 But if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and cleanse us from everything we’ve done wrong.
1JN 1:10 10 If we claim, “We have never sinned,” we make him a liar and his word is not in us.
1JN 2:1 1 My little children, I’m writing these things to you so that you don’t sin. But if you do sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous one.
1JN 2:2 2 He is God’s way of dealing with our sins, not only ours but the sins of the whole world.
1JN 2:3 3 This is how we know that we know him: if we keep his commandments.
1JN 2:4 4 The one who claims, “I know him,” while not keeping his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in this person.
1JN 2:5 5 But the love of God is truly perfected in whoever keeps his word. This is how we know we are in him.
1JN 2:6 6 The one who claims to remain in him ought to live in the same way as he lived.
1JN 2:7 7 Dear friends, I’m not writing a new commandment to you, but an old commandment that you had from the beginning. The old commandment is the message you heard.
1JN 2:8 8 On the other hand, I am writing a new commandment to you, which is true in him and in you, because the darkness is passing away and the true light already shines.
1JN 2:9 9 The one who claims to be in the light while hating a brother or sister is in the darkness even now.
1JN 2:10 10 The person loving a brother and sister stays in the light, and there is nothing in the light that causes a person to stumble.
1JN 2:11 11 But the person who hates a brother or sister is in the darkness and lives in the darkness, and doesn’t know where to go because the darkness blinds the eyes.
1JN 2:12 12 Little children, I’m writing to you because your sins have been forgiven through Jesus’ name.
1JN 2:13 13 Parents, I’m writing to you because you have known the one who has existed from the beginning. Young people, I’m writing to you because you have conquered the evil one.
1JN 2:14 14 Little children, I write to you because you know the Father. Parents, I write to you because you have known the one who has existed from the beginning. Young people, I write to you because you are strong, the word of God remains in you, and you have conquered the evil one.
1JN 2:15 15 Don’t love the world or the things in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in them.
1JN 2:16 16 Everything that is in the world—the craving for whatever the body feels, the craving for whatever the eyes see and the arrogant pride in one’s possessions—is not of the Father but is of the world.
1JN 2:17 17 And the world and its cravings are passing away, but the person who does the will of God remains forever.
1JN 2:18 18 Little children, it is the last hour. Just as you have heard that the antichrist is coming, so now many antichrists have appeared. This is how we know it is the last hour.
1JN 2:19 19 They went out from us, but they were not really part of us. If they had been part of us, they would have stayed with us. But by going out from us, they showed they all are not part of us.
1JN 2:20 20 But you have an anointing from the holy one, and all of you know the truth.
1JN 2:21 21 I don’t write to you because you don’t know the truth but because you know it. You know that no lie comes from the truth.
1JN 2:22 22 Who is the liar? Isn’t it the person who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This person is the antichrist: the one who denies the Father and the Son.
1JN 2:23 23 Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father, but the one who confesses the Son has the Father also.
1JN 2:24 24 As for you, what you heard from the beginning must remain in you. If what you heard from the beginning remains in you, you will also remain in relationship to the Son and in the Father.
1JN 2:25 25 This is the promise that he himself gave us: eternal life.
1JN 2:26 26 I write these things to you about those who are attempting to deceive you.
1JN 2:27 27 As for you, the anointing that you received from him remains on you, and you don’t need anyone to teach you the truth. But since his anointing teaches you about all things (it’s true and not a lie), remain in relationship to him just as he taught you.
1JN 2:28 28 And now, little children, remain in relationship to Jesus, so that when he appears we can have confidence and not be ashamed in front of him when he comes.
1JN 2:29 29 If you know that he is righteous, you also know that every person who practices righteousness is born from him.
1JN 3:1 1 See what kind of love the Father has given to us in that we should be called God’s children, and that is what we are! Because the world didn’t recognize him, it doesn’t recognize us.
1JN 3:2 2 Dear friends, now we are God’s children, and it hasn’t yet appeared what we will be. We know that when he appears we will be like him because we’ll see him as he is.
1JN 3:3 3 And all who have this hope in him purify themselves even as he is pure.
1JN 3:4 4 Every person who practices sin commits an act of rebellion, and sin is rebellion.
1JN 3:5 5 You know that he appeared to take away sins, and there is no sin in him.
1JN 3:6 6 Every person who remains in relationship to him does not sin. Any person who sins has not seen him or known him.
1JN 3:7 7 Little children, make sure no one deceives you. The person who practices righteousness is righteous, in the same way that Jesus is righteous.
1JN 3:8 8 The person who practices sin belongs to the devil, because the devil has been sinning since the beginning. God’s Son appeared for this purpose: to destroy the works of the devil.
1JN 3:9 9 Those born from God don’t practice sin because God’s DNA remains in them. They can’t sin because they are born from God.
1JN 3:10 10 This is how God’s children and the devil’s children are apparent: everyone who doesn’t practice righteousness is not from God, including the person who doesn’t love a brother or sister.
1JN 3:11 11 This is the message that you heard from the beginning: love each other.
1JN 3:12 12 Don’t behave like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did he kill him? He killed him because his own works were evil, but the works of his brother were righteous.
1JN 3:13 13 Don’t be surprised, brothers and sisters, if the world hates you.
1JN 3:14 14 We know that we have transferred from death to life, because we love the brothers and sisters. The person who does not love remains in death.
1JN 3:15 15 Everyone who hates a brother or sister is a murderer, and you know that murderers don’t have eternal life residing in them.
1JN 3:16 16 This is how we know love: Jesus laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers and sisters.
1JN 3:17 17 But if someone has material possessions and sees a brother or sister in need but refuses to help—how can the love of God dwell in a person like that?
1JN 3:18 18 Little children, let’s not love with words or speech but with action and truth.
1JN 3:19 19 This is how we will know that we belong to the truth and reassure our hearts in God’s presence.
1JN 3:20 20 Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts and knows all things.
1JN 3:21 21 Dear friends, if our hearts don’t condemn us, we have confidence in relationship to God.
1JN 3:22 22 We receive whatever we ask from him because we keep his commandments and do what pleases him.
1JN 3:23 23 This is his commandment, that we believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love each other as he commanded us.
1JN 3:24 24 Those who keep his commandments dwell in God and God dwells in them. This is how we know that he dwells in us, because of the Spirit he has given us.

1JN 4:3 3 and every spirit that doesn’t confess Jesus is not from God. This is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming and is now already in the world.
1JN 4:4 4 You are from God, little children, and you have defeated these people because the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.
1JN 4:5 5 They are from the world. So they speak from the world’s point of view and the world listens to them.
1JN 4:6 6 We are from God. The person who knows God listens to us. Whoever is not from God doesn’t listen to us. This is how we recognize the Spirit of truth and the spirit of error.

1JN 4:8 8 The person who doesn’t love does not know God, because God is love.
1JN 4:9 9 This is how the love of God is revealed to us: God has sent his only Son into the world so that we can live through him.
1JN 4:10 10 This is love: it is not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son as the sacrifice that deals with our sins.
1JN 4:11 11 Dear friends, if God loved us this way, we also ought to love each other.

1JN 4:13 13 This is how we know we remain in him and he remains in us, because he has given us a measure of his Spirit.
1JN 4:14 14 We have seen and testify that the Father has sent the Son to be the savior of the world.
1JN 4:15 15 If any of us confess that Jesus is God’s Son, God remains in us and we remain in God.
1JN 4:16 16 We have known and have believed the love that God has for us. God is love, and those who remain in love remain in God and God remains in them.
1JN 4:17 17 This is how love has been perfected in us, so that we can have confidence on the Judgment Day, because we are exactly the same as God is in this world.
1JN 4:18 18 There is no fear in love, but perfect love drives out fear, because fear expects punishment. The person who is afraid has not been made perfect in love.
1JN 4:19 19 We love because God first loved us.
1JN 4:20 20 Those who say, “I love God” and hate their brothers or sisters are liars. After all, those who don’t love their brothers or sisters whom they have seen can hardly love God whom they have not seen!

JUD 1:1 1 Jude, a slave of Jesus Christ and brother of James. To those who are called, loved by God the Father and kept safe by Jesus Christ.
JUD 1:2 2 May you have more and more mercy, peace, and love.
JUD 1:3 3 Dear friends, I wanted very much to write to you concerning the salvation we share. Instead, I must write to urge you to fight for the faith delivered once and for all to God’s holy people.
JUD 1:4 4 Godless people have slipped in among you. They turn the grace of our God into unrestrained immorality and deny our only master and Lord, Jesus Christ. Judgment was passed against them a long time ago.
JUD 1:5 5 I want to remind you of something you already know very well. The Lord, who once saved a people out of Egypt, later destroyed those who didn’t maintain their faith.
JUD 1:6 6 I remind you too of the angels who didn’t keep their position of authority but deserted their own home. The Lord has kept them in eternal chains in the underworld until the judgment of the great day.
JUD 1:7 7 In the same way, Sodom and Gomorrah and neighboring towns practiced immoral sexual relations and pursued other sexual urges. By undergoing the punishment of eternal fire, they serve as a warning.
JUD 1:8 8 Yet, even knowing this, these dreamers in the same way pollute themselves, reject authority, and slander the angels.
JUD 1:9 9 The archangel Michael, when he argued with the devil about Moses’ body, did not dare charge him with slander. Instead, he said, “The Lord rebuke you!”
JUD 1:10 10 But these people slander whatever they don’t understand. They are destroyed by what they know instinctively, as though they were irrational animals.
JUD 1:11 11 They are damned, for they follow in the footsteps of Cain. For profit they give themselves over to Balaam’s error. They are destroyed in the uprising of Korah.
JUD 1:12 12 These people are like jagged rocks just below the surface of the water waiting to snag you when they join your love feasts. They feast with you without reverence. They care only for themselves. They are waterless clouds carried along by the winds; fruitless autumn trees, twice dead, uprooted;
JUD 1:13 13 wild waves of the sea foaming up their own shame; wandering stars for whom the darkness of the underworld is reserved forever.
JUD 1:14 14 Enoch, who lived seven generations after Adam, prophesied about these people when he said, “See, the Lord comes with his countless holy ones,
JUD 1:15 15 to execute judgment on everyone and to convict everyone about every ungodly deed they have committed in their ungodliness as well as all the harsh things that sinful ungodly people have said against him.”
JUD 1:16 16 These are faultfinding grumblers, living according to their own desires. They speak arrogant words and they show partiality to people when they want a favor in return.
JUD 1:17 17 But you, dear friends, remember the words spoken beforehand by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.
JUD 1:18 18 They said to you, “In the end time scoffers will come living according to their own ungodly desires.”
JUD 1:19 19 These people create divisions. Since they don’t have the Spirit, they are worldly.
JUD 1:20 20 But you, dear friends: build each other up on the foundation of your most holy faith, pray in the Holy Spirit,
JUD 1:21 21 keep each other in the love of God, wait for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, who will give you eternal life.
JUD 1:22 22 Have mercy on those who doubt.
JUD 1:23 23 Save some by snatching them from the fire. Fearing God, have mercy on some, hating even the clothing contaminated by their sinful urges.
JUD 1:24 24 To the one who is able to protect you from falling, and to present you blameless and rejoicing before his glorious presence,
JUD 1:25 25 to the only God our savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, belong glory, majesty, power, and authority, before all time, now and forever. Amen.

REV 1:6 6 who made us a kingdom, priests to his God and Father—to him be glory and power forever and always. Amen.

REV 1:8 8 “I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, “the one who is and was and is coming, the Almighty.”

REV 1:10 10 I was in a Spirit-inspired trance on the Lord’s day, and I heard behind me a loud voice that sounded like a trumpet.
REV 1:11 11 It said, “Write down on a scroll whatever you see, and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.”
REV 1:12 12 I turned to see who was speaking to me, and when I turned, I saw seven oil lamps burning on top of seven gold stands.
REV 1:13 13 In the middle of the lampstands I saw someone who looked like the Human One. He wore a robe that stretched down to his feet, and he had a gold sash around his chest.
REV 1:14 14 His head and hair were white as white wool—like snow—and his eyes were like a fiery flame.
REV 1:15 15 His feet were like fine brass that has been purified in a furnace, and his voice sounded like rushing water.
REV 1:16 16 He held seven stars in his right hand, and from his mouth came a sharp, two-edged sword. His appearance was like the sun shining with all its power.
REV 1:17 17 When I saw him, I fell at his feet like a dead man. But he put his right hand on me and said, “Don’t be afraid. I’m the first and the last,
REV 1:18 18 and the living one. I was dead, but look! Now I’m alive forever and always. I have the keys of Death and the Grave.
REV 1:19 19 So write down what you have seen, both the scene now before you and the things that are about to unfold after this.
REV 1:20 20 As for the mystery of the seven stars that you saw in my right hand and the seven gold lampstands, here is what they mean: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.

REV 2:2 2 I know your works, your labor, and your endurance. I also know that you don’t put up with those who are evil. You have tested those who say they are apostles but are not, and you have found them to be liars.
REV 2:3 3 You have shown endurance and put up with a lot for my name’s sake, and you haven’t gotten tired.
REV 2:4 4 But I have this against you: you have let go of the love you had at first.
REV 2:5 5 So remember the high point from which you have fallen. Change your hearts and lives and do the things you did at first. If you don’t, I’m coming to you. I will move your lampstand from its place if you don’t change your hearts and lives.
REV 2:6 6 But you have this in your favor: you hate what the Nicolaitans are doing, which I also hate.
REV 2:7 7 If you can hear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches. I will allow those who emerge victorious to eat from the tree of life, which is in God’s paradise.

REV 2:11 11 If you can hear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches. Those who emerge victorious won’t be hurt by the second death.

REV 2:15 15 In the same way, you have some who follow the Nicolaitans’ teaching.
REV 2:16 16 So change your hearts and lives. If you don’t, I am coming to you soon, and I will make war on them with the sword that comes from my mouth.

REV 2:19 19 I know your works, your love and faithfulness, your service and endurance. I also know that the works you have done most recently are even greater than those you did at first.
REV 2:20 20 But I have this against you: you put up with that woman, Jezebel, who calls herself a prophet. You allow her to teach and to mislead my servants into committing sexual immorality and eating food sacrificed to idols.

REV 2:23 23 and I will even put her children to death with disease. Then all the churches will know that I’m the one who examines minds and hearts, and that I will give to each of you what your actions deserve.
REV 2:24 24 As for the rest of you in Thyatira—those of you who don’t follow this teaching and haven’t learned the so-called “deep secrets” of Satan—I won’t burden you with anything else.
REV 2:25 25 Just hold on to what you have until I come.
REV 2:26 26 To those who emerge victorious, keeping my practices until the end, I will give authority over the nations—
REV 2:27 27 to rule the nations with an iron rod and smash them like pottery—
REV 2:28 28 just as I received authority from my Father. I will also give them the morning star.
REV 2:29 29 If you can hear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.

REV 3:3 3 So remember what you received and heard. Hold on to it and change your hearts and lives. If you don’t wake up, I will come like a thief, and you won’t know what time I will come upon you.
REV 3:4 4 But you do have a few people in Sardis who haven’t stained their clothing. They will walk with me clothed in white because they are worthy.
REV 3:5 5 Those who emerge victorious will wear white clothing like this. I won’t scratch out their names from the scroll of life, but will declare their names in the presence of my Father and his angels.
REV 3:6 6 If you can hear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.
REV 3:7 7 “Write this to the angel of the church in Philadelphia: These are the words of the one who is holy and true, who has the key of David. Whatever he opens, no one will shut; and whatever he shuts, no one opens.
REV 3:8 8 I know your works. Look! I have set in front of you an open door that no one can shut. You have so little power, and yet you have kept my word and haven’t denied my name.
REV 3:9 9 Because of this I will make the people from Satan’s synagogue (who say they are Jews and really aren’t, but are lying)—I will make them come and bow down at your feet and realize that I have loved you.
REV 3:10 10 Because you kept my command to endure, I will keep you safe through the time of testing that is about to come over the whole world, to test those who live on earth.
REV 3:11 11 I’m coming soon. Hold on to what you have so that no one takes your crown.
REV 3:12 12 As for those who emerge victorious, I will make them pillars in the temple of my God, and they will never leave it. I will write on them the name of my God and the name of the city of my God, the New Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from my God. I will also write on them my own new name.
REV 3:13 13 If you can hear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.
REV 3:14 14 “Write this to the angel of the church in Laodicea: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the ruler of God’s creation.
REV 3:15 15 I know your works. You are neither cold nor hot. I wish that you were either cold or hot.
REV 3:16 16 So because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I’m about to spit you out of my mouth.
REV 3:17 17 After all, you say, ‘I’m rich, and I’ve grown wealthy, and I don’t need a thing.’ You don’t realize that you are miserable, pathetic, poor, blind, and naked.
REV 3:18 18 My advice is that you buy gold from me that has been purified by fire so that you may be rich, and white clothing to wear so that your nakedness won’t be shamefully exposed, and ointment to put on your eyes so that you may see.
REV 3:19 19 I correct and discipline those whom I love. So be earnest and change your hearts and lives.
REV 3:20 20 Look! I’m standing at the door and knocking. If any hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to be with them, and will have dinner with them, and they will have dinner with me.
REV 3:21 21 As for those who emerge victorious, I will allow them to sit with me on my throne, just as I emerged victorious and sat down with my Father on his throne.
REV 3:22 22 If you can hear, listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.”
REV 4:1 1 After this I looked and there was a door that had been opened in heaven. The first voice that I had heard, which sounded like a trumpet, said to me, “Come up here, and I will show you what must take place after this.”
REV 4:2 2 At once I was in a Spirit-inspired trance and I saw a throne in heaven, and someone was seated on the throne.
REV 4:3 3 The one seated there looked like jasper and carnelian, and surrounding the throne was a rainbow that looked like an emerald.
REV 4:4 4 Twenty-four thrones, with twenty-four elders seated upon them, surrounded the throne. The elders were dressed in white clothing and had gold crowns on their heads.
REV 4:5 5 From the throne came lightning, voices, and thunder. In front of the throne were seven flaming torches, which are the seven spirits of God.
REV 4:6 6 Something like a glass sea, like crystal, was in front of the throne. In the center, by the throne, were four living creatures encircling the throne. These creatures were covered with eyes on the front and on the back.
REV 4:7 7 The first living creature was like a lion. The second living creature was like an ox. The third living creature had a face like a human being. And the fourth living creature was like an eagle in flight.
REV 4:8 8 Each of the four living creatures had six wings, and each was covered all around and on the inside with eyes. They never rest day or night, but keep on saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is coming.”
REV 4:9 9 Whenever the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to the one seated on the throne, who lives forever and always,
REV 4:10 10 the twenty-four elders fall before the one seated on the throne. They worship the one who lives forever and always. They throw down their crowns before the throne and say,
REV 4:11 11 “You are worthy, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, because you created all things. It is by your will that they existed and were created.”
REV 5:1 1 Then I saw a scroll in the right hand of the one seated on the throne. It had writing on the front and the back, and it was sealed with seven seals.
REV 5:2 2 I saw a powerful angel, who proclaimed in a loud voice, “Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?”
REV 5:3 3 But no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth could open the scroll or look inside it.
REV 5:4 4 So I began to weep and weep, because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or to look inside it.
REV 5:5 5 Then one of the elders said to me, “Don’t weep. Look! The Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has emerged victorious so that he can open the scroll and its seven seals.”
REV 5:6 6 Then, in between the throne and the four living creatures and among the elders, I saw a Lamb, standing as if it had been slain. It had seven horns and seven eyes, which are God’s seven spirits, sent out into the whole earth.
REV 5:7 7 He came forward and took the scroll from the right hand of the one seated on the throne.
REV 5:8 8 When he took the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb. Each held a harp and gold bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
REV 5:9 9 They took up a new song, saying, “You are worthy to take the scroll and open its seals, because you were slain, and by your blood you purchased for God persons from every tribe, language, people, and nation.
REV 5:10 10 You made them a kingdom and priests to our God, and they will rule on earth.”
REV 5:11 11 Then I looked, and I heard the sound of many angels surrounding the throne, the living creatures, and the elders. They numbered in the millions—thousands upon thousands.
REV 5:12 12 They said in a loud voice, “Worthy is the slaughtered Lamb to receive power, wealth, wisdom, and might, and honor, glory, and blessing.”
REV 5:13 13 And I heard every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and in the sea—I heard everything everywhere say, “Blessing, honor, glory, and power belong to the one seated on the throne and to the Lamb forever and always.”
REV 5:14 14 Then the four living creatures said, “Amen,” and the elders fell down and worshipped.
REV 6:1 1 Then I looked on as the Lamb opened one of the seven seals. I heard one of the four living creatures say in a voice like thunder, “Come!”
REV 6:2 2 So I looked, and there was a white horse. Its rider held a bow and was given a crown. And he went forth from victory to victory.
REV 6:3 3 When the Lamb opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say, “Come!”
REV 6:4 4 Out came another horse, fiery red. Its rider was allowed to take peace from the earth so that people would kill each other. He was given a large sword.
REV 6:5 5 When he opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say, “Come!” So I looked, and there was a black horse. Its rider held a balance for weighing in his hand.
REV 6:6 6 I heard what sounded like a voice from among the four living creatures. It said, “A quart of wheat for a denarion, and three quarts of barley for a denarion, but don’t damage the olive oil and the wine.”
REV 6:7 7 When he opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature say, “Come!”
REV 6:8 8 So I looked, and there was a pale green horse. Its rider’s name was Death, and the Grave was following right behind. They were given authority over a fourth of the earth, to kill by sword, famine, disease, and the wild animals of the earth.
REV 6:9 9 When he opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar those who had been slaughtered on account of the word of God and the witness they had given.
REV 6:10 10 They cried out with a loud voice, “Holy and true Master, how long will you wait before you pass judgment? How long before you require justice for our blood, which was shed by those who live on earth?”
REV 6:11 11 Each of them was given a white robe, and they were told to rest a little longer, until their fellow servants and brothers and sisters—who were about to be killed as they were—were finished.
REV 6:12 12 I looked on as he opened the sixth seal, and there was a great earthquake. The sun became black as funeral clothing, and the entire moon turned red as blood.
REV 6:13 13 The stars of the sky fell to the earth as a fig tree drops its fruit when shaken by a strong wind.
REV 6:14 14 The sky disappeared like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved from its place.
REV 6:15 15 Then the kings of the earth, the officials and the generals, the rich and the powerful, and everyone, slave and free, hid themselves in caves and in the rocks of the mountains.
REV 6:16 16 They called to the mountains and the rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of the one seated on the throne and from the Lamb’s wrath!
REV 6:17 17 The great day of their wrath has come, and who is able to stand?”
REV 7:1 1 After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth. They held back the earth’s four winds so that no wind would blow against the earth, the sea, or any tree.
REV 7:2 2 I saw another angel coming up from the east, holding the seal of the living God. He cried out with a loud voice to the four angels who had been given the power to damage the earth and sea.
REV 7:3 3 He said, “Don’t damage the earth, the sea, or the trees until we have put a seal on the foreheads of those who serve our God.”
REV 7:4 4 Then I heard the number of those who were sealed: one hundred forty-four thousand, sealed from every tribe of the Israelites:
REV 7:5 5 From the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand were sealed; from the tribe of Reuben, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Gad, twelve thousand;
REV 7:6 6 from the tribe of Asher, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Naphtali, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Manasseh, twelve thousand;
REV 7:7 7 from the tribe of Simeon, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Levi, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Issachar, twelve thousand;
REV 7:8 8 from the tribe of Zebulun, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Joseph, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Benjamin, twelve thousand were sealed.
REV 7:9 9 After this I looked, and there was a great crowd that no one could number. They were from every nation, tribe, people, and language. They were standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They wore white robes and held palm branches in their hands.
REV 7:10 10 They cried out with a loud voice: “Victory belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb.”
REV 7:11 11 All the angels stood in a circle around the throne, and around the elders and the four living creatures. They fell facedown before the throne and worshipped God,
REV 7:12 12 saying, “Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and might be to our God forever and always. Amen.”
REV 7:13 13 Then one of the elders said to me, “Who are these people wearing white robes, and where did they come from?”
REV 7:14 14 I said to him, “Sir, you know.” Then he said to me, “These people have come out of great hardship. They have washed their robes and made them white in the Lamb’s blood.
REV 7:15 15 This is the reason they are before God’s throne. They worship him day and night in his temple, and the one seated on the throne will shelter them.
REV 7:16 16 They won’t hunger or thirst anymore. No sun or scorching heat will beat down on them,
REV 7:17 17 because the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne will shepherd them. He will lead them to the springs of life-giving water, and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.”
REV 8:1 1 Then, when the Lamb opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
REV 8:2 2 Then I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.
REV 8:3 3 Another angel came and stood at the altar, and he held a gold bowl for burning incense. He was given a large amount of incense, in order to offer it on behalf of the prayers of all the saints on the gold altar in front of the throne.
REV 8:4 4 The smoke of the incense offered for the prayers of the saints rose up before God from the angel’s hand.
REV 8:5 5 Then the angel took the incense container and filled it with fire from the altar. He threw it down to the earth, and there were thunder, voices, lightning, and an earthquake.
REV 8:6 6 Then the seven angels who held the seven trumpets got ready to blow them.
REV 8:7 7 The first angel blew his trumpet, and hail and fire mixed with blood appeared, and was thrown down to the earth. A third of the earth was burned up. A third of the trees were burned up. All the green grass was burned up.
REV 8:8 8 Then the second angel blew his trumpet, and something like a huge mountain burning with fire was thrown down into the sea. A third of the sea became blood,
REV 8:9 9 a third of the creatures living in the sea died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
REV 8:10 10 Then the third angel blew his trumpet, and a great star, burning like a torch, fell from heaven. It fell on a third of the rivers and springs of water.
REV 8:11 11 The star’s name is Wormwood, and a third of the waters became wormwood, and many people died from the water, because it became so bitter.
REV 8:12 12 Then the fourth angel blew his trumpet, and a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars so that a third of them became dark. The day lost a third of its light, and the night lost a third of its light too.
REV 8:13 13 Then I looked and I heard an eagle flying high overhead. It said with a loud voice, “Horror, horror, oh! The horror for those who live on earth because of the blasts of the remaining trumpets that the three angels are about to blow!”
REV 9:1 1 Then the fifth angel blew his trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to earth, and he was given the key to the shaft of the abyss.
REV 9:2 2 He opened the shaft of the abyss; and smoke rose up from the shaft, like smoke from a huge furnace. The sun and air were darkened by the smoke from the shaft.
REV 9:3 3 Then locusts came forth from the smoke and onto the earth. They were given power like the power that scorpions have on the earth.
REV 9:4 4 They were told not to hurt the grass of the earth or any green plant or any tree. They could only hurt the people who didn’t have the seal of God on their foreheads.
REV 9:5 5 The locusts weren’t allowed to kill them, but only to make them suffer for five months—and the suffering they inflict is like that of a scorpion when it strikes a person.
REV 9:6 6 In those days people will seek death, but they won’t find it. They will want to die, but death will run away from them.
REV 9:7 7 The locusts looked like horses ready for battle. On their heads were what seemed to be gold crowns. Their faces were like human faces,
REV 9:8 8 their hair was like women’s hair, and their teeth were like lions’ teeth.
REV 9:9 9 In front they had what seemed to be iron armor upon their chests, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of many chariots and horses racing into battle.
REV 9:10 10 They also have tails with stingers, just like scorpions; and in their tails is their power to hurt people for five months.
REV 9:11 11 Their king is an angel from the abyss, whose Hebrew name is Abaddon, and whose Greek name is Apollyon.
REV 9:12 12 The first horror has passed. Look! Two horrors are still coming after this.
REV 9:13 13 Then the sixth angel blew his trumpet, and I heard a voice from the four horns of the gold altar that is before God.
REV 9:14 14 It said to the sixth angel, who had the trumpet, “Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates.”
REV 9:15 15 Then the four angels who had been made ready for that hour, day, month, and year were released to kill a third of humankind.
REV 9:16 16 The number of cavalry troops was two hundred million. I heard their number.
REV 9:17 17 And this is the way I saw the horses and their riders in the vision: they had breastplates that were fiery red, dark blue, and yellow as sulfur. The horses’ heads were like lions’ heads, and out of their mouths came fire, smoke, and sulfur.
REV 9:18 18 By these three plagues a third of humankind was killed: by the fire, smoke, and sulfur coming out of their mouths.
REV 9:19 19 The horses’ power is in their mouths and their tails, for their tails are like snakes with heads that inflict injuries.
REV 9:20 20 The rest of humankind, who weren’t killed by these plagues, didn’t change their hearts and lives and turn from their handiwork. They didn’t stop worshipping demons and idols made of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood—idols that can’t see or hear or walk.
REV 9:21 21 They didn’t turn away from their murders, their spells and drugs, their sexual immorality, or their stealing.
REV 10:1 1 Then I saw another powerful angel coming down from heaven. He was robed with a cloud, with a rainbow over his head. His face was like the sun, and his feet were like fiery pillars.
REV 10:2 2 He held an open scroll in his hand. He put his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land.
REV 10:3 3 He called out with a loud voice like a lion roaring, and when he called out, the seven thunders raised their voices.
REV 10:4 4 When the seven thunders spoke, I was about to write, but I heard a voice from heaven say, “Seal up what the seven thunders have said, and don’t write it down.”
REV 10:5 5 Then the angel I saw standing on the sea and on the land raised his right hand to heaven.
REV 10:6 6 He swore by the one who lives forever and always, who created heaven and what is in it, the earth and what is in it, and the sea and what is in it, and said, “The time is up.
REV 10:7 7 In the days when the seventh angel blows his trumpet, God’s mysterious purpose will be accomplished, fulfilling the good news he gave to his servants the prophets.”
REV 10:8 8 Then the voice I heard from heaven spoke to me again and said, “Go, take the opened scroll from the hand of the angel who stands on the sea and on the land.”
REV 10:9 9 So I went to the angel and told him to give me the scroll. He said to me, “Take it and eat it. It will make you sick to your stomach, but sweet as honey in your mouth.”
REV 10:10 10 So I took the scroll from the angel’s hand and ate it. And it was sweet as honey in my mouth, but when I swallowed it, it made my stomach churn.

REV 11:2 2 But don’t measure the court outside the temple. Leave that out, because it has been given to the nations, and they will trample the holy city underfoot for forty-two months.
REV 11:3 3 “And I will allow my two witnesses to prophesy for one thousand two hundred sixty days, wearing mourning clothes.
REV 11:4 4 These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.
REV 11:5 5 If anyone wants to hurt them, fire comes out of their mouth and burns up their enemies. So if anyone wants to hurt them, they have to be killed in this way.
REV 11:6 6 They have the power to close up the sky so that no rain will fall for as long as they prophesy. They also have power over the waters, to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with any plague, as often as they wish.
REV 11:7 7 “When they have finished their witnessing, the beast that comes up from the abyss will make war on them, gain victory over them, and kill them.
REV 11:8 8 Their dead bodies will lie on the street of the great city that is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where also their Lord was crucified.
REV 11:9 9 And for three and a half days, members of the peoples, tribes, languages, and nations will look at their dead bodies, but they won’t let their dead bodies be put in a tomb.
REV 11:10 10 Those who live on earth will rejoice over them. They will celebrate and give each other gifts, because these two prophets had brought such pain to those who live on earth.
REV 11:11 11 “But after three and a half days, the breath of life from God entered them, and they stood on their feet. Great fear came over those who saw them.
REV 11:12 12 Then they heard a loud voice from heaven say to them, ‘Come up here.’ And they went up to heaven in a cloud, while their enemies watched them.
REV 11:13 13 At that hour there was a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell. Seven thousand people were killed by the earthquake, and the rest were afraid and gave glory to the God of heaven.”
REV 11:14 14 The second horror is over. The third horror is coming soon.
REV 11:15 15 Then the seventh angel blew his trumpet, and there were loud voices in heaven saying, “The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and his Christ, and he will rule forever and always.”
REV 11:16 16 Then the twenty-four elders, who were seated on their thrones before God, fell on their faces and worshipped God.
REV 11:17 17 They said, “We give thanks to you, Lord God Almighty, who is and was, for you have taken your great power and enforced your rule.
REV 11:18 18 The nations were enraged, but your wrath came. The time came for the dead to be judged. The time came to reward your servants, the prophets and saints, and those who fear your name, both small and great, and to destroy those who destroy the earth.”
